Charles River Laboratories to Acquire Frontage’s Bioanalysis and DMPK Businesses
PDF Version 
– Strengthens Charles River's Bioanalysis and DMPK Capabilities to Support Clients Across the Drug Development Lifecycle – 
– Advances Pathway to Purpose Strategy and Enhances Long-Term Growth and Value Creation – 
WILMINGTON, Mass. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 9, 2026--
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) announced today that it has entered into definitive agreements to acquire Frontage Holdings Corporation’s bioanalysis and DMPK operations in Exton, Pennsylvania for approximately $470 million in cash, subject to customary closing adjustments. In addition to the initial purchase price, the transaction includes additional payments of up to $75 million , contingent on future performance of the acquired businesses. The transaction is expected to close during the first half of 2027, subject to required shareholder and regulatory approvals, and other customary closing conditions.
Birgit Girshick , Chief Executive Officer, commented, “The planned acquisition accelerates our strategy to expand our bioanalysis capabilities and enhance our offering in an attractive, high-growth market. As biologics and increasingly complex modalities become a larger part of development pipelines, clients are seeking scientific partners that can support programs from early development through the clinic. By adding Frontage’s clinical bioanalysis expertise, talented scientific team, and strong client relationships, we will be better positioned to meet those evolving needs.”
“This acquisition will advance our Pathway to Purpose strategy by expanding our presence in clinical bioanalysis, strengthening our scientific leadership, and enhancing our ability to serve clients across the drug development lifecycle. Our combined bioanalysis and DMPK offering will provide a more integrated solution that accelerates development timelines and improves continuity from preclinical through clinical testing. The transaction is expected to enhance our growth profile and support long-term value creation for clients and shareholders. We look forward to welcoming Frontage’s talented bioanalysis and DMPK team to the Charles River family,” Ms. Girshick concluded.
Frontage’s laboratory testing sites that will be acquired provide a comprehensive suite of bioanalysis, biomarker, and DMPK (drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics) testing services for large and small molecules, primarily supporting clinical development programs for biopharmaceutical clients. The planned acquisition includes a CLIA-certified central laboratory and encompasses two sites in Exton, Pennsylvania that operate across approximately 150,000 square feet and employ approximately 340 people.
Strategic Rationale 
The planned acquisition of Frontage’s bioanalysis and DMPK businesses will expand Charles River’s capabilities in the high-growth clinical bioanalysis sector and enhance its ability to support clients from early-stage research through clinical development. The transaction complements Charles River’s existing strength in preclinical bioanalysis primarily for biologics and complex modalities, while adding scale and capacity to support future growth.
Accelerates Long-Term Bioanalysis Growth Strategy - Bioanalysis represents an attractive long-term growth opportunity as increasing demand across biologics, complex modalities, and advanced therapies requires additional scientific data and specialized assays. As a result, the bioanalysis market sector is expected to expand from approximately $6 billion in 2026 to approximately $8 to $9 billion in 2031, representing annual growth of 6% to 8%, with higher growth expected in biologics and complex modalities, as well as for clinical-phase testing. The planned acquisition complements Charles River’s ongoing investments in its bioanalysis capabilities, including capacity additions, positioning the Company to capitalize on attractive long-term growth opportunities.
Expands Clinical Bioanalysis Presence and Client Continuity – Clients increasingly seek continuity from laboratory testing partners as programs advance from preclinical to clinical development, as bioanalysis data generated from preclinical programs will help guide their early clinical decisions. Currently, approximately 15% of Charles River’s bioanalysis revenue is generated from clinical-phase testing. The planned acquisition will meaningfully expand the Company’s clinical bioanalysis capabilities and scale, enabling broader support across the drug development lifecycle including late-stage clinical diagnostic testing. In 2025, the majority of Frontage’s bioanalysis revenue was generated during clinical development. A more balanced and integrated bioanalysis portfolio is expected to strengthen Charles River’s client relationships, increase share of wallet, and improve client retention throughout longer-duration clinical programs.
Strengthens Scientific Leadership in High-Growth Modalities – Biologics and complex modalities represent the fastest-growing segments of the bioanalysis sector and account for approximately 75% of Charles River’s bioanalysis revenue. As these therapies become a larger share of development pipelines, demand for increasingly sophisticated bioanalysis solutions continues to grow. Frontage’s bioanalysis expertise will complement Charles River’s existing scientific capabilities, further enhancing its leading portfolio in advanced therapies while also expanding its small molecule bioanalysis capabilities. The acquisition is also expected to unlock additional synergies across the Discovery and Safety Assessment (DSA) and Manufacturing Solutions segments.
Financial Details 
The bioanalysis and DMPK businesses that will be acquired represented approximately 40% of Frontage’s total 2025 revenue of $256.7 million . Charles River expects revenue of the acquired businesses will grow at the projected bioanalysis sector growth rate over the next five years.
The transaction is expected to be neutral to non-GAAP earnings per share in 2027 and accretive thereafter. Items excluded from non-GAAP earnings per share are expected to include all acquisition-related costs, primarily amortization of intangible assets, advisory fees, certain costs associated with acquisition-related efficiency initiatives, and certain third-party integration costs.
The acquisition and associated fees are expected to be financed through Charles River’s credit facility and available cash.
The acquired businesses are expected to be reported as part of Charles River’s DSA segment.
Transaction Details and Structure 
Frontage Holdings Corporation is a publicly traded company on The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong. Charles River is participating in a consortium with Hongkong Tigermed Co., Limited (a subsidiary of Hangzhou Tigermed Consulting Co., Ltd.) and Dr. Song Li to first take Frontage private, after which Frontage will be restructured and Charles River will ultimately own the assets and liabilities related to its bioanalysis and DMPK businesses in Exton, Pennsylvania . Further details are as follows:
Charles River is acquiring Frontage together with Frontage’s controlling shareholder, Tigermed, and Frontage’s Chairman of the Board, Dr. Song Li . The three parties have formed a consortium and set up an acquisition vehicle that will privatize Frontage, which is listed on The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited , by way of a court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement, following which Frontage’s listing will be withdrawn.
Immediately following completion of the privatization, the parties will separate Frontage’s businesses into separate subsidiaries. Charles River will retain the bioanalysis and DMPK businesses described above through sole ownership of the acquisition vehicle and certain Frontage subsidiaries, and Frontage’s remaining businesses will be transferred to Tigermed and Dr. Song Li (or his affiliates) through the distribution of other subsidiaries of Frontage.
Completion of the privatization is subject to a number of approvals and conditions, including passing of the requisite resolutions at the general meeting of Tigermed, regulatory approvals, approval by Frontage shareholders and sanction of the scheme by the Grand Court of the Cayman Islands . Tigermed, Dr. Song Li and certain trusts controlled by him have each undertaken to support the transaction. Further details will be set out in the scheme document that will be sent to Frontage shareholders.
Advisers 
J.P. Morgan and CICC are acting as joint financial advisers to the consortium. Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP and Jia Yuan Law Offices are serving as legal counsels. Kirkland & Ellis is the legal counsel to the joint financial advisers.
Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
This press release contains a forward-looking, non-GAAP financial measure: non-GAAP earnings per share accretion related to the proposed acquisition described herein. Non-GAAP financial measures exclude, but are not limited to acquisition-related costs, which primarily include amortization, third-party advisory fees, and certain integration costs. The corresponding GAAP financial measure is not provided because the items that are excluded from GAAP to calculate the comparable non-GAAP measure are dependent on future events that are not able to be reliably predicted by management and are not part of routine operating activities. The Company is unable to provide such a reconciliation without unreasonable effort due to the uncertainty and inherent difficulty in predicting the occurrence, the financial impact, and the periods in which the aggregate acquisition may be recognized. The occurrence, timing and amount of any of the items excluded from GAAP to calculate non-GAAP could significantly impact our GAAP results.
There are limitations in using non-GAAP financial measures, as they are not presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and may be different than non-GAAP financial measures used by other companies. In particular, we believe that the inclusion of supplementary non-GAAP financial measures in this press release helps investors to gain a meaningful understanding of our core operating results and future prospects without the effect of these often-one-time charges, and is consistent with how management measures and forecasts the Company's performance, especially when comparing such results to prior periods or forecasts. We believe that the financial impact of the proposed acquisition (and in certain cases, the evaluation of such proposed acquisition, whether or not ultimately consummated) is often large relative to our overall financial performance, which can adversely affect the comparability of our results on a period-to-period basis. In addition, certain activities and their underlying associated costs, such as business acquisitions, generally occur periodically but on an unpredictable basis. Non-GAAP results also allow investors to compare the Company’s operations against the financial results of other companies in the industry who similarly provide non-GAAP results. The non-GAAP financial measures included in this press release are not meant to be considered superior to or a substitute for results of operations presented in accordance with GAAP. The Company intends to continue to assess the potential value of reporting non-GAAP results consistent with applicable rules and regulations.
Caution Concerning Forward-Looking Statements 
This press release includes forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements may be identified by the use of words such as “anticipate,” “believe,” “expect,” “intend,” “will,” “would,” “may,” “estimate,” “plan,” “outlook,” and “project,” and other similar expressions that predict or indicate future events or trends or that are not statements of historical matters. These statements include statements regarding: the proposed acquisition of Frontage’s bioanalysis and DMPK business; expectations regarding the terms and the timing of the closing of the proposed acquisition including regarding the satisfaction of required shareholder, regulatory and court approvals; expectations with respect to the impact of the proposed acquisition on the Company, its product and service offerings, client perception, operating margin and related cost savings, revenue, including third-party revenue, revenue growth rates, earnings per share, and GAAP or non-GAAP financial results; expectations regarding the separation of the acquired business from Frontage’s other operations and the integration of the acquired business; expectations regarding any earnout payments that may become payable in respect of the acquired business; the Company’s expectations concerning projected future financial and operating performance, including with respect to revenue and booking activity and related financial metrics; the Company's commitment to, and ability to create long-term value for shareholders and to successfully execute on the strategies described herein; client demand, including trends and the future demand for the Company’s products and services; the impact of foreign exchange; and the Company’s plans or prospects, expectations and long-term goals associated with our business.
Forward-looking statements are based on Charles River’s current expectations and beliefs, and involve a number of risks and uncertainties that are difficult to predict and that could cause actual results to differ materially from those stated or implied by the forward-looking statements. Those risks and uncertainties include, but are not limited to: the ability to successfully complete the proposed acquisition and the related privatization of Frontage; the risk that the required regulatory, shareholder or court approvals are not obtained, or are not obtained on the anticipated timetable, or that other conditions to the transaction are not satisfied, and the risk that the transaction is therefore delayed or does not complete; the risk that the separation of the acquired business from Frontage’s other operations is delayed, costs more than anticipated or is not completed as contemplated, including the risk that required third-party consents are not obtained; the ability to successfully integrate the acquired business, and risks and uncertainties associated with that business, including the potential loss of clients or key personnel; uncertainty as to whether any earnout payment will become payable and the resulting impact on the total consideration for the transaction; ; and the demand, proposal and booking trends (including net book-to-bill) in the Company’s DSA business segment. Furthermore, these and other risks relating to the Company are set forth in the documents filed by Charles River with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including without limitation, the Risk Factors in the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K filed February 18, 2026. Because forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties, actual results and events may differ materially from results and events currently expected by Charles River, and Charles River assumes no obligation and expressly disclaims any duty to update information contained in this press release except as required by law.
About Charles River 
Charles River provides essential products and services to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies and leading academic institutions around the globe accelerate their research and drug development efforts. Our dedicated employees are focused on providing clients with exactly what they need to improve and expedite the discovery, early-stage development and safe manufacture of new therapies for the patients who need them. To learn more about our unique portfolio and breadth of services, visit www.criver.com .

Estelle Brachlianoff, CEO of the Group, stated:
“Veolia delivered strong growth in the third quarter, with revenue up +5.0%(1), driven notably by the
performance of our international activities and Water. This momentum reflects the strength of our
positioning, offering unique solutions to address critical needs. Current context confirms that Veolia
relies on powerful structural trends, including water security, resource sovereignty, and the growing
demand for essential environmental services.
(1) At constant scope and forex and excluding energy prices

We continued to improve our operational performance, with a further 50-basis-point increase in
EBITDA margin. This achievement demonstrates the benefits of our recurring efficiency plans, the
strict discipline of our operational management and our ability to implement additional action plans
whenever required.
The transformation of our portfolio towards international and innovative activities, with higher value
creation, is progressing rapidly. The integration of Clean Earth has got off to a successful start,
strengthening our platform in the United States, while our disposal plan is well underway, with €570
million of disposals already signed at an average multiple of 10.4 times EBITDA.
Building on these solid results we fully confirm our 2026 guidance and our GreenUp trajectory.”

organic growth of +5.1%(2), in the target range of +5% to +6%(2), and margin increase of
+50bps:

Clean Earth acquisition and hybrid debt repayment. Confirmation of leverage ratio equal or
slightly above 3x at year-end.
Continued Group profile transformation towards international and
technologies
● Successful start of Clean Earth integration in Hazardous Waste in the US, in line with
the plan, after closing in June. Organization in place and ready to deliver synergies starting
in 2027
● ~€2bn+ disposal plan well underway with €570M already signed at a 10.4x 2025
EBITDA multiple and all processes launched

MAIN BUSINESS DEVELOPMENTS
NEW - Global - Veolia strengthens its position as the world leader in desalination with major
contracts in the Middle East. Nearly 200 million euros in contracts in Oman and the United Arab
Emirates, for a total capacity of 490,000 m³/day. 18% of the world’s desalination capacity has been
built with Veolia’s advanced technologies and innovative solutions, making it the global leader in
Water Technologies.
NEW - Spain - Veolia wins a major €1 billion, 25-year drinking water services contract in
Spain. Veolia announces that it has been selected as the winning bidder by The Metropolitan
Council of Barcelona for the landmark €1 billion, 25-year tender for the management of essential
drinking water services across eight municipalities in the Barcelona metropolitan area, serving
more than 230,000 residents. This contract will consolidate the Group’s long lasting presence and
commitment to Spain which is set to become its third-largest market in the coming years.
NEW - United Kingdom - Veolia wins £0.7bn Waste Contracts with East London and Surrey.
In September, Veolia won a £527m waste contract for Surrey Councils to deliver essential services
to over 420,000 residents. AI innovations and increased data analytics will be implemented to help
increase recycling rates. In July, Veolia won a 10-year contract with East London Waste Authority
at around £183 million, with Veolia delivering recycling and waste services for 1.2 million residents.
Veolia now partners with more than half of London’s local authorities, delivering social value and
recycling and waste treatment services to over 5 million Londoners.
NEW - Saudi Arabia - Veolia signs three strategic agreements to accelerate the Kingdom's
environmental security. Veolia announced the signing of three strategic memorandums of
understanding in water technologies and hazardous waste management. These agreements
address major challenges for the Kingdom: preservation of water resources, energy efficiency,
decarbonization of industry, and development of local skills. Established with three leading
economic and industrial players in Saudi Arabia, these partnerships strengthen Veolia’s
longstanding commitment in the country and its contribution to the ambitions of Saudi Vision 2030,
aligning with the objectives of its strategic GreenUp program.
US - Veolia completes Clean Earth deal, doubling its U.S. Hazardous Waste business and
expanding its growth platform. Veolia reinforces its position as a world’s leading hazardous
waste management company, effectively doubling U.S. hazardous waste revenues. The $3 billion
transaction adds robust pretreatment, storage and disposal capabilities, 2,600 highly trained
people, and an expanded presence to Veolia’s American offering, making the company an even
greater powerhouse for innovative environmental services and solutions. Backed by a strong
integration track record, the transaction will deliver $120 million of synergies by year 4.
Global - Veolia launched in London a new global offer for data centers, Data Center
Resource 360, designed to address the critical environmental and operational challenges facing
the rapidly expanding digital infrastructure sector, while supporting the resilience of communities
and responding to their critical resource needs. The offer places a particular emphasis on their
integration and acceptability into local ecosystems, at a time when environmental security is
emerging as a key strategic priority.
In addition, in the context of this new offer, Veolia works with Amazon to develop reclaimed
Water for cooling systems for Data Centers. Collaboration combines Veolia's advanced water
reuse technologies with Amazon AI and cloud capabilities to advance more sustainable strategies
for data center infrastructure. This supports Amazon’s goal to be water positive in direct data
center operations by 2030 and aligns with the objectives of Veolia’s GreenUp strategic program
regarding resource preservation, pollution control, and decarbonization.
3
Water Technologies - Veolia accelerates growth in microelectronics with €343 million in
water technology bookings since the beginning of the year, confirming strong commercial
momentum in a strategic growth market. Major contract wins with leading semiconductor
manufacturers in Singapore and the United States, including ultrapure water production and
wastewater reclamation to zero liquid discharge standards. Full water-cycle expertise, from
ultrapure water to reuse and advanced wastewater treatment, supporting Veolia’s GreenUp
strategy and customers’ operational resilience.
Australia - Veolia strengthens its leadership in PFAS treatment in Australia with the
acquisition of the country's major soil remediation player. The Group reinforces its position as
a pioneer in the fight against PFAS contamination in Australia, with the acquisition of Enviropacific
acting as a double growth booster - accelerating both its geographic expansion and its capabilities
in hazardous waste treatment - fully aligned with its global GreenUp strategy. The transaction, part
of usual tuck-ins, is valued at AUD 228 million (Enterprise Value) and was closed at the end of
March 2026. Enviropacific reported FY25 turnover of approximately AUD c.250 million, with nearly
300 employees.
Colombia - Veolia strengthens its leadership in Latin America with a landmark Water
contract in Colombia to modernize Cúcuta’s Water infrastructure. Veolia will lead an ambitious
plan in partnership with Cúcuta municipality to modernize the city's water infrastructure and
address long-standing water and sanitation needs. The plant will considerably reduce water losses
from the current 42% to below 30%, bringing it in line with the best systems in the country and in
Latin America. This contract represents around €100 million in average annual revenue over 20
years, i.e. an estimated c.€2 billion backlog.
France - Veolia unveils its plan to accelerate heating and cooling networks in France to help
cities adapt to heatwaves. Faced with the increasing frequency and intensity of heatwaves,
Veolia aims to make heating-cooling networks an essential infrastructure for urban adaptation to
climate change. More than 100 sites have been identified in France to support the accelerated
deployment of these urban networks, which are capable of simultaneously producing heat and cold
from local, renewable, or recovered energy sources, enabling service for up to 3 million people.
These projects will be based on energy recovery solutions from urban wastewater, geothermal
energy, data centers, and waste-to-energy plants, to accelerate their development, continuing the
innovative "Ecothermal Grid" offering.
Czech Republic - Veolia drives the Czech coal exit with a multi-energy transformation in
Karviná. The Group is transforming the Karviná plant into a multi-energy plant, eliminating coal
use by 2029, while serving approximately 50,000 households. Based on local and circular energy
sources, the new system will reduce annual CO2 emissions by 200,000 tonnes while ensuring
long-term price stability and air quality improvements for the Karviná and Havířov regions.

Charles River Laboratories Announces Third-Quarter 2026 Results
Download PDF 497.7 KB 
WILMINGTON, Mass. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 4, 2026--
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) today reported its results for the third quarter ended September 26, 2026 .
Key Highlights 
Reports third-quarter revenue of $982.7 million , GAAP earnings per share of $6.86 , and non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.09 .
Organic revenue growth of 4.7%, outperforming the Company's prior outlook and representing a return to organic revenue growth for the second consecutive quarter.
Operating margin increased year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating margin increasing 330 basis points to 23.0% and GAAP operating margin increasing 730 basis points to 20.6%.
Non-GAAP earnings per share increased 27.2% year-over-year.
Increases 2026 guidance for revenue and non-GAAP earnings per share.
Organic revenue guidance increasing by 100 basis points and non-GAAP earnings per share guidance increasing by $0.15 at midpoint.
Guidance increases primarily driven by third-quarter outperformance, led by a better-than-expected performance in the DSA segment and a lower tax rate.
Charles River unveiled its Pathway to Purpose strategic vision and Create the Future™ initiative at its 2026 Investor Day , outlining initiatives designed to enhance operational excellence, strengthen scientific leadership, and drive long-term value creation.
The Company advanced modernization efforts through the implementation of its Endosafe ® Cartridge Technology Automated Manufacturing Suite , which utilizes a fully automated production suite to increase production capacity and strengthen manufacturing controls and digital traceability. In addition, the Company partnered with Autolomous to launch Apollo Orchestrate™ , a new capability within Charles River's Apollo ® platform to digitize and transform laboratory workflows, increase efficiency, and provide greater transparency and connectivity with clients.
Charles River has also taken steps to continue to strengthen its scientific capabilities. It recently announced an industry collaboration with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ( FDA ) to validate preclinical screening tools to quantify and rank the abuse potential of new drugs.
To further advance its Alternative Methods Advancement Project™ (AMAP™) initiative, the Company introduced a new, rapid cell banking program designed to significantly accelerate product release timelines in its Biologics Testing Solutions business by incorporating in vitro next-generation sequencing capabilities into the cell bank production process. In addition, its Virtual Control Group (VCG) database and methodology will be used in an upcoming Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)-compliant safety assessment study for Ipsen.
Third-Quarter Results 
Revenue was $982.7 million , a decrease of 2.2% from $1,004.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by the impact of the May 2026 divestitures. On an organic basis, revenue increased 4.7%, driven by revenue growth in the Manufacturing Solutions (Manufacturing) and Discovery and Safety Assessment (DSA) segments. Organic revenue growth excludes the effect of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign currency translation.
In the third quarter of 2026, the GAAP operating margin was 20.6%, compared to 13.3% in the third quarter of 2025, driven primarily by a benefit of $44.6 million in the DSA segment from the reversal of acquired non-income tax reserves following newly enacted tax legislation and completion of certain tax requirements in a foreign jurisdiction. The GAAP net income available to common shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 was $333.1 million , or $6.86 per diluted share, compared to GAAP net income of $54.4 million , or $1.10 per diluted share for the same period in 2025. The GAAP net income and earnings per share increases included a benefit totaling $245.6 million , or $5.06 per share, associated with the reversal of acquired tax reserves following newly enacted tax legislation and completion of certain tax requirements in a foreign jurisdiction.
On a non-GAAP basis, the third-quarter operating margin increased to 23.0% from 19.7% in the third quarter of 2025, primarily as a result of the benefit of the CDMO divestiture and operating leverage from higher sales volume for safety assessment services. Non-GAAP net income was $150.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 24.8% from $120.3 million for the same period in 2025. Third-quarter diluted earnings per share on a non-GAAP basis were $3.09 , an increase of 27.2% from $2.43 per share in the third quarter of 2025. The non-GAAP net income and earnings per share increases were driven primarily by the higher operating margin and a lower tax rate.
Birgit Girshick , Chief Executive Officer, said, “In the third quarter, we were encouraged by the continued strength of the biopharmaceutical demand environment and that was reflected in our financial results. Revenue and earnings per share outperformed our prior expectations, DSA net bookings and proposals continued to show robust, year-over-year increases, and we continued to make meaningful progress towards our strategy and long-term financial targets. We see significant opportunities to continue to strengthen Charles River’s position as a leading scientific partner for regulated testing across the drug development continuum. Through our Pathway to Purpose strategy, we are building a more agile, client-centric organization that will deepen client relationships, expand engagement across our portfolio, and increase our share of R&D spend as demand trends continue to improve."
Third-Quarter Segment Results 
Discovery and Safety Assessment (DSA) 
Revenue for the DSA segment was $596.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of 0.7% from $600.7 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by the divestiture of certain European Discovery Services sites. Organic revenue increased by 5.9%, driven primarily by higher study volume for regulated safety assessment services.
In the third quarter of 2026, the DSA segment’s GAAP operating margin increased to 28.9% from 20.5% in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the reversal of acquired non-income tax reserves. On a non-GAAP basis, the operating margin increased to 26.8% from 25.4% in the third quarter of 2025. The non-GAAP operating margin increase was primarily driven by operating leverage from higher study volume for regulated safety assessment services, as well as lower sourcing costs for large research models.
Manufacturing Solutions (Manufacturing) 
Revenue for the Manufacturing segment was $178.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of 6.2% from $190.7 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by the CDMO divestiture. Organic revenue increased 7.4%, driven by strong demand in both the Biologics Testing Solutions and Microbial Solutions businesses.
The Manufacturing segment’s GAAP operating margin was 35.7%, compared to 20.9% in the third quarter of 2025. On a non-GAAP basis, the operating margin increased to 38.6% from 26.7% in the third quarter of 2025. The GAAP and non-GAAP increases were driven primarily by the benefit of the CDMO divestiture.
Research Models and Services (RMS) 
Revenue for the RMS segment was $207.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of 2.8% from $213.5 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by the Cell Solutions divestiture. Organic revenue decreased by 0.6%, due primarily to lower revenue for small research models in North America and for large research models. The decline was partially offset by higher revenue for small research models in China and for research model services, particularly the Insourcing Solutions business.
In the third quarter of 2026, the RMS segment’s GAAP operating margin increased to 19.9% from 16.2% in the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to lower costs related to the Cell Solutions divestiture and restructuring initiatives. On a non-GAAP basis, the operating margin decreased to 24.4% from 25.0%. The non-GAAP operating margin decrease was primarily driven by the impact of an unfavorable revenue mix, both geographically and related to large research models.
2026 Guidance Update 
The Company is increasing its 2026 revenue and earnings per share guidance, which was last updated on August 5, 2026 . This increase primarily reflects the third-quarter outperformance, which was principally driven by the better-than-expected performance in the DSA segment and a lower tax rate. On a GAAP basis, the Company is also increasing its earnings per share guidance, due primarily to the third-quarter benefit associated with the reversal of acquired tax reserves.

Non-GAAP Reconciliations 
The Company reports non-GAAP results in this press release, which exclude often-one-time charges and other items that are outside of normal operations. A reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP results is provided in the schedules at the end of this press release.
Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
This press release contains non-GAAP financial measures, such as non-GAAP earnings per share, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP operating margin, and non-GAAP net income. Non-GAAP financial measures exclude, but are not limited to, the amortization of intangible assets and the purchase accounting step-up adjustment on inventory and certain long term biological assets, and other charges and adjustments related to our acquisitions and divestitures, including expenses associated with evaluating and integrating acquisitions and divestitures, including advisory fees, certain transition costs, and certain other transaction-related costs, as well as fair value adjustments associated with contingent consideration; charges, gains, and losses attributable to businesses or properties we plan to close, consolidate, or divest, including the divestitures of our CDMO and Cell Solutions businesses, the sale of certain of our European Discovery Services sites, and the sale of certain assets including real estate; severance and other costs associated with our restructuring initiatives; investment gains or losses associated with our venture capital and certain other strategic equity investments; certain legal costs and adjustments related to an NHP inventory charge in our DSA segment related to now concluded U.S . government investigations into the NHP supply chain; legal and advisory costs related to entering into a Cooperation Agreement with a shareholder; tax effect of all of the aforementioned matters; and adjustments related to the derecognition of certain deferred tax assets due to the CDMO Gene Therapy intangible asset impairment charge, the recognition of deferred tax assets expected to be utilized as a result of changes to the Company's international financing structure, the revaluation of deferred tax liabilities as a result of foreign tax legislation, and the tax benefit recognized as a result of the changes in tax law enacted in a foreign jurisdiction. This press release also refers to our revenue on both a GAAP and non-GAAP basis: on a non-GAAP basis, we define “organic revenue growth” as reported revenue growth adjusted for foreign currency translation, acquisitions, and divestitures. We exclude these items from the non-GAAP financial measures because they are outside our normal operations. There are limitations in using non-GAAP financial measures, as they are not presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and may be different than non-GAAP financial measures used by other companies. In particular, we believe that the inclusion of supplementary non-GAAP financial measures in this press release helps investors to gain a meaningful understanding of our core operating results and future prospects without the effect of these often-one-time charges, and is consistent with how management measures and forecasts the Company's performance, especially when comparing such results to prior periods or forecasts. We believe that the financial impact of our acquisitions and divestitures (and in certain cases, the evaluation of such acquisitions and divestitures, whether or not ultimately consummated) is often large relative to our overall financial performance, which can adversely affect the comparability of our results on a period-to-period basis. In addition, certain activities and their underlying associated costs, such as business acquisitions, generally occur periodically but on an unpredictable basis. We calculate non-GAAP integration costs to include third-party integration costs incurred post-acquisition. Presenting revenue on an organic basis allows investors to measure our revenue growth exclusive of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign currency exchange fluctuations more clearly. Non-GAAP results also allow investors to compare the Company’s operations against the financial results of other companies in the industry who similarly provide non-GAAP results. The non-GAAP financial measures included in this press release are not meant to be considered superior to or a substitute for results of operations presented in accordance with GAAP. The Company intends to continue to assess the potential value of reporting non-GAAP results consistent with applicable rules and regulations. Reconciliations of the non-GAAP financial measures used in this press release to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures are set forth in this press release, and can also be found on the Company’s website at ir.criver.com .

About Charles River 
Charles River provides essential products and services to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies and leading academic institutions around the globe accelerate their research and drug development efforts. Ouster Announces Results for Third Quarter 2026
November 3, 2026
PDF Version 
Record product revenue, achieving 15th straight quarter of growth 
Lidar and camera shipments of more than 27,000 units 
SAN FRANCISCO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 3, 2026--
Ouster, Inc. (Nasdaq: OUST) (“Ouster” or the “Company”), a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI, announced financial results for the three months ended September 30, 2026 .
“We delivered a strong third quarter, with $59 million in revenue and more than 27,000 total sensors shipped, cementing Ouster’s evolution into a comprehensive platform that meets the diverse, global demands of Physical AI. Our Stereolabs cameras had a record quarter of shipments, unlocked by our investments in capacity to meet surging growth in the robotics sector,” said Ouster CEO Angus Pacala .
“The market reception for Rev8 has been decisive. As the world’s first native color lidar, Rev8 is a paradigm shift that is proving to be an undeniable competitive differentiator. Hundreds of customers have already chosen Rev8 for their mission critical applications. Customer demand has been robust while we ramp initial production, and we expect our delivery cadence to accelerate into 2027. The breakout performance of Stereolabs proves our vision of a unified platform is exactly what the market demands. From farms and distribution centers to last mile delivery, the world’s most innovative companies are choosing Ouster. We provide the complete stack of lidar, vision, compute, and software required to bring Physical AI into the real world.”
Third Quarter 2026 Highlights: 
$59 million in revenue, up 50% year over year and up 9% sequentially.
Shipped more than 27,000 lidar and camera sensors for revenue, of which lidar was approximately 27% of the total.
GAAP gross margin of 43%, essentially flat year over year and down 600 bps sequentially.
GAAP net loss of $14 million , an improvement of $8 million year over year and an improvement of $4 million sequentially.
Non-GAAP gross margin 1 of 47%, down 100 bps year over year and down 700 bps sequentially.
Adjusted EBITDA 1 loss of $3 million , an improvement of $5 million year over year and an improvement of $1 million sequentially.
Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and short-term investments of $421 million as of September 30, 2026 .
1 Adjusted EBITDA and non-GAAP gross margin are non-GAAP financial measures. See Non-GAAP Financial Measures for additional information and reconciliations of these measures to their respective most directly comparable financial measures calculated in accordance with U.S . GAAP.
Revenue 
Ouster delivered third quarter revenue of $59 million , an increase of 50% year over year and 9% sequentially. Product revenue of $56 million was an increase of 42% year over year and 6% sequentially, primarily driven by customers in the industrial and robotics verticals for use cases in warehouse automation, defense, construction, mapping, and data collection. The Company shipped over 27,000 units, of which lidar was approximately 27% of the total.
Gross Margin 
GAAP gross margin was 43%, compared with 42% in the third quarter of 2025 and 49% in the second quarter of 2026. A one-time refund positively impacted second quarter gross margin by approximately 1,000 basis points. Non-GAAP gross margin was 47%, compared with 47% in the third quarter of 2025 and 53% in the second quarter of 2026. Non-GAAP gross margin excludes the impact of stock-based compensation expenses, and certain other items outside of ordinary operations.
Fourth Quarter 2026 Outlook: 
For the fourth quarter of 2026, Ouster expects to achieve $61 million to $64 million in total revenue.
Upcoming Investor Events 
Ouster management is scheduled to participate in the following upcoming investor events:
ROTH Technology Conference - November 18, 2026 , New York City 
Northland Growth Conference - December 16, 2026 (Virtual)
Conference Call Information 
Ouster will host a conference call and live webcast for analysts and investors at 5:00 p.m. ET today, November 3, 2026 to discuss its financial results and business outlook. Interested parties may listen to a live webcast of the conference call. Registration for the webcast can be completed by visiting the following website: https://edge.media-server.com/mmc/p/5gs6eo5t . The webcast will be available for replay for at least 30 days after the conference call on Ouster’s investor website at https://investors.ouster.com/ .
About Ouster 
Ouster (Nasdaq: OUST) is a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI across industrial, robotics, automotive, and smart infrastructure. With a unified platform of high-performance digital lidar, cameras, AI compute, sensor fusion and perception software, and AI models, Ouster delivers solutions that improve quality of life in the physical world. Headquartered in San Francisco, CA , Ouster has a global presence serving thousands of customers with offices in the Americas , Europe , and Asia-Pacific . For more information about our products, visit www.ouster.com , contact our sales team, or connect with us on X or LinkedIn.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
In addition to its results determined in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (“GAAP”), Ouster believes the non-GAAP measures of Non-GAAP Gross Profit, Non-GAAP Gross Margin and Adjusted EBITDA are useful in evaluating its operating performance. Ouster calculates Non-GAAP Gross Profit as gross profit (loss) excluding amortization of acquired intangibles, acquisition and integration-related charges, and stock-based compensation expense. Non-GAAP Gross Margin is calculated as Non-GAAP Gross Profit divided by revenues. Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as net loss excluding interest expense (income), net, other (income) expense, net, stock-based compensation expense, provision for (benefit from) income taxes, amortization of acquired intangibles, acquisition and integration-related charges, depreciation expenses, certain litigation expenses, gain on lease termination and other items. Ouster believes that Non-GAAP Gross Profit, Non-GAAP Gross Margin, and Adjusted EBITDA may be helpful to investors because it provides consistency and comparability with past financial performance and may be helpful in comparison with other companies, some of which use similar non-GAAP information to supplement their GAAP results. Adjusted EBITDA is also used by the Board and management as a performance metric for compensation purposes. The non-GAAP financial information is presented for supplemental informational purposes only and should not be considered a substitute for financial information presented in accordance with GAAP, and may be different from similarly titled non-GAAP measures used by other companies. Reconciliation tables of the most comparable GAAP financial measures to the non-GAAP financial measures are included at the end of this press release.

The Chemours Company Reports Third Quarter Results
November 2, 2026
PDF Version 
WILMINGTON, Del. , Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Chemours Company ("Chemours" or "the Company") (NYSE: CC), a global chemistry company with leading market positions in Thermal & Specialized Solutions ("TSS"), Titanium Technologies ("TT"), and Advanced Performance Materials ("APM"), today announced its financial results for the third quarter 2026.
Key Third Quarter 2026 Results & Recent Highlights 1 
Net Sales of $1.5 billion , up slightly from the prior-year quarter, reflecting an approximately 10% year-over-year pricing increase in TT and 26% year-over-year growth in APM Performance Solutions.
Net Income attributable to Chemours of $196 million , or $1.29 per diluted share, compared with Net Income attributable to Chemours of $46 million , or $0.31 per diluted share, in the corresponding prior-year quarter.
Adjusted Net Income 2 of $31 million , or $0.21 per diluted share, compared with Adjusted Net Income of $26 million , or $0.17 per diluted share, in the corresponding prior-year quarter.
Adjusted EBITDA 2,3 of $200 million , compared with $189 million in the prior-year quarter, driven by improved pricing in TT and growth in APM Performance Solutions.
As previously announced, entered into a settlement with the State of North Carolina and 11 local entities to resolve litigation relating to PFAS and other historical discharges from Fayetteville Works, as well as claims of PFAS contamination unrelated to that site, including from the use of AFFF.
Formally launching Chemours' liquid cooling portfolio, including four two-phase direct-to-chip and one immersion cooling fluid under the Faizeon™ liquid cooling brand.
Completed the sale of the Kuan Yin property for total net consideration of ~$340 million , including the remaining land parcel for $56 million of gross proceeds.
"Our third-quarter results demonstrate strong year-over-year performance in TT and APM, reflecting pricing execution in TiO 2 and increased demand across Performance Solutions' high-value AI infrastructure including data center and semiconductor end markets," said Denise Dignam , Chemours President and CEO. "We also continued to make meaningful progress under our Pathway to Thrive, including reaching a settlement with the State of North Carolina , driving operational improvements through the Chemours Business System, and closing the sale of the final parcel of land associated with our former Kuan Yin property. While we continue to navigate TSS stationary aftermarket dynamics and a softer macroeconomic environment, we remain focused on disciplined execution of our strategic priorities and the factors within our control to drive long-term returns for shareholders."

Third quarter 2026 Net Sales were approximately $1.5 billion , an increase of approximately 3% compared with the prior-year quarter. The year-over-year increase in Net Sales was driven by a 5% increase in pricing, partially offset by a 2% decrease in volumes and a slight currency headwind. The pricing increase was primarily driven by previously announced price actions in TT, complemented by a favorable mix shift toward APM Performance Solutions. Lower year-over-year volumes primarily reflected anticipated lower North American stationary AC aftermarket sales of TSS Opteon TM blends compared with elevated demand in the prior-year quarter.
Third quarter 2026 Net Income attributable to Chemours was $196 million , or $1.29 per diluted share, compared with $46 million , or $0.31 per diluted share, in the prior-year quarter. Current-year third-quarter Net Income included the receipt of $150 million related to the PFAS insurance proceeds MOU that was executed in connection with the finalization of the judicial consent order ("JCO") with the State of New Jersey . This was presented as a reduction to Selling, general, and administrative expense. Third quarter Adjusted Net Income increased 19% compared with the prior-year quarter, aligned with trends in Adjusted EBITDA as highlighted below.
Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was $200 million , compared with $189 million in the prior-year quarter. The increase was driven by pricing momentum in TT and a favorable mix shift toward APM Performance Solutions, partially offset by lower TSS volumes associated with the North American stationary AC aftermarket dynamics noted above and higher costs across each business.

Performance Solutions Net Sales increased 26%, reflecting continued order book strength and momentum in high-value specialty products serving data center and semiconductor end markets.
APM segment third quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDA increased 71% to $24 million compared with the prior-year quarter, while Adjusted EBITDA Margin increased two points to 7%. The increase in Adjusted EBITDA was primarily driven by a favorable mix shift toward higher-value Performance Solutions products serving data center and semiconductor end markets, partially offset by higher costs incurred during the period.
Sequentially, APM segment third quarter 2026 Net Sales increased approximately 3%, driven by a 2% increase in price and a 1% increase in volume. Performance Solutions Net Sales increased 8%, reflecting continued order book strength and momentum in high-value specialty products serving data center and semiconductor end markets.
Other Non-Reportable Segment 
The Performance Chemicals and Intermediates business in the Company's Other Non-Reportable Segment had Net Sales and Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter 2026 of $13 million and $1 million , respectively.
Corporate Expenses 
Corporate Expenses were $46 million in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of approximately $1 million compared with the prior-year quarter.
Liquidity and Capital Allocation 
As of September 30, 2026 , consolidated gross debt was $3.9 billion . Debt, net of $698 million in unrestricted 4 cash and cash equivalents, was $3.2 billion , resulting in a Net Leverage ratio of approximately 4.3x on a trailing twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA basis. Total liquidity was $1.7 billion , composed of $698 million in unrestricted cash and cash equivalents and $953 million of revolving credit facility capacity, net of outstanding letters of credit.
Operating cash flows for the third quarter of 2026 were $149 million , which includes the aforementioned receipt of $150 million in restricted cash related to the PFAS insurance proceeds MOU in connection with the finalization of the JCO with the State of New Jersey , partially offset by an approximately $100 million use of restricted cash to fund settlement payments associated with the 2025 settlement with the State of New Jersey and approximately $25 million of taxes related to the property sale in Kuan Yin . This is compared with $146 million of operating cash flows in the prior-year quarter.
Capital expenditures for the third quarter of 2026 amounted to $51 million , an increase compared with $41 million in the prior-year quarter.
Free Cash Flows for the third quarter of 2026 were $98 million , compared with $105 million in the third quarter of 2025.
Fourth Quarter 2026 Outlook 
In the fourth quarter, the Company expects consolidated Net Sales to decrease in the range of 5% to 10%, sequentially, driven by seasonality in TSS and TT, with consolidated Adjusted EBITDA expected to range between $160 million and $185 million . Corporate Expenses are expected to be approximately $40 million to $45 million . The Company also anticipates capital expenditures to be between $75 million and $85 million , with positive Free Cash Flows.
TSS expects Net Sales will sequentially decrease in the high-teens to low-twenties percentage range, driven by traditional seasonal patterns related to the North American cooling season. Adjusted EBITDA is expected to be between $105 million and $115 million .
TT expects a sequential Net Sales decrease in the high single-digit to low-teens percentage range, driven by seasonality. Adjusted EBITDA is expected to range between $60 million and $65 million .
APM expects a sequential Net Sales increase in the low-to-mid teens percentage range, driven by order book strength for Performance Solutions products and certain customer contractual obligations benefiting the fourth quarter. Adjusted EBITDA for APM is expected to be between $40 million and $45 million .
Full Year 2026 Outlook 
The Company expects 2026 Net Sales to grow approximately 2% over 2025, with Adjusted EBITDA between $775 million and $800 million . Capital expenditures are anticipated to be between $220 million and $230 million , with overall Free Cash Flow Conversion above 15%, which includes receipt of $150 million in restricted cash related to the PFAS insurance proceeds MOU in connection with the finalization of the JCO with the State of New Jersey , partially offset by legal settlement payments in the year related to the finalization of the JCO with the State of New Jersey and the announced settlement with the State of North Carolina during the third quarter of 2026 as well as the taxes associated with the Kuan Yin property sale now complete. The Company now anticipates achieving a Net Leverage ratio below 4.2x in 2026.

About The Chemours Company 
The Chemours Company (NYSE: CC) is a global leader in providing industrial and specialty chemical products for markets, including coatings, plastics, refrigeration and air conditioning, transportation, semiconductor and advanced electronics, general industrial, and oil and gas. Through our three businesses – Thermal & Specialized Solutions, Titanium Technologies, and Advanced Performance Materials – we deliver application expertise and chemistry-based innovations that solve customers' biggest challenges. Our flagship products are sold under prominent brands such as Opteon™, Freon™, Ti-Pure™, Nafion™, Teflon™, Viton™, and Krytox™. Headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, and listed on the NYSE under the symbol CC, Chemours has approximately 5,700 employees and 28 manufacturing sites and serves approximately 2,400 customers in approximately 110 countries. For more information, visit chemours.com or follow us on LinkedIn .
Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
We prepare our financial statements in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP). Within this press release, we may make reference to Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted EPS, Adjusted EBITDA, Free Cash Flows, Free Cash Flow Conversion, Total Debt Principal, Net and Net Leverage Ratio which are non-GAAP financial measures. The Company includes these non-GAAP financial measures because management believes they are useful to investors in that they provide for greater transparency with respect to supplemental information used by management in its financial and operational decision making. Management uses Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted EPS and Adjusted EBITDA, which adjust for (i) certain non-cash items, (ii) certain items we believe are not indicative of ongoing operating performance, or (iii) certain nonrecurring, unusual or infrequent items to evaluate the Company's performance in order to have comparable financial results to analyze changes in our underlying business from period to period. Additionally, Free Cash Flows, Free Cash Flow Conversion, Total Debt Principal, Net and Net Leverage Ratio are utilized as liquidity measures to assess the cash generation of our businesses and ongoing liquidity position.
Accordingly, the Company believes the presentation of these non-GAAP financial measures, when used in conjunction with GAAP financial measures, is a useful financial analysis tool that can assist investors in assessing the Company's operating performance and underlying prospects. This analysis should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. This analysis, as well as the other information in this press release, should be read in conjunction with the Company's financial statements and footnotes contained in the documents that the Company files with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The non-GAAP financial measures used by the Company in this press release may be different from the methods used by other companies. The Company does not provide a reconciliation of certain forward-looking non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP reported financial measures on a forward-looking basis because it is unable to predict with reasonable certainty the ultimate outcome of unusual gains and losses, potential future asset impairments and pending litigation without unreasonable effort. These items are uncertain, depend on various factors, and could have a material impact on GAAP reported results for the guidance period. For more information on the non-GAAP financial measures, please refer to the attached schedules or the table, "Reconciliation of GAAP Financial Measures to Non-GAAP Financial Measures (Unaudited)" and materials posted to the Company's website at investors.chemours.com.

New Faizeon™ portfolio of two-phase direct-to-chip and immersion cooling fluids address rising AI heat loads with superior performance and reduced energy and water use 
WILMINGTON, Del. , Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Chemours Company ("Chemours") (NYSE: CC), today launched Faizeon™ two-phase liquid cooling solutions 1 , for artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), and high-density data centers. The portfolio includes dielectric fluids engineered for both two-phase direct-to-chip and two-phase immersion cooling, giving data center operators and technology partners highly efficient options that can support evolving system architectures and remove heat from high-power processors and servers.
Faizeon™ fluids use phase change, in which the fluid absorbs heat and changes from liquid to vapor, to enable efficient, reliable heat removal as AI and HPC drive higher chip power and rack densities. In independent third-party testing , a two-phase direct-to-chip system using Faizeon™ 200 fluid maintained a Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) at up to 19 degrees Celsius lower than a single-phase, water-based fluid, while using a lower coolant flow rate.
"AI's rapid growth is increasing the demands on data center infrastructure, and cooling is becoming a critical constraint," said Denise Dignam , President and CEO at Chemours. "With our liquid cooling solutions, we are applying more than 90 years of thermal management expertise to help data centers manage higher heat loads while improving performance and dramatically reducing energy and water demand. Our Faizeon™ liquid cooling team is collaborating across the data center ecosystem, to bring together the expertise, testing, and support needed to confidently deploy two-phase liquid cooling at scale."
Faizeon™ two-phase liquid cooling fluids for direct-to-chip and immersion cooling: 
Faizeon™ 100 fluid – A low-pressure two-phase direct-to-chip fluid designed for system architectures where operating pressure, materials compatibility, and infrastructure considerations are central to deployment planning.
Faizeon™ 110 fluid – A low-pressure two-phase direct-to-chip fluid with an intermediate boiling point and zero ozone depletion potential for advanced direct-to-chip cooling systems.
Faizeon™ 200 fluid – A high-performance two-phase direct-to-chip fluid—and industry standard for medium pressure systems—offering performance and environmental balance, designed for advanced cooling architectures serving high-density AI and HPC processors.
Faizeon™ 220 fluid – Chemours' highest-performance two-phase direct-to-chip fluid, well suited for applications where rapid heat removal is critical, including high-density GPU environments, advanced AI clusters, and HPC deployments.
Faizeon™ 500 fluid – A two-phase immersion cooling fluid, formerly Opteon™ 2P50 dielectric fluid, purpose-built for full-server immersion cooling with excellent dielectric properties, full-server heat capture, ultra-high-density AI deployment support, and waste heat recovery potential.
Benefits of Faizeon™ fluids: 
Superior heat transfer: Through phase change Faizeon™ fluids absorb and remove high heat loads from processors and server components.
Lower cooling-related energy demand: Systems designed for Faizeon™ fluids can reduce the energy required for data center cooling, improving facility efficiency.
Minimal cooling-related water consumption: Faizeon™-enabled systems can nearly eliminate cooling-related water use, depending on system design and operating conditions.
Fluid circularity: Faizeon™ fluids are engineered to support recovery, reprocessing, and reuse.
To support continued innovation and accelerated adoption of advanced liquid cooling technologies, Chemours has collaborated across the data center ecosystem to help advance the adoption of two-phase liquid cooling technologies. These efforts include engagements with the U.S. Department of Energy's   Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), NTT DATA , 2CRSi , DataVolt , Munters , Accelsius , and ZutaCore . Learn more at Faizeon.com .
About The Chemours Company 
The Chemours Company (NYSE: CC) is a global leader in providing industrial and specialty chemicals products for markets, including coatings, plastics, refrigeration and air conditioning, transportation, semiconductor and advanced electronics, general industrial, and oil and gas. Through our three businesses – Thermal & Specialized Solutions, Titanium Technologies, and Advanced Performance Materials – we deliver application expertise and chemistry-based innovations that solve customers' biggest challenges. Our flagship products are sold under prominent brands such as Opteon™, Freon™, Ti-Pure™, Nafion™, Teflon™, Viton™, and Krytox™. Headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware and listed on the NYSE under the symbol CC, Chemours has approximately 5,700 employees and 28 manufacturing sites and serves approximately 2,400 customers in approximately 110 countries. For more information, visit chemours.com or follow us on LinkedIn .

title: Measure more, manage better: trinamiX and Eurofins Agro Testing showcase new approach to feed analysis at EuroTier 2026

Measure more, manage better: trinamiX and Eurofins Agro Testing showcase new approach to feed analysis at EuroTier 2026
At EuroTier 2026 in Hanover, Germany, Eurofins Agro Testing and trinamiX, a subsidiary of BASF, will present a joint approach that brings high-quality analytics directly into day-to-day farm operations. By combining trinamiX’s mobile near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy with Eurofins Agro Testing’s extensive calibration models, analysis results are available exactly where they are needed: directly on site and within seconds. Visitors are welcome to hear more about this approach at booth A60 in hall 20 from November 10-13, 2026. 
Successful feeding starts with knowing what is actually in the feed. However, silage and other feed materials are subject to natural variations, for example due to weather conditions, harvest timing, or ensiling methods. Identifying these (often short-term) changes in feed quality enables more informed decisions, more precise ration adjustments, and greater efficiency on the farm.
More frequent measurements create greater transparency. Greater transparency enables better decisions. This is what the joint approach from trinamiX and Eurofins Agro Testing stands for: “Measure more, manage better”.
Feed advisors in particular benefit from real-time results. They can assess quality parameters directly on site together with their customers and provide evidence-based recommendations. This provides a solid basis for decision-making and strengthens collaboration between advisors and farmers.
Determination of key quality parameters across numerous feed types 
The joint solution covers a broad range of feed and raw materials. Users can determine numerous relevant quality and nutritional parameters, including dry matter, crude protein, crude fiber, starch, sugars, and energy values for various country-specific evaluation systems.
The applications are available for many feed categories, including fresh forage, silage, hay, cereals, oilseeds, extraction meals, and finished feed. They support both livestock feed and equine feed applications.
Easy analysis with a portable spectrometer and cloud-based evaluation 
The solution has been specifically designed for ease of use in everyday agricultural operations. With the portable trinamiX PAL Two spectrometer, users analyse feed samples directly in the field, at the silo, or in the barn. The device captures the sample's near-infrared (NIR) spectrum and transfers the data to the cloud. The analysis is then performed using Eurofins Agro Testing's comprehensive calibration models. Results are available within seconds on both the smartphone and the spectrometer display.
All measurement data is automatically stored in the customer portal, where it can be viewed, compared, and documented at any time. In addition, reports and datasets can be exported in various formats and integrated into existing feeding and farm management processes via interfaces.
 
Notes to editors 
About Eurofins Agro Testing 
Eurofins Agro Testing consists of a network of agricultural laboratories worldwide and is part of Eurofins Scientific. Eurofins Agro Testing provides the agri-food industry with analytical results, calculations, and advice, that are used by farmers, growers and advisors to aid the management of farming systems, to improve soil and crop health and yield, and to accelerate the transition to more sustainable farming practices. 
www.eurofins.com/agro-testing   
About trinamiX GmbH  
trinamiX GmbH develops cutting-edge biometric and mobile NIR spectroscopy solutions, which are used in both consumer electronics and industrial designs. The company’s products enable humans and machines to better capture data with the goal of understanding the world around us. This results in improved decision making as well as stronger biometric security. trinamiX, based in Ludwigshafen (Germany), was founded in 2015 as a wholly owned subsidiary of BASF.

Ad-hoc: Statement by the Executive Board of Evonik Industries AG, October 30, 2026
The Executive Board of Evonik Industries AG has carefully reviewed the letter from BASF SE dated October 22, 2026, expressing its interest in making a voluntary public takeover offer. Based on the information available, the Executive Board has decided not to enter into negotiations with BASF SE. The Executive Board remains focused on its strategic direction and further development of Evonik as an independent company.
At the same time, the Executive Board has expressed its willingness to engage in a purely informational and confidential exchange with BASF SE in order to explain Evonik Industries AG’s position and to give BASF SE the opportunity to outline its rationale and the key considerations underlying its interest.
Evonik: Leading beyond chemistry
Evonik goes beyond the boundaries of chemistry with its combination of innovative strength and leading technological expertise. The global chemical company, headquartered in Essen, Germany, is active in more than 100 countries and generated sales of €14.1 billion and earnings (adjusted EBITDA) of €1.9 billion in 2025. The common motivation of the approximately 31,000 employees: to provide customers with a decisive competitive advantage with tailor-made products and solutions as a superforce for industry, thereby improving people's lives. In all markets. Every day.

content_excerpt: Update on Oyu Tolgoi seismic event 30 October 2026 share LONDON 1100 GMT  Underground operations at the Oyu Tolgoi copper mine in Mongolia are being progressively restarted following completion of safety reviews. A seismic event on 29 October 2026 led to a localised rockfall confined to a temporary storage zone adjacent to the production area, with no structural impact to the cave or its operating infrastructure. Featured by GroenvermogenNL for advancing scalable hydrogen production
Prodrive Technologies featured in GroenvermogenNL on scaling green hydrogen production
We are proud to share that Prodrive has been featured by GroenvermogenNL, highlighting our role in accelerating the hydrogen transition through innovative SiC-based rectifier technology and scalable turnkey solutions. Our ambition is to become a global market leader in enabling efficient, scalable, and cost-effective hydrogen production.
Discover the full story
In the article and accompanying video, our Sales Director for Hydrogen, Wouter van Gennip, discusses the growing demand for efficient and scalable hydrogen infrastructure, the role of rectifier technology in reducing the cost of hydrogen production, and how innovations in power electronics can accelerate the energy transition.
Explore the full feature to learn how Prodrive is helping electrolyzer manufacturers, system integrators, EPCs and hydrogen project developers scale green hydrogen production more efficiently.
Read the article
Enabling the next generation of green hydrogen
Through our advanced power electronics expertise for over 30+ years, we help electrolyzer manufacturers, system integrators and project developers accelerate the deployment of green hydrogen infrastructure.
A key example is Typhon, our 6 MW silicon carbide (SiC)-based turnkey rectifier solution. Designed specifically for industrial hydrogen applications, Typhon delivers high efficiency, a compact footprint, and the scalability required for large-scale hydrogen projects. By reducing energy losses and simplifying system integration, the platform helps lower the overall cost of hydrogen production. 
Learn more
From field testing to customer deliveries in 2028
Prodrive is already demonstrating several prototypes and field-test setups at our headquarters in Son, the Netherlands. In mid-2027, we plan to begin trial runs with the first production units.
From 2028, we expect to start supplying customers as we take the next step toward market-scale deployment.
Planning your next hydrogen project? Let’s explore how we can support your path toward scalable deployment.

share

Rio Tinto confirms that at approximately 18:00 (local time) on 29 October, seismic activity occurred along a rock fault zone at Oyu Tolgoi in Mongolia, resulting in ground vibration in the underground mine.
There have been no fatalities. Three employees sustained injuries.
Underground operations are currently paused in line with procedure, subject to completion of a safety review.

Lilly reports third-quarter 2026 financial results, raises full-year guidance and highlights regulatory progress across the portfolio
October 29, 2026
PDF Version 
Revenue in Q3 2026 increased 39% to $24.4 billion driven primarily by Mounjaro and Zepbound. 
Q3 revenue included approximately $900 million of benefits, primarily from $410 million of Jardiance milestones (no further milestones remain) and favorable adjustments to rebate and discount estimates. 
Q3 2026 EPS increased by 16% to $7.22 on a reported basis and increased by 7% to $7.48 on a non-GAAP basis. Q3 2026 reported and non-GAAP EPS included $4.57 of acquired IPR&D charges compared to $0.71 in Q3 2025. 
Increased the midpoint of our 2026 full-year revenue guidance by $5.5 billion to be in the range of $91.0 to $92.0 billion and raised underlying non-GAAP EPS guidance for the full year by $4.07 at the midpoint, which was more than offset by $4.57 of acquired IPR&D charges from Q3 business development activity, resulting in an updated range of $35.00 to $36.00 . 
Regulatory progress included U.S . FDA approvals of Mounjaro to reduce cardiovascular risk in adults with type 2 diabetes; Onswik, a once-weekly basal insulin for adults with type 2 diabetes; Inluriyo with Verzenio for adults with ER+, HER2-, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer; and an expanded indication for Jaypirca in adults with untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma. 
Pipeline highlights included positive topline results from a head-to-head Phase 3 trial of retatrutide versus Ozempic 2 mg in adults with type 2 diabetes, Phase 3 results from Ebglyss in moderate-to-severe hand and foot atopic dermatitis and Phase 2 results from EloraTZP in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, with Phase 3 trials to start in Q4 2026. 
Business development activity in Q3 2026 included the completed acquisition of AtaiBeckley to advance therapies for treatment-resistant depression and other mental health conditions. Subsequent to quarter end, we completed the acquisition of Merida Biosciences, to advance treatments for serious autoimmune and allergic diseases. 
INDIANAPOLIS , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 and provided updated 2026 financial guidance.
" Lilly had another strong quarter, exceeding our prior expectations and allowing us to raise our full-year outlook," said David A. Ricks , Lilly chair and CEO. "Revenue growth was driven by broad global consumer demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound, the global launches of Foundayo, expanded U.S . coverage for obesity care and a doubling in our newest products in oncology, immunology and neuroscience. To drive durable long-term growth, we continue to invest in our drug-making and technology capabilities, with multiple business development deals and partnerships signed and closed, and with new manufacturing expansions in Texas and Virginia . Lilly is executing well across the value chain, and our potential for impact on human health continues to expand."

Third-Quarter Reported Results
In Q3 2026, worldwide revenue was $24.4 billion , an increase of 39% compared with Q3 2025, driven by a 53% increase in volume, partially offset by a 15% decrease in realized prices. Key Products 1 revenue grew to $17.1 billion in Q3 2026, led by Mounjaro and Zepbound. Key Products revenue in the Immunology, Oncology, and Neuroscience therapeutic areas grew 100% in Q3 2026 compared to Q3 2025.
Revenue in the U.S . increased 34% to $15.1 billion , driven by a 41% increase in volume, partially offset by a 7% decrease in realized prices. The increase in U.S . volume was driven by Zepbound and Mounjaro. The decline in realized prices was primarily driven by Zepbound, partially offset by adjustments to estimates for rebates and discounts.
Revenue outside the U.S . increased 47% to $9.3 billion , driven by a 76% increase in volume, partially offset by a 29% decrease in realized prices. The volume increase outside the U.S . was driven by Mounjaro. Jardiance revenue outside the U.S . included sales-based milestones of $410 million in Q3 2026 and $200 million in Q3 2025, associated with the company's collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim . Additionally, Q3 2025 revenue included $180 million associated with the divestiture of the rights to Cialis in select markets outside of the U.S . Lower realized prices outside the U.S . were driven primarily by the inclusion of Mounjaro on the National Reimbursement Drug List (NRDL) in China .
Gross margin increased 40% to $20.5 billion in Q3 2026. Gross margin as a percent of revenue was 83.9%, an increase of 1.0 percentage points versus the same quarter last year. The increase was primarily driven by favorable product mix and improved cost of production, partially offset by lower realized prices.
In Q3 2026, research and development expenses increased 23% to $4.2 billion , or 17% of revenue, driven by continued investments in the company's early and late-stage portfolio.
Marketing, selling, and administrative expenses increased 14% to $3.1 billion in Q3 2026, primarily driven by promotional efforts supporting ongoing and planned launches.
In Q3 2026, the company recognized acquired in-process research and development (IPR&D) charges of $4.2 billion compared with $656 million in Q3 2025. The Q3 2026 charges primarily related to the acquisitions of AtaiBeckley Inc. and Curevo Inc. 
The effective tax rate was 23.3% in Q3 2026 compared with 22.8% in Q3 2025, primarily driven by the unfavorable tax impact of nondeductible acquired IPR&D charges, with a larger impact occurring in 2026. The Q3 2025 effective tax rate was also unfavorably impacted by U.S . tax law changes.
In Q3 2026, net income and earnings per share (EPS) were $6 .5 billion and $7.22 , respectively, compared with net income of $5 .6 billion and EPS of $6.21 in Q3 2025. EPS in Q3 2026 and Q3 2025 included acquired IPR&D charges of $4.57 and $0.71 , respectively.

On a non-GAAP basis, Q3 2026 gross margin increased 40% to $20.6 billion . Gross margin as a percent of revenue was 84.4%, an increase of 0.8 percentage points versus the same quarter last year. The increase was primarily driven by favorable product mix and improved cost of production, partially offset by lower realized prices.
The non-GAAP effective tax rate was 24.0% in Q3 2026 compared with 17.7% in Q3 2025, primarily driven by the unfavorable tax impact of nondeductible acquired IPR&D charges, with a larger impact occurring in 2026.
On a non-GAAP basis, Q3 2026 net income and EPS were $6.7 billion and $7.48 , respectively, compared with net income of $6 .3 billion and EPS of $7.02 in Q3 2025. Non-GAAP EPS in Q3 2026 and Q3 2025 included acquired IPR&D charges of $4.57 and $0.71 , respectively.
