West Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Results
October 29, 2026
PDF Version 
Raising Full-Year Net Sales and Adjusted-Diluted EPS guidance 
EXTON, Pa. , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc. (NYSE: WST), a leading provider of innovative, high-quality injectable solutions and services, today announced its financial results for the third quarter of 2026.
Third-Quarter 2026 Summary (comparisons to prior-year period) 
Net sales of $874.5 million increased 8.7%; organic growth was 11.9%.
Diluted earnings per share ("EPS") of $3.02 increased 57.3%.
Adjusted-diluted EPS of $2.66 increased 35.7%.
The Company repurchased $231 million of stock in the quarter, bringing the year-to-date total to $685 million .
Year-to-date operating cash flow was $403 million . Capital expenditures were $125 million .
The Company also announced on October 19, 2026 , that its Board of Directors declared a fourth-quarter dividend of $0.26 per share, an increase of 18% over the $0.22 per share paid in the prior quarter.
Outlook for Full-Year 2026 
Full-year 2026 net sales guidance increased to a range of $3 .41 billion to $3 .42 billion, up from the previous range of $3 .345 billion to $3 .380 billion.
Full-year 2026 adjusted-diluted EPS guidance increased to a range of $9.38 to $9.48 , up from the previous range of $8.85 to $9.05 .
Michel Lagarde , President and Chief Executive Officer, commented: "I am pleased to report strong third-quarter 2026 results, with net sales and adjusted EPS exceeding our expectations. Our results were again led by our High-Value Product (HVP) Components business. The robust sales performance drove strong operating income margin expansion and EPS growth. As a result of our team's strong execution in the third quarter, we are increasing our full-year 2026 guidance."
Mr. Lagarde concluded: "I want to thank our global teams for their relentless focus on execution to deliver products and services for our customers and the patients they serve. West is a critical primary containment and drug delivery partner for pharmaceutical companies, biotechs and CDMOs around the world. We are grateful for the trust our customers put in us, and we remain committed to driving continuous improvement to even better serve their current and future needs."
Proprietary Products Segment
Net sales of $728.8 million grew by 12.6% and increased 16.6% on an organic basis.
High-Value Product ("HVP") Components net sales of $466.7 million increased 19.7% and rose 20.3% on an organic basis. HVP Components accounted for 53% of total company net sales in the quarter.
HVP Delivery Devices net sales of $99.1 million were flat, and were up 26.4% on an organic basis excluding foreign currency translation effects and the impact of the divestiture of SmartDose® 3.5mL. HVP Delivery Devices accounted for 11% of total company net sales in the quarter. 
SmartDose® 3.5mL net sales represented $11.8 million in the quarter and $29.8 million in the prior-year quarter and are excluded from both periods to calculate organic growth.
Standard Products net sales of $163.0 million increased by 2.9% and rose 3.1% on an organic basis. Standard Products accounted for 19% of total company net sales this quarter.
West Vantage Segment
Net sales of $145.7 million decreased by 7.3% and declined 6.6% on an organic basis. West Vantage accounted for 17% of total company net sales in the quarter.
Full-Year 2026 Financial Guidance 
The Company is increasing its full-year 2026 net sales guidance range to $3 .41 billion to $3 .42 billion, up from the previous range of $3 .345 billion to $3 .380 billion. 
Organic net sales growth guidance increased to a range of 11.3% to 11.6%, up from the prior range of 10% to 11%.
SmartDose® 3.5mL generated $55.3 million in net sales in the second half of 2025 and generated $11 .8 million in net sales in the third quarter of 2026. No additional SmartDose® 3.5mL product sales are expected for the remainder of the year. These net sales are excluded in both periods to calculate full-year 2026 organic growth.
The Company is increasing its full-year 2026 adjusted-diluted EPS guidance range to $9.38 to $9.48 , up from the previous range of $8.85 to $9.05 .
Full-year 2026 capital spending guidance is updated to a range of $215 million to $220 million, down from the prior range of $250 million to $275 million.
Third-Quarter 2026 Conference Call 
Management will host a conference call at 8 a.m. EDT today. The live webcast can be accessed in the "Investors" section of the Company's website by clicking here .
To participate in the Q&A portion of the conference call, please register in advance by clicking here .
Registered telephone participants will receive the dial-in number along with a unique PIN number that will enable them to ask questions on the call.
An accompanying slide presentation will be posted in the "Investors" section of the Company's website.
A replay of the webcast will be available on the Company's website for approximately 90 days after the event.
About West
West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc. is a leading provider of innovative, high-quality injectable solutions and services. As a trusted partner to established and emerging drug developers, West helps ensure the safe, effective containment and delivery of life-saving and life-enhancing medicines for patients. With over 10,000 team members across 50 sites including 26 manufacturing facilities worldwide, West helps support our customers by delivering over 41 billion components and devices each year. Headquartered in Exton, Pennsylvania , West in its fiscal year 2025 generated $3.07 billion in net sales. West is traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: WST) and is included in the Standard & Poor's 500 index. For more information, visit www.westpharma.com .
All trademarks and registered trademarks used in this release are the property of West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc. or its subsidiaries, in the United States and other jurisdictions, unless otherwise noted.

During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 , the Company recorded pre-tax charges of $6.3 million and $9.3 million , respectively, related to our two existing restructuring programs: (i) $5.8 million and $7.7 million , respectively, within other expense (income), related to severance and retention benefit charges and the acceleration of depreciation and lease costs in connection with the Company's January 2025 restructuring plan and (ii) $0.5 million and $1.6 million , respectively, within selling, general and administrative expenses, for professional services relating to our 2024 plan to optimize the legal structure of the Company and its subsidiaries. In addition, we recorded a one-time tax cost of $12.0 million associated with an internal legal entity restructuring which occurred in the first quarter of 2026. During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025 , the Company recorded pre-tax charges of $2.5 million and $21.9 million , respectively, related to our two existing restructuring programs: (i) $0.9 million and $17.5 million , respectively, within other expense (income), related to severance, acceleration of depreciation and lease costs in connection with the Company's January 2025 restructuring plan and (ii) $1.6 million and $4.4 million , respectively, within selling, general and administrative expenses, for professional services relating to our 2024 plan to optimize the legal structure of the Company and its subsidiaries. In addition, we recorded income tax charges of $2.0 million in the first quarter of 2025, related primarily to withholding tax and capital gains incurred in executing our plan to optimize our legal structure. 
(2) 
During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 , the Company recorded pre-tax benefit of $54.0 million and $45.7 million , respectively, related to M&A activities, primarily related to the Company's agreement to sell its SmartDose® 3.5mL On-Body Delivery System and associated facilities to AbbVie. The net benefit is composed of a net gain on the sale of its SmartDose® 3.5mL On-Body Delivery System assets of $55 .7 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 within other expense (income). The Company recorded a one-time tax cost of $22 .4 million associated with the gain on the sale of SmartDose® 3.5mL On-Body Delivery System. The Company recorded a net benefit of $1 .9 million and net charges of $0 .3 million, respectively, within other expense (income), related to employee benefits in connection with the sale agreement. The Company recorded the remaining $3 .6 million and $9 .7 million, respectively, within selling, general and administrative expenses, relating to professional services in connection with other M&A activities. 
(3) 
During the nine months ended September 30, 2026 , the Company recorded cost-method investment impairment charges of $3.5 million within other expense (income). 
(4) 
During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 , the Company recorded $0.5 million and $1.4 million , respectively, of amortization expense in association with an acquisition of increased ownership interest in Daikyo. During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, the Company recorded $0.0 million and $0 .2 million, respectively, of amortization expense within selling, general and administrative expenses associated with an intangible asset acquired during the second quarter of 2020. During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, the Company recorded $0 .4 million and $1 .3 million, respectively, of amortization expense in association with an acquisition of increased ownership interest in Daikyo. 
(5)

content_excerpt: West Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Results October 29, 2026 PDF Version Raising Full-Year Net Sales and Adjusted-Diluted EPS guidance EXTON, Pa. , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc. title: BorgWarner Wins Multiple eMotor Business Awards in China
query: https://www.borgwarner.com/newsroom/press-releases
content_text:
BorgWarner Wins Multiple eMotor Business Awards in China
Three new business awards span range-extended, battery-electric and hybrid vehicle applications
Programs awarded by leading original equipment manufacturers 
Production expected to begin between 2027 and 2028
Auburn Hills, Michigan, October 29, 2026 – BorgWarner has secured multiple eMotor business awards in China for a range of electrified and hybrid vehicle programs. The new business broadens the company’s customer base, expands the application of its eMotor technologies and further strengthens BorgWarner’s electrified propulsion portfolio in China.
“We are pleased to establish and expand our eMotor business with customers across China,” said Isabelle McKenzie, Vice President of BorgWarner Inc. and President and General Manager, PowerDrive Systems. “The breadth of these programs demonstrates our ability to address diverse application requirements through strong product performance, cost optimization and localized manufacturing. With our established engineering and production footprint in China, we are well positioned to support customers as they develop their next generation of electrified vehicles.”
The awards include BorgWarner’s first eMotor program with the China joint venture operations of a leading global original equipment manufacturer (OEM). The company will supply its high-voltage hairpin P1 eMotor stator and rotor assemblies for the customer’s next-generation range-extended vehicle platform. Delivering 115kW of peak power, up from 100kW in the previous generation, the motor is designed to provide additional power during rapid acceleration while supporting efficient electricity generation during range-extending operation. The eMotor design features an optimized cooling structure and increased efficiency across the operating-range to support overall vehicle efficiency and reliability requirements.
BorgWarner will also continue to supply high-voltage hairpin main drive eMotor stator and rotor assemblies for a leading Chinese new energy vehicle OEM’s next-generation SUV platforms. Designed for a 715V high-voltage architecture, the solution delivers 300kW of peak power and 495Nm of peak torque. The customized stator and permanent-magnet rotor  
assemblies provide the high power and torque density required for demanding traction applications.
In another program, BorgWarner will supply stator and rotor assemblies for a 130kW P2 eMotor to an electric drive system supplier. Featuring BorgWarner’s proprietary S-winding technology, the motor uses a continuous-wave winding configuration designed to support compact packaging, low alternating-current losses and high-power density. The eMotor will be integrated into hybrid propulsion systems for several vehicle programs intended for global markets.
BorgWarner’s next generation eMotor products deliver advancements in power output, power density and energy efficiency. Optimized electromagnetic designs and cooling structures increase peak efficiency and extend the high-efficiency operating range, helping reduce vehicle energy consumption across a broader range of operating conditions. BorgWarner’s internally developed design and local manufacturing footprint enable fast to market products with consistent quality, and reliable delivery.

BorgWarner Secures High-Voltage Inverter Business Win
BorgWarner awarded next-generation high-voltage inverter business for future battery-electric vehicle (BEV) programs
New inverter platform continues established customer business into the next vehicle generation
Advanced inverter technology supports improved efficiency, optimized manufacturability and enhanced scalability for electric propulsion systems
Auburn Hills, Michigan, October 29, 2026 – BorgWarner has secured a new award to supply its next-generation high-voltage traction inverter technology for future battery-electric vehicle programs from a major global automotive manufacturer. BorgWarner currently supplies inverter technology to the customer, and the new award extends this existing business to the customer’s next generation of electric vehicles. The award further strengthens BorgWarner's position as a leading provider of advanced power electronics solutions for electric vehicles.
"This award reflects the confidence customers place in BorgWarner's power electronics expertise and our ability to deliver innovative, high-performance electrification solutions," said Isabelle McKenzie, Vice President of BorgWarner Inc. and President and General Manager, PowerDrive Systems. "As automakers continue to expand their electric vehicle portfolios, we remain committed to helping them achieve greater efficiency, performance and scalability through advanced inverter technologies." 
The high-voltage traction inverter converts the battery's direct current (DC) into alternating current (AC) to power the electric motor. As a critical component of the electric drivetrain, the inverter plays a key role in vehicle efficiency, performance and overall energy management.
The new inverter platform incorporates BorgWarner's latest power module technology and a simplified design architecture. Advanced manufacturing innovations and a compact system layout help optimize efficiency, while supporting cost competitiveness and improved packaging flexibility.
This business win underscores BorgWarner's continued leadership in power electronics and electrification technologies. Leveraging its proven inverter expertise and a scalable technology roadmap, BorgWarner is helping customers develop the next generation of high-performance battery-electric vehicles.

title: BorgWarner to Supply New Aluminum-Wire eMotor to Major Chinese OEM
query: https://www.borgwarner.com/newsroom/press-releases
content_text:
BorgWarner to Supply New Aluminum-Wire eMotor to Major Chinese OEM
Marks a new technological advancement in BorgWarner’s electric motor portfolio
Suitable for generator motors in hybrid applications and traction motors used in auxiliary drive applications
Reduces wire weight by more than 60% and cost by more than 80% for comparable product specifications
Auburn Hills, Michigan, October 29, 2026 – BorgWarner has secured its first business award for its new aluminum-wire eMotor technology from a major Chinese original equipment manufacturer (OEM), marking the technology’s first introduction to the market. The product features aluminum-wire hairpin winding technology and will be used in hybrid vehicles across multiple applications, including generator motors and traction motors for auxiliary drive applications. Start of production is expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.
BorgWarner has collaborated with this customer across multiple product areas for more than 15 years. This latest award expands the partnership into a new application by incorporating aluminum conductors and hairpin winding technology into BorgWarner’s hybrid product portfolio.
“We are proud to introduce BorgWarner’s aluminum-wire eMotor technology to the market through this program and to further strengthen our long-standing relationship with the customer,” said Isabelle McKenzie, Vice President of BorgWarner Inc. and President and General Manager, PowerDrive Systems. “The technology combines aluminum conductors with BorgWarner’s hairpin winding expertise to deliver significant weight and cost benefits. Supported by our comprehensive local product engineering and manufacturing capabilities, we have optimized the motor design, manufacturing processes and connection technologies to meet the requirements of hybrid generator and auxiliary drive applications.”
The award demonstrates BorgWarner’s continued innovation in electric motor technology. Compared with a conventional copper-wire motor of comparable specifications, the aluminum-wire solution maintains peak torque and peak power while reducing weight by more than 60% and reducing costs by more than 80%.  
Aluminum-wire technology is also well suited for generator motors in hybrid applications and traction motors used for auxiliary drive applications, giving customers greater flexibility in developing various hybrid architectures.

title: BorgWarner Secures Engine Control Module Business with Major Global OEM
query: https://www.borgwarner.com/newsroom/press-releases
content_text:
BorgWarner Secures Engine Control Module Business with Major Global OEM
Win capitalizes on BorgWarner’s array of flexible, custom-designed controllers
Start of production slated for 2029
Auburn Hills, Michigan, October 29, 2026 – BorgWarner, a global product leader in delivering innovative and sustainable mobility solutions, will soon supply engine control modules (ECMs) on an internal-combustion engine (ICE) pick-up truck platform for one of its longstanding global OEM customers. The new, high-volume contract extends the company’s existing customer relationship through 2034, with production expected to begin in 2029.
BorgWarner’s ECM is designed specifically for the platform, providing increased content and functionality, greater control flexibility, and a compact design to meet tight packaging requirements. The company has supplied ECMs to this customer since 2020 on several of its existing applications. 
“Securing this strategic ECM program win maintains BorgWarner’s electronics leadership and extends our engagement with this long-time partner through 2034,” said Isabelle McKenzie, Vice President of BorgWarner Inc. and President and General Manager, PowerDrive Systems. “This program builds on our strong relationship with the customer and reflects the value of close collaboration. By combining our deep expertise in engine control technology with an understanding of the customer’s requirements, we are helping deliver a solution tailored to the needs of this important platform.” 
BorgWarner has a range of light-vehicle controllers for hybrid and combustion engines that deliver precise control of engine management systems for diesel, gasoline direct injection (GDi) and port fuel injection applications. Additionally, these ECMs utilize BorgWarner’s custom, cost-competitive Application Specific Integrated Circuits that meet the latest emissions requirements. With high levels of fuel control flexibility, the controllers are manufactured to be fully compatible with all injectors currently on the market. The ECM offers multiple pin-connection configurations, integrated exhaust aftertreatment functionality, and a flexible design enabled by an advanced microprocessor. Further, its GDi control can support 500-bar system pressures. 
Beyond light-vehicle ICE engine controllers, BorgWarner has an array of solutions and technology to support a wide range of propulsion needs, including battery management controllers, motor controllers, commercial vehicle engine controllers, light and commercial vehicle transmission controllers, plus more.

title: BorgWarner Wins Three Conquest Turbo Business Awards with Global Powertrain Leader
query: https://www.borgwarner.com/newsroom/press-releases
content_text:
BorgWarner Wins Three Conquest Turbo Business Awards with Global Powertrain Leader
Wins include both variable turbine geometry (VTG) and wastegate turbochargers
Technology to deploy in customer’s light-vehicle gasoline platforms
Turbochargers help reduce emissions and improve fuel efficiency
Auburn Hills, Michigan, October 29, 2026 – BorgWarner, a global product leader in delivering innovative and sustainable mobility solutions, has captured three conquest business wins with a global powertrain technology leader, including one contract for its variable turbine geometry (VTG) turbocharger and two for its wastegate turbocharger. The technology will be used on the customer’s light-vehicle gasoline platforms in South America and Europe. 
BorgWarner’s VTG turbochargers for gasoline applications are designed to provide reliable operation under demanding operating conditions while meeting high-boost pressure requirements. Engineered for excellent thermodynamic adaptation to Miller-cycle gasoline engines and exhaust temperatures of up to 1050°C, the technology improves thermodynamic efficiency while delivering strong engine response at lower RPMs for nearly instant acceleration and optimum power output. Additionally, the technology helps reduce emissions, improve fuel efficiency and enhance transient performance. 
“We value our longstanding relationship with this global leader in powertrain technology and the opportunity to support its evolving business and broader commodity strategy,” said Dr. Volker Weng, Vice President of BorgWarner Inc. and President and General Manager, Turbos and Thermal Technologies. “These contracts reflect the trust we have established with the customer and the strength of our offerings, including competitive solutions and deep technical expertise. We look forward to continuing to support the customer with innovations that deliver lasting value.” 
Meeting the highest quality standards, BorgWarner’s wastegate turbochargers feature scalable compressor and turbine stages that can be tailored to individual customer requirements. Designed for gasoline applications, the turbochargers deliver excellent response and power density, improved noise, vibration and harshness (NVH), enhanced fuel economy and reduced emissions. Offering many of the same advanced features as the VTG turbocharger, the wastegate turbocharger is available with single- and twin-scroll, as well as dual-volute turbine designs. It provides both pneumatic and electric actuation for the wastegate and integrated compressor recirculation valve and has a dedicated compressor and turbine stages. 
Start of production for all three turbochargers is scheduled for 2027.

title: BorgWarner Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Results, Increases 2026 Adjusted EPS Guidance, Announces 9 Awards Across Portfolio to Support Long-Term Profitable Growth
query: https://www.borgwarner.com/newsroom/press-releases
content_text:
BorgWarner Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Results, Increases 2026 Adjusted EPS Guidance, Announces 9 Awards Across Portfolio to Support Long-Term Profitable Growth
Auburn Hills, Michigan, October 29, 2026 – BorgWarner Inc. (NYSE: BWA) today reported third quarter results for 2026.
Third Quarter Results and Business Highlights 
BorgWarner (the “Company”) achieved a U.S. GAAP operating margin of 8.7% during the third quarter of 2026, or an increase of 180 basis points, compared with the third quarter of 2025. The Company achieved an adjusted operating margin of 10.9%, or an increase of 20 basis points, compared with the third quarter of 2025. The Company’s continued focus on cost controls allowed it to deliver strong performance despite a lower industry production environment.
The Company successfully executed a debt tender and make-whole redemption to reduce its gross debt balance by $864 million during the third quarter of 2026.
The Company repurchased approximately $175 million of its outstanding shares and paid a $35 million cash dividend to its shareholders during the third quarter of 2026.
The Company continued to make progress in its product readiness across its portfolio offerings for the data center and industrial markets. Additionally, the Company has accelerated its quoting activity for its industrial solutions.
New Business Awards Across Portfolio 
The Company secured multiple new business awards that are expected to support its long-term profitable growth, including the following:
Foundational Awards 
Engine control module award with a global OEM for a new internal combustion engine pickup truck platform. Production is expected to begin in 2029.
Three conquest turbocharger awards with a global powertrain leader for light vehicle gasoline platforms in South America and Europe. Production is expected to begin in 2027.
eProduct Awards 
First aluminum-wire eMotor program award with a major Chinese OEM for hybrid vehicles, including generator and traction motors for auxiliary drive applications. Production is expected to begin in 2026.
Three eMotor awards with leading OEMs in China for range-extended, battery-electric and hybrid vehicle applications. Production is expected to begin between 2027 and 2028.
High-voltage inverter award with a global OEM for its next-generation battery-electric vehicle programs. This award builds on an established customer relationship.
Third Quarter Summary: 
U.S. GAAP net sales of $3,487 million, a decrease of approximately 2.9% compared with the third quarter of 2025.
Excluding the impact of foreign currencies, organic net sales decreased 3.1% compared with the third quarter of 2025.
U.S. GAAP net earnings of $1.08 per diluted share, an increase of 47.9% compared with the third quarter of 2025.
Excluding $0.31 of net losses per diluted share related to non-comparable items (detailed in the table below), adjusted net earnings were $1.39 per diluted share, an increase of 12.1% compared with the third quarter of 2025.
U.S. GAAP operating income of $302 million, or 8.7% of net sales.
Excluding $79 million of pretax expenses related to non-comparable items, adjusted operating income was $381 million, or 10.9% of net sales.
Net cash provided by operating activities of $320 million.
Free cash flow of $195 million.
Financial Results: 
The Company believes the following table is useful in highlighting non-comparable items that impacted its U.S. GAAP net earnings per diluted share. The non-comparable items presented below are calculated after tax using the corresponding effective tax rate discrete to each item and the weighted average number of diluted shares for the periods presented. The Company defines adjusted earnings per diluted share as earnings per diluted share adjusted to eliminate the impact of restructuring expense, merger, acquisition and divestiture expense, other net expenses, discontinued operations and other gains and losses not reflective of the Company’s ongoing operations and related tax effects.
Net sales were $3,487 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of approximately 2.9% compared with the third quarter of 2025. This decrease was primarily driven by declining market production volumes and lower Battery Energy Systems segment sales. Net earnings for the third quarter of 2026 were $221 million, compared with net earnings of $158 million for the third quarter of 2025. Net earnings per diluted share for the third quarter of 2026 were $1.08, up 47.9% from $0.73 per diluted share for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted net earnings per diluted share for the third quarter of 2026 were $1.39, up 12.1% from adjusted net earnings per diluted share of $1.24 for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted net earnings for the third quarter of 2026 excluded net non-comparable items of $(0.31) per diluted share, while adjusted net earnings for the third quarter of 2025 excluded net non-comparable items of $(0.51) per diluted share. These and other non-comparable items are listed in the table above, which is provided by the Company for comparison with other results and the most directly comparable U.S. GAAP measures. The increase in adjusted net earnings per diluted share was primarily due to a lower full year effective tax rate and the impact of a lower share count resulting from share repurchases in 2025 and 2026.
Full Year 2026 Guidance Update: The Company increased its 2026 adjusted earnings per share guidance due to the expected impacts of the Company's share repurchases and a decline in its full year effective tax rate.
At the midpoint of its 2026 guidance, the Company expects to deliver another year of adjusted operating margin expansion and adjusted earnings per share growth despite the Company’s expectation that its weighted light vehicle market will be down 2% to down 1% and a $10 million to $15 million industrial R&D investment to support long-term profitable growth. Net sales are expected to be in the range of $14.0 billion to $14.2 billion in 2026, compared with 2025 net sales of approximately $14.3 billion. The Company’s net sales guidance range has been narrowed from its previous forecast of $14.0 billion to $14.3 billion due to lower industry production expectations at the high-end of the Company’s previous guidance. The Company’s net sales guidance implies a year-over-year change in organic net sales of down 4% to down 2.5%. The Company’s net sales guidance includes an expected year-over-year sales decline of approximately $250 million in the Company’s Battery Energy Systems segment, which represents approximately a 1.7% headwind to organic net sales growth in 2026. Foreign currencies are expected to result in a year-over-year increase in sales of approximately $250 million primarily due to the strengthening of the Euro and Chinese Renminbi against the U.S. dollar.
U.S. GAAP operating margin is expected to be in the range of 9.3% to 9.6% in 2026. Excluding the  impact of non-comparable items and the add-back of intangible asset amortization expense, adjusted operating margin is expected to be in the range of 10.7% to 10.9%. U.S. GAAP net earnings are expected to be within the range of $4.65 to $4.84 per diluted share. Excluding the impact of noncomparable items, adjusted net earnings are expected to be in the range of $5.20 to $5.35 per diluted share, compared with the Company’s previous adjusted net earnings guidance range of $5.05 to $5.30 per diluted share. This increase is due to the expected impacts of the Company's share repurchases and a decline in its full year effective tax rate. Full year operating cash flow is expected to be in the range of $1,600 million to $1,700 million, while free cash flow is expected to be in the range of $900 million to $1,100 million, consistent with the Company’s previous guidance.
At 9:30 a.m. ET today, a brief conference call concerning third quarter 2026 results and full year guidance will be webcast at: https://www.borgwarner.com/investors . Additionally, an earnings call presentation will be available at https://www.borgwarner.com/investors .

content_text:
Syensqo materials help advance medical technologies from heart surgery to implants
Advanced materials enable medical-device innovations in cardiothoracic care, cardiac implants, spinal surgery and surgical instruments
 
Brussels, October 29, 2026 - Advanced materials play an important role in the development of medical technologies. From devices used for complex heart surgery to pacemakers, spinal implants and surgical instruments, they can help make medical technologies lighter, more precise, compatible with the human body or better suited to medical imaging.
Syensqo works with medical-device manufacturers to develop high-performance materials that can meet demanding requirements where conventional materials or metals may fall short, helping improve how medical devices perform for patients and healthcare professionals.
“Behind every medical device is a series of critical choices about how it needs to perform, both for healthcare professionals and for patients,” said Natalie Dragunat, Global Marketing Manager, Healthcare at Syensqo. “Our role is to bring advanced materials science into that equation, helping medical-device innovators solve complex challenges and turn new possibilities into technologies that can make a difference in patient care.”
Syensqo’s advanced materials are helping drive innovation across a range of medical applications, including:
Protecting the heart after complex surgery : Thoracic Innovations uses a Syensqo high-strength resin in its sternal spacer , designed to protect the heart and stabilize the chest when it needs to remain temporarily open following certain cardiothoracic procedures.
Enabling long-term cardiac implants : Biotronik selected a Syensqo high-performance polymer for its pacemakers , combining biocompatibility for indefinite implantation with transparency to support precise electrode placement during surgery.
Supporting bone integration in spinal surgery : A Syensqo biomaterial is used in a spinal fusion cage developed by Shanghai REACH Medical Instrument , combining bone-relevant mechanical properties with bioactive functionality designed to support bone integration.
Improving surgical instruments : An orthopedic surgical guide developed by Hanisch Medical and TechImport using a Syensqo advanced polymer is up to 70% lighter than traditional metal versions and enables unobstructed X-ray imaging during surgery.
Improving surgical lighting and ergonomics : MezLight uses a Syensqo high-performance polymer in its reusable surgical task light, providing focused illumination while reducing the physical strain associated with traditional surgical headlamps. The material also enables durability and repeated steam sterilization.
Advancing orthopedic implants : GLW Medical Innovation uses a Syensqo high-performance polymer in its ApolloAnkle ™ Fracture Plating System , combining 3D-printed titanium with a bone-like polymer to support fracture fixation while enabling improved visibility during medical imaging.
Building on more than 60 years of high-performance polymer innovation, Syensqo is also working with medical-device manufacturers early in the development process. In 2026, the company joined MedTech Innovator , a global accelerator for medical-device, diagnostic and digital-health companies, to provide materials and application expertise to emerging healthcare companies.
“Some of the most important decisions in medical-device development are made at the very beginning of the product design,” said Marie-Beatrice Madec, Head of Marketing Life Solutions at Syensqo. “That’s why we work with innovators from day one, bringing advanced materials expertise into the design process when it can make the greatest difference, while staying alongside them as their technologies evolve, from initial concept to solutions ready for the healthcare market.”
Syensqo will also be present at COMPAMED 2026 in Düsseldorf, Germany, from 16 to 19 November ( booth 8AL14 ), continuing the dialogue with medical-device manufacturers and innovators.
By combining materials expertise with close collaboration across the healthcare ecosystem, Syensqo aims to support the development of medical technologies that improve care for patients and healthcare professionals.

Rio Tinto celebrates opening of $1.4 billion lithium projects in Argentina
29 October 2026
share
CATAMARCA, Argentina--(BUSINESS WIRE)--
President of Argentina Javier Milei and Catamarca Governor Raúl Jalil today joined Rio Tinto Chief Executive Simon Trott to celebrate a major milestone for Argentina’s lithium industry, marking the official opening of Rio Tinto’s Fénix 1B expansion and Sal de Vida operation in Catamarca following a combined investment of around $1.4 billion.
Both projects achieved first production in the second quarter ahead of plan and are now ramping up production. They will add 25,000 tonnes of annual lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) capacity once fully ramped up, strengthening Rio Tinto’s standing and Argentina’s position as a leading supplier of lithium for global markets.
The celebrations included a visit to Fénix by President Milei and Governor Jalil, hosted by Simon Trott, and an inauguration event recognising both projects with national and provincial authorities, employees, suppliers and representatives of local and Indigenous communities.
President of Argentina Javier Milei said: “The expansion of the Fénix project is a historic milestone that demonstrates the potential of Argentina’s mining sector. This was made possible by the country once again creating incentives for the production of resources that are essential to the modern world.
“We are proud that a company of this scale once again sees Argentina as a reliable partner and is investing in our country, validating the decisions we have taken over the past few years.”
Rio Tinto Chief Executive Simon Trott said: “Today is a proud moment for Rio Tinto and an important milestone for Argentina’s lithium industry, as we grow our position as a leading global supplier. It was a privilege to welcome President Milei, Governor Jalil and national and provincial authorities, and I thank them for joining us to recognise the work behind Fénix 1B and Sal de Vida.
“These two projects build on nearly three decades of lithium production in Catamarca and the expertise of our Argentine workforce. They demonstrate our industry-leading project delivery capability, as we execute with discipline towards our global target of 200,000 tonnes lithium carbonate equivalent annual production capacity by 2028.
“The delivery of these projects reflects the dedication of our people, the capabilities of Argentine suppliers and our partnerships with local communities and governments. Our focus now is on safely ramping up production, delivering reliable, high-quality lithium to our customers, and creating lasting value for our shareholders and Argentina.”
Fénix began operations in 1997 as Argentina’s first commercial lithium operation. The Fénix 1B expansion adds 10,000 tonnes of annual LCE capacity to the existing operation, increasing its total target of annual LCE capacity to approximately 40,000 tonnes.
Sal de Vida is a new lithium carbonate operation located approximately 20 kilometres northeast of Fénix, with a target of annual LCE capacity of 15,000 tonnes.
The projects form part of Rio Tinto’s growing lithium business in Argentina, which includes operations and projects across Catamarca, Jujuy and Salta, including the Rincon lithium project.
Rio Tinto’s growth in Argentina is strengthening the country’s supplier network. Around 70% of the approximately $4 billion in growth capital to be invested across our lithium operations in Argentina is expected to be spent with local suppliers.

title: Lilly's retatrutide delivered greater A1C reduction and more than double the weight loss of Ozempic's highest approved dose in head-to-head trial
source: Eli Lilly and Company - Official RSS
query: https://investor.lilly.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Lilly's retatrutide delivered greater A1C reduction and more than double the weight loss of Ozempic's highest approved dose in head-to-head trial
October 28, 2026
PDF Version 
In adults with type 2 diabetes, retatrutide lowered A1C by an average of 2.2% vs. 1.8% with Ozempic 2 mg at 80 weeks 
Participants taking retatrutide lost an average of 44 lbs to 47 lbs (20% to 21%) vs. 21 lbs (9%) with Ozempic 2 mg at 80 weeks 
TRANSCEND-T2D-2 marks the sixth Phase 3 trial in which retatrutide has delivered powerful efficacy, reinforcing its potential to transform cardiometabolic care 
INDIANAPOLIS , Oct 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY), the maker of Mounjaro (tirzepatide) and Foundayo (orforglipron), today announced positive topline results from TRANSCEND-T2D-2, a head-to-head Phase 3 trial comparing retatrutide with injectable Ozempic 2 mg in adults with type 2 diabetes. At 80 weeks, retatrutide met the primary and all key secondary endpoints, delivering greater A1C reduction and substantially more weight loss than Ozempic. 1,2 
Kenneth Custer , Ph.D., Executive Vice President and President of Lilly Cardiometabolic Health : "Head-to-head trials show patients and physicians how a potential new medicine compares with treatments that are available and reimbursed today. In TRANSCEND-T2D-2, the first Phase 3 trial comparing retatrutide with another incretin medicine, retatrutide delivered greater A1C reduction and more than double the weight loss of the highest approved dose of Ozempic for type 2 diabetes. Based on these results and those from across our Phase 3 program, we believe retatrutide, if approved, could shift the treatment paradigm for people living with type 2 diabetes, obesity and related cardiometabolic conditions."
In the TRANSCEND-T2D-2 trial, both doses of retatrutide lowered A1C by an average of 2.2% compared to 1.8% with Ozempic at 80 weeks. Participants taking retatrutide lost an average of 44.3 lbs (19.5%; 9 mg) and 47.4 lbs (20.9%; 12 mg) compared to 20.9 lbs (9.4%) with Ozempic. Retatrutide also delivered greater improvements than Ozempic across certain cardiovascular risk factors, including non-HDL cholesterol, triglycerides and systolic blood pressure. 1

In TRANSCEND-T2D-2, the most common adverse events with retatrutide (9 mg, 12 mg vs. Ozempic) were diarrhea (28.3%, 32.7% vs. 26.4%), nausea (21.2%, 23.8% vs. 21.3%), constipation (14.2%, 13.1% vs. 19.8%), vomiting (10.2%, 15.0% vs. 13.2%) and dyspepsia (10.4%, 8.5% vs. 11.6%). The incidence of dysesthesia with retatrutide (9 mg, 12 mg vs. Ozempic) was 4.8%, 6.5% vs. 2.7%, while the incidence of urinary tract infections was 5.8%, 4.2% vs. 5.8%. The majority of these events were mild-to-moderate and typically resolved during treatment. Treatment discontinuation rates due to adverse events were 4.8%, 7.9% vs. 2.7% with retatrutide 9 mg and 12 mg vs. Ozempic, respectively.
Detailed results from TRANSCEND-T2D-2 will be presented at a future medical meeting and published in a peer-reviewed journal.
Frequently Asked Questions 
1. Why are head-to-head trials important? 
Head-to-head trials compare a potential new medicine directly with a treatment already in use, giving patients and physicians evidence that reflects the choices they face every day. As the number of effective treatments for type 2 diabetes and obesity has grown, Lilly believes these direct comparisons are increasingly important.
2. Why did TRANSCEND-T2D-2 compare retatrutide with Ozempic 2 mg? 
TRANSCEND-T2D-2 compared retatrutide with injectable Ozempic 2 mg because it is the highest approved dose, making it a meaningful point of comparison. In the trial, retatrutide delivered greater A1C reduction and more than double the weight loss of Ozempic. Lilly is also comparing retatrutide head-to-head with tirzepatide in TRIUMPH-5, an ongoing Phase 3 trial in adults with obesity with or without type 2 diabetes.
3. How did retatrutide compare with Ozempic? 
In TRANSCEND-T2D-2, both doses of retatrutide delivered greater A1C reduction and more than double the weight loss of Ozempic 2 mg at 80 weeks. Participants taking retatrutide lowered their A1C by an average of 2.2% compared to 1.8% with Ozempic and lost an average of 44.3 lbs (19.5%; 9 mg) and 47.4 lbs (20.9%; 12 mg) compared to 20.9 lbs (9.4%) with Ozempic. The most common adverse events with retatrutide were gastrointestinal-related. Treatment discontinuation rates due to adverse events were 4.8% (9 mg) and 7.9% (12 mg) with retatrutide, compared to 2.7% with Ozempic.
4. What could these results mean for people with type 2 diabetes? 
In TRANSCEND-T2D-2, people taking the highest dose of retatrutide lost an average of 47.4 lbs (20.9%), more than double the weight loss seen with Ozempic, along with greater A1C reduction. In TRIUMPH-2, people with type 2 diabetes and obesity taking the highest dose lost an average of 49.6 lbs (20.8%). Weight loss has historically been more difficult for people living with type 2 diabetes, and Lilly believes that, if approved, retatrutide could shift how the disease is treated.
5. Is anyone legally allowed to sell retatrutide to patients? 
No. Retatrutide is an investigational molecule that has not been approved by FDA or any regulatory organization anywhere in the world. Anyone purporting to sell retatrutide to consumers is breaking the law.
About retatrutide
Retatrutide is an investigational, once-weekly, triple hormone receptor agonist. Retatrutide is a single molecule that activates the body's receptors for glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 ( GLP-1 ), and glucagon. Lilly is studying retatrutide in several Phase 3 clinical trials to evaluate its potential efficacy and safety in obesity and overweight with at least one weight-related medical problem, type 2 diabetes, knee osteoarthritis pain, moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea, chronic low back pain, cardiovascular outcomes, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Retatrutide is an investigational molecule that cannot be legally sold or marketed for human use.
About TRANSCEND-T2D-2 and TRANSCEND clinical trial program
TRANSCEND-T2D-2 (NCT06260722) is a Phase 3, randomized, open-label trial comparing once-weekly retatrutide (9 mg and 12 mg) with once-weekly Ozempic 2 mg in 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with metformin, with or without an SGLT2 inhibitor. Participants with a baseline A1C of 7.0% to 10.5% were randomized 2:2:1 to retatrutide 9 mg, retatrutide 12 mg or Ozempic 2 mg. The primary objective was to demonstrate that retatrutide 12 mg is noninferior to Ozempic 2 mg in A1C reduction at 80 weeks. Retatrutide was initiated at 2 mg and increased every four weeks to the 9 mg or 12 mg target dose. TRANSCEND-T2D-2 also includes an extension period in which approximately 650 participants continue treatment with retatrutide for an additional 24 weeks to evaluate long-term efficacy and safety.
The TRANSCEND-T2D Phase 3 clinical trial program is evaluating the safety and efficacy of retatrutide for the treatment of adults with type 2 diabetes across three global registrational trials. The program, which began in 2024, has enrolled more than 2,050 participants.
Endnotes and References: 
All comparisons of retatrutide vs. Ozempic 2 mg were controlled for family-wise type 1 error, except superiority of retatrutide 9 mg vs. Ozempic 2 mg in change in A1C and in systolic blood pressure, which were prespecified secondary endpoints and showed nominal statistical significance. A1C noninferiority for retatrutide 9 mg vs. Ozempic 2 mg was met under family-wise type 1 error control as a key secondary endpoint.
All data included in this press release are for the efficacy estimand. The efficacy estimand represents efficacy had all randomized participants remained on study intervention (with possible dose interruptions and modifications) for 80 weeks without initiating additional antihyperglycemic medication (>14 days of use).
FOUNDAYO INDICATION AND SAFETY SUMMARY WITH WARNINGS
Foundayo (fown-DAY-oh) is a prescription medicine used with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity to help adults with obesity, or some adults with overweight who also have weight-related medical problems, to lose excess body weight and keep the weight off.
Foundayo should not be used with other  GLP-1  receptor agonist medicines. 
It is not known if Foundayo is safe and effective for use in children. 
Warnings – Foundayo may cause tumors in the thyroid, including thyroid cancer. Watch for possible symptoms, such as a lump or swelling in the neck, hoarseness, trouble swallowing, or shortness of breath. If you have any of these symptoms, tell your healthcare provider.
Do not use Foundayo if you or any of your family have ever had a type of thyroid cancer called medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). 
Do not use Foundayo if you have Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2). 
Do not use Foundayo if you have had a serious allergic reaction to orforglipron or any of the ingredients in Foundayo. 
Foundayo may cause serious side effects, including:
Inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis). Stop taking Foundayo and call your healthcare provider right away if you have severe pain in your stomach area (abdomen) that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting. Sometimes you may feel the pain from your abdomen to your back.
Severe stomach problems. Stomach problems, sometimes severe, have been reported in people who use Foundayo. Tell your healthcare provider if you have stomach problems that are severe or will not go away.
Dehydration leading to kidney problems. Diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting may cause a loss of fluids (dehydration), which may cause kidney problems. It is important for you to drink fluids to help reduce your chance of dehydration. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not go away.
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) . Your risk for getting low blood sugar may be higher if you use Foundayo with medicines that can cause low blood sugar, such as an insulin or sulfonylurea. Signs and symptoms of low blood sugar may include dizziness or light-headedness, sweating, confusion or drowsiness, headache, blurred vision, slurred speech, shakiness, fast heartbeat, anxiety, irritability, mood changes, hunger, weakness, or feeling jittery.
Serious allergic reactions. Stop using Foundayo and get medical help right away if you have any symptoms of a serious allergic reaction, including swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat, problems breathing or swallowing, severe rash or itching, fainting or feeling dizzy, or very rapid heartbeat.
Changes in vision in patients with type 2 diabetes. Tell your healthcare provider if you have changes in vision during treatment with Foundayo.
Gallbladder problems. Gallbladder problems have happened in some people who use Foundayo. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you get symptoms of gallbladder problems, which may include pain in your upper stomach (abdomen), fever, yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice), or clay-colored stools.
Food or liquid getting into the lungs during surgery or other procedures that use anesthesia or deep sleepiness (deep sedation). Foundayo may increase the chance of food getting into your lungs during surgery or other procedures. Tell your healthcare providers that you are taking Foundayo before you are scheduled to have surgery or other procedures.
Common side effects
The most common side effects of Foundayo include nausea, constipation, diarrhea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach (abdominal) pain, headache, swollen belly, feeling tired, belching, heartburn, gas, and hair loss. These are not all the possible side effects of Foundayo. Talk to your healthcare provider about any side effect that bothers you or doesn't go away.
Tell your doctor if you have any side effects. You can report side effects at 1-800-FDA-1088 or www.fda.gov/medwatch . 
Before taking Foundayo 
Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you take.  Foundayo may affect the way some medicines work, and some medicines may affect the way Foundayo works. 
Pregnancy Exposure Registry : There will be a pregnancy exposure registry for women who have taken Foundayo during pregnancy. The purpose of this registry is to collect information about the health of you and your baby. Talk to your healthcare provider about how you can take part in this registry, or you may contact Eli Lilly and Company at 1-800-LillyRx (1-800-545-5979). 
If you take birth control pills by mouth, talk to your healthcare provider before you take Foundayo. Birth control pills may not work as well while taking Foundayo.  Your healthcare provider may recommend another type of birth control for 30 days after starting Foundayo and for 30 days after each dose increase of Foundayo. 
Talk to your healthcare provider about low blood sugar and how to manage it.  Tell your healthcare provider if you are taking medicines to treat diabetes including an insulin or sulfonylurea. 
Review these questions with your healthcare provider: 
❑ Do you have other medical conditions, including problems with your pancreas or kidneys, or severe problems with your liver, severe problems with your stomach, such as slowed emptying of your stomach (gastroparesis) or problems digesting food?
❑ Do you have a history of diabetic retinopathy?
❑ Are you scheduled to have surgery or other procedures that use anesthesia or deep sleepiness (deep sedation)?
❑ Are you pregnant or plan to become pregnant? Foundayo may harm your unborn baby.
❑ Are you breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed? Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with Foundayo.
❑ Do you take any other prescriptions or over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements?
How to take 
Take Foundayo exactly as your healthcare provider tells you to. 
Use Foundayo with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. 
Take Foundayo by mouth 1 time each day, with or without food. 
Swallow tablets whole. Do not break, crush, or chew the tablet. 
If you miss a dose, take it as soon as possible.  Do not  take  2  doses of Foundayo in the same day. 
Do not take more than 1 tablet per day. 
If you miss taking Foundayo for 7 or more days in a row, call your healthcare provider to talk about how to restart your treatment. 
If you take too much Foundayo, call your healthcare provider or Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222 or go to the nearest hospital emergency room right away. 
Learn more 
Foundayo is a prescription medicine available in 0.8 mg, 2.5 mg, 5.5 mg, 9 mg, 14.5 mg, or 17.2 mg oral tablets. For more information, call 1-800-545-5979 or go to foundayo.lilly.com .
This summary provides basic information about Foundayo but does not include all information known about this medicine. Read the information that comes with your prescription each time your prescription is filled. This information does not take the place of talking with your doctor. Be sure to talk to your doctor or other healthcare provider about Foundayo and how to take it. Your doctor is the best person to help you decide if Foundayo is right for you.

MOUNJARO INDICATIONS AND SAFETY SUMMARY WITH WARNINGS 
Mounjaro ® (mown-JAHR-OH) is an injectable prescription medicine used along with diet and exercise to improve blood sugar (glucose) in adults and children 10 years of age and older with type 2 diabetes and to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events such as heart attack, stroke, or death in adults with type 2 diabetes who are at high risk for these events.
It is not known if Mounjaro is safe and effective for use in children under 10 years of age. 
Warnings - Mounjaro may cause tumors in the thyroid, including thyroid cancer. Watch for possible symptoms, such as a lump or swelling in the neck, hoarseness, trouble swallowing, or shortness of breath. If you have any of these symptoms, tell your healthcare provider.
Do not use Mounjaro if you or any of your family have ever had a type of thyroid cancer called medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC).
Do not use Mounjaro if you have Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).
Do not use Mounjaro if you are allergic to it or any of the ingredients in Mounjaro.
Mounjaro may cause serious side effects, including: 
Inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis). Stop using Mounjaro and call your healthcare provider right away if you have severe pain in your stomach area (abdomen) that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting. Sometimes you may feel the pain from your abdomen to your back. 
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Your risk for getting low blood sugar may be higher if you use Mounjaro with another medicine that can cause low blood sugar, such as a sulfonylurea or insulin. Signs and symptoms of low blood sugar may include dizziness or light-headedness, sweating, confusion or drowsiness, headache, blurred vision, slurred speech, shakiness, fast heartbeat, anxiety, irritability, or mood changes, hunger, weakness and feeling jittery.
Serious allergic reactions. Stop using Mounjaro and get medical help right away if you have any symptoms of a serious allergic reaction, including swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat, problems breathing or swallowing, severe rash or itching, fainting or feeling dizzy, and very rapid heartbeat. 
Dehydration leading to kidney problems. Diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting may cause a loss of fluids (dehydration), which may cause kidney problems. It is important for you to drink fluids to help reduce your chance of dehydration. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not go away.
Severe stomach problems. Stomach problems, sometimes severe, have been reported in people who use Mounjaro. Tell your healthcare provider if you have stomach problems that are severe or will not go away. 
Changes in vision. Tell your healthcare provider if you have changes in vision during treatment with Mounjaro.
Gallbladder problems. Gallbladder problems have happened in some people who use Mounjaro. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you get symptoms of gallbladder problems, which may include pain in your upper stomach (abdomen), fever, yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice), and clay-colored stools.
Food or liquid getting into the lungs during surgery or other procedures that use anesthesia or deep sleepiness (deep sedation). Mounjaro may increase the chance of food getting into your lungs during surgery or other procedures. Tell all your healthcare providers that you are taking Mounjaro before you are scheduled to have surgery or other procedures.
Common side effects 
The most common side effects of Mounjaro include nausea, diarrhea, decreased appetite, vomiting, constipation, indigestion, and stomach (abdominal) pain. These are not all the possible side effects of Mounjaro. Talk to your healthcare provider about any side effect that bothers you or doesn't go away. 
Tell your healthcare provider if you have any side effects. You can report side effects at 1-800-FDA-1088 or www.fda.gov/medwatch .
Before using Mounjaro 
Your healthcare provider should show you how to use Mounjaro before you use it for the first time. 
Talk to your healthcare provider about low blood sugar and how to manage it. 
If you take birth control pills by mouth, talk to your healthcare provider before you use Mounjaro. Birth control pills may not work as well while using Mounjaro. Your healthcare provider may recommend another type of birth control for 4 weeks after you start Mounjaro and for 4 weeks after each increase in your dose of Mounjaro.
Review these questions with your healthcare provider: 
❑ Do you have other medical conditions, including problems with your pancreas, or severe problems with your stomach, such as slowed emptying of your stomach (gastroparesis) or problems digesting food?
❑ Do you take other diabetes medicines, such as insulin or sulfonylureas?
❑ Do you have a history of diabetic retinopathy?
❑ Are you scheduled to have surgery or other procedures that use anesthesia or deep sleepiness (deep sedation)?
❑ Are you pregnant, plan to become pregnant, breastfeeding, or plan to breastfeed? It is not known if Mounjaro will harm your unborn baby. Mounjaro may pass into your breast milk.
❑ Do you take any other prescription medicines or over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements?
How to take 
Read the Instructions for Use that come with Mounjaro.
Use Mounjaro exactly as your healthcare provider says.
A caregiver may give you Mounjaro injections, or you may self-inject if a healthcare provider determines that it is appropriate.
Inject Mounjaro under the skin (subcutaneously) of your stomach (abdomen), thigh, or another person should inject in the back of the upper arm. Do not inject Mounjaro into a muscle (intramuscularly) or vein (intravenously).
Use Mounjaro 1 time each week, at any time of the day. 
Do not mix insulin and Mounjaro together in the same injection.
You may give an injection of Mounjaro and insulin in the same body area (such as your stomach area), but not right next to each other.
Change (rotate) your injection site with each weekly injection. Do not use the same site for each injection.
If you take too much Mounjaro, call your healthcare provider or Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222 or go to the nearest hospital emergency room right away.
Learn more 
Mounjaro is a prescription medicine available as a pre-filled single-dose pen in 2.5 mg, 5 mg, 7.5 mg, 10 mg, 12.5 mg, or 15 mg per 0.5 mL injection. For more information, call 1-800-LillyRX (800-545-5979) or go to www.mounjaro.lilly.com . 
This summary provides basic information about Mounjaro but does not include all information known about this medicine. Read the information that comes with your prescription each time your prescription is filled. This information does not take the place of talking with your healthcare provider. Be sure to talk to your healthcare provider about Mounjaro and how to take it. Your healthcare provider is the best person to help you decide if Mounjaro is right for you.

GE HealthCare reports third quarter 2026 financial results
October 28, 2026
PDF Version 
Delivers top- and bottom-line growth ahead of Company expectations and raises full-year 2026 guidance
Revenue growth of 7.2%, and Organic revenue growth* of 6.2%
Organic orders growth of 4.0%, book-to-bill of 1.03 times and backlog of $23.7 billion 
Net income margin of 11.1% and Adjusted earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) margin* of 16.6%; diluted EPS of $1.36 grew 39.1% and Adjusted EPS* of $1.34 grew 25.1%
Cash flow from operating activities of $907 million and Free cash flow* of $793 million 
CHICAGO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 28, 2026--
GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 .
GE HealthCare President and CEO Peter Arduini said, “We delivered strong top-line growth and margin expansion across all segments, and robust EPS growth in the third quarter. This reflects our teams’ commercial execution, disciplined operational focus enabled by Heartbeat, and continued customer adoption of our innovations. With our improved performance year-to-date and momentum in the business, we are raising guidance for the year.”
Third quarter 2026 total company financial performance (1) 
Revenues of $5.5 billion , up 7.2%, including Organic revenue growth* of 6.2%, with growth across all segments.
Total orders up 4.0% organically, book-to-bill of 1.03 times and backlog of $23.7 billion , driven by healthy demand.
Net income attributable to GE HealthCare of $615 million versus $446 million , and Adjusted EBIT* of $913 million versus $761 million .
Net income margin of 11.1% versus 8.7%, up 250 basis points (bps). Adjusted EBIT margin* of 16.6% versus 14.8%, up 180 bps, with both measures driven by volume, price and cost productivity, and favorable year-over-year net tariff impact, partially offset by inflation.
Diluted EPS of $1.36 versus $0.98 , up $0.38 ; Adjusted EPS* of $1.34 versus $1.07 , up $0.27 .

Third quarter capital deployment (1) 
Cash flow from operating activities of $907 million , up $314 million . Free cash flow* of $793 million , up $310 million . Both measures include a tariff refund of $55 million .
Capital expenditures of $114 million compared to $110 million in the prior year.
Cash and cash equivalents of $2.9 billion and access to $3.5 billion of revolving credit facilities. Total debt outstanding of $10.0 billion .

Non-GAAP financial measures 
The non-GAAP financial measures presented in this press release are supplemental measures of GE HealthCare’s performance and its liquidity that the Company believes will help investors understand its financial condition, cash flows, and operating results, and assess its future prospects. When read in conjunction with the Company’s U.S . GAAP results, these non-GAAP financial measures provide a baseline for analyzing trends in GE HealthCare’s underlying businesses and can be used by management as one basis for making financial, operational, and planning decisions. Descriptions of the reported non-GAAP measures are included below.
The Company reports Organic revenue and Organic revenue growth rate to provide management and investors with additional understanding and visibility into the underlying revenue trends of the Company’s established, ongoing operations, as well as provide insights into overall demand for its products and services. To calculate these measures, the Company excludes the effect of acquisitions, dispositions, and foreign currency rate fluctuations.
The Company reports EBIT, Adjusted EBIT, Adjusted EBIT margin, Adjusted net income, and Adjusted earnings per share to provide management and investors with an additional understanding of its business by highlighting the results from ongoing operations and the underlying profitability factors, on a normalized basis. To calculate these measures the Company excludes, and reflects in the detailed reconciliations below, the following adjustments as applicable: Interest and other financial charges – net, Net (income) loss attributable to noncontrolling interests, Non-operating benefit (income) costs, Benefit (provision) for income taxes and certain tax related adjustments, and certain non-recurring and/or non-cash items. GE HealthCare may from time to time consider excluding other non-recurring items to enhance comparability between periods. Adjusted EBIT margin is calculated by taking Adjusted EBIT divided by Total revenues for the same period.
The Company reports Adjusted tax expense and Adjusted ETR to provide management and investors with a better understanding of the normalized tax rate applicable to the business and provide more consistent comparability across periods. Adjusted tax expense excludes the income tax related to the pre-tax income adjustments included as part of Adjusted net income and certain income tax adjustments, such as adjustments to deferred tax assets or liabilities. The Company may from time to time consider excluding other non-recurring tax items to enhance comparability between periods. Adjusted ETR is Adjusted tax expense divided by income before income taxes less the pre-tax income adjustments referenced above.
The Company reports Free cash flow and Free cash flow conversion to provide management and investors with an important measure of the ability to generate cash on a normalized basis and provide insight into the Company’s flexibility to allocate capital. Free cash flow is Cash from (used for) operating activities – continuing operations including cash flows related to the additions and dispositions of property, plant, and equipment (“PP&E”) and additions of internal-use software. Free cash flow does not represent residual cash flows available for discretionary expenditures, due to the fact that the measure does not deduct the capital required for debt repayments. Free cash flow conversion is calculated by taking Free cash flow divided by Adjusted net income.
Management recognizes that these non-GAAP financial measures have limitations, including that they may be calculated differently by other companies or may be used under different circumstances or for different purposes. In order to compensate for the discussed limitations, management does not consider these measures in isolation from or as alternatives to the comparable financial measures determined in accordance with U.S . GAAP. The detailed reconciliations of each non-GAAP financial measure to the most directly comparable U.S . Non-GAAP financial measures in outlook 
GE HealthCare calculates forward-looking non-GAAP financial measures, including Organic revenue growth, Adjusted EBIT margin, Adjusted ETR, Adjusted EPS, and Free cash flow based on internal forecasts that omit certain amounts that would be included in U.S . GAAP financial measures. GE HealthCare does not provide reconciliations of these forward-looking non-GAAP financial measures to the respective U.S . GAAP metrics as it is unable to predict with reasonable certainty and without unreasonable effort certain items such as the impact of changes in currency exchange rates, impacts associated with business acquisitions or dispositions, timing and magnitude of restructuring activities, and revaluation of strategic investments, amongst other items. The timing and amounts of these items are uncertain and could have a substantial impact on GE HealthCare’s results in accordance with U.S . GAAP.
Key performance indicators 
Management uses the following metrics to provide a leading indicator of current business demand from customers for products and services.
Organic orders growth: Rate of change period-over-period of contractual commitments with customers to provide specified goods or services for an agreed upon price, and excluding the effects of: (1) recent acquisitions and dispositions with less than a full year of comparable orders; and (2) foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations in order to present orders on a constant currency basis.
Book-to-bill: Total orders divided by Total revenues within a given financial period (e.g., quarter or FY).

title: Strength across all core businesses drives BASF Group’s considerable growth in EBITDA before special items

content_text:
Home

Strength across all core businesses drives BASF Group’s considerable growth in EBITDA before special items 
Business & Financial News | October 28, 2026 
Media
BASF Group in third quarter 2026: 
Strength across all core businesses drives BASF Group’s considerable growth in EBITDA before special items 
Sales: €16.4 billion (Q3 2025: €14.3 billion) 
EBITDA before special items: €1.6 billion (Q3 2025: €1.4 billion)  
Outlook 2026: EBITDA before special items of between €7.4 billion and €7.8 billion (previous forecast: €6.9 billion to €7.7 billion) 
BASF delivered another strong quarter. Sales increased by 14 percent compared with the prior-year quarter to reach €16.4 billion. The increase was mainly driven by considerably higher prices (plus 12%) and slightly higher volumes (plus 2%). At €1.6 billion, EBITDA before special items rose significantly by 15 percent compared with the third quarter of 2025. All core businesses contributed to this. 
“The strong year-to-date performance of our core businesses gives us confidence to narrow our forecast range for EBITDA before special items upward,” said Dr. Markus Kamieth, Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors of BASF, when presenting the figures for the third quarter of 2026 together with Chief Financial Officer Dr. Dirk Elvermann. BASF now expects EBITDA before special items of between €7.4 billion and €7.8 billion in the 2026 business year (previous forecast from Half-Year Financial Report 2026: between €6.9 billion and €7.7 billion).
BASF Group’s business development in the third quarter of 2026 
Sales  in the third quarter of 2026 amounted to €16.4 billion, €2 billion above the prior-year period’s figure. This was mainly due to considerably higher prices in the Chemicals, Materials, Surface Technologies and Industrial Solutions segments. Prices improved slightly in Nutrition & Care, while Agricultural Solutions recorded a slight decline in prices. Volumes increased substantially in the Chemicals and Nutrition & Care segments and slightly in the Industrial Solutions, Materials and Surface Technologies segments. A significant decline in volumes in the Agricultural Solutions segment had a dampening effect. Positive currency effects in all segments, especially relating to the U.S. dollar and the Chinese renminbi, contributed to the sales increase. Sales in Other improved considerably.
EBITDA before special items  increased by €213 million compared with the prior-year quarter to €1.6 billion. This was due to the considerable earnings increase in the Chemicals, Nutrition & Care, Materials and Industrial Solutions segments, which more than offset the decline in earnings in Agricultural Solutions and Surface Technologies. EBITDA before special items in Other decreased considerably compared with the prior-year period. At 10.0 percent, the EBITDA margin before special items  was at the level of the prior-year period. 
EBITDA amounted to €1.2 billion in the third quarter of 2026, matching the level recorded in the prior-year period. EBITDA included special items  totaling minus €437 million in the third quarter of 2026. These resulted in particular from transformation expenses for restructuring measures, primarily at the Ludwigshafen site, as well as from a settlement of a legal dispute in the Care Chemicals division.
EBIT  stood at minus €98 million, compared with €232 million in the prior-year quarter. Depreciation and amortization amounted to €1.3 billion (Q3 2025: €976 million), including an impairment in the Monomers division (€318 million). 
Net income  amounted to €155 million (Q3 2025: €172 million). Earnings per share  came in at €0.18 in the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 2025: €0.19). Earnings per share adjusted  for special items and amortization of intangible assets were €0.72 (Q3 2025: €0.52).
In the third quarter of 2026, cash flows from operating activities  amounted to €1.1 billion, €275 million below the level of the prior-year quarter. The decrease was mainly attributable to €507 million cash being tied up in inventories, predominantly as a result of higher raw materials prices, whereas €6 million had been released in the prior-year period. 
Cash flows from investing activities  amounted to minus €89 million, compared with minus €767 million in the prior-year quarter. This change was attributable in part to payments of €434 million received from the disposal of shares in Harbour Energy. Moreover, payments made for intangible assets and property, plant and equipment decreased by €401 million, mainly owing to lower payments relating to the Verbund site in Zhanjiang, China. Free cash flow amounted to €523 million in the third quarter of 2026, up by €125 million compared with the level of the prior-year quarter.
BASF Group outlook for 2026 
Given the continuing uncertainty surrounding further geopolitical and global economic developments, BASF maintains the macroeconomic assumptions published in the Half-Year Financial Report 2026:
Growth in gross domestic product: 2.5 percent
Growth in industrial production: 2.0 percent 
Growth in chemical production: 1.8 percent
Average euro/dollar exchange rate of $1.17 per euro
Average annual oil price (Brent crude) of $80 per barrel
As the business year has progressed and there is greater visibility regarding the expected earnings development, BASF is able to provide a more specific forecast range for BASF Group’s EBITDA before special items for the 2026 business year than was published in the BASF Half-Year Financial Report 2026. Compared with the previous forecast, BASF has raised the lower end of the EBITDA before special items range and slightly increased the upper end (previous forecast from the Half-Year Financial Report 2026 in parentheses):
EBITDA before special items of between €7.4 billion and €7.8 billion (between €6.9 billion and €7.7 billion)
Free cash flow of between €1.5 billion and €2.3 billion (unchanged)
CO 2 emissions of between 17.2 million metric tons and 18.2 million metric tons (unchanged) 
  About BASF 
At BASF, we create chemistry for a sustainable future. Our ambition: We want to be the preferred chemical company to enable our customers’ green transformation. We combine economic success with environmental protection and social responsibility. Around 95,000 employees in the BASF Group contribute to the success of our customers in nearly all sectors and almost every country in the world. Our portfolio comprises, as core businesses, the segments Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, and Nutrition & Care; our standalone businesses are bundled in the segments Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. BASF generated sales of around €60 billion in 2025. BASF shares are traded on the stock exchange in Frankfurt (BAS) and as American Depositary Receipts (BASFY) in the United States. title: 28 October 2026 Jenoptik Baltic secures major contract to expand Lithuania’s “Via Toll” enforcement network Jenoptik Baltic secures major contract to expand Lithuania’s “Via Toll” enforcement network with more than 200 ANPR cameras. read more
