content_text:
Jenoptik Baltic secures major contract to expand Lithuania’s “Via Toll” enforcement network
28 October 2026 
Jenoptik Baltic, part of Jenoptik Smart Mobility Solutions and formerly known as FIMA ITS, has been awarded a significant low single-digit million euros contract by Via Lietuva. The contract involves the delivery and installation of more than 200 new Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras  across Lithuanian national roads and complements the successful previous installation of the same cameras. This deployment supports the launch of the “Via Toll” electronic road toll system on January 1st, 2027, which replaces the current e-vignettes for heavy goods and commercial vehicles with distance-based tolling.
Simonas Šidlauskas, Managing Director of Jenoptik Baltic, commented: “We are delighted that Via Lietuva will expand its network using our proven GardoVia technology. We look forward to supporting Lithuania’s transition to its new tolling framework.”
Martynas Gedaminskas, CEO of Via Lietuva, stated: “A new electronic road toll system in Lithuania will come into operation at the start of 2027. A smooth transition requires a range of tasks of varying complexity, and one of the planned measures is to strengthen enforcement. To ensure the effective collection of road tolls, we are increasing the number of traffic surveillance cameras on toll roads in Lithuania.”
The project entails installing Jenoptik’s GardoVia universal ANPR camera at about 125 strategic locations within twelve months. GardoVia is a cost-effective, police-graded camera designed to reliably identify license plates and categorize vehicles. It is widely used for various applications, e.g. civil security solutions, parking management, access control, and toll enforcement. By expanding the monitoring network on paid road sections, the system will enhance the automatic detection and recording of toll violations.
Gerrit Palm, Vice President EMEA region of Jenoptik SMS, added: “This contract highlights the successful integration of our former partner FIMA ITS into the Jenoptik family. It demonstrates our ability to combine global presence with local expertise and service excellence to deliver strong value to our customers.”
The agreement underscores Jenoptik Baltic’s continued commitment to supporting safer roads and efficient mobility solutions in the region, reinforcing its position within the Jenoptik Smart Mobility Solutions portfolio.

title: Six Companies Launch Joint R&D to Build a Quantum-Computing-Based Materials Development Platform
query: https://www.holdings.toppan.com/en/news/
content_text:
Six Companies Launch Joint R&D to Build a Quantum-Computing-Based Materials Development Platform
Project selected by NEDO for innovative materials development platforms using quantum technology; demonstrates practical use cases that integrate quantum computing and AI technologies
Tweet 
Tokyo – October 28, 2026 –TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TOPPAN Holdings; TYO: 7911), AISIN CORPORATION (AISIN; TYO: 7259), Asahi Kasei Corporation (Asahi Kasei; TYO: 3407), SoftBank Corp. (SoftBank; TYO: 9434), AGC Inc. (AGC; TYO: 5201), and DIC Corporation (DIC; TYO: 4631) jointly announced today that their joint proposal, “Research and Development of Innovative Materials Development Platforms Using Quantum Technology” (hereinafter the “Project”), has been selected by the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO). 1 The Project was chosen under NEDO’s solicitation for the “Research and Development Project of the Enhanced Infrastructures for Post-5G Information and Communication Systems ”.
Following this selection, the six companies entered into a joint agreement to conduct research and development on constructing a new materials development platform utilizing quantum computers from fiscal 2026 (the year ending March 31, 2027) through fiscal 2028. The Project aims to establish a next-generation materials development platform by integrating quantum-computing-based calculations with AI technologies such as machine learning, thereby bridging the gap between demonstration and real-world application.
Background
For Japanese chemical and materials manufacturers to maintain global competitiveness, an urgent priority is to establish technologies that dramatically improve the discovery of new materials as well as development efficiency. In recent years, progress has been made in data-driven approaches—where AI predicts and explores new materials based on historical materials data—as well as computational science simulations based on physical laws. However, while data-driven methods face a challenge in securing sufficient, high-quality, and high-precision training data, computational science faces the issue of surging computational costs for higher accuracy and larger scale calculations. 
There is strong optimism for quantum computers operating on the principles of quantum mechanics to address such challenges. Quantum computers have the potential to simulate the properties of molecules and electrons governed by quantum mechanics more efficiently than conventional computers. However, since there are currently limitations in qubit 2 count and error rates, large-scale calculations using quantum computers alone are still not a reality.
To overcome these hurdles, the Project will establish a methodology that combines quantum-computing-based calculations with AI, mitigating constraints on calculation precision and scale. Rather than targeting a single specific material, the materials development technologies will be applied cross-sectionally across a broad range of industrially vital materials systems, with each of the six companies handling verification in their respective domains of strength. In addition, through collaboration with specialized quantum computing institutions, the companies will advance applicability verifications across diverse materials while working together to create practical value for industrial application.
Overview of the Project
1. Verification of Quantum Computing Application Areas 
Verify the applicability of quantum computing for numerous major materials with high industrial demand, including materials required for next-generation batteries, optical functional materials for new displays and sensors, and superconducting materials for next-generation devices. 
2. Development of Quantum Computing Utilization Technologies 
Develop technologies that integrate quantum-computing-based calculations with AI to expand the scope of computational methods and verify solutions to scale and cost limitations inherent in conventional computing methods. 
3. Simulation Demonstration and Experiment Feedback 
Synthesize materials and evaluate their performance based on simulation results (including those using quantum computing) and compare experiment results against simulation data to improve predictive accuracy and verify the benefits of practical application of quantum computing. 
Roles of Participating Companies
TOPPAN Holdings 
Execute hybrid methods combining quantum and classical algorithms on quantum computers for additive materials to verify quantum computing application; develop combined quantum computing and AI methods; provide experiment feedback. 
AISIN 
Verify quantum computing application for superconducting materials; compare results with conventional material development methods; forecast practical implementation timelines in material development environments.
Asahi Kasei 
Verify platforms utilizing quantum computing for materials development through applicability studies of quantum computing to organic compounds (such as electrolytes), polymer materials, and inorganic materials (such as electrodes), combined with feedback from experimental results.
SoftBank Corp. 
Utilize a computing platform connecting quantum computers with supercomputers to generate high-level data useful for material development, along with developing data utilization technologies using AI; carry out demonstrations to optimize material development across diverse domains, including energy-related materials such as next-generation batteries. 
AGC 
Develop and evaluate material development methods combining quantum computing with existing computational science and AI technologies for inorganic materials (such as optical glass) and organic materials (such as electronic materials); derive insights and establish design guidelines to enhance materials exploration and design. 
DIC 
Integrate quantum computing, simulation, and data science technologies to predict key material properties prior to synthesis for colorants and semiconductor materials, while establishing and validating novel research methodologies that accelerate the efficient design and development of high-performance materials.
Future Steps
By combining data on quantum computing and AI with the experimental data obtained through the Project, the six companies will work toward constructing a continuously evolving materials development platform, contributing to the creation of cross-industry innovation.
1 For details on the call for proposals and selection results, please visit: https://www.nedo.go.jp/koubo/CD3_100424.html (in Japanese)
2 A qubit is the fundamental unit of quantum information in quantum computing.

title: Oct. 28, 2026 Business & Products Veolia and Sumitomo Chemical Selected to Participate in the Ministry of the Environment of Japan's FY2026 Model Project for Plastic Resource Circulation
source: Sumitomo Chemical - News Releases Filter / Press Releases
query: https://www.sumitomo-chem.co.jp/english/news/category/newsreleases/
content_text:
Veolia and Sumitomo Chemical Selected to Participate in the Ministry of the Environment of Japan's FY2026 Model Project for Plastic Resource Circulation
Oct. 28, 2026
Veolia Jenets K.K.
Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.
Veolia Jenets K.K. (“Veolia”) and Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd. (“Sumitomo Chemical”) have been selected to participate in the Ministry of the Environment of Japan’s FY2026 Model Project for Plastic Resource Circulation (the “Model Project”). By combining Mechanical Recycling (“MR”) and chemical recycling (“CR”), the two companies aim to advance resource utilization rates and conversion rates into chemicals in the recycling of plastic containers and packaging.
Up until now, plastic containers and packaging separately collected under Japan’s Containers and Packaging Recycling Act (“collected plastic containers and packaging”) have been handled by recycling operators and then recycled using either MR or CR as the sole recycling method. Beginning in FY2027, the System will enable MR operators and CR operators to form joint groups and combine different recycling methods to further advance in quality and yield of the recycling of collected plastic packaging. The Model Project is intended to promote the use of the System.
Some collected plastic containers and packaging are difficult to make efficient use of due to differences in material composition, contamination, or the use of composite materials. As a result, conventional MR has achieved a recycling rate of only approximately 50% for collected plastic containers and packaging.* Through participation in the Model Project, waste plastics derived from residues generated during the MR process will be recycled through CR. This combined approach is expected to increase the resource utilization rate of collected plastic containers and packaging to approximately 80%. In addition, CR will enable waste plastics from residues generated in the MR process, which have previously been used mainly for energy recovery, to be recycled into chemicals of equivalent quality to fossil-derived virgin products, expanding their use to include chemical feedstocks.
Under the Model Project, drawing on its expertise in waste management, sorting, and resource recovery, Veolia will promote the efficient use of materials suitable for MR while developing a sorting and supply scheme to channel plastics difficult to process through MR to CR. Through these efforts, Veolia aims to improve the resource utilization rate and add greater value to recycled resources. Sumitomo Chemical will seek to apply its CR technology to efficiently convert pyrolysis oil derived from plastics sorted and supplied by Veolia for CR into basic chemicals, such as ethylene and propylene, using a proprietary catalyst currently under development. 
Veolia and Sumitomo Chemical will leverage the results of the studies and verification conducted under the Model Project and strengthen their collaboration with a wide range of stakeholders—including municipalities, recycling operators, product manufacturers, and customers. Through these efforts, the two companies will seek to achieve the practical implementation of a resource-circulation scheme and CR technology and contribute to the realization of a circular society.
About Veolia Jenets
Veolia Jenets K.K. is a group company of Veolia, a global leader in environmental services. Established in 1997, it operates an integrated portfolio of water, waste, and energy businesses in Japan. Leveraging expertise developed both globally and domestically, it provides locally rooted services throughout Japan.
In the waste sector, Veolia collects, sorts, and recycles plastics, including plastic containers and packaging, thereby supporting the transition to a circular economy.
About Sumitomo Chemical
Sumitomo Chemical is a diversified chemical company that supports a broad range of industries, and the everyday lives of people, through its Agro & Life Solutions, ICT & Mobility Solutions, and Advanced Medical Solutions businesses, Essential & Green Materials. The Company regards resource circulation and the reduction of GHG emissions as key priorities, and promotes the development and practical implementation of technologies, products, and businesses, including chemical recycling.
 
*Source: Research Report: Estimated Effective Utilization Rates by Plastic Type (FY2024), The Japan Containers and Packaging Recycling Association.

October 27, 2026

WILMINGTON, Del. , Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Chemours Company ("Chemours") (NYSE: CC) today announced that the Board of Directors of Chemours declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.0875 per share on the Company's common stock for the fourth quarter of 2026. The dividend will be paid on December 15, 2026 , to stockholders of record as of the close of business on November 16, 2026 .

The Chemours Company (NYSE: CC) is a global leader in providing industrial and specialty chemicals products for markets, including coatings, plastics, refrigeration and air conditioning, transportation, semiconductor and advanced electronics, general industrial, and oil and gas. Through our three businesses – Thermal & Specialized Solutions, Titanium Technologies, and Advanced Performance Materials – we deliver application expertise and chemistry-based innovations that solve customers' biggest challenges. Our flagship products are sold under prominent brands such as Opteon™, Freon™, Ti-Pure™, Nafion™, Teflon™, Viton™, and Krytox™. Headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware and listed on the NYSE under the symbol CC, Chemours has approximately 5,700 employees and 28 manufacturing sites and serves approximately 2,400 customers in approximately 110 countries. NXP Semiconductors Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
October 27, 2026 at 4:10 PM EDT
Announces $5 Billion Increase in Share Repurchase Authorization 
EINDHOVEN, The Netherlands , Oct. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NXP Semiconductors N.V. (NASDAQ: NXPI) today reported financial results for the third quarter, which ended September 27, 2026 . “NXP delivered third-quarter revenue of $3.8 billion , up 19 percent year-on-year and 8 percent sequentially. Our performance was driven by accelerating contributions from our company-specific growth drivers in automotive and industrial as well as continued momentum in data center infrastructure. Strong profitability leading to free cash flow generation enables NXP to invest in innovative solutions and expand manufacturing capabilities that support our long-term growth objectives, while continuing to return capital to shareholders through our newly announced $5 billion share repurchase authorization. Looking ahead, we see significant opportunities as software-defined vehicles drive increasing demand for our next-generation solutions, while data center infrastructure and Trusted Physical AI applications create new vectors for long-term growth,” said Rafael Sotomayor , NXP President and Chief Executive Officer.
Key Highlights for the Third Quarter 2026: 
Revenue was $3.79 billion , up 19 percent year-on-year;
GAAP gross margin was 57.8 percent, GAAP operating margin was 32.4 percent and GAAP diluted Net Income per Share was $3.48 ;
Non-GAAP gross margin was 58.6 percent, non-GAAP operating margin was 37.1 percent, and non-GAAP diluted Net Income per Share was $4.20 ;
Cash flow from operations was $1.26 billion , with net capex investments of $50 million , resulting in non-GAAP free cash flow of $1.21 billion or 31.9 percent of revenue;
Capital return during the quarter was $359 million , representing 29.8 percent of third quarter non-GAAP free cash flow. Dividends paid during the quarter were $256 million , and share buybacks were $103 million ;
On August 4, 2026 , NXP announced that its Trimension™ Ultra-Wideband (UWB) ranging and radar solutions will be deployed by the BMW Group across its fleet, starting with selected 2026 vehicle programs;
On August 12, 2026 , NXP broke ground on its assembly and test site expansion in Malaysia ;
On September 28, 2026 , VSMC, the joint venture between Vanguard International Semiconductor Corporation (VIS) and NXP Semiconductors N.V. , marked the grand opening of its first 300mm fab in Singapore ; and
The NXP Board of Directors, in October after quarter end, authorized a $5 billion share repurchase program in addition to the $1.3 billion remaining under the prior authorization.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
In managing NXP 's business on a consolidated basis, management develops an annual operating plan, which is approved by our Board of Directors, using non-GAAP financial measures, that are not in accordance with, nor an alternative to, U.S . generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). In measuring performance against this plan, management considers the actual or potential impacts on these non-GAAP financial measures from actions taken to reduce costs with the goal of increasing our gross margin and operating margin and when assessing appropriate levels of research and development efforts. In addition, management relies upon these non-GAAP financial measures when making decisions about product spending, administrative budgets, and other operating expenses. We believe that these non-GAAP financial measures, when coupled with the GAAP results and the reconciliations to corresponding GAAP financial measures, provide a more complete understanding of the Company’s results of operations and the factors and trends affecting NXP’s business. We believe that they enable investors to perform additional comparisons of our operating results, to assess our liquidity and capital position and to analyze financial performance excluding the effect of expenses unrelated to core operating performance, certain non-cash expenses and share-based compensation expense, which may obscure trends in NXP 's underlying performance. This information also enables investors to compare financial results between periods where certain items may vary independent of business performance, and allow for greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management. 
These non-GAAP financial measures are provided in addition to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP. The presentation of these and other similar items in NXP’s non-GAAP financial results should not be interpreted as implying that these items are non-recurring, infrequent, or unusual. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP measures to the most comparable measures calculated in accordance with GAAP are provided in the financial statements portion of this release in a schedule entitled “Financial Reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP Results (unaudited).” Please refer to the NXP Historic Financial Model file found on the Financial Information page of the Investor Relations section of our website at https://investors.nxp.com for additional information related to our rationale for using these non-GAAP financial measures, as well as the impact of these measures on the presentation of NXP 's operations.
In addition to providing financial information on a basis consistent with GAAP, NXP also provides the following selected financial measures on a non-GAAP basis: (i) Gross profit, (ii) Gross margin, (iii) Research and development, (iv) Selling, general and administrative, (v) Other income, (vi) Operating income (loss), (vii) Operating margin, (viii) Financial Income (expense), (ix) Income tax benefit (provision), (x) Results relating to foundry equity-accounted investees, (xi) Net income (loss) attributable to stockholders, (xii) Earnings per Share - Diluted, (xiii) EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA and trailing 12 month adjusted EBITDA, and (xiv) free cash flow, trailing 12 month free cash flow and trailing 12 month free cash flow as a percent of Revenue. The non-GAAP information excludes, where applicable, the amortization of acquisition related intangible assets, the purchase accounting effect on inventory and property, plant and equipment, merger related costs (including integration costs), certain items related to divestitures, share-based compensation expense, restructuring and asset impairment charges, extinguishment of debt, foreign exchange gains and losses, income tax effect on adjustments described above and results from non-foundry equity-accounted investments.
The difference in the benefit (provision) for income taxes between our GAAP and non-GAAP results relates to the income tax effects of the GAAP to non-GAAP adjustments that we make and the income tax effect of any discrete items that occur in the interim period. Discrete items primarily relate to unexpected tax events that may occur as these amounts cannot be forecasted (e.g., the impact of changes in tax law and/or rates, changes in estimates or resolved tax audits relating to prior year tax provisions, the excess or deficit tax effects on share-based compensation, etc.).

title: Patrik Jonsson to retire after 36 years; Ilya Yuffa named president, Lilly Global Markets
source: Eli Lilly and Company - Official RSS
query: https://investor.lilly.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Patrik Jonsson to retire after 36 years; Ilya Yuffa named president, Lilly Global Markets
October 27, 2026
PDF Version 
Yuffa will take on an expanded role as the company scales for its next phase of growth 
Key highlights: 
Patrik Jonsson , executive vice president and president, Lilly International , has decided to retire at the end of 2026 after a 36-year career at Lilly .
On Jan. 1, 2027 , Ilya Yuffa will take on an expanded role as executive vice president and president, Lilly Global Markets, overseeing customer strategy and execution worldwide.
Laura Steele will be promoted to president, Lilly USA , and Elias Khalil will be promoted to group vice president and president, Lilly Europe and Canada .
INDIANAPOLIS , Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced that Patrik Jonsson , executive vice president and president, Lilly International , has decided to retire at the end of 2026 after a 36-year career at Lilly .
Jonsson joined the company in 1990 as a sales representative in Sweden . He went on to lead Lilly in Sweden , Scandinavia, Italy and Japan, then served as president of Lilly Bio-Medicines and Lilly Immunology, as well as president of Lilly USA and Lilly 's cardiometabolic health business, before leading Lilly International .
"For more than three decades, Patrik has dedicated his career to improving lives by bringing our medicines to people around the world," said David A. Ricks , Lilly chair and CEO. "He has held multiple executive roles in the company spanning drug development and customer operations, including head of immunology, cardiometabolic health and Lilly USA . Today he applies his deep expertise in global launches across Lilly International . Patrik is a patient-focused, engaging team leader who has mentored countless colleagues. On behalf of our Board, leadership team and thousands of employees he has worked alongside, I thank Patrik for his service to our company."
Effective Jan. 1, 2027 , Lilly 's U.S . and international businesses will come together as Lilly Global Markets, led by Ilya Yuffa , who will become executive vice president and president, Lilly Global Markets.
Bringing these organizations together will accelerate decision-making, increase scalability and provide a unified capability to improve human health through expanded access to medicines around the world.
Yuffa joined Lilly in 1996 as a financial analyst and has held leadership roles in finance, business development, sales and general management, including president and general manager of Lilly 's Italy Hub, which covered more than 25 countries, president of Lilly Bio-Medicines, president of Lilly International and currently executive vice president and president, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities.
Ricks continued, "To build on our momentum, now is the right time to consolidate our geographies for greater impact. Ilya has run both our international and U.S . businesses, and his range of experience and commitment to excellence make him uniquely qualified to lead our customer-facing operations worldwide. He is joined by a proven team with the expertise and focus to help us reach even more people with our medicines."
The following executives will lead the company's six geographic hubs and report to Yuffa:
Laura Steele , currently group vice president, U.S. Cardiometabolic Health , will be promoted to president, Lilly USA . In 23 years at Lilly , Steele has held leadership roles in marketing, value and access, and commercial operations inside and outside the U.S ., including Lilly 's U.S . neuroscience business.
Elias Khalil , currently president and general manager of Lilly 's Italy Hub, will be promoted to group vice president and president, Lilly Europe and Canada . In 18 years at Lilly , Khalil has held leadership roles across the Gulf region, Saudi Arabia and the U.S . neuroscience business.
Nabil Daoud will continue in his role as group vice president and president, Lilly InterContinental.
Karla Alcazar , Huzur Devletsah and Winselow Tucker will continue in their roles as president and general manager of Lilly Japan , Lilly China and Lilly India , respectively.
About Lilly 
Lilly is a medicine company turning science into healing to make life better for people around the world. We've been pioneering life-changing discoveries for 150 years, and today our medicines help tens of millions of people across the globe. Harnessing the power of biotechnology, chemistry and genetic medicine, our scientists are urgently advancing new discoveries to solve some of the world's most significant health challenges: redefining diabetes care; treating obesity and curtailing its most devastating long-term effects; advancing the fight against Alzheimer's disease; providing solutions to some of the most debilitating immune system disorders; and transforming the most difficult-to-treat cancers into manageable diseases. With each step toward a healthier world, we're motivated by one thing: making life better for millions more people. That includes delivering innovative clinical trials that reflect the diversity of our world and working to ensure our medicines are accessible and affordable. To learn more, visit Lilly.com and Lilly.com/news , or follow us on Facebook , Instagram , and LinkedIn . C-LLY

Charles River Leverages Virtual Control Groups in GLP Studies
PDF Version 
Collaboration highlights ongoing commitment to industry modernization and the highest animal welfare standards 
WILMINGTON, Mass. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 27, 2026--
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) today announced that its Virtual Control Group (VCG) database and methodology, aimed at reducing animal use, will be used in an upcoming Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)-compliant study for Ipsen. This collaboration highlights Charles River’s and Ipsen’s dedication and commitment to championing the 3Rs (Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement of animal use in research) while upholding the highest scientific standards. Charles River’s VCG program operates under the Alternative Methods Advancement Project™ (AMAP™), an initiative aimed at minimizing animal use in research whenever scientifically appropriate.
“This partnership exemplifies Charles River’s scientific leadership and commitment to modernizing our company and the industry,” said Dr. Namandjé N. Bumpus , Chief Scientific and Innovation Officer, Charles River. “By advancing VCGs, we are driving innovation for safety studies and reducing animal use where scientifically appropriate.”
By combining toxicology and regulatory expertise, historical control data, advanced statistical methods, and AI-powered analytics, VCGs can digitally replace a portion of concurrent control animals in safety studies. This approach lessens reliance on animal use while enhancing data clarity, offering a modern, ethical, and scientifically robust solution for developers seeking efficient decision-making. Charles River will supply VCG data to Ipsen to facilitate prospective analysis of general toxicology endpoints.
Advancing Virtual Control Groups 
Virtual Control Groups may be able to impact study timelines, enhance data quality, and meet evolving regulatory expectations for the 3Rs .
Up to 12% reduction in animal use where scientifically appropriate, without compromising regulatory-grade rigor
Greater statistical power, particularly for detecting rare spontaneous findings that may otherwise obscure study outcomes
More consistent interpretation, leveraging large, curated historical datasets to contextualize unexpected results
As Charles River continues to advance innovative approaches through AMAP, collaborations like this demonstrate how science, technology, and expertise can work together to reduce animal use while maintaining the rigorous standards required to bring new therapies to patients.
About the Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP)
The Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP) is a Charles River-led initiative dedicated to developing New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and exploring innovative scientific and technological solutions aimed at reducing reliance on traditional animal testing. As we enter the next frontier of drug development, AMAP enables strategic, purpose-driven investment to shape a future in which more patients can access the treatments and medicines they need safely, swiftly, and successfully. AMAP is supported by our global, cross-functional Scientific Advisory Board led by Dr. Namandjé N. Bumpus .
About Charles River
Charles River provides essential products and services to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies and leading academic institutions around the globe accelerate their research and drug development efforts. Our dedicated employees are focused on providing clients with exactly what they need to improve and expedite the discovery, early-stage development and safe manufacture of new therapies for the patients who need them. To learn more about our unique portfolio and breadth of services, visit www.criver.com .

title: Stereolabs Launches ZED Box 2 Series for Physical AI and Vision in Production Robots
query: https://investors.ouster.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Stereolabs Launches ZED Box 2 Series for Physical AI and Vision in Production Robots
October 27, 2026
PDF Version 
The high-performance edge AI series brings up to 2070 TFLOPS of compute, innovative cooling, and native support for up to 8 synchronized GMSL2 cameras for 360° multi-view perception. 
PARIS --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 27, 2026--
Stereolabs , an Ouster, Inc. company and leader in 3D AI vision, today introduced the ZED Box 2 Series, a new generation of industrial edge AI computers engineered for autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), robot vision, and spatial AI systems requiring high-throughput multi-camera perception and edge processing.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261027977847/en/ 
Stereolabs ZED Box 2 with 4 ZED X stereo cameras and 4 ZED X One S connected
ZED Box 2 Max takes vision AI computing to the next level. Powered by NVIDIA® Jetson Thor™ with up to 2,070 FP4 TFLOPS and 128 GB of memory, ZED Box 2 Max is built to run generative AI, vision-language-action (VLA) models and multi-sensor fusion directly on the robot, enabling advanced perception and real-time decision-making at the edge.
Robots are moving from pilots to fleets, and each machine now carries multiple cameras and sensors. At that scale, the interface is a key aspect: GMSL2 has become the interface of choice for robot vision due to its low latency and reliability. Additionally, robotics teams want a complete system instead of separate components: AI compute, hardware synchronized sensors, and software that keeps working release after release.
"Robot vision shouldn’t take five suppliers," said Edwin Azzam , CTO and co-founder of Stereolabs. “With ZED Box 2 Series, we provide robotics developers with the unified compute, cameras, lidar, and perception software that come from one team that tests them together and stands behind all of it. Plug in your cameras and you can have reliable 360° perception in minutes, not weeks."
Up to 8x Cameras for Full Surround Perception 
Designed for complex visual environments where a single stereo sensor is insufficient, the ZED Box 2 Series natively supports up to eight GMSL2 camera inputs via dual Quad Fakra-Z connectors. This enables integration of up to eight ZED X cameras for full 360-degree surround vision, multi-angle robotic cell manipulation, and multi-sensor fusion with high resolution digital lidar.
To ensure accurate temporal alignment across high-speed camera streams, the ZED Box 2 Series features hardware-level frame synchronization via a dedicated SYNC + IO interface, supporting internal synchronization and external trigger modes across multiple devices. Capabilities include:
360° perception for AMRs navigating dynamic environments
Multi-view perception for humanoids and manipulation
Large-scale multi-camera video analytics
Robots combining camera vision with lidar and other sensors
Robotic workcells combining viewpoints to eliminate occlusions
Two Models for Different AI Workloads 
Both ZED Box 2 models share the same camera interface and software, but differ in compute and cooling. Powered by NVIDIA Jetson Orin™ NX 16GB with up to 157 TOPS, ZED Box 2 runs neural depth, tracking, and multi-camera fusion in real time from a fanless enclosure only 55 mm tall, small enough to disappear inside an AMR or a robot cell. With the NVIDIA Jetson Thor T4000 or T5000 and up to 2070 FP4 TFLOPS, ZED Box 2 Max runs vision-language-action and foundation models directly on the robot. It adds 10 GbE and extra control I/O for humanoids and larger autonomous machines.
Full Range of I/O for All Robot Needs 
A robot needs more than cameras to understand its environment. It should be able to connect to lidar, GNSS, IMUs, motor controllers, and fleet networks, and keep all its sensors on a common timeline. The ZED Box 2 Series brings connectivity, synchronization and onboard computing together in one compact platform, without extra adapters or custom carrier boards.
The ZED Box 2 Series is built for every sensor in your robot. Both models feature two Gigabit Ethernet ports, HDMI for on-site debugging, and USB 3 for GNSS receivers, external IMUs and peripherals. ZED Box 2 features two CAN bus ports, sync and GPIO. For more demanding systems, ZED Box 2 Max expands connectivity with four CAN bus ports, four USB ports, four PWM outputs for direct actuator control, and a QSFP port providing four 10 GbE links for lidar and other high-bandwidth sensors.
Hardened Design for Robotics 
Housed in a compact, innovative cooled black aluminum enclosure, the ZED Box 2 Series is engineered to operate reliably in harsh environments ranging from -20°C to +50°C. Key hardware specifications include:

Ready-to-Deploy Vision AI Kits 
Both ZED Box models support the ZED X camera family and the same ZED SDK, with ROS 2 and NVIDIA Isaac ROS support.
They ship in segment-ready kits with cameras, cables and mounts defined for each application. Examples include:
AMRs and Robot Cells: surround safety awareness and multi-view tracking
Off-Road and Industrial Machines: rugged GMSL2 cameras and lidar for harsh outdoor duty
Physical AI Data Collection: synchronized multi-sensor capture for training robot foundation models
Humanoids: 360° head and torso perception for data collection and teleop
Availability 
The ZED Box 2 , ZED Box 2 Max - T4000 and ZED Box 2 Max - T5000 are available to order today through the Stereolabs store and authorized global distributors in 256GB, 1TB, and 2TB NVMe SSD configurations. Shipping begins October 2026 for ZED Box 2 and end of November 2026 for ZED Box 2 Max. For complete datasheets, pinout diagrams, and purchasing information, visit www.stereolabs.com .
About Stereolabs 
Stereolabs , a wholly owned subsidiary of Ouster, Inc. (Nasdaq: OUST), is a leader in 3D vision and depth perception for Physical AI. Its ZED camera family and ZED SDK platform provide real-time depth sensing, spatial mapping, and AI-powered object understanding for robotics, industrial automation, and smart spaces.

query: https://www.evonik.com/en/media.html
content_text:
Evonik to showcase new polyurethane additive innovations at PU China 2026
Two global and two Asia debuts supporting foam performance, processing efficiency and customers'
sustainability goals
Broader local portfolio and enhanced supply security for customers in China
Launch of a new visual identity for Evonik Interface & Polyurethane Additives
Under the theme “Beyond the Surface”, Evonik will showcase its latest additive solutions for polyurethane (PU) foams at PU China 2026 in Shanghai from November 3-5. Highlights include two global and two Asia product debuts, reflecting Evonik's ongoing commitment to advancing foam performance, processing efficiency, and to offering more sustainable solutions, including negligible-emission catalysts and lower-GWP (Global Warming Potential) surfactants.
Backed by decades of expertise, Evonik offers a comprehensive portfolio of catalysts, surfactants, release agents, performance additives and specialty amines for a wide range of PU applications. Combining global innovation with local manufacturing, technical expertise and customer support, Evonik helps customers address evolving market and application requirements.
“At PU China 2026, visitors will discover the latest innovations we’ve developed to address evolving industry needs, alongside the global trade fair launch of our new visual identity for our business line,” said Hang Xu, Head of Evonik Interface & Polyurethane Additives in Asia Pacific. “Supported by growing local capabilities, including the expansion of specialty amines production capacity in Nanjing earlier this year, we are well positioned to offer local customers in China and the wider region a broader portfolio, enhanced security of supply and local technical support.”
Evonik’s key innovation highlights at PU China 2026 include:
Rigid foam solutions for efficient thermal insulation: 
Driven by growing demand for energy efficiency, Evonik’s TEGOSTAB® silicone surfactants, together with DABCO® and POLYCAT® amine catalysts, support excellent insulation performance and low-emission processing across appliance, construction and cold chain applications. Advanced catalyst packages for next-generation spray foam systems boost stability and processing efficiency while enabling safer spraying and faster worker re-entry. For rigid foam panels, TEGOSTAB® B 84840 and EP-R-S 81 improve surface quality, reduce voids and lower lambda values for better insulation. In demanding appliance applications, TEGOSTAB® B 84813, B 84841 and B 84851 help improve foam flow, formulation compatibility and thermal performance.
Flexible foam solutions for recovery and hand feel: 
For mattress-in-a-box and specialty comfort foams, Evonik’s additive solutions support consumer expectation for lasting comfort and consistent performance. Making its global debut at the event, TEGOSTAB® B 8273, together with ORTEGOL® 700, improves post-compression recovery in mattress-in-a-box applications. For viscoelastic and molded MDI-based foams, TEGOSTAB® B 8211 and the globally launched B 8292 deliver tailored hand feel, optimized cell structure, low emissions and robust processing stability.
Low-emission and lower carbon footprint for automotive molded foams: 
Advanced additive technologies for automotive interiors support cleaner cabin air. Making their Asia debut, DABCO® NE 1067 Negligible Emission catalyst and DABCO® SI 1218 LO Low-Odor surfactant help foamers meet OEM targets and minimize VOC exposure for workers and consumers. Evonik will also showcase its Low Carbon Footprint (LCF) surfactants, TEGOSTAB® B 8751 LCF and B 8763 LCF, which offer a reduced Global Warming Potential (GWP) compared with conventional surfactants, without compromising foam quality or processing efficiency.
Processing and performance additives for specialized PU applications: 
Evonik offers a broad additive toolbox to optimize processing and performance across specialty PU applications. For coatings, adhesives, sealants and elastomers (CASE), heat-activated, delayed-action catalysts such as POLYCAT® SA 8 and POLYCAT® SA 21 provide targeted reactivity and stable processing, while VERSALINK® diamine curatives extend processing windows and improve mechanical properties. The internal release additives ORTEGOL® IR 3 and IR 5 enable reliable demolding and processing at low use levels in molded and pultruded PU composites for structural profiles, frames, light weight construction and automotive parts.
For more information, visit Evonik’s trade show stand #40 in Hall 1, at the Shanghai World Expo Exhibition and Convention Centre from November 3-5, or visit the links below.

Evonik goes beyond the boundaries of chemistry with its combination of innovative strength and leading technological expertise. The global chemical company, headquartered in Essen, Germany, is active in more than 100 countries and generated sales of €14.1 billion and earnings (adjusted EBITDA) of €1.9 billion in 2025. query: https://corporate.dow.com/en-us/news.html
content_text:
Dow Launches DOWSIL™ IE-5619 Emulsion 
Fluoro-alternative technology for durable water and oil repellency in textiles
Third-generation silicone-organic hybrid technology offers durable water and oil repellency through innovative fluoro-alternative chemistry, helping brands and mills address evolving application requirements. 
MIDLAND, Mich. – October 27, 2026 – Dow (NYSE: DOW) today announced the launch of DOWSIL™ IE-5619 DWOR Emulsion , a durable water and oil repellent (DWOR) agent featuring innovative fluoro-alternative chemistry for the global textile industry. This silicone-organic hybrid technology is designed to offer both water and oil repellency, helping textile chemical formulators, mills and brands address evolving regulatory, environmental and consumer expectations.
Meeting the industry need for fluoro-alternative DWOR solutions 
“For years, achieving meaningful oil repellency in textiles typically required fluorinated chemistries, which are now facing increasing restrictions,” said Juan Carlos Medina, Ph.D., Global Strategic Marketing Director at Dow. “DOWSIL™ IE-5619 helps close that gap with a silicone-based, fluoro-alternative solution that delivers durable water and oil repellency while preserving the softness, breathability and aesthetics consumers expect. It is designed to integrate into existing finishing processes, enabling customers to adopt a fluoro-alternative solution with confidence.”
Key features and benefits of DOWSIL™ IE-5619 DWOR Emulsion
DOWSIL™ IE-5619 is 30% solids concentrate designed for conventional textile finishing. It is effective across a range of fabrics including synthetic, natural, and blended fibers (performance must be confirmed for each fabric type and source).
Key benefits include:
Dual repellency: Helps repel oil-based contaminants such as olive oil, cooking oils, motor oil and sebum, while also providing protection against common water-based stains such as wine, coffee and milk.
Fluoro-alternative chemistry: Silicone-organic hybrid polymer technology developed to offer durable water and oil repellency for textile applications.
Durable performance: Designed to maintain water and oil repellency after 20+ home laundering cycles (results depend on fabric and formulation).
Comfort and aesthetics: Offers a soft hand feel, helps preserve breathability, and supports tape and logo adhesion without the need for additional surface treatments.
Easy integration: Compatible with current manufacturing processes; typical use levels are 1–3% based on the weight of the fabric, with 1–3 minutes curing at 150°C minimum and can be optimized to customer-specific processes and performance targets.
Availability and how to engage 
DOWSIL™ IE-5619 DWOR Emulsion is sold globally across the textile supply chain including textile chemical formulators, mills, and brands. Dow will work with customers to understand application needs and support product validation on specific fabrics and finishing lines.
To learn more about DOWSIL™ IE-5619 DWOR Emulsion or request a sample, contact your Dow representative or reach out through Dow Customer Support.
About Dow 
Dow (NYSE: DOW) is one of the world’s leading materials science companies, serving customers in high-growth markets such as packaging, infrastructure, mobility and consumer applications. Our global breadth, asset integration and scale, focused innovation, leading business positions and commitment to sustainability enable us to achieve profitable growth and help deliver a sustainable future. We operate manufacturing sites in 30 countries and employ approximately 36,000 people. Dow delivered sales of approximately $43 billion in 2024. References to Dow or the Company mean Dow Inc. and its subsidiaries. Learn more about us and our ambition to be the most innovative, customer-centric, inclusive and sustainable materials science company in the world by visiting dow.com .

Non-GAAP Measures Disclosures 
We supplement the reporting of our financial information determined under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles in the United States of America (GAAP) with certain non-GAAP financial information. The non-GAAP financial information presented excludes certain significant items that may not be indicative of, or are unrelated to, results from our ongoing business operations. We believe that these non-GAAP measures provide investors with additional insight into the company's ongoing business performance. These non-GAAP measures should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the related GAAP measures, and other companies may define such measures differently. We encourage investors to review our financial statements and publicly-filed reports in their entirety and not to rely on any single financial measure. The following definitions are provided:
Core Operating Earnings/(Loss), Core Operating Margins and Core Earnings/(Loss) Per Share 
Core operating earnings/(loss) is defined as GAAP Earnings/( l oss) from operations excluding the FAS/CAS service cost adjustment. The FAS/CAS service cost adjustment represents the difference between the Financial Accounting Standards (FAS) pension and postretirement service costs calculated under GAAP and costs allocated to the business segments. Core operating margins is defined as Core operating earnings/(loss) expressed as a percentage of revenue. Core earnings/(loss) per share is defined as GAAP Diluted earnings/(loss) per share excluding the net earnings/(loss) per share impact of the FAS/CAS service cost adjustment and Non-operating pension and postretirement expenses . Non-operating pension and postretirement expenses represent the components of net periodic benefit costs other than service cost. Pension costs allocated to BDS and BGS businesses supporting government customers are computed in accordance with U.S. Government Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), which employ different actuarial assumptions and accounting conventions than GAAP. CAS costs are allocable to government contracts. Other postretirement benefit costs are allocated to all business segments based on CAS, which is generally based on benefits paid. Management uses core operating earnings/(loss), core operating margins and core earnings/(loss) per share for purposes of evaluating and forecasting underlying business performance. Management believes these core measures provide investors additional insights into operational performance as they exclude non-service pension and post-retirement costs, which primarily represent costs driven by market factors and costs not allocable to government contracts. A reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measure is provided on page 12.
Free Cash Flow 
Free cash flow is GAAP operating cash flow reduced by capital expenditures for property, plant and equipment . Management believes free cash flow provides investors with an important perspective on the cash available for shareholders, debt repayment, and acquisitions after making the capital investments required to support ongoing business operations and long term value creation. Free cash flow does not represent the residual cash flow available for discretionary expenditures as it excludes certain mandatory expenditures such as repayment of maturing debt. Management uses free cash flow as a measure to assess both business performance and overall liquidity. See Table 2 on page 2 for a reconciliation of free cash flow to the most directly comparable GAAP measure, operating cash flow.

27 Oct 2026 
Applied Materials to Increase its Strategic Investment in BE Semiconductor Industries
Duiven, the Netherlands, October 27, 2026 - BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. (the “Company” or “Besi”) (Euronext Amsterdam: BESI; OTC markets: BESIY), a leading manufacturer of assembly equipment for the semiconductor industry, acknowledged today the press release from Applied Materials, Inc. (“Applied”) in which Applied announced on October 26, 2026, an increase in its strategic share ownership to approximately 20% of Besi’s outstanding shares. 
According to Applied’s press release, Applied views its investment in Besi as long-term. Applied does not intend to seek board representation at Besi, nor does it currently have plans to purchase additional shares of Besi.
Besi and Applied have collaborated together since 2020 on the development and commercialization of integrated hybrid bonding production systems for leading semiconductor manufacturers. The collaboration brings together Applied’s expertise in front-end manufacturing and Besi’s leading technologies in die placement, interconnect and assembly solutions. Recently, the companies have expanded their collaboration with Besi joining Applied’s EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner. Areas of collaboration target next-generation 3D IC scaling, logic and memory integration, the scaling of thermo-compression bonding and new die-on-wafer, die-on-die and die-on-panel integration platforms.
Richard W. Blickman, Besi’s Chief Executive Officer, commented :
“We welcome Applied’s increased strategic investment as further confirmation of Besi’s hybrid bonding and wafer-level assembly strategy. It also highlights future areas of potential collaboration between the companies targeting next generation AI and photonics systems for the industry’s leading customers.”

BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. Announces Q3-2026 Results
Q3-26 Revenue and Net Income of € 283.4 Million and € 107.2 Million Up 113.6% and 323.7%, Respectively, vs. Q3-25. Orders of € 342.6 million Up 17.0% vs. Q2-26 and 96.1% vs. Q3-25. YTD-26 Revenue and Net Income Up 69.0% and 179.1%, Respectively, vs. YTD-25. YTD-26 Hybrid Bonding Orders More than Doubled Vs. Fiscal 2025. Total Cumulative Unit Demand Exceeds 215 Systems. New € 100 Million Share Repurchase Program Initiated
Duiven, the Netherlands, October 22, 2026 - BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. (the “Company" or "Besi") (Euronext Amsterdam: BESI; OTC markets: BESIY), a leading manufacturer of assembly equipment for the semiconductor industry, today announced its results for the third quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026.
Key Highlights Q3-26
Revenue of € 283.4 million increased by € 33.5 million, or 13.4%, vs. Q2-26 due primarily to increased shipments for datacenter and AI related mainstream computing applications. Up € 150.7 million or 113.6% vs. Q3-25 primarily due to growth in computing end markets with strength in hybrid bonding, photonics and datacenter applications
Orders of € 342.6 million increased by € 49.7 million, or 17.0%, vs. Q2-26 and € 167.9 million or 96.1%, vs. Q3-25 primarily due to increased orders for hybrid bonding, datacenter and AI related mainstream computing applications
Besi’s gross margin of 65.2% decreased by 0.5 points vs. Q2-26 but was above prior guidance. It increased 3.0 points vs. Q3-25 due primarily to a more favorable product mix and price increases
Net income of € 107.2 million increased by 20.4% vs. Q2-26 and 323.7% vs. Q3-25 due to higher revenue levels and disciplined expense management. Similarly, Besi’s net margin increased to 37.8% vs. 35.6% in Q2-26 and 19.0% in Q3-25
Net cash of € 246.6 million at September 30, 2026, increased by € 82.6 million vs. June 30, 2026, principally due to increased profitability and cash flow from operations
Key Highlights YTD-26
Revenue of € 718.1 million increased by € 293.1 million, or 69.0%, vs. YTD-25 primarily due to broad-based growth in computing end markets and, to a lesser extent, an increase in mobile shipments.  Growth in computing end markets principally resulted from increased demand for photonics and datacenter applications and, to a lesser extent, hybrid bonding and mainstream electronics demand
Orders of € 905.2 million rose € 470.6 million, or 108.3%, vs. YTD-25 due to growth across all end-user markets with strength in hybrid bonding, photonics and datacenter applications
Besi’s gross margin of 64.9% increased by 1.8 points vs. YTD-25 primarily due to a more favorable product mix and the pass through of price increases to help offset higher supply chain costs
Net income of € 247.8 million increased by € 159.0 million, or 179.1%, vs. YTD-25 primarily due to significantly higher revenue, higher gross margins and cost control efforts which limited operating expense development. Similarly, Besi’s net margin increased to 34.5% vs. 20.9% in YTD-25
Q4-26 Outlook  
Revenue expected to be flat to +/-5% vs. the € 283.4 million in Q3-26 as certain customers request delivery dates for Q3-26 orders in alignment with H1-27 production capacity plans
Gross margin expected to range between 63-65% vs. the 65.2% realized in Q3-26
Operating expenses expected to increase by 5-10% vs. the € 55.1 million reported in Q3-26 due primarily to higher strategic consulting costs

Infineon introduces power distribution board reference design to simplify evaluation of 800 V AI power systems
Technology news
Oct 27, 2026 
Munich, Germany – 27 October 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) is introducing its High-Voltage Power Distribution Board (HV PDB), a complete reference design for next-generation power supply architectures in AI data centers. The reference board allows customers to evaluate ±400 V and 800 V power distribution systems and accelerate their deployment. As a system-level platform, the HV PDB integrates high-voltage protection, intermediate bus conversion, power regulation and telemetry management onto a single board. This enables designers to reduce development complexity and time-to-market while gaining valuable insights into system efficiency, protection behavior and power orchestration. The platform is designed for high-voltage power supply architectures in AI server racks.
With a footprint of 480 × 125 mm², the HV PDB supports both ±400 V and 800 V distribution architectures and delivers an output power of up to 12 kW. It includes input fuses, a dual hot-swap module, EMI filtering, two 6 kW high-voltage IBC modules (±400 V to 50 V) and two regulated 2.5 kW IBC modules (48 V to 12 V). The dual hot-swap module supports up to 32 kW and provides safe startup, fault isolation, telemetry monitoring and system protection. Fully gallium nitride (GaN)-based HV IBC modules achieve a peak efficiency of up to 98.5 percent, followed by regulated 12 V conversion stages. The dedicated MCU board manager based on the PSOC™ 3 handles telemetry, system monitoring and intelligent energy management. In addition, the platform combines Infineon’s silicon, silicon carbide (SiC), and GaN technologies in a complete high-voltage power conversion solution for next-generation AI servers and data centers.
The HV PDB also serves as a flexible evaluation platform, allowing developers to operate the entire power chain or isolate individual stages for architectural studies. Telemetry and PMBus connectivity enable system-level monitoring and coordination, while a PSOC evaluation board interface allows developers to implement custom firmware. Alternative IBC modules, EMI filter configurations and power management approaches can also be evaluated. This modular approach provides insights into the startup sequence, fault behavior and overall system performance. The HV PDB is designed to accommodate industry-standard half-brick HV IBC and quarter-brick MV IBC power converter modules with standardized pinouts, providing customers with the flexibility to use alternative, drop-in compatible solutions according to their specific system requirements.
Availability 
Infineon’s high-voltage power distribution board will be available in November 2026 and showcased at electronica 2026 in Munich from November 10 to 13 (hall C3, booth 502).
More information is available at http://www.infineon.com/ibc .
About Infineon
Infineon Technologies AG is a global semiconductor leader in power systems and IoT. Infineon drives decarbonization and digitalization with its products and solutions. The Company had around 57,000 employees worldwide (end of September 2025) and generated revenue of about €14.7 billion in the 2025 fiscal year (ending 30 September). Infineon is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: IFX) and in the USA on the OTCQX International over-the-counter market (ticker symbol: IFNNY).

Infineon introduces LinearFET technology for automotive power distribution applications
Technology news
Oct 27, 2026 
Munich, Germany – 27 October 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) has launched LinearFET, a new MOSFET technology that enables automotive manufacturers to simplify the design of next-generation solid-state power distribution systems for electric and software-defined vehicles. By integrating solutions for current sharing, inrush current control, and short-circuit robustness directly at the device level, LinearFET removes key technical barriers that have limited the broader adoption of solid-state power distribution architectures in modern vehicles.
As vehicles become increasingly electrified and software-defined, traditional power distribution architectures are reaching their limits. Engineers designing modern power distribution systems face three persistent challenges: safely paralleling MOSFETs to scale current capability, controlling high inrush currents during capacitor charging, and ensuring robust operation during short-circuit events. Addressing these typically requires additional circuitry, complex control strategies, or over-dimensioned components, increasing system complexity, board space, cost, and development effort.
LinearFET addresses all three directly at the MOSFET level: it enables predictable current sharing when paralleling MOSFETs for scalable high-current designs, provides controlled charging of large capacitive loads without external limiters, and delivers enhanced short-circuit robustness to help meet demanding automotive safety requirements. By incorporating these capabilities into the power device, LinearFET simplifies system design while improving robustness and safety.
The technology is suited for applications including power distribution units, battery disconnect switches, solid-state fuse systems, and zonal power architectures. It enables automotive designers to implement more compact and cost-efficient systems with significantly lower implementation complexity while maintaining high reliability and safety standards, supporting the industry's transition from conventional fuse-box architectures toward software-controlled networks required in future electric and software-defined vehicles.

title: Infineon introduces ENDOPACK™ chip-embedding platform for scalable traction inverter development Technology news Oct 27, 2026

content_text:
Infineon introduces ENDOPACK™ chip-embedding platform for scalable traction inverter development
Technology news
Oct 27, 2026 
Munich, Germany – 27 October 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) has introduced ENDOPACK™, a new brand for advanced chip-embedding solutions, available across a broad range of voltage classes, form factors, and applications. Building on years of successful low-voltage chip-embedding production, Infineon is now extending the technology to high-voltage power electronics. ENDOPACK Cell is the industry's first automotive-qualified, high-voltage chip-embedding solution designed for PCB integration. With 1200 V Automotive Gen2p CoolSiC™ MOSFET technology built directly into the board, it enables automotive manufacturers to develop traction inverters faster and scale them across vehicle platforms through greater design flexibility and reuse, while improving efficiency, power density, and semiconductor utilization.
As vehicle development cycles continue to shorten, automotive manufacturers face sustained cost pressure and the need to meet increasing efficiency and power density requirements while reusing architectures across multiple vehicle programs. Most importantly, they require technologies that enable them to develop and scale traction inverters significantly faster. Traditional architectures often require developing new designs for each application or power class, limiting flexibility and slowing deployment. ENDOPACK Cell addresses these challenges by leveraging standardized PCB design processes and proven manufacturing infrastructure, enabling development cycles up to three times faster than conventional solutions. In addition, it can be seamlessly transferred to a production line that remains entirely design-agnostic, enabling rapid iteration without the need to continuously adapt manufacturing processes.
Instead of placing power semiconductors on top of a substrate, ENDOPACK Cell is embedded directly in the PCB structure, combining advanced semiconductor performance with the flexibility and mature manufacturing ecosystem of PCB technology. The architecture enables a reduced inductance below 2 nH compared to 20 nH, enabling 30 percent lower switching losses and approximately 99.5 percent efficiency under CLTC conditions. Prototype and simulation data indicate up to 200 kW/L peak power density with the potential at vehicle-level to improve the vehicle range by 7 percent.
One of the most important advantages of ENDOPACK Cell is the resulting design freedom. Chip quantity and placement can be adapted to power requirements and installation space, while geometry is no longer largely determined by fixed module housing. Multiple cells can be integrated into a single PCB, allowing the power stage to be configured according to the performance and architecture requirements of specific vehicle platforms. This approach reduces engineering effort and allows a common design to be reused across platform generations.
ENDOPACK represents Infineon's new category trademark for advanced PCB chip-embedding technologies, providing a scalable foundation that helps automotive manufacturers bring new inverter platforms to market faster while supporting long-term platform scalability, design flexibility, and cost-efficient reuse across vehicle generations.
Availability 
ENDOPACK CELL is ready for mass production. Vehicles powered by ENDOPACK Cell are planned to enter mass production in 2027. Further information is available at www.infineon.com/endopack .

Asahi Kasei has announced that the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has issued a ruling in favor of Koki Ikeda, a member of the company’s athletic team.
Ikeda, a competitive race walker, had been suspected of blood doping, the practice of storing one’s own blood for subsequent autotransfusion to raise performance. On February 14, 2025, the Disciplinary Tribunal of World Athletics sanctioned Ikeda with a 4-year period of ineligibility to compete, as well as nullification of his results and forfeiture of his medals dating from June 20, 2023. Certain of his innocence, Asahi Kasei supported Ikeda’s appeal to CAS.
In its ruling, CAS recognized the validity of Ikeda’s physiological and medical arguments underpinned by substantial evidence. The ruling overturned the sanctions of the Disciplinary Tribunal, restoring his former results and medals, and allowing him to resume competition immediately.
“It’s extremely gratifying to have my innocence recognized at last,” said Ikeda. “I’m deeply grateful to everyone who continued to believe in me, and never stopped lending me their generous support. I look forward to resuming competition so I can repay my debt of gratitude with results.”
Asahi Kasei has stated that it fully supports valid measures to ensure the integrity of international athletic competition, including the elimination of all forms of doping. The company believes that athletes erroneously accused of wrongdoing must be afforded adequate procedures to establish their innocence without being unduly sanctioned.

Applied Materials to Increase its Strategic Investment in BE Semiconductor Industries
Oct 26, 2026 at 4:30 PM EDT
PDF Version 
Applied enters into agreement to increase its investment to approximately 20 percent of outstanding shares, reinforcing the companies’ long-term strategic partnership in advanced packaging 
SANTA CLARA, Calif. , Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) today announced it is increasing its investment in BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. (Besi) ( Euronext Amsterdam : BESI), a leading manufacturer of assembly equipment for the semiconductor industry, to approximately 20 percent of Besi’s outstanding shares. The share purchase would add to Applied Materials’ current investment in Besi, which Applied initially made in April 2025 .
The companies have a longstanding strategic collaboration, which began in 2020 and was recently expanded with Besi joining Applied Materials’ EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner. The expanded partnership extends the companies’ co-innovation beyond hybrid bonding into new interconnect architectures and applications supporting the semiconductor industry’s AI-driven scaling roadmap. Areas of collaboration include next-generation 3D IC scaling, logic and memory integration, scaling of thermo-compression bonding and new die-on-wafer, die-on-die and die-on-panel integration platforms.
“Applied Materials is adding to its investment in Besi as hybrid bonding technology and next-generation interconnect architectures become increasingly critical enablers of energy-efficient AI compute performance,” said Dr. Prabu Raja , President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “We also look forward to furthering our strategic collaboration with Besi and delivering the innovative products and technologies our customers need to scale AI systems.”
Applied Materials has entered into an accelerated share purchase agreement for the Besi shares, and the delivery of the shares is subject to the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the HSR Act).
Applied Materials views its investment in Besi as long term. Applied currently has no intention to increase its investment in Besi beyond approximately 20 percent, and Applied does not intend to seek board representation at Besi.
Forward-Looking Statements 
This press release contains forward-looking statements regarding the purchase of Besi shares by Applied Materials. These statements and their underlying assumptions are subject to risks and uncertainties. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements include the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the HSR Act and the risks and uncertainties described in our filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including our most recent Forms 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K. All forward-looking statements are based on management’s current estimates, projections and assumptions, and we assume no obligation to update them.
About Applied Materials 
Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) is the leader in materials engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor and advanced display in the world. The technology we create is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation chips. At Applied, we push the boundaries of science and engineering to deliver material innovation that changes the world. Learn more at www.appliedmaterials.com .

title: Volkswagen Group strengthens its strategic semiconductor ecosystem through partnership with NXP
query: https://media.nxp.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Volkswagen Group Strengthens its Strategic Semiconductor Ecosystem Through Partnership with NXP
October 26, 2026
10:00 AM CET (UTC+1)
by NXP Semiconductors 
Press Release 
Share 
Twitter 
LinkedIn 
Facebook 
Volkswagen Group and NXP Semiconductors, one of the world’s leading automotive semiconductor companies, are expanding their cooperation in automotive semiconductor technology
NXP has been selected as a strategic technology partner, providing its microcontrollers (MCUs) as a common building block for Group’s future zonal software-defined vehicle architecture
Common MCU technology reduces complexity and supports scalable deployment across brands and vehicle segments
Wolfsburg, October 26, 2026 – Volkswagen Group and NXP Semiconductors today announced ahead of the International Suppliers Fair (IZB) in Wolfsburg that they had agreed on a strategic partnership. NXP’s S32K5 family of microcontrollers (MCUs) is intended to serve as an important building block of Volkswagen Group’s future software-defined vehicle (SDV) architecture, supporting zonal control across all brands and vehicle segments. The first vehicle featuring the new architecture is planned for 2027.
Modern vehicles must support a growing number of digital functions. Managing these functions through separate electronic control units (ECUs) increases complexity in development and parts management and limits scalability. Zonal architecture addresses this challenge by using powerful microcontrollers to consolidate multiple vehicle functions into fewer ECUs.
Next to high-performance processors that provide the central computing power and make complex decisions for AI-enabled functions such as automated driving and advanced infotainment, the S32K5 MCUs serve as the core processors of the vehicle's zonal controllers. They connect sensors and actuators, collect and process data from specific areas of the vehicle, and manage functions such as lighting, body, comfort, chassis and safety systems. These capabilities provide the foundation for the central computing platform to run AI algorithms and perform advanced functions.
NXP’s S32K5 MCUs enable functions that previously required separate chips and ECUs to be consolidated within zonal controllers, reducing hardware complexity. They are intended to serve as a common building block for the future zonal SDV architecture developed by Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies, LLC (RV Tech), the joint venture between Volkswagen Group and Rivian. The architecture is intended to be used across both companies’ vehicles, enabling brand-specific features and experiences.
The partnership is part of Volkswagen Group’s broader semiconductor strategy. Through direct, long-term partnerships with leading semiconductor companies, Volkswagen Group combines its automotive expertise with cutting-edge chip technology to strengthen supply resilience and jointly shape key technologies for future vehicle generations. The approach supports the Group Target Picture 2030 and aims to leverage synergies across brands and regions and harmonize key technologies.
“Semiconductors are strategic technology for the automotive industry. Over the past years, we have systematically expanded our technology ecosystem and built partnerships with leading companies across the value chain. Our partnership with NXP is another step in this journey, showing how Volkswagen Group is taking a more active role in the semiconductor value chain: defining our technology needs early, leveraging our scale across brands and creating greater long-term planning certainty for both sides.”
Karsten Schnake, Member of the Extended Executive Committee and Member of the Volkswagen Brand Board of Management responsible for Procurement 
“Our future zonal architecture, developed by RV Tech and supported by strategic technology partners such as NXP, creates a scalable technology foundation for multiple Group brands and vehicle segments. By harmonizing key technologies across the Group, we reduce complexity, leverage scale and accelerate innovation while enabling advanced digital capabilities. This allows us to bring digital innovations to our customers faster and continuously enhance our vehicles throughout their lifecycle.”
Werner Tietz, Member of the Extended Volkswagen Group Executive Committee responsible for Group Research and Development 
“Intelligent, software-defined vehicles must operate safely, securely and reliably. Together with Volkswagen Group and RV Tech, NXP is bringing scalable real-time compute, trusted edge intelligence and continuous software innovation together to create a scalable foundation for the next generation of intelligent vehicles.”
Rafael Sotomayor, President and CEO, NXP Semiconductors 
“Software-defined differentiation is the new auto benchmark, and NXP is excited that the S32K5 family of MCUs has been adopted into RV Tech’s innovative new zonal architecture, one of the most sophisticated approaches to streamlined development and differentiating features in the automotive industry today. As a core processor for the vehicle’s zonal controllers, S32K5 is built for safe real-time compute, fast and secure OTA updates and the consolidation of functions that together create a basis for a flexible, continuously updateable vehicle.”
Lars Reger, Executive Vice President and CTO, NXP Semiconductors 
About NXP Semiconductors
NXP Semiconductors N.V. (NASDAQ: NXPI) is the trusted partner for innovative solutions in the automotive, industrial & IoT, mobile, and communications infrastructure markets. NXP's "Brighter Together" approach combines leading-edge technology with pioneering people to develop system solutions that make the connected world better, safer, and more secure. The company has operations in more than 30 countries and posted revenue of $12.27 billion in 2025. Find out more at www.nxp.com .
