title: Infineon to establish the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for gallium nitride power semiconductors on 300-millimeter wafers in Europe Business & Financial Press Oct 27, 2026
query: https://www.infineon.com/about/press
content_text:
Infineon to establish the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for gallium nitride power semiconductors on 300-millimeter wafers in Europe
Business & Financial Press
Oct 27, 2026 
Investment of around €1.1 billion in the Villach site as a global competence center for power semiconductors 
Next-generation power semiconductors to meet growing demand for energy-efficient chips, including AI data centers, energy infrastructure, e-mobility and robotics 
Ramp-up aligned with market demand 
€319 million in funding under the European Chips Act to strengthen technological sovereignty 
Munich, Germany/Vienna, Austria – 27 October 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG is establishing the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for next-generation gallium nitride (GaN) power semiconductors on 300-millimeter wafers in Europe. As part of the project, Infineon will invest around €1.1 billion in its existing cleanroom facilities at the Villach site by 2034. Leveraging both the existing and upgraded infrastructure will enable highly efficient and cost-effective expansion of manufacturing capacity. Production is scheduled to start by the end of 2027. Infineon’s investment addresses the rapidly growing demand for high-performance power supply solutions. Gallium nitride enables significant efficiency gains in numerous applications, such as AI data centers, energy infrastructure, e-mobility, robotics and consumer electronics.
Infineon is a leader in gallium nitride power electronics. Two years ago, Infineon achieved a technological milestone by successfully processing the world’s first 300-millimeter gallium nitride wafers. Chip production on 300-millimeter wafers is more advanced and significantly more efficient than 200-millimeter wafer production, since the larger wafer diameter yields 2.3 times as many chips per wafer. Infineon is now transferring this technology to the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility serving customers.
“This substantial investment shows our clear commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem and Europe’s technological sovereignty. By establishing high-volume manufacturing on 300-millimeter wafers, we will be the first company in the world to bring gallium nitride power electronics into volume production,” says Jochen Hanebeck, CEO of Infineon Technologies AG . “In doing so, we are paving the way for the widespread use of gallium nitride in a wide range of key applications in areas such as artificial intelligence, energy infrastructure, e-mobility and robotics. This new, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility translates innovation leadership into direct customer benefits.”
Christian Stocker, Federal Chancellor of the Republic of Austria: “With Infineon’s billion-euro investment, we are witnessing one of the largest single investments in the history of Austria’s high-tech industry. This is not only a strong commitment to Austria as a business location but also helps ensure that the future of the semiconductor industry will not be shaped solely in Asia or the United States, but also in Austria and Europe. Villach will thus become home to a globally unique production facility for one of the key technologies that will shape the future. This will strengthen our international competitiveness and secure jobs and value creation in Austria. After all, Austria may not be a country with unlimited natural resources, but it is a country with an unlimited wealth of talent. Our cutting-edge research sets international standards, and companies such as Infineon demonstrate every day how innovation made in Austria works. These are precisely the strengths we want to build on with our industrial strategy so that, by 2035, Austria will once again rank among the world’s top ten industrial nations.”
Wolfgang Hattmannsdorfer, Austrian Federal Minister for Economic Affairs: “Chips are as important to tomorrow’s economy as oil was to yesterday’s. Europe currently accounts for only around 10 percent of global chip production. For me, the conclusion is clear: We must also manufacture this key technology in Europe. Austria is already a leader in energy-efficient chips. Relative to our population, we rank first in the EU in business R&D spending in the semiconductor sector. With our industrial strategy, we intend to build on this lead and not only research new technologies but also manufacture them on an industrial scale. This benefits the entire economy: Statistically, every job in the chip industry can provide six additional jobs across the broader economy. That is why we intend to support Infineon’s new chip production with up to 319 million euros - subject to clear funding criteria for the location. This will ensure that public funds strengthen value creation and jobs in Austria over the long term.”
The investment in this first-of-a-kind technology is being supported under the European Chips Act. The European Commission approved €319 million in state aid. The formal funding commitment by the Austrian Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism is expected within the stipulated time limits. By approving the funding from the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism, the European Commission is not only enabling the expansion of manufacturing capacities in Europe but is also generating positive spillover effects in related sectors – for example, through cross-border collaboration with universities and research institutions and improved access to innovative technologies and products for start-ups and small and medium-sized enterprises.
“Competitiveness and technological sovereignty emerge where excellent research is translated into industrial value creation. This is precisely where our flagship project comes in: From Austria, we are bringing innovation into industrial application, strengthening our technological leadership and securing highly skilled jobs. Microelectronics is a key industry with enormous leverage for the economy and society. The entire Austrian semiconductor ecosystem benefits – from research organizations and universities to industrial partners. We are thus sustainably strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and strategic autonomy in microelectronics,” emphasizes Sabine Herlitschka, CEO of Infineon Technologies Austria AG. 
The investment strengthens Villach’s role as a global competence center for power electronics and new semiconductor materials. Infineon Austria currently employs around 5,800 people, approximately 4,800 of them at the Villach[1] site. Together with universities, research institutions, start-ups and industry partners, Infineon forms the core of an internationally recognized microelectronics ecosystem in southern Austria. The establishment of the new 300-millimeter GaN manufacturing facility will also create positive synergies with the power electronics research and development activities located in Villach.
Gallium nitride is an advanced semiconductor material that can switch and convert electricity much more efficiently. This enables smaller, more powerful and more energy-efficient electronic systems with lower energy loss and reduced heat generation. Analysts expect the market for GaN power semiconductors to grow to approximately USD 3.5 billion by 2031, representing annual growth of around 35 percent between 2025 and 2031.[2]
[1] Fiscal year 2025, as of September 30, 2025
[2] Yole Group: Power GaN 2026 report. https://www.yolegroup.com/product/report/power-gan-2026/ 
Images from the press briefing will be available here starting at approximately 9:15 a.m. CET: https://www.apa-fotoservice.at/galerie/40217 
About Infineon
Infineon Technologies AG is a global semiconductor leader in power systems and IoT. Infineon drives decarbonization and digitalization with its products and solutions. The Company had around 57,000 employees worldwide (end of September 2025) and generated revenue of about €14.7 billion in the 2025 fiscal year (ending 30 September). Infineon is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: IFX) and in the USA on the OTCQX International over-the-counter market (ticker symbol: IFNNY).

title: Syensqo recognized by Avio with Raw Material Supplier Award
source: Syensqo - Press Releases (Press Release Finder distribution)
query: https://www.pressreleasefinder.com/Syensqo/
content_text:
Syensqo recognized by Avio with Raw Material Supplier Award
Recognition highlights Syensqo's strategic partnership with Avio and its contribution to advanced space and defence programs
 
Brussels, October 26, 2026 - Syensqo has been recognized by Avio with an award in the Raw Material supplier category during its supplier day event, held on October 15, 2026, at Avio's facility in Colleferro, Italy.
The award highlights Syensqo's role as a strategic supplier to Avio across its space and defence activities, recognizing the strength of the companies' longstanding partnership and their shared commitment to quality, reliability and innovation.
The recognition follows the announcement in April 2026 of a new long-term supply agreement between Syensqo and Avio, further reinforcing their collaboration in advanced materials for demanding aerospace and defence applications.
 Syensqo supplies high-performance ablative materials, resin transfer molding (RTM) resins and adhesives for Avio's space launch programs, including Vega-C, as well as defence applications. Engineered to withstand extreme thermal and mechanical stresses, these materials are used in critical components such as rocket motor nozzles, exit cones and structural elements.
"Receiving this recognition from Avio is a great honor and a testament to the dedication of our teams and the strength of our longstanding partnership. We are proud to contribute our advanced materials expertise to Avio's programs and remain committed to supporting the next generation of space launch systems." Rodrigo Elizondo, President of Syensqo Composite Materials.

title: New data on Lilly's investigational treatment olomorasib at ESMO 2026 show durable first-line activity in KRAS G12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer
source: Eli Lilly and Company - Official RSS
query: https://investor.lilly.com/rss.xml
content_text:
New data on Lilly's investigational treatment olomorasib at ESMO 2026 show durable first-line activity in KRAS G12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer
October 25, 2026
PDF Version 
Data presented at ESMO highlight the promising efficacy of olomorasib in combination with standard-of-care immunotherapy with or without chemotherapy in first-line advanced KRAS G12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) across PD-L1 expression levels 
First-line treatment options remain an unmet need for patients with KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC, as most patients do not receive second-line therapy due to the aggressive nature of the disease 
Lilly expects first randomized Phase 3 data from SUNRAY-01 in first-line KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC in the first half of 2027 
INDIANAPOLIS , Oct. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced new first-line data on olomorasib, its investigational, next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor, at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress in Madrid, Spain . Results shared in a poster presentation from the Phase 1/2 LOXO-RAS-20001 trial and the safety lead-in portion of the Phase 3 SUNRAY-01 trial of olomorasib plus Merck's anti-PD-1 therapy KEYTRUDA ® (pembrolizumab), without chemotherapy, in first-line KRAS G12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) show that median progression-free survival (PFS) and duration of response (DOR) had not been reached after a median follow-up of nearly 21 months, with durable activity observed across PD-L1 levels. Separate results in a rapid oral presentation show olomorasib plus chemoimmunotherapy (pembrolizumab, pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy) achieved an investigator-assessed overall response rate (ORR) of 62% and median DOR of 14.5 months in first-line advanced KRAS G12C NSCLC with a median of nearly 19 months follow up. 
Dr. Marcelo V. Negrao , Associate Professor of Thoracic and Head and Neck Medical Oncology at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center and presenting author of the study: "Responses lasting a median of more than a year in patients across all PD-L1 tumor expression levels - including many with low expression - is the type of progress we want to see in the first-line setting. The data presented at ESMO support continued study of olomorasib with immunotherapy, with or without chemotherapy, to give patients the possibility of more options from the outset of their treatment journey, where we successfully utilize other genomically-targeted therapies in lung cancer."
KRAS G12C mutations occur in approximately 13% of people with NSCLC, the most common form of lung cancer. 1 These patients generally have high-risk clinical characteristics and more comorbidities. 2 There are no approved targeted therapies for the first-line treatment of KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC; standard of care is immunotherapy with or without chemotherapy, and most patients do not go on to second-line therapy. 3 KRAS G12C inhibitors have been limited in this setting because toxicity has been a persistent challenge for some combinations with immunotherapy. 4 
Olomorasib is a potent, selective next-generation oral KRAS G12C inhibitor specifically intended to target the mutation: it binds the mutated protein and locks it in its inactive state, with properties that allow for high predicted target occupancy and potency, potentially allowing for safer, flexible combination with standard-of-care immunotherapy, with or without chemotherapy.
Jacob Van Naarden , Executive Vice President and President of Lilly Oncology: " KRAS G12C-mutant lung cancer has been notoriously difficult to treat, and for most patients, the disease is so aggressive that the first line is their only line, underscoring just how critical that first treatment choice is. These results deepen our conviction in the role olomorasib could play in combination with standard PD1-based backbone therapy, while potentially offering a tolerability profile that doesn't require prophylactic medications. We recognize that the oncology community has been waiting for years for a targeted therapy regimen that can address first-line patients with G12C mutations, and we are hopeful that the pivotal Phase 3 data on olomorasib in combination with chemoimmunotherapy in the first half of next year will be a seminal moment for the field."
In a poster presentation, updated results for olomorasib plus pembrolizumab without chemotherapy in 85 patients receiving first-line treatment for KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC showed durable efficacy across all PD-L1 expression levels. The majority of patients (64%) had PD-L1 expression of 50% or higher. The median DOR and median PFS was not yet reached after a median follow-up of 20.7 months, in either the overall population or in those patients (64%) with PD-L1 expression of 50% or higher. The safety profile was consistent with previous reports and the known profiles of each medicine. The most common Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were increased ALT (15.3%), increased AST (12.9%) and diarrhea (8.2%). TRAEs led to olomorasib dose reduction in 31.8% of patients and discontinuation of the treatment regimen in 11.8% of patients. No Grade 5 TRAEs occurred. No prophylactic medications for olomorasib are required by the protocol.
In a separate rapid oral presentation, the updated, single arm analysis of olomorasib plus chemoimmunotherapy (pembrolizumab, pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy), with an additional nine months of follow up, included 77 patients receiving first-line treatment for advanced KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC, with a median follow-up of 18.7 months. Most (74%) had a PD-L1 expression below 50%. The investigator-assessed confirmed ORR was 62% (48/77), median DOR was 14.5 months (95% CI, 8.5-not estimable [NE]), and median PFS was 11.6 months (95% CI, 9.5-21.5). The safety profile was consistent with previous reports and the known profiles of each medicine. The most common Grade 3 or higher TRAEs were neutropenia (21%), anemia (17%), increased alanine aminotransferase (12%) and thrombocytopenia (12%). TRAEs led to olomorasib dose reduction in 19.5% of patients and discontinuation of the treatment regimen in 7.8%. No Grade 5 TRAEs occurred. No prophylactic medications for olomorasib are required by the protocol.
Together, these analyses support the rationale for the ongoing Phase 3 SUNRAY-01 study (NCT06119581) in first-line KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC. SUNRAY-01 is a global master protocol containing two randomized Phase 3 trials. Part A is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled evaluation of olomorasib plus pembrolizumab versus placebo plus pembrolizumab in patients with PD-L1 expression of 50% or higher. Part B, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled evaluation of olomorasib plus chemoimmunotherapy versus placebo plus chemoimmunotherapy in patients regardless of PD-L1 expression, has completed enrollment. Part C of the study is designed to assess olomorasib plus pembrolizumab in patients with PD-L1 expression below 50%. The olomorasib program, which includes the SUNRAY-02 Phase 3 trial in patients with resectable and unresectable non-metastatic disease, spans early and advanced NSCLC across all PD-L1 expression levels, evaluating olomorasib in combination with immunotherapy, with or without chemotherapy.
For more information on Lilly 's oncology pipeline, click here .
Frequently Asked Questions 
What is olomorasib and how does it work? 
Olomorasib (LY3537982) is an investigational, oral, potent, and highly selective next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor from Lilly . It was specifically intended to target KRAS G12C, a mutated form of the KRAS protein: it binds the mutated protein and locks it in its inactive state, with properties that allow for high predicted target occupancy and potency as monotherapy or in combination. Olomorasib is being studied in KRAS G12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and other solid tumors.
Is olomorasib approved? 
No. Olomorasib is an investigational medicine and is not approved by the FDA or any other regulatory authority for any use. The FDA has granted two Breakthrough Therapy designations: olomorasib with pembrolizumab for first-line KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC with PD-L1 expression of 50% or higher, and olomorasib alone for previously treated KRAS G12C-mutant advanced pancreatic cancer. Breakthrough Therapy designation is designed to expedite the development and review of medicines for serious conditions. It does not mean a medicine is approved.
What clinical trial data exist for olomorasib in first-line KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC? 
At ESMO 2026, Lilly presented updated analyses of investigational olomorasib in first-line KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC from the Phase 1/2 LOXO-RAS-20001 trial and the safety lead-in portion of the Phase 3 SUNRAY-01 trial. In a poster presentation, updated results for olomorasib plus pembrolizumab without chemotherapy included 85 patients receiving first-line treatment for KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC after a median follow-up of 20.7 months, demonstrated durable efficacy across all PD-L1 expression levels. The majority of patients (64%) had a PD-L1 expression of 50% or higher. The median DOR and median PFS was not yet reached after a median follow-up of 20.7 months, in either the overall population or in those patients with PD-L1 expression of 50% or higher. At 18 months, the PFS rate was 55% in the overall patient population and 65% in patients with PD-L1 expression of 50% or higher.
A separate rapid oral presentation of olomorasib plus chemoimmunotherapy included 77 patients receiving first-line treatment for advanced KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC, with a median follow-up of 18.7 months. Most (74%) had a PD-L1 expression below 50%. The investigator-assessed confirmed ORR was 62% (48/77), median DOR was 14.5 months (95% CI, 8.5-not estimable [NE]), and median PFS was 11.6 months (95% CI, 9.5-21.5).
Are there clinical trials of olomorasib, and what is SUNRAY-01? 
Yes. SUNRAY-01 ( NCT06119581 ) is a global master protocol containing two Phase 3 studies of olomorasib in first-line KRAS G12C-mutant advanced or metastatic NSCLC. Part A is randomized, double-blind and placebo-controlled, comparing olomorasib plus pembrolizumab with placebo plus pembrolizumab in patients with PD-L1 expression of 50% or higher. Part B compares olomorasib plus chemoimmunotherapy with placebo plus chemoimmunotherapy regardless of PD-L1 expression and has completed enrollment. Part C of the study is designed to assess patients with PD-L1 expression below 50%. SUNRAY-02 ( NCT06890598 ) is a global, Phase 3 study in an early-stage setting studying olomorasib in resected and unresectable NSCLC. Eligibility and locations are listed at clinicaltrials.gov .
What is KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC, and why has first-line treatment been challenging? 
KRAS G12C is an oncogenic driver mutation in the KRAS gene that can promote cancer growth and occurs in approximately 13% of people with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the most common form of lung cancer. 1 Biomarker testing identifies the mutation. People with KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC generally have higher-risk disease; first-line treatment is currently immunotherapy with or without chemotherapy, and most do not go on to second-line therapy. 2,3 KRAS has long been difficult to target because of its protein structure, and toxicity has been a persistent challenge for some combinations of KRAS G12C inhibitors with immunotherapy. 4,5 
KEYTRUDA ® is a registered trademark of Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC , a subsidiary of Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ , USA.
About Olomorasib 
Olomorasib (LY3537982) is an investigational, oral, potent, and highly selective next-generation inhibitor of the KRAS G12C protein. KRAS is the most common oncogene across all tumor types, and KRAS G12C mutations occur in 13% of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and 1–3% of patients with other solid tumors. 1 Olomorasib is a highly potent covalent inhibitor with potential for greater than 90% target occupancy, which may allow for safer combinations with less toxicity. 6 
Olomorasib is currently being studied in KRAS G12C-mutant cancers in combination with pembrolizumab with or without chemotherapy for first-line treatment of advanced NSCLC, in combination with immunotherapy for the treatment of resected and unresectable NSCLC, and as monotherapy and in combinations in other advanced solid tumors ( NCT06119581 , NCT06890598 , and NCT04956640 ).
About Lilly 
Lilly is a medicine company turning science into healing to make life better for people around the world. We've been pioneering life-changing discoveries for 150 years, and today our medicines help tens of millions of people across the globe. Harnessing the power of biotechnology, chemistry and genetic medicine, our scientists are urgently advancing new discoveries to solve some of the world's most significant health challenges: redefining diabetes care; treating obesity and curtailing its most devastating long-term effects; advancing the fight against Alzheimer's disease; providing solutions to some of the most debilitating immune system disorders; and transforming the most difficult-to-treat cancers into manageable diseases. With each step toward a healthier world, we're motivated by one thing: making life better for millions more people. That includes delivering innovative clinical trials that reflect the diversity of our world and working to ensure our medicines are accessible and affordable. title: Lilly presents first clinical data in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer for its investigational, next-generation, FRα-targeting ADC at ESMO 2026
source: Eli Lilly and Company - Official RSS
query: https://investor.lilly.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Lilly presents first clinical data in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer for its investigational, next-generation, FRα-targeting ADC at ESMO 2026
October 24, 2026
PDF Version 
Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) in combination with bevacizumab demonstrated a 79% confirmed objective response rate and 100% disease control rate, with similar activity observed across FR α expression levels 
Clinical activity with Sofe-M was maintained even in patients with prior PARP inhibitor exposure, patients who typically experience poor outcomes with platinum-based chemotherapy 
Sofe-M is currently being studied in both platinum-sensitive and platinum-resistant ovarian cancer in multiple Phase 3 studies as part of the FRAmework-01 master protocol 
INDIANAPOLIS , Oct. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced new Phase 1 data showing that its investigational folate receptor alpha (FRα) antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) plus bevacizumab achieved a confirmed objective response rate (cORR) of 79% and a disease control rate (DCR) of 100% in patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC). A cORR of 79% or higher was seen in both poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi)-treated and PARPi-naïve patients. These data will be shared in an oral presentation at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Annual Congress in Madrid, Spain .
FRα is expressed in almost all ovarian cancers, at much higher levels than in healthy tissue, making it a target that can help direct treatment to tumor cells. Sofe-M is an FRα-targeting ADC composed of an Fc-silent, FRα-specific humanized monoclonal antibody linked to exatecan, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, via a proprietary cleavable polysarcosine linker. The antibody is designed to bind FRα on the surface of tumor cells, delivering exatecan directly into the tumor cell to disrupt DNA replication.
Jacob Van Naarden , Executive Vice President and President of Lilly Oncology: "The standard of care for platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer has remained unchanged for a decade and demands new treatment options. Results for Sofe-M show a promising efficacy and tolerability profile across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer, regardless of FRα expression levels or prior treatment. These data give us confidence as we continue to study Sofe-M in our Phase 3 FRAmework-01 program to bring this potential new medicine to the women who need it."
The Phase 1 study is evaluating Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in patients with advanced solid tumors, including a cohort of 33 women with PSOC who received Sofe-M (4 mg/kg) plus bevacizumab (15 mg/kg). Patients received a median of three prior systemic regimens (range 1–6), including prior PARPi (67%) and prior bevacizumab (70%). As of the July 6, 2026 , data cutoff, the cORR among the 29 patients with measurable disease was 79.3% (23/29; 6 complete responses [CR, 20.7%] and 17 partial responses [PR, 58.6%]), and DCR was 100%. Responses were consistent across FRα expression levels and prior PARPi exposure. Median duration of response (DOR) and median progression-free survival (PFS) were not reached at median follow-ups of 6.2 and 10.2 months, respectively.
Chrisann Kyi , MD, Gynecologic Medical Oncologist & Early Drug Development Specialist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center : "The durable and robust responses we've seen in patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer are important, particularly in a PARPi pretreated population, where the response rate seen with Sofe-M exceeds what has been reported in published platinum re-challenge studies. The observed safety profile and low discontinuation rates, combined with early efficacy results, support the continued investigation of Sofe-M as a potentially meaningful new option for patients."
Sofe-M plus bevacizumab demonstrated a safety profile consistent with the known profiles of each medicine. No new safety signals were observed. The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) across all patients included epistaxis (73%), nausea (73%), anemia (58%), neutropenia (55%), and fatigue (52%). The most common Grade ≥3 TEAEs were neutropenia (42%) and anemia (24%); febrile neutropenia occurred in 3% of patients, and G-CSF prophylaxis was not mandated. Any-grade neuropathy occurred in 9% of patients, with no Grade ≥3 events. Dose reductions occurred in 42% of patients, and 6% discontinued treatment due to an adverse event.
The FRAmework-01 program is evaluating Sofe-M in three global Phase 3 trials across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer: Part A tests Sofe-M as monotherapy in platinum-resistant disease; Part B tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing a PARPi; and Part C tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in PARPi-naïve platinum-sensitive disease. The study is being conducted in partnership with the European Network for Gynaecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO/NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG), and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT).
For more information on Lilly 's oncology pipeline, click here .
Frequently Asked Questions 
What is sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M)? 
Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) is an investigational folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) being studied for the treatment of ovarian cancer and other solid tumors. It is designed to selectively bind to cancer cells expressing FRα and deliver a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload directly to those cells.
What is an antibody-drug conjugate? 
An antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) is a type of medicine that pairs an antibody with a cell-killing payload. The antibody is designed to recognize and bind to a specific protein found on the surface of cancer cells, and the payload is released once the ADC reaches its target, allowing the medicine to attack cancer cells while limiting exposure to healthy tissue. 1
How is Sofe-M different from other FRα-targeted ADCs? 
Sofe-M is designed to target FRα across a broad range of expression levels, including in tumors with lower FRα expression. In this Phase 1 study, Sofe-M plus bevacizumab showed a confirmed objective response rate of 79.3% in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC), with consistent activity across FRα expression levels and regardless of prior PARP inhibitor exposure. Earlier studies in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) also demonstrated responses observed across all FRα expression levels and in patients previously treated with mirvetuximab soravtansine (MIRV). 2 These results are being further evaluated in Lilly 's ongoing Phase 3 FRAmework-01 program, which is studying Sofe-M across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer.
What are the results with sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) in the treatment of platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)?
The Phase 1 study demonstrated encouraging clinical activity, including a confirmed objective response rate (cORR) of 79.3% and a disease control rate (DCR) of 100%, in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer. Activity was observed across FRα expression levels and regardless of prior PARP inhibitor exposure. Median duration of response (DOR) and median progression-free survival (PFS) were not reached at median follow-ups of 6.2 and 10.2 months, respectively. Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) plus bevacizumab demonstrated a safety profile consistent with the known profiles of each medicine, with no new safety signals observed and a low rate of discontinuation due to adverse events (6%). These findings support continued investigation of Sofe-M in the ongoing Phase 3 FRAmework-01 trial.
In this study Sofe-M was dosed at 4 mg/kg. Why is it dosed at 3mg/kg in the Phase 3 FRAmework-01 trial? 
The 3 mg/kg dose of Sofe-M was selected as the recommended phase 3 dose (RP3D), based on analysis of the safety, efficacy and PK data as monotherapy. The ORR was comparable between the two doses, with ORRs of 59.0% (95% CI 42.1, 74.4) and 58.8% (95% CI 32.9, 81.6), at 4 mg/kg and 3mg/kg doses, respectively. Safety signals were higher at 4 mg/kg versus 3 mg/kg, with Grade ≥3 TRAEs at 56.4% vs 35.3% and dose reductions of 41.0% vs 23.5%.
What are historical clinical trial results for standard of care in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)? 
For patients who recur after platinum-based chemotherapy and PARP inhibitor (PARPi) maintenance, published real world data on subsequent platinum re-challenge have shown modest response rates, with an objective response rate (ORR) of 41.9%. 3 Other studies of platinum-based regimens, such as OCEANS, were conducted prior to the routine use of PARPi maintenance and did not include patients previously treated with a PARPi, 4 a population that now represents a majority of patients with recurrent PSOC, including those enrolled in Sofe-M's Phase 1 study.
What is platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)? 
Platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC) is characterized as ovarian cancer that comes back more than six months after platinum-based chemotherapy. While people with PSOC can often be treated with platinum again, the disease tends to return, and each recurrence can leave fewer treatment options and shorter remissions. 5 
What is the current unmet need in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)? 
The standard of care for PSOC has remained largely unchanged for more than a decade, even as understanding of which patients benefit from it has evolved. Approximately 50% of PSOC patients have HRD-positive tumors, meaning their tumors carry a specific DNA-repair deficiency. 6 These patients tend to have longer progression-free survival with upfront platinum-based chemotherapy plus a PARP inhibitor (PARPi). 6 However, when these patients do recur after PARPi maintenance, response rates to subsequent platinum-based treatment are modest. 6 Patients with non-HRD-positive tumors see minimal benefit from PARPi to begin with and generally have a poorer prognosis overall. 6 Despite these different outcomes between HRD-positive and HRD-negative patients, treatment approaches for PSOC have not meaningfully changed to reflect that distinction.
What is the difference between platinum-resistant (PROC) and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)?
The difference comes down to timing. If ovarian cancer returns more than six months after platinum-based chemotherapy, it's considered platinum-sensitive, and patients often respond well to platinum treatment again. If the cancer returns within six months, or continues growing during treatment, it's considered platinum-resistant, and platinum-based chemotherapy is generally no longer effective. Because platinum resistance tends to develop gradually, each recurrence can bring a shorter remission, even while a patient's disease is still classified as platinum-sensitive. 6
What is folate receptor alpha (FRα), and why is FRα expression level important in treating ovarian cancer? 
FRα is expressed in almost all ovarian cancers, at much higher levels than in healthy tissue, making it a target that can help direct treatment to tumor cells. 7 FRα expression level refers to the amount of the protein present on a tumor and may influence eligibility for or response to certain FRα-targeted therapies. 7 
How is the FRAmework-01 clinical trial designed? 
FRAmework-01 is a global, three-part Phase 3 trial studying sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer in a single program: Part A tests Sofe-M as monotherapy in platinum-resistant disease; Part B tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing a PARPi; and Part C tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in PARPi-naïve platinum-sensitive disease. 
The trial's main measure of success across all three parts is how long patients go without their cancer progressing. The study is being conducted in partnership with the European Network for Gynaecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO/NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG), and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT). Enrollment is ongoing globally with first registrational dose in Q4 2025 for PROC and in Q1 2026 for PSOC.
About Ovarian Cancer 
Ovarian cancer is the sixth leading cause of cancer death among women in the United States . 8 While most patients initially respond to platinum-based chemotherapy, approximately 70% will experience recurrence, leading to progressively shorter remission periods with each subsequent treatment. 6 When cancer recurs during or within six months of platinum therapy, known as platinum-resistant disease, patients face limited treatment options. 6,9 
About Sofetabart Mipitecan 
Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M; LY4170156) is composed of an Fc-silent, folate receptor alpha (FRα) specific humanized monoclonal antibody linked to exatecan, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, via a proprietary cleavable polysarcosine linker (PSARlink). Sofe-M was designed to target FRα across all expression levels with improved therapeutic index. FRα is a cell-surface glycoprotein encoded by the gene FOLR1 that binds to the essential nutrients folic acid and reduced folates, bringing them into cells to facilitate cell division and growth. FRα is overexpressed in many solid tumors such as ovarian and endometrial cancers. Sofe-M has received Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) and is currently being evaluated in the Phase 3 FRAmework-01 program. The study is being conducted in partnership with the European Network for Gynaecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO/NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG), and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT). 
About FRAmework-01 
FRAmework-01 ( NCT07213804 ) is a Phase 3, randomized, open-label, three-part study evaluating sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M; LY4170156) in patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer. Part A tests Sofe-M as monotherapy in platinum-resistant disease; Part B tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing a PARPi; and Part C tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in PARPi-naïve platinum-sensitive disease. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival (PFS), assessed by the investigator in Part A and by blinded independent central review (BICR) in Parts B and C. Key secondary endpoints are overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, and safety. The FRAmework-01 study is in partnership with the European Network for Gynecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO / NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG) , and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT) .
More information on FRAmework-01 can be found on clinicaltrials.gov .

Charles River, Labcorp, and FDA Collaborate to Validate New Preclinical Methods for Abuse Potential Assessment
PDF Version 
Joint research effort seeks to improve abuse potential assessment tools to support drug development and public health decision-making 
WILMINGTON, Mass. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 22, 2026--
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) today announced a Research Collaboration Agreement (RCA) with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Labcorp for developing sensitive screening tools to quantify and rank the abuse potential of new drugs, including abuse-deterrent formulations (ADFs) and emerging drugs of abuse. The agreement establishes a joint research framework to enhance objective, standardized metrics for quantifying abuse potential in preclinical models which may inform regulatory assessments of abuse potential under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA).
“Assessing abuse potential is essential for identifying risks and ensuring the safety of new drugs,” said Dr. Namandjé N. Bumpus , Chief Science and Innovation Officer, Charles River. “This collaboration will improve public health safeguards and ultimately amplify our shared efforts to protect patients and communities.”
Evaluating Abuse Potential
Abuse potential assessments are vital components of the safety evaluation of central nervous system-active compounds and are relied upon by FDA and the Drug Enforcement Administration for scheduling control measures.
Enhancing objective, reproducible methods to assess abuse potential is important for advancing regulatory science and supporting evidence-based decision-making. This collaboration will help evaluate approaches that could improve the consistency and sensitivity of abuse potential assessments, ultimately contributing to efforts to protect public health.
Charles River has extensive expertise in assessing abuse potential, having conducted over 100 abuse potential studies and contributed to assessments of the abuse potential of 15 FDA-approved products. As part of its participation in the collaboration, Charles River will leverage behavioral economic models of supply and demand to analyze self-administration data. These models assess the relative reinforcing properties of substances, helping researchers evaluate abuse potential and compare it with that of known drugs of abuse. A recent behavioral economics pilot conducted at Charles River’s Mattawan site provided preliminary proof-of-concept data that demonstrated the promise of this approach.
The collaboration aims to improve sensitivity, accuracy, and consistency across laboratories, ultimately enhancing public health by more reliably and effectively assessing the abuse potential of new drugs.
About Charles River
Charles River provides essential products and services to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies and leading academic institutions around the globe accelerate their research and drug development efforts. Our dedicated employees are focused on providing clients with exactly what they need to improve and expedite the discovery, early-stage development and safe manufacture of new therapies for the patients who need them. To learn more about our unique portfolio and breadth of services, visit www.criver.com .

title: Rio Tinto to invest $1.9 billion to develop the Kangwinan bauxite project in Western Cape York, Queensland

Rio Tinto to invest $1.9 billion to develop the Kangwinan bauxite project in Western Cape York, Queensland
23 October 2026
share
MELBOURNE, Australia--(BUSINESS WIRE)--
Rio Tinto will invest $1.9 billion 1 to develop the Kangwinan bauxite project on Western Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, underpinning the long-term future of its Weipa Operations and continued supply to its international customers and its Australian alumina refineries.
Kangwinan highlights Rio Tinto’s continued commitment to mining in Australia and will sustain its position as one of the world’s leading high-quality bauxite producers.
This brownfield investment will leverage Rio Tinto’s project execution capability and reflects continued application of the company’s disciplined capital allocation framework. It will add 20 million tonnes of annual bauxite production capacity in Weipa, leveraging some existing infrastructure, with first output targeted in 2029 and full production expected by 2032.
The project will replace production from the Andoom mine near Weipa as it reaches the end of its life this decade, while increasing Weipa Operations’ annual capacity to about 44 million tonnes, from current production of around 38 million tonnes per year. It will also help compensate for the planned end of production at the Gove mine in the Northern Territory in 2029.
Rio Tinto Aluminium & Lithium Chief Executive Jérôme Pécresse said: “Kangwinan is a strong vote of confidence in Weipa, in the quality of its bauxite, the capability of its workforce, and the future of the communities and businesses closely connected to our operations.
“The project represents the most significant new mining investment in Queensland in recent years and is a sign of Rio Tinto’s long-term commitment to its bauxite business, the State and our integrated mine-to-metal aluminium value chain.
“For more than 60 years, we have operated in Western Cape York, building a world-class bauxite business and enduring relationships with Traditional Owners and local communities. Cultivating and expanding that ongoing partnership will be critical to the long-term success of our operations.
“As Kangwinan moves forward, and with the planned acquisition of the Aurukun Bauxite Project, we will keep listening and working together to create lasting value for Western Cape York, while respecting the connection Traditional Owners have to Country and making sure they continue to benefit sustainably from our operations.
“This investment will support jobs, create opportunities for local and regional businesses, and help us continue supplying our customers with the high-quality bauxite they have relied on for decades.”
Kangwinan, where early works began in 2025, will establish a new bauxite production centre 15 kilometres south-east of Rio Tinto’s Amrun mine, which is located 40km south of the town of Weipa. A 15-kilometre conveyor will transport ore from Kangwinan to expanded stockyard facilities and the existing Amrun wharf.
The wharf will be expanded to accommodate larger capesize vessels, improving supply-chain efficiency and reducing freight costs.
Construction will ramp up in 2027 and is expected to support more than 1,300 construction jobs. Longer term, the project will help sustain Rio Tinto’s residentially based workforce of around 1,500 people in the Western Cape.
In addition to its Kangwinan investment, Rio Tinto last month agreed to acquire, subject to government approvals, the adjacent Aurukun Bauxite Project from current owners Glencore (70%) and Mitsubishi (30%) to support its long-term growth plans in Western Cape York, using existing and planned infrastructure. The combined Amrun, Kangwinan and Aurukun operations are expected to support Weipa Operations well beyond the middle of this century.
1 All currency figures are in US dollars. Kangwinan’s total capital estimate of $1.9 billion is inclusive of $150 million for early works, which was pre-approved in 2025. This replacement capital expenditure is incorporated within Rio Tinto’s mid-term capital guidance. The investment is expected to deliver an internal rate of return of approximately 22%, based on third party market forecasts as at Q4 2026.
Additional information 
Rio Tinto’s Australian aluminium operations span bauxite mines, alumina refineries and aluminium smelters, directly employing more than 5,000 people and supporting thousands more jobs across the country. The Kangwinan project, alongside recent agreements to support the future of the Bell Bay, Tomago and Boyne smelters, demonstrates how Rio Tinto is investing across its integrated aluminium value chain to support Australian production and jobs for years to come.
The project was named Kangwinan at the request of the Wik Waya Traditional Owners. Kangwinan is a protector of all sacred, ceremonial and female protocols of the Wik Waya tribe. It is also the name of the black female crow, a totem of the Wik Waya people. Rio Tinto will continue to work with Traditional Owners to minimise impacts on cultural heritage, waterways and important access routes.
Environmental permits for the Kangwinan project were previously secured through the State and Commonwealth-approved South of Embley Environmental Impact Statement (EIS).
If the Aurukun acquisition proceeds, Rio Tinto would assess the appropriate environmental approvals pathway for its future development, in consultation with State and Commonwealth agencies, and work closely with Traditional Owners throughout the next stages of planning and development.
This announcement is authorised for release to the market by Matthew Whyte, Rio Tinto’s Group Company Secretary.

title: Lilly breaks ground in Richmond to expand American manufacturing of next-generation cancer medicines, advancing its build-out of 10 new U.S. sites since 2020

Lilly breaks ground in Richmond to expand American manufacturing of next-generation cancer medicines, advancing its build-out of 10 new U.S. sites since 2020
October 22, 2026
PDF Version 
First Lilly site to produce both active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished medicines in a fully integrated facility 
Site will create 650 high-wage jobs 
INDIANAPOLIS , Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) broke ground today on a new $5 billion manufacturing facility just west of Richmond, Virginia , in Goochland County , one of 10 new U.S . manufacturing sites announced since 2020 and one of five among them that will produce active pharmaceutical ingredients (API). As part of the company's more than $50 billion push to expand medicine production in the U.S ., the Richmond site will be Lilly 's first to produce both API and finished medicines in a fully integrated facility, with dedicated API capacity for bioconjugate and large-molecule medicines.
The facility will produce antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), targeted cancer treatments designed to combine the precision of antibodies with potent cytotoxic medicines to attack diseased cells directly while limiting exposure to healthy tissue. ADCs are also being explored for autoimmune diseases and other conditions.
David A. Ricks , Lilly Chair and CEO: "We are developing a new generation of medicines designed to target cancer cells with greater precision, yielding more powerful treatments with potentially fewer side effects. This $5 billion investment means we can make them right here in America. Lilly Richmond will help make sure this innovative science can reach the people who need it."
Building a talent pipeline in Richmond 
Making advanced medicines in the U.S . requires a highly skilled workforce. Lilly is building that workforce in Virginia , offering long-term careers where people can grow close to home. Lilly has committed $40 million to support the Virginia Center for Advanced Pharmaceutical Manufacturing , a statewide network of industry, government, and higher education partners that will prepare Virginians for those careers. The network will include a pilot-scale, hands-on training center in Goochland County , with a targeted opening in 2028.
Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger : " Lilly 's investment is a powerful vote of confidence in Virginia , our people, and our ability to compete for the industries and good jobs that will shape our future. Today's groundbreaking marks an exciting milestone in this partnership, and we are proud that Virginia will play an important, durable role in Lilly 's continued global growth and innovation."
Lilly is currently hiring in Richmond and expects the new facility to create 650 high-wage jobs like engineers, scientists, operations personnel, and lab technicians – along with approximately 1,800 construction jobs as the site is built and brought online. Visit the Lilly Richmond career page for open positions or join Lilly 's talent community for future opportunities.
Jonathan Christy , Chairman of the Goochland County Board of Supervisors : " Lilly 's groundbreaking marks a significant investment in Goochland County and an exciting step forward for our community. We proudly welcome Lilly and the opportunities this project will create for quality jobs, economic growth, and lifesaving innovation."
By pairing a highly skilled workforce with advanced technologies and specialized manufacturing, the Richmond site will help support a reliable supply of safe, high-quality medicines. It will use state-of-the-art technologies, including machine learning, AI, digitally integrated systems and advanced data analytics, to drive right-first-time execution, with digital automation embedded throughout the site to streamline operations.
The Richmond facility will be built and operated to the highest standards for safety, quality and environmental stewardship, and Lilly is committed to being a good neighbor in Goochland County and a trusted partner across Virginia . The site is targeting a Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Gold certification, demonstrating Lilly 's focus on sustainable performance as it expands advanced manufacturing in the U.S .
Lilly has announced 10 U.S. sites since 2020:
Five will produce API: 
Richmond, Virginia ; Huntsville, Alabama ; Houston, Texas ; and two sites in Lebanon, Indiana – Lebanon API and Lilly Medicine Foundry, which will also focus on new production methods and making medicines for clinical trials
Four will make injectable medicines and manufacture devices: 
Research Triangle Park and Concord, North Carolina ; Kenosha, Wisconsin ; and Lehigh Valley, Pennsylvania 
One will make genetic medicines in Lebanon, Indiana ; Lebanon Advanced Therapies
Additional quotes for media use 
Ambassador Jamieson Greer , U.S . Trade Representative: " President Trump's America First Trade Policy is accelerating our nation's reindustrialization, incentivizing companies to proudly build, invest, and expand their operations domestically. Lilly 's new Richmond facility will ensure that life-saving medicines are manufactured on American soil. Today's groundbreaking stands as a powerful testament that there is no substitute for the resilience of the American economy and the skill of the American worker."
About Lilly 
Lilly is a medicine company turning science into healing to make life better for people around the world. We've been pioneering life-changing discoveries for 150 years, and today our medicines help tens of millions of people across the globe. Harnessing the power of biotechnology, chemistry and genetic medicine, our scientists are urgently advancing new discoveries to solve some of the world's most significant health challenges: redefining diabetes care; treating obesity and curtailing its most devastating long-term effects; advancing the fight against Alzheimer's disease; providing solutions to some of the most debilitating immune system disorders; and transforming the most difficult-to-treat cancers into manageable diseases. With each step toward a healthier world, we're motivated by one thing: making life better for millions more people. title: UnternehmerTUM Accelerator, Microsoft, Infineon Technologies, and NVIDIA Launch Physical AI Growth Lab for Europe's Most Promising Startups Business & Financial Press Oct 22, 2026
query: https://www.infineon.com/about/press
content_text:
UnternehmerTUM Accelerator, Microsoft, Infineon Technologies, and NVIDIA Launch Physical AI Growth Lab for Europe's Most Promising Startups
Business & Financial Press
Oct 22, 2026 
Munich, Germany – 22 October 2026 – UnternehmerTUM Accelerator, Microsoft, Infineon, and NVIDIA, today launched the Physical AI Growth Lab, an equity-free accelerator for Europe's most promising physical AI, robotics, and industrial AI startups. Running from January to April 2027, the program combines expertise, infrastructure, capital access, and enterprise networks to help founders scale.
Program Made for Startups to Scale 
The program is led by UnternehmerTUM Accelerator and supports startups that are based in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) or building for EMEA, have a working prototype or minimum viable product (MVP), bring at least one technical co-founder, run teams of up to 20 people, and were founded within the last three years. The program runs in a hybrid format with in-person sessions in Munich. During this time, the 10–15 selected startups get access to Microsoft for Startups benefits including USD 350.000 in Azure Credits, access to the NVIDIA SDKs and open models, benefits from the NVIDIA Inception program for startups, and access to Infineon’s hardware foundation for Physical AI. This includes its semiconductor stack, power semiconductors, microcontrollers, sensors, and connectivity solutions that make physical AI systems actionable in the real world. Startups also access mentoring from 170+ deep tech experts, direct introductions to enterprise customers, and connections to a network of 200+ investors. 
Physical AI: From Simulation to Reality to Europe's Market Leaders 
Physical AI — the convergence of foundation models, simulation, and robotics — moves artificial intelligence from the digital world into machines, factories, and logistics networks. 
Europe has great potential. In 2026 Europe will hold approximately 22.5% of the global physical AI market in 2026, supported by regulatory clarity under the EU AI Act and Germany's High-Tech Strategy 2025. Startups that build now, backed by the right technical foundation and early enterprise customers, have the opportunity to become category leaders before the market consolidates around dominant platforms.
Four Partners, One Goal: Accelerating Startup Success 
UnternehmerTUM Accelerator, Microsoft, Infineon, and NVIDIA cover the entire path from prototype to commercial scale. By backing startups with access to capital, infrastructure, and industry experts, this partnership ensures that the next generation of physical AI companies is developed in EMEA. 
UnternehmerTUM Accelerator , ranked Europe’s leading startup hub for the third consecutive year, brings 170+ mentors, 200+ investors, and a track record of launching scalable companies like Sereact, RobCo and Sewts. Startups coming out of UnternehmerTUM Accelerator have raised almost 4 Billion EUR in funding. 
Microsoft provides Azure's AI and cloud infrastructure along with a global enterprise network.
NVIDIA deploys its full physical AI stack and open models, from training and simulation to edge deployment, plus Inception Program benefits.
Infineon supplies the semiconductor stack, power semiconductors, microcontrollers, sensors, and connectivity solutions that make physical AI systems actionable in the real world.
"The European physical AI market is growing rapidly, and the moment is now to support startups with access to capital, infrastructure, and technology. With Microsoft, Infineon, and NVIDIA, we're showing how real acceleration works," says Inga vom Holtz, Director Startups and Investments, UnternehmerTUM .
“Germany’s next major economic opportunity lies at the intersection of artificial intelligence and industrial expertise. With the Physical AI Growth Lab, we are bringing startups, technology partners and established companies together to turn prototypes into market-ready solutions. This is an important step toward strengthening Germany’s position as a leading hub for the development and adoption of Physical AI,” says Agnes Heftberger, Corporate Vice President & CEO of Microsoft Germany & Austria
“EMEA founders working on robotics and industrial AI need access to the right tools early, while their products are still taking shape,” said Eran Rosenberg, Head of EMEA Physical AI Startups at NVIDIA . "The Physical AI Growth Lab brings NVIDIA physical AI SDKs, open models, and NVIDIA Inception benefits to startups in the program, so they can train, simulate, and deploy on one platform as they scale.”
“The future of robotics will be built through collaboration,” says Allan Frederiksen, Technology and Innovation Officer at Infineon. “As a semiconductor leader, we provide the electronics foundation that turns intelligence into motion. Through the Physical AI Growth Lab, we provide startups with access to technology expertise, development platforms and a strong ecosystem of industry partners and investors, helping accelerate the path from prototype to scalable real-world solutions. Startups are a melting pot of innovation, and together with our partners we aim to foster this momentum. We see physical AI as a major growth opportunity, and an entire ecosystem is forming around it, driving the technological leap toward autonomous robotic systems.”
Applications Open Now 
The program runs from January to April 2027 in a hybrid format with in-person sessions in Munich. Applications open now. Deadline: November 13, 2026. 
More information about the program: https://physical-ai.accelerator.unternehmertum.de/ 
About UnternehmerTUM 
UnternehmerTUM is a unique platform for the development of innovations. UnternehmerTUM actively identifies innovative technologies and initiates new business through the systematic networking of talents, technologies, capital and customers. UnternehmerTUM offers founders and startups a complete service from the initial idea to IPO. A team of over 500 experienced entrepreneurs, including scientists and investors, supports startups with business creation, market entry and financing – also with venture capital. For established companies, a team of experienced consultants offers access to the UnternehmerTUM ecosystem. UnternehmerTUM has many years of expertise in the development of innovation strategies and the implementation of technology-driven business ideas. Founded in 2002 by the entrepreneur Susanne Klatten, the non-profit UnternehmerTUM GmbH is the leading center for innovation and business creation in Europe with more than 100 high-growth technology startups every year - including Celonis, Proxima Fusion, and Isar Aerospace.
About Microsoft 
Microsoft Germany GmbH was founded in 1983 as a subsidiary of Microsoft Corporation (Redmond, U.S.A.) and employs more than 3,000 people across seven locations in Germany: Berlin, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Cologne, Munich, Stuttgart and Walldorf. Together with our 30,000 partners in Germany, we support organizations with innovative solutions for the intelligent cloud and intelligent edge, helping them succeed in the digital transformation and the age of AI.
Microsoft is also a global leader in areas including productivity software, IT security, innovative hardware and development platforms, including those based on open-source technologies. Through LinkedIn, our professional network connects more than 950 million people worldwide, while Xbox and Game Pass provide gaming experiences across platforms.
Microsoft is investing in the expansion of AI infrastructure and cloud capacity as well as in developing digital skills in Germany. Together with government, business and academia, we participate in a wide range of initiatives and projects to ensure that everyone can benefit from the progress of our digital society.
About Infineon
Infineon Technologies AG is a global semiconductor leader in power systems and IoT. Infineon drives decarbonization and digitalization with its products and solutions. The Company had around 57,000 employees worldwide (end of September 2025) and generated revenue of about €14.7 billion in the 2025 fiscal year (ending 30 September). Infineon is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: IFX) and in the USA on the OTCQX International over-the-counter market (ticker symbol: IFNNY).

Philippe Kehren appointed to Cefic Board and Executive Committee
Oct 22, 2026 
Share to 
Opens in a new window Opens in a new window 
Solvay today announced that CEO Philippe Kehren has been appointed to the Board and Executive Committee of Cefic , the European Chemical Industry Council, and will serve as Chair of Cefic's Advocacy Forum . 
Cefic represents the chemical industry in Europe and engages with EU institutions, policymakers and stakeholders on issues affecting the sector's competitiveness, sustainability and long-term development.   
Philippe Kehren's appointment comes at a critical time for the European chemical industry as companies navigate competitiveness pressures, high energy costs, industrial transformation and decarbonization. 
Through these roles, Philippe Kehren will contribute to industry discussions on the conditions needed to maintain a sovereign, innovative and sustainable industrial base in Europe. 
“Philippe brings deep industrial experience and a clear understanding of the challenges facing our sector today. His leadership will be a real asset to Cefic as we work to strengthen the case for a competitive chemical industry in Europe. We are delighted to welcome him to the Board and Executive Committee, and particularly value his willingness to lead our Advocacy Forum at such an important moment for our industry.” 
"I have always been fascinated by industry and by the role it plays in creating prosperity across generations. Today, Europe's chemical industry faces a difficult reality: competitiveness, energy and sustainability have become inseparable challenges. Addressing them requires honest conversations about trade-offs and practical solutions. I am honored to join Cefic's Board and Executive Committee and look forward to working with industry peers, policymakers and stakeholders to help strengthen Europe's industrial base and ensure it remains a place where companies can invest, innovate and manufacture."

October 22, 2026
JFE Steel Corporation
Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Company, Inc.
Mitsubishi Chemical Corporation
JFE Steel, Mitsubishi Gas Chemical, and Mitsubishi Chemical Commence Demonstration Project to
Develop a Carbon Recycling Supply Chain at Mizushima Complex
— Demonstration ranges from utilizing steelmaking process by-product gas to producing methanol and
propylene —
JFE Steel Corporation (Headquarters: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo; President: Masayuki Hirose, hereinafter
referred to as "JFE Steel"), Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Company, Inc. (Headquarters: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo;
President: Yoshinori Isahaya, hereinafter referred to as "Mitsubishi Gas Chemical"), and Mitsubishi
Chemical Corporation (Headquarters: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo; President: Manabu Chikumoto, hereinafter
referred to as "Mitsubishi Chemical")—collectively referred to as "the Three Companies"—have
commenced a supply chain demonstration project (hereinafter referred to as "the Demonstration Project")
at the Mizushima Complex (Kurashiki City, Okayama Prefecture) in September 2026. This Demonstration
Project is being conducted based on the demonstration plan announced by the Three Companies in March
2025, aimed at achieving a carbon-recycling society.
JFE Steel has commenced the supply of by-product gas generated from its steelmaking processes for the
Demonstration Project. Mitsubishi Gas Chemical has begun producing methanol using this by-product gas
at its newly constructed Carbopath™*1 demonstration plant within its Mizushima Plant. Furthermore,
Mitsubishi Chemical has begun producing propylene using this methanol as raw material at its existing
demonstration facility (utilizing the DTP®*2 process).
＜Roles of the three companies and material flow in the Demonstration Project＞
The Three Companies will continue the Demonstration Project, evaluate its economic viability, and
identify challenges and pathways toward commercialization. Furthermore, the Three Companies will
explore broader opportunities for collaboration with other businesses within the Mizushima Complex.
＜A concept for carbon recycling through cross-industry collaboration in the Mizushima Complex＞
*1, Carbopath™ is a carbon recycling platform utilizing methanol, promoted by Mitsubishi Gas Chemical.
*2, DTP®: Dominant Technology for Propylene production
DTP® is a registered trademark of JGC Corporation.

title: Amkor Technology and NVIDIA Advance Strategic Partnership for AI Infrastructure

Amkor Technology and NVIDIA Advance Strategic Partnership for AI Infrastructure
New $1.3 billion agreement supports further expansion in South Korea , building on the companies’ recent Arizona collaboration 
TEMPE, Ariz. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 21, 2026--
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced additional investments in South Korea for capacity expansion initiatives with NVIDIA. With this latest commitment, Amkor’s multi-year agreements with NVIDIA in Arizona and South Korea total $3 billion . The initiatives support growing demand for next-generation AI and accelerated computing platforms.
Advanced packaging technologies are essential to enabling the performance, power efficiency and integration required for next-generation computing systems. The prepayments align Amkor's manufacturing capacity with NVIDIA’s long-term growth plans and support increasing demand for advanced packaging solutions.
“Our partnership with NVIDIA underscores the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling next-generation AI platforms,” said Kevin Engel , president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology . “These investments build on our global manufacturing footprint and strengthen our ability to support customers through our operations in both the United States and South Korea.”
“Growing demand for accelerated computing is increasing the need for advanced packaging capacity,” said Debora Shoquist , executive vice president, operations of NVIDIA. “Our work with Amkor helps us scale production of current and next-generation platforms while strengthening the resilience of our global supply chain.”
This collaboration further strengthens Amkor’s role as a strategic manufacturing partner for NVIDIA and reinforces the companies’ shared commitment to supporting the continued expansion of AI infrastructure.
Amkor will also exhibit at NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C. from Nov. 30 - Dec. 3 , where the company will showcase its advanced packaging and test capabilities and engage with customers, policymakers and industry leaders.
About Amkor Technology, Inc. 
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR) is the world’s largest U.S. headquartered OSAT and is a global leader in outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services. With a strong track record of innovation, a broad and diverse geographic footprint and solid partnerships with lead customers, Amkor delivers high-quality solutions that enable the world’s leading semiconductor and electronics companies to bring advanced technologies to market. The company’s comprehensive portfolio includes advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package solutions targeting applications for smartphones, data centers, artificial intelligence, automobiles and wearables. For more information visit amkor.com .

title: Ouster Sensors Play Key Role in Forterra's Lancer Completing 1,426 Missions and 88 Casualty Evacuation Operations in Ukraine
query: https://investors.ouster.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Ouster Sensors Play Key Role in Forterra's Lancer Completing 1,426 Missions and 88 Casualty Evacuation Operations in Ukraine
October 21, 2026
PDF Version 
Expanding a multi-year strategic partnership to enhance soldier safety while increasing force projection, Forterra plans to further advance its AutoDrive platform with Ouster REV8 native color lidar for next-gen defense vehicles 
SAN FRANCISCO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 21, 2026-- Ouster, Inc. (Nasdaq: OUST), a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI, and Forterra , the leader in autonomous mission systems for military operations in contested environments, today announced that Forterra's Lancer autonomous ground vehicles have completed 1,426 missions and 88 casualty evacuation operations in Ukraine including Ouster Rev7 OS1 digital lidar at the core of their sensor fusion perception stack. Forterra built and delivered 105 Lancers in under six months, and across more than 7,300 miles they have run routes that would otherwise have put a crew inside the vehicle.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261021344872/en/ 
Forterra's Lancer keeps crews out of harm's way, this one lost on a mission in Ukraine with no one aboard.
The Lancers arrived in Ukraine in October 2025 . Built on the Polaris RANGER XP 1500 and modified in theater with Starlink for resilient communications, each vehicle carries up to 750 kilograms of critical equipment to the war fighters. Lancers are operating in high danger zones where persistent drone surveillance makes crewed vehicles high value targets and creates unnecessary risk for personnel. Instead, uncrewed Lancer systems deliver essential supplies and evacuate wounded soldiers without undue risk to additional personnel.
“Forterra exists to take people out of harm’s way, and in Ukraine , Lancer is doing that every day under constant drone surveillance,” said Forterra CEO Josh Araujo . “As we advance AutoDrive toward higher levels of autonomy, Ouster sensors give us the perception foundation required by the next generation of vehicles.”
To date, Forterra has integrated AutoDrive across more than 50 vehicle platforms deployed in over ten countries. This includes the Squad Multipurpose Equipment Transport (SMET) program and the Marine Corps ROGUE Fires platform, which recently entered Block 2 production, making it the most widely deployed autonomous driving system in the defense industry and the first system fielded by the U.S . military to enable autonomous maneuver of ground vehicles.
Forterra’s AutoDrive capability is built upon Forterra’s 24 years of operational experience and over $500 million invested in engineering development and operations. Throughout a multi-year partnership, Ouster digital lidar has been a key part of Forterra’s AutoDrive platform and its operational success.
Ouster's sensors enable 360-degree situational awareness for autonomous ground vehicles operating in complex and unpredictable environments. Each Ouster OS1 sensor covers ground that would otherwise require several narrow field-of-view sensors, which means fewer units for Forterra to integrate, power, and maintain on every vehicle. Additionally, lidar ranges are independent of ambient light, and dual returns report both an obscurant and the surface behind it, so perception holds in fog, dust, rain, and darkness.
"Forterra operates autonomous ground vehicles in some of the most challenging environments on the planet, where reliable perception and safety are critical to the vehicle operators and soldiers," said Angus Pacala , co-founder and CEO of Ouster. "Ouster's technology gives these vehicles a detailed, real-time understanding of their surroundings, helping them navigate complex terrain and operate with greater confidence when GPS, road markings and ideal conditions cannot be relied upon."
Next- Gen Sensing , Built to Automotive Standards 
Ouster's next-generation native color digital lidar, Rev8, is designed for ASIL-B functional safety to ISO 26262, cybersecurity to ISO 21434, and support for automotive ethernet, all requirements that unmanned ground vehicle programs increasingly demand.
Off-road work causes constant vibration and shock and subjects lidar sensors to temperatures that swing from arctic cold to desert heat. Rev8 is the most rugged lidar family Ouster has built yet, qualified from -40 °C to +85 °C and ingress-protected against dust and water, allowing sensing in the harshest conditions. Rev8 also captures color in the same silicon as the 3D data, giving perception software a second channel alongside range for classifying what is in the scene.
About Ouster 
Ouster (Nasdaq: OUST) is a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI across industrial, robotics, automotive, and smart infrastructure. With a unified platform of high-performance digital lidar, cameras, AI compute, sensor fusion and perception software, and AI models, Ouster delivers solutions that improve quality of life in the physical world. Headquartered in San Francisco, CA , Ouster has a global presence serving thousands of customers with offices in the Americas , Europe , and Asia-Pacific . For more information about our products, visit www.ouster.com , contact our sales team , or connect with us on X or LinkedIn .
About Forterra 
Forterra is the autonomy backbone for distributed, mission-aware, resilient military operations in contested environments. Building the foundational autonomy platforms that coordinates weapons, sensors, and users through distributed mobility, compute, and communications, anywhere, under fire, without risking human life, Forterra empowers its customers to deploy autonomy as a force multiplier, extending reach, readiness survivability and effectiveness across the battlespace and industrial applications. Forterra is headquartered in Clarksburg, Md., with offices in Arlington, Va., Winter Park, Fl., Ketchum, Id. and Palo Alto, Ca. To learn more, go to forterra.com .

title: 3M and AWS collaborate to advance optical connectivity innovation
query: https://investors.3m.com/news-events/press-releases/rss
content_text:
3M and AWS collaborate to advance optical connectivity innovation
Oct 21, 2026 • 10:28 AM EDT 
Download as PDF
AWS is investing in 3M's Expanded Beam Optical technology for its data center infrastructure 
SAINT PAUL, Minn. , Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 3M  (NYSE: MMM) and  Amazon Web Services (AWS) today announced an expanded strategic collaboration. AWS plans to deploy and scale 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) platform for its data center infrastructure. Together, the two leading American companies will advance co-innovation and investment in optical connectivity and the critical infrastructure needed for next-generation super intelligence (SI), also known as artificial intelligence (AI). 
"AWS's adoption of 3M's EBO platform demonstrates the potential of our optical connectivity technology to meet the performance demands of next-generation data center infrastructure," said Wendy Bauer, Group President of 3M's Transportation and Electronics Business Group. "By combining AWS's infrastructure expertise and scale with 3M's innovation and materials science capabilities, we can accelerate EBO deployment, advance our transformation and strengthen U.S. innovation and investment." 
"Our work with 3M reinforces our commitment to supporting good jobs here in the U.S.," said Jens Gruenkemeir, Vice President of Supply Chain & Procurement at Amazon. "Beyond powering the services people use every day, from online banking and hospital data records to streaming entertainment and retail purchases, our data center investments are unlocking economic opportunities in the communities where we invest and across the supply chain, including the hundreds of jobs being supported by 3M as a result of its collaboration with Amazon."   
The collaboration and related investments are expected to strengthen the U.S. economy by supporting more than 500 jobs directly and indirectly, including the creation of more than 100 new roles through 2027 across Minnesota, Texas and Wisconsin. These planned roles will support customer co-innovation, technology advancement and supply chain development across 3M's optical networking portfolio and help accelerate industrywide adoption through collaboration with partners. 
3M expects to contribute nearly $0.5 billion to the U.S. economy through its optical connectivity business. This investment will accelerate innovation in optical networking and fiber termination, enable commercialization at scale and drive adoption across the data center industry.
The collaboration builds on 3M's announcement earlier this year that it will double production capacity at its Menomonie, Wisconsin, manufacturing facility, and is expected to support U.S. manufacturing partners involved in equipment and production scale-up throughout the supply chain.
