Danaher Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
WASHINGTON , Oct. 21, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Danaher Corporation (NYSE: DHR) today announced results for the third quarter 2026. All results in this release reflect only continuing operations and period-to-period comparisons are year-over-year unless otherwise noted.
Key Third Quarter 2026 Results 
Net earnings were $1.2 billion, or $1.71 per diluted common share, up 34.5% year-over-year.
Non-GAAP adjusted diluted net earnings per common share grew 11.5% to $2.11.
Revenues increased 8.5% year-over-year to $6.6 billion.
Non-GAAP core revenue excluding respiratory revenue increased 5.5% year-over-year and non-GAAP core revenue increased 3.0% year-over-year.
Operating cash flow was $1.9 billion and non-GAAP free cash flow was $1.6 billion.
Julie Sawyer Montgomery, President and Chief Executive Officer, stated, "We delivered better-than-expected third quarter revenue, earnings and cash flow, and are encouraged by the improving trends we saw across our end markets. The continued acceleration in core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue, together with DBS-driven execution drove double-digit adjusted EPS growth and underscored our ability to convert improving demand into strong financial performance."
Ms. Sawyer Montgomery continued, "Danaher has built a strong foundation, and the time I've spent with our teams and customers during my transition into the CEO role has only reinforced my conviction in the opportunities ahead. Looking forward, the opportunity for Danaher is clear: to become the defining leader in Life Sciences and Diagnostics–a company that unambiguously gains share, delivers sustainable profitable growth, and helps our customers improve outcomes for patients around the world."
Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2026 Outlook 
Danaher Corporation (the "Company") does not reconcile non-GAAP forecasted core sales growth, adjusted operating profit margin and adjusted diluted net earnings per common share to their respective, comparable measure prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) because (except for estimated amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets of $0.5 billion for the fourth quarter and $1.9 billion for the year ending December 31, 2026 and the estimated impact of foreign currency on sales, which is estimated to be flat in the fourth quarter and increase sales by 1.0% in the full year, assuming the currency exchange rates in effect as of September 25, 2026) the additional elements that would be reflected in any such GAAP measures (such as the impact of currency exchange rates on profitability, future acquisitions, divested product lines, discrete tax adjustments, impairments, gains and losses on investments and the outcome of legal proceedings) are difficult to predict and estimate and are often dependent on future events that may be uncertain or outside of our control. The impact of these additional elements could be material to our results computed in accordance with GAAP.
For the fourth quarter 2026, the Company anticipates that non-GAAP core revenue excluding respiratory revenue will increase in the 4.0% to 5.0% range year-over-year. We expect respiratory revenue to be an approximately 150 basis point headwind, resulting in core revenue growth of approximately 3.0%.
For full year 2026, the Company is increasing its full year adjusted diluted net earnings per common share guidance to a range of $8.57 to $8.62 versus previous guidance of $8.45 to $8.60.
Conference Call and Webcast Information 
Danaher will discuss its third quarter results and financial guidance for the fourth quarter and full year 2026, including as applicable key assumptions with respect thereto, during its investor conference call today starting at 8:00 a.m. ET. The call and an accompanying slide presentation will be webcast on the "Investors" section of Danaher's website, www.danaher.com , under the subheading "Events & Presentations." A replay of the webcast will be available in the same section of Danaher's website shortly after the conclusion of the presentation and will remain available until the next quarterly earnings call.
The conference call can be accessed by dialing 800-267-6316, within the U.S. or +1 203-518-9783 outside the U.S. a few minutes before 8:00 a.m. ET and notifying the operator that you are dialing in for Danaher's earnings conference call (Conference ID: DHRQ326). A replay of the conference call will be available shortly after the conclusion of the call and until November 4, 2026. You can access the replay dial-in information on the "Investors" section of Danaher's website under the subheading "Events & Presentations."
ABOUT DANAHER 
Danaher is a leading global life sciences, diagnostics and biotechnology innovator committed to advancing the power of science and technology to improve human health. Through a connected ecosystem of industry-leading businesses, the Company works closely with customers to solve many of their most complex scientific challenges by accelerating discovery, development and the delivery of life-changing therapies. Powered by the Danaher Business System and 60,000 associates worldwide, the Company strives for continuous improvement, operational excellence and Innovation at the Speed of Life . Explore more at www.danaher.com .

Calculations of these measures, explanations of what these measures represent and the reasons why we believe these measures provide useful information to investors, a reconciliation of these measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measures, where applicable, and other information relating to these non-GAAP measures are included in the supplemental reconciliation schedule attached.

Statement Regarding Non-GAAP Measures 
Each of the non-GAAP measures set forth above should be considered in addition to, and not as a replacement for or superior to, the comparable GAAP measure, and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures reported by other companies. Management believes that these measures provide useful information to investors by offering additional ways of viewing Danaher Corporation's ("Danaher" or the "Company") results that, when reconciled to the corresponding GAAP measure, help our investors:
with respect to the profitability-related non-GAAP measures, understand the long-term profitability trends of our business and compare our profitability to prior and future periods and to our peers;
with respect to the non-GAAP measures related to core sales, identify underlying growth trends in our business and compare our sales performance with prior and future periods and to our peers; and
with respect to free cash flow (the "FCF Measure"), understand Danaher's ability to generate cash without external financings, strengthen its balance sheet, invest in its business and grow its business through acquisitions and other strategic opportunities (although a limitation of free cash flow is that it does not take into account the Company's debt service requirements and other non-discretionary expenditures, and as a result the entire free cash flow amount is not necessarily available for discretionary expenditures).
Management uses the non-GAAP measures referenced above to measure the Company's operating and financial performance, and uses core sales and non-GAAP measures similar to Adjusted Diluted Net Earnings Per Common Share From Continuing Operations, Adjusted Operating Profit and the FCF Measure in the Company's executive compensation program.
The items excluded from the non-GAAP measures set forth above have been excluded for the following reasons:
With respect to the profitability-related non-GAAP measures:
Amortization of Intangible Assets: We exclude the amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets because the amount and timing of such charges are significantly impacted by the timing, size, number and nature of the acquisitions we consummate. While we have a history of significant acquisition activity we do not acquire businesses on a predictable cycle, and the amount of an acquisition's purchase price allocated to intangible assets and the related amortization term are unique to each acquisition and can vary significantly from acquisition to acquisition. Exclusion of this amortization expense facilitates more consistent comparisons of operating results over time between our newly acquired and long-held businesses, and with both acquisitive and non-acquisitive peer companies. We believe however that it is important for investors to understand that such intangible assets contribute to sales generation and that intangible asset amortization related to past acquisitions will recur in future periods until such intangible assets have been fully amortized.
Restructuring Charges: We exclude costs incurred pursuant to discrete restructuring plans that are fundamentally different (in terms of the size, strategic nature and planning requirements, as well as the inconsistent frequency, of such plans) from the ongoing productivity improvements that result from application of the Danaher Business System. Because these restructuring plans are incremental to the core activities that arise in the ordinary course of our business and we believe are not indicative of Danaher's ongoing operating costs in a given period, we exclude these costs to facilitate a more consistent comparison of operating results over time.
Other Adjustments: With respect to the other items excluded from the profitability-related non-GAAP measures, we exclude these items because they are of a nature and/or size that occur with inconsistent frequency, occur for reasons that may be unrelated to Danaher's commercial performance during the period and/or we believe that such items may obscure underlying business trends and make comparisons of long-term performance difficult. 
With respect to core sales and core sales excluding respiratory testing, (1) we exclude the impact of currency translation because it is not under management's control, is subject to volatility and can obscure underlying business trends, (2) we exclude the effect of acquisitions and divested product lines because the timing, size, number and nature of such transactions can vary significantly from period-to-period and between us and our peers, which we believe may obscure underlying business trends and make comparisons of long-term performance difficult and (3) beginning with the Company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q in the third quarter of 2026, we exclude tariff refunds to customers to help customers better understand underlying growth trends in the Company's business that otherwise may be obscured by such item.
With respect to core sales excluding respiratory testing, we exclude the impact of revenues related to the sale of respiratory testing products in the Company's molecular diagnostics business in the Diagnostics segment. Demand for respiratory testing depends significantly on the severity levels of influenza and influenza-like illness in a given period, and these severity levels are not under management's control. As a result, presenting core sales on a basis that combines respiratory testing revenue with other Diagnostics business revenues can obscure underlying growth trends within the Diagnostics businesses. The Company believes that this measure complements core sales, enhances investors' understanding of the historical and anticipated performance of the Diagnostics businesses as a whole, including with respect to underlying growth trends and facilitates comparisons of period-to-period performance. 
With respect to the FCF Measure, we deduct payments for additions to property, plant and equipment (net of the proceeds from capital disposals) to demonstrate the amount of operating cash flow for the period that remains after accounting for the Company's capital expenditure requirements.

content_text:
Revenue Grew 9% Including 6% Organic Revenue Growth 
Grew GAAP Diluted EPS 9% and Adjusted EPS 15% 
Outstanding performance driven by proven growth strategy and PPI Business System 
WALTHAM, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- 
Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. (NYSE: TMO), the world leader in serving science, today reported its financial results for the third quarter ended September 26, 2026.
Third Quarter Highlights 
Third quarter revenue grew 9% to $12.14 billion
Third quarter GAAP diluted earnings per share (EPS) grew 9% to $4.64
Third quarter adjusted EPS grew 15% to $6.68
“We are very pleased to deliver another excellent quarter, with outstanding financial performance on both the top and bottom line,” said Marc N. Casper, chairman and chief executive officer of Thermo Fisher Scientific. “We’re advancing our proven growth strategy, which is resonating strongly with our customers, and our PPI Business System is enabling outstanding execution across the company.”
Casper added, “Looking ahead, we’re well positioned to deliver an excellent 2026 as we continue to drive long-term value creation for all of our stakeholders and build an even brighter future for our company.”
Growth Strategy and Capital Deployment 
Advanced our proven growth strategy, launching a range of high-impact, innovative new products during the quarter. Highlights include the Thermo Scientific™ Orbitrap™ Isora™ mass spectrometer , the first Orbitrap system designed for isotope ratio analysis, enabling faster, simplified workflows and providing deeper insights into the origin and composition of samples for environmental and life sciences research; the Thermo Scientific™ EMPAD™ G2 electron detector enabling faster, more detailed electron microscopy characterization of advanced materials to support the development of next-generation electronics, memory and energy technologies; the FDA-cleared EliA™ CTD 13 Screen in the U.S., a new autoimmune test for systemic connective tissue diseases, including lupus, helping laboratories streamline testing and providing clinicians with reliable information to inform patient care; and the Ion 560 Chip , the highest-throughput sequencing chip for the Ion GeneStudio™ S5 platform, providing nearly twice the sequencing capacity of the prior offering to enable laboratories to process more samples and meet growing genomic profiling needs in oncology research.
Strengthened our industry-leading commercial engine and deepened our trusted partner status with customers. In partnership with Mayo Clinic, we launched Precure , a pioneering initiative that will combine data from more than one million patient samples with our differentiated proteomics ecosystem, including Orbitrap™ mass spectrometry and Olink™ technologies, to generate new insights into disease progression, enable earlier detection and advance precision medicine. In South Korea, we opened our first AI-Automation Innovation Center, bringing together our advanced analytical technologies, automation and AI to enable our customers to accelerate innovation and enhance R&D productivity. In our channel businesses, we also opened a highly automated distribution center in Kentucky, to enhance speed, flexibility and assurance of supply for our customers across North America.
Continued to successfully execute our capital deployment strategy. During the quarter, we completed our previously announced divestiture of our microbiology business.
Financial Results 
Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 grew 9% to $12.14 billion, versus $11.12 billion in the same quarter of 2025. Organic revenue growth was 6%.
GAAP Earnings Results 
GAAP diluted EPS in the third quarter of 2026 was $4.64, 9% growth versus the third quarter of 2025. GAAP operating income for the third quarter of 2026 was $2.26 billion, 17% higher than the year-ago quarter. GAAP operating margin was 18.6%, compared with 17.4% in the third quarter of 2025.
Non-GAAP Earnings Results 
Adjusted EPS for the third quarter of 2026 was $6.68, 15% growth versus the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted operating income for the third quarter of 2026 was $2.97 billion, 15% higher than the year-ago quarter. Adjusted operating margin was 24.5%, compared with 23.3% in the third quarter of 2025.
Annual Guidance for 2026 
The company will provide updated 2026 financial guidance during its earnings conference call this morning at 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time.
Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
Adjusted EPS, adjusted net income, adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, free cash flow, and organic revenue growth are non-GAAP measures that exclude certain items detailed after the tables that accompany this press release, under the heading “Supplemental Information Regarding Non-GAAP Financial Measures.” The reconciliations of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures are provided in the tables that accompany this press release.
Conference Call 
Thermo Fisher Scientific will hold its earnings conference call today, October 21, 2026, at 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time. During the call, the company will discuss its financial performance, as well as future expectations.
The call will be webcast live on the “Investors” section of our website, www.thermofisher.com . You can access the conference call by dialing (833) 461-5787 within the U.S. or +1 (585) 542-9983 outside the U.S. The access code is 500554659.
The earnings press release and related information can also be found on the Investor Relations section of our website, under the heading “Financials”. A replay of the call will be available under “News, Events & Presentations” until the next quarterly earnings call.
About Thermo Fisher Scientific 
Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. is the world leader in serving science, with annual revenue over $45 billion. Our Mission is to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. Whether our customers are accelerating life sciences research, solving complex analytical challenges, increasing productivity in their laboratories, improving patient health through diagnostics or the development and manufacture of life-changing therapies, we are here to support them. Our global team delivers an unrivaled combination of innovative technologies, purchasing convenience and pharmaceutical services through our industry-leading brands, including Thermo Scientific, Applied Biosystems, Invitrogen, Gibco, Fisher Scientific, Unity Lab Services, Patheon and PPD. For more information, please visit www.thermofisher.com .

Supplemental Information Regarding Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
In addition to the financial measures prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), we use certain non-GAAP financial measures such as organic revenue growth, which is reported revenue growth, excluding the impacts of acquisitions/divestitures and the effects of currency translation. We report these measures because Thermo Fisher management believes that in order to understand the company’s short-term and long-term financial trends, investors may wish to consider the impact of acquisitions/divestitures, and/or foreign currency translation on revenues. Thermo Fisher management uses these measures to forecast and evaluate the operational performance of the company as well as to compare revenues of current periods to prior periods.
We report adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, adjusted net income, and adjusted EPS. We believe that the use of these non-GAAP financial measures, in addition to GAAP financial measures, helps investors to gain a better understanding of our core operating results and future prospects, consistent with how management measures and forecasts the company’s core operating performance, especially when comparing such results to previous periods, forecasts, and to the performance of our competitors. Such measures are also used by management in their financial and operating decision-making and for compensation purposes. To calculate these measures we exclude, as applicable:
Certain transaction-related costs, including charges for the sale of inventories revalued at the date of acquisition, significant transaction-related third-party costs, changes in estimates of contingent acquisition-related consideration, and other costs associated with obtaining short-term financing commitments for pending/recent acquisitions. We exclude these costs because we do not believe they are indicative of our normal operating costs.
Costs/income associated with restructuring activities and large-scale abandonments of product lines, such as reducing overhead and consolidating facilities. We exclude these costs because we believe that the costs related to restructuring activities are not indicative of our normal operating costs.
Equity in earnings/losses of unconsolidated entities; impairments of long-lived assets; and certain other gains and losses that are either isolated or cannot be expected to occur again with any predictability, including gains/losses on investments, the sale of businesses, product lines, and real estate, significant litigation-related matters, curtailments/settlements of pension plans, and the early retirement of debt. We exclude these items because they are outside of our normal operations and/or, in certain cases, are difficult to forecast accurately for future periods.
The expense associated with the amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets because a significant portion of the purchase price for acquisitions may be allocated to intangible assets that have lives of up to 20 years. Exclusion of the amortization expense allows comparisons of operating results that are consistent over time for both our newly acquired and long-held businesses and with both acquisitive and non-acquisitive peer companies.
The noncontrolling interest and tax impacts of the above items and the impact of significant tax audits or events (such as changes in deferred taxes from enacted tax rate/law changes), the latter of which we exclude because they are outside of our normal operations and difficult to forecast accurately for future periods.
We report free cash flow, which is operating cash flow less net capital expenditures, to provide a view of the continuing operations’ ability to generate cash for use in acquisitions and other investing and financing activities. The company also uses this measure as an indication of the strength of the company. Free cash flow is not a measure of cash available for discretionary expenditures since we have certain non-discretionary obligations such as debt service that are not deducted from the measure.
Thermo Fisher Scientific does not provide GAAP financial measures on a forward-looking basis because we are unable to predict with reasonable certainty and without unreasonable effort items such as the timing and amount of future restructuring actions, transaction-related charges as well as gains or losses from sales of real estate and businesses, the early retirement of debt and the outcome of legal proceedings. The timing and amount of these items are uncertain and could be material to Thermo Fisher Scientific’s results computed in accordance with GAAP.
The non-GAAP financial measures of Thermo Fisher Scientific’s results of operations and cash flows included in this press release are not meant to be considered superior to or a substitute for Thermo Fisher Scientific’s results of operations prepared in accordance with GAAP. Reconciliations of such non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures are set forth in the tables above.

Infineon collaborates with NVIDIA on gallium nitride-based power conversion systems for 800 VDC AI data centers
Business & Financial Press
Oct 21, 2026 
Munich, Germany – 21 October 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) is advancing its collaboration with NVIDIA on 800 Volt direct current (VDC) power architectures for AI data centers. Timed with NVIDIA's GTC Berlin developer conference, the announcement centers on the high-voltage intermediate bus converter (IBC), one of the most critical and demanding conversion stages in the power delivery chain of AI data centers. Infineon's gallium nitride (GaN) technology is emerging as well-suited technology of choice for this stage. This builds on the companies' joint work first announced in May 2025 and detailed further in October 2025, which centered on enabling serviceable, hot-swappable 800 VDC server racks.
“AI is fundamentally reshaping the demands we place on power infrastructure, and semiconductors are at the heart of solving that challenge,” said Jochen Hanebeck, CEO, Infineon Technologies AG. “Our collaboration with NVIDIA on 800 Volt power architectures shows what is possible when deep semiconductor expertise meets the pace of innovation required by AI. Gallium nitride-based system solutions are a key enabler of this next generation of data centers, and Infineon is proud to help power the AI era from grid to core.”
Driven by the extreme power draw of AI workloads, data centers have adopted intermediate-bus architectures in which an IBC steps down the main bus voltage feeding accelerator cards into a lower-voltage rail, allowing downstream stages to efficiently generate the tight core and point-of-load rails that AI processors require. This multi-stage approach reduces distribution losses, all while meeting strict constraints on board area, thermal limits and uptime. As AI infrastructure scales, 800 VDC is being introduced alongside existing AC and lower-voltage DC architectures as an additional distribution option for higher-density compute.
Gallium nitride is well suited to meet these requirements. Compared to silicon, GaN allows power devices to switch significantly faster with lower losses, which enables higher switching frequencies of up to 1 MHz at the IBC stage. This in turn allows the size of magnetic components and passives to shrink considerably, directly translating into higher power density and lower board heights, a critical advantage as rack space becomes an increasingly scarce resource in AI data centers. At the same time, GaN's low conduction and switching losses support best-in-class conversion efficiency, helping to limit heat generation even as power levels per rack continue to climb toward the megawatt range. These characteristics make GaN the preferred semiconductor technology today capable of meeting the combined demands of power density, efficiency, and fast transient response at the IBC stage, a position Infineon has built on the back of many years of leadership in GaN development and manufacturing. In combination with PSoC™ control C3 and EiceDRIVER™ product families, full system solutions for IBCs are provided by Infineon.
Infineon's GaN portfolio supports the full range of conversion ratios required at the HV IBC stage, including 800 V to 50 V, 800 V to 12 V, and 800 V to 6 V, giving data center operators the flexibility to optimize rack architectures without compromising on power density or efficiency. At this combination of high switching frequency, power density and efficiency, the GaN power switches are used to their full benefits. Infineon’s technology leadership in power semiconductors relies on extensive in-house manufacturing capabilities as well as application and system expertise built up over many years. The company’s portfolio spans IBC solutions across silicon, gallium nitride and silicon carbide , supporting customers along the entire range of their design requirements.
Infineon and NVIDIA collaborate along the entire data center power chain. title: Solvay and IUCN scale industry-first biodiversity framework to Rosignano, Italy
query: https://www.solvay.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Solvay and IUCN scale industry-first biodiversity framework to Rosignano, Italy
Oct 21, 2026 
Share to 
Opens in a new window Opens in a new window 
From Dombasle to Rosignano: Solvay and IUCN expand science-based biodiversity action across industrial operations.
Solvay and the International Union for Conservation of Nature ( IUCN ) are expanding their collaboration on biodiversity with the launch of a new IUCN RHINO (Rapid, High - Integrity Nature-positive Outcomes) program at Solvay's Rosignano site in Italy. 
As the first chemical company to pilot and implement the IUCN RHINO framework , Solvay is working with IUCN to better understand the interactions between its operations and nature, prioritize actions where they can have the greatest impact, and contribute to global biodiversity goals through science-based, measurable approaches.   
The new program builds on the work carried out at Solvay's Dombasle site in France. Over the past year, Solvay and IUCN completed a comprehensive biodiversity assessment and , using the RHINO methodology, identified priority species and habitats to help the Dombasle team and develop a science-based roadmap through 2030. The roadmap includes biodiversity monitoring, habitat restoration, ecological corridor development, invasive species management, and measures to further reduce impacts on local ecosystems. 
Building on these lessons, Solvay and IUCN carried out an initial review in Rosignano across five interconnected operational areas: the industrial site, Santa Luce Lake, the Cecina River basin, the Ponteginori solution mining area, and the San Carlo quarry, which supplies natural limestone for soda ash production. The review has already identified opportunities to strengthen biodiversity outcomes across the landscape. 
Over the next 18 months, detailed ecological assessments will be caried out to establish biodiversity baselines and identify priority conservation actions, with IUCN providing scientific advice and review. By the end of 2027, Solvay aim s to establish science-based biodiversity objectives, monitoring indicators, and a long-term action plan to guide implementation through 2030 and beyond. 
A particular focus will be placed on Santa Luce Lake , a former industrial reservoir that has evolved into a Natura 2000 protected area and State Nature Reserve. Today, the site hosts around 200 bird species and illustrates how long-term stewardship and collaboration can create opportunities for biodiversity conservation alongside industrial activity. Building on decades of work with conservation partner LIPU and other local stakeholders, the roadmap will seek to strengthen habitat management, ecological connectivity, and ecosystem resilience.         
As an industrial company, we know our operations interact with nature. Our responsibility is to understand our dependencies, reduce the pressures we exert, and increase our positive impact. That's why our collaboration with IUCN matters. In Dombasle , we developed a science-based roadmap for biodiversity action. In Rosignano , we're building on those lessons in one of our most diverse and complex landscapes. This is about moving from commitment to implementation, and demonstrating that industry can be part of the solution." 
"The biodiversity crisis requires action at scale. Through the IUCN RHINO approach, we are helping companies identify where they can have the greatest positive impact for species and ecosystems. The work in Dombasle and now starting in Rosignano shows that species extinction risk metrics can guide decision making. The ambition now must be to turn assessments into targets for reducing threats to species and those targets into meaningful outcomes" 
The Rosignano program contributes to Solvay's commitment to dedicate 30% of its permeable land located near biodiversity-sensitive areas to conservation and restoration with measurable positive impacts by 2030, while supporting the objectives of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework .

About Solvay 
Solvay, a pioneering chemical company with a legacy rooted in founder Ernest Solvay's pivotal innovations in the soda ash process, is dedicated to delivering essential solutions globally through its workforce of over 8,400 employees. Since 1863, Solvay harnesses the power of chemistry to create innovative, sustainable solutions that answer the world’s most essential needs such as purifying the air we breathe and the water we drink, preserving our food supplies, protecting our health and well-being, creating eco-friendly clothing, making the tires of our cars more sustainable and cleaning and protecting our homes. Solvay’s unwavering commitment drives the transition to a carbon-neutral future by 2050, underscoring its dedication to sustainability and a fair and just transition. As a world-leading company with €4.3 billion in net sales in 2025, Solvay is listed on Euronext Brussels and Paris (SOLB). For more information about Solvay, please visit solvay.com or follow Solvay on LinkedIn.    
About IUCN 
The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) is the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network. IUCN harnesses the experience , resources , and reach of its 1,400 Member organizations and the input of around 17,000 experts. IUCN provides public, private and non- governmental organizations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress , economic development and nature conservation to take place together . Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide . Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities , these projects work to reverse habitat loss , restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being . 
About the RHINO approach 
The IUCN RHINO (Rapid, High-Integrity Nature-positive Outcomes) approach provides a science-based framework to help organizations assess biodiversity impacts, identify priority actions, and measure progress over time. The methodology incorporates the STAR (Species Threat Abatement and Restoration) metric, enabling actions to be prioritized based on their potential contribution to reducing species extinction risk and supporting ecosystem health.

query: https://www.tosoh.co.jp/news/release/
content_text:
TOP 
ニュース

無架橋発泡体用ポリエチレン「ペトロセンCZ11」の開発 ～中央物産との共同開発により、ポリエチレン発泡体の再資源化と耐熱性を両立～ 
NEWS RELEASE
2026年10月21日
東ソー株式会社
広報・IR室
印刷する
2026.10.21
ニュースリリース
無架橋発泡体用ポリエチレン「ペトロセンCZ11」の開発 
～中央物産との共同開発により、ポリエチレン発泡体の再資源化と耐熱性を両立～
東ソーは、株式会社中央物産（以下、中央物産）との共同開発により、無架橋 ※1 でありながら、高い耐熱性を有する発泡体が得られるポリエチレン「ペトロセンCZ11」を開発いたしました。本製品は、国内初の高い耐熱性を保持した無架橋発泡体用ポリエチレンとなります。主に空調保温材などの用途を想定しており、このたび中央物産の空調保温パイプの発泡層向け材料としての採用が決定いたしました。
自動車内装材や空調保温材などの耐熱性が求められる分野では、軽量かつ加工性に優れるポリエチレンと、耐熱性を付与するための架橋剤を加えて製造する架橋ポリエチレン発泡体が広く使用されています。一方で、従来の架橋ポリエチレン発泡体は、三次元網目構造 ※2 により再溶融が難しく、マテリアルリサイクル ※3 が困難であることから、端材の多くが廃棄されていました。
2050年カーボンニュートラルの実現に向け、資源循環の重要性が高まる中、ポリエチレン発泡体の再資源化と耐熱性の両立は、業界全体の課題となっていました。
今回開発した「ペトロセンCZ11」は、当社が長年培ってきたポリマー設計技術により、ポリエチレン単体で高発泡成形性と高い耐熱性を実現したものです。「ペトロセンCZ11」を使用することで、従来品と同等以上の性能を維持しながら、押出成形 ※4 時に架橋剤を使用しない無架橋ポリエチレン発泡体の製造が可能となります。
架橋剤を使用しないことで再溶融・再加工が可能となり、リサイクル後の物性変化も小さいことから、マテリアルリサイクルの実現に貢献します。さらに、架橋に必要な熱加工工程を省略できることから、製造時の環境負荷低減が期待されます。
今回の採用を皮切りに、当社は空調保温材をはじめ、自動車内装材など、耐熱性が求められる発泡製品分野への展開を進めてまいります。さまざまな発泡製品へ展開することで、複合プラスチックを含む発泡体の水平リサイクル ※5 の促進も期待されます。
当社は、長年培ってきた技術と経験を結集し、イノベーション創出に挑戦し続けることで、持続可能な社会の実現に貢献してまいります。
提供元：中央物産 
架橋剤などにより分子間を結合させる処理を行っていないこと
高分子の分子同士が三次元的に結合した構造
廃棄物を新たな製品の原料として再利用するリサイクル方法
加熱溶融した樹脂を金型から連続的に押し出して成形する方法
リサイクル前と後で用途を変えない資源循環の方法

title: GE HealthCare announces five new global collaborations to advance the next generation of theranostics imaging
query: https://investor.gehealthcare.com/rss.xml
content_text:
GE HealthCare announces five new global collaborations to advance the next generation of theranostics imaging
October 20, 2026
PDF Version 
Leading institutions will evaluate StarGuide GX i across quantitative imaging, dynamic imaging and emerging theranostic applications
Clinical experience from more than 1,000 patient studies was established ahead of the European Association of Nuclear Medicine (EANM) 2026 Annual Meeting in Vienna, Austria 
Insights will help guide the future evolution of GE HealthCare's digital SPECT/CT platform and inform the next generation of nuclear medicine imaging
CHICAGO & VIENNA --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 20, 2026--
GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) today announced a global clinical evaluation program spanning three continents and five internationally recognized institutions to assess StarGuide™ GX, i its next-generation digital 4D SPECT/CT system. Participating institutions include Hadassah Medical Center in Israel ; Mayo Clinic in the United States ; Oncopole Claudius Regaud – Institut Universitaire du Cancer de Toulouse in France ; Peking University First Hospital in China ; and Rambam Health Care Campus.
Across the program, participating institutions will evaluate image quality, quantitative performance, dynamic imaging and workflow while providing clinical and research feedback to help inform the future evolution of StarGuide GX.
“Nuclear medicine is entering a new era in which imaging is expected to do more than identify disease – it is increasingly being used to quantify biological processes, support treatment decisions and monitor response to therapy,” said Erez Levy , Executive Director, Molecular Imaging, GE HealthCare . “By working across multiple regions and care environments, we aim to generate clinical and research insights that can help inform innovation as imaging, quantitation and workflow needs evolve.”
Expanding quantitative and dynamic imaging capabilities 
StarGuide GX uses dual-sided cadmium zinc telluride (dsCZT) detector technology and is designed to support high-sensitivity, high-resolution imaging, quantitative imaging and dynamic acquisitions. Its detector configuration allows the detectors to move close to the patient during imaging, while its patented dual-collimator detector design is intended to eliminate the need for manual external collimator exchanges and streamline imaging workflows.
Additionally, the system is engineered to support radionuclides across a broad energy range and, in research settings, it may also be evaluated for imaging radionuclides associated with emerging alpha-emitter research, including Actinium-225, focused on the potential to expand theranostic applications. ii 
“The technological innovations introduced by StarGuide GX are particularly exciting for the future of theranostics,” shared Prof. Frederic Courbon, Head of the Imaging Department , Oncopole Claudius Regaud – Institut Universitaire du Cancer de Toulouse. “The system's ergonomic design and flexibility have the potential to significantly improve workflow while supporting precision in quantitative imaging and high-energy radionuclide applications. Our first experience suggests that StarGuide GX represents a meaningful step forward in enabling advanced theranostic practices.”
StarGuide GX also uses NVIDIA RTX™ accelerated computing to support image reconstruction, and includes a Low-Medium Energy collimator that is designed to provide up to 2.67-times system volume sensitivity. iii 
Global collaborations advance nuclear medicine research 
Five new, global clinical collaborations will evaluate the platform across diverse care settings: iv 
Hadassah Medical Center ( Israel ): Evaluate advanced quantitative capabilities following the system’s recent field upgrade.
Mayo Clinic ( United States ): Evaluate advanced quantitative and dynamic imaging applications.
Oncopole Claudius Regaud – Institut Universitaire du Cancer de Toulouse ( France ): Assess StarGuide GX, the department's general-purpose SPECT/CT platform, across routine oncology imaging and clinical research.
Peking University First Hospital ( China ): Explore novel tracer research and preclinical applications.
Rambam Health Care Campus ( Israel ): Evaluate StarGuide GX imaging workflows through extensive clinical use across a broad range of nuclear medicine applications and tracers.
These new collaborations build on GE HealthCare’s work with University Hospital Essen in Germany , which in June 2026 opened a new state-of-the-art Nuclear Medicine Center featuring the world’s first installation of StarGuide GX SPECT/CT.
To date, these diverse healthcare institutions have scanned more than 1,000 patients.
StarGuide GX received CE Mark in November 2025 and is available for sale in select European Union member states. The system is 510(k) pending with the U.S . FDA and is not currently available for sale in the United States .
For more information about GE HealthCare’s molecular imaging portfolio, visit gehealthcare.com or see the system in the company’s booth at the European Association of Nuclear Medicine’s 2026 Annual Meeting, October 17-21 in Vienna, Austria .
About GE HealthCare Technologies Inc. 
GE HealthCare is a leading global healthcare solutions provider of advanced medical technology, pharmaceutical diagnostics, and AI, cloud and software solutions that help clinicians tackle the world’s most complex diseases. Serving patients and providers for 130 years, GE HealthCare is delivering bold innovations designed for the next era of medicine across its Advanced Imaging Solutions, Pharmaceutical Diagnostics and Patient Care Solutions segments to help clinicians deliver more personalized, precise patient care. We are a $20.6 billion business with approximately 54,000 colleagues working to create a world where healthcare has no limits.
GE HealthCare is proud to be among 2026 Fortune World’s Most Admired Companies™. 
Follow us on LinkedIn , Facebook , Instagram , or visit our website for our latest news and perspectives .
StarGuide GX is CE marked and 510(k) pending with the U.S. FDA. Not available for sale in the United States.
Investigational tracers. Not approved by the U.S. FDA or any other regulatory authority for clinical use.
StarGuide GX with Low-Medium collimator has up to a 2.67-times increase in system volume sensitivity compared with NM/CT 870 DR with LEHRS collimator. System volume sensitivity measured per NEMA NU-1 2023, with adaptations for StarGuide GX.
The products and applications evaluated may be investigational, may not be commercially available in all markets and may be subject to applicable regulatory requirements. Evaluation activities and timelines vary by institution.

title: BASF signs Letter of Intent with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs to advance next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
query: https://www.basf.com/global/en/investors/calendar-and-publications/investor-releases
content_text:
BASF signs Letter of Intent with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs to advance next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
Establishing new production capacity for semiconductor materials supporting chip technologies below 2 nanometers  
Expanding BASF’s Kuanyin site with a strengthened Innovation Center and advanced quality analysis capabilities  
Strengthening supply chain resilience and enhancing customer support in Taiwan and beyond  
Taipei – October 20, 2026 – BASF today signed a Letter of Intent (LOI) with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), underscoring its long-term commitment to supporting the growth of Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem. Through this investment, BASF’s Electronic Materials business is expanding its Kuanyin site in Taoyuan with additional production capacity for advanced semiconductor materials, enhanced quality analysis capabilities, and an expanded Innovation Center. The investment is designed to support increasing global demand for leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing technologies, including advanced nodes below 2 nanometers, while strengthening supply chain resilience and customer proximity.
“Taiwan is a global hub for semiconductor innovation and manufacturing, with leading-edge process technologies and a highly integrated industry ecosystem. Setting the strategic base for BASF’s global Electronic Materials operations in Taiwan in 2025 reflected the strategic importance of Taiwan within the global semiconductor ecosystem and reinforced our confidence in the market’s long-term growth potential,” said Gops Pillay, President, Global Operating Division of BASF.
As the semiconductor industry progresses toward process nodes below 2 nanometers, demand for advanced, high-purity specialty chemical formulations continues to rise. Through the expansion of its Kuanyin site, BASF will strengthen its Innovation Center and broaden its technical and analytical capabilities for leading-edge semiconductor technologies supporting the AI era. The investment will deepen collaboration with key industry partners, enabling the joint development of next-generation materials while reinforcing Taiwan’s position as a global semiconductor innovation hub.
The investment will further strengthen BASF’s local manufacturing, quality assurance and technical service capabilities in Taiwan, enabling the company to provide customers with a more reliable supply of advanced semiconductor materials, faster technical support, and closer collaboration. At the same time, it will enhance supply chain resilience and reinforce BASF’s role as a trusted long-term partner to the semiconductor industry.
“The signing of this Letter of Intent marks another important milestone in BASF’s long-term commitment to the semiconductor industry,” said Jens Liebermann, Senior Vice President, Global Electronic Materials business and Chairman of BASF Taiwan. “As semiconductor technologies continue to advance, innovation in materials must keep pace with our customers’ evolving needs. By strengthening our local manufacturing, innovation, and technical service capabilities, we are deepening collaboration with our customers and accelerating the development of materials solutions for future technology generations, while further enhancing supply chain resilience.”
As a trusted materials partner to the global semiconductor industry, BASF’s Electronic Materials business has maintained a strong presence in Taiwan for more than two decades. The business provides high-performance process chemicals and customized formulation solutions for the advanced semiconductor and display industry as well as specialized metal systems for consumer electronics applications. 
 
About BASF’s Dispersions & Resins division  
The Dispersions & Resins division of BASF develops, produces and markets a range of high-quality polymer dispersions, resins, additives and electronic materials worldwide. These raw materials are used in formulations for several industries, including coatings, construction, adhesives, printing and packaging, electronics and paper. With its comprehensive product portfolio and extensive knowledge of the industry, the Dispersions & Resins division offers its customers innovative and sustainable solutions and helps them advance their formulations. For further information about the Dispersions & Resins division, please visit  www.dispersions-resins.basf.com 
 
About BASF 
At BASF, we create chemistry for a sustainable future. Our ambition: We want to be the preferred chemical company to enable our customers’ green transformation. We combine economic success with environmental protection and social responsibility. Around 95,000 employees in the BASF Group contribute to the success of our customers in nearly all sectors and almost every country in the world. Our portfolio comprises, as core businesses, the segments Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, and Nutrition & Care; our standalone businesses are bundled in the segments Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. title: 10/20/2026 High Performance Polymers Evonik launches new, stiffer VESTAKEEP® PEEK dental grades, widening the possibilities of dental applications for PEEK-based materials Evonik has introduced two new PEEK grades designed for use in long-term dental prosthetics.
query: https://www.evonik.com/en/media.html
content_text:
10/20/2026
Evonik launches new, stiffer VESTAKEEP® PEEK dental grades, widening the possibilities of dental applications for PEEK-based materials
Evonik has introduced two new PEEK grades designed for use in long-term dental prosthetics. 
New grades feature greater rigidity and excellent polishability, suitable for fixed and removable prosthetic restorations
Absorption of masticatory forces remains the same for superior patient comfort
Designed for 100% compatibility with standard CAD/CAM workflows
Darmstadt, Germany. Evonik has introduced two new PEEK grades designed for use in long-term dental prosthetics. One of the latest developments from its High Performance Polymers business line, VESTAKEEP® DC4760 and VESTAKEEP® DC4780 feature remarkable bone-like stiffness, durability, high biocompatibility and excellent processability in dental labs, enlarging the portfolio of metal-free and lightweight dental materials
“The launch of these two new VESTAKEEP® grades are in line with Evonik’s strategy to serve a growing consumer interest in a greater range of metal-free materials for manufacturing dental bridges or long-lasting fixed and removable prosthetic restorations,” said Marc Knebel, head of the PEEK medical applications team at Evonik’s High Performance Polymers business line. “Thanks to their natural color, neutral taste and lightweight properties, PEEK-based dental frameworks are greatly valued by patients looking for an alternative to metal-alloy based materials.”
The new dental grades join an existing range of VESTAKEEP® products for dental applications and are based on a patented formulation that brings high structural rigidity. This property was further defined in an independent study recently published in “Dental Materials.” Conducted by leading members of Charité University Medicine in Berlin and the Einstein Center Digital Future research group, the analysis found VESTAKEEP® DC4760 and VESTAKEEP® DC4780 to have a level of stiffness high enough for use in implant-supported dentures and other high-load dental prosthetics.
“The key feature of these new VESTAKEEP® dental grades is their combination of higher stiffness and their ability to maintain the flexural strength expected for long-term dental prostheses. Thanks to this, VESTAKEEP® can now be used for a broader range of high quality, aesthetic & long-lasting multi-unit frameworks that provide elevated patient comfort” said Jacques-Antoine Raust, Business Manager in Evonik’s Medical Systems team.
Both VESTAKEEP® DC4760 and VESTAKEEP® DC4780 feature excellent polishability for improved machining with established dental laboratory equipment. This allows the benefit of a smooth and immediate integration into daily operations for dental lab technicians and dentists. Evonik’s new PEEK grades continue to retain previous dental grades’ well-established, excellent wear and plaque accumulation resistance for durable hygiene and aesthetics. Additionally, the increased stiffness of both products leads to better modulus matching between acrylic veneers and PEEK, which can increase the longevity of dentures
VESTAKEEP® DC4760 (dentin colored PEEK) and VESTAKEEP® DC4780 (gingiva colored PEEK) are available as rods or CAD/CAM discs with full biocompatibility for long-term mucosal contact. Along with the product, Evonik will provide customers regulatory support for their own MDR registration.
Evonik’s experts will also present their latest solutions for medical applications from November 16 to 19 at the COMPAMED trade show, Hall 8B, Booth D04, in Düsseldorf, Germany.
To learn more about Evonik’s solutions on display at COMPAMED, please visit: https://www.evonik.com/en/events/2026/compamed.html 
For more information on Evonik’s VESTAKEEP® range of products for medical applications, please visit: https://www.evonik.com/en/markets/market_1345345/vestakeep-peek-for-medical-devices.html 
Evonik: Leading beyond chemistry
Evonik goes beyond the boundaries of chemistry with its combination of innovative strength and leading technological expertise. The global chemical company, headquartered in Essen, Germany, is active in more than 100 countries and generated sales of €14.1 billion and earnings (adjusted EBITDA) of €1.9 billion in 2025. The common motivation of the approximately 31,000 employees: to provide customers with a decisive competitive advantage with tailor-made products and solutions as a superforce for industry, thereby improving people's lives. In all markets. Every day.
About Advanced Technologies
The Advanced Technologies segment includes Evonik’s market-leading businesses that leverage technological expertise and process know-how. These businesses feature high-performance polymers and crosslinking agents, hydrogen peroxide and silica, as well as feed ingredients. In 2025, the segment generated sales of €5.9 billion with around 9,200 employees.

SAINT PAUL, Minn. , Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 3M (NYSE: MMM) today reported third-quarter results.
"We delivered another quarter of strong results, including solid sales growth, continued margin expansion, double-digit EPS growth, and robust free cash flow," said William Brown, 3M Chairman and CEO. "Improving productivity through structural transformation and a stronger pipeline of differentiated technologies reinforce our confidence in the full-year outlook and long-term growth and margin potential. I want to thank the 3M team for their focus on customers and disciplined execution, which continues to strengthen our performance and create shareholder value."

Strategic and operational highlights
The following are recently announced highlights:
3M entered into an expanded strategic commercial relationship with Amazon to deploy and scale 3M's optical connectivity and other Data Center related products. 3M issued a warrant to Amazon to purchase up to 3.2 million shares of 3M common stock based upon the achievement of $6 billion in cumulative sales of optical connectivity and other Data Center related products over the next seven years, and other event-based milestones.
3M is collaborating with Genius Electronic Optical Co., Ltd. (GSEO), an optical technology company, to advance technology development and manufacturing for 3M's Expanded Beam Optics (EBO) solutions. In support of these efforts, 3M is investing to acquire ~4.7% of GSEO's common shares. The collaboration brings together 3M's EBO technology leadership, optical interconnect expertise, materials science, manufacturing scale and customer relationships with GSEO's precision optics manufacturing capabilities and production scale.
3M introduced Cooling Film technology for fleet and rail applications , expanding its portfolio of thermal management solutions for transportation customers. Applied to vehicle roofs, the highly reflective performance film uses thermal management technology to reduce heat buildup and help keep interiors noticeably cooler.
3M showcased how its materials science expertise supports innovation in golf equipment through its collaboration with PING . By pairing PING's expertise in club design and custom manufacturing with 3M's broad portfolio of materials science solutions, the two companies can collaborate on engineering solutions that turn complex technical challenges into repeatable, high-quality results on the course.
3M and BOE established a joint innovation laboratory to accelerate next-generation display technology development.  The joint research and development platform brings together BOE's display innovation and end-use application expertise with 3M's materials science capabilities to accelerate higher-performance solutions across LCD, OLED and MLED applications, including improvements in light efficiency, foldable displays and ultra-narrow bezel processes.
3M continued to expand its work with U.S. and international government customers, with third-quarter awards supporting defense, health care, and emergency response needs. Awards included PELTOR™ communication and hearing protection solutions for various U.S. military services and Scott SCBAs for the U.S. Navy, respirator and SCBA products for the National Institutes of Health, and respirators for international customers, reflecting 3M's growing work with government partners around the world.

Tongsuh Petrochemical, a wholly owned South Korean subsidiary of diversified global company Asahi Kasei, has obtained the “Reasonable Assurance” verification for the Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) of acrylonitrile (AN). Produced at its Ulsan manufacturing site and based on a rigorous audit of the plant, data, processes, and documents, this verification provides a high level of assurance and meets the growing customer demand for independent and verified carbon footprint data.
The audit was conducted by Socotec Certification Japan, which reviewed the methodology, source data, and reporting process used to calculate the fiscal 2025 PCF for acrylonitrile from raw material procurement through production. Acrylonitrile is an essential chemical intermediate used in a wide range of applications, including ABS resins, acrylamide, acrylic fibers, and carbon fiber precursor materials. The “Reasonable Assurance” verification confirms that the carbon footprint information meets a high level of verification and reliability and exceeds the requirements necessary for a “Limited Assurance.”
Tongsuh Petrochemical has advanced lower-carbon production over the past several years. In 2021, the company obtained ISCC PLUS certification, a globally recognized sustainability certification scheme that supports traceability of bio-based and circular feedstocks. Since 2022, the company has been producing and marketing acrylonitrile based on biomass-derived propylene using a mass-balance approach.
Asahi Kasei has stated it will continue to reduce greenhouse gas emissions associated with acrylonitrile production through ongoing improvements in proprietary catalyst and manufacturing technologies. Furthermore, the company has expanded the utilization of biomass-based feedstocks. Through these efforts, the company aims to further enhance the value it provides to customers by combining lower-carbon materials with highly reliable environmental data. Asahi Kasei seeks to strengthen its position as a global sustainability partner for industries pursuing decarbonization across their supply chains.
About Asahi Kasei 
Asahi Kasei is a diversified global company that contributes to life and living for people around the world. Since its foundation in 1922, with businesses in ammonia and cellulose fiber, Asahi Kasei has consistently grown through proactive portfolio transformation to meet the evolving needs of every age. With 50,000 employees worldwide, the company contributes to sustainability by providing solutions to the world’s challenges across its three business sectors: Healthcare, Homes, and Material. For more information, visit https://www.asahi-kasei.com/ .

title: 3M announces collaboration with GSEO to advance Expanded Beam Optical manufacturing and development

3M announces collaboration with GSEO to advance Expanded Beam Optical manufacturing and development
Oct 19, 2026 • 5:31 PM EDT 
Download as PDF
ST. PAUL, Minn. , Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 3M (NYSE: MMM) today announced a collaboration with Genius Electronic Optical Co., Ltd.  (GSEO, Taiwan: 3406), an optical technology company, to advance technology development and manufacturing for 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) solutions. In support of these efforts, 3M expects to make a strategic investment to acquire approximately 4.7% of GSEO's common shares as part of the company's private placement of newly issued shares, subject to customary closing conditions.
The collaboration brings together 3M's EBO technology leadership, optical interconnect expertise, materials science, manufacturing scale and customer relationships with GSEO's precision optics manufacturing capabilities and production scale. Together, the companies aim to support EBO commercialization and long-term capacity expansion to meet growing demand from hyperscale data centers and other advanced connectivity applications.
"3M is investing in capabilities and partnerships that can accelerate innovation for our customers," said William Brown, 3M Chairman and CEO. "By selecting GSEO as a manufacturing partner and investing in the company, we are strengthening the path to scale next-generation optical connectivity solutions for high-performance data center infrastructure."
GSEO's existing precision optics manufacturing capabilities and technical development experience are expected to support manufacturing readiness for 3M's EBO ferrules, co-packaged optics solutions and related optical interconnect applications. The collaboration is part of 3M's broader EBO ecosystem strategy, which includes continued work with customers and partners across the optical interconnect market.
"GSEO is pleased to expand its relationship with 3M as we work together to advance optical interconnect solutions for next-generation data center infrastructure," said Micro Kuo, GSEO CEO and President. "This collaboration brings together complementary technology and manufacturing strengths to support continued innovation and help meet the performance demands of high-growth connectivity markets."
3M expects the strategic investment to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.

LOGIQ Focus is powered by cSound Architecture and combined with comprehensive digital tools to deliver advanced image quality and premium-level performance for confident, everyday full-body ultrasound
CHICAGO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 19, 2026--
GE HealthCare today announced LOGIQ™ Focus, a new addition to its LOGIQ family of general imaging ultrasound systems, designed to bring advanced imaging tools to a broader range of ultrasound exams. LOGIQ Focus is a versatile ultrasound system that pairs high-quality LOGIQ imaging with AI-enabled, automation and productivity tools intended to support greater confidence, consistency and efficiency across routine and more complex care areas.
"As demand for imaging grows, clinicians shouldn't have to choose between image quality and efficiency," said Karley Yoder , Chief Executive Officer, Ultrasound Solutions (USS), Advanced Imaging Solutions, GE HealthCare . "LOGIQ Focus builds on more than 30 years of LOGIQ innovation to deliver both, combining advanced imaging and clinician-centered AI-enabled tools that care teams rely on every day."
LOGIQ Focus is built on cSound™ Architecture with advanced speckle reduction imaging and offers a range of multi-purpose and specialty probes. The ultrasound system is also equipped with a High Definition Ultrasound (HDU) display that aims to provide enhanced clarity and crisp images, helping clinicians visualize subtle structures and fine tissue differences, and advanced flow visualization tools designed to provide users with the flexibility to view flow with more clarity.
A third-party study showed that 90 percent of participants rated the overall image quality of LOGIQ Focus as excellent, and the ultrasound system was 26 percent faster than the predicate system. i,ii The Vscan Air™ CL probe is compatible with the LOGIQ Focus, giving clinicians added flexibility with wireless, cable-free scanning.
LOGIQ Focus supports a range of imaging tools and digital solutions designed to streamline workflow, minimize re-work and interruptions while keeping clinicians in control and supporting more informed clinical decisions:
AI-enabled and automation   tools designed to reduce manual steps, save time and improve consistency across users, including Auto Preset Assistant that automatically detects the anatomy being scanned and activates the corresponding preset. Clinicians can save up to five clicks during each exam with this tool and spend up to 25 percent less time on AI-automated tasks. iii,iv 
Productivity tools designed to help standardize exams, produce reproducible images, and streamline reporting like AutoEF, which automatically measures ejection fraction—a widely used measurement to assess heart function—and Scan Assistant, which guides users through exam protocols.
Verisound digital tools include Verisound Collab v for virtual collaboration, allowing clinicians to easily communicate within their network.
Comprehensive liver solutions to improve liver assessments, including Ultrasound-Guided Fat Fraction , enabling more consistent assessment of liver fat burden and 2D shear wave elastography, supporting the evaluation of tissue stiffness changes associated with fibrosis.
"We designed LOGIQ Focus around what clinicians told us they need most: confidence on the first pass, a workflow that keeps pace, and a system they can count on to be there when they need it," said Michael Greene , General Manager, General Imaging, Primary Care and Automated Breast Ultrasound , USS, GE HealthCare . "LOGIQ Focus includes features so care teams spend less time on the system and more time with the patient, on a connected platform designed to evolve with their needs."
LOGIQ Focus is designed to perform consistently over time, simplify clinical operations, and remain serviceable and secure. The system incorporates SonoDefense, a multilayer cybersecurity approach for GE HealthCare ultrasound devices, which uses a defense-in-depth strategy with security controls deployed in multiple independent layers to help keep systems functional and protect patient data.
LOGIQ Focus is part of a wave of innovation across GE HealthCare's portfolio supported by more than $5 billion in innovation investment since 2023. LOGIQ Focus is one of the several new products expected to contribute 1 to 2 percent of revenue growth for the company.
LOGIQ Focus is 510(k) cleared and CE Marked. These ultrasound systems are available in other markets where regulatory approval has been granted. For more information, visit: https://www.gehealthcare.com/en/products/ultrasound/logiq/logiq-focus .

title: BASF and HSCC are pursuing a potential joint venture across the polyamide 6 value chain
query: https://www.basf.com/global/en/investors/calendar-and-publications/investor-releases
content_text:
BASF and HSCC are pursuing a potential joint venture across the polyamide 6 value chain
Braine l’Alleud, Belgium, and Fuzhou, China; October 19, 2026 – BASF SE and Highsun Holding Group (HSCC) have signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding to explore the combination of their respective European activities across the polyamide 6 (PA6) value chain in a 50:50 joint venture. Additionally, both companies are evaluating the inclusion of their global extrusion activities outside of North America in the joint venture. The engineering plastics downstream businesses of BASF and HSCC are not in scope of the evaluation. 
“The European chemical industry needs to become more competitive. It requires supportive industrial policies as well as consolidation to create stronger companies that are better positioned to compete successfully on a global scale. BASF intends to actively shape this development,” said Dr. Markus Kamieth, Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors of BASF SE. “Together with HSCC, we are exploring opportunities to strengthen our polyamide 6 businesses by combining the most competitive assets, the best technologies and the best commercial expertise both companies have to offer. The combination of selected complementary assets in a cost-efficient setup would strengthen our competitive position through improved asset utilization and lower costs, supporting attractive long-term offerings for our customers.”
Project teams from both companies have been established and will advance the evaluation of the potential cooperation.
As a leading producer of polyamide 6 and precursors, BASF is serving multiple industries including packaging and textiles. With production assets in Ludwigshafen, Germany; Antwerp, Belgium; Caojing, China; and Freeport, Texas, the company operates one of the largest production networks for polyamides worldwide. 
“BASF is a global leading chemical company with outstanding technological capabilities and deep industry heritage. We are looking forward to examining possible collaboration opportunities with BASF to jointly take our polyamide 6 and precursor businesses to the next level. We believe this cooperation could unlock strong synergies between both parties and deliver more competitive products and solutions to customers,” said Chen Zhong, President and CEO of HSCC.
Headquartered in Fuzhou, Fujian Province, China, HSCC is a multinational enterprise integrating chemicals, chemical fibers, and advanced new materials. The group is recognized as a leading producer of caprolactam and operates 31 manufacturing centers at different locations in China as well as in Europe, building a fully integrated value chain from basic chemical raw materials to high end new materials.
  
About BASF 
At BASF, we create chemistry for a sustainable future. Our ambition: We want to be the preferred chemical company to enable our customers’ green transformation. We combine economic success with environmental protection and social responsibility. Around 95,000 employees in the BASF Group contribute to the success of our customers in nearly all sectors and almost every country in the world. Our portfolio comprises, as core businesses, the segments Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, and Nutrition & Care; our standalone businesses are bundled in the segments Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. BASF generated sales of around €60 billion in 2025. BASF shares are traded on the stock exchange in Frankfurt (BAS) and as American Depositary Receipts (BASFY) in the United States. Further information at  www.basf.com . 
 
About Highsun Holding Group (HSCC)  
Founded in Fujian China in 1984, HSCC, the world’s leading caprolactam producer, delivers comprehensive solutions across the polyamide industry chain and advanced new materials. Headquartered in Changle, Fuzhou, Fujian Province, the company operates four global industrial bases in Fujian Province, Jiangsu Province, Guangdong Province, and Limburg, the Netherlands. Collaborating with leading industry partners, HSCC drives the large-scale adoption of sustainable technologies – including chemical recycling – pioneering the transition to a zero-carbon future. By aligning industrial progress with environmental stewardship, the company fosters a symbiotic relationship between economic growth and planetary well-being. Further information at  www.hscc.com .

Chemours and Local Officials Take Action to Protect Refrigerant Intellectual Property at Chillventa
October 19, 2026
PDF Version 
Action reflects Chemours' commitment to innovation, intellectual property protection, our customers, and fair competition in the refrigerants industry 
WILMINGTON, Del. , Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Chemours Company ("Chemours") (NYSE: CC), a global chemistry company, today announces that it has taken action to protect its intellectual property relating to refrigerant technology during Chillventa 2026 in Nuremberg, Germany . Local courts issued injunctions against four companies infringing upon Chemours' intellectual property and patents of select hydrofluoroolefin (HFO) refrigerant blends.
This action showcases Chemours' unwavering commitment to protecting its innovation and intellectual property investments in advanced refrigerant technologies and across applications. Enforcing intellectual property rights supports industry-wide innovation, fair competition, our customers, and continued technology development.
"Innovation does not happen by accident; it is built on years of research, development, and investment," said Joseph Martinko , President, Thermal & Specialized Solutions at Chemours. "Protecting intellectual property is essential to preserving incentives for innovation, advancing refrigerant technology, and supporting fair competition. Chemours will continue to take appropriate action to defend its intellectual property rights and protect the innovations that help our customers meet evolving industry needs."
Chemours is actively working with enforcement authorities around the globe and educating customers, vendors, and other stakeholders to raise awareness about these Patent Infringing products and the importance of buying genuine refrigerants .
About The Chemours Company 
The Chemours Company (NYSE: CC) is a global leader in providing industrial and specialty chemicals products for markets, including coatings, plastics, refrigeration and air conditioning, transportation, semiconductor and advanced electronics, general industrial, and oil and gas. Through our three businesses – Thermal & Specialized Solutions, Titanium Technologies, and Advanced Performance Materials – we deliver application expertise and chemistry-based innovations that solve customers' biggest challenges. Our flagship products are sold under prominent brands such as Opteon™, Freon™, Ti-Pure™, Nafion™, Teflon™, Viton™, and Krytox™. Headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware and listed on the NYSE under the symbol CC, Chemours has approximately 5,700 employees and 28 manufacturing sites and serves approximately 2,400 customers in approximately 110 countries. Evonik is expanding its ruminant portfolio with the launch of Lypron®, a rumen-protected lysine solution designed to deliver targeted amino acid nutrition and support efficient, balanced feeding strategies in modern livestock production.
query: https://www.evonik.com/en/media.html
content_text:
Evonik launches Lypron® to complete its amino acid balancing concept for ruminants 
Delivers targeted lysine for precise amino acid balancing 
High and reliable metabolizable lysine that supports consistent performance in ruminants 
Non-GMO solution that enhances nitrogen efficiency for more sustainable production
Essen, Germany. Evonik is expanding its ruminant portfolio with the launch of Lypron®, a rumen-protected lysine solution designed to deliver targeted amino acid nutrition and support efficient, balanced feeding strategies in modern livestock production.
Developed in collaboration with Sipena, a French specialist in coating technologies that will exclusively manufacture the product for Evonik, Lypron® delivers metabolizable lysine precisely where it is needed. This ensures optimal utilisation of nutrients to support high performance in ruminants.
Lysine is one of the most limiting amino acids in ruminant nutrition and plays a critical role in performance. With its high and reliable metabolizable lysine content, Lypron® enables producers to balance diets for amino acids more precisely, boosting profitability by reducing the need for expensive protein sources.
“With Lypron®, we are expanding our ruminant solutions to complement our established products like Mepron®,” said Marion Hax, Head of the Specialty Nutrition Product Line at Evonik Animal Nutrition. “Completing our amino acid balancing concept allows us to support customers in achieving both higher performance and more sustainable feeding strategies.”
By improving the dietary amino acid balance, Lypron® supports the use of low protein diets, optimizing nitrogen utilization. This can contribute to lower nitrogen excretion, helping farms reduce environmental impact while maintaining productivity.
“Lypron® helps nutritionists optimize amino acid supply, increase productivity, and reduce reliance on excess dietary protein, which is increasingly important both economically and environmentally,” said Claudia Parys, Global Head of the Ruminant Business at Evonik Animal Nutrition.
Lypron® enables more flexible feeding strategies, including low protein and soy reduced diets. As a non-GMO solution, it supports market requirements in regions where GMO free production is essential, while maintaining high performance standards.
Evonik: Leading beyond chemistry
Evonik goes beyond the boundaries of chemistry with its combination of innovative strength and leading technological expertise. The global chemical company, headquartered in Essen, Germany, is active in more than 100 countries and generated sales of €14.1 billion and earnings (adjusted EBITDA) of €1.9 billion in 2025. The common motivation of the approximately 31,000 employees: to provide customers with a decisive competitive advantage with tailor-made products and solutions as a superforce for industry, thereby improving people's lives. In all markets. Every day.
About Advanced Technologies
The Advanced Technologies segment includes Evonik’s market-leading businesses that leverage technological expertise and process know-how. These businesses feature high-performance polymers and crosslinking agents, hydrogen peroxide and silica, as well as feed ingredients. In 2025, the segment generated sales of €5.9 billion with around 9,200 employees.
