title: AGC Biologics to Support Development and Manufacturing of Flen Health’s Next-Generation Enzyme Therapy for Diabetic Foot Ulcers
source: Asahi Glass - News releases (newsroom JSON list)
query: https://www.agc.com/en/news/detail/news_all.json
content_text:
AGC Biologics to Support Development and Manufacturing of Flen Health’s Next-Generation Enzyme Therapy for Diabetic Foot Ulcers
－Providing process development and GMP manufacturing services for recombinant enzymes－
AGC Biologics, a global biopharmaceutical contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) within the AGC Group, has entered into an agreement with Belgian biopharmaceutical company Flen Health to provide process development and GMP* manufacturing services for recombinant enzymes for use in a next-generation therapy for diabetic foot ulcers.
At its Heidelberg site in Germany, AGC Biologics will carry out process development and manufacturing activities for lactoperoxidase and glucose oxidase. This work will support Flen Health's planned Investigational New Drug (IND) application and Phase II clinical trial in the United States.
Advancing a Next-Generation Enzyme Therapy for Diabetic Foot Ulcers 
In 2024, approximately 589 million adults worldwide, or about one in nine, were living with diabetes. Its prevalence is projected to rise further. 
Diabetic foot ulcers are chronic wounds that develop on the feet of people with diabetes. More than one in five people with diabetes are estimated to be at risk of developing a diabetic foot ulcer during their lifetime. Effective treatment options remain limited, creating a strong need for new therapeutic approaches. 
To address this unmet medical need, Flen Health is developing a next-generation therapy using recombinant enzymes. The therapy is based on Flaminal ® , Flen Health’s wound treatment gel that combines enzymes and alginate and is marketed primarily in Europe.
Expanding the Collaboration from a Feasibility Program to GMP Manufacturing 
AGC Biologics and Flen Health began a feasibility program in July 2025. At its Heidelberg site, AGC Biologics has since undertaken technology transfer for the manufacturing processes of lactoperoxidase and glucose oxidase. It has also developed cultivation and purification processes and implemented analytical methods. 
Under the new agreement, the collaboration will advance to the next stage, covering process development, scale-up and GMP manufacturing. AGC Biologics plans to manufacture the recombinant enzymes at the 100-liter and 1,000-liter scales.
AGC Biologics Heidelberg Site 
Development Activities at the Heidelberg Site 
Under its medium-term management plan, AGC plus-2026 , the AGC Group has defined three social values that it aims to create through its products and technologies. One of these values is “Well-being.” The Group aims to contribute to safe, secure and healthy living by ensuring the stable provision of products and services essential to daily life and healthcare.
Through its Life Science business, the AGC Group provides CDMO services for biopharmaceuticals and a wide range of other modalities. By supporting customers from early-stage development through commercial production, the Group aims to contribute to the health of people worldwide.
〈Notes〉 
* 
GMP: Good Manufacturing Practice. GMP refers to standards designed to ensure pharmaceutical quality and safety by controlling the entire process from the receipt of raw materials through manufacturing and shipment. 
About Flen Health 
Flen Health is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to developing innovative therapies for unmet needs in wound care. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Kontich, Belgium, the company has more than 25 years of experience delivering trusted wound and skin healing solutions across Europe and in more than 40 countries worldwide. Flen Health is now leveraging this expertise to bring its novel therapeutics to the U.S. market. For more information, visit www.flenhealth.com . 
About the AGC Group 
AGC Inc. is a global materials company operating across a wide range of products and industries. Founded in 1907 with flat glass production as its original business, AGC has expanded its operations in line with changing societal needs, providing materials and solutions based on its core material and production technologies. Today, the AGC Group operates in more than 30 countries and regions, with businesses spanning glass, electronics, chemicals, life science, and ceramics. Guided by its purpose, “AGC, an everyday essential part of our world,” the Group provides value to society through the pursuit of innovation.

title: Research conducted at University of Michigan published in Anesthesia & Analgesia Practice demonstrates GE HealthCare End-tidal Control software may help to reduce fresh gas flow
query: https://investor.gehealthcare.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Research conducted at University of Michigan published in Anesthesia & Analgesia Practice demonstrates GE HealthCare End-tidal Control software may help to reduce fresh gas flow
October 16, 2026
PDF Version 
Study of nearly 13,000 adult general anesthesia cases found clinician use of End-tidal Control software i at a large multisite academic medical center was associated with a reduction in fresh gas flow, sevoflurane consumption and estimated CO 2 equivalents during maintenance of anesthesia
End-tidal Control software automatically adjusts fresh gas flow concentrations of O 2 and anesthetic agent concentrations to maintain targets set by the clinician, and, as one study shows, with more accuracy versus manual control for safe ii , low-flow iii anesthesia
CHICAGO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 16, 2026--
GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) today announced the publication of research conducted at the University of Michigan iv evaluating the use of End-tidal Control software across a large multisite academic health system in Anesthesia & Analgesia Practice . The retrospective observational study analyzed 12,818 adult general anesthesia cases performed at University of Michigan Health – Ann Arbor locations between April 1, 2023 and September 30, 2024 on anesthesia machines with End-tidal Control software.
The study found End-tidal Control was used in 6,755 cases (52.7%) and its use was associated with:
62.3% reduction in median fresh gas flow during maintenance of anesthesia
39.3% reduction in sevoflurane consumption
“Health systems are looking for practical ways to support clinicians while advancing more sustainable care,” said John Beard , MD, anesthesiologist and Chief Medical Officer of Patient Care Solutions at GE HealthCare . “This research at the University of Michigan adds important real-world evidence of End-tidal Control use at scale and how it may help reduce fresh gas flows and anesthetic agent consumption.”
End-tidal Control software supports the clinician in maintaining clinician-set targets for end-tidal anesthetic agent and oxygen concentrations with greater accuracy than manual adjustments. v End-tidal Control supports low-flow anesthesia, which may help reduce the amount of anesthetic agent utilized and potentially lower greenhouse gas emissions and costs. vi 
“Our team wanted to understand not only if End-tidal Control would be chosen for use in routine practice, but also how its use was associated with anesthesia delivery and environmental measures across a large academic health system,” said Douglas A. Colquhoun, MB ChB, MSc, MPH, Associate Professor of Anesthesiology at the University of Michigan vii . “These findings suggest that End-tidal Control had a high adoption rate and, when used in real-world practice by anesthesia clinical teams it could translate to significant reductions in fresh gas flow resulting in projected cost saving and benefits for the environment.”
The study also found variation in End-tidal Control use was significantly driven by the in-room anesthesia clinician, underscoring the importance of workflow, education and implementation considerations when deploying anesthesia technologies at scale.
GE HealthCare designs anesthesia solutions to support care that can help clinicians think one step ahead. End-tidal Control software can be used with the Aisys™ CS 2 anesthesia delivery system to enhance perioperative care.

title: GE HealthCare's MINItrace™ Magni achieves CE Mark; Copper-64 expands PETtrace™ Solid Target Platform beyond Gallium-68

GE HealthCare's MINItrace™ Magni achieves CE Mark; Copper-64 expands PETtrace™ Solid Target Platform beyond Gallium-68
October 15, 2026
PDF Version 
MINItrace Magni combines a compact, self-shielded design with automated operation to help healthcare providers establish and expand local production of radioisotopes used in PET tracers
Copper-64 expands the PETtrace Solid Target Platform beyond Gallium-68, supporting research in both copper-based imaging agents and the potential Copper-64/Copper-67 theranostic pair
CHICAGO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 15, 2026--
GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) today announced that its MINItrace Magni cyclotron has achieved CE Mark and that its PETtrace Solid Target Platform is expanding beyond Gallium-68 with support for Copper-64 (⁶⁴Cu) production. Together, the developments reflect the company’s focus on helping institutions build the production capabilities behind their molecular imaging programs—from establishing local PET radioisotope production to supporting research into emerging radiopharmaceuticals.
For healthcare providers building or expanding a positron emission tomography (PET) program, access to tracers is an important consideration. Many PET radioisotopes have short half-lives, making proximity between production and use a factor in supply planning. Cyclotrons produce these radioisotopes, which can then be incorporated into radiotracers used in PET imaging. Local production can give providers greater control over supply and scheduling while reducing reliance on external production and transportation.
“The molecular imaging landscape is being reshaped by the expansion of theranostics, the introduction of new PET tracers, and demand across oncology, neurology and cardiology,” said Erez Levy , Vice President of Molecular Imaging at GE HealthCare . “As tracer portfolios broaden, healthcare providers need reliable access to radioisotopes and the flexibility to respond to changing clinical needs. That calls for a longer-term view of radiopharmaceutical production—one that supports established services while allowing institutions to prepare for new clinical and research applications.”
MINItrace™ Magni: supporting local production through compact design and automation
For institutions seeking to establish or expand in-house production, MINItrace Magni brings together a compact, self-shielded design and simplified operation. The cyclotron is designed to produce Fluorine-18 (¹⁸F), Carbon-11 (¹¹C), Oxygen-15 (¹⁵O) and Nitrogen-13 (¹³N) for PET tracers. Its CE Mark represents an important milestone for a system designed around the needs of in-house PET radioisotope production.
Aiming to help extend day-to-day operations, MINItrace Magni features an intuitive user interface and a three-click workflow designed to streamline routine production steps. Automated features are intended to simplify setup and operation, including auto-tuning, which prepares the cyclotron and targets, tunes the beam and manages target irradiation.
Producing the radioisotope is only one part of preparing a PET tracer. When used with GE HealthCare’s TRACERcenter Solutions, MINItrace Magni is designed to support a broader PET radiopharmacy workflow based on an institution’s clinical, operational and tracer-production needs. This approach supports providers in developing tailored local radiopharmaceutical capabilities aligned to the specific requirements of their molecular imaging programs, while considering both current and future departmental needs to create a sustainable holistic solution.
Copper-64: broadening the possibilities for PETtrace production
Alongside decisions about where to produce radioisotopes, institutions must consider which radioisotopes their programs will need. For those seeking to broaden their production capabilities, the addition of Copper-64 extends the PETtrace Solid Target Platform beyond the production of Gallium-68, for which it was introduced in 2022, and Zirconium-89, which was made available in early 2026. The capability broadens the range of isotopes that may be produced using PETtrace cyclotron infrastructure, allowing customers to build on the platform as their isotope needs evolve.
Copper-64’s relevance includes exploring its potential role in connecting imaging with investigational therapeutic applications. It enables PET imaging and is also being studied with investigational Copper-67 agents as a potential diagnostic and therapeutic pair. This research sits within the broader field of theranostics, which connects molecular imaging with targeted radionuclide therapy. Clinical research is evaluating Copper-64-labeled compounds in areas including prostate cancer and HER2-positive breast cancer.
Supporting that work involves more than the cyclotron alone. GE HealthCare’s capabilities in cyclotrons, targetry, radiochemistry synthesis, molecular imaging and services are intended to help institutions establish solid-target production as part of a broader radiopharmacy workflow.
“A molecular imaging program needs a plan for the tracers it uses today and the ones it may want to explore tomorrow,” said Nicolas Durand-Schaefer , General Manager, Molecular Imaging, International, GE HealthCare . “MINItrace Magni’s CE Mark is an important milestone for a compact, versatile cyclotron designed to support local radioisotope production and enable healthcare providers to build radiopharmacy capabilities without the need for large-scale production infrastructure. Adding Copper-64 to PETtrace broadens the platform’s capabilities to support copper-based imaging and theranostics research. Our focus is on helping institutions connect the practical demands of running a radiopharmacy with their longer-term clinical and research ambitions.”
Both developments build on more than 40 years of GE HealthCare experience in cyclotron and PET radiopharmacy technologies, extending the company’s focus on the production capabilities and workflows that support molecular imaging.

title: Tungsten supply: Europe must act now

content_text:
Tungsten supply: Europe must act now 
VDMA calls for a stronger European raw materials strategy 
Published by: Plansee Group 
· 
Last updated:
15. October 2026 
Due to its unique properties, tungsten is indispensable for numerous applications in the high-tech industry. At the same time, Europe’s supply of this critical raw material is coming under increasing pressure. The VDMA, the largest network organization for mechanical engineering in Germany and Europe, warns of the risks associated with heavy dependence on just a few supplier countries, which are currently reflected in market disruptions and rising prices. A secure raw materials supply is essential for industrial value creation and competitiveness in Europe. 
In its current position paper, “A secure tungsten supply for European industry,” the VDMA therefore calls for targeted measures to make Europe’s raw materials supply more resilient over the long term. 
The focus is on four key demands: 
Strengthening the European circular economy 
Securing access to primary raw materials 
Effective protection against state-subsidized dumping imports 
Improving the industrial framework conditions in Europe 
Recycling and strategic partnerships for a resilient tungsten supply 
CERATIZIT, a business area of the Plansee Group, is a member of the VDMA. The Plansee Group is the largest tungsten supplier in the Western world and has systematically made its raw materials supply more resilient over many years. Recycling plays a central role in this: 92 percent of the tungsten processed comes from recycled material. The Plansee Group keeps valuable tungsten in the cycle and reduces the need for primary raw materials. In addition, the company relies on long-term offtake agreements with mine operators to secure the long-term supply of tungsten. 
“A resilient raw materials supply does not emerge overnight. The Plansee Group set important priorities for this more than two decades ago. For European industry to remain competitive and become more independent in the long term, reliable political framework conditions and effective measures for a secure raw materials supply are needed.” – Karlheinz Wex, Executive Board Chairman of the Plansee Group 
Read more about the background and specific demands in the full VDMA position paper “Tungsten Supply Under Pressure: Europe Must Act Now” . 
Related links
VDMA

About the Plansee Group: Focus on Molybdenum and Tungsten
With its products, the Plansee Group enables applications at the cutting edge of what is technically and physically feasible – in electronics, medical technology, energy supply, mechanical engineering, the construction industry, mobility, and security and defense. 
Headquartered in Reutte, Tyrol, the group specializes in the powder metallurgical processing of the high-performance materials molybdenum and tungsten . The value chain extends from the processing of scrap and ore concentrates through the manufacture of intermediate products and blanks to the development and production of customer-specific components and tools. 
The Plansee Group, with its parent company Plansee Holding AG, unites two strong business areas : 
· Plansee High-Performance Materials, specializing in metallic products made of molybdenum and tungsten. 
· Ceratizit, focused on tools made of hard metal (tungsten carbide) for the trades, machining, and industrial manufacturing. 
The Plansee Group ensures long-term security of supply for its key materials through recycling and long-term partnerships with mining operators. The Plansee Group holds a 31 percent stake in the Chilean molybdenum processor Molymet and a 10 percent stake in the tungsten mining operator Almonty. 
With 11,120 employees at 36 production sites, the Plansee Group generated consolidated revenue of 2.35 billion euros in fiscal year 2025/26. The fiscal year ends on the last day of February.

title: AGC Uses Generative AI to Turn Manufacturing Expertise into Organizational Knowledge
source: Asahi Glass - News releases (newsroom JSON list)

AGC Uses Generative AI to Turn Manufacturing Expertise into Organizational Knowledge
－Voice data supports knowledge transfer and more advanced improvement activities－
AGC (AGC Inc., Headquarters: Tokyo; President: Yoshinori Hirai), a world-leading manufacturer of glass, chemicals and other high-tech materials, has jointly developed SmartLogger ® Voice with Computer Engineering & Consulting Ltd. (“CEC”; Headquarters: Tokyo; President: Takashi Himeno). The speech recognition-based data collection system is designed to streamline the collection of work logs at manufacturing sites.
AGC applies transcription and generative AI-based data structuring and analysis to the voice data collected by the system. This process converts shop-floor know-how and decision-making information into digital assets that can be used across the organization.
Conceptual overview of SmartLogger ® Voice 
Verification at AGC manufacturing sites confirmed reductions in the time required for work analysis and the preparation of knowledge-transfer materials. The verification also confirmed that tacit knowledge, such as the experience and decision-making criteria of skilled workers, can be accumulated as organizational knowledge. Rapidly organizing and sharing shop-floor information has also helped support more advanced data-driven decision-making.
Manufacturers face continuing challenges in improving productivity, addressing labor shortages, and transferring the knowledge and experience of skilled workers to the next generation. Much of this know-how exists in conversations and verbal explanations during daily operations and often goes unrecorded and underutilized. By using SmartLogger ® Voice, AGC can continuously capture knowledge generated on the shop floor and manage it as a reusable digital asset.
AGC plans to expand the application of the system to areas including safety activities, equipment maintenance and knowledge management. Through these efforts, AGC aims to accelerate the digitalization of shop-floor knowledge and advance its value creation DX ＊ initiatives.
The AGC Group has positioned the promotion of value creation DX as one of the key strategies under its medium-term management plan AGC plus-2026 . The Group is combining its manufacturing expertise with digital technologies to improve productivity, create new value and strengthen competitiveness. AGC will continue to explore the use of advanced technologies, including generative AI, to support the transformation of manufacturing operations and sustainable growth.
Use Case 1: Streamlining Shop-Floor Work Analysis by Reducing Analysis Time by 90% or More Compared with Conventional Approaches 
AGC uses SmartLogger ® Voice for shop-floor work analysis, which was previously conducted using stopwatches and video cameras. Workers verbally record the tasks they perform, and generative AI automatically organizes and analyzes the resulting data.
This approach has reduced work analysis time to one-tenth or less of the conventional level. It has also significantly reduced the workload associated with data collection and analysis, helping accelerate the PDCA cycle for data-driven improvement activities.
Use Case 2: Combining Experience, Intuition, and Data for Knowledge Transfer and Digital Knowledge Asset Creation 
AGC uses SmartLogger ® Voice to transfer the decision-making criteria and know-how of skilled workers to the next generation. Skilled workers verbally explain key decision points and the factors they consider when making decisions on the shop floor.
Generative AI then organizes and structures the content and converts it into formats such as knowledge-transfer materials, decision flows and Q&A documents. This process enables knowledge traditionally dependent on individual experience and professional judgment to be transformed into digital assets that can be shared and utilized across the organization.
SmartLogger ® Voice in use for shop-floor work analysis at AGC's Yokohama Technical Center 
* 
DX (Digital Transformation):
Refers to the use of digital technologies and data-driven approaches to improve business processes, operational efficiency, and value creation. 
Development of SmartLogger ® Voice 
Roles of AGC and CEC 
・ 
AGC Inc.: Developed software that converts voice data into text and generates structured data 
・ 
Computer Engineering & Consulting Ltd.: Developed the speech-recognition technology and voice-data collection system 
Main Features of SmartLogger ® Voice 
・ 
Data collection without interrupting work: A voice-triggered recording function captures spoken information during work. 
・ 
No device operation required: Workers can record information while maintaining their normal workflow. 
・ 
Improved efficiency from data collection through analysis: Collecting only the required data reduces the workload involved in data organization and analysis.

AGC Inc. is a global materials company operating across a wide range of products and industries. Today, the AGC Group operates in more than 30 countries and regions, with businesses spanning glass, electronics, chemicals, life science, and ceramics. title: onsemi and Sungrow Advance Utility-Scale Energy Storage Performance with SiC Hybrid Technology

onsemi and Sungrow Advance Utility-Scale Energy Storage Performance with SiC Hybrid Technology
October 14, 2026 at 6:01 AM EDT
PDF Version 
Advanced EliteSiC hybrid technology maximizes usable energy as electricity demand surges
Summary 
As AI-driven electricity demand accelerates worldwide, utilities and energy providers are under growing pressure to store and deliver energy more efficiently. Battery energy storage system (BESS) providers are seeking advanced power conversion technologies to improve performance and system economics. To address these needs, Sungrow has adopted onsemi’s latest SiC hybrid power module technology for its PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform. The design improves system efficiency, helping utilities and energy providers increase usable energy output while lowering operating costs.
News Highlights 
onsemi’s EliteSiC hybrid power module enables the highest-density battery energy storage system deployments, helping energy providers meet growing electricity demand from AI, renewable energy and electrification
New BESS architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, helping maximize energy delivered to the grid while reducing losses and improving reliability
Sungrow’s PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform integrates onsemi’s latest EliteSiC hybrid power module technology, optimized for high-power DC-AC energy conversion in utility-scale battery storage applications
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- onsemi (Nasdaq: ON) today announced that Sungrow, a global leader in renewable energy technology, has adopted onsemi’s latest EliteSiC silicon carbide (SiC) hybrid power module technology for the Sungrow PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform. The integration enables improved efficiency and enhanced system performance for utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS).
Helping Sungrow Deliver More Usable Energy 
The PowerTitan 3.0 platform incorporates onsemi’s high-density power integrated modules (PIMs) , optimized for advanced three-level inverter architectures used in high-power energy storage applications.
Compared with the previous-generation platform, the new architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, enabling higher-power battery storage deployments without sacrificing efficiency. The architecture supports power conversion units rated up to 450 kW, contributing to the platform’s increased power density and higher-power deployment capability.
With the performance advantages of SiC , the solution supports key system-level benefits including:
Peak efficiency exceeding 99.3% to reduce energy loss in utility-scale systems
Increased power density supports higher-power BESS deployments
Enhanced thermal performance supports reliable operation in high-power applications
Improved system economics through a hybrid SiC design optimized for large-scale deployment
The design win builds on a long-standing strategic relationship between onsemi and Sungrow. Through extensive engineering and validation activities, the companies collaborated throughout platform definition, system optimization and qualification to meet the demanding performance requirements of next-generation energy storage deployments.
“PowerTitan 3.0 represents Sungrow’s continued innovation in advanced energy storage system design,” said Chen Peng, General Manager of Energy Storage Conversion Product Line at Sungrow Energy Storage Business Unit. “By integrating advanced technologies and collaborating with strategic partners such as onsemi, Sungrow is accelerating the deployment of higher-performance storage solutions that deliver greater value throughout the lifecycle of energy assets. With growing market recognition, Sungrow estimates delivering 10 GWh of PowerTitan 3.0 across Europe in 2026, further supporting the region’s transition toward a more flexible and resilient energy system.”
“At utility scale, even small improvements in power conversion efficiency can have a meaningful impact on battery energy storage system (BESS) performance and total cost of ownership,” said Sergio Fissore, Vice President and General Manager, IPD Power Division, onsemi. “Our EliteSiC hybrid power module enables higher-efficiency, higher-density energy storage systems that help maximize usable energy and improve system reliability. Together with Sungrow, we're advancing the power conversion technologies needed to support the next generation of energy infrastructure.”
Why Fractions of a Percent Matter 
At utility scale, even small efficiency improvements can generate meaningful financial and environmental benefits. According to onsemi analysis, a 0.4% efficiency improvement delivered by the new SiC hybrid module could save more than 475 MWh of energy annually in a 100 MW battery energy storage installation compared with the previous-generation module.
Those energy savings can help reduce operating costs, increase usable energy delivered to customers and lower overall emissions. The architecture also enables higher overload capability and improved thermal performance, helping customers extract more usable energy from every storage asset.
Supporting the Infrastructure Behind the AI Era 
Utilities and energy providers are seeking ways to store more energy, reduce conversion losses and improve overall system economics to meet unprecedented demand amid the AI infrastructure buildout and electrification transition.
Industry forecasts project the battery energy storage market will more than double by 2030 as utilities invest in infrastructure needed to support increasing electricity demand and renewable energy deployment. At the same time, energy storage providers are moving toward higher-power, higher-voltage architectures to improve system economics.

Danaher Collaborates with NVIDIA to Advance Autonomous Science
Collaboration will bring together NVIDIA AI technologies and Danaher's scientific instruments, laboratory workflows and data 
WASHINGTON , Oct. 14, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Danaher Corporation (NYSE: DHR) today announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to advance autonomous science and help accelerate the pace of scientific discovery. As part of Danaher's broader effort to shape the future of AI-enabled science, the companies are working to combine Danaher's scientific instrumentation, automation technologies, laboratory workflow software and domain expertise with NVIDIA accelerated computing and AI technologies. The goal is to help researchers move faster from prediction to experimental evidence, creating a continuous learning cycle where experiments inform models and models help design better experiments.
"AI is reshaping how science is conducted, and Danaher is at the forefront of that transformation," said Julie Sawyer Montgomery, President and Chief Executive Officer of Danaher. "We are collaborating around a shared vision for more connected, adaptive and accessible innovation, helping researchers solve consequential challenges and translate discovery into human impact."
"The next era of scientific discovery will be driven by a continuous loop between AI and experimentation," said Kimberly Powell, Vice President of Healthcare at NVIDIA. "Together with Danaher, we are bringing accelerated computing and physical AI into the lab - connecting models with instruments and real experimental data, where experiments improve models and models design better experiments, helping researchers compress years of discovery into months."
Danaher and NVIDIA are working to integrate AI into scientific instruments through edge computing like NVIDIA DGX Spark, accelerated analytics and data processing with RAPIDS, real-time inference, scientific reasoning and foundation model technologies, including BioNeMo Open Models. Initial efforts focus on a select group of priority instruments, with the potential to expand across a broader portfolio over time. The companies are exploring how scientific and physical AI, such as NVIDIA Cosmos world models and Omniverse Digital Twins, can support more intelligent instruments and laboratory workflows, while keeping experimental evidence at the center of scientific decision-making.
The collaboration seeks to advance Danaher's commitment to connected science by bringing AI, accelerated computing, instruments, workflows and experimental data together to produce experimental evidence. Danaher aims to help researchers reduce the time and complexity of moving from an AI-generated prediction to the experimental evidence needed to act on it, while preserving customer choice in models, standards and technology providers.

ASML reports €11.7 billion total net sales and €5.0 billion net income in Q3 2026 
Full-year 2026 total net sales expected to be between €44 billion and €45 billion, with a gross margin around 56% 
VELDHOVEN, the Netherlands, October 14, 2026 – Today, ASML Holding NV (ASML) has published its 2026 third-quarter results. 
Q3 total net sales of €11.7 billion, gross margin of 57.5%, net income of €5.0 billion
ASML expects Q4 2026 total net sales between €14.2 billion and €15.2 billion, and a gross margin around 57%
Full-year 2026 total net sales expected to be between €44 billion and €45 billion, with a gross margin around 56%

Gross margin (%) 54.0 57.5 
Net income 2,918 4,960 
EPS (basic; in euros) 7.59 12.95 
End-quarter cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments 7,582 12,735 
Numbers have been rounded for readers' convenience. A complete summary of US GAAP Consolidated Statements of Operations is published on www.asml.com.
CEO statement and outlook 
"In the third quarter we reported a record total net sales of €11.7 billion, towards the high end of our guidance, reflecting the strong execution of our ramp-up. Installed Base Management sales 1 came in above guidance at €3.3 billion as a result of the continued strong demand for productivity upgrades. This drove the gross margin above guidance at 57.5%.
"Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments. In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030. 
"With such strong visibility and an order book momentum that continues to increase quarter on quarter this year, we now expect that our supply as currently planned for both 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet the demand of our customers 2 . Given this, we are investigating ways to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase we previously communicated. In addition, we continue to provide significant wafer capacity to our customers through our productivity upgrade portfolio.
"We expect fourth-quarter 2026 total net sales between €14.2 billion and €15.2 billion, with a gross margin around 57%. We expect R&D costs of around €1.2 billion and SG&A costs of around €0.4 billion. We expect total net sales for 2026 to be between €44 billion and €45 billion, with a gross margin around 56%," said ASML President and Chief Executive Officer Christophe Fouquet.
Update share buyback program and dividend 
In the third quarter, we purchased around €4.1 billion worth of shares under the current 2026–2028 share buyback program.
An interim dividend over 2026 of €1.88 per ordinary share will be made payable on November 4, 2026.
Details of the share buyback program as well as transactions pursuant thereto, and details of the dividend are published on ASML's website (www.asml.com/investors).
1 Installed Base Management sales equals our net service and field option sales. 
2 This refers to the figures in our Q2 2026 financial results press release, where we stated that we plan to increase 2026 low NA EUV and DUV immersion capacity by 30% in 2027, and are investigating a further 30% increase for both in 2028.

About ASML 
ASML is a leading supplier to the semiconductor industry. The company provides chipmakers with hardware, software and services to mass produce the patterns of integrated circuits (microchips). Together with its partners, ASML drives the advancement of more affordable, more powerful, more energy-efficient microchips. ASML enables groundbreaking technology to solve some of humanity's toughest challenges, such as in healthcare, energy use and conservation, mobility and agriculture. ASML is a multinational company headquartered in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, with offices across EMEA, the US and Asia. Every day, ASML’s more than 45,500 employees (FTE) challenge the status quo and push technology to new limits. ASML is traded on Euronext Amsterdam and NASDAQ under the symbol ASML. Discover ASML – our products, technology and career opportunities – at www.asml.com.

ST. PAUL, Minn. and CHARLOTTE, N.C. , Oct. 14, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- 3M and Discovery Education today named 8 th  grader Raji Doshi as the winner of the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge , the nation's premier middle school science competition. Raji lives in Farmington, Connecticut, and attends Stanford Online High School. She distinguished herself by engineering a natural algae-and-aragonite system, an inventive solution to address ocean acidification by increasing alkalinity and removing carbon dioxide from seawater. As the grand prize winner, Raji received a $25,000 cash prize and the prestigious title of "America's Top Young Scientist."
Raji spent the summer competing against nine other finalists and ultimately secured the win during final Challenge events at 3M global headquarters in St. Paul, Minnesota, on Oct. 12 and 13, 2026. The 2026 finalists, ages 11 to 14, each identified an everyday problem, developed an innovative solution, and pitched their project through a one- to two-minute entry video. Their proposals aligned to 3M technology platforms including climate tech and safety, and finalists were evaluated on their creativity, scientific knowledge, communication effectiveness, ingenuity, application of STEM principles, and demonstration of research.
Raji's project, Engineering a Novel Durable Algae-Aragonite Alkalinity System to Reduce CO2-Driven Ocean Acidification , tests whether macroalgae cultivation paired with natural calcium carbonate buffers could create a durable, low-cost system for reducing coastal acidification, a growing threat to marine ecosystems. The solution reflects the 3M Young Scientist Challenge's focus on encouraging middle school students to think creatively, apply the power of STEM, and develop real-world solutions that can make a meaningful impact. Through carbonite chemistry analysis, Raji demonstrated the efficacy of aragonite in increasing algae biomass, removing carbon dioxide, and substantially lowering dissolved carbon dioxide. She also developed a Michaelis-Menten computational model to identify an optimal aragonite dose, a step toward making climate solutions more practical for coastal communities.  
"The 3M Young Scientist Challenge highlights the incredible potential of young people to tackle real-world challenges through science," said William Brown, 3M Chairman and CEO. "The talent and creativity displayed by this year's finalists was exceptional, and we congratulate Raji on earning the title of America's Top Young Scientist."
Each 3M Young Scientist Challenge finalist is paired with a 3M scientist who mentors and works with them one-on-one over the summer to transform their ideas from concept to prototype. This year's winner was paired with Deborah Isabelle, a product engineering specialist at 3M.
"Raji's project reminds us that when you're passionate about something, you can use that interest to change the world," said Isabelle. "She loves collecting seashells and was distressed that ocean acidification is starting to damage the seashells and the creatures that live inside them. It was that passion that led her to create ALKACORE to address the ocean acidification issue."
The second and third place winners from the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge also receive special recognition, including a $1,000 prize. This year's runners-up are:
Aaisha Asif , a 7th grader from Sarasota, Fla., Pine View, Sarasota County Schools
Sharvi Mahajan , a 9th grader from San Diego, Calif., Westview High School, Poway Unified School District
The remaining top finalists from the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge, in alphabetical order by last name, are:
Ahmed Abdelsalam , a 7 th  grader from Cambridge, Mass., Darby Vassall Upper School, Cambridge Public Schools
Aiden Jo , a 9 th  grader from Houston, Texas, Strake Jesuit College Prepratory, Houston Independent School District
Roy Kim , an 8 th  grader from Beaverton, Ore., Whitford Middle School, Beaverton School District
Arika Kundu , an 8 th  grader from Shorewood, Minn., Minnetonka Middle School East, Minnetonka Public Schools
Millie Pradawong , a 9 th  grader from Fairfax, Va., James Madison High School, Fairfax County
Naboshree Santra , a 7 th  grader from Oviedo, Fla., Jackson Heights Middle School, Seminole County Public Schools
Abigail Stein , an 8 th  grader from Nashville, Tenn., Harding Academy, Nashville Independent Schools
"When students have the support to follow their curiosity, their ideas can grow into real-world innovation," said Brian Shaw, Chief Executive Officer of Discovery Education. "For 19 years, our partnership with 3M has paired students with working scientists who coach them from ideation to working prototype. We applaud Raji and every Young Scientist for the dedication and imagination they bring to this challenge, and we're grateful to 3M for helping us make hands-on scientific inquiry a thrill to watch."
Now in its 19th year, the 3M Young Scientist Challenge continues to inspire and challenge middle school students to think creatively and apply the power of STEM to develop real-world solutions. Former America's Top Young Scientists have given TED Talks, filed patents, founded nonprofits, and made the Forbes 30 Under 30 list. In addition, a 3M Young Scientist Challenge Alumni Network was formed in fall 2022 and includes more than 100 former challenge winners, finalists, and mentors, who take part in networking opportunities and more.
The award-winning competition supplements the 3M and Discovery Education program Young Scientist Lab , which provides no-cost dynamic digital resources for students, teachers, and families to explore, transform, and innovate the world around them. All the resources are also available on Discovery Education Experience , the essential companion for engaged PreK-12 classrooms.
To learn more about the 3M Young Scientist Challenge and meet this year's winners and finalists, visit youngscientistlab.com .
About 3M 
3M (NYSE: MMM) is focused on transforming industries around the world by applying science and creating innovative, customer-focused solutions. Our multi-disciplinary team is working to solve tough customer problems by leveraging diverse technology platforms, differentiated capabilities, global footprint, and operational excellence. Discover how 3M is shaping the future at  3M.com/news . 
About Discovery Education 
Discovery Education is a global education technology leader whose innovative solutions empower educators and progress student learning. Discovery Education's solutions have served more than 100 million students globally, supporting effective teaching and learning in 45% of U.S. K-12 schools and in 100+ countries and territories. The company's portfolio includes award-winning core and supplemental curriculum, high-quality standards-aligned content, and AI-enabled teaching and learning tools. Solutions span math, science, literacy, social studies, and career-connected learning, including instructionally-aligned content developed through one-of-a-kind partnerships with industry leaders to bring real-world relevance into every lesson. News Releases
Sumitomo Chemical Launches New Fungicide Velera™ in Paraguay
Expanding the Overseas Rollout of Products Containing the New Active Ingredient Pavecto™ 
Oct. 14, 2026
Sumitomo Chemical has launched its product Velera™, a fungicide containing the active ingredient Pavecto™ (active ingredient trademark; common name: metyltetraprole), in Paraguay in South America. This marks the Company’s first time bringing to market a product containing Pavecto™ outside of Japan.
Pavecto™ is one of the active ingredients included in B2020, the Company’s pipeline of products to be submitted for registration in major markets by 2020. It is expected to become a blockbuster product that will drive the growth of the Sumitomo Chemical Group’s agricultural business. Through the internal and external evaluations that have been conducted to date, Pavecto™ has been confirmed to be effective against pathogens resistant to existing QoI fungicides (*1) , and is expected to contribute to fungicide resistance management. In addition, based on its efficacy, Pavecto™ is the only fungicidal active ingredient positioned in Subgroup 11A (*2) , which was newly established under Group 11, to which QoI fungicides belong, by the Fungicide Resistance Action Committee (*3) .
Velera™ is a fungicide that contains Pavecto™ as its active ingredient and has been registered for use on soybeans in Paraguay. It provides protection from major soybean diseases, including target spot, and late-season diseases such as Cercospora leaf blight, purple seed stain, and Septoria brown spot. Sumitomo Chemical believes this product will offer agricultural producers a new option for protecting crops and ensuring crop yields.
Pavecto™ and products containing it have been available in Japan since 2023. Outside Japan, Velera™ has now been launched in Paraguay. Regulatory reviews by the relevant authorities for Pavecto™ and products containing it are under way in key markets such as Brazil and Europe, as well as in other countries.　Sumitomo Chemical will continue to take the necessary steps toward obtaining registrations for Pavecto™ and products containing as quickly as possible.
Sumitomo Chemical will continue to contribute to sustainable agriculture and the stable supply of food around the world. It will do so by providing innovative solutions tailored to the needs of agricultural producers.
The Product's packaging 
Velera™ logo 
(*1) A fungicide with a mode of action known as a quinone outside inhibitor (QoI), which suppresses fungal growth by inhibiting mitochondrial respiration in pathogens and thereby stopping energy production.
(*2) Based on Sumitomo Chemical’s research as of October 2026.
(*3) An international organization that helps prevent the development of resistance to fungicides in agriculture and proposes suitable use methods.

Rio Tinto releases third quarter 2026 production results
14 October 2026
share
Strong operational performance at Oyu Tolgoi copper and Pilbara iron ore 
MELBOURNE, Australia--(BUSINESS WIRE)--
Rio Tinto Chief Executive Simon Trott said: “We delivered strong operational performance in the third quarter. Oyu Tolgoi copper production increased 29% year-to-date, with the operation running at a ~450 kt annualised rate in the quarter, and global iron ore sales are up 3% year-to-date. The Simandou iron ore mine hit an annualised production run-rate of ~10 Mtpa (100% basis) in the quarter as the project continues to ramp up.
“We are finishing the year with momentum, with significant opportunities to accelerate improvements in safety, productivity and reliability through implementation of our operating system. We remain on track for a $1.8 billion annualised productivity benefit run-rate by the end of 2026. Our major projects remain on schedule and budget, underwriting our growth profile to 2030.
“We made further significant steps in decarbonising our business in the third quarter, with our Pacific Aluminium smelter repowering arrangements now well progressed.
“Today, we announce that we have achieved more than $2 billion 1 of capital release year-to-date, as we actively manage our portfolio with discipline to maximise long-term value, as part of the $5 to 10 billion capital release program.”
Executive Summary 
Operational excellence: ~1% YTD increase in copper equivalent (CuEq 2 ) production, driven by growth from Oyu Tolgoi copper and Pilbara iron ore.
Copper: Oyu Tolgoi production increased by 27% YoY in Q3 and 29% YTD. At Kennecott, we successfully completed the rebuild of the flash converting furnace at end-August ahead of plan.
Iron ore: Q3 global iron ore sales were 90.8 Mt, up 3% YoY, while Pilbara sales increased 2% YoY. Simandou hit an annualised production run-rate of ~10 Mtpa (100% basis) in Q3 as the project ramps up and remains on track to reach a 60 Mtpa production run-rate during H2 2028 3 .
Aluminium : Consistent, stable performance across the full operating system. Pacific smelter repowering arrangements are now well progressed, following the Tomago and Bell Bay power agreements in Q3.
Lithium : Production up 33% YTD despite adverse weather impacting Q3 operations. Fenix 1B ramp-up continues to progress well.

title: Applied Materials Set to Outperform as AI Drives Sustained Demand for Wafer Fab Equipment
query: https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Applied Materials Set to Outperform as AI Drives Sustained Demand for Wafer Fab Equipment
Oct 13, 2026 at 12:45 PM EDT
PDF Version 
Company expects strong multi-year growth as global AI infrastructure buildout fuels demand for leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging – areas where Applied has built market leadership 
Expects wafer fab equipment (WFE) spending to grow faster through 2030 than over the past decade; targets more than 2 percentage points of WFE share gain from calendar 2025 to 2030 
Targets higher profitability through 2030 with non-GAAP gross margin target of approximately 54 percent and non-GAAP operating margin target of approximately 40 percent 
Committed to distribute 80 to 100 percent of free cash flow to shareholders over time 
SAN FRANCISCO , Oct. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- At its 2026 SEMICON West Investor Breakfast Presentation held today, Applied Materials, Inc. presented its longer-term growth expectations and outlined how its leadership in materials engineering positions the company to outperform the wafer fab equipment (WFE) market over the coming years.
“The global buildout of AI infrastructure is driving a new era of growth for wafer fab equipment,” said Gary Dickerson , President and CEO of Applied Materials. “Applied Materials has built leadership in the fastest growing areas of the market that have the greatest impact on AI computing performance, power efficiency and cost, and our advanced services offerings enable chipmakers to increase yield and fab output. Our industry-leading capabilities position Applied for continued growth and outperformance in the years ahead.”
The race for AI computing leadership requires tremendous technology innovation and capacity expansion to support infrastructure scaling, which is fueling sustained WFE investments – bigger than any of the industry’s past growth drivers. The growth and diversity of AI applications from generative to agentic and physical AI require increasing amounts of silicon. Applied expects leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging to drive around 75 percent of WFE growth from 2025-2030. Applied has strong number-one process equipment positions in all three areas and is targeting to gain more than 2 percentage points of WFE market share from calendar 2025 to 2030.
To support the industry’s capacity expansion, Applied is utilizing its unique eBeam technology and advanced service solutions to help chipmakers accelerate the ramp of new process nodes and optimize yield, output and cost in high-volume manufacturing. With the industry’s highest resolution and fastest imaging capabilities, Applied’s eBeam equipment portfolio is expected to generate $2 billion in revenue in calendar year 2026. The company is expecting service revenue to grow more than 20 percent this calendar year and to exceed $12 billion in revenue by calendar year 2030, representing a mid-teens compound annual growth rate.
“For the past 10 years, Applied Materials has been making strategic investments to build the industry’s most enabling portfolio for AI computing,” said Brice Hill , Senior Vice President and CFO. “As AI drives wafer fab equipment growth, we are focused on further increasing profitability and operating leverage while investing in R&D programs that will fuel our outperformance into the future.”
Based on the company’s expectations for semiconductor industry growth, Applied is investing to more than double its R&D lab and manufacturing capacity from current levels by 2030. The company yesterday unveiled its new Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center in Silicon Valley , the world’s largest facility dedicated to collaborative semiconductor process technology and manufacturing equipment R&D. To date, Applied has announced 15 EPIC Center partnerships with leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and universities. Applied has also recently expanded its manufacturing infrastructure in Austin, Texas , Singapore and Treviso, Italy .
Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
Forward-looking non-GAAP gross margin and non-GAAP operating margin targets for 2030 assume non-GAAP adjustments as applicable for future periods, which we are unable to predict without unreasonable efforts due to their inherent uncertainty. Free cash flow is a non-GAAP measure and is defined as net cash provided by operating activities less capital expenditures. Management uses non-GAAP financial measures to evaluate the company’s operating and financial performance and for planning purposes, and as performance measures in its executive compensation program. Applied believes these measures enhance an overall understanding of its performance and investors’ ability to review the company’s business from the same perspective as the company’s management, and facilitate comparisons of results with prior periods on a consistent basis by excluding items that management does not believe are indicative of Applied’s ongoing operating performance. There are limitations in using non-GAAP financial measures because the non-GAAP financial measures are not prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, may be different from non-GAAP financial measures used by other companies, and may exclude certain items that may have a material impact upon our reported financial results.
Forward-Looking Statements 
This press release contains forward-looking statements, including those regarding anticipated growth and trends in our businesses and markets, industry outlooks and demand drivers, technology transitions, our business and financial performance and market share positions, our capital allocation and cash deployment strategies, our investment and growth strategies, our development of new products and technologies, the plans and expectations for the EPIC Center, our business outlook, expectations for our financial performance for calendar year 2026, our business and financial targets for 2030, and other statements that are not historical facts. These statements and their underlying assumptions are subject to risks and uncertainties and are not guarantees of future performance. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements include, without limitation: the level of demand for our products; global economic, political and industry conditions, including changes in interest rates and prices for goods and services; global trade issues, changes in trade and export regulations, license requirements, and their interpretation, and our ability to obtain licenses or authorizations on a timely basis, if at all; changes in tariffs, any retaliatory measures, and our ability to mitigate the impact of tariffs; the effects of geopolitical turmoil or conflicts; demand for semiconductor chips and electronic devices; customers’ technology and capacity requirements; the introduction of new and innovative technologies, and the timing of technology transitions; our ability to develop, deliver and support new products and technologies; our ability to meet customer demand, and our suppliers' ability to meet our demand requirements; the concentrated nature of our customer base; our ability to expand our current markets, increase market share and develop new markets; market acceptance of existing and newly developed products; our ability to obtain and protect intellectual property rights in key technologies; cybersecurity incidents affecting us or our suppliers, customers or vendors; our ability to achieve the objectives of operational and strategic initiatives, align our resources and cost structure with business conditions, and attract, motivate and retain key employees; acquisitions, investments and divestitures; changes in income tax laws; the variability of operating expenses and results among products and segments, and our ability to accurately forecast future results, market conditions, customer requirements and business needs; our ability to ensure compliance with applicable law, rules and regulations; and other risks and uncertainties described in our filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including our most recent Forms 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K. All forward-looking statements are based on management’s current estimates, projections and assumptions, and we assume no obligation to update them.

The technology we create is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation chips. At Applied, we push the boundaries of science and engineering to deliver material innovation that changes the world. Learn more at www.appliedmaterials.com .

title: Charles River Collaborates with Magellan Stem Cells to Advance Stem Cell and Regenerative Medicine Development
source: Charles River - News Releases / Press Releases

content_text:
View printer-friendly version 
Charles River Collaborates with Magellan Stem Cells to Advance Stem Cell and Regenerative Medicine Development
PDF Version 
Collaboration leverages next-generation sequencing (NGS) services to advance development and commercialization of an off-the-shelf therapy for osteoarthritis and future programs 
WILMINGTON, Mass. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 13, 2026--
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) and Magellan Stem Cells , a private Australian biotech and cell-therapy firm, announce their collaboration to support Magellan in the development and clinical advancement of its proprietary stem cell-based therapies and regenerative medicine solutions. The partnership will leverage Charles River’s specialized expertise in biologics quality control, current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) viral and release testing, and extensive development support services. By integrating Charles River's comprehensive testing and development solutions with Magellan’s advances in cell therapy development, manufacturing and clinical application, the collaboration aims to drive innovation and create shared value.
“Working with organizations at the forefront of innovation allows us to expand our GMP testing capabilities and help accelerate the delivery of safe, compliant therapies to patients,” said Kerstin Dolph , Corporate Senior Vice President, Global Manufacturing, Charles River. “We are excited to support Magellan as they work towards advancing Zelestrocel from the clinic to potential commercialization.”
Charles River will provide viral safety testing using cGMP Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) for Cell and Gene Therapy (CGT), supporting a high-quality therapy development process aligned with international regulatory standards. Charles River’s NGS service offering highlights the Company's commitment to the 3Rs (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) through its Alternative Methods Advancement Project™ (AMAP™), which develops and implements New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and other innovative strategies to reduce reliance on animal testing while supporting efficient product development.
Magellan recently concluded Phase I/II clinical trials of its lead proprietary allogeneic, off-the-shelf stem cell therapy candidate – Zelestrocel - for osteoarthritis and is preparing to launch its pivotal Phase III program. Alongside this, Magellan has purposefully vertically integrated scalable manufacturing capability into its development pathway, having secured GMP certification from the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) for its manufacturing facility in Melbourne, Australia (1 of only 4 GMP certified cell therapy manufacturing facilities in Australia ).
"As we prepare for the next stage of Zelestrocel's development, having access to advanced testing technologies and collaborating with experienced partners is critical to our success," said Magellan Stem Cells CEO Assoc. Professor Julien Freitag .
Magellan’s COO Nick Bliesner highlights that "Charles River's GMP NGS capabilities provide an innovative approach to viral safety testing that supports both product quality and regulatory readiness. This collaboration strengthens our ability to advance Zelestrocel toward commercialization with confidence."
Modernizing Biologics Testing with NGS
NGS is revolutionizing the way advanced therapeutics are characterized and tested, ensuring high-quality products are delivered to patients. NGS has transformed the landscape of genetic analysis and pathogen detection with its high throughput, scalability, and speed.
Charles River’s cGMP NGS testing services accelerate development timelines without compromising safety and meets regulatory requirements for accuracy, reliability, and compliance with GMP, FDA, EMA, and ICH Q5A and Q5B.
To further enhance NGS capabilities, Charles River has acquired Pathoquest, a leader in NGS solutions for in vitro characterization and quality control testing of biopharmaceutical products. The acquisition enables Charles River to deliver even faster and more advanced sequencing-based testing to clients across the development pipeline.
Biologics Testing Solutions
Backed by decades of cell banking and cell line characterization expertise , Charles River’s full range of CGMP-compliant cell bank production and storage services include 9 CGMP-compliant ISO-6 cleanroom suites, 8-10 week cell bank completion to release, and over 2,000 cell and viral banks produced supporting client programs from research and development through commercial manufacturing.
About the Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP)
The Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP) is a Charles River-led initiative dedicated to developing New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and exploring innovative scientific and technological solutions aimed at reducing reliance on traditional animal testing. As we enter the next frontier of drug development, AMAP enables strategic, purpose-driven investment to shape a future in which more patients can access the treatments and medicines they need safely, swiftly, and successfully. AMAP is supported by our global, cross-functional Scientific Advisory Board led by Dr. Namandjé N. Bumpus .
About Magellan Stem Cells 
Magellan Stem Cells aims to develop innovative cell therapies with the capability of addressing unmet clinical needs, leading to significant community impact/benefit. Magellan’s leading proprietary cell therapy - Zelestrocel – is a defined allogeneic (donor) stem cell therapy for the treatment of osteoarthritis (OA). Magellan is founded on innovative research and development and clinical application, supported by a vertically integrated and scalable commercial manufacturing platform which provides the opportunity to address the unmet clinical need of OA (which affects >500million people globally). Visit: magellanstemcells.com.au 
About Charles River
Charles River provides essential products and services to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies and leading academic institutions around the globe accelerate their research and drug development efforts. Our dedicated employees are focused on providing clients with exactly what they need to improve and expedite the discovery, early-stage development and safe manufacture of new therapies for the patients who need them. To learn more about our unique portfolio and breadth of services, visit www.criver.com .

title: 10/13/2026 Interface & Polyurethane Additives Evonik, Toyotsu Chemiplas and Sanyo Chemical launch polyurethane recycling initiative in Japan Evonik has partnered with Toyotsu Chemiplas Corporation and Sanyo Chemical Industries, Ltd. to develop a recycling model for polyurethane foam in Japan for Japan. The partners aim to convert discarded foam into recycled polyols and amines for use in new polyurethane products.
query: https://www.evonik.com/en/media.html
content_text:
Evonik, Toyotsu Chemiplas and Sanyo Chemical launch polyurethane recycling initiative in Japan
Collaboration combines expertise in collection, logistics, and chemical recycling
Initiative targets recovery of polyols and amines from post-consumer polyurethane foam and production scrap
Partners will evaluate the process, with the aim of commercializing the recycling model in Japan
Evonik has partnered with Toyotsu Chemiplas Corporation and Sanyo Chemical Industries, Ltd. to develop a recycling model for polyurethane foam in Japan for Japan. The partners aim to convert discarded foam into recycled polyols and amines for use in new polyurethane products. The initiative forms part of Evonik’s wider efforts to scale  polyurethane recycling through collaboration across the value chain.
Polyurethane foam is widely used in everyday products, including automotive seats, mattresses, and furniture. However, used foam is frequently incinerated or sent to landfill, while conventional mechanical recycling generally restricts its use to lower-value applications. Chemical recycling offers the potential to recover important raw materials, such as polyols and amines, and thereby help close the loop in flexible polyurethane foam production.
Polyurethane foam made with 100% recycled polyol using Evonik's chemical recycling process 
Within the partnership, Toyotsu Chemiplas will coordinate the initiative and contribute its collection network and logistics expertise. Sanyo Chemical will provide its expertise in polyol development and process technology, while Evonik will contribute its proprietary hydrolysis-based chemical recycling process and technical expertise.
Evonik's pilot plant for PU recycling in Hanau, Germany 
“This collaboration with our Japanese partners represents an important step toward developing a practical recycling model for polyurethane foam in Japan. It also reflects Evonik’s ambition to scale polyurethane recycling by building strong partnerships across the value chain. By combining local collection and logistics expertise with polyol development and our chemical recycling technology, we aim to recover valuable raw materials for use in new, high-quality polyurethane foams and support more circular polyurethane value chains,” said Dr. Martin Trocha, Head of Comfort & Adhesives in Evonik’s business line Interface & Polyurethane Additives.
The partners plan to develop a system for collecting both post-consumer polyurethane foam and post-industrial scrap. The collected material will be chemically recycled into high-purity polyols and amines, intended for reuse as raw materials in the manufacture of new polyurethane products.
Proposed recycling model for polyurethane foam in Japan
The hydrolysis-based chemical recycling process from Evonik is designed to produce recycled polyols with high purity and consistent quality. The process provides polyurethane foam manufacturers with a drop-in solution and can significantly reduce carbon footprint compared to virgin materials. New polyurethane foam has already been successfully produced using 100 percent recycled polyol derived from the process.
The three companies will jointly evaluate the entire process, from collection and sorting to the production of recycled polyols and the manufacture of new polyurethane products. This work will include quality assessments and further updates to Evonik’s existing life cycle assessment to reflect the proposed value chain in Japan. The objective is to commercialize the technology and establish a scalable recycling model for polyurethane foam in Japan.
About the partnership
Toyotsu Chemiplas is responsible for coordinating the initiative and will contribute its collection network and logistics expertise. Sanyo Chemical will contribute its expertise in polyol development and process technology. Evonik will provide its hydrolysis chemical recycling technology and technical expertise as part of its global efforts to support the scale-up of polyurethane recycling through partnerships.
Further information:
Polyurethane recycling at Evonik 
Evonik's Interface & Polyurethane Additives business line 
Evonik: Leading beyond chemistry
Evonik goes beyond the boundaries of chemistry with its combination of innovative strength and leading technological expertise. The global chemical company, headquartered in Essen, Germany, is active in more than 100 countries and generated sales of €14.1 billion and earnings (adjusted EBITDA) of €1.9 billion in 2025. The common motivation of the approximately 31,000 employees: to provide customers with a decisive competitive advantage with tailor-made products and solutions as a superforce for industry, thereby improving people's lives. In all markets. Every day.
About Custom Solutions
The Custom Solutions segment focuses on innovation-driven, tailor-made solutions for customers in specific growth markets. These solutions include additives for coatings, adhesives and sealants, polyurethane foams and lubricants, catalysts, and ingredients for the cosmetics, cleaning and pharmaceutical industries. In 2025, the segment generated sales of €5.4 billion with around 9,500 employees.

title: Syensqo wins Fakuma Innovation Award 2026
source: Syensqo - Press Releases (Press Release Finder distribution)
query: https://www.pressreleasefinder.com/Syensqo/
content_text:
Syensqo wins Fakuma Innovation Award 2026
 
Brussels, October 13, 2026 -  Syensqo , a global leader in high-performance polymers, has won first place in the Compounding & Materials category of the inaugural Fakuma Innovation Award 2026 for its Ryton ® PPS XE3500 OR , demonstrated in an extruded busbar manufactured by Standard-Metallwerke .
Designed specifically for DC fast-charging busbars, Ryton ® PPS XE3500 OR addresses the demanding insulation requirements of charging systems capable of taking an EV battery from 20% to 80% in around 20 minutes. The material combines high temperature resistance and dielectric strength with excellent impact toughness, while maintaining its distinctive orange color for reliable high-voltage identification and enhanced safety. Its durability and temperature stability support longer-lasting components and can enable higher power density and more compact designs, with the potential to reduce material use and service needs over the product lifetime.
“As charging power increases, materials must deliver greater electrical safety and thermal reliability without compromising design freedom or manufacturability. Ryton ® PPS XE3500 OR brings these requirements together in a material designed for established extrusion processes, helping our customers develop safer, more compact and durable fast-charging systems,” said Andreas Lutz, Sales Manager Automotive EMEA at Syensqo.
Presented for the first time in 2026 by Schall Messen and K-Zeitung, the Fakuma Innovation Award recognizes technological progress across the plastics value chain. Entries were evaluated by an independent expert jury, with Syensqo selected among five nominees in the Compounding & Materials category.
Syensqo's award-winning technology is already in series production and is being showcased through a demonstrator at Fakuma 2026, Hall B4, Booth 4213, where visitors can discuss its performance and applications with Syensqo experts.

南陽化成株式会社の株式取得（完全子会社化）に関するお知らせ
東ソーは、旭化成株式会社との合弁会社である南陽化成株式会社について、旭化成株式会社保有の全株式（50％）を取得し、完全子会社化することを決定いたしましたので、以下の通りお知らせいたします。
１．株式取得の内容
南陽化成株式会社は、HDIモノマーの製造を目的として、1980年に日本ポリウレタン工業株式会社（現 東ソー）と旭化成株式会社の折半出資により設立されました。現在は、当社および旭化成株式会社が原料などを供給し、南陽化成株式会社が製造したHDIモノマーを両社がそれぞれ引き取る形で事業を運営しています。このたび、旭化成株式会社が保有する南陽化成株式会社の株式（50％）を当社が取得し、南陽化成株式会社を完全子会社化することといたしました。
２．株式取得の目的
当社は、南陽化成株式会社の完全子会社化を通じてHDIモノマーの安定確保を図り、HDI誘導品事業の安定的な運営につなげます。本件は、2026年9月末に商業運転を開始したHDI誘導品新プラント ※ におけるHDIモノマーの安定調達にも寄与するものです。
