Renishaw celebrates 15 years at Miskin and completion of first-phase development
October 2026
This year, Renishaw is celebrating the 15th anniversary of the purchase of its Miskin site in South Wales, and the completion of the first phase of a further £70 million development of the facility. Announced in 2022, this investment will ultimately double the size of the Miskin site, giving the company space to expand manufacturing capacity to meet rising demand for its world-leading precision metrology, additive manufacturing and position measurement products.
Renishaw completed the acquisition of the 193-acre site, situated to the west of Cardiff, from Robert Bosch Ltd in September 2011. It started with modest operations and at the time of the formal opening of the facility in October 2012 by then First Minister of Wales, Carwyn Jones (now Lord Jones), employee numbers were around 25, compared to around 950 today. Following the completion of the first development phase (Hall 3), usable space has grown to 617,000 sq ft (57,350 sqm) and will total 880,000 sq ft (81,765 sqm) once Hall 4 is completed and operational, establishing the Miskin facility as one of the UK's largest advanced manufacturing sites. 
Renishaw has continued to invest throughout its tenure, with around £150 million spent to date on acquiring the site, refurbishing legacy buildings, developing the new halls, and installing advanced manufacturing equipment. The latter currently includes 134 CNC machine tools producing around one million parts per month, three PCB assembly lines, robotic assembly and automated warehousing, with more equipment on order to support customer requirements.
Manufacturing capacity to support future growth
The latest phase of development demonstrates Renishaw's long-term confidence in the UK and its commitment to creating highly skilled jobs and supporting economic growth for years to come.
Hall 3 is used to manufacture Renishaw's metal additive manufacturing (AM) systems, AGILITY® co-ordinate measuring machines (CMMs) and also houses a multimillion-pound automated storage and retrieval warehousing system. Hall 4 was constructed as a shell building, with its future utilisation dependent on sales demand and capacity requirements. Due to exceptional demand for Renishaw's position encoders from manufacturers of semiconductor equipment, driven by the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), some of that additional capacity is now required, and Hall 4 will be partially occupied over the coming months. 
A focus on sustainability and people
Beyond increasing manufacturing capacity, the development of the new halls has been designed to deliver long-term operational and environmental benefits, supporting Renishaw's wider commitment to achieving Net Zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scopes 1 and 2 by 2028. The company's long-term ambition is for all buildings at the Miskin site to operate at Net Zero, and both new halls have been designed to achieve Net Zero Carbon in Operation.
Alongside the manufacturing expansion, Renishaw has also invested in a new employee wellbeing centre, which includes a spacious restaurant and fitness suite. The wider development has also enhanced the site's outdoor environment, including a range of landscaped external spaces, picnic areas and a 2 km perimeter walking route designed to encourage outdoor activity and wellbeing.
Commitment to the future
The expansion of the Miskin site represents a major long-term investment in UK manufacturing, sustainability and skills development. It reinforces Renishaw's commitment to South Wales and the UK while providing a modern, low-carbon manufacturing environment that showcases the best of British engineering. 
Jim Long, Director of Group Manufacturing, said, “Our long-term commitment to manufacturing is exemplified by the investment that we have made in Miskin over the past 15 years and I would like to thank the many people from across our business who have supported the development of this world-class facility.”
He concluded, “The significant ongoing investment by our Board to increase our production capabilities demonstrates a huge vote of confidence in our manufacturing operations and people, at an exciting time for the business.”

title: Applied Materials and Intel Collaborate to Accelerate Chipmaking Innovations for AI-Driven Computing

Applied Materials and Intel Collaborate to Accelerate Chipmaking Innovations for AI-Driven Computing
Oct 6, 2026 at 9:00 AM EDT
PDF Version 
Collaborations at Applied’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Intel’s R&D campus in Oregon aim to develop breakthroughs in next-generation transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging technologies for AI chips and systems 
Collaboration builds on the companies’ long history of working together to solve complex semiconductor device scaling challenges 
SANTA CLARA, Calif. , Oct. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT), the leader in materials engineering for the semiconductor industry, today announced it is working with Intel Corporation (Nasdaq: INTC) to accelerate development of chipmaking innovations for next-generation transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging technologies. The collaboration will bring together cutting-edge capabilities from Applied’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Intel’s R&D campus in Hillsboro, Oregon to shorten time-to-market of advanced semiconductor technologies essential to AI computing.
“Applied and Intel share a decades-long history of deep collaboration focused on pushing the boundaries of materials engineering to advance the semiconductor roadmap,” said Gary Dickerson , President and CEO of Applied Materials. “Bringing our teams together at the EPIC Center will deepen that partnership and accelerate the transistor, interconnect and packaging innovations needed to drive the future of AI computing.”
“The demand for AI computing is driving the need for major advances in performance, power efficiency, and packaging. Intel is focused on delivering those innovations and doing it in close collaboration with partners across the ecosystem,” said Lip-Bu Tan , CEO of Intel . “Applied Materials is an important partner, and we look forward to expanding our work together at the EPIC Center to help accelerate the path from the lab to high-volume manufacturing in the United States.”
Teams from Applied Materials and Intel are collaborating on next-generation materials, process technologies and device architectures for advanced logic nodes targeting AI workloads, and will continue this work at the EPIC Center. The collaboration spans both front-end and back-end-of-line advancements, including interconnect scaling. The collaboration also involves development of advanced packaging technologies for Foveros-based 3D stacking, supporting higher interconnect density, improved power delivery, and enhanced thermal performance for high-performance compute platforms designed to accelerate emerging agentic AI workloads.
“With the chipmaking roadmap becoming more complex at each process node, accelerating innovations in semiconductor devices, interconnects and packaging requires deeper collaboration across R&D and manufacturing,” said Dr. Prabu Raja , President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “We look forward to working closely with Intel as a founding partner of the EPIC Center to shorten development cycles and bring new technologies to market faster.”
“Accelerating our R&D to keep pace with the rapid buildout of AI infrastructure is critical to delivering the technology, manufacturing excellence and foundry services our customers expect from Intel Foundry,” said Naga Chandrasekaran, Executive Vice President, Chief Technology and Operations Officer and General Manager of Intel Foundry. “Applied Materials’ new EPIC Center provides an environment where our teams can collaborate even more closely and at higher velocity to accelerate materials development and process innovations.”
Applied’s new EPIC (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) Center in Silicon Valley , which is scheduled to be operationally ready this year, is designed from the ground up to dramatically reduce the time it takes to commercialize breakthrough technologies from early-stage research to full-scale manufacturing. For chipmakers, the EPIC Center will provide earlier access to Applied’s R&D portfolio, faster cycles of learning and accelerated transfer of next-generation technologies into high-volume manufacturing, within a secure collaborative environment. In addition, the co-innovation programs at the EPIC Center will provide Applied with greater multi-node visibility to guide R&D investments while increasing R&D productivity and value sharing.

These statements and their underlying assumptions are subject to risks and uncertainties and are not guarantees of future performance. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements include, without limitation: the demand for semiconductors and customers’ technology requirements; the ability to develop new and innovative technologies; the ability to obtain and protect intellectual property rights in key technologies; the ability to achieve the objectives of the EPIC Center; and other risks and uncertainties described in Applied’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including Applied’s most recent Forms 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K. All forward-looking statements are based on management’s current estimates, projections and assumptions, and Applied assumes no obligation to update them.

The technology we create is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation chips. At Applied, we push the boundaries of science and engineering to deliver material innovation that changes the world. Learn more at www.appliedmaterials.com .

Danaher Completes Acquisition of Masimo Corporation
WASHINGTON , June 10, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Danaher Corporation (NYSE: DHR), a global science and technology innovator, announced today that it has completed the acquisition of Masimo Corporation, a leading specialty diagnostics provider of pulse oximetry and other patient monitoring solutions, primarily in acute care treatment settings.
Masimo's trusted brand, advanced sensor technology and AI-enabled patient monitoring bring complementary and powerful new capabilities to the Danaher diagnostics portfolio. As a result of the transaction, Masimo is now a wholly-owned subsidiary of Danaher and Masimo common stock has ceased trading on the Nasdaq Stock Market. Masimo will continue to operate under the Masimo brand and will be a stand-alone operating company within Danaher's Diagnostics segment.
"Masimo is a strong strategic fit for Danaher. Together, we expect to strengthen our ability to deliver differentiated products in acute care settings and accelerate Masimo's growth and global reach," said Julie Sawyer Montgomery, Executive Vice President of Diagnostics at Danaher. "We are excited to welcome the Masimo team to Danaher."
The consideration payable to former Masimo stockholders will be paid in accordance with the terms of the merger agreement, as further described in the definitive transaction materials filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Second Quarter and Full Year 2026 Outlook 
There is no change to Danaher's previously communicated second quarter and full-year 2026 guidance range, excluding the expected contribution from Masimo. The Company does not expect a material contribution from Masimo in the second quarter of 2026. The Company intends to update full-year 2026 guidance in connection with its second quarter earnings release to incorporate Masimo's expected contribution.

AGC Biologics Awarded Multiple Cell Therapy Projects at Its Yokohama Site
－Supporting Diverse Development Needs from Academia to Biotechnology Companies－
AGC Biologics, the biopharmaceutical Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) business of AGC Inc. (Headquarters: Tokyo; President: Yoshinori Hirai), is establishing its Yokohama site as a new development and manufacturing hub in Japan.
As part of the Yokohama site launch, AGC Biologics launched cell therapy process development services at the AGC Yokohama Technical Center in July 2025.Since then, the company has been awarded multiple projects from academic institutions and biotechnology companies in Japan and overseas. These projects include a range of modalities, including exosome- and T cell-based programs.
Leveraging Expertise Across AGC Biologics' Global Network 
AGC Biologics is establishing development and manufacturing capabilities at the Yokohama site through technical collaboration and personnel exchanges with its Milan site, which has extensive experience * in the development and commercial manufacturing of cell and gene therapies.
One of these projects involves the transfer of a customer program from the Milan site to the Yokohama site, where future development and manufacturing activities will be conducted in Japan. Through coordination across its global network, AGC Biologics provides flexible development and manufacturing support tailored to customers' evolving needs and business environments.
Supporting Clinical Translation of Virus-Specific T Cell Therapy Research at Institute of Science Tokyo 
Among the projects currently being supported is a research program led by the Institute of Science Tokyo aimed at advancing third-party virus-specific T cell therapy for treatment-resistant adenovirus infections following hematopoietic cell transplantation toward clinical application.
Patients undergoing hematopoietic cell transplantation often experience impaired immune function and are at increased risk of severe or prolonged viral infections, highlighting the need for new therapeutic approaches.
At the Yokohama site, AGC Biologics supports this program through process development and analytical method development activities intended to facilitate future clinical and manufacturing implementation.
Comments on the Project 
Takahiro Kamiya, M.D., Ph.D.
Junior Associate Professor, Department of Pediatrics and Developmental Biology, Graduate School of Medical and Dental Sciences, Institute of Science Tokyo 
“Viral infections following hematopoietic cell transplantation represent a major clinical challenge in patients with compromised immune function and can lead to severe, potentially life-threatening complications. With support from the Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development (AMED) under its Research Program for Intractable Diseases, we are advancing the research and development of virus-specific T-cell therapy toward clinical implementation for refractory adenovirus infections following hematopoietic cell transplantation.
AGC Biologics has accumulated extensive experience in the development and manufacturing of cell therapy products through its global operations. As we prepare for this collaboration, we have also been impressed by the strength of its research and development capabilities, its robust infrastructure, and the dedication and enthusiasm of its team.
Through this collaboration, we aim to further develop our technology into a robust and reproducible manufacturing process with consistently high quality, and to accelerate our efforts toward clinical implementation so that this therapy can be delivered to patients as a new treatment option as soon as possible.“
Tadashi Murano　President, Life Science Company, AGC Inc. 
"Since launching cell therapy process development services at the AGC Yokohama Technical Center in July 2025, AGC Biologics has been awarded multiple projects from a broad range of customers, including academic institutions and biotechnology companies in Japan and abroad.
We believe this reflects growing demand for development and manufacturing infrastructure supporting cell therapies in Japan. By combining technologies developed across our global network with AGC's unique materials expertise, we provide globally aligned development support services to customers worldwide.
Going forward, we will continue to provide integrated support from early-stage development through commercialization, helping accelerate our customers' research and development activities."
Under its medium-term management plan, AGC plus-2026 , the AGC Group has identified “Well-being” as one of the social values it aims to create through its products and technologies. AGC Biologics operates an integrated global GMP system across Japan, the United States, and Europe. Through this platform, the company continues to expand its CDMO services across a wide range of modalities. It aims to support customers from early-stage development through commercial production and to contribute to the realization of innovative biopharmaceuticals.
〈Notes〉 
* 
AGC Biologics S.p.A. (100% subsidiary, headquartered in Italy) has a track record of six commercial manufacturing approvals in the field of gene and cell therapies, where such experience remains limited globally. Additionally, it holds the top share as a CDMO in terms of the number of contract development and manufacturing projects for Ex Vivo gene therapy drugs (as of Sep 2026, based on AGC’s internal research). 
About the AGC Group 
AGC Inc. is a global materials company operating across a wide range of products and industries. Founded in 1907 with flat glass production as its original business, AGC has expanded its operations in line with changing societal needs, providing materials and solutions based on its core material and production technologies. Today, the AGC Group operates in more than 30 countries and regions, with businesses spanning glass, electronics, chemicals, life science, and ceramics. Guided by its purpose, “AGC, an everyday essential part of our world,” the Group provides value to society through the pursuit of innovation.

title: Oct. 6, 2026 Business & Products Sumitomo Chemical Achieves Production-Scale Manufacturing of Liquid Crystal Polymer (LCP) Using Biomass Feedstock in Preparation for Mass Production The Company Will Begin Supplying Samples Produced Through Biomanufacturing
source: Sumitomo Chemical - News Releases Filter / Press Releases
query: https://www.sumitomo-chem.co.jp/english/news/category/newsreleases/
content_text:
News Releases

News Releases
Sumitomo Chemical Achieves Production-Scale Manufacturing of Liquid Crystal Polymer (LCP) Using Biomass Feedstock in Preparation for Mass Production
The Company Will Begin Supplying Samples Produced Through Biomanufacturing 
Oct. 6, 2026
Sumitomo Chemical has achieved production-scale manufacturing of liquid crystal polymer (LCP) that contains a portion of monomer derived from biomass feedstock (bio-based LCP (*1) ). As a global supplier in the LCP market, the Company is preparing a mass production system for bio-based LCP leveraging biomanufacturing technology. It also plans to begin providing customers with samples obtained from this production-scale manufacturing.
LCP is a type of super engineering plastic that offers excellent heat resistance and flame retardancy. Its outstanding fluidity, in particular, makes it well-suited to a wide range of applications, from electronic devices such as smartphones to automotive components and office automation equipment. While most of the raw materials used to produce LCP have traditionally been derived from fossil resources, there is growing demand for shifting to biomass feedstock and reducing the carbon footprint (*2) in order to achieve a sustainable society.
In response to rising customer demand, Sumitomo Chemical has been advancing the development of bio-based LCP. In June 2025, the Company established technology to mass-produce the material and has since been advancing studies to scale up this technology. It has now confirmed through production-scale manufacturing that it can produce LCP partially containing biomass-derived monomers at a quality equivalent to that of LCP made with conventional fossil-based feedstock (*3) .
The manufacturing process to produce the bio-based LCP used by Sumitomo Chemical adopts a segregation approach, in which biomass feedstock and non-biomass feedstock are kept completely separate from each other during production. This makes it possible to clearly quantify the amount of biomass feedstock included in the final product. There is also another approach, known as mass balance, in which biomass feedstock and non-biomass feedstock are mixed together, and the characteristics of the biomass feedstock are allocated to part of the product output in proportion to the amount of biomass feedstock used. Sumitomo Chemical will assess the characteristics of each approach to utilize a method that best meets customer needs.
As part of its long-term vision, Sumitomo Chemical has positioned itself as a company that solves social issues through innovative technologies. In its biomanufacturing, the Company is pursuing the hybridization of chemical and biological technologies.
In the green bio (*4) field, Sumitomo Chemical is working toward the achievement of a regenerative society through both chemical crop protection products and biorationals (*5) . In the red bio (*4) field, it is contributing to human health through pharmaceutical development, CDMO (*6) services based on cell culture technologies, and regenerative medicine and cell therapy. In the white bio (*4) and gray bio (*4) fields, it is promoting sustainable manufacturing through the utilization of biomass-derived feedstock with organic synthesis technologies and omics technologies (*7) .
Going forward, Sumitomo Chemical will continue to create value by leveraging chemical technologies and biotechnology, and contribute to solving society's challenges by providing innovative solutions.
(*1) An LCP produced using a principal raw material, a biomass derived monomer made from 100% biomass feedstock. The portion of the biomass-derived content of the bio-based LCP equivalent to our existing compounding grade, SUMIKASUPER E6008, is approximately 30% based on raw material weight. 
(*2) A measurement of the total greenhouse gas emissions released during each stage of a product’s life cycle—from raw material procurement to manufacturing, use, and disposal—expressed in terms of the equivalent CO₂ emissions. 
(*3) Based on an internal evaluation carried out by Sumitomo Chemical in accordance with ASTM International standards, the Company confirmed that, from the perspective of heat resistance, fluidity, and the mechanical properties of the material—the key characteristics that represent the advantages of LCP— LCP that contains a portion of monomer derived from biomass feedstock (bio-based LCP) is equivalent in quality to LCP made with conventional fossil-based feedstock. 
(*4) Terms used to classify, by color, the fields in which biotechnology is applied: green for food and agriculture, red for medicine, white for industry and energy, and gray for the environment. 
(*5) Microbial crop protection products derived from natural sources, plant growth regulators and rhizosphere microbial products, and solutions that use these products to protect crops from pests and diseases or improve crop quality and yield. 
(*6) CDMO is an acronym of Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization, a business that undertakes process development and manufacturing for customers. 
(*7) Technologies that comprehensively analyze biological molecules such as genes, proteins, and metabolites.

title: Skyworks Completes Combination with Qorvo
query: https://investors.skyworksinc.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Skyworks Completes Combination with Qorvo
Expands technology portfolio and addressable market, with $500 million or more in expected annual cost synergies and immediate non-GAAP EPS accretion 
IRVINE, Calif., Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Skyworks (Nasdaq: SWKS) today announced the successful completion of its combination with Qorvo. The close of the transaction creates a U.S.-based, global leader in high-performance radio frequency (RF), power management, and analog and mixed-signal semiconductor solutions. 
“This combination is about far more than bringing two companies together,” said Phil Brace, chief executive officer and president of Skyworks. “Our customers are tackling increasingly complex challenges and need partners with the capabilities, engineering expertise and scale to help them innovate faster. Together, we are well positioned to deliver more integrated, system-level solutions and accelerate the next generation of connected technologies. Today marks an important milestone—but it is only the beginning. We see an extraordinary opportunity to create long-term value for our customers, shareholders and employees while helping shape the future of our industry.”
The transaction creates a larger, more diversified semiconductor company, combining complementary RF, analog, and power technologies with expanded engineering capabilities — approximately 8,000 engineers and more than 12,000 issued and pending patents. 
In Mobile, the combination broadens its RF front-end portfolio, positioning the company to benefit from rising RF complexity. As 5G-Advanced evolves and the industry moves toward 6G, smartphones are expected to support more frequency bands, new spectrum and AI-driven features, increasing demand for highly integrated RF solutions.
Beyond Mobile, the combination more than doubles Skyworks' addressable market and establishes a platform spanning physical AI and connected edge, defense and aerospace, data center and networking, and automotive. It also broadens the technology portfolio into RF GaN, low-voltage power, and wired broadband.
Skyworks will benefit from greater end-market breadth, strengthened domestic manufacturing, and annualized cost synergies of $500 million or more, expected to be realized within 24 to 36 months post-close when the companies are fully integrated. 
The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS while maintaining a favorable capital structure. Skyworks will provide financial guidance on its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call on Nov. 3. 
Bob Bruggeworth, former chief executive officer and president of Qorvo and a member of the Skyworks Board of Directors, added, “This next chapter begins with an immense amount of pride. I've had the opportunity to see firsthand our teams preparing for this moment with tremendous focus and discipline. I have great confidence in the future of the combined company and its ability to deliver on the promise of the combination.”
Under the terms of the merger agreement, Qorvo shareholders are entitled to receive $32.50 in cash and 0.960 of Skyworks’ common share for each share of Qorvo common stock they owned. Legacy Skyworks shareholders own approximately 63% of the combined company and legacy Qorvo shareholders own approximately 37%, on a fully diluted basis. The company will continue to operate as Skyworks and trade under the SWKS ticker symbol on the NASDAQ market.
As previously announced, Phil Brace will continue to serve as chief executive officer and president of Skyworks. Bob Bruggeworth, Richard Clemmer and Chris Koopmans, formerly on the Qorvo board of directors, have each joined the Skyworks Board of Directors. 
Advisors 
Qatalyst Partners and Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC acted as financial advisors to Skyworks, with Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP serving as Skyworks’ legal advisor.
Centerview Partners LLC was exclusive financial advisor and Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP acted as legal advisor to Qorvo.
About Skyworks 
Skyworks® is a global leader in high-performance RF, precision timing, power management and mixed-signal solutions that power the intelligent, connected world. Through deep engineering expertise, Skyworks helps customers address rising complexity and deliver seamless connectivity across smartphones, vehicles, networks and critical infrastructure. 
From defense and aerospace systems to the connected edge, AI infrastructure and next-generation automotive platforms, Skyworks provides the essential technologies that connect, synchronize and power physical AI, as intelligence moves out of the data center and into the real world. Harnessing decades of technical leadership and trusted partnerships across the technology ecosystem, Skyworks helps the world's leading innovators bring next-generation products and services to market. 
Skyworks is a member of the S&P 500® market index (Nasdaq: SWKS). For more information, please visit www.skyworksinc.com .

These forward-looking statements include information relating to future events, prospects, expectations and results of Skyworks (e.g., certain projections and business trends, including with respect to future sales and revenue, as well as statements regarding the recently completed combination with Qorvo, Inc. query: https://www.evonik.com/en/media.html
content_text:
Evonik develops new biodegradable excipients for oral drug delivery
Product innovation to be presented at CPHI 2026 in Milan on October 7, 12:30 PM at Sustainability Spotlight Stage 16F60
First non-commercial lab-scale volumes are available for joint development projects with selected partners
Biodegradable polymer platform builds on Evonik’s seven-decade track record in oral drug delivery
Evonik is developing a novel biodegradable polymer platform that will form the basis for the next generation of its EUDRAGIT® functional excipients for oral drug delivery . The polymers combine a biodegradable end-of-life profile with performance comparable to today’s industry standards for solubility enhancement and delayed-release coatings. Material is currently available in non-commercial lab-scale volumes for joint development projects with selected partners.
“Sustainability is becoming a design criterion in pharmaceutical development, alongside quality, efficacy and safety. With the next generation of EUDRAGIT®, we are moving from measuring sustainability to actively engineering it. This opens up new possibilities for formulators to choose both functionality and a biodegradable end-of-life profile in materials they can process with the equipment and methods they already use,” said Thilo Krapfl, Head of Oral Drug Delivery Solutions at Evonik Health Care.
Biodegradable excipients are increasingly desirable because they allow pharmaceutical companies to build sustainability into drug products from the design stage. Biodegradability can help reduce environmental persistence while maintaining the functionality needed for effective oral drug delivery. The new polymers are classified as biodegradable according to standardized testing (OECD 301 F and OECD 301 B (>60%).
EUDRAGIT® polymers are polymethacrylates suitable for a wide range of drug delivery applications. Used individually or in combination, they enable virtually any target release profile, including immediate and delayed release. In addition, selected EUDRAGIT® grades can be used for solubility enhancement of poorly soluble drug substances. They are compatible with all relevant processing technologies, including hot melt extrusion and spray drying. The new biodegradable excipients are designed to deliver the proven functionality formulators expect from EUDRAGIT®, including reliable solubility enhancement and targeted release performance.
Evonik’s Health Care business offers integrated solutions that support pharmaceutical companies worldwide in bringing complex oral and parenteral drug products to market. At CPHI Milan, the company will showcase its portfolio of innovations including the award-winning EUDRACAP® colon , and plant-based squalene, PhytoSquene® , its advanced parenteral excipients , CDMO services and biopharma solutions .

Syensqo introduces a new guar technology for fragrance and softness delivery in laundry care
Jaguar ® Care is a new natural polymer solution that enhances fragrance deposition and softness while helping protect fabrics through repeated washes
 
Brussels, October 5, 2026 - Syensqo announces the launch of Jaguar ® Care , a new natural [1] , non-microplastic polymer designed to enhance sensorial performance in modern laundry detergents.
Based on Syensqo’s guar technology, Jaguar ® Care boosts the deposition of fragrance oils and capsules while delivering softness, including in short and cold wash cycles. It also helps protect fibers from pilling, repairs fuzz and improves garment durability over repeated washes.
“Jaguar ® Care gives laundry detergent formulators a new solution to create differentiated products that combine a best-in-class sensorial experience with convenience and care. It enables formulators to combine cleaning and care benefits in convenient 2-in-1 laundry products, while helping consumers keep their clothes looking and feeling good for longer,” said Max Chabert, Global Marketing Manager, Home Care at Syensqo.
The new solution responds to growing consumer expectations for long-lasting fragrance, convenience, and garment durability. By bringing these benefits together in a natural ingredient, Jaguar ® Care supports the development of high-performing laundry products and more sustainable approaches to clothing care.
Jaguar ® is a registered trademark of Syensqo. 
 
[1] Natural Origin Index (Ino) = 0.78, according to ISO 16128:2.

title: Proterial and FEV Jointly Validate xEV Traction Motor Concept Using Amorphous Alloy and High-Performance Heavy-Rare-Earth-Free Magnet Technology Simulation Study Indicates Potential for Higher Efficiency, Increased Output, and Reduced Weight
source: Hitachi Metals - Proterial 2026 Press Releases / Press Releases
query: https://www.proterial.com/e/press/2026/
content_text:
TOP 
News Release 
2026 
Proterial and FEV Jointly Validate xEV Traction Motor Concept Using Amorphous Alloy and High-Performance Heavy-Rare-Earth-Free Magnet Technology Simulation Study Indicates Potential for Higher Efficiency, Increased Output, and Reduced Weight 
R&D 
Proterial and FEV Jointly Validate xEV Traction Motor Concept Using Amorphous Alloy and High-Performance Heavy-Rare-Earth-Free Magnet Technology
Simulation Study Indicates Potential for Higher Efficiency, Increased Output, and Reduced Weight
October 5, 2026 
Proterial, Ltd.
FEV
Proterial, Ltd. (“Proterial”), a leading manufacturer of advanced materials and components, and FEV, a global engineering and consulting partner for mobility, energy, and software, have jointly investigated and validated an electrified-vehicle (xEV) traction motor concept that combines Proterial’s amorphous alloy technology with its high-performance heavy-rare-earth (HRE) -free neodymium sintered magnet technology. Bringing together Proterial’s advanced materials expertise and FEV’s capabilities in electric drive design, simulation, benchmarking, and system-level evaluation, the partners developed and assessed a traction motor concept designed to make full use of the characteristics of these materials. Simulation results indicate the potential to improve motor efficiency while simultaneously increasing output and reducing weight compared with a defined 230-kW-class reference motor. The study also highlights the potential to reduce resource and procurement risks associated with HREs. Proterial and FEV will continue exploring how advanced material technologies can be translated into tangible benefits at the traction motor and complete drive-system level. 
The results of this study will be jointly presented by FEV and Proterial at the Aachen Automotive Colloquium, to be held in Aachen, Germany, from October 5 to 7, 2026. 
1. Background
As the mobility industry continues to pursue decarbonization and improved energy efficiency, demand is increasing for traction motors and drive systems with lower power consumption, higher performance, and reduced reliance on critical raw materials. In electrified vehicles (xEVs), improving efficiency supports lower electricity consumption and longer driving range; in other applications, such as heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) equipment, data centers, electric vertical takeoff and advanced air mobility, exemplified by eVTOL aircraft, and robotics, higher-efficiency electric motors can help reduce overall energy demand. Amorphous alloy is attracting attention because it can reduce motor losses. Compared with conventional electrical steel sheets commonly used in electric motor cores, amorphous alloy offers lower iron loss. For neodymium magnets used in xEV traction motors, there is also strong demand to reduce dependence on HREs, which face resource constraints, and to mitigate procurement risk. To address these market needs, Proterial has developed continuous lamination and bonding technology for amorphous alloy ribbon suitable for punching into motor cores, as well as high-performance HRE-free neodymium sintered magnets that can be applied to xEV traction motors. Proterial established the Motor Solutions Department within its Marketing & Sales Division in November 2025 and is promoting initiatives to verify the value of its products from the perspective of traction motors and complete drive systems, and to develop optimized solutions for customer applications rather than individual products alone.
2. Overview and Results of the Study
As part of these initiatives undertaken by its Motor Solutions Department, Proterial is working with FEV, with project promotion support from Beyond Materials Corporation, to evaluate the application of amorphous alloy and HRE-free magnet technology to xEV traction motors.
In this study, FEV established a reference motor model for a 230 kW drive unit, representative of modern passenger-car battery electric vehicle (BEV) applications, using silicon steel sheets for the motor core. The effect of applying amorphous alloy was then evaluated through electromagnetic simulation. Rather than simply replacing the motor core material, the partners examined a traction motor concept that reflects current trends in electric drive systems, including inverter and reduction gears, while making best use of the low-iron-loss characteristics of amorphous alloy, due to an increased maximum motor speed. The reduction ratio of the transmission was adjusted so that the maximum torque and speed during vehicle operation would be equivalent to that of the reference drive unit (Table 1). The study also applied Proterial’s high-performance HRE-free neodymium sintered magnet, which combines high magnetic performance, due to a high remanence flux density, and strong resistance to demagnetization, due to a high coercivity, without relying on HREs. Compared with the reference, the simulation results indicate the potential to improve motor efficiency while simultaneously increasing output to 300 kW and reducing weight by 27 % (Table 1).

3. Future Outlook
Proterial and FEV intend to continue exploring how advanced material technologies can be translated into measurable benefits in electric motors and complete drive systems. Through its Motor Solutions Department and in collaboration with its business divisions, Proterial will continue to verify material value from the perspective of customer applications and propose optimized solutions. FEV will contribute its engineering, simulation, benchmarking, and system-integration expertise to assess how new materials can support next-generation electric drive concepts. Together, the partners aim to support higher-efficiency electric mobility and other emerging applications, including eVTOLs and humanoid robots, while contributing to a more sustainable society.
4. Presentation at the Aachen Automotive Colloquium
The results of this joint study will be presented by FEV and Proterial at the Aachen Automotive Colloquium, to be held in Aachen, Germany, from October 5 to 7, 2026. A mock-up of the traction motor structure examined in this study will also be on display at FEV's Booth No. 9.

About Proterial
Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, Proterial is a leading manufacturer of advanced materials, primarily metal-based materials.
In the motor field, the company’s business divisions collaborate under the leadership of the Motor Solutions Department to serve as development partners for customers. Proterial verifies the value of materials from the perspective of motors and complete drive systems and proposes optimal solutions.
As a manufacturer capable of providing a comprehensive range of motor materials, Proterial will continue to contribute to lower electricity consumption in xEVs and reduced power consumption in air-conditioning and data-center equipment through the application of its products to high-efficiency motors. The company will also contribute to a sustainable society by providing solutions for emerging applications, including eVTOLs and humanoid robots.
About FEV
FEV is a global engineering and consulting partner for mobility, energy and software. Since 1978, FEV has been developing innovative technologies and solutions across the entire product lifecycle – from strategy and concept development through engineering and validation to implementation, optimization and support. Combining engineering expertise with software, digital technologies and AI, FEV helps its customers develop sustainable technologies, intelligent systems and future-oriented solutions. With around 5,600 employees at more than 45 locations worldwide, FEV serves customers across a wide range of industries.
About Beyond Materials
Beyond Materials is a joint venture established by Mitsubishi Corporation and FEV Consulting GmbH. By combining the two companies’ expertise in the materials industry, global networks, insights into customer needs across industries such as automotive, energy, and robotics, and capabilities in end-product design and development, Beyond Materials provides consulting and engineering-related solutions to companies throughout the materials industry and its value chain. Its services include market and technology research, strategy development, product development, and proof-of-concept testing.

Notes and Terms
Note: The numerical values described in this document are simulation results based on specified conditions and are not guaranteed product values.
xEV: A general term for electrified vehicles, including battery electric vehicles (BEVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), and related vehicles.
eVTOL: A next-generation aircraft capable of vertical takeoff and landing using electric power (electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft).
Amorphous alloy: A metallic material with no crystalline structure, obtained by rapidly cooling a molten alloy.
Reference Model: The reference model values include nominal values.
WLTP Class 3: An international standard driving cycle applied to typical passenger vehicles, simulating real-world driving conditions from urban roads to highways.
ARTEMIS MW 150 Drive Cycle: One of the driving patterns developed under Europe’s ARTEMIS (Assessment and Reliability of Transport Emission Models and Inventory Systems) project; it is widely used to evaluate fuel consumption, electricity consumption, emissions, and motor efficiency.
Heavy rare earths: Rare-earth elements with relatively high atomic weights, such as terbium (Tb) and dysprosium (Dy).
Remanence B r and coercivity H cJ : Key magnetic properties of permanent magnets. Remanence indicates magnetic flux density retained after magnetization, while coercivity indicates resistance to demagnetization.

content_text:
チルド飲料の賞味期限を長くする「DNP無菌充填対応容器 PETカップタイプ」を開発
リサイクルPETを使用し、無菌充填技術と組み合わせて環境配慮と賞味期限延長に対応 
ニュースリリース 
製品・サービス 
パッケージ 
環境 
大日本印刷株式会社（本社：東京、代表取締役社長：北島義斉、以下：DNP）は、高い酸素バリア性を備えたポリエチレンテレフタレート（PET） ＊1 カップと、DNPの無菌充填技術を組み合わせ、飲料の賞味期限延長に対応する「DNP無菌充填対応容器 PETカップタイプ」を開発しました。
本製品は、透明性とバリア性が高いPETカップとDNPが長年培ってきた無菌充填技術を組み合わせることで、飲料の賞味期限延長と化石資源の使用抑制に貢献します。これにより、飲料メーカーや流通事業者が抱える食品ロスや廃棄コストの削減、販売エリアの拡大に貢献します。
DNPは第一弾として、トーヨービバレッジ株式会社との協業により、「DNP無菌充填対応容器 PETカップタイプ」を使用した飲料容器の提供を2027年に開始します。
DNP無菌充填対応容器 PETカップタイプのイメージ
【開発の背景】
チルド飲料市場では、食品ロスや廃棄コストの削減に向けて、賞味期限を延長できる飲料の充填技術と、それに対応する容器の開発が求められています。今回、トーヨービバレッジから「PET素材によるカップ容器の実現」について要望を受けたことを契機に、DNPは無菌充填技術やカップ成形技術、リサイクルPET活用技術を掛け合わせて、「DNP無菌充填対応容器 PETカップタイプ」を開発しました。これにより、賞味期限の延長と化石資源の使用抑制の両立を実現します。
【「DNP無菌充填対応容器 PETカップタイプ」の特長】
1．賞味期限を延長
本製品のカップ本体は、PET樹脂の物性により、中身の劣化を防ぐ酸素バリア性を当社従来品比25％高めています。また、無菌充填時やラベル装着時の高温に耐えられる設計とすることで、飲料の鮮度を保ちながら充填するDNPの無菌充填システムとの組み合わせが可能となりました。これによりチルド飲料の賞味期限を延長でき、生活者への利便性につながります（当社調べ）。
2．リサイクルPETを使用することで環境へ配慮
本製品のカップ本体に使用するPET樹脂の10％にリサイクルPETを採用することで、バージンPETの使用量を抑え、化石資源の使用抑制に貢献します。
3．飲料メーカーの廃棄ロス削減や在庫管理の効率化に貢献
「DNP無菌充填対応容器 PETカップタイプ」を使用することで、チルド飲料のロングライフ化につながり、飲料メーカーや流通事業者の柔軟な在庫運用が可能になります。これにより、食品ロスや廃棄コストの低減につながります。また、ロングライフ化により、従来は難しかった遠隔地への展開が可能となり、飲料メーカーや流通事業者にとって販売エリア拡大が期待できます。
【今後の展開】
DNPは、開発した「DNP無菌充填対応容器 PETカップタイプ」を飲料メーカーへ提供し、関連する無菌充填システムを含めて2027年度までに累計16億円の売上を目指します。今後は飲料の特性に合わせて、さらにバリア性を高めた製品開発を進め、飲料の賞味期限の延長やおいしさの維持など付加価値の向上を目指していきます。
なお、2026年10月14日（水）～16日（金）に東京ビッグサイト・東ホールで行う「2026東京国際包装展（TOKYO PACK 2026）」のDNPブース（東1ホール ブースNO.1R13） ＊2 で本製品を紹介します。
＊1 ポリエチレンテレフタレート ： プラスチックの一種で再生利用が可能です。飲料容器などに広く使用されています。
＊2 DNPのTOKYOPACK 2026の出展概要 → https://www.dnp.co.jp/biz/eventseminar/event/20178525_4966.html

title: AGC Receives an Excellence Award at the “9th SX Awards” for its Fluorine Resource Recycling Initiative
source: Asahi Glass - News releases (newsroom JSON list)
query: https://www.agc.com/en/news/detail/news_all.json
content_text:
AGC Receives an Excellence Award at the “9th SX Awards” for its Fluorine Resource Recycling Initiative
AGC (AGC Inc.; Headquarters: Tokyo; President: Yoshinori Hirai) has received an Excellence Award at the 9th SX Awards, organized by the Sustainable Management Promotion Organization (SuMPO), in recognition of its efforts to advance a circular economy for fluorine resources. The award was presented for the initiative titled “From recycled circular fluorite to Fluon ™ PTFE: Building a Domestic Circular Economy for Fluorine Resources”.
Left: Yasushi Umeda, Chair of the SX Awards Selection Committee 
Right: Tatsuo Momii, President, Chemicals Company, AGC Inc. 
Fluorine-based products offer excellent properties, including heat resistance, chemical resistance and electrical insulation. They are used across a wide range of industries, including the semiconductor, automotive, construction, and aerospace industries. However, natural fluorite, the primary raw material used in fluorochemical production, is concentrated in a limited number of regions. Consequently, ensuring a stable supply while reducing the environmental impact associated with natural-resource extraction has become an important challenge.
To address these challenges, AGC draws on its extensive expertise in fluorine chemistry to recover and recycle fluorine from waste generated at its own plants. AGC also uses recycled circular fluorite produced from fluorine-containing by-products generated by the semiconductor industry and other sectors. Through these initiatives, AGC is promoting the circular use of fluorine resources both within the AGC Group and across the broader value chain.
In addition, to enhance confidence in the use of recycled materials and make their circular value more visible, AGC uses third-party verification based on UL 2809 to verify the proportion of recycled raw materials used. AGC first completed third-party verification for Fluon ™ PTFE , one of the most widely used fluoropolymers, and is gradually extending this initiative to other products .
The award recognized AGC's successful implementation of fluorine-resource recycling in high-performance materials, an area in which such initiatives have traditionally been difficult to realize. It also acknowledged AGC's efforts to reduce the use of natural fluorite and support a stable supply of raw materials, and the potential for broader benefits across industries that utilize fluorine-based materials.
Under its medium-term management plan AGC plus-2026 , the AGC Group has positioned "Deepening Sustainability Management" as one of its key strategies. Going forward, AGC will continue to leverage its unique materials and technologies and actively contribute to the realization of a circular economy for fluorine resources.

title: onsemi and Synaptics Announce Revised Merger Agreement

onsemi and Synaptics Announce Revised Merger Agreement
October 1, 2026 at 4:34 PM EDT
PDF Version 
Revised Terms to Deliver Higher onsemi Shareholder Value through Immediate EPS Accretion 
Amended Agreement Follows Thorough Review of Unsolicited Competing Proposal 
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. and SAN JOSE, Calif., Oct. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- onsemi (NASDAQ: ON) and Synaptics Incorporated (NASDAQ: SYNA) ("Synaptics") today announced they have amended their June 25, 2026 merger agreement. The amendment follows an unsolicited competing proposal received from a third party.
Under the revised agreement, onsemi will acquire Synaptics for $123 per share in cash for an aggregate value of approximately $5.7 billion as compared to approximately $7 billion for the prior agreement. The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive to onsemi’s non-GAAP earnings per share and provides value certainty for Synaptics’ shareholders.
“As was the case when we initially announced the acquisition, Synaptics addresses an important aspect of our strategic direction, and we believe the revised merger agreement represents a more financially attractive transaction for our shareholders,” said Hassane El-Khoury, President and CEO of onsemi. “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration, and we now expect the transaction to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS upon closing. In addition, we have identified incremental opportunities to create shareholder value beyond the previously announced $200 million of annual run-rate synergies. These additional benefits from revenue synergies and insourcing of a portion of Synaptics’ production are expected to be realized after the initial 18 months post-close, further strengthening the long-term earnings and cash flow profile of the combined company.”
El-Khoury continued, “Synaptics is accretive to our long-term model, with a strong growth outlook and attractive gross margin profile that will help accelerate onsemi’s evolution. Additionally, Synaptics complements growth in our AI data center business, and brings to onsemi its highly profitable human-machine interface, and sensing products businesses that generate strong and predictable cash flows, providing the combined company with a durable funding engine to accelerate its connected compute capabilities.”
After careful review with its financial and legal advisors, the Synaptics Board unanimously determined that the onsemi transaction, as amended, continues to be in the best interests of Synaptics and its shareholders.
"Our Board has been singularly focused on delivering the best outcome for our shareholders, and today's amended agreement reflects that commitment," said Rahul Patel, Synaptics President and CEO. “By transitioning to an all-cash structure, we are providing value certainty at a meaningful premium as compared to current value. We are confident this path is the right choice for our shareholders."
The transaction will be financed through a combination of cash on hand and committed financing. onsemi has obtained fully committed debt financing from Morgan Stanley. The amended merger agreement does not include a closing condition related to onsemi’s financing.
The transaction is still expected to close by mid-2027, subject to approval by Synaptics shareholders, the receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. The transaction has been approved by the United States Federal Trade Commission, and regulators in other jurisdictions are reviewing the transaction.
More Information: 
Investor Presentation: onsemi & Synaptics Revised Merger Terms 
About onsemi 
onsemi (Nasdaq: ON) delivers intelligent power and sensing technologies that enable electrification, energy efficiency, safety, and automation across automotive, industrial, and AI data center end-markets. With a highly differentiated and innovative product portfolio, onsemi helps customers solve complex challenges to achieve higher efficiency, improved performance, and lower system cost, while supporting a safer, cleaner, and more energy-efficient world. The company is part of the S&P 500® index. Learn more at www.onsemi.com .
About Synaptics Incorporated 
Synaptics (Nasdaq: SYNA) is driving innovation in AI at the Edge, bringing AI closer to end users and transforming how we engage with intelligent connected devices, whether at home, at work, or on the move. As a go-to partner for forward-thinking product innovators, Synaptics powers the future with its cutting-edge Synaptics Astra™ AI-Native embedded compute, wireless connectivity, and multimodal sensing solutions. We’re making the digital experience smarter, faster, more intuitive, secure, and seamless. From touch, display, and biometrics to AI-driven wireless connectivity, video, vision, audio, speech, and security processing, Synaptics is a force behind the next generation of technology enhancing how we live, work, and play.

title: Applied Materials and Besi Expand Strategic Partnership to Advance Next-Generation Packaging for AI Scaling
query: https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Applied Materials and Besi Expand Strategic Partnership to Advance Next-Generation Packaging for AI Scaling
Oct 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM EDT
PDF Version 
Besi joins Applied's EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner, extending a collaboration that began in 2020 with the companies' joint Hybrid Bonding Center of Excellence in Singapore 
Expanded collaboration targets next-generation 3D IC scaling, logic and memory integration, and photonics applications supporting AI infrastructure build-out 
Partnership expands beyond die-to-wafer hybrid bonding to new hybrid bonding platforms, scaling of thermo-compression bonding (TCB), and new die-on-wafer, die-on-die and die-on-panel architectures 
SANTA CLARA, Calif. and DUIVEN, The Netherlands , Oct. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) and BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. (Besi) ( Euronext Amsterdam : BESI) today announced an expansion of their longstanding strategic partnership, with Besi joining Applied's EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner. The collaboration builds on the companies’ joint development program launched in 2020 and extends co-innovation beyond hybrid bonding into new interconnect architectures and applications supporting the semiconductor industry's AI-driven scaling roadmap.
As the AI infrastructure build-out drives demand for higher-density, higher-bandwidth chip-to-chip and chip-to-package interconnects, the expanded partnership is intended to give mutual customers earlier access to co-optimized process and assembly solutions spanning the full advanced packaging flow – from wafer-level hybrid bonding through panel-scale integration.
In 2020, Applied and Besi established a joint Center of Excellence at Applied's Advanced Packaging Development Center in Singapore , combining Applied's process expertise in etch, planarization, deposition, wafer cleaning, metrology, inspection and particle defect control with Besi's die placement, interconnect and assembly technology. That collaboration resulted in Kinex™ , the industry’s first integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system.
“Besi has been a trusted partner since we began co-developing next-generation hybrid bonding solutions,” said Gary Dickerson , President and CEO of Applied Materials. “With Besi joining EPIC as an Innovation Partner, we’re extending that collaboration across the interconnect technologies our customers need to scale AI systems. Bringing this work into Applied's EPIC Center gives both companies earlier visibility into where the roadmap is headed and lets us co-optimize the full packaging flow.”
“Our center of excellence with Applied in Singapore has been foundational to Besi's hybrid bonding roadmap,” said Richard Blickman , CEO and Chairman of the Board of Management of Besi. “Joining Applied's EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner is a natural next step, giving us a seat alongside the leading logic, memory and systems companies as we advance TCB scaling, die-on-panel integration and the interconnect technologies that will define the next generation of AI and photonics systems”
As an Innovation Partner, Besi engineers will work alongside Applied's teams at the EPIC Center to accelerate joint development across a broader set of interconnect and integration technologies. While advanced packaging was historically treated as a back-end assembly step, technologies such as hybrid bonding and panel-level integration now depend on the same materials engineering disciplines that define front-end wafer fabrication.
“Advanced packaging is no longer a back-end assembly step – it is a materials engineering challenge that demands the same precision and cleanliness as front-end wafer fabrication,” said Dr. Prabu Raja , President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “Developing these technologies together with Besi engineers in a front-end R&D environment like the EPIC Center will allow us to treat them as one connected flow rather than a series of isolated steps. That gives our mutual customers earlier access to co-optimized solutions and a faster path from development to high-volume manufacturing.”
The expanded scope of collaboration will focus on next-generation 3D IC scaling and logic and memory integration for AI compute and memory architectures, with expected R&D programs to include:
New platforms for die-to-wafer hybrid bonding, building on the companies' existing Singapore Center of Excellence 
Scaling of thermo-compression bonding (TCB) and its surrounding process ecosystem
New die-on-wafer, die-on-die and die-on-panel integration platforms
Photonics-enabled interconnect applications supporting co-packaged optics and AI system scaling
Applied’s new, $5 billion * EPIC (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) Center in Silicon Valley represents the largest-ever U.S . investment in advanced semiconductor equipment and process technology R&D. The center, which will be operationally ready this year, is designed from the ground up to dramatically reduce the time it takes to commercialize breakthrough technologies from early-stage research to full-scale manufacturing.
*Capital spending is expected to scale over time to approximately $5 billion as customer projects commence. 
About Applied Materials 
Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) is the leader in materials engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor and advanced display in the world. The technology we create is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation chips. At Applied, we push the boundaries of science and engineering to deliver material innovation that changes the world. Learn more at www.appliedmaterials.com .

Ouster Partners with Seneca to Advance Autonomous Drone Technology for Wildfire Response Operations
October 1, 2026
PDF Version 
Ouster's REV8 OS1 Max native color digital lidar powers next-generation autonomous drones with enhanced 3D perception for safer, faster operations in complex wildfire environments 
SAN FRANCISCO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 1, 2026--
Ouster, Inc. (Nasdaq: OUST), a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI, and Seneca , an autonomous aviation company developing advanced drone technology to support wildfire response, today announced a partnership to integrate Ouster’s Rev8 native color lidar into Seneca's autonomous drone platform.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261001404293/en/ 
Ouster Rev8 OS1 Max digital lidar at the center of the Seneca Argo-1 mast
The collaboration combines Ouster's high-resolution, rugged Rev8 OS1 Max digital lidar with Seneca's autonomous drone platform to enhance perception, navigation, and obstacle avoidance in demanding outdoor environments. By integrating the digital lidar into its perception stack, Seneca aims to enable its drones to operate safely at higher speeds across the three mission areas that define its platform: carrying heavy cargo to the fire line, following terrain for mapping and vegetation management, and inspecting structures and utility infrastructure. Longer range gives an aircraft more time to react to what is ahead, and 256 channels at up to 4K horizontal resolution hold that detail as speed increases.
Smoke, dust, rapidly changing terrain, and limited visibility make wildfire operations uniquely challenging for autonomous aircraft. Previously, Seneca relied on infrared sensors and cameras for collision avoidance, mapping, and object detection. With Ouster's Rev8 native color digital lidar, Seneca generates a precise 3D representation of its surroundings, delivering reliable navigation and environmental awareness whether a drone is hauling cargo, tracing a ridgeline, or inspecting a utility span in harsh and unpredictable conditions.
“Seneca's fire agency partners operate in some of the most unforgiving environments – obviously heat, but also sometimes extreme cold. Ouster Rev8 OS1 Max has been invaluable in minimizing concerns about sensor durability and performance,” said Stuart Landesberg , CEO of Seneca. “Its IP68/IP69K rating, shock tolerance, and broad temperature range mean we can fly in conditions that would ground other platforms, meaning we can support firefighters, utilities, and communities on missions that were previously unsafe, inefficient, or impossible.”
Seneca selected the Ouster Rev8 OS1 Max for its performance, its qualification from -40 °C to +85 °C for the range of conditions fire crews work in, responsive engineering support, and a product roadmap aligned with the future of autonomous systems. Ouster's NDAA §164 and BABA-compliant digital lidar platform also supports Seneca's commitment to aircraft that are designed and assembled in America.
"Reliable lidar and perception technologies are the foundation of autonomous systems operating in the physical world," said Angus Pacala , CEO of Ouster. "Our digital lidar equips Seneca with accurate, real-time 3D perception data that enhances environmental awareness and supports safe, reliable autonomous flights for drone-based firefighting missions."
About Ouster 
Ouster (Nasdaq: OUST) is a global leader in high-performance lidar sensors and intelligent software solutions that bring physical AI to life across the automotive, industrial, robotics, and smart infrastructure sectors. Ouster’s technology delivers performance, reliability, and affordability to accelerate the adoption of autonomous systems at scale and drive meaningful improvements in safety, efficiency, and sustainability. Ouster is headquartered in San Francisco, CA , with offices in the Americas , Europe , and Asia-Pacific . For more information about our products, visit www.ouster.com , contact our sales team , or connect with us on X or LinkedIn .
About Seneca 
Seneca builds advanced firefighting technology for situations that were previously unsafe, inefficient, or impossible. Based in Sausalito, California, the company develops autonomous heavy-lift drone systems that carry suppressant to the fire line, follow terrain for mapping and vegetation management, and inspect structures and utility infrastructure, with one pilot operating multiple aircraft. Seneca's systems are designed, built, and sourced in America, and serve fire agencies, utilities, and property owners. The company's mission is to protect 500 million acres in the U.S. and allied nations by 2035.

SCHOTT Pharma makes decarbonization measurable 
SCHOTT Pharma makes decarbonization measurable
Thursday, October 1, 2026 , Mainz, Germany 
SCHOTT Pharma’s Product Carbon Footprint calculation tool for pharmaceutical primary packaging was successfully validated by an independent third party
It quantifies product carbon footprints and enables fact-based comparisons between products
This approach supports informed customer decisions on product decarbonization and measures to reduce Scope 3 emissions
SCHOTT Pharma, a pioneer in drug containment solutions and delivery systems, has had its Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) calculation tool for pharmaceutical primary packaging independently validated in line with the Together for Sustainability (TfS) PCF Guideline . As pharmaceutical companies increasingly focus on reducing Scope 3 emissions across their value chains, the need for comparable, externally validated product carbon data is growing. SCHOTT Pharma is committed to advancing decarbonization solutions in the supply chain, including the planned use of pharmaceutical glass with a up to 50% lower CO 2 e product footprint 1  and new circular packaging approaches . However, to translate such solutions into measurable benefits, their environmental impact must be quantified consistently and transparently. The new PCF calculation tool now gives pharmaceutical companies access to emissions data for vials or prefillable glass and polymer syringes, covering both the containers themselves and the upstream value chain.
“Decarbonization requires collaboration across the value chain. Our validated calculation tool provides the data foundation that helps customers and suppliers jointly identify, prioritize, and scale effective emission-reduction measures,” said Reinhard Mayer, CFO of SCHOTT Pharma.
An independent audit by GUTcert validated SCHOTT Pharma’s methodology to calculate PCFs for products such as prefillable syringes and vials. Image: SCHOTT Pharma
jpg 
 
5.1 MB 
Providing a reliable basis for Scope 3 reduction decisions
Most pharmaceutical companies have set ambitious decarbonization targets, with supply-chain-related emissions accounting for the largest share of their carbon footprint. To identify and prioritize effective Scope 3 reduction measures, they increasingly need objective product-level carbon data from their suppliers. However, differing calculation methodologies without external validation often make product carbon footprints difficult to compare across suppliers and products. SCHOTT Pharma addresses this challenge by aligning its calculation approach with the TfS PCF Guideline, which covers the requirements of most customer requests. To strengthen reliability and ensure consistent application, the methodology and calculation tool were independently validated by GUTcert .
The independent validation by GUTcert was conducted in accordance with ISO 14067:2019 (including Annex C), the GHG Protocol Product Standard, and the TfS 3.0 framework. It assessed the underlying methodology and SCHOTT Group’s PCF Guideline 2.0 , as well as the calculation logic and data flows, system boundaries, data quality and assumptions, and reporting approach.
To demonstrate practical applicability, GUTcert also verified three representative product carbon footprints from SCHOTT Pharma’s portfolio: a sterile 1 ml long syriQ® glass syringe, a sterile 1 ml long SCHOTT TOPPAC® polymer syringe, and a 2 ml Core Vial in TopLine quality. Emissions were calculated in grams of CO 2 e per unit produced using a cradle-to-gate approach covering raw material extraction, pre-production, upstream transportation, production, and storage.
The combination of a validated methodology and representative PCFs demonstrates SCHOTT Pharma’s ability to reliably apply the standards of the TfS PCF Guideline to real-world pharmaceutical packaging solutions.
“Reducing Scope 3 emissions starts with informed decisions. Comparable PCF data helps us and our customers identify where product innovations can create the greatest environmental impact. With our validated calculation tool, we are now able to provide this data reliably across our portfolio,” said Dr. Arne Kloke, Head of Sustainability & Service at SCHOTT Pharma.
By creating a standardized and externally verified approach to product carbon footprinting, SCHOTT Pharma is helping establish the data foundation needed for decarbonization across the pharmaceutical value chain.
1 Compared to conventional FIOLAX® pharma glass. More information: https://www.schott.com/en-gb/products/pharmaceutical-tubing-p1000372/product-variants/fiolax-pro-ocf

About SCHOTT Pharma
Human health matters. That is why SCHOTT Pharma designs containment solutions grounded in science to ensure that medications are safe and easy to use for people around the world. Every minute, more than 30,000 people receive an injection packed in a SCHOTT Pharma product. The portfolio comprises drug containment solutions and delivery systems for injectable drugs ranging from prefillable glass and polymer syringes to cartridges, vials, and ampoules. Every day, a team of around 5,000 people from over 65 nations works at SCHOTT Pharma to contribute to global health. The company is represented in all main pharmaceutical hubs with 17 manufacturing sites in Europe, North and South America, and Asia. With over 1,000 patents and technologies developed in-house and a state-of-the-art R&D center in Switzerland, the company is focused on developing innovations for the future. title: Proterial Makes Fiscal 2026 Disclosures Based on the TCFD and TNFD Recommendations
source: Hitachi Metals - Proterial 2026 Press Releases / Press Releases

content_text:
Proterial Makes Fiscal 2026 Disclosures 
Based on the TCFD and TNFD Recommendations
September 30, 2026 
Proterial, Ltd.
Proterial, Ltd. (hereafter “Proterial”) today made disclosures for fiscal 2026 regarding the impact of climate change on its business activities, in line with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). 
In addition, in a first for the company, Proterial also disclosed information based on the recommendations of the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD), in an effort to step up action on issues related to natural capital and biodiversity. 
1. Background and Purpose of the Information Disclosures
Proterial views the impact of issues related to climate change, natural capital and biodiversity on its business activities as one of its key management challenges.
In June 2021, Proterial expressed its support for the TCFD recommendations and has since continually analyzed and disclosed information on the impact that climate change has on its business activities. By gaining an accurate understanding of the risks and opportunities related to climate change, reflecting those insights in its management strategy and making highly transparent information disclosures, Proterial has strived to gain the trust of stakeholders while achieving sustainable growth through these efforts.
With the loss of the biodiversity that provides ecosystem services becoming a global issue in recent years, efforts to achieve nature positivity (nature restoration: halting and reversing the loss of biodiversity to put nature back on a path to recovery) by 2030 have accelerated globally. As one of those efforts, in 2023 the final recommendations (v1.0) of the TNFD were announced as an international framework for companies to evaluate their natural capital and biodiversity-related dependencies, impacts, risks and opportunities, and disclose information from a financial perspective.
Given this background, Proterial has made information disclosures based on the TNFD recommendations for the first time. Going forward, Proterial will make ongoing enhancements to these disclosures in an effort to manage and better mitigate its nature-related risks, expand the information it provides to stakeholders, and improve its corporate value.
2. Key Points of the Disclosures for Fiscal 2026
(1) Disclosures based on the TCFD recommendations
(i) CO 2 emissions (Scope 1 + 2) for the entire Proterial Group in fiscal 2025 decreased 16% year on year. Toward achieving the target 38% reduction in emissions compared with fiscal 2015 levels by fiscal 2030, Proterial has steadily advanced energy-saving measures and efforts to adopt renewable energy.
(ii) Proterial obtained third-party certification for its Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 Category 1 emissions in an effort to ensure the transparency and reliability of greenhouse gas emissions data.
(iii) Proterial developed an enterprise risk management (ERM) system to step up its risk management activities. Based on its environmental strategy to turn risks associated with climate change into growth opportunities, Proterial is aiming to achieve green growth.
TCFD disclosure materials:
https://www.proterial.com/e/tcfd/ 
(2) Disclosures based on the TNFD recommendations
(i) Based on the TNFD disclosure framework (v1.0), Proterial used the LEAP approach (see note) to conduct an analysis targeting the direct operations of the Proterial Group.
(Note) LEAP approach: an approach used by companies to identify their relationship with nature and assess their nature-related risks and opportunities. The LEAP approach involves four stages: Locate (L) the interface with nature, Evaluate (E) dependencies and impacts on nature, Assess (A) nature-related risks and opportunities, and Prepare (P) to respond to and report on nature-related information.
(ii) Of the priority sites that were identified, Proterial conducted scenario analyses for the sites, namely the Proterial, Ltd. Yasugi Works and the Proterial Metals, Ltd. Tsuchiura Works, to qualitatively identify nature-related risks and opportunities of high importance. In conjunction with these efforts, Proterial disclosed its fiscal 2024 results and fiscal 2030 targets regarding key response measures and related metrics.
(iii) Going forward, Proterial will expand the scope of analysis to other priority sites in the Proterial Group as well as upstream and downstream sites along the supply chain, while continuing to explore ways to enhance its disclosures.
TNFD disclosure materials:
https://www.proterial.com/e/sustainability/tnfd.html 
Looking ahead, Proterial will continue to appropriately identify and manage risks and opportunities related to environmental capital while seeking ongoing dialogue with stakeholders to pursue its stated vision of being “a high-performance material company that supports a sustainable society.”

title: TOPPAN Establishes FC-BGA Substrate Production Site in Singapore
query: https://www.holdings.toppan.com/en/news/
content_text:
TOPPAN Establishes FC-BGA Substrate Production Site in Singapore
Aiming to deliver a stable supply of high-density semiconductor package substrates from ADVANCED SUBSTRATE TECHNOLOGIES PTE., LTD., TOPPAN’s first overseas production site for FC-BGAs
Tweet 
Tokyo - September 30, 2026 - TOPPAN Inc. (TOPPAN), a TOPPAN Group company and wholly owned subsidiary of TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TYO: 7911), has recently established a production site for Flip Chip Ball Grid Array　(FC-BGA) substrates, high-density semiconductor packages, at ADVANCED SUBSTRATE TECHNOLOGIES PTE., LTD. (AST) in the Republic of Singapore.
This plant marks TOPPAN’s first overseas production facility for FC-BGA substrates, supported by the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) and BROADCOM Inc., a leading provider of semiconductors for telecommunications. A ceremony to mark the opening was held on September 29.
Background and Objectives of AST Establishment
With the widespread adoption of generative AI and data centers, data traffic volumes have skyrocketed, leading to a rapid global increase in demand for cutting-edge FC-BGA substrates to support this growth. Within that growing demand, there has been an urgent need to increase capacity specifically for delivering a stable supply of large-size, high-layer-count substrates required for AI and networking equipment. While TOPPAN had focused on increasing production primarily at its Niigata Plant, a new production facility was necessary to adapt to the increased manufacturing workload associated with larger size and higher layer count substrates and to meet growing future demand. Furthermore, from the perspective of business continuity planning (BCP) to prepare for natural disasters and geopolitical risks, it was essential to establish a risk-diversification system involving multiple facilities.
AST Attributes
・TOPPAN's first overseas FC-BGA production facility 
This is TOPPAN's first FC-BGA substrate production facility outside Japan. By also expanding major operations overseas with a move like this, TOPPAN will further strengthen its global production network.
・Focus on high-demand, large-size, high-layer-count substrates 
By specializing in the manufacturing of large-size, high-layer-count substrates—essential for generative AI, machine learning (ML), and large-scale network switches—AST will contribute to a stable supply in response to rising demand.
・Establishment of 70,000 m² state-of-the-art facility and development of highly skilled workforce 
AST operates a facility of approximately 70,000 m² in the vicinity of Jurong Lake District and employs more than 200 highly skilled engineers and technicians. AST has also established R&D functions to meet future market needs, as well as collaborative partnerships with local educational institutions.
Inauguration Ceremony
AST held a ceremony on September 29 to mark the opening. The ceremony was attended by approximately 200 people, including high-ranking government officials, including Mr. Gan Kim Yong, Singapore’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Trade and Industry, and Mr. Png Cheong Boon, Chairman, EDB, as well as representatives from partner companies and major clients.
A product exhibition area was set up at the venue to showcase AST’s cutting-edge FC-BGA substrates and TOPPAN’s diverse product lineup. Attendees expressed strong interest in semiconductor packaging technology for AI and networking applications, for which global demand is on the rise.
Comment from Mr. Satoshi Oya, TOPPAN Holdings Representative Director, President & COO
The reason we chose Singapore as our global strategic hub is that we were deeply impressed not only by the business environment and locational advantages from the global perspective, but also by their forward-thinking approach—always looking toward the future—and their ability to bring those ideas to fruition. I am confident that being able to walk alongside all of you in this wonderful place will provide a major boost to AST’s growth. Through a strong partnership with BROADCOM, TOPPAN and AST will deliver innovative technologies from Singapore to the global market and contribute to the development of a next-generation, highly digital society.
Future Goals
To meet global demand for cutting-edge semiconductor package substrates, TOPPAN has designated AST as its first overseas production site for FC-BGA substrates. Production will start in 2026, with TOPPAN aiming to support the development of global digital infrastructure by raising the FC-BGA business’s production capacity to at least 2.5 times its fiscal 2022 level by the end of fiscal 2027.
