title: Monsanto unanimously wins first Roundup™ trial since U.S. Supreme Court decision
query: https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/
content_text:
Monsanto unanimously wins first Roundup™ trial since U.S. Supreme Court decision
Summary
Missouri verdict demonstrates that plaintiffs could not prove their claims following the U.S. Supreme Court’s landmark decision in Durnell 
St. Louis, October 29, 2026 – A Missouri Circuit Court jury today reached a unanimous defense verdict in favor of Monsanto in the three-plaintiff case of Theresa Aretino, et al. v. Monsanto Company , the first Roundup™ trial to take place since the U.S. Supreme Court’s landmark ruling in Monsanto v. Durnell . The jury found for Monsanto on the design defect, fraud and negligence claims that each of the three plaintiffs pursued at trial following the Supreme Court’s favorable decision in Durnell, which preempted their failure-to-warn claims. 
“We are pleased with the jury’s favorable verdict for Monsanto validating our belief that there is no evidence to prove design defect, fraud or negligence claims in the Roundup™ litigation,” said Bill Dodero, U.S. General Counsel and Global Head of Litigation. “This verdict should send a strong signal that plaintiffs who wish to pursue claims in the court system following the Durnell ruling will face significant challenges both in demonstrating they have viable claims and putting forth the necessary evidence to prove them in court.” 
The first trial following Durnell 
In June 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court issued a landmark ruling in the Durnell Roundup™ case, affirming that the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) expressly preempts state law claims based on failure-to-warn theories when the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has made a definitive determination on product safety. These claims have been a central theory in the Roundup™ litigation to date. With failure-to-warn claims no longer available, the Aretino plaintiffs pursued design defect and negligence claims. The verdict marks the first time a court has tested the sufficiency of evidence to support design defect and negligence claims at trial in the post- Durnell landscape. 
Glyphosate’s safety 
Glyphosate remains one of the most studied agricultural tools in history. The overwhelming weight of scientific evidence and the consensus of regulatory bodies and their scientific assessments worldwide support the safety of glyphosate-based herbicides when used as directed. The U.S. EPA has repeatedly and unequivocally determined that glyphosate is not likely to be carcinogenic and has consistently approved Roundup™ labels that contain no cancer warnings. 
The company will continue to back the safety of its glyphosate-based herbicides – critical tools that farmers rely on to produce affordable food and feed the world – and will vigorously defend its products in any remaining litigation.

title: Arkema showcases its innovative materials for higher-performance, more sustainable sport at ISPO 2026
source: Arkema - High Performance Polymers News / Newsroom / News
query: https://hpp.arkema.com/en/
content_text:
Arkema showcases its innovative materials for higher-performance , more sustainable sport at ISPO 2026
Download the PDF 
On 4 and 5 November in Amsterdam, Arkema will present its latest innovations in high-performance materials for sports equipment, footwear, technical textiles and accessories. The Group will highlight its Pebax ® EVA+ range for midsole foams, as well as its partnership with Movmenta in connected footwear.
As partner to the world’s leading sports brands for several decades, Arkema develops specialty materials renowned for their lightness, energy return, durability and performance. At the show, the Group will demonstrate how these materials help reconcile two key industry requirements: enhancing performance and accelerating the transition to more circular solutions.
Pebax ® EVA+: a new generation of foams for sports footwear
The Pebax ® EVA+ range , a new generation of compounds, is designed for midsole foams in running, trail, hiking and safety footwear. These grades are compatible with conventional EVA processes. They enhance foam performance while allowing manufacturers to keep their existing equipment. The Pebax ® EVA+ range thus offers a balance between performance, ease of processing and cost competitiveness.
Meet us at Booth 6B12
Towards connected running shoes with Movmenta 
Arkema will also present its partnership with Movmenta , which created SOLLO, an ultra-lightweight, battery-free smart sensor integrated into running shoes. This innovative solution gives athletes access to real-time performance data by tracking foam wear over time.
A comprehensive portfolio for the sports industry
Visitors will be able to discover the Group’s materials for sports applications:
Pebax ® elastomers , the benchmark for lightness and energy return
Rilsan ® PA11 , a high-performance bio-based polyamide with a low carbon footprint* for sports equipment and technical textiles
Rilsan ® Clear transparent polyamides , for optical and protective equipment
Platamid ® adhesive solutions , for footwear and technical textile assembly
Arkema will also present its circular economy initiatives under its Virtucycle ® program , dedicated to the recycling of high-performance materials.
*Compared with an equivalent fossil-based long-chain polyamide, based on the IPCC 2021 GWP100 cradle-to-gate indicator (including biogenic CO₂ uptake), in accordance with ISO 14067. 
Learn more about
Sport and leisure

Notice regarding the Establishment of a Share Repurchase Facility
(Under the provisions of its Articles of Incorporation
pursuant to paragraph 1, Article 459 of the Companies Act of Japan)
At the Board of Directors meeting held on October 30, 2026, Tokyo Electron Limited (TEL) resolved to establish a
facility for the repurchase of its own shares under the provisions of its Articles of Incorporation pursuant to
paragraph 1, Article 459 of the Companies Act, as follows.
1. Reason for Establishing Share Repurchase Facility
TEL intends to establish a share repurchase facility to enable flexible repurchases of its own shares in accordance
with its capital policy, taking into account its current cash position as well as growth investment capital aimed at
medium- to long-term profit growth.
2. Details of the Share Repurchase Facility
1) Type of shares to be repurchased: Shares of common stock
2) Total number of shares to be repurchased: Up to 25 million shares
(Equivalent to 1.1% of outstanding shares excluding treasury stock)
3) Total purchase amount for share repurchase: Up to 150 billion yen
4) Period of repurchase: From November 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027
5) Method of repurchase (planned): Market purchase through the Tokyo Stock Exchange based on
a discretionary trading contract
(Note) Depending on market conditions and other factors, it is possible that no share repurchase, or a share repurchase of only a portion
of the above, will be carried out.
(Reference) Status of treasury stock as of September 30, 2026
Number of outstanding shares (Excluding treasury stock): 2,269,837,310 shares
Number of treasury shares : 70,326,355 shares
*TEL implemented a 5-for-1 common stock split on October 1, 2026. The above share numbers are presented on the assumption that
the stock split had been implemented on September 30, 2026.
Treasury stock excludes the Company shares owned by the executive compensation Board Incentive Plan (BIP) trust account and the
share-delivering Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) trust account.

content_text:
MilliporeSigma Opens €300 Million Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Center in Daejeon 
MilliporeSigma opened a €300 million Daejeon center, expanding regional capacity and access to critical bioprocessing materials. 
Subscribe
Share 
Icons revealed to the left 
29 Oct 2026 
| 
Burlington, Massachusetts, United States of America 
The company’s largest life science investment in Asia-Pacific to date expands regional manufacturing capacity 
Integrated digital systems support automated data capture and end-to-end batch traceability 
Advances the company’s in-region-for-region strategy, bringing critical products closer to customers across Asia-Pacific 
State-of-the-art facility designed to eliminate on-site fossil-fuel use and improve energy and water efficiency 
MilliporeSigma, the U.S. and Canada Life Science business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, today announced the opening of a new Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center in Daejeon, South Korea. The center represents an investment of more than €300 million, the company’s largest Life Science investment in Asia-Pacific to date.
The 44,500-square-meter site expands the company’s regional manufacturing capacity for critical materials and solutions used in the development and production of biologic medicines. It gives biopharmaceutical manufacturers across Asia-Pacific closer access to the materials and solutions needed to develop and produce biologic medicines.
"Reliable access to critical materials is essential at every stage of biologics manufacturing,” said Jean-Charles Wirth, Member of the Executive Board and CEO, Life Science of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Daejeon brings advanced production closer to biopharma manufacturers across Asia-Pacific, giving them greater supply confidence, as they move from development to commercial scale. The center adds the regional capacity customers need and delivers the quality and consistency they expect from us.”
From Daejeon, the company will supply bioprocessing products used from early process development through commercial-scale manufacturing. These include cell culture media in dry powder and liquid formats, including pre-GMP small-scale custom products through imMEDIAte ADVANTAGE®, process liquids and ready-to-use cleaning-in-place solutions; and single-use sterile sampling solutions based on the NovaSeptum® Sterile Sampling System. Together, they help customers accelerate development, scale production, maintain controlled manufacturing environments and reduce contamination risk. Cell culture media and process liquids will use animal-component-free raw materials and be manufactured to consistent global quality standards.
“The completion of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center, a world-leading bioscience company, marks a historic turning point in Daejeon’s rise as a global bio hub—not just for Korea, but for the world." said Tae-Jeong Heo, Mayor of Daejeon. “We will provide our full support to ensure that Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s foundational technologies at the Daedeok Innopolis and the capabilities of the local community can be brought together seamlessly. We will focus the city’s resources on building a world-class global bio ecosystem through close collaboration among industry, academia, research institutions, and hospitals.”
The center’s integrated digital ecosystem is designed to support automated data capture and end-to-end batch traceability, increasing process transparency and supporting quality management and regulatory compliance.
The facility is designed to eliminate the use of fossil fuels on-site while increasing energy and water efficiency through the use of solar power, a heat-pump system, energy recovery in air handling units, and rainwater reuse.
The Daejeon center is a key part of the company’s in-region-for-region strategy. It builds on recent investments across the company’s global network, including BioReliance® drug product testing in Darmstadt, Germany, and filtration manufacturing in Blarney, Ireland. Across this network, the company is bringing critical products and services closer to customers while applying consistent global quality standards.

Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, operates across healthcare, life science and electronics.
More than 62,000 employees work to make a positive difference to millions of people’s lives every day by creating more joyful and sustainable ways to live. From providing products and services that accelerate drug development and manufacturing as well as discovering unique ways to treat the most challenging diseases to enabling the intelligence of devices – the company is everywhere. In 2025, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, generated sales of € 21.1 billion in 65 countries.
The company holds the global rights to the name and trademark “Merck” internationally. The only exceptions are the United States and Canada, where the business sectors of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, operate as MilliporeSigma in life science, EMD Serono in healthcare and EMD Electronics in electronics. Since its founding in 1668, scientific exploration and responsible entrepreneurship have been key to the company’s technological and scientific advances. To this day, the founding family remains the majority owner of the publicly listed company. For more information about Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, visit www.emdgroup.com .

Hydro breaks ground on new press in Cressona, Pennsylvania
On October 27, Hydro marked the start of construction of a new 5,900 tonne indirect extrusion press line at Cressona, Pennsylvania. The USD 53.5 million investment will modernize production capabilities and strengthen Hydro's North American manufacturing footprint, with operations expected to commence in the first quarter of 2028.
From left to right: Rep. Jamie Barton, Pennsylvania House of Representatives, 124th District; Joseph Yutko, PE, Sr. Director Project Engineering, Hydro; Mike Hammer, VP & General Manager, Central Region, Hydro; Jeff Lehman, BUP President, Extrusion North America, Hydro; Michael Shay, District Director, Congressman Dan Meuser's Office; Rep. Tim Twardzik, Pennsylvania House of Representatives, 123rd District; Larry Padora, Schuylkill County Board of Commissioners; Jason Reilly, Vice President, Distribution & Regional Sales, Hydro (Photo: Art Clagett/Simone Associates) 
This indirect extrusion press investment marks the latest step in Hydro’s strategic modernization efforts in North America. The investment will replace equipment from the 1950’s, bringing with it Industry 4.0 technology, advanced automation, increased energy efficiency and best in class safety performance.
“We are extremely proud of this new equipment and the additional capabilities it brings to Hydro Cressona . This project will improve efficiency, enhance product quality and expand our indirect extrusion capacity to serve the growing needs of our key customers,” says Mike Hammer, Vice President & General Manager of Hydro Extrusion North America’s Industrial and Distribution Region.
Demand for indirect extrusions continues to grow in the commercial transportation , automotive , and electrical markets , where customers increasingly require high performance profiles with consistent dimensions, superior grain structure, and consistent mechanical properties. With this expanded indirect extrusion capacity, Hydro is well positioned to capitalize on these trends.
Investing in American competitiveness
Hydro has a robust presence in the United States, with nearly 6,000 employees and 19 production sites across 14 states. With plans to invest more than USD 800 million over the next five years, the company has raised concerns about the impact of U.S. tariff policy on the competitiveness of domestic manufacturing. Extrusion presses and other specialized equipment produced only in Europe are currently subject to elevated and frequently changing tariffs that increase costs and drive uncertainty. 
"This investment is about much more than a new piece of equipment. It is about Cressona, our employees, our customers and the future of manufacturing in North America. Cressona continues to serve as the keystone of our North American operations, and we’ve invested more than USD 150 million in the site over the past three years. We remain fiercely committed to investing in our U.S. operations, but the aluminium industry needs more nuanced trade policies that do not increase the cost of capital equipment and hinder industrial growth,” says Jeff Lehman, Business Unit President, Extrusion North America.
Hydro's Extrusion plant in Cressona, Pennsylvania, USA is one of the largest facilities of its kind in the world. (Photo: Hydro) 
About Hydro Cressona
Hydro’s facility in Cressona, Pennsylvania , was originally built in 1942 by the U.S. government and is the largest aluminium extrusion site in the western hemisphere, with~15.8 hectares (148,000 square meters) under roof. The site has more than 1,200 employees, nine extrusion presses, three extrusion ingot casting units, extensive fabrication capabilities and a distribution warehouse.
What is an indirect extrusion press?
Aluminium extrusion shapes heated aluminium by forcing it through a die to create a specific profile. In conventional direct extrusion, the aluminium billet moves toward a stationary die. In indirect extrusion, the die instead moves into the billet, reducing friction between the billet and the container.
The process can provide more consistent dimensions, grain structure, and mechanical properties, making it well suited to demanding applications where consistency and product performance are important. At Hydro Cressona, demand for indirect extrusions is growing in markets including commercial transportation, automotive and electrical. Indirect extrusion is a specialized process, while direct extrusion remains the more commonly used method for producing aluminium profiles.

What does Nobel Prize-winning science have to do with Umicore? The connection lies in turning fundamental chemistry into practical applications. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognized research that advances our understanding of how molecules can be created with greater precision.
That journey from fundamental chemistry to practical application is also relevant to Umicore. Within Precious Metals Chemistry , we support customers and research partners working on complex chemical transformations where catalyst performance and selectivity are important considerations.
At the heart of this year’s Nobel Prize: chirality
Some molecules can exist in two forms that are mirror images of each other, much like our left and right hands. This property is known as chirality. Although these forms share the same chemical composition, they can behave differently in biological and chemical systems.
This difference can have important consequences. In pharmaceuticals, for example, one form of a molecule may provide the desired therapeutic effect, while its mirror image may be less active or even cause unwanted side effects. Understanding and controlling chirality has therefore become an important aspect of modern chemistry.
What role do catalysts play?
A catalyst helps a chemical reaction take place without being consumed in the process. It can also help steer the reaction towards the product chemists want to make.
Asymmetric catalysis enables chemists to selectively produce desired molecular structures and has expanded the possibilities for designing increasingly complex molecules.
The research recognized by this year’s Nobel Prize advanced scientific understanding of asymmetric synthesis and contributed to the development of catalytic approaches that are now widely used in pharmaceutical, fine chemical and specialty chemical applications.
This is also where the connection with Umicore Precious Metals Chemistry becomes tangible. Pharmaceuticals are one of the sectors served by the business, which provides specialized catalysts and reagents used in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).
From scientific discovery to industrial application
Turning scientific advances into practical applications requires deep expertise across chemistry and materials technology. At Umicore, we bring together capabilities in catalysis, materials science and process technologies to translate that knowledge into solutions for complex industrial applications. That ability to connect science with technology and industrial know-how is how innovation can ultimately deliver value for industry and society.
Geert Olbrechts, Chief Technology Officer of Umicore
Scientific breakthroughs in asymmetric catalysis continue to support innovation in areas ranging from healthcare and agriculture to advanced materials and specialty ingredients.
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry is a reminder of the lasting value of fundamental scientific research and of the impact it can have when scientific discovery finds its way into practical applications.

Text in:
Umicore today inaugurated Zilverbos and the connecting road next to its site in Hoboken, together with Cathy Berx, Governor of the Province of Antwerp, Koen Kennis, Alderman for Mobility of the City of Antwerp, the Hoboken district, the Municipality of Hemiksem and other partners. 
Both projects bring an important change to the historically evolved interface between industrial activities and the surrounding residential area. Zilverbos is the green zone that creates greater distance between the industrial site and the Moretusburg residential neighbourhood. The connecting road between Moretusburg and Hemiksem provides a safer and clearer separation between public traffic and the industrial activities on the site.
Both projects are the result of years of preparation and collaboration with the City of Antwerp, the Hoboken district and other partners. Since 2020, Umicore has invested approximately €125 million in the two projects combined.
“With Zilverbos and the connecting road, historically evolved situations around the site have been structurally addressed. Umicore in Hoboken has played an important industrial role for generations, and with that comes our responsibility for the environment in which we operate. We know that these projects have significantly changed the neighbourhood in recent years. We are grateful to residents for their patience and involvement throughout this process,” said Johan Ramharter, Site Director Umicore Hoboken.
Where residential areas, public traffic and industrial activities were located very close to one another for many years, both projects create greater distance and a clearer separation between the site and its surroundings. They form part of Umicore’s broader efforts to further reduce the impact of its activities on the surrounding environment, in cooperation with public authorities and local partners.
Johan Ramharter
Green zone named Zilverbos
During the inauguration, the name of the green zone was announced: Zilverbos. The name has been placed on the new insect hotel at the north-eastern corner of the site. Zilverbos comprises around 11,000 native trees and shrubs across five hectares and will gradually develop further into a wooded area in Moretusburg. The area is not open to the public and has no recreational function.
Zilverbos creates a structural spatial separation between residential areas and industry. The Umicore site dates back to 1887. As industrial and residential development continued, the site and residential area gradually came closer together over time. In Curiestraat, for example, homes were still being built in 1958 just a few metres from the industrial site.
The zone forms part of Umicore’s environmental improvement projects in Hoboken aimed at further reducing exposure to lead and other metals. The twice-yearly blood lead measurements were among the factors underpinning the development of the green zone.
To create the zone, from 2020 onwards Umicore offered residents in the area closest to the site the opportunity to sell their homes voluntarily. In total, 186 homes were acquired. Four homes were retained and integrated into the new surroundings.
“Residential areas and industry both fulfil an important role in our society. The challenge is to enable them to coexist in a responsible way. The green zone, now Zilverbos, contributes to this by literally creating more distance between residential areas and industry. In this way, it gives concrete shape to a future-oriented and balanced development of the area,” said Cathy Berx, Governor of the Province of Antwerp.
The name Zilverbos emerged from proposals by local residents, employees of the Umicore site in Hoboken and the Heemkundige Kring Hoboken. The name refers to “de Zilver”, as the plant and its predecessors have been known locally for generations, thereby linking the industrial history of the location with its new green setting.
New connecting road makes traffic safer and clearer
Together with Zilverbos, the approximately two-kilometre-long connecting road between Moretusburg and Hemiksem was inaugurated. The connecting road is expected to open to traffic on 16 November 2026. Umicore made 3.7 hectares of its own land available for the project.
The connecting road provides a structural solution to a historically evolved situation. Part of Adolf Greinerstraat still runs through the site, where public traffic, cyclists and pedestrians share the route with industrial traffic. After the connecting road opens, this section will be closed as a public road and incorporated into the Umicore site. The new road, with a four-metre-wide segregated two-way cycle path alongside it, directs public traffic along the site and thus provides a clear and safe separation of traffic flows. Both have been integrated into the surroundings, with landscaping and facilities for the collection and infiltration of rainwater.
Umicore developed and financed the connecting road in cooperation with the City of Antwerp and the Hoboken district. The City and the district oversee, among other things, alignment with urban policy, the quality of the execution and safety for the different road users.
“With this connecting road, we are making traffic flows around the industrial area safer and clearer. Cyclists will have a separate and comfortable connection, while public and industrial traffic will no longer get in each other’s way. This project shows what targeted cooperation between a company, the City and the district can concretely deliver for mobility, accessibility and quality of life,” said Koen Kennis, Alderman for Mobility of the City of Antwerp.
The Umicore site in Hoboken recycles hundreds of thousands of tonnes of complex recyclable materials each year and recovers 17 different valuable metals from them, including critical metals that are essential to European industry. Gold, silver, platinum, palladium and rhodium, among others, find their way back into applications that are part of our daily lives and our economy after recycling, from electronics to mobility and advanced technologies. By recovering these metals and bringing them back into circulation, Umicore contributes to a more circular and resilient supply of raw materials in Europe.

Tokyo Electron Technology Solutions Fujii Head Office and Hosaka Office Achieve Platinum Status in RBA VAP
Tokyo Electron Technology Solutions Fujii Head Office and Hosaka Office (Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan) have earned Platinum Status, the highest recognition available, under the Responsible Business Alliance (RBA) * Validated Assessment Program (VAP), with a perfect score of 200.
Conducted by RBA-approved third-party auditors, the VAP assesses compliance with the RBA Code of Conduct across Labor, Health and Safety, Environment, Ethics, and Management Systems.
Tokyo Electron Technology Solutions Fujii Head Office and Hosaka Office underwent their third RBA VAP audit, achieving a perfect score across all evaluated categories in the initial audit.
Tokyo Electron Group remains committed to advancing sustainability-focused management practices in alignment with its Corporate Philosophy: “We strive to contribute to the development of a dream-inspiring society through our leading-edge technologies and reliable service and support.”
*RBA (Responsible Business Alliance): The RBA is the world’s largest coalition of electronics and other industries dedicated to responsible and sustainable business practices in global supply chains. Tokyo Electron became a member of the RBA in 2015, and since then we have been working with our suppliers to fully comply with the RBA Code of Conduct.

content_text:
Albemarle Announces Quarterly Common Stock Dividend 
CHARLOTTE, N.C. , Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Board of Directors of Albemarle Corporation  (NYSE: ALB) today announced that it declared a quarterly common stock dividend of $0.41 per share. The dividend, which has an annualized rate of $1.64, is payable Jan. 4, 2027, to shareholders of record at the close of business as of Dec. 18, 2026.
About Albemarle 
Albemarle Corporation (NYSE: ALB) is a world leader in transforming essential resources into critical ingredients for mobility, energy, connectivity and health. We partner to pioneer new ways to move, power, connect and protect with people and planet in mind. content_text:
Two-Year Data of Pimicotinib Demonstrated Durable Tumor Control and Sustained Improvement in TGCT Symptoms and Joint Function 
The company announced today new two-year follow up results from the Phase 3 MANEUVER study evaluating pimicotinib in patients with TGCT. 
Share 
Icons revealed to the left 
26 Oct 2026 
| 
Darmstadt, Germany 
Improvements in symptoms of pain, stiffness, and range of motion were sustained through two years 
Tumor responses remained robust 1 and durable 2 
Not intended for UK-based media 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, today announced new two-year follow up results from the Phase 3 MANEUVER study evaluating pimicotinib in patients with tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT). The study showed that among patients initially randomized to pimicotinib, improvements in symptoms and joint function were observed as early as Week 5, sustained through two years, and continued to improve over time. Tumor responses remained robust 1 and durable, 2 and the safety profile was consistent with previous analyses. The findings are being presented today in the Sarcoma poster session at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 (Presentation # 3747P). 
"For people living with TGCT, the impact of the disease is often felt through persistent limitations in mobility, physical function and the ability to carry out everyday activities," said Vinod Ravi, MD, MS, MBA, Department of Sarcoma Medical Oncology, Division of Cancer Medicine, UT MD Anderson, an investigator on the MANEUVER trial. "What is encouraging about these two-year findings is the consistency of improvements, not only in the durability of tumor response, but across the symptoms and functional outcomes that matter to patients. Together with the observed safety profile, these results provide important insight into the potential for pimicotinib to deliver meaningful benefit over time."
The new analysis in patients initially randomized to pimicotinib found that at Week 97, mean changes from baseline were 19.6% in range of motion, -3.9 in stiffness (as measured by the Worst Stiffness Numeric Scale Rating), -3.1 in pain (as measured by the Brief Pain Inventory worst pain rating) and +7.4 in physical function (as measured by the patient-reported PROMIS-PF scale).
Tumor responses also remained robust 1 and durable 2 through two years. Objective Response Rate (ORR) by blinded independent review committee (BICR) per RECIST v1.1 was 76.2% (95% CI: 63.8, 86.0), remaining unchanged from the one-year analysis, while ORR per BIRC based on tumor volume score (TVS) increased from 74.6% at one year to 77.8% (95% CI: 65.5, 87.3) at two years. Median duration of response was not reached at the time of analysis, and median treatment duration was 22.6 months (range: 1.8-33.6 months) at the March 1, 2026 data cutoff. Fifty-four percent of patients initially randomized to pimicotinib remained on treatment at two years.
In MANEUVER, pimicotinib was well-tolerated, with no evidence of cholestatic hepatotoxicity or hair/skin hypopigmentation. During the randomized, double-blind treatment phase of the trial, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) leading to treatment discontinuation occurred in one patient (1.6%) treated with pimicotinib; TEAEs leading to dose reduction occurred in 7.9% (n=5) of pimicotinib-treated patients.
"These two-year findings add to the growing body of evidence from the MANEUVER study demonstrating the potential for pimicotinib to meaningfully address some of the burden of TGCT," said David Weinreich, MD, MBA, Global Head of R&D and Chief Medical Officer for the Healthcare business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “The sustained improvements observed across symptoms, physical function and tumor control reinforce the potential of pimicotinib to address aspects of TGCT that can affect patients every day. These results add to our evolving understanding of the long-term benefit that pimicotinib may provide for people living with this debilitating rare tumor."
TGCT is a rare, locally aggressive tumor occurring in or around the joints leading to progressive worsening of symptoms including pain and reduced mobility of the affected joint, significantly impacting physical function in what is typically an otherwise healthy and young adult population. Patient-reported experiences indicate that up to half of people with TGCT may initially receive an incorrect diagnosis, which can delay appropriate disease management. 3 If left untreated or in recurrent cases, TGCT may result in cumulative morbidity and irreversible damage to the bone, joint and surrounding tissues.
Pimicotinib was approved in China by the China National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) in December 2025 and in Canada by Health Canada in June 2026 for the treatment of adult patients with symptomatic TGCT. A regulatory application is currently under review by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and other regulatory agencies.
1 54% ORR as assessed by BIRC based on RECIST v1.1 at week 25 vs. 3% with placebo; p 2 The majority (77%) of patients with response at 25 weeks maintained this clinical benefit after an additional 12 months of treatment.
3 Stern S, et al. Localized and diffuse tenosynovial giant cell tumor: real-world results from a patient observational registry. Future Oncol . 2025;21(12):1501-1510.

About MANEUVER 
The pivotal, global Phase 3 MANEUVER study is a three-part, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to assess the efficacy and safety of pimicotinib in patients with TGCT who were eligible for systemic therapy and have not received prior anti-CSF-1/CSF-1R therapy.
The ongoing study is being conducted by Abbisko Therapeutics and enrolled patients globally in U.S., Canada and Europe (n=49) and China (n=45).
In the double-blind Part 1, 94 patients were randomized 2:1 to receive either 50 mg QD of pimicotinib (n=63) or placebo (n=31) for 24 weeks. In addition to the primary endpoint of ORR at week 25, as measured by RECIST v1.1 by BICR, secondary endpoints include tumor volume score (TVS), relative range of motion, stiffness by Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), pain by Brief Pain Inventory (BPI), and physical function measured by Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS-PF).
After the double-blind Part 1, all eligible patients from either arm could continue to the open-label Part 2 and receive up to 24 weeks of pimicotinib treatment. Patients who completed Part 2 could then enter the open-label extension phase (Part 3) for extended treatment and safety follow-up.
About Pimicotinib (ABSK021) 
Pimicotinib, developed by Abbisko Therapeutics, is a novel, orally administered, selective and potent small-molecule inhibitor of CSF-1R. Pimicotinib has been approved for the treatment of adult patients with symptomatic TGCT for which surgical resection will potentially cause functional limitation or relatively severe morbidity by China National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) and Health Canada. It has been granted breakthrough therapy designation (BTD) for the treatment of inoperable TGCT by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and priority medicine (PRIME) designation from the European Medicines Agency (EMA). Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, holds worldwide commercialization rights for pimicotinib.
About Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, operates across life science, healthcare and electronics. More than 62,000 employees work to make a positive difference to millions of people’s lives every day by creating more joyful and sustainable ways to live. From providing products and services that accelerate drug development and manufacturing as well as discovering unique ways to treat the most challenging diseases to enabling the intelligence of devices – the company is everywhere. In 2025, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, generated sales of € 21.1 billion in 65 countries.
The company holds the global rights to the name and trademark “Merck” internationally. The only exceptions are the United States and Canada, where the business sectors of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, operate as MilliporeSigma in life science, EMD Serono in healthcare and EMD Electronics in electronics. Since its founding in 1668, scientific exploration and responsible entrepreneurship have been key to the company’s technological and scientific advances. To this day, the founding family remains the majority owner of the publicly listed company.

title: October 23, 2026 Hydro's third quarter 2026: Solid results and strong performance
source: Norsk Hydro - News Subscription / Investor News Subscription
query: https://www.hydro.com/en/global/investors/news-subscription/
content_text:
Hydro's third quarter 2026: Solid results and strong performance
Hydro’s adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was NOK 9,089 million, up from NOK 5,996 million in the same quarter last year. Higher all-in metal prices and higher alumina prices contributed positively in the quarter, along with improved earnings in Recycling and Extrusions. The strong performance was partially offset by higher anode and energy costs in Aluminium Metal, increased energy costs in Bauxite & Alumina due to gas supply disruptions, a stronger NOK vs USD, and negative price area differences in Energy.
Alunorte resumed regular operations following temporary gas supply disruptions 
Free cash flow of NOK 1.4 billion impacted by higher metal prices and associated working capital requirements and prepayments
First metal produced at HalZero test facility, marking important milestone for carbon-free technology track
Commercial momentum continues for Hydro's low-carbon and recycled aluminium portfolio
New PPAs secured, further strengthening Hydro's long-term power position
Hydro delivered strong profitability in the quarter, with adjusted earnings per share increasing from NOK 1.0 in the third quarter of 2025, to NOK 2.3 in the third quarter of 2026. Free cash flow was NOK 1.4 billion, as strong adjusted EBITDA was partly offset by higher net operating capital, primarily driven by increased metal prices and associated working capital requirements and prepayments. While this development reflects the current market environment, improving cash conversion and working capital efficiency remains a clear priority going forward. Consequently, Hydro has updated its year-end capex guiding to around NOK 12.5 billion, down from NOK 13.5 billion, and net working capital guiding to around NOK 32 billion, up from NOK 30 billion. The twelve month adjusted RoaCE ended at 12.5 percent.
“Hydro’s third quarter results reflect strong operational performance amplified by market tailwinds. Record high liquid metal production from our Norwegian smelter system, combined with strong pricing throughout the quarter drove solid earnings and strong profitability. Operational excellence enables us to capture more of the upside when markets are strong and, more importantly, builds resilience when markets turn,” says Eivind Kallevik, President and CEO of Hydro. 
During the third quarter, disruption in natural gas supplies to Alunorte temporarily reduced production at the refinery. Through mitigating actions, including securing alternative LNG supply, Hydro maintained operational continuity and successfully restored alumina production.
Aluminium Metal benefited from higher all-in metal prices and strong operational performance, while Recycling and Extrusions delivered improved earnings supported by strong recycling margins. Hydro's Norwegian smelters increased liquid metal production to record levels, reinforcing Hydro's position as a reliable supplier of low-carbon aluminium to European customers. 
In parallel, Hydro experienced continued momentum for its low-carbon and recycled products, with leading brands like CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty , General Motors , and Mercedes-Benz integrating Hydro’s solutions in their product lines. 
“We continue to see strong demand for our low-carbon and recycled offerings from some of the world’s leading consumer brands. When brands like CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty and Mercedes-Benz choose Hydro, they place their trust in our quality, reliability, and ability to help them achieve their ambitions. That trust has commercial value and reinforces our confidence in the long-term opportunities for low-carbon and recycled aluminium,” says Kallevik.
Hydro reached an important milestone in the development of its HalZero technology by producing aluminium for the first time, demonstrating the core electrolysis technology beyond laboratory scale. The achievement marks an important step toward Hydro’s long-term ambition of eliminating emissions from electrolysis and anode production. Further testing, piloting and technology development remain before any potential industrial application. Enova awarded NOK 82 million in funding to support the concept development and planning of an industrial concept pilot.
“This is an important milestone and a significant step forward in the development of HalZero. Producing the first metal demonstrates that the electrolysis technology works and paves the way for the continued development of a game changing technology with the potential to enable emission-free aluminium production in the future,” says Kallevik.
During the quarter, Slovalco began the restart of primary aluminium production following the agreement announced in July on long-term framework conditions with the Slovak government. The restart commenced in late August, marking the return of capacity curtailed during the European energy crisis in 2022. The first phase targets an annual production capacity of 75,000 tonnes by the end of February 2027. The restart reflects the importance of competitive power, predictable regulatory frameworks, and effective industrial policy in maintaining and rebuilding Europe's industrial base.
Results and market development per business area 
Adjusted EBITDA for Bauxite & Alumina decreased compared to the third quarter of last year, to NOK 283 million from NOK 1,290 million, mainly driven by lower alumina sales prices, natural gas supply disruptions resulting in higher LNG sourcing costs and unfavourable BRL/USD exchange rate effects. This was partly offset by lower raw material costs and lower fixed costs. 
PAX traded up throughout the third quarter 2026 to USD 370 per mt at the end on the quarter, diverging from Chinese alumina prices moving down. Despite lower alumina production at certain refineries in Indonesia because of raw material supply challenges, the World ex-China alumina market was oversupplied in the quarter. China's alumina market became increasingly oversupplied during the quarter as new refinery capacity came on line. Chinese alumina prices were close to the marginal cash production cost. Approximately half of China’s alumina production depends on bauxite imported from Guinea. The government of Guinea is considering the possibility of restricting annual bauxite exports volume, but no formal announcement has been made. 
Adjusted EBITDA for Energy decreased in the third quarter compared to the same period last year, to NOK 411 million from NOK 828 million. The decrease is mainly due to a loss on price area differences compared to a gain in the same period last year.
Average Nordic power prices increased in the third quarter compared with both the previous quarter and the same quarter last year. The increase was mainly driven by weak hydrological conditions and higher power prices in Continental Europe. Price area differences between the south and north of the Nordic market were above the previous quarter and below the same period last year. The price difference between central Norway and northern Sweden widened significantly compared with both the previous quarter and the same quarter last year.
The Nordic hydrological balance at the end of the quarter was 13 TWh below normal, compared to 15 TWh below normal at the end of last quarter and 1 TWh below normal at the same time last year. Norwegian hydropower reservoirs were around 67.8 percent of full capacity at the end of the quarter, which is below the normal for this time of year of 82.8 percent. The distribution was uneven, with lower than normal levels in the southern and central Norway, and higher than normal levels in the north.
Adjusted EBITDA for Aluminium Metal increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, to NOK 7,031 million from NOK 2,732 million, due to higher all-in metal prices, partly offset by lower sales volume, higher energy and carbon cost, and weaker USD to NOK. Global primary aluminium consumption was slightly higher compared to the third quarter of 2025, driven by a 3.0 percent increase in Asia. Primary consumption in the World ex. China is estimated to be down compared to the third quarter of 2025. The Middle East crisis continued to affect the aluminium market and prices during the third quarter. Following indications that the conflict might be nearing an end at the end of the second quarter, tensions increased again in the third quarter, directly contributing to higher aluminium prices. Throughout the quarter the market traded in a range between USD 3,100 per mt and USD 3,300 per mt. Consequently, the three month aluminium price increased slightly throughout the third quarter of 2026, starting the quarter at USD 3,076 per mt and ending at USD 3,170 per mt. 
Adjusted EBITDA for Metal Markets decreased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year, to NOK 125 million from NOK 154 million, due to lower results from sourcing and trading activities, partly offset by higher results from recyclers. 
Adjusted EBITDA for Extrusions increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, to NOK 1,189 million from NOK 1,107 million, driven by higher recycling margins in combination with increased sales volume, partly offset by higher maintenance cost, higher SG&A cost and negative currency effects mainly from stronger NOK/USD. 
CRU estimates that European extrusion demand increased by 1 percent in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, following weaker market conditions in the first half of the year. Automotive demand remained positive, supported by continued growth in battery electric vehicle production. Non-automotive transportation also turned positive after a weak start to the year, while building and construction remained broadly stable in the quarter.
CRU estimates that North American extrusion demand remained broadly unchanged in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, following a decline in the first half of the year. Commercial transportation continued to grow, supported by improving truckload rates, with further growth expected going forward. The industrial segment also remained solid, supported in part by continued datacenter investments. Automotive demand remained subdued, reflecting persistent headwinds in electric vehicle production.
Other key financials
Compared to the second quarter of 2026, Hydro’s adjusted EBITDA increased to NOK 9,089 million from NOK 8,923 million, mainly due to higher all-in metal and alumina prices and lower fixed costs in the third quarter of the year. This was partially offset by higher energy costs in Bauxite & Alumina due to gas supply disruptions and seasonally lower Extrusion volumes and margins.
Net income (loss) amounted to NOK 5,263 million in the third quarter of 2026. Net income (loss) included unrealized derivative losses, mainly on LME related contracts of NOK 204 million, environmental cost of NOK 111 million, rationalization charges and closure costs of NOK 81 million, and impairment charges on fixed assets of NOK 70 million. The tax effect on these adjustments reflected a standardized tax rate for taxable gains and tax deductible losses. Adjusted net income (loss) for the first quarter ended at NOK 4,372 million. 
Hydro’s net debt decreased from NOK 16.3 billion to NOK 15.4 billion during the third quarter of 2026. The net debt decrease was mainly due to positive EBITDA contributions, partially offset by net operating capital build, investments and negative other operating cash flow. 
Adjusted net debt decreased from NOK 22.8 billion to NOK 21.9 billion, mainly driven by the decrease in net debt.
Reported earnings before financial items and tax (EBIT), and net income include effects that are disclosed in the quarterly report. Adjustments to EBITDA, EBIT, and net income (loss) are defined and described as part of the alternative performance measures (APM) section in the quarterly report.

title: Manganese: Essential ingredient of the modern world

Manganese: Essential ingredient of the modern world

Many critical raw materials play vital roles in the economy, often enabling niche yet essential high-tech applications. Manganese, however, is different. As a key ingredient in traditional industry and clean mobility, it’s a metal on which the world fundamentally depends.
Unlike many critical raw materials, manganese is not rare; global ore supply is relatively abundant. Yet its importance is irreplaceable. No alternative material performs the same function in steelmaking, where manganese removes oxygen and sulphur, providing strength and workability. In the energy transition, high-grade refined manganese is increasingly essential in EV batteries, helping to improve safety, performance and lowering cost. 
Sourcing concentration
While manganese ore is widely distributed, around 90% of refining capacity – particularly for battery-grade High-Purity Manganese Sulphate Monohydrate (HPMSM) – is concentrated in China. This creates a strategic bottleneck and is a primary reason why refined manganese is considered a critical raw material.
Vincent Braet, Purchase Manager for Manganese at Umicore, explains: “If you look at it geographically, manganese is quite well spread globally. But refining capacity is highly centralized in China, especially for high-purity manganese used in batteries. That’s where the criticality comes from.” 
Manganese in advanced battery chemistries
Umicore makes extensive use of manganese in nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) cathode materials. NMC offers an optimal balance of energy density, stability and cost, making it an attractive chemistry for electric vehicles. By combining nickel for higher energy, manganese for safety and structural stability, and cobalt for power, NMC enables longer driving range while maintaining performance and durability. 
In the context of NMC cathode-active materials, manganese acts as a structural stabilizer, allowing for longer life cycle of the final battery. It also improves thermal stability, for improved battery safety
Pierre-Etienne, Research, Development and Innovation Director
Manganese is also critical for lithium-manganese-rich (LMR) batteries, an area of growing importance for Umicore. LMR is one of the most promising new battery materials for the volume segment of the EV market. With less nickel and cobalt, the manganese-rich chemistry offers lower metal costs at NMC-like energy density. Crucially, it poses an alternative to lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, with equivalent safety, longer driving ranges and good recyclability. As such, LMR is seen as one of the most promising new battery materials. Umicore has developed and protected specific LMR cathode-active materials that can be produced in its sites in Finland and Poland.
As Pierre-Etienne explains: “ The biggest advantage of LFP is the lower raw material cost and therefore the lower battery and overall EV price. As a result, our focus is on maximizing the amount of manganese and reducing the use of cobalt and nickel, while preserving performance. As a result, we see manganese playing a crucial role, in the volume segment of the EV battery market. We have developed a large catalogue of NMC and LMR to maximize the use of each technology.” 
He adds that an advantage for Umicore is that these technologies do not require separate production facilities. “High-nickel or high-manganese battery materials can be produced in the same factories, allowing us to use the same production capacity for different grades of NMC and LMR technologies.” 
Looking ahead, manganese looks set to become even more important in battery technologies as manufacturers seek to reduce material costs, ease reliance on nickel and cobalt, and support more affordable electric vehicles. As Pierre-Etienne says: “I would say there’s an all-round tendency in cathode technology to increase the manganese concentration.” 
Manganese may also feature in future solid-state batteries, which replace a liquid electrolyte with a solid substance. Although not yet on the market, solid-state batteries are expected to offer far higher energy density, thereby extending EV driving ranges beyond what is possible today. Umicore holds key patents for this new battery technology and has developed a specific LMR grade for solid-state batteries.
Broader industrial applications
Within Umicore’s Cobalt and Specialty Materials (CSM) business, manganese is used in products such as manganese acetate and manganese carbonate, primarily as catalysts in the chemical industry. A key example is the production of purified terephthalic acid (PTA), a precursor for polymers such as PET.
Manganese compounds are also used as driers in coatings and inks, fertilizers, animal feed, and agrochemicals. This breadth of applications underlines manganese’s broader industrial relevance: even when it is not the most visible or high-value material, it often performs enabling roles in processes and products that modern economies rely on.
Transparency and sustainability
As well as the concentration of refining capacity in China, transparency is another sourcing challenge for manganese. While manganese may not carry the same level of ESG concern over responsible sourcing as cobalt, nickel and lithium, clearer visibility across the supply chain is still needed. “The visibility on the complete supply chain is still not where we’d like it to be,” says Vincent.
Improving that transparency means looking beyond direct suppliers to understand where material originates, how it is processed, and which risks may exist further upstream.
On the plus side, Vincent adds that “manganese typically has a much lower carbon footprint compared with other battery raw materials.” This is because manganese ore generally contains a relatively high concentration of the metal (40% or more), meaning less material needs to be mined and processed to extract usable metal. 
For battery makers, this means that increasing the manganese content in cathode materials can help reduce the overall carbon footprint of the material mix, as well as lowering raw material costs. As Vincent puts it, this can be “an additional advantage” of manganese-rich battery chemistries
Recycling – limited role, for now
Because manganese is relatively low value, it has not traditionally been a priority material for recovery.
Manganese typically costs $2 per kg, which reduces the incentive for recycling compared to other metals.
Thomas Martens, Commercial & Value Chain Director, Umicore Cobalt & Specialty Materials
EV battery recycling is unlikely to provide a major near-term source of recycled manganese. Vincent notes that batteries entering the recycling stream over the next 10 to 15 years still contain “more cobalt and nickel than manganese,” meaning “the amount of manganese that you will get now from recycling is still limited. However, that could change as future battery chemistries use more manganese.” 
A unique position
Manganese occupies a distinctive place among critical raw materials: abundant in nature, yet essential and sometimes irreplaceable in application. Its long-established role in steelmaking underpins modern infrastructure, while its growing use in battery materials positions it as an important enabler of the energy transition.
As demand grows for electric vehicles, renewable energy storage and resilient infrastructure, manganese is set to become increasingly strategic to both industrial production and the energy transition. It may not be the rarest or most expensive material on earth, but manganese is certainly an essential ingredient of the modern world.

title: 21 October 2026 Jenoptik raises EBITDA margin guidance for fiscal year 2026 to approximately 22 percent, following a strong third quarter read more
source: Jenoptik - News and Ad-hoc Releases / Regulatory Disclosures / IR News
query: https://www.jenoptik.com/investors/news-and-adhoc-releases
content_text:
Jenoptik raises EBITDA margin guidance for fiscal year 2026 to approximately 22 percent, following a strong third quarter 
21 October 2026 
The Jenoptik Group saw strong demand in the OEM businesses in the first nine months of 2026, especially from the semiconductor equipment industry. Due to amongst other things a change in product mix the Group’s EBITDA margin improved to approximately 22 percent in the first nine months of 2026 compared with 17.5 percent in the prior year, based on preliminary figures. Therefore, the Executive Board now expects an EBITDA margin of around 22 percent also for the full fiscal year 2026 (previously 20 to 21 percent).
Revenue growth in the current year is anticipated by the Executive Board to be unchanged between 5 and 9 percent compared with the prior year.
The high order intake momentum continued in the third quarter, in particular in the semiconductor equipment business. Based on preliminary figures, the order intake of the Group came to 1.1 billion euros in the first nine months (prior year: 777.3 million euros). Group revenue amounted to more than 800 million euros (prior year 753.2 million euros) and EBITDA to almost 180 million euros (prior year: 131.8 million euros).
Jenoptik will publish its figures for the first nine months of the current year on November 10, 2026.

query: https://www.hydro.com/en/global/media/news/
content_text:
Hydro reaches key milestone in development of zero-emission aluminium technology
Hydro has produced aluminium using its new HalZero electrolysis technology for the first time. The milestone marks an important step in Hydro’s work to develop a new primary aluminium production process with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions.
Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre is handed the first metal made from HalZero electrolysis technology by Hanne Simensen, Executive Vice President Hydro Aluminium Metal. (Photo: Anders Vindegg / Hydro) 
Since 2016, Hydro’s technology teams have been working to develop HalZero , an entirely new process for producing primary aluminium, which could replace the technology used globally today, first patented in 1886. The new technology is based on converting alumina into aluminium chloride before electrolysis in a process designed to keep chlorine and carbon in closed loops. The long-term ambition is to eliminate CO2 emissions from both electrolysis and anode production, releasing oxygen instead of CO2.
Hydro has now produced metal from aluminium chloride for the first time at its research and test facility at Herøya in Porsgrunn, Norway. The test facility was built with support from Enova, a state enterprise owned by the Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment, which awarded NOK 141 million in 2023 for the construction and operation of the facility. The test center has been in operation since January 2026, and is being used to test the individual process steps in the HalZero technology.
“This is an important milestone for Hydro and Norway’s technology and research communities, and a significant step forward in the development of HalZero. Producing the first metal demonstrates the technology developed in partnership with leading Norwegian research institutions, including NTNU and SINTEF, works. It paves the way for the continued development, maturation and testing of a technology with the potential to enable emission-free aluminium production in the future,” says Eivind Kallevik, President and CEO of Hydro.
HalZero is a long-term technology development program and one of Hydro’s most demanding technology initiatives in decades. Producing the first metal represents a major step forward, although several years of targeted testing and piloting remain before the technology could be ready for industrial use.
The main HalZero processes are being tested at the Porsgrunn facility. At this stage, production still generates CO2 emissions. The next step will focus on developing an industrial concept pilot, with the ambition of integrating and testing all the necessary process steps together.
The purpose of the pilot will be to establish the basis for the further industrial scaling of HalZero, with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions from primary aluminium production.
“Aluminium is a critical material for the energy transition and for transport, buildings, and infrastructure. If the world is to succeed in reducing emissions, we must also transform the way aluminium is produced. Developing an entirely new technology is demanding and takes time, but Hydro has both the expertise and a responsibility to help move the aluminium industry forward. That is what we are working to achieve with HalZero,” says Kallevik.
At Hydro’s Technology Center at Herøya in Porsgrunn, Norway, technologists are developing the HalZero production technology. (Photo: Narrativ) 
Hydro has invested significant resources in developing HalZero over several years. Funds from the climate and energy component of Norway’s CO2 compensation scheme are also used to support this work. Further progress depends on using the test facility over the coming years for systematic learning, testing and continued technology development. The experience gained at the test center will provide the basis for further work on the industrial concept pilot and subsequent assessments of industrial scale deployment.
Enova has now granted an additional NOK 82 million for the development of the project’s next phase , an industrial concept pilot for HalZero.
About HalZero
Primary aluminium is currently produced mainly using the Hall-Héroult process. Developed in 1886, this electrolysis technology remains the dominant industrial method for producing primary aluminium. In the process, oxygen from alumina reacts with carbon anodes, generating CO2 emissions.
HalZero is Hydro’s proprietary technology for primary aluminium production. It is based on converting alumina into aluminium chloride before electrolysis. In the HalZero process, chlorine and carbon are kept in closed loops, enabling the process to eliminate CO2 emissions from electrolysis and anode production.
HalZero is part of Hydro’s technology roadmap towards net-zero emissions from aluminium production.

query: https://www.hydro.com/en/global/media/news/
content_text:
Enova supports development of zero-emission aluminium technology with NOK 82 million
Enova, a state enterprise owned by the Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment, has awarded Hydro close to NOK 82 million for a feasibility study for the next phase in the development of HalZero, Hydro’s technology for aluminium production with net-zero CO2 emissions.
The first metal from the electrolysis at HalZero. (Photo: Anders Vindegg / Hydro) 
The funding from Enova will be used for concept development and planning of an industrial pilot facility (Industrial Concept Pilot, ICP), laying the foundation for further development and scaling of the technology.
“The support from Enova enables us to further develop the plans for the next phase of HalZero. This is an important step in developing and scaling the technology toward potential deployment at industrial scale,” says Hanne Simensen, Executive Vice President of Hydro Aluminium Metal.
HalZero is Hydro’s long-term technology development program for a new primary aluminium production process in which carbon is reused in a closed loop, with the aim of eliminating direct CO2 emissions from production.
On October 19, 2026, Hydro marked a key milestone in the development of HalZero, producing aluminium with the new electrolysis technology for the first time .
At Hydro’s test facility at Herøya in Porsgrunn, key parts of the process are currently being tested and further developed. The facility, which was also built with support from Enova , enables Hydro to qualify the technology step by step at a smaller scale, build operational experience and reduce technical risk before further scaling to pilot facility. The experience and results from the test facility form the basis for the continued development of HalZero.
The planned pilot facility will be significantly larger than the current test facility and will bring together all the key process steps in one integrated facility. The aim is to demonstrate the technology under conditions closer to industrial operation, test how the different parts of the process work together and establish the basis for further scaling. The plan is to build the facility in Grenland.
“Developing technology for zero-emission aluminium production is both costly and demanding. It is therefore natural for Enova to support Hydro’s work on new solutions that can contribute to the transition to a low-emission society,” says Evy Glørstad, CEO of Enova.
The funding does not constitute a decision to build the pilot facility. Any future realization of the facility will depend on the results of further technology development, completion of project development and future investment decisions.
About HalZero
Primary aluminium is currently produced mainly using the Hall-Héroult process. Developed in 1886, this electrolysis technology remains the dominant industrial method for producing primary aluminium. In the process, oxygen from alumina reacts with carbon anodes, generating CO2 emissions.
HalZero is Hydro’s proprietary technology for primary aluminium production. It is based on converting alumina into aluminium chloride before electrolysis. In the HalZero process, chlorine and carbon are kept in closed loops, enabling the process to eliminate CO2 emissions from electrolysis and anode production.
HalZero is part of Hydro’s technology roadmap towards net-zero emissions from aluminium production.

query: https://www.dnp.co.jp/news/
content_text:
社員のウェルビーイング向上に向けて「東京グリーンビズ・ラウンジ」に参画
市谷オフィス内に緑の特設ラウンジを設置 
企業情報 
サステナビリティ 
環境 
人権・労働 
人的資本 
大日本印刷株式会社（DNP）は、東京都が推進する「東京グリーンビズ」のコラボレーションパートナーとして、オフィス内に緑のある空間を設けて休息体験を提供する「東京グリーンビズ・ラウンジ」の取り組みに参画しました。2026年10月14日（水）～16日（金）に、東京都の市谷オフィス内の社員用共用スペースに、緑豊かな特別ラウンジを開設しました。
   
「東京グリーンビズ」と「東京グリーンビズ・ラウンジ」について
東京都では、「自然と調和した持続可能な都市」を目指し、都民や企業とともに、東京の緑を「まもる」「育てる」「活かす」取り組みを進める、100年先を見据えた緑のプロジェクト「東京グリーンビズ」を推進しています。「東京グリーンビズ・ラウンジ」は、その一環として、都内のオフィスビルに期間限定で特設ラウンジを開設するもので、緑あふれる空間での休息体験を提供します。各参画企業は利用者向けアンケートを実施し、その結果から休息効果を検証します。
＊詳細はこちら → https://www.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/information/press/2026/09/2026092408 
特設ラウンジ設置の狙いと概要
DNPは、市谷地区の敷地内に緑地「市谷の杜」 ＊ を創生・育成するなど、緑豊かな空間づくりや生物多様性の保全に取り組んでいます。また、職場に緑を取り入れるなど、社員のウェルビーイング向上につなげる取り組みも進めています。市谷オフィスではワークスペースや食堂などから市谷の杜が望め、社員が日常的に緑を感じられる環境となっています。
今回、本取り組みに参画し、これまで緑を配置していなかった市谷オフィス内のスペースに「東京グリーンビズ・ラウンジ」を設置しました。社員があらためて、職場に緑があることの価値や、仕事の合間にリフレッシュすることの大切さを実感する機会の創出を目指しました。
事務局から提供されたグリーンインテリアを市谷オフィスの社員共用スペースに設置するとともに、緑に囲まれて短時間の仮眠ができるスペースや、スマートフォンを預けてハーブなどの香りや感触を楽しめるスペースを設けました。
＊「市谷の杜」について → DNPの価値創出の中核拠点である市谷地区再開発の一環として創生した緑地で、社屋を囲うように広がっています。東京・武蔵野台地の固有の在来種を植栽し、かつての雑木林をイメージした自然に近い森を再現した緑地です。環境省の「自然共生サイト」に認定されたほか、「緑の都市賞」国土交通大臣賞などを受賞しています。（ https://www.global.dnp/ja/sustainability/ichigaya-forest/ ）

query: https://www.schmalz.com/en/career-company/latest/news
content_text:
Vacuum Pump for Mobile Robots
With the intelligent vacuum pump GSP, Schmalz is introducing an electric vacuum generator for mobile robotics applications and intralogistics processes. The demand-based pump control and automatic leakage detection adapt the power output to actual needs. As a result, energy consumption is reduced by up to 90 percent compared to conventional electric vacuum generators.
The intelligent control system detects whether the workpiece is airtight or porous and adapts the power output accordingly in real time. This can result in energy savings of up to 90 percent.
Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and automated guided vehicles (AGVs) have long since moved beyond mere transportation: They grasp, move, and handle objects on their own. Vacuum technology is key here: it combines gentle gripping with speed, flexibility, and reliability in dynamic processes.
Two technologies have become established in vacuum handling: electric vacuum generators, such as rotary vane or claw pumps, and pneumatic vacuum generators, known as ejectors. These are compact, lightweight, and suitable for dynamic processes. They require compressed air, which must be generated either centrally or locally. This requires two energy conversions: from electrical energy to compressed air and from compressed air to a vacuum. This makes the process energy-intensive.
Electric vacuum generators create a vacuum directly and do not require compressed air. However, many traditional solutions are large and heavy. Their mechanical parts also make them less dynamic, which means they should run as continuously as possible, even when a vacuum is not needed at times. Compact and energy-efficient solutions such as the ECBPMi and ECBPi vacuum generators, as well as the GCPi compact pump from Schmalz, partially bridge this gap. However, their maximum power of 50 liters per minute limits the range of applications, particularly in intra-logistic environments. Until now, there has been no solution for mobile and decentralized applications that provides a connection between a compact design, fast response, and high power.
Retrofitting without additional infrastructure
Schmalz addresses this need with the fully electric, ready to connect 24-V vacuum pump GSP. This pump enables automation solutions to be integrated flexibly into existing facility designs, independent of the compressed air network. This facilitates retrofitting and use in the automotive, glass, and packaging industries.
With a suction rate of 50 to 150 liters per minute, the intelligent vacuum pump GSP covers a wide range of applications. The vacuum pre-charge with the LQE compact valve and the integrated silencer reduce operating noise. In many cases, additional soundproofing measures are not necessary.
Up to 90 percent less energy consumption
At the heart of the vacuum pump is its intelligent control system. The speed automatically adapts to the actual vacuum level required. For airtight workpieces, the pump reduces its speed to zero and thus consumes virtually no energy. At the same time, it offers power reserves for fast cycles and for handling workpieces with leakage. Compared to conventional electric vacuum generators, the vacuum pump GSP saves up to 90 percent in energy. For mobile, battery-powered applications, this means significantly longer runtime or the ability to use smaller batteries.
Plug and play from the very first use
Designed for immediate use, the vacuum pump GSP is ready to operate right out of the box. No manual software setup is required. In combination with the LQE compact valve, Schmalz offers a plug-and-play solution in which the pump and valve communicate with each other autonomously. During the wait time between two gripping cycles, the system begins building up vacuum. At the next pick, the stored vacuum generates a targeted inflow pulse that accelerates the gripping process: This causes the workpiece to be drawn in more quickly. Atmospheric ventilation via the compact valve reduces energy consumption during workpiece release by up to 99 percent compared to conventional compressed-air blow-off methods. This interaction increases the possible cycle frequency and supports dynamic handling processes in order fulfillment and intra-logistic operations.
Automatic Start of Operations and Diagnostics
The NFC interface simplifies start of operations and diagnostics through smartphone access. Process and device data can be viewed at any time on the integrated color display and are transmitted to the higher-level PLC during IO-Link operation. The pump automatically detects whether it is connected to an IO-Link master and switches to the appropriate mode on its own. Using the transmitted vacuum values and diagnostic information, the system identifies potential malfunctions early on. Alternatively, the pump can also be controlled via standard I/O. The pump automatically determines the material porosity of the workpiece being handled—whether cardboard box, plastics, or metal—and adapts the flow rate accordingly.
Process reliability even during a power outage
The vacuum pump GSP automatically detects leakage as it occurs and adjusts the pump capacity without requiring any user intervention. Optionally, it can be designed for an uninterruptible power supply (UPS). This ensures that air-tight workpieces are held in place for up to 20 hours, even in the event of a power or grid failure.
Robot-to-Goods processes enable autonomous order picking that does not require a central compressed air system. Autonomous robots retrieve orders from the storage facility on their own. The vacuum pump GSP is particularly compact, lightweight, and energy-efficient, which extends battery life.
The vacuum generator is suitable for applications requiring low levels of compressed air, such as loading and unloading sheet metal parts in preform presses and joining machines, as well as for material handling in intra-logistic operations.
When combined with the LQE electrical compact valve, Schmalz creates a perfectly coordinated system. It enables exceptionally fast pickup and set-down times, up to 99% less energy consumption when setting down parts compared to conventional methods, and significantly lower noise levels.

title: 2026.10.16 お知らせ 東ソーの挑戦「車載用高耐熱性柔軟ポリウレタンの開発」を更新しました
query: https://www.tosoh.co.jp/news/
content_text:
TOP 
東ソーについて 
東ソーの挑戦 
車載用高耐熱性柔軟ポリウレタンの開発 
研究 
開発 
2026.10.16 
車載用高耐熱性柔軟ポリウレタンの開発
近年、自動車の電動化や自動運転技術の進展に伴い、電装部品 ※ の搭載数が増加しています。電装部品の多くは、熱や湿気、衝撃などからの保護を目的に「封止材」による封止処理が施されています。今後ますます需要拡大が見込まれる電装部品の封止材用途として、高耐熱性柔軟ポリウレタンの開発に挑戦しました。
ECU（電子制御ユニット）、センサー、カメラなどの自動車に装備されている電子機器の総称
目次
この研究になぜ取り組んだの？
ポリウレタンの可能性を広げ、自動車の先端機能を支えたい
近年、自動車の電装部品は、車内スペースの確保や車体の軽量化のため、小型化・集積化が進み、また高性能化に伴い搭載数も増えています。電装部品は、外気温や自己発熱などの影響により、最大で－40℃～150℃まで温度が変化します。そのため、封止材にも幅広い温度域で長期間安定して機能することが求められます。現在、封止材の材料は耐熱性と低温柔軟性を両立できるシリコーンが主流ですが、シリコーンに含まれる物質の影響により通電障害や電装基材との接着不良などの課題が存在します。これらの課題を解決するため、影響物質が含まれていない「ポリウレタン」で、－40℃以下の低温柔軟性、150℃以上の耐熱性を満たす開発に着手しました。なお、対応可能な温度域の観点でシリコーンはポリウレタンよりも優れているため、ポリウレタンで代替するという発想は今までに例がなく、未知なる挑戦でした。
封止材とは？
封止材用途における今回の開発品の位置付け
開発品のポイントは？
トレードオフの関係にある物性の両立
ポリウレタンは、原料となるポリオールとイソシアネートの反応によって得られる樹脂で、その種類の豊富さから幅広い物性設計が可能です。ポリオールには、高耐熱であるポリカーボネートジオール（PCD）を選定して検討開始しました。しかし、当社の既存PCDでは－40℃の低温領域で硬くなる傾向があり目標値を満足できませんでした。そこで、－40℃で柔軟性にも優れる新規PCDの開発に着手。－40℃の低温柔軟性と150℃の耐熱性はトレードオフ、つまり一つ得たら一つ失うという物性関係であるため、両立させるのは非常に大変でした。最適な原料の選定、原料の適切な量での組み合わせなど、仮説を立てながら数百回繰り返し評価をして目標物性をクリアしていくのは、まさに泥臭く根気のいる作業でした。
もう一つの壁が、粘度の調整です。封止材は、電装部品に注入する際の作業性の観点から低粘度であることが求められますが、低粘度化すると耐熱性が悪化する傾向に…。そこで耐熱性を維持したまま減粘するために、これまでにない発想で新規PCDの骨格をチューニングすることで目標粘度に到達できました。
このようにトレードオフの関係にある複数の物性を満たすために根気強く開発を進めた結果、シリコーンと同等の－40℃の低温柔軟性と150℃の耐熱性を有しながら通電障害などの課題もなく、さらにシリコーンよりも安価で提供できるポリウレタンの開発に成功しました。
この研究を通して感じたことは？
末端製品を意識した、きめ細かなヒアリングの重要性
当社は原料メーカーであり、封止材を使用する電装部品メーカーとの間に封止材メーカーが介在します。そのため、ポリウレタンに求められる物性は把握できても、封止材についての正確な情報を得ることは困難である中、封止材の特許調査や関係者へのきめ細かいヒアリングを通して末端製品を意識したポリウレタンを開発しました。特に関係者とのヒアリングでは、物性だけでなく市場の要望など多くの情報を得ることができ、ユーザー目線に立った開発につなげることができました。
今回の研究は どう生かされるの？
自動車の先端機能を支える電装部品の信頼性に貢献
本開発品は、－40℃～150℃の幅広い温度域に対応できる初のポリウレタンです。そのため、市場でのインパクトは大きく、封止材以外の用途にも展開が可能と考えています。現在は、封止材と同様に電装部品に使用される接着剤や放熱ギャップフィラー ※ 用途への展開を検討しています。本開発品は、シリコーンに匹敵する耐熱性と低温柔軟性を有しながらも、シリコーンより安価に提供でき、かつ安全性も高いことから、今後ますます進化していく自動車の先端機能を支える電装部品の信頼性に貢献できることを期待します。

Tokyo Electron Group remains committed to advancing sustainability-focused management practices in alignment with its Corporate Philosophy: “We strive to contribute to the development of a dream-inspiring society through our leading-edge technologies and reliable service and support.”
*RBA (Responsible Business Alliance): The RBA is the world’s largest coalition of electronics and other industries dedicated to responsible and sustainable business practices in global supply chains. Tokyo Electron became a member of the RBA in 2015, and since then we have been working with our suppliers to fully comply with the RBA Code of Conduct.
