Mental wellbeing is not something we can take for granted. At Umicore, safety always comes first, and that goes beyond physical safety alone. Just like creating secure working conditions, supporting mental wellbeing requires attention, intention, and space for open conversation. With this belief at its core, Umicore marked an important milestone with the launch of its first Global Safety Commitment Day, a new annual moment to reflect, connect, and care. Introduced by the Executive Leadership Team, this first edition focused on a theme that affects every colleague every day: mental wellbeing at work. 
A standstill moment for reflection
For several weeks, it was impossible not to notice the energy around Mental Wellbeing Day. Across Umicore, colleagues shared pictures, reflections, and testimonies about their sessions. The overall feedback was overwhelmingly positive, and genuinely heart‑warming to see.
Our Global Safety Commitment Day was designed as a standstill moment for everyone at Umicore: a pause from daily operations to reflect on how we feel at work, how we interact with each other, and how mental wellbeing shapes both performance and safety. Across sites and offices, teams joined facilitated sessions that encouraged open discussion, story sharing, and practical reflection. A pause that Umicore plans to do every year focusing on a different safety topic.
There was strong participation and real engagement. People spoke openly, without blame, and shared ideas in a very transparent way. It was clear that this was a topic people truly cared about.
Mental wellbeing is often about the small things
One of the strongest takeaways was that mental wellbeing at work is not necessarily about big projects or complex initiatives. Very often, it is about the small, everyday things: helping a colleague, having a real check‑in, communicating well, involving people, or simply taking the time to talk about how we are doing.
Many sessions also helped teams better recognize early signs when someone might not be feeling well. That awareness is an important step in creating a more attentive and caring work environment.
At the same time, the discussions clearly showed that wellbeing is a shared responsibility. Mental wellbeing is not something the company can deliver on its own. As leadership also emphasized, wellbeing is a verb: it is something we all need to nurture every single day. For many colleagues, this resulted in concrete personal commitments, from healthier habits to making more space for meaningful conversations.
Another key insight from the sessions was the connection between mental wellbeing and workplace safety. When people feel well, they are more attentive, more aware of risks, and better able to respond to unsafe situations. Mental wellbeing directly supports a safer workplace. This reinforces Umicore’s broader belief that mental wellbeing, like safety, is a prerequisite for sustainable performance and long‑term success.
Keeping the conversation going
One of the most important outcomes of the day is cultural: helping to lift the taboo around mental wellbeing. It is okay to talk about how you feel, and no one is alone. The day made that message more visible and tangible across the organization.
The ambition does not stop with one event. Sites are encouraged to build on the momentum and embed mental wellbeing more deeply into their ongoing safety culture. Sometimes that starts with a very small change: asking each other less often “How are you doing?” and more often “How are you feeling today?” can open the door to a more honest conversation.
Feedback and ideas from colleagues are already shaping what the themes and topics of future editions of the Global Safety Commitment Day could be, reinforcing it as a lasting tradition rather than a one‑off moment. Because when we feel safe, mentally and physically, we communicate better, support each other, and thrive together.

title: The Battery Show North America 2026: Arkema highlights material solutions for production of EV and ESS batteries
source: Arkema - High Performance Polymers News / Newsroom / News
query: https://hpp.arkema.com/en/
content_text:
The Battery Show North America 2026 : Arkema highlights material solutions for production of EV and ESS batteries
Arkema, a global leader in Specialty Materials, will showcase its unique portfolio of solutions and innovations for battery electric vehicles (BEV) and energy storage systems (BESS) at the upcoming US Battery Show 2026 in Detroit, Michigan (US), October 12-15, Booth # 2714.
EV batteries need range, safety and compact design, while stationary storage demands low cost, long life and large-scale reliability. Arkema will present solutions specifically designed for both markets, including materials for use both inside and outside the cell.
“While ESS production has increased significantly in the past year, we continue to see healthy demand across all segments of the battery market, Nicolas Champagne, global market manager for batteries and datacenter applications at Arkema, said. “We are actively looking at the needs of all battery segments to offer solutions that meet both existing and emerging technology needs.” 
EV Batteries – Material Solutions to improve range, safety and compact design
Arkema is working closely with battery manufacturers to improve upon both existing and new materials for use in EV battery applications. Efforts include solutions that significantly increase energy density, including recently introduced Incellion ® branded acrylic binders designed for silicon-based anodes, and Kynar ® PVDF products used as a cathode binder and separator coating in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. These solutions are designed to support higher active-material loading and the development of higher-energy-density battery cells.
The group also provides a wide range of materials that improve thermal management and other safety-related needs outside the battery pack, including Rilsan ® Polyamide 11 , Reafree ® coating resins, Zenimid ® Polyimide, Rilsamid ® Polyamide 12, Sartomer ® UV-curable materials, Bostik adhesives and other materials.
ESS Batteries – Solutions to improve value, lifecycle and scalability
ESS battery applications require a different balance of cost, safety and scalability. Arkema is working with manufacturers to offer unique solutions across those products. The group offers both Kynar ® PVDF and Incellion ® binders for use in LFP systems, the primary chemistry in stationary energy storage.
Additionally, the group introduced new Incellion ® binders for primer coatings and ceramic-based separator layers that complement existing Kynar ® Flex PVDF coating products already in use.
To address the industrialization of new battery technologies, Arkema recently introduced advanced research and production capabilities notably  with the successfully completion of a 15% PVDF capacity expansion at its Calvert City, Kentucky plant in June 2026.
Battery Circularity and Recycling 
Arkema supports battery circularity through products such as Albone ® hydrogen peroxide, a high-purity solution that is critical to hydrometallurgical recycling to recover metals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel from end-of-life batteries. Arkema also offers Bostik silicone free thermal gap fillers to support cleaner disassembly processes during the recycling process.
To learn more about all of Arkema’s efforts in this market, visit the Arkema booth #2714 at the US Battery Show in Detroit.
Kynar ® , Incellion ® , Rilsan ® , Reafree ® , Sartomer ® , Albone ® are registered trademarks, and Rilsamid TM is a trademark of the Arkema Group.
Zenimid® is a registered trademark of PI Advanced Materials Co., Ltd.

ALUMINIUM 2026: Hydro invests to strengthen resilience across the aluminium value chain 
Hydro will be present at the ALUMINIUM 2026 trade fair in Düsseldorf from October 6 to 8. During the fair, Hydro will present how it is future proofing customer products and businesses across European industry through investments in renewable power, recycling, partnerships, and production capacity.
Hydro's exhibition stand at ALUMINIUM 2026. (Photo: Anders Vindegg / Hydro) 
Since ALUMINIUM 2024, Hydro has entered several long-term renewable power agreements, invested in new production and recycling capacity in Europe, entered new partnerships with brands like Mercedes-Benz and CHANEL Fragrance and Beauty as well as customer agreements covering close to 360,000 tonnes of low-carbon aluminium for Europe’s electricity infrastructure.
The aluminium products from Hydro are critical to energy infrastructure, mobility, and building and construction as they contribute to future proofing customers. Value chain transparency, documentation, low-carbon and recycled content, and the way Hydro works with customers to deliver circular solutions demonstrates how aluminium is part of the solution.
The commitments come as aluminium is increasingly recognized as a critical raw material and Europe seeks to reduce vulnerabilities in strategic industrial value chains. Combined, the investments strengthen Hydro’s ability to supply responsibly produced aluminium through changing energy, market and geopolitical conditions.
“Disruptions in global supply chains over the past years underline how critical reliable access to aluminium is for Europe. As Europe’s largest primary aluminium producer, Hydro plays a key role in securing our customer’s access to renewable based, low-carbon aluminium from a transparent value chain. We continue to invest in production, in recycling and in renewable energy to provide our customers with this critical material,” says Eivind Kallevik, President and CEO of Hydro.
CEO Eivind Kallevik at Hydro's extrusion plant in Raeren, Belgium. The plant is specialized in extruding long lengths and precision-profiles, as well as anodized and machined components. (Photo: Christine Fon / Hydro) 
Securing renewable power for aluminium production
Competitive renewable power is fundamental to Hydro’s ability to produce and supply low-carbon aluminium to European customers. 
To reinforce this position, Hydro has entered into new long-term renewable power agreements for its Norwegian aluminium operations since ALUMINIUM 2024. The agreements provide increased predictability for stable, low-carbon aluminium production. 
Hydro is also investing NOK 1.2 billion in the Illvatn pumped-storage power plant , its largest hydropower development in more than 20 years. The project will increase flexibility in Hydro’s renewable power production portfolio and make better use of water resources.
Hydro will build a new pumped storage power plant in Sogn and as part of the project establish a new 8 kilometer tunnel from Fivlemyrane (1,018 meters above sea level) to Illvatn (1,382 meters above sea level). (Photo: Bosko Janjusevic/Hydro) 
At the same time, continued development of renewable power production and grid capacity is needed to maintain competitive industrial production, enable electrification and support new industrial activity. Hydro is therefore pursuing opportunities to develop additional renewable energy production alongside its long-term power sourcing.
“Long-term contracts, investments in existing hydropower plants and the development of new renewable generation are complementary measures. Together, they can provide greater predictability for industry while contributing to a stronger and more flexible power system,” says Kallevik.
Expanding supply for Europe’s electricity infrastructure
Europe’s electrification ambitions depend not only on expanding renewable power generation, but also on building and modernizing the infrastructure required to transport electricity.
Hydro is investing NOK 1.65 billion in a new wire rod casthouse at its Karmøy aluminium plant in Norway . The investment will add 110,000 tonnes of annual capacity for low-carbon aluminium wire rod used in power cables.
With a new wire rod casthouse at Karmøy, Hydro can produce more aluminium wire for a rapidly growing market. (Photo: Anders Vindegg / Hydro) 
Hydro has entered an agreement to supply up to 274,000 tonnes of aluminium wire rod to NKT through 2033 , and approximately 85,000 tonnes to Nexans between 2026 and 2030 . Together, the agreements cover close to 360,000 tonnes of aluminium for European power transmission and distribution infrastructure.
“By linking new industrial capacity with long-term customer commitments, Hydro is supporting more predictable access to a critical material for Europe’s electricity grid,” says Kallevik.
Keeping more aluminium in circulation, returning it to new products
Hydro reached a capacity of around 850,000 tonnes of annual post-consumer aluminium scrap recycling by the end of 2025, and is investing EUR 180 million in a new recycling plant in Torija, Spain . 
The facility in Torija will have an annual production capacity of 120,000 tonnes and will be able to process up to 70,000 tonnes of post-consumer aluminium scrap. Hydro has also i ntegrated Alumetal’s four plants in Poland and Hungary into its European recycling network , adding 280,000 tonnes of annual capacity for recycled foundry alloys.
Hydro is additionally working with customers and partners to return end-of-life aluminium to new products. The expanded partnership with Mercedes-Benz includes the introduction of Hydro CIRCAL recycled aluminium containing at least 75 percent post-consumer scrap into series production for the next generation of Mercedes-Benz’ large electric vehicles in Europe.
The fully electric Mercedes-Benz CLA in the electrolysis hall at Hydro Årdal, where Hydro produces low-carbon aluminium for European industry. (Photo: Halvor Molland / Hydro) 
In the Train2Train pilot led by Siemens Mobility , aluminium recovered from decommissioned trains will be recycled at Hydro’s facility in Ghlin, Belgium, and processed into new extrusion billets to produce rail components at Hydro’s extrusion facility in Harderwijk, the Netherlands.
In Norway, aluminium from the existing façade of an office building in Oslo is being recovered, recycled through Hydro’s European network, demonstrating how façade aluminium can remain in circulation through full material traceability. 
Hydro enables Norway’s first closed-loop aluminium façade in Oslo refurbishment. (Photo: Emilian Liliegren-Helgesen / Hydro) 
“These partnerships and projects demonstrate how recycling, traceability, and manufacturing can keep aluminium in circulation across European value chains. Collecting, recycling, and reusing more aluminium in Europe reduces emissions, preserves valuable resources, and gives customers access to products with documented origin and recycled content,” says Kallevik.
Restoring competitive aluminium production
In July 2026, Hydro’s joint venture Slovalco announced an agreement with the Slovak government enabling the restart of 75,000 tonnes of curtailed primary aluminium capacity .
Slovalco plans to invest EUR 100 million in the restart. Primary production at the plant was curtailed in 2022 amid high European energy prices. The restart comes as European production has declined and the region has become increasingly dependent on imported aluminium.
Slovalco will restart production of 75,000 tonnes of primary alumunium. (Photo: Halvor Molland / Hydro) 
“Europe has the industrial expertise and market demand needed to build competitive aluminium value chains. What we need is the long-term political commitment and predictable framework conditions that make investment possible. Hydro continues to invest because we see a future for European industry, with lower emissions, more recycling and a secure supply of reliable aluminium for our customers,” says Kallevik.
Hydro will present its investments and customer solutions at ALUMINIUM 2026 in Düsseldorf from October 6 to 8 under the theme “Future-proofing industries.”

content_text:
Update on Alunorte gas supply situation
Hydro provides an update on the natural gas supply situation at the Alunorte alumina refinery.
Alunorte was informed in August 2026 by its supplier CELBA of disruptions to natural gas availability. Consequently, Alunorte has not received contracted gas deliveries and is currently sourcing gas in the market at spot based prices. Alunorte is in parallel progressing a long-term gas supply solution on competitive terms. 
The potential third quarter 2026 financial impact for Bauxite & Alumina from the reduced production and purchasing gas at prices above the contract price may be USD 75 to 100 million. The estimated gas arbitrage impact for Alunorte for the fourth quarter of 2026 is between USD 90-110 million.
Alunorte does not expect further interruption to gas supply as a result of the current situation and continues to manage the matter in close collaboration with infrastructure owner CELBA and the relevant authorities. 
The financial impact remains uncertain and is subject to gas prices, contractual developments, and the implementation of a long-term solution. 
Alunorte is also pursuing available legal remedies and other measures to protect its contractual rights and interests under the existing gas supply agreement.

content_text:

2026.10.05 
スパッタ法により作製するSi添加GaN薄膜
これまでの2つのコラムでは、東ソーが開発したGaNターゲットと、その成膜技術についてご紹介しました。第3回となる本コラムでは、GaNに不純物としてSiを添加した「Si添加GaNターゲット」を取り上げます。Si添加GaNターゲットを用いる利点は、高導電性のGaN膜を成膜できることです。高性能なGaNデバイスの実現には、このような高導電性GaN膜が重要であり、Si添加GaNターゲットを用いた成膜技術は、デバイス性能の向上に加え、生産性の向上にも貢献することが期待されます。
目次
GaNにおけるSiドーピングとスパッタリング法
半導体プロセスでは、半導体の電気的特性や導電性を制御するためにドーピング技術が用いられています。ドーピングとは、半導体に微量の不純物（ドーパント）を添加し、導電性を制御する技術です。不純物を添加することで半導体中に自由電子やホールが生成され、これらが電荷を運ぶキャリアとして機能します。キャリアが自由電子の場合は「n型」、ホールの場合は「p型」と呼ばれます。
GaNでは代表的なn型ドーパントとしてSiが広く用いられており、スパッタリング法でSiを添加する方法の一つに、coスパッタ法があります。GaN膜の成膜における一般的なcoスパッタ法では、GaターゲットとSiターゲットを同時にスパッタリングし、窒素ガスを導入したリアクティブスパッタリングによって、Siを添加したn型GaN膜を成膜します。しかし、coスパッタ法ではGaターゲットとSiターゲットをそれぞれ制御する必要があるため、膜の均一性や組成を精密に制御することが難しいという課題があります。また、各ターゲットの成膜条件が相互に影響し合うため、プロセス条件の最適化が複雑になる場合があります。こうした課題は成膜プロセスの複雑化につながり、量産化を進めるうえでの障壁となります。
これに対し東ソーでは、あらかじめSiを添加した単一のGaNターゲットを用いることで、Si添加GaN膜を作製する方法に着目しました。この方法では、成膜プロセスの簡略化に加え、量産に適した安定成膜の実現が期待されます。
高純度・高密度Si-GaNターゲットの開発
そこで東ソーは、Si添加GaN（Si-GaN）ターゲットの開発に着手しました。GaNはもともと焼結が難しい材料であり、さらにSiを均一に分散させながら高純度・高密度のターゲットを作製することは、技術的に難易度の高い課題です。当社は、独自の合成・焼結技術を駆使してこの課題を克服し、高純度・高密度のSi-GaNターゲットの開発に成功しました。表に各ターゲットの物性値を示します。Siを添加していないundoped-GaN（ud-GaN）ターゲットと同様に、従来品に比べ高純度・高密度を実現していることがわかります。
また、ud-GaNターゲットと同様に、最大φ12インチ（約300 mm）の大口径Si-GaNターゲットの開発にも成功しています。さらに、ターゲット中のSi濃度は、10 19 ～10 21 atoms/cm 3 の範囲で制御可能です。これにより、デバイスの用途に応じて、適切なSi濃度のターゲットを選択できます。
Si-GaN膜中のSi濃度分布と電気特性
ここからは、開発したSi-GaNターゲットを用いてスパッタリング成膜したSi-GaN膜の評価結果をご紹介します。ここでは、c-Al 2 O 3 基板上に成膜したSi-GaN膜について、膜中におけるSiの分布を評価した結果を示します。
まず、膜中のSi濃度および深さ方向の分布を調べるため、SIMS分析を行いました。中央の図から、膜の深さ方向にわたってSiが均一な濃度で含まれていることがわかります。また、Si濃度を10 19 ～10 21 atoms/cm 3 の範囲で制御できることも確認されました。これは、ターゲットのSi濃度を選択することで、膜中のSi濃度を制御できることを示しています。右の図は、Si-GaN膜の断面におけるSiの分布をEPMAで分析した結果です。Siは特定の箇所に偏ることなく、膜中に均一に分散していることがわかります。これらの結果から、Si-GaN膜中のSiは、深さ方向および面内方向のいずれにおいても均一に分布しており、その濃度も制御可能であることが確認されました。
さらに、各手法で成膜したSi-GaN膜のキャリア濃度と抵抗率を比較した結果、当社のSi-GaNターゲットを用いてスパッタリング成膜した膜は、特に高キャリア濃度領域において、MOCVDやMBEで成膜した膜と同等、またはそれを上回る低抵抗率を示しました。MOCVDやMBEと比べて量産性に優れるスパッタリング法により、このような特性を有するSi-GaN膜が得られたことは、デバイス応用に向けて有用な成果であると考えています。
GaN HEMTへのSi-GaN膜の応用
ここで、高品質なSi-GaN膜をスパッタリング法で成膜することによるメリットの一例をご紹介します。図に示すのは、代表的なGaNデバイスであるGaN HEMTです。GaN HEMTでは、AlGaN/GaN界面に二次元電子ガス（2DEG）と呼ばれる高移動度の電子キャリアが生成され、この2DEGがチャネルとして機能することで、高速スイッチングや高周波動作が可能になります。そのため、6Gをはじめとする次世代通信技術への応用が期待されており、さらなる性能向上に向けた研究開発が進められています。
一方で、デバイス性能を向上させるためには、さまざまな課題があります。その一つが、金属電極とAlGaN/GaN層との界面における接触抵抗の低減です。ソース電極およびドレイン電極には、Ti、Al、Ni、Auなどの金属が用いられます。これらの金属はAlGaN層またはGaN層上に成膜され、熱処理を経て電極として形成されます。近年では、これらの金属材料のみで電極を形成する場合、接触抵抗のさらなる低減や信頼性の確保には限界があることが指摘されています。これは、GaNがワイドバンドギャップ半導体であり、金属との界面において電流注入を妨げる障壁が形成されやすいためです。
そこで近年、高濃度n型GaN（n + -GaN）層を用いた電極形成技術が注目されています。これは、AlGaN/GaN層に溝を形成し、その部分に高濃度のn型ドーパントを添加したn + -GaN層を形成した後、その上に金属電極を形成する手法です。n + -GaN層を挿入することで接触抵抗が低減し、電気特性が改善されることが報告されています。n + -GaN層の形成手法としては、スパッタリング法、MOCVD法、MBE法などが報告されています。その中でもスパッタリング法は、比較的低温で成膜できることや高濃度ドーピングが可能であることなどから、優位性を有する手法の一つと考えられます。当社のSi-GaNターゲットを用いて、高キャリア濃度のSi-GaNスパッタ膜を形成できれば、他の手法と比べて簡便かつ量産性に優れたプロセスにより、デバイス性能の向上に貢献できると考えています。
さいごに
ここまでご紹介したように、Si-GaNターゲットを用いることで、簡便なプロセスによる高品質なSi-GaN膜の形成が可能です。本技術をGaNデバイスに適用することで、デバイスのさらなる高性能化や製造コストの低減を実現し、GaNデバイスの普及拡大に貢献できると考えています。
Si-GaNターゲットをはじめとするGaNターゲット製品や、スパッタリングによるGaN膜の成膜技術について、ご不明な点やご相談がございましたら、下記のお問い合わせフォームよりお気軽にお問い合わせください。

title: Arkema invests €10 million in its global battery R&D center of excellence in the Lyon region
source: Arkema - High Performance Polymers News / Newsroom / News
query: https://hpp.arkema.com/en/
content_text:
Arkema invests €10 million in its global battery R&D center of excellence in the Lyon region
Download the PDF 
Arkema continues to invest in the battery business value chain and announces a €10 million expansion project for its Global Battery Center of Excellence located in Oullins-Pierre-Bénite, in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region of France.
This investment reflects the Group’s strategy of continuously strengthening its research capabilities in advanced materials for batteries within its global network of R&D laboratories covering the entire battery value chain. 
Following the inauguration in Normandy in September 2025 of a laboratory dedicated to solvent-free battery electrode manufacturing , as well as several investments in Asia and the Americas, this expansion further strengthens a particularly dense global R&D network, that combines the expertise developed in France with that of the Group’s research centers in China, South Korea, Japan and the United States. Thanks to this international organization, Arkema is accelerating the development of innovative solutions capable of addressing the technological and industrial challenges of next-generation batteries.
Located at the heart of the Rhône-Alpes Research Center , the Battery Center of Excellence is entering a new phase of its development. Its footprint will be tripled, and its research infrastructure will be modernized, including notably a significant increase in the digitalization of R&D activities. This expansion will consolidate the role of this French center as Arkema’s global reference platform for the development of advanced materials serving both current batteries and the next generations under development.
The project will enable the Group’s R&D teams to prepare for the future industrial standards of cell manufacturers and accelerate the integration of Arkema’s advanced materials into their production processes. By replicating their customers’ manufacturing conditions, researchers will be able to better anticipate implementation constraints and contribute to the development of more efficient batteries delivering greater energy density, faster charging times and enhanced safety.
This investment marks a major milestone in Arkema’s ambition to support the rapid evolution of the battery market. By strengthening our Battery Center of Excellence in France, we are equipping our global network and teams with state-of-the-art tools that will enable them to develop, in close collaboration with our customers, the materials that will contribute to the performance of tomorrow’s batteries.”
Armand Ajdari, Arkema’s Chief technology Officer
The implementation of this project has been made possible in particular through the support provided by the French Research Tax Credit ( Crédit d’Impôt Recherche ) and by the French State as part of the France 2030 program.

title: maxon acquires strategic minority stake in Synapticon
query: https://www.maxongroup.com/en/news-and-events/news
content_text:
maxon acquires strategic minority stake in Synapticon
Download 
Contact us 
Share current page 
The Swiss maxon Group is expanding its expertise in the field of motion control through a strategic partnership with the German company Synapticon. The goal of the collaboration is the joint development of high-performance drive solutions with integrated functional safety, based on optimally combined components from both companies. 
As part of this partnership, the maxon Group has acquired a minority stake in Synapticon. The company, based in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, is a leading provider of intelligent motion control solutions with integrated, certified safety functions. Together, the partners are building a comprehensive portfolio of mechatronic drive systems, which already includes market-ready solutions.
Synapticon follows a "software-first" approach and develops pioneering software and hardware for drive control in robotics and mechanical engineering. The company offers one of the world’s leading portfolios of highly compact, powerful, and intelligent motion control technologies. Its products are used in robotic arms, autonomous transport systems, and complex industrial machinery, among others.
Customers are already benefiting from intelligent, highly integrated solutions based on technologies from maxon and Synapticon. The close collaboration enables efficient further development of existing products and targeted alignment with new applications.
Considering increasing functional safety requirements in many high-tech industries, this investment represents an important strategic step for maxon. The partnership strengthens maxon's position as a provider of future-proof drive systems in dynamically growing markets such as robotics, medical technology, intralogistics, and industrial automation.
Nikolai Ensslen, CEO of Synapticon, states: “This partnership with maxon is of great strategic importance for Synapticon. Together, we will push the boundaries of motion control even further. The market opportunities arising from this collaboration are tremendous.”
Dr. Stefan Müller, CTO of the maxon Group, adds: “Our collaboration with Synapticon opens new possibilities for expanding our expertise in highly integrated drive systems. It enables us to offer even more powerful and safer solutions to our customers.”
The companies have agreed not to disclose the financial terms of the investment.
Contact information 
If you have any questions, please contact the maxon Newsroom:
For inquiries by phone, please call +41 41 662 43 81, or send an e-mail to media@maxongroup.com.
Pictorial material 
Current images can be found by clicking on the download button of this media release.
About maxon: The Swiss specialist for quality drives 
maxon is a leading provider of high-precision electric motors and drive systems, developing solutions tailored to the needs of customers in medical technology, industrial automation, aerospace, mobility, and robotics. Founded in 1961, the Swiss company is family-owned by the Braun family and headquartered in Sachseln, in the canton of Obwalden. maxon Group employs around 3,000 people worldwide across ten production sites and is represented in more than 40 countries.
About Synapticon 
Synapticon is a leading full-stack provider of intelligent drive and safety technologies for robotics and mechanical engineering. Headquartered in Schönaich near Stuttgart and with locations in Silicon Valley and Shenzhen, the company develops and produces highly integrated solutions for motion control and functional safety. The product portfolio includes the award-winning and safety-certified SOMANET Circulo and Integro servo drive families, power-dense actuators for robotics and mechanical engineering from the ACTILINK series, the OBLAC and MOTORCORTEX software solutions and the POSITRON Safety AI platform for the most demanding applications in the field of functional safety. With its software-first approach, deeply integrated electronics and innovative control technology, Synapticon reduces engineering complexity while increasing performance, precision and efficiency. Leading developers of industrial, collaborative, mobile and humanoid robots and complex machines worldwide rely on Synapticon as a trusted partner for the realisation of their most ambitious products.

title: maxon at the SPS 2025: New drive solutions for robotics, automation and mobility
query: https://www.maxongroup.com/en/news-and-events/news
content_text:
maxon at the SPS 2025: New drive solutions for robotics, automation and mobility
Download 
Contact us 
Share current page 
At the SPS trade fair from November 25 to 27, 2025, maxon will present a wide range of new products. From highly integrated robotic actuators to powerful servo drives and controllers: a diverse technology portfolio awaits visitors at the maxon booth in Hall 3, Stand 468.
One focus at the maxon booth will be the further developed robotics solutions, in particular the High Efficiency Joints (HEJ). These compact, highly integrated quasi-direct drive (QDD) actuators combine motor, gearhead, sensors, and electronics in a single, robust housing. Following the successful launch of the HEJ 90 (140 Nm), the HEJ 70 with 62 Nm torque now follows - ideal for smaller robots. The HEJ 50 variant is also currently in production and will be available from early 2026. The powerful HEJ "Hercules" with over 250 Nm is under development.
With this scalable platform, maxon consistently pursues the goal of shortening development times and reducing the overall costs for modern robotics.
Additions to the maxon portfolio
At SPS, maxon will present several additions to its product portfolio: 
IDX 70 - Compact high-performance servo drive with safety certification 
The new IDX 70 combines high power density with a compact footprint, making it ideal for mobile robotics, cobots, and driverless transport systems (AGVs). The IDX 70 offers an excellent torque-to-weight ratio and is suitable for demanding industrial environments thanks to its robust design. The certified Safe Torque Off function (STO) and Safe Brake Control (SBC) ensure compliance with the highest safety standards.
EC frameless DT 50 - Flexible, dynamic, efficient 
The new EC frameless DT 50 is a brushless motor without a flange and now also available with integrated Hall sensors. The design allows for optimal installation versatility, whether in articulated joints, machine tools, or exoskeletons. With high torque density and outstanding efficiency, it enables precise, dynamic motion with minimal heat generation. Additional sizes — 38 mm, 65 mm, and 85 mm — will be available next year.
Strain wave gearheads - precision in the smallest space 
With the new Strain wave gearheads, maxon expands its portfolio, especially for applications with high demands on precision in torque transmission. The backlash-free design ensures exact motion control in minimal installation space – ideal for robotic arms, surgical instruments, or optical applications. In combination with maxon drives, this results in a perfectly matched drive system from a single source - currently available in diameters of 55mm and 62mm. Additional sizes and variants are planned and will be presented at SPS. 
EPOS4 Module/Compact 60/20 STO - Compact controllers with integrated safety 
The new positioning controllers, with certified STO function up to SIL 3 / PL e category 3, combine advanced control performance and safety in a compact form. They enable precise motion control in modular machines, collaborative robots, or autonomous vehicles. Thanks to versatile interfaces, they can be seamlessly integrated into existing automation systems.
MiniMACS6 AMP 4IF1 Profinet - multi-axis controller for networked systems 
The MiniMACS6 AMP 4-IF1 Profinet adds a Profinet communication interface to the successful MACS family. This positions the controller as a key link between motion control and industrial networking. In production environments and robotic systems, it ensures precise real-time coordination of multiple axes and processes.
BIKEDRIVE AIR S e-bike drive: efficiency meets driving experience 
In addition to industrial applications, maxon will also be showcasing its latest innovation in the field of lightweight electromobility: the BIKEDRIVE AIR S –the lightest full-power e-bike drive in its class. With a drive weight of just 2 kg, 90 Nm torque, and whisper-quiet operation, the system sets new standards for a sporty yet natural riding experience.

Meet us in Hall 3, Stand 468, and talk to our experts about the latest drive solutions.

title: maxon at Hannover Messe 2026: Robotics drives, latest portfolio additions, and functional safety
query: https://www.maxongroup.com/en/news-and-events/news
content_text:
maxon at Hannover Messe 2026: Robotics drives, latest portfolio additions, and functional safety
Download 
Contact us 
Share current page 
At Hannover Messe 2026, maxon will present itself with an updated trade fair appearance. From April 20 to 24, the maxon Germany team will showcase the latest highlights from our product portfolio.
At Hannover Messe, maxon traditionally introduces its latest portfolio additions. Here is what visitors can expect at our booth:
Robotics solutions: maxon’s High Efficiency Joints (HEJ) bring motion to robotics. They enable humanoid robots to operate in unstructured environments and are also suitable for industrial applications. At Hannover Messe, we will present the proven High Efficiency Joint 90, as well as the new, smaller HEJ 70.
Drives: In our highlight showcases, we present a wide range of maxon drives combined with gearheads and sensors. Among them is the EC frameless DT 50 M: easy to integrate into customer applications thanks to its separate stator and rotor design, offering high efficiency and dynamic torque. Another example is the ECX PRIME 16L - the long version of our brushless motor with ironless winding. These are just two of many new additions.
EC frameless DT50M 
1 / 6 
Gearheads: Since launching our new GSW strain wave gear series, we have continuously developed it further. Our gearheads transmit high torques precisely and efficiently and can be combined with a wide range of maxon drives. In Hannover, we will, for example, present the GSW 20 in combination with an ECX PRIME drive.
Industrial drives: Our IDX series meets industrial standards and is a proven plug-and-play solution - for industrial applications or autonomous vehicles in intralogistics. At Hannover Messe, we will present the IDX 70 Safe Control, featuring integrated functional safety up to SIL3 / PL e, Cat. 3.
Precision, performance and integrated safety
Electronics: Functional safety is also becoming increasingly important in this field, which is why maxon continues to develop its control solutions accordingly. One example is the EPOS4 Compact 60/20 STO (Safe Torque Off). Visitors can also see the smallest controllers in the maxon portfolio: ESCON2 Nano 24/2 and ESCON2 Micro 60/5. We will also present the MiniMACS6, our freely programmable multi-axis controller, now also available with a PROFINET interface. In addition, we will demonstrate our predictive maintenance solution, maxon MIND, and explain why the motor is the best sensor in a customer application.
Parvalux: The UK-based company Parvalux, part of maxon, specializes in small and medium-sized geared motors. Parvalux solutions drive windshield wipers in high-speed trains or move patients in hospitals. At Hannover Messe, we will show how maxon and Parvalux products can be ideally combined, for example, the maxon IDX industrial drive with the Parvalux GB 28 right-angle gearbox.
At our booth, we will also present various live demos showcasing our drive solutions in action. The maxon Germany team will be available for any questions.
You can find us at Hannover Messe in Hall 13, Booth C51. 
For further information, please contact the maxon Newsroom . 
Learn more about our solutions .

query: https://www.maxongroup.com/en/news-and-events/news
content_text:
The completely revised maxon catalog 2026/2027 has been released

The completely revised maxon catalog 2026/2027 has been released 
maxon has fundamentally revised its catalog. The new structure is designed to make access to products and applications easier while providing a clearer overview of the company, its markets, and its technological capabilities. 
The maxon Catalog 2026/2027 has been completely reconceived. As part of a targeted portfolio streamlining, redundancies were minimized and complexity reduced. The revised structure of the product categories now features clearly organized introductory pages that enable a quick entry into each portfolio segment. This is complemented by a new “Welcome” section that positions maxon as a company and clearly communicates at a glance what maxon stands for.
A particular focus has been placed on the Market Solutions, which now have their own dedicated section. Each maxon business unit (Medical, Aerospace, Industrial Automation, and Mobility) is presented on a double-page spread, with the respective expertise in the relevant submarkets clearly highlighted.
In addition, the areas of Robotics, Space, and Electronics are presented separately within the Market Solutions. This demonstrates maxon’s broad market competence and enables targeted browsing while maintaining a clear overview of the core markets. The section “Technology – short and to the point” has also been completely revised.
The stars of the new catalog, of course, remain the products. The portfolio has been expanded with several highlights, including the brushless ECX PRIME 4-pole motors for high speeds and torque, the powerful ECX FLAT flat motors with fan, new diameters of the EC frameless high‑torque motors, and the backlash-free GSW planetary gearheads. The new products are complemented by the versatile ESCON2 servo controllers and the EPOS4 positioning controllers.
The new catalog is available as an e-paper .

Homepage > So, what is mRNA" id="mrna" class="Wrapper-sc-s3066g-0 indexstyles__CarouselWrapper-sc-15tnf59-0 fXtPHr hEyxpP"> mRNA란 무엇인가요?
메신저 RNA(mRNA)는 이미 여러분의 몸 안에 존재합니다. mRNA는 세포가 무엇을 해야 하는지 지시하는 "메시지"를 전달합니다. 
질환에 다른 방식으로 대항하기 무한한 치료 더 많은 사람들 돕기 더 많은 의약품을, 더 빠르게 
질환에 다른 방식으로 대항하기 
mRNA 의약품은 면역체계를 촉진시켜 질환을 치료하거나 예방하는 도구들을 생성함으로써 전통적인 의약품과는 다른 방식으로 질환과 맞서 싸웁니다. 
알아보기
무한한 치료
mRNA가 하나의 질환을 치료할 수 있다면, 수많은 질환을 치료할 수 있다고 우리는 믿습니다. 우리는 현재 치료법이 없는 질환을 치료하기 위해 mRNA를 활용할 것입니다. 
알아보기
더 많은 사람들 돕기
mRNA 의약품에는 동물성 식품이나 보존제가 들어가지 않아, 가능한 많은 사람들이 생명을 구하는 의약품에 접근할 수 있습니다. 
알아보기
더 많은 의약품을, 더 빠르게
우리의 플랫폼은 수일 내로 여러 mRNA의 설계, 연구, 테스트를 가능하게 합니다. 우리의 새로운 생산법은 더 많은 사람들을 위한 의약품을 더 빠르게 얻을 수 있게 합니다.

Homepage > So, what is mRNA" id="quest-ce-que-larnm" class="Wrapper-sc-s3066g-0 indexstyles__CarouselWrapper-sc-15tnf59-0 fXtPHr hEyxpP"> Qu'est ce que l'ARNm ?
L'ARN messager (ARNm) est déjà présent dans votre organisme. Il est porteur d'un “message” - des instructions qui indiquent à vos cellules ce qu'elles ont à faire. 
Une nouvelle manière de lutter contre les maladies De nombreuses possibilités de traitements Aider un plus grand nombre de personnes Davantage de médicaments, plus rapidement 
Une nouvelle manière de lutter contre les maladies
Les médicaments à ARNm luttent contre les maladies d'une manière différente par rapport aux médicaments traditionnels : ils stimulent votre système immunitaire pour lui faire fabriquer des outils servant à traiter ou à prévenir une maladie. 
EN SAVOIR PLUS SUR L’ARNm
De nombreuses possibilités de traitements
Nous sommes convaincus que si l'ARNm peut permettre de traiter une maladie, il est capable d'en traiter de nombreuses autres. Nous utiliserons l'ARNm pour traiter des maladies dont le besoin médical est important. 
EN SAVOIR PLUS SUR L’ARNm
Aider un plus grand nombre de personnes
Les médicaments à base d'ARNm ne contiennent ni de produits d'origine animale, ni de conservateurs, rendant ces traitements accessibles à un très grand nombre de patients. 
EN SAVOIR PLUS SUR L’ARNm
Davantage de médicaments, plus rapidement
Notre plateforme permet d'effectuer très rapidement, en quelques jours, les étapes de conception, de recherche et de test de nombreux médicaments. Nos techniques de production innovantes nous permettent de donner accès à nos traitements à un plus grand nombre de personnes, plus rapidement. 
EN SAVOIR PLUS SUR L’ARNm

Homepage > So, what is mRNA" id="was-ist-mrna" class="Wrapper-sc-s3066g-0 indexstyles__CarouselWrapper-sc-15tnf59-0 fXtPHr hEyxpP"> Was ist mRNA?
mRNA ist bereits natürlich in ihrem Köper vorhanden . Sie trägt eine “Botschaft“, die die Zellen anleitet, Proteine herzustellen. 
Neue Ansätze in der Infektionsprävention Innovative Behandlungsoptionen Hilfe für mehr Menschen Mehr Arzneimittel schneller entwickeln 
Neue Ansätze in der Infektionsprävention
mRNA-Arzneimittel bekämpfen Krankheiten auf eine andere Weise als herkömmliche Arzneimittel, indem sie Ihr Immunsystem dazu anregen, selbst Werkzeuge zur Behandlung oder Vorbeugung von Krankheiten auszubilden. 
MEHR ÜBER MRNA
Innovative Behandlungsoptionen
mRNA kann zahlreiche Krankheiten behandeln. Wir planen mRNA zur Behandlung von Krankheiten einzusetzen , für die es derzeit keine Behandlung gibt. 
MEHR ÜBER MRNA
Hilfe für mehr Menschen
Da mRNA-Arzneimittel keine tierischen Produkte oder Konservierungsstoffe enthalten, sind lebensrettende Medikamente für möglichst viele Menschen zugänglich. 
MEHR ÜBER MRNA
Mehr Arzneimittel schneller entwickeln
Unsere Plattform ermöglicht die schnelle Entwicklung, Erforschung und Prüfung mehrerer mRNA Produkte innerhalb weniger Wochen. Unsere neuartigen Produktionsmethoden ermöglichen es uns, mehr Menschen schneller mit Medikamenten zu versorgen. 
MEHR ÜBER MRNA

query: https://www.heidenhain.com/news
content_text:
RCN 2001 and RCN 5001 series 
Absolute angle encoders for high productivity
System accuracy of ±2” / ±4”
Integrated stator coupling
Hollow through shaft with ∅ 20 mm / ∅ 35 mm
Position values per revolution: 26 bits / 28 bits
High permissible shaft speeds
Integrated temperature sensor
Interfaces: EnDat 2.2 , Fanuc Serial Interface αi, Mitsubishi high speed interface
Available with functional safety
Sustainability with TRUE IMAGE TECHNOLOGY
Product query
Service query
High permissible shaft speeds 
With a purely serial interface, the RCN 2001 and RCN 5001 series encoders permit shaft speeds of up to 3000 rpm, enabling applications that are both highly dynamic and highly accurate.
Easy temperature measurement 
Evaluation of the temperature in direct drive motor windings can be performed in combination with the  EIB 5200  sensor box from HEIDENHAIN. The temperature data and position data are transmitted to the control via the purely digital interface.
High accuracy 
The RCN 2001 and RCN 5001 series angle encoders feature a high line count of 16,384 lines and excellent signal quality. Low motor current noise and smooth operating behavior are the benefits, especially in rotary axes powered by direct drive motors.
Reliable scanning 
Thanks to optimized scanning, even liquid contamination and condensation have very little effect on the scanning signals or motor control. Disturbances in the machining process caused by encoder contamination are thereby largely avoided.

title: ERM 2000 series
query: https://www.heidenhain.com/news
content_text:
ERM 2000 series 
Incremental angle encoders with magnetic scanning
Easy mounting with only little adjustment work
Continuous operation at high shaft speeds
Rugged and tolerant to contamination
Graduation accuracy: ±2.5” to ±72”
Signal periods: 1024 to 7200
Diameters: 64 mm to 452 mm
Interfaces: 1 V PP , TTL, EnDat 2.2 
Product query
Service query
Compact and versatile 
The ERM 2000 series angle encoders feature various drum sizes and geometries. Large inside diameters of up to 512 mm facilitate cable routing through the encoder. Their compact design permits installation in tight spaces.
High permissible shaft speeds 
The modular bearingless design of these encoders permits high shaft speeds in continuous operation and reversing duty, even when installed with mechanical fault exclusion. These high shaft speeds do not increase the acoustic operating noise of the encoder.
Sturdy and tolerant to contamination 
The MAGNODUR measuring standard is particularly tolerant to contamination. The resulting consistent signal quality makes these encoders suitable for harsh shopfloor conditions.
The extremely accurate ERM 2203 
Even with their high permissible shaft speeds, the ERM 2203 angle encoders feature high accuracy and robust scanning.

title: How a strand of glass makes global communication possible  Speak into your phone abroad and hear an instant translation. Behind that moment lies a global network of optical fibers carrying data at the speed of light. New technologies such as Hollow Core and Multicore fibers are now pushing the limits of what these networks can do.
source: Heraeus - News and Stories / Newsroom / News
query: https://www.heraeus.com/en/news-and-stories/
content_text:
Optical Fibers: The Invisible Infrastructure Behind the Daily Digital Life
You speak into your phone in a foreign country. A second later, it answers in another language. What feels instant is anything but simple. Behind that moment of convenience, data travels as light through optical fibers across global networks.  With more than a century of expertise in high-purity quartz glass, we at Heraeus contribute to the material technologies that make advanced optical fiber—and thus modern digital life—possible.  
AI generated 
Only a decade ago, understanding a foreign language without studying it seemed unrealistic. Today, it fits in your pocket. Everyday moments like this make it easy to overlook the complexity behind them, and the vast, invisible infrastructure quietly supporting modern life.
It goes like this: In madrid, for example, a tourist from Japan speaks into a smartphone. The audio is sent to a nearby telecom hub, then routed across Europe to a cloud data center in (e.g.) Ireland, where it is processed by powerful AI-driven language models before being returned as translated speech.
For users, it all happens in a fraction of a second. For data though, it travels thousands of kilometers before the translation appears on the screen. This is where optical fiber plays a quiet but essential role.
Comparable in size to a human hair, optical fibers are strands of glass that carry information as pulses of light between telecom hubs, internet exchange points, and data centers. Without this infrastructure, many of the digital services we rely on every day would simply not function.
Did you know?
Internet travels as light in glass fibers. 
Inside an optical fiber, digital information is encoded into tiny flashes of laser light. The glass structure guides this light with remarkable efficiency, allowing it to travel long distances with minimal loss. Signals move through fiber at roughly two-thirds the speed of light in a vacuum — around 200,000 kilometers per second. To put that into perspective: at this speed, a signal travels around earth 5 times in a second. 
Telecommunication and data communication: what's the difference? 
Not all optical fibers serve the same purpose, and the distinction becomes increasingly important as data volumes continue to grow.
One major application is telecommunication . Optical fiber forms the global backbone of modern communications , connecting cities, countries, and continents through terrestrial and submarine networks before ultimately reaching the devices we use every day. When someone in Paris calls a colleague in Singapore, the signal travels through thousands of kilometers of optical fiber.
AI generated 
Another major application is data communication (datacom) . Here, optical fiber is typically used over much shorter distances, primarily within and around data centers. The focus is on moving enormous volumes of data as quickly as possible . Optical fiber connects servers that continuously exchange information and, in some cases, links multiple data centers so they can operate together as if they were one giant computer. This is what enables cloud computing, AI workloads, and high-resolution video streaming with almost no noticeable delay. 
AI generated 
The translation you triggered on your phone relies on both: long-distance telecom networks to move data around, and high-speed datacom connections to process it inside servers. Together, they form the layered infrastructure that powers the digital world.
However, while telecom networks span vast distances, the real explosion in data traffic is happening inside data centers. Artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and streaming services generate enormous amounts of data that must be processed and moved within confined spaces. As a result, datacom places particularly high demands on fiber performance — in terms of speed, capacity, and density.
 
Did you know?
Size doesn't determine capacity. 
One hair-thin optical fiber can carry an astonishing amount of information. If every resident of London pressed "Play" on the same Netflix movie at exactly the same moment, a single optical fiber could carry all that data.
This is why advanced fiber technologies are becoming especially critical for datacom applications. 
The material behind the network 
Whether data travels across continents or within a single data center, the performance of optical fiber ultimately depends on one critical factor: the material it is made from.
At the heart of optical fiber lies a remarkably pure material: high-purity quartz glass. 
For optical fiber, purity determines how far light can travel before it needs a boost. The purer the glass, the farther a light signal can travel without losing strength. In a standard telecom fiber, that distance is around 50 kilometers. By comparison, even in the clearest ocean water, you can usually only see about 20 meters before light fades from view.
Producing such ultra-pure material requires precise manufacturing and deep expertise in materials science.
The process begins with a cylinder-shaped preform — a scaled-up version of the fiber’s internal structure. This preform is then heated and drawn into an optical fiber just 125 micrometers thick, about the thickness of a human hair. From a single preform with an outer diameter of 200 mm and a length of 3 meters, more than 7,000 kilometers of single-mode fiber can be produced.
 
Credit: Martin Böttcher/Heraeus 
Basis for next generations
As new demands emerge — from AI-driven data processing to ever-growing global connectivity — the requirements for fiber performance continue to increase. Advanced concepts such as Hollow Core and Multicore fibers build on this material foundation, pushing the limits of what optical fibers can achieve.
We have worked with quartz glass for more than a century, developing materials used in industries ranging from semiconductors to aerospace. From the late 1960s, Heraeus played a key role in early optical fiber development, going on to supply quartz glass for Germany’s first test line in 1978. In 1991, we started to expand our market position and production capacity – helping build the digital infrastructure we rely on today. By now, almost 2 billion kilometers of optical fiber deployed world-wide are made from Heraeus quartz glass.
Today, we continue to build on this expertise, supporting the development of next-generation optical fiber technologies for increasingly data-intensive applications.
 
A new generation of optical fibers
As artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and video streaming expand, demand for data transmission continues to grow — especially inside data centers, where enormous volumes of information move constantly between servers. Thanks to optical fiber, several data centers can also work together as though they were one giant facility.
Global internet traffic has increased more than tenfold over the past decade, and data center workloads continue to grow rapidly. To keep thousands of servers working together, the internal network of a state-of-the-art data center can provide up to 13 petabits of bandwidth per second — the theoretical equivalent of moving around 140 exabytes of data per day, enough to transfer more than 9 billion full-length 4K movies. Looking ahead, technologies such as autonomous driving, industrial robotics, and immersive digital environments will require even faster and more reliable data exchange.
These environments require fibers that can carry more data, reduce delay, and fit into limited physical space. 
One emerging technology is Hollow Core fiber.
In conventional fibers, light travels through solid glass. Hollow Core fibers guide light through tiny air-filled channels. 
 
Hollow Core fibers enable faster signal transmission, therefore lower latency – approaching the fundamental physical limit – because light travels through air rather than glass. This allows signals to travel at close to 300,000 kilometers per second—roughly seven and a half times around the earth in one second. In practical terms, this means data centers can be connected more quickly and efficiently, even over long distance. As a result, companies gain greater flexibility in choosing where to build new facilities, i.e. in locations with more space or lower energy costs, without sacrificing performance.
Dr. Ansgar Meissner
Product Manager Hollow Core Fiber
Heraeus Covantics
Hollow Core fibers also offer additional advantages in bandwidth and lower signal attenuation, meaning they can transmit data with less loss and support higher capacity. This enables geographically distributed data centers to operate as one, giving companies greater freedom in where they build new facilities. 
At the same time, manufacturing hollow-core fibers is highly complex. Precisely structuring microscopic air channels over long distances while maintaining mechanical stability and optical performance requires advanced materials expertise and extremely controlled production processes.
 
Multicore Fiber – More Capacity in the same space
Another emerging concept is Multicore fiber. 
Traditional fibers contain a single light pathway. Multicore fibers integrate several independent light-guiding cores within the same strand of glass.
Multicore fibers increase transmission capacity by enabling multiple parallel data streams within a single fiber — essentially multiplying the amount of information that can be carried without increasing the physical footprint. This is particularly valuable in data centers, where space and scalability are critical constraints. However, manufacturing Multicore fibers is equally challenging.
 
Each core must be precisely positioned and isolated to prevent signal interference, while maintaining uniform performance across all channels. Achieving this level of precision at scale requires advanced preform design, tight process control, and deep expertise in optical materials.
Martin Böttcher
Global Head of Multicore Fiber Business
Heraeus Covantics
The next chapter of global connectivity
As digitalization continues to accelerate, the demands on optical fiber infrastructure are growing. Applications are becoming more data-intensive, data centers are more powerful, and networks are more complex. At the same time, the materials that underpin this infrastructure must meet ever-higher performance requirements. 
Fiber technology may appear simple — just light traveling through glass. But turning that basic physics into reliable infrastructure for the modern digital economy requires innovation, entrepreneurial thinking, and deep expertise. At Heraeus Covantics, teams are working closely with our partners to translate advanced fiber concepts into practical technologies that support the next generation of digital communication.
Jan Vydra
Executive Vice President Fiber Optics
Heraeus Covantics
And as new technologies emerge, this invisible infrastructure will become even more critical. Future applications such as fully autonomous mobility, real-time digital twins of entire cities, or seamless human-machine interaction may depend on data speeds and capacities that today’s networks are only beginning to approach.
Without continued advances in optical fiber, many of these possibilities would remain out of reach. Just as today’s digital services rely on fiber to function, tomorrow’s innovations will depend on pushing its limits even further.

title: Leica Geosystems launches Leica CS50 field controller and Leica Captivate 2027 for faster, more reliable fieldwork
source: Hexagon AB - Leica Geosystems News / Newsroom / News

content_text:
Leica Geosystems launches Leica CS50 field controller and Leica Captivate 2027 for faster, more reliable fieldwork 
HEERBRUGG, Switzerland, 27 October 2026 – Leica Geosystems,
part of Hexagon, today introduced the Leica CS50 field controller and
Leica Captivate 2027 field software, designed to help surveyors work
more efficiently, maintain reliable positioning in challenging
environments, and set out points with greater confidence. 
The CS50 keeps up with the demanding timelines of fieldwork, even
when handling large survey datasets. Captivate 2027 adds AI-RTK for
faster and more reliable GNSS positioning around obstructions,
camera-based GNSS visual stakeout, and shared projects for efficient
collaboration.
Surveying crews increasingly need to work with large CAD and IFC
files on site, measure close to buildings and vegetation that can
disrupt GNSS signals, and access the right project data quickly. The
latest Captivate releases address surveyors’ evolving work realities
with advances across instruments and software that deliver overall
productivity gains:
Work efficiently with complex datasets: The CS50
combines fast processing and a multi-touch display with a tactile,
backlit keypad. Its rugged design supports familiar one-handed
operation, while fast, responsive performance helps surveyors work
efficiently with large datasets in the field.
AI-RTK for reliable GNSS measurements in challenging
environments: This new Leica GS18 feature uses artificial
intelligence to distinguish reliable GNSS signals from those disrupted
by the environment to help maintain accurate positioning.
Find stakeout points faster: Visual stakeout
overlays stakeout points onto the live camera view of the Leica GS18 I,
showing surveyors which way to go and helping them reach points easily
and quickly.
Keep field and office teams working with the right
project information: Collaborative projects provide a common
structure for project information, files, and settings across Captivate,
Leica Infinity, and Hexagon GeoCloud, making it easier to find and work
with the right project data across field and office workflows.
“The way surveyors work is evolving, with more data, greater
connectivity, faster instruments, and new capabilities such as AI
becoming part of everyday workflows,” says Hans-Martin Zogg, Head of
Business Line Surveying at Hexagon’s Geomatics Division. “Our focus is
on turning new possibilities into practical benefits in the field, while
building on the workflows, skills and experience surveyors already
have.”
The CS50 and Captivate 2027 reflect that approach. The CS50 works
with Captivate GNSS smart antennas and total stations, including the new
Leica TS20, giving crews one controller and a familiar Captivate
interface across GNSS and total station workflows, while the new
capabilities in Captivate 2027 fit into the way surveyors already
work.
For more information about the CS50, visit https://leica-geosystems.com/products/total-stations/controllers/leica-cs50 
To learn more about Captivate 2027, visit https://leica-geosystems.com/products/total-stations/software/leica-captivate/new-features 
Explore the new workflows in the on-demand webinar: How to be ready for your next big surveying opportunity 
For further information, please contact: 
Christine Grahl
Director, Content Marketing, at Hexagon's Geomatics Division
Email: christine.grahl@hexagon.com 
Phone: +1 248 339 6889

Delivering value every day to professionals in surveying, construction, infrastructure, mining, mapping and other geospatial content-dependent industries, Leica Geosystems leads the industry with innovative solutions to empower our autonomous future.

A change is taking place at the operational helm of the maxon Group: After 35 years with the company, including 15 years as CEO, Eugen Elmiger is handing over the position to Andreas Richter. Mr. Elmiger will remain with the company as Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors. 
After 35 years at maxon, including 15 years as CEO, Eugen Elmiger will hand over the operational leadership of the maxon Group in March 2027 to the current Chief Operating Officer (COO) and Deputy CEO, Andreas Richter . Mr. Elmiger will remain with the company as Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors with a focus on strategic responsibilities.
Mr. Elmiger joined the maxon Group in 1991 and was appointed CEO in 2011. When he started in 1991, the maxon group, formerly known as Interelectric ag, generated sales of approximately CHF 50 million and employed 408 people. Today, the maxon Group has more than 3,000 employees worldwide, and annual sales for 2025 amounted to nearly CHF 600 million.
Mr. Elmiger has played a decisive role in shaping the development of the maxon Group over several decades. Under his leadership, the company further strengthened its international market position, expanded into new business areas, and continuously increased its capacity for innovation.
Mr. Elmiger: “This is the right time to hand over responsibility to the next generation. I look forward to continuing to help shape maxon’s future as Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors.”
Andreas Richter: With the maxon Group since 2020 
The Board of Directors has appointed Andreas Richter as the new CEO of the maxon Group. He joined the company in 2020 and has served as Chief Operating Officer ever since. In this role, Mr. Richter was responsible for all production sites of the maxon Group.
The succession plan is part of a long-term and carefully prepared transition process. Until the change takes effect in March 2027, Mr. Elmiger will continue to fully perform his role as CEO and will actively support the transition to a new leadership team.
Next stage of the generational change 
The CEO transition continues the most recent generational change within the maxon Group. It began in June 2026, when the Group announced that principal shareholder Dr. Karl-Walter Braun would hand over the chairmanship of the Board of Directors to his daughter, Dr. Bianca Braun.
Bianca Braun is pleased that the Group will continue to rely on proven leadership in its operational management in the future: “With Andreas Richter, we are gaining a CEO who knows maxon exceptionally well and will consistently drive the future development of our company. He has many years of leadership experience within the maxon Group and believes strongly in the group’s focus on continuity, innovation, and sustainable growth.”
Additional leadership changes within the group 
The CEO transition is part of a forward-looking evolution of maxon’s leadership organization. As part of this succession plan, additional changes are being made to the company’s leadership teams:
Stefan Müller, Chief Technology Officer (CTO) at maxon, will also be appointed Deputy CEO.
Daniel von Wyl , currently Managing Director of the Sachseln production site (maxon motor ag), will become Chief Operating Officer (COO), assuming responsibility for maxon’s global production sites and succeeding Andreas Richter in this role.
Dominik Stockmann , currently Head of Development at the Sachseln site, will become Managing Director of the site, succeeding Daniel von Wyl in this position.
With these succession arrangements, the maxon Group is creating the conditions for continuity, stability, and the company’s continued successful development.
Additional Information 
The maxon Newsroom is available for inquiries.
For telephone inquiries, please call +41 41 662 43 81, or email media@maxongroup.com .

title: New Chair of the Board of Directors and stable fiscal year at maxon
query: https://www.maxongroup.com/en/news-and-events/news
content_text:
New Chair of the Board of Directors and stable fiscal year at maxon
Download 
Contact us 
Share current page 
The Braun family that owns the maxon Group is undergoing a generational change. Dr. Karl-Walter Braun will remain on the Board of Directors, but will relinquish the chairmanship. His daughter Dr. Bianca Braun is now taking over. 
Those who work at maxon often remain loyal to the company for many years. The average length of service in the Swiss maxon companies is just over nine years. The main shareholder of the maxon Group, Dr. Karl-Walter Braun, also contributes to this cut: He officially joined the company in 1977 and will be able to celebrate his 49th year of service in 2026; last year he also celebrated his 80th birthday.
Now the time has come for him to drive forward the generational change in the company. As of June 2026, he will hand over the chairmanship of the Board of Directors to his daughter Dr. Bianca Braun, but will remain a member of the Board of Directors. Dr. Karl-Walter Braun: "A successful generational change cannot be taken for granted. I am very pleased that Bianca is now moving up. She has the right skill set to do so and has known the company from different perspectives for many years."
Bianca Braun helped out in maxon's production departments before and during her studies. She has been a member of the Board of Directors since 2007, and from 2012 she took on operational responsibility as Head of Group Audit and Consulting. 
Bianca Braun, born in 1978, spent her school years in Obwalden and Zug. She studied Technology Management at the University of St. Gallen and wrote her doctorate on family-run companies. Dr. Bianca Braun: "Family-run companies are a model for success, and maxon is the best example of this – because we think long-term. That was also the motto of my father, who prudently developed the company and, together with the management, led it to its current size. I want to continue on this course and at the same time set new accents."
There is another change on the Board of Directors of the maxon Group: Kurt Kwapil is stepping down from the board after 14 years. The Board of Directors thanks him for his commitment and wishes him all the best.
maxon Group keeps sales stable in 2025 
Financially, the maxon Group can look back on a stable fiscal year. Annual sales amounted to CHF 595.2 million, which corresponds to a small increase of 0.1 percent compared to the previous year (previous year: CHF 594.7 million). Operating cash flow amounted to CHF 75.5 million in the past financial year (previous year: CHF 73.9 million).
The result was influenced by the strong Swiss franc. Currency-related sales losses amounted to CHF 20.2 million in 2025. Over the last three years, currency losses totalled CHF 68.2 million. The maxon Group expects the upward pressure on the Swiss franc to continue.
Employees had to be flexible 
Geopolitical circumstances also shaped the annual result. Last year, for example, maxon was concerned about the availability of rare earth magnets from China. Since China had temporarily ordered export controls on these magnets, the supply situation was very different, which led to fluctuating production utilization. In the meantime, the situation has eased again. In addition, maxon was also temporarily affected by the US tariffs. Thanks to the high proportion of customers from the medical sector, which is exempt from the customs regime, maxon was less affected than other Swiss industrial companies.
By sales area, sales were maintained or improved with a few exceptions. In the Americas, sales remained similar last year at CHF 181.7 million (previous year: CHF 181.8 million), in Europe they fell to CHF 283.8 million (previous year: CHF 294.0 million), and in Asia and Oceania, sales increased to CHF 128.9 million (previous year: CHF 118.4 million).
maxon continues to invest consistently in research and development. Compared to 2024, expenditure increased slightly to CHF 52.4 million (previous year: CHF 47.8 million), which corresponds to 8.8 percent of sales.
In 2025, the maxon Group shipped a total of 4.6 million products (previous year: 4.9 million, -6.2 percent). The number of full-time employees rose slightly to 2985 (previous year: 2947.2, +1.3 percent); a total of 3197 people worked for maxon worldwide at the end of 2025. 
Eugen Elmiger, CEO of the maxon Group, was satisfied with the result achieved. "Of course, we would prefer to grow, but 2025 was a challenging year for us, and that's why we're happy that we were able to maintain sales." The U.S. tariffs and the supply problems with the magnets had demanded a lot from maxon employees. "From management to the production line, flexibility was required because we always had to react quickly to the changing situation," says Elmiger. Once again, it has been shown that maxon employees lend a hand when necessary. "I am extremely grateful for this, because supplying our customers is always our top priority," says Elmiger.
Main shareholder Dr. Karl-Walter Braun is also satisfied. The maxon Group still has virtually no bank debt and a decent liquidity reserve: "However, maxon will continue to plan cautiously and we will have to continue to react flexibly to changing situations."
The maxon Group remains cautiously optimistic for the current year. Orders have risen significantly since the beginning of the year. The higher demand is particularly noticeable in the Aerospace, Mobility, Medical and Robotics business units. With integrated drive units, intelligent motion control solutions and complete mechatronic systems, maxon is increasingly evolving from a component supplier to a system partner. Accordingly, additional production capacities are being built up in several areas.
Learn more 
If you have any questions, please contact the maxon Newsroom. 
For inquiries by phone, please call +41 41 662 43 81, or send an e-mail to media@maxongroup.com.
Images 
Current images can be found by clicking on the download button of this news.
About maxon: The Swiss Specialist for Quality Drives 
maxon is a leading supplier of precision electric motors and drive systems, developing solutions tailored to the needs of customers in the medical, industrial automation, aerospace, mobility, and robotics sectors. Founded in 1961, the Swiss company is owned by the Braun family and is headquartered in Sachseln (canton of Obwalden). The maxon Group employs around 3200 people at eleven production sites worldwide and is represented in over 40 countries.

ELECTRONICA 
Messe München,  GERMANY

Event's official website 
Materials driving the future of electronics
From semiconductors and printed circuit boards to smart devices, batteries and advanced sensors, the electronics industry is facing growing demands for performance, miniaturization and reliability.
At Electronica 2026, Arkema will showcase solutions spanning the entire electronics value chain. Leveraging expertise in high-performance polymers, advanced coating materials, specialty adhesives and electroactive polymers, the Group helps manufacturers develop more efficient, durable and sustainable electronic systems.
High Performance Polymers
From consumer electronics and wearables to batteries, data centers and semiconductor applications, Arkema's portfolio includes leading high-performance polymers such as Rilsan® PA11, Pebax® TPE, Kynar® PVDF and Zenimid™ PI. These solutions help address key challenges related to lightweighting, durability, thermal management and impact resistance
Foranext ® etching gases are used in the manufacturing of semiconductors and microchips. They enable high-precision plasma etching, equipment cleaning, and the miniaturization of electronic components. Leveraging its expertise in process control and supply reliability, Arkema supports manufacturers across the electronics industry.
For AI cooling systems : Oleris ® n-Heptanoic acid, a 100% bio-based building block for next-generation dielectric fluids. Polyol Ester (POE) cooling fluids made with Oleris ® n-Heptanoic acid deliver: low viscosity for efficient heat transfer,  High flash point for improved safety, Excellent stability at low temperatures.
Coating Solutions
Through advanced coating and resin technologies, including Sartomer ®  UV curable resins, Arkema contributes to the protection and performance of displays, printed circuit boards and electronic assemblies. These materials support the ongoing evolution of smaller, more powerful and more reliable electronic devices.
Adhesives
Born2Bond™ adhesives provide high-precision, fast and reliable bonding, sealing, potting and encapsulations solutions for electronic components, including miniature parts. Our portfolio offers a wide range of viscosities, open times, and curing speeds to meet diverse manufacturing requirements. Designed for durability, theses adhesives resist to vibration, impact while maintaining long-term performance. 
Electroactive Polymers
Through its Piezotech ® range, Arkema develops electroactive polymers for sensors, wearables, human-machine interfaces, robotics (tactile sensors for humanoid robot hands) and printed electronics. These innovative materials enable new possibilities for flexible, lightweight and intelligent electronic systems.
Zenimid™ Polyimide Solutions for Advanced Electronics
Our ZENIMID™ range offers polyimide solutions in the form of films and varnishes for electronic applications requiring high performance in terms of insulation, protection, and thermal resistance. These advanced materials open up new possibilities for the design of more reliable, durable, and high-performance electronic components and systems, particularly for demanding environments.
