BorgWarner Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
4 minutos de lectura 
BWA 
This ETF Weeds Out Small-Cap Underperformers 
BorgWarner BWA reported third-quarter sales of just under $3.5 billion, with adjusted operating margin expanding 20 basis points year over year to 10.9% and adjusted earnings per share rising 12%. The automotive supplier said its performance reflected cost-control efforts amid declining vehicle production and a sales headwind from its Battery Energy Systems business. 
Light-vehicle eProduct sales increased 33% from a year earlier to $630 million, driven primarily by European demand. President and CEO Joe Fadool said the growth demonstrated that previously awarded electrification business was beginning to contribute to results, particularly as hybrid and electric-vehicle penetration rises in Europe. 
3 Must-Buy Stocks Boosting Value with Buybacks—Act Now 
“Our adjusted operating margin and adjusted earnings per share performance was strong in the quarter,” Fadool said, citing margin expansion and earnings growth despite a declining production environment. 
Third-Quarter Results and Capital Returns 
Chief Financial Officer Craig Aaron said foreign exchange provided an $8 million year-over-year sales benefit in the quarter, while the battery business reduced sales by $54 million. The remaining organic sales decline was $58 million, or 1.6%, roughly in line with the decline in BorgWarner’s weighted light-vehicle production market. 
Is Adient’s guidance cut a positive sign for the auto suppliers? 
Adjusted operating income was $381 million, compared with $385 million a year earlier. On an organic basis, adjusted operating income declined $6 million on $112 million of lower sales, with cost reductions helping offset volume pressure, Aaron said. 
Free cash flow totaled $195 million in the quarter. BorgWarner used $175 million for share repurchases and paid $35 million in dividends, returning about $210 million to shareholders. The company said it expects to return more than $700 million to shareholders during 2026, including planned fourth-quarter buybacks. 
Third-quarter adjusted operating margin: 10.9%, versus 10.7% a year earlier. 
Third-quarter adjusted EPS: Up $0.15, or 12%, year over year. 
Third-quarter light-vehicle eProduct sales: $630 million, up 33%. 
Third-quarter free cash flow: $195 million. 
Updated 2026 Outlook 
BorgWarner narrowed the high end of its full-year revenue outlook, citing a refined view of industry production, while maintaining its adjusted operating-margin forecast and increasing adjusted EPS guidance. 
The company now expects 2026 sales of $14.0 billion to $14.2 billion, compared with prior guidance of $14.0 billion to $14.3 billion. It expects weighted end markets to decline 1% to 2% for the year, compared with its prior expectation of flat to down 3%. 
The company maintained its full-year adjusted operating margin outlook of 10.7% to 10.9%. Its organic sales outlook calls for a decline of 4% to 2.5%, including an estimated 170-basis-point headwind from lower battery-business sales related to the lack of North American incentives and weaker European demand. 
Adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.20 to $5.35 per diluted share from $5.05 to $5.30. Aaron said the increase reflected third-quarter and planned fourth-quarter share repurchases, along with a lower expected full-year effective tax rate. The company maintained projected free cash flow of $900 million to $1.1 billion. 
For the fourth quarter, Aaron said revenue is expected to be about $3.43 billion, down roughly $123 million from the average quarterly sales level in the first nine months, primarily reflecting production conditions. BorgWarner also expects about $10 million of industrial research and development spending in the quarter. 
Automotive Awards and 2027 Expectations 
BorgWarner announced nine business awards during the quarter across its foundational and eProduct portfolios. The awards included engine control modules for a new internal-combustion pickup-truck platform, turbocharger contracts for gasoline vehicles in South America and Europe, aluminum-wire e-motor technology for a Chinese OEM’s hybrid applications, three additional e-motor awards in China, and a next-generation high-voltage inverter award for battery-electric vehicles. 
Fadool said the aluminum-wire e-motor technology reduces wire weight by more than 60% and wire cost by more than 80% compared with a conventional copper-wire motor while maintaining peak torque and power. 
Looking toward 2027, Aaron said BorgWarner expects modest growth above the automotive market as recent business awards begin contributing to revenue. The company also expects $300 million of turbine-generator revenue next year. 
The company expects its PowerDrive Systems business to grow about 20% in 2026 after approximately 30% growth in 2025. Aaron said the company’s objective for the business unit remains mid-teens year-over-year conversion on sales growth. 
Data Center and Industrial Expansion 
BorgWarner highlighted progress in products designed for data center and industrial applications, including turbine generators, battery energy storage systems and microgrid inverters. 
The company said its partner plans to expand external turbine-generator demonstrations during the fourth quarter because of customer interest. Subsystem UL compliance is largely complete, and system certification is underway. BorgWarner has completed construction of its final assembly plant in North Carolina and expects manufacturing-floor and capital installation in December, followed by production trials by year-end. 
Fadool said customer discussions with hyperscalers have centered on meeting specifications, manufacturing tolerances, quality, reliability, efficiency and emissions. He said speed to market is important and that BorgWarner’s automotive manufacturing experience could enable it to bring products to market in 18 to 24 months, roughly half the time of some industrial competitors. 
For microgrid inverters, BorgWarner has shipped samples to seven customers and has begun initial quoting with its first major customer. The company expects UL certification in early 2027. It also developed an 800-volt power supply unit for data centers and displayed it at the Data Center World Power Industry event in Dallas. 
BorgWarner expects to be production-ready for its battery energy-storage offerings in 2027. Fadool said customer validation and UL processes are advancing, with engagement across both NMC and LFP cell applications. 
While the company said current political conditions may slow the completion of some data-center program agreements in the near term, Fadool said quoting activity remains high and that BorgWarner sees no long-term change in demand for its products. 
About BorgWarner BWA 
BorgWarner Inc BWA is a global automotive technology company that develops and manufactures propulsion and mobility systems for vehicle manufacturers and commercial vehicle customers. The company serves both internal-combustion and electrified vehicle markets, with a portfolio focused on improving vehicle efficiency, performance, emissions, and electrification. 
Its products and technologies include turbochargers, emissions and thermal-management systems, transmission components, friction products, battery systems, battery charging equipment, power electronics, electric motors, and other electric-drive components.

NEW YORK, Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Leading securities law firm Bleichmar Fonti & Auld LLP announces that a class action lawsuit has been filed against The Chemours Company (NYSE:CC) and certain of the company’s senior executives for securities fraud after a significant stock drop resulting from potential violations of the federal securities laws.
If you invested in Chemours, you are encouraged to obtain additional information by visiting: https://www.bfalaw.com/cases/chemours-class-action-lawsuit .
Key Details of the Chemours ($CC) Class Action: 
Lead Plaintiff Deadline: December 7, 2026
Alleged Misconduct: Securities fraud alleging Chemours misrepresented the strength of demand for its Opteon products
Stock Drop: August 5, 2026 – 18.63% Stock Drop
Court: U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware
Action: Contact BFA Law to discuss your rights
Investors have until December 7, 2026 to ask the Court to be appointed to lead the case. The complaint asserts securities fraud claims under Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 on behalf of investors in Chemours securities. The class action is pending in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. It is captioned Darcy v. The Chemours Company , No. 26-cv-1299.
Why is Chemours Being Sued for Securities Fraud? 
Chemours offers a range of industrial and specialty chemical products, including Opteon, a set of refrigeration chemicals with a reduced ozone-depletion footprint. In late 2020, Congress enacted the U.S. AIM Act, which directed the EPA to oversee the transition to alternative refrigerants that present a lesser impact to the ozone layer.
According to the complaint, Chemours stated that continued adoption of the AIM Act drove sustained growth for its Opteon products. Chemours stated that the “sustained double-digit” Opteon expansion would be “driven by the continued regulatory adoption” of the AIM Act. What’s more, Chemours provided 2026 net sales guidance of 3% to 5% growth and 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $800M – $900M, driven by “higher . . . demand” in its Opteon segment.
As alleged, Chemours failed to disclose that customers were already oversupplied with Opteon products because of the AIM Act transition, leading to an “oversupplied channel heading into 2026.”
Why did Chemours’s Stock Drop? 
On August 4, 2026, Chemours announced Q2 2026 financial results, revealing an approximately 1% year-over-year decrease in net sales and cutting 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance by about 11% (to $775M – $825M from $800M – $900M). Chemours also revealed that customers had “built additional inventory” of Opteon products the prior year, that aftermarket channels had been filled, and that Chemours was selling into an “oversupplied channel heading into 2026.”
On this news, Chemours’s stock dropped $3.34 per share, or 18.63%, from a closing price of $17.93 per share on August 4, 2026, to $14.59 per share on August 5, 2026.

Merck Opens Bioprocessing Center in South Korea
Merck's largest life sciences investment to date in the Asia-Pacific region expands regional manufacturing capacity.
Merck has opened its new bioprocessing production center for the Asia-Pacific region in Daejeon, South Korea. The investment in the center totals more than 300 million euros and is the company’s largest life sciences investment to date in the Asia-Pacific region. The 44,500 m² facility expands Merck’s regional manufacturing capacity for critical materials and solutions used in the development and production of biologic drugs. This will provide biopharmaceutical manufacturers throughout the Asia-Pacific region with faster access to the materials and solutions they need for the development and production of biologics.
“Reliable access to critical materials is crucial at every stage of biologics manufacturing,” said Jean-Charles Wirth, a member of Merck’s Executive Board and CEO of Life Science. “Daejeon brings advanced manufacturing closer to biopharmaceutical manufacturers in the Asia-Pacific region and strengthens supply security during the transition from development to commercial production. The center provides the regional capacity that customers need and delivers the quality and consistency they expect from Merck.”
© Merck
From Daejeon, Merck will supply bioprocessing products used from early-stage process development through commercial-scale manufacturing. These include cell culture media in dry powder and liquid forms, including small-scale, custom pre-GMP products via Immediate Advantage, process fluids and ready-to-use solutions for cleaning-in-place (CIP), as well as sterile single-use sampling solutions based on the NovaSeptum Sterile Sampling System. These products help customers accelerate development, scale up production, maintain controlled manufacturing environments, and reduce the risk of contamination. Raw materials free of animal-derived components are used for cell culture media and process fluids. Manufacturing is carried out in accordance with globally uniform quality standards.
“The completion of the new bioprocessing production center by Merck, a leading global science and technology company, marks a historic turning point for Daejeon’s development into a global bio-hub—not only for Korea, but for the entire world,” said Tae-Jeong Heo, Mayor of Daejeon. “We will do everything in our power to optimally integrate Merck’s key technologies in Daedeok Innopolis with local expertise. Furthermore, we will strategically deploy the city’s resources to build a world-leading biotechnology ecosystem through close collaboration among industry, universities, research institutions, and hospitals.”
The center’s integrated digital ecosystem supports automated data collection and end-to-end batch traceability. This increases process transparency and contributes to quality management as well as regulatory compliance.
The facility is designed to operate without fossil fuels on-site while simultaneously increasing energy and water efficiency—through the use of solar energy, a heat pump system, energy recovery in the ventilation systems, and the reuse of rainwater.
The center in Daejeon is a key component of Merck’s “In-Region-for-Region” strategy. It builds on recent investments in the company’s global network, including BioReliance®’s pharmaceutical product testing facility in Darmstadt and the filtration manufacturing facility in Blarney, Ireland. Within this network, Merck brings key products and services closer to its customers while ensuring consistent quality standards worldwide.

content_text:
Belgium's Syensqo ends C6O4 fluorosurfactant production in Italy
30 Oct '26
2 min read
Pic: Syensqo
Insights
Syensqo has ended production of C6O4, the last fluorosurfactant used in some fluoropolymer output at Italy's Spinetta Marengo site.
It fulfils a 2022 pledge to phase out fluorosurfactants by 2026 after research since 2019 enabled a new polymerisation process.
Nearly all its fluoropolymers are now made without PFAS processing aids.
Syensqo announces the end of production of C6O4, the last fluorosurfactant used in the manufacture of certain fluoropolymers at its Spinetta Marengo site (Italy). With this step, the company delivers on the innovation commitment it announced in 2022 to phase out fluorosurfactants by 2026, while continuing to produce the high-performance materials that enable critical technologies in semiconductors, batteries, hydrogen and other specialized industrial applications.
Fluorosurfactants are manufacturing aids used in the production of certain fluoropolymers and have been a particular focus of regulatory and public attention within the broader PFAS discussion. The company’s investment in Research and Innovation since 2019 has enabled the development of a new polymerization process that doesn’t require the use of fluorosurfactants, while maintaining the performance and reliability customers expect from fluoropolymers. These non-fluorosurfactant polymerization technologies have since been rolled out across product lines, allowing Syensqo to now cease the production of C6O4 in Italy.
Syensqo has ended production of C6O4, the last fluorosurfactant used in some fluoropolymer output at Italy's Spinetta Marengo site.
It fulfils a 2022 pledge to phase out fluorosurfactants by 2026 after research since 2019 enabled a new polymerisation process.
Nearly all its fluoropolymers are now made without PFAS processing aids.
"This milestone reflects years of investment in innovation. We have developed manufacturing technologies that eliminate the need for fluorosurfactants while continuing to provide the high-performance fluoropolymers our customers rely on for critical applications including semiconductors, clean energy and healthcare. Fluoropolymers remain essential materials for technologies that support the energy transition, medical innovation, clean water and digital infrastructure.", Mike Radossich, CEO of Syensqo. 
The production stop of C6O4 reflects Syensqo's strategy to reduce emissions from manufacturing processes and combine it with continued innovation in high-performance polymers, while supporting evolving regulatory expectations through science-based solutions.
Nearly 100% of the company's fluoropolymers are now manufactured without these PFAS processing aids. A small number (approx. 1% of the sites' production volume) of highly specialized fluoropolymers, primarily supporting hydrogen and semiconductor applications, still require additional research and qualification before transitioning to the new manufacturing technology. Existing C6O4 inventories will be used to manufacture these fluoropolymers using the best available technology for emissions reduction.
With one of the industry's broadest portfolios of specialty polymers in the industry, Syensqo combines deep materials science expertise with customer collaboration to develop solutions tailored to the world's most demanding applications. The transition to non-fluorosurfactant manufacturing further strengthens the group's ability to deliver high-performance materials with an increasingly sustainable manufacturing footprint.

Elektros Inc. Examines Potential U.S. Lithium Opportunity
4 min read 
ELEK LTH1! 
Company evaluates a potential northern New York lithium opportunity as domestic supply-chain activity grows 
WEST PALM BEACH, FL / ACCESS Newswire / October 29, 2026 / Federal Actions Put Domestic Lithium in the Spotlight 
Lithium has become an important material in the battery supply chain, including for electric vehicles, grid storage and certain defense-related power systems. As the United States seeks to strengthen domestic critical-mineral capacity, federal agencies have announced funding agreements, awards and project-support initiatives involving companies developing lithium resources and battery materials. Against this backdrop, ELEKTROS Inc. ELEK is evaluating whether a potential hard-rock lithium opportunity in northern New York, near the Canadian border, could fit its longer-term strategy. The location remains under consideration only; ELEKTROS is not announcing an acquisition, verified mineral resource or mine-development decision. 
Publicly Announced Examples of U.S. Government Support 
In September 2023, the U.S. Department of Defense announced a $90 million agreement with Albemarle Corporation under Defense Production Act Title III authorities to support the planned reopening of the Kings Mountain lithium mine in North Carolina and expand domestic lithium production. In August 2024, the Department of Defense announced an $11.8 million award to Lithium Nevada Corporation, a subsidiary of Lithium Americas, to accelerate development of lithium carbonate extraction and processing at Thacker Pass, Nevada. These are examples of federal support for domestic lithium production-not evidence that ELEKTROS has a government agreement or that the companies have been awarded a specific military lithium-supply purchase contract. 
More Recent Project Developments 
In June 2025, the U.S. Department of Energy identified federal awards of $150 million for Albemarle's Kings Mountain lithium-materials processing project and $225 million for TerraVolta's Liberty Owl lithium extraction and refining project. In June 2026, EnergyX announced that it had been selected by the U.S. Army for a conditional long-term lease to develop a lithium-processing facility at Red River Army Depot in Texas. EnergyX described the proposed facility as intended to process lithium into battery-grade materials and nuclear-grade lithium isotopes. The Army-related announcement concerns a conditional lease and planned facility; it should not be described as a completed lithium supply contract or as proof of current commercial deliveries. 
Why These Announcements Matter 
Together, these public announcements demonstrate that federal agencies have used multiple tools-including Defense Production Act awards, Department of Energy project funding and a conditional Army-site lease-to encourage domestic mineral and battery-material capacity. Each arrangement has its own conditions, milestones and risks. Federal support for other companies does not mean ELEKTROS is eligible for funding, has applied for an award, has received government support, or will secure a contract. Any future opportunity for ELEKTROS would depend on its own project merits, legal rights, technical results, permitting, financing and commercial arrangements. 
Evaluating a Potential Northern New York Opportunity 
A domestic hard-rock lithium project could potentially benefit from proximity to North American processing and manufacturing networks. Those benefits have not been established for the location under consideration. Responsible evaluation would require confirming ownership and mineral rights, reviewing geological information, arranging independent sampling where appropriate, assessing environmental and permitting obligations, and testing the practical economics of extraction, transportation, processing and financing. No verified resource, reserve, feasibility study, permit, transaction or production schedule is being announced. 
A Broader Electric-Mobility Strategy 
ELEKTROS is also exploring potential pathways to advance its multi-port electric-vehicle charging patent, U.S. Patent No. 12,522,100 B1. The company's areas of interest span potential lithium opportunities and EV-charging technology, two distinct areas within the broader electric-mobility ecosystem. The patent does not establish commercial adoption, a completed prototype, a licensing agreement, a customer contract or revenue. 
Management Perspective 
"Federal agencies have publicly recognized the importance of building stronger domestic supply chains for lithium and other critical materials," the company said. "ELEKTROS is evaluating potential opportunities with a focus on due diligence, verifiable milestones and commercially realistic economics. We believe it is important to assess opportunities carefully and to communicate clearly about what has-and has not-been achieved." 
About ELEKTROS Inc. 
ELEKTROS Inc. is a publicly traded company on the OTC market under ticker symbol ELEK. Its areas of interest include hard-rock lithium opportunities, EV-charging infrastructure and patented EV-charging technology. The potential northern New York location discussed in this release has not been announced as an acquired asset or a producing mine. This release contains forward-looking statements under applicable securities laws concerning possible property acquisition, lithium mineralization, resources, mining, processing, transportation, government programs, financing, future customers, charging technology and commercial opportunities. These statements are expectations, not guarantees. ELEKTROS has not announced a completed New York acquisition, an independently verified mineral resource or reserve, a feasibility study, a mining permit, an operating mine, a production schedule, a refinery supply agreement, a government award or a commercial charging prototype. The government awards, agreements and project announcements described above relate to other companies and do not imply that ELEKTROS has received, applied for, or will receive government funding or contracts. Risks include geological uncertainty, title and mineral rights, permitting, environmental obligations, capital availability, commodity prices, processing capacity, logistics, counterparties, technology development, competition and market volatility. Eli Lilly LLY reported 39% revenue growth and 7% non-GAAP earnings-per-share growth, including acquisition costs. Management raised 2026 revenue guidance to $91.5 billion at the midpoint (from $86 billion) and trimmed non-GAAP EPS guidance to $35.50 at the midpoint from $36, accounting for acquisitions.
Why it matters: Lilly shares rose 6% intraday on Oct. 29 as investors processed another quarter of remarkably strong revenue and underlying earnings growth.
Obesity drug Zepbound’s rapid uptake as part of the new Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program and deeper demand for obesity drugs in the cash-pay market internationally look like the biggest sources of this outperformance.
The bottom line: We’re maintaining our $980 per share fair value estimate for wide-moat Lilly. While we see momentum around the shares due to strong performance and rotation out of other sectors, we think market prices have risen above Lilly’s fundamental value.
Our near- and long-term revenue projections are well ahead of consensus. We’ve raised our 2026 revenue forecast from $90.4 billion to $92.7 billion, reflecting 42% sales growth this year, but our changes didn’t significantly alter our valuation.
While acquisitions are masking underlying operating leverage in 2026, we expect revenue growth to fall back to earth (18% growth) in 2027, which looks more in line with operating expense growth and less likely to drive operating leverage.
Coming up: International expansion of oral GLP-1 Foundayo should accelerate as it gains approval in more markets (potentially broader European approval this year), and US diabetes approval would also allow Lilly to point to more favorable data relative to Novo’s.
We’re watching 2027 data in oncology (Inluriyo, early-stage breast cancer) and neurology (Kisunla, cognitively unimpaired Alzheimer’s patients diagnosed via blood test) for confidence in Lilly’s long-term growth trajectory outside of diabetes and obesity.

Written by Giann Liguid

The company plans to invest approximately US$4 billion in growth capital across its Argentine lithium operations and expects to spend around 70 percent of it with local suppliers.
Tigarto / Adobe Stock 
Rio Tinto (ASX:RIO,NYSE:RIO,LSE:RIO) opened two lithium operations in Argentina's Catamarca province on Thursday (October 29), which is touted to add 25,000 metric tons of annual lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) capacity once fully ramped up. 
To date, Rio Tinto has invested roughly US$1.4 billion in the Fénix 1B expansion and the new Sal de Vida operation. Both reached first production ahead of plan in the second quarter and are now ramping up.
Fénix began operating in 1997 as Argentina's first commercial lithium operation. The 1B expansion adds 10,000 metric tons of annual LCE capacity there, which raises the operation's total target to about 40,000 metric tons. Sal de Vida sits roughly 20 kilometers northeast of Fénix and targets 15,000 metric tons a year.
CEO Simon Trott linked the two projects to Rio Tinto's global target of 200,000 metric tons of annual LCE production capacity by 2028.
"Our focus now is on safely ramping up production, delivering reliable, high-quality lithium to our customers, and creating lasting value for our shareholders and Argentina," Trott said.
In Salta, Rio Tinto is building the US$2.5 billion Rincon project, which targets approximately 60,000 metric tons of annual battery-grade lithium carbonate capacity. 
In March, the company secured a US$1.175 billion financing package for Rincon from four lenders. 
Construction at Rincon started in 2025. Rio Tinto expects first production in 2028, followed by a three-year ramp-up to full capacity running across an expected lifespan of 40 years.
Outside Argentina, Rio Tinto took majority control of Nemaska Lithium (TSX:NMX) in Québec in February this year with a 53.9 percent stake and assumed direct management of the company. The Québec government holds the remaining 46.1 percent through Investissement Québec.
Rio Tinto said it plans to invest more than US$300 million in its Québec lithium business this year.

Rio Tinto Opens Two Argentine Lithium Projects Backed by $1.4 Billion
Rio Tinto has launched two lithium ventures in Argentina, underpinned by a total commitment of $1.4 billion, as the mining group accelerates its push into battery metals. The Fénix 1B expansion and the Sal de Vida operation, both located in Catamarca province, commenced first production during the second quarter of 2026, ahead of schedule, and are currently increasing output.
Once running at full capacity, the pair will contribute 25,000 tonnes of yearly lithium carbonate equivalent capacity, according to the company. At an inauguration event attended by President Javier Milei and Catamarca Governor Raúl Jalil, Rio Tinto chief executive Simon Trott said the developments draw on almost thirty years of lithium output in the province and the skills of the firm's Argentine employees. He also referenced the company's worldwide ambition of reaching 200,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent annual capacity by 2028.
Project Details
The $530-million Fénix 1B expansion contributes 10,000 tonnes of yearly capacity, raising the site's overall target to about 40,000 tonnes. Fénix started producing in 1997, becoming Argentina's first commercial lithium operation. Rio Tinto is evaluating a further expansion, with an investment decision anticipated in 2028 or 2029.
Sal de Vida, a new lithium carbonate facility situated roughly 20 km northeast of Fénix, is designed for 15,000 tonnes per year. Its initial phase required an investment of $374 million.
Both operations belong to an integrated production hub in the Salar del Hombre Muerto, whose combined resource base stands at approximately 19 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent. Running the sites jointly enables infrastructure sharing, efficiency gains and efforts to lower water use. Fénix employs direct lithium extraction, whereas Sal de Vida uses conventional evaporation ponds.
Counting Fénix, Sal de Vida and Olaroz, Rio Tinto's nominal lithium capacity in Argentina totals roughly 100,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent per year. Its wider Argentine holdings include a 66.5% interest in Olaroz and complete ownership of the Rincón project, which extends across Catamarca, Jujuy and Salta provinces.
Market Context
Argentina is projected to generate around 172,700 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2026, a 48% rise over the prior year and over five times the 2018 figure. Between January and August 2026, lithium exports brought in $1.467 billion, up 190.5% compared with the same period twelve months earlier.
Rio Tinto intends to direct close to 70% of its planned $4 billion in Argentine lithium growth capital toward local suppliers. The spending dovetails with Milei's push to draw foreign investment via market-friendly reforms and the Large Investment Incentive Regime, which grants tax, legal and foreign-exchange advantages for 30 years to eligible projects exceeding $200 million in value.
Benchmark Mineral Intelligence projects worldwide lithium demand climbing from 2 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2026 to 7 million tonnes by 2050, chiefly on electric vehicle and energy storage growth. Argentina's Mining Secretariat anticipates the country may surpass Chile in lithium output by 2029 and achieve yearly production of 573,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent by 2035.

content_text:
Merck outlines 2027 as ‘another year of investment’ despite recent clinical wins
By
Angus Liu 
Oct 29, 2026 11:23am 
Merck 
Earnings 
Keytruda 
sac-TMT 
Merck ramps up R&D and commercial investments to secure its post-Keytruda future. (Photo by Kena Betancur/Getty Images)
Even as a wave of clinical trial wins bolsters its momentum, Merck & Co. is prioritizing ongoing pipeline and commercial expansions over near-term margin growth, hoping to gird its long-term prospects past Keytruda's loss of exclusivity.
For 2027, “we see it as another year of investment, as we invest behind our expansive pipeline and our new product launches to drive long-term growth,” Merck’s CFO Caroline Litchfield said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call Thursday.
Litchfield made the comment in response to a question about whether Merck has seen enough R&D progress recently that the company may start to turn its attention to earnings growth as it looks beyond 2030.
At least for 2027, Merck expects underlying operating expenses to increase at a mid- to high-single-digit rate, “reflecting our conviction in the significant opportunity from our expanding pipeline and the growing portfolio of new product launches,” Litchfield said.
“We will continue to invest in value-creating opportunities that drive both near- and long-term growth,” Litchfield said of Merck’s capital allocation plans. “Business development remains an important priority, and we retain financial flexibility within a strong investment-grade credit rating to pursue additional science-driven, value-enhancing transactions.”
One of the key new clinical programs that Merck plans to invest in next year is advancing its PD-1xVEGF bispecific MK-2010, partnered with China’s SBP Group (formerly Sino Biopharmaceutical), into phase 3.
Following “productive discussions” with the FDA and “the totality of data generated to date,” Merck will initiate phase 3 development for MK-2010, including combinations with Kelun-Biotech-partnered TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate sac-TMT, in first-line non-small cell lung cancer in the first half of 2027, Marjorie Green, Merck’s head of oncology global clinical development, told investors during an Oct. 26 event. This plan was confirmed by Merck’s R&D chief Dean Li, M.D., Ph.D., on Thursday’s call.
The decision comes as sac-TMT, used alongside Keytruda, delivered a 51% progression-free survival benefit against Keytruda-chemo in first-line, PD-L1-negative NSCLC in a China phase 3. In parallel, sac-TMT’s first global phase 3 readout, in endometrial cancer, also showed consistent data with previous China results. 
Beyond sac-TMT, positive phase 3 results from Moderna-partnered mRNA cancer vaccine intismeran autogene and diabetic macular edema candidate remigromig drew some recent investor scrutiny. 
On the mRNA immunotherapy specifically, jacked-up investor expectations have overshadowed the otherwise strong data itself. 
During Thursday’s call, Li called the INTerpath-001 melanoma trial “a landmark study in its own right,” citing a comment from Antoni Ribas, M.D., Ph.D., a leading melanoma clinical researcher from the University of California Los Angeles.
“Because of that, we would hope that upon approval that the NCCN guidelines would potentially define this as a new standard of care,” Li said.
Looking into 2027, Merck expects some top-line pressure, as Litchfield flagged the potential for more “moderate” growth thanks to more than $2 billion of negative impact from generic competition affecting Bridion, the Januvia family and Bayer-partnered Adempas.
Keytruda, while still a major pillar of Merck’s business, will “see growth moderating” as it has reached peak penetration in several indications, she said. Total Keytruda sales, including the subcutaneous Keytruda Qlex, reached $8.6 billion during the third quarter, up 6% year over year.
Merck is locked in a patent fight with Halozyme over Keytruda Qlex. An injunction was recently ordered by a Dutch patent court that affects the subcutaneous drug’s rollout in eight European nations. 
The injunction was put in place until a hearing is held, and it “doesn’t speak to the merits of our belief,” Merck’s CEO Rob Davis noted on the call. “We continue to feel very, very good that we have a position both in the U.S. and in Europe.”
Meanwhile, in the vaccines business, Merck’s HPV vaccine Gardasil enjoyed a rally thanks to “favorable public-sector purchasing patterns and higher net pricing” in the U.S., with 14% year-over-year growth to $2 billion, according to an earnings release.
For vaccines overall, Litchfield said a $250 million buy-in from the CDC this year will unwind in 2027.
On other recent launch progress, pulmonary arterial hypertension med Winrevair nearly doubled sales to $694 million in the third quarter, and kidney cancer drug Welireg grew sales by 56% to $307 million. 
Also in the infectious disease department, sales of Merck’s RSV preventive Enflonsia jumped 138% year over year to $187 million as inventory builds ahead of a new RSV season.
For 2026, Merck narrowed the range of its full-year revenue guidance to between $66.8 billion and $67.3 billion.

content_text:
Hamburg Hosts 2026 European Gene Therapy Conference
By 
Kevin Davies, PhD 
October 29, 2026 
Credit: Kevin Davies, PhD
HAMBURG —The historic German port city of Hamburg is playing host to the European Society of Gene & Cell Therapy (ESGCT) conference this week.
As noted in the opening session, the Port of Hamburg was established more than 800 years ago. It is also a proud center of editing—newspapers rather than genes—as the site of the headquarters of Der Speigel and Die Zeit . And of course, Hamburg famously helped forge the sound and legend of the “Fab Four”—the Beatles played numerous gigs between 1960-62 in the central St. Pauli district. It was also where Ringo Starr met his future bandmates in 1960.
Patient safety, expanding access to gene therapy, and progress towards an HIV vaccine were prominent themes among the early talks at ESGCT 2026. In the opening plenary session, Dimitrios Mougiakakos, MHBA, discussed his group’s research on CAR T therapy for lupus, noting progress but some patient deaths. “Lower risk does not mean no risk,” he said, pointing to the rapid production of CAR T cells as a potential risk factor. A “Volkswagen approach” might be better than a “Ferrari approach,” he concluded.
Italian professor Giuliana Ferrari, PhD, discussed her team’s research on beta-thalassemia, one of the “less rare of the rare diseases,” characterized by more than 400 different globin gene mutations. Ferrari noted that some of the patients in the ex vivo TIGET-BTHAL Phase I/II trial, which began in 2015, had restarted blood transfusions, while others remained transfusion-independent after nine years, producing respectable levels of hemoglobin.
Ferarri’s team has spent several years optimizing manufacturing protocols to launch a new trial, Bthal FT007-01. The first two patients have been enrolled in this Phase IIb trial, an academic initiative between Italian groups designed to provide affordable access to gene therapy. Refinements include the implementation of a shorter 40-hour cell culture and gene transduction protocol (down from 60 hours) and a change in conditioning regimen.
HIV hope 
In addition to his academic position at Scripps Research Institute, Bill Schief, PhD, is also the vice president of protein design at Moderna. Although he acknowledged he was a slightly unusual choice for a plenary speaker, as his work was not technically gene therapy, he relished the chance to present his team’s promising work on the quest to engineer a specific immune response and to develop a functional HIV vaccine.
The statistics remain sobering: More than 40 million people live with HIV, but more than 20 percent do not receive antiretroviral therapy. There are 1.2 million new HIV infections and 570,000 deaths per year. All told, 44 million people have died of AIDS, and global funding for AIDS research is going down. “We need a vaccine,” Schief emphasized.
Schief and colleagues are designing vaccines to guide the immune system toward antibodies that target conserved, vulnerable regions of the HIV envelope protein. Hope resides in the development of broadly effective Abs (bnAbs). A successful HIV vaccine will need to induce multiple classes of bnAbs, Schief said.
Schief reviewed research to deliver a sequence of immunogens, using priming, “shepherding,” and “polishing,” with the goal of producing bnAbs and long-lived plasma cells to sustain production. The strategy is “very complicated but not crazy,” Schief said, citing the need for serum bnAbs to have breadth, potency, and durability.
Over the past two years, researchers have reported clinical results and animal studies that represent significant advances towards their goal. In 2025, Schief’s team reported promising Phase I results in Science . IAVI G002, conducted in the U.S., tested an mRNA vaccine designed to activate the desired antibody precursors, followed by a different mRNA vaccine intended to advance their development. IAVI G003 was conducted in Rwanda and South Africa, testing the initial vaccine approach in African populations.
“Let’s make sure the strategy works there [in Africa],” Schief said. The findings provided proof of concept but stopped short of a full vaccine. Earlier this year, Schief and colleagues published in Nature results showing that germline-targeting vaccines can induce pre-specific bnAbs in memory B cells and serum in non-human primates.
CAR T promise 
Michel Sadelain, MD, PhD, presented a compelling overview of the promise of CAR T therapy in oncology and other therapeutic areas. Of the seven CAR T therapies approved in the U.S. to date, five target CD19. In oncology, survival duration has quadrupled from about six months to more than 25 months. Sadelain said there was promising data in other fields, including rheumatology (lupus, arthritis, and scleroderma), as well as preliminary results in neurology (myasthenia gravis). This progress has all been achieved with the original two molecular designs that yielded Yescarta and Kymriah: CD28z CAR and 4-1BBz CAR.
But progress in tackling solid tumors with CAR therapy has not kept pace with hematological malignancies, Sadelain said. He listed five primary challenges in this regard:
The need to increase functional persistence of T cells
Potency
Sensitivity
The need to understand and prevent toxicity
New targets
In one line of research, Sadelain’s team revisited signaling strength, with a view to tempering it. In 2025, the group showed that by switching from three ITAMs to a single ITAM, they could create a strong effector function with much greater persistence. This “1XX” signaling module was taken to the clinic in B-cell lymphoma , with excellent responses seen administering as few as 25 million cells—a tenth of the regular dose (100-400 million cells).
In another approach, Sadelain’s team has used CRISPR to develop a new CAR— the HLA-independent T cell (HIT) receptor —that is at least 10-fold more sensitive. The characterization of this CAR in solid tumors such as renal cell carcinomas in immunodeficient mice continues.
 
*ESGCT 2026; Hamburg, Germany; October 27-30, 2026.

A potential new tool for Cinema 4D is raising more questions about the direction of creative software.
(Image credit: Maxon)

Maxon teased what looks like another AI tool for 3D artists in an X video, possibly for Cinema 4D , and the reaction isn’t good, though probably as expected. There's little detail so far, but the prospect of more AI entering creative software is already rubbing some artists the wrong way.
Over on X users bombarded the teaser video with reactions, from the somewhat restrained, “You guys are gulping the whole AI stuff without its users in mind” to the angry, “I’m going to have a good laugh when they use AI to reverse-engineer all your programs, and you go bankrupt. If you’ve got the nerve to screw us artists over, I hope you get a taste of your own medicine,” and the blunt, “A slop generator, cool”.
🐦‍⬛✍️
Coming soon. https://t.co/6rEbIPTWBR October 28, 2026 
Some looked beyond outrage and perhaps gave Maxon some leeway to see where this can help: “If you want to use AI in a 3D program, the most useful feature would be for making UVs. I hate UV'ing; it's like making the model again,” says a user.
Of all the comments, I find this one from ‘Augenhorn’ sums up the situation generally with AI in creative apps, with just the right balance of cynicism, scepticism and grudging concession: “This is not how people will use it. They will feed in AI slop to get out a slop Model and then fiddle around with it tiredly, only to go all the way over to get scammed by Higgsfield. Anyway, nice feature though; it’s all not your fault… love and pay C4D for 14 years now.”
Maxon embraces generative AI
This isn’t Maxon’s first time with AI, and it follows Autodesk's lead in using the tech to make 3D modelling and animation more accessible. In March, Maxon announced a partnership with Tencent Cloud to bring its HY 3D generative AI engine into Cinema 4D , letting artists generate base 3D models and UVs from text prompts or image references. The plan is to let artists take those AI-generated starting points into Cinema 4D's existing tools to sculpt, refine, animate and render them. This could tease a fuller reveal of that integration.
Cinema 4D remains one of the best 3D modelling software packages , and also now supports AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude, which can use the software's tools to handle jobs like organising scenes, creating material variations, and setting up renders. The idea is to take some of the more repetitive work off an artist's hands while keeping them in control of the scene.
But there's a difference between an assistant that helps you get through a tedious afternoon of production work and a tool that generates 3D assets from a prompt, and artists have different opinions on where that line should sit, even as brands like Maxon, Autodesk, and Adobe begin to blur it. Maxon's AI plans have already attracted criticism, including its response to Digital Twin, its tool for placing existing 3D product models into AI-generated marketing environments.

The wider creative AI dilemma
With all this in mind, and knowing AI is affecting creative jobs , it's unsurprising that when another AI tease appears, some artists don't exactly reach for the champagne. The bigger concern is how quickly creative software companies are embracing generative AI, and whether the promise of faster workflows is worth the potential cost to the craft and the people who make a living from it.
It's not yet clear whether this latest teaser ties into the planned Tencent integration, Cinema 4D's existing AI assistant tools, or something entirely different. Until Maxon provides more detail, it's hard to judge what the tool will actually do, let alone whether artists should welcome it or worry about it.
Still, Maxon is finding that selling AI features to a creative audience isn't as easy as some software companies might have hoped. Artists want to see what these tools can do, but they also want to know why they're being made, how they'll fit into a real working day and what the company thinks the future of 3D art should look like.

Merck Opens €300 Million Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center in Daejeon, South Korea 
Merck's Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center Opening Ceremony Darmstadt, Germany, Oct. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- 
Merck's largest life science investment in Asia-Pacific to date expands regional manufacturing capacity 
Integrated digital systems support automated data capture and end-to-end batch traceability 
Advances Merck's in-region-for-region strategy, bringing critical products closer to customers across Asia-Pacific 
State-of-the-art facility designed to eliminate on-site fossil-fuel use and improve energy and water efficiency 
Merck, a leading science and technology company, today opened its new Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center in Daejeon, South Korea. The center represents an investment of more than €300 million, the company's largest Life Science investment in Asia-Pacific to date. 
The 44,500-square-meter site expands the Merck's regional manufacturing capacity for critical materials and solutions used in the development and production of biologic medicines. It gives biopharmaceutical manufacturers across Asia-Pacific closer access to the materials and solutions needed to develop and produce biologic medicines.
"Reliable access to critical materials is essential at every stage of biologics manufacturing," said Jean-Charles Wirth, Member of the Executive Board of Merck, and CEO Life Science. "Daejeon brings advanced production closer to biopharma manufacturers across Asia-Pacific, giving them greater supply confidence, as they move from development to commercial scale. The center adds the regional capacity customers need and delivers the quality and consistency they expect from Merck."
From Daejeon, Merck will supply bioprocessing products used from early process development through commercial-scale manufacturing. These include cell culture media in dry powder and liquid formats, including pre-GMP small-scale custom products through imMEDIAte ADVANTAGE®, process liquids and ready-to-use cleaning-in-place solutions; and single-use sterile sampling solutions based on the NovaSeptum® Sterile Sampling System. Together, they help customers accelerate development, scale production, maintain controlled manufacturing environments and reduce contamination risk. Cell culture media and process liquids will use animal-component-free raw materials and be manufactured to consistent global quality standards. 
"The completion of Merck's Asia-Pacific Bioprocessing Production Center, a world-leading bioscience company, marks a historic turning point in Daejeon's rise as a global bio hub—not just for Korea, but for the world." said Tae-Jeong Heo, Mayor of Daejeon. "We will provide our full support to ensure that Merck's foundational technologies at the Daedeok Innopolis and the capabilities of the local community can be brought together seamlessly. We will focus the city's resources on building a world-class global bio ecosystem through close collaboration among industry, academia, research institutions, and hospitals." 
Story Continues 
The center's integrated digital ecosystem is designed to support automated data capture and end-to-end batch traceability, increasing process transparency and supporting quality management and regulatory compliance.
The facility is designed to eliminate the use of fossil fuels on-site while increasing energy and water efficiency through the use of solar power, a heat-pump system, energy recovery in air handling units, and rainwater reuse. 
The Daejeon center is a key part of Merck's in-region-for-region strategy. It builds on recent investments across the company's global network, including BioReliance® drug product testing in Darmstadt, Germany, and filtration manufacturing in Blarney, Ireland. Across this network, Merck is bringing critical products and services closer to customers while applying consistent global quality standards. 
About Merck 
Merck, a leading science and technology company, operates across life science, healthcare and electronics. More than 62,000 employees work to make a positive difference to millions of people's lives every day by creating more joyful and sustainable ways to live. From providing products and services that accelerate drug development and manufacturing as well as discovering unique ways to treat the most challenging diseases to enabling the intelligence of devices – the company is everywhere. In 2025, Merck generated sales of € 21.1 billion in 65 countries. 
Scientific exploration and responsible entrepreneurship have been key to Merck's technological and scientific advances. This is how Merck has thrived since its founding in 1668. The founding family remains the majority owner of the publicly listed company. Merck holds the global rights to the Merck name and brand. The only exceptions are the United States and Canada, where the business sectors of Merck operate as MilliporeSigma in life science, EMD Serono in healthcare, and EMD Electronics in electronics. 
All Merck press releases are distributed by e-mail at the same time they become available on the Merck website. Please go to www.merckgroup.com/subscribe to register online, change your selection or discontinue this service.

content_text:
SCHOTT Poonawalla Renamed SCHOTT Pharma India, Reaffirms Long-Term Commitment to Indian Pharma Market 
Written By : sheeba farhat Published On 2026-10-29T15:46:32+05:30   |   Updated On 29 Oct 2026 3:46 PM IST 
New Delhi: SCHOTT Poonawalla Private Limited will become SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, marking an important new chapter in the company's journey and strengthening its connection with the global SCHOTT Pharma organization.
The new identity more clearly reflects the India business’s place within SCHOTT Pharma’s global network and its role in advancing high-quality drug containment and delivery solutions for the pharmaceutical and biotech industries. It brings together the company’s strong manufacturing footprint, long-standing customer relationships and deep market expertise in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global capabilities, innovation and scientific excellence.
For customers, partners and employees, this is a change in name, not a change in commitment. There is no change in ownership, management, employees, business strategy, operations, products, services or existing customer commitments.
The transition reinforces SCHOTT Pharma India’s long-term commitment to customers in India and international markets, while creating a stronger and more consistent connection to the global SCHOTT Pharma brand.
Building on a heritage of more than 140 years, the new identity brings the company’s heritage and future ambition under one global name, reflecting the values that continue to define SCHOTT Pharma: innovation, quality, scientific excellence and trust.
Also Read: TPG to acquire 35% stake in SCHOTT Poonawalla from SII 
SCHOTT Pharma India represents both continuity and progress: the same trusted business, capabilities and relationships, now with an identity that more clearly reflects who we are today and where we are headed.
Roy Joseph, CEO & Managing Director, SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, said, “SCHOTT Pharma India represents the next chapter of our journey, combining our strength in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global innovation and expertise. We see significant opportunity to build on our capabilities, deepen collaboration with pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners, and advance drug containment and delivery solutions. As we move forward, our focus remains on growing with our customers and contributing to the safe and reliable delivery of critical therapies to patients worldwide.”
“SCHOTT Pharma India plays a critical role in patient care. With more than 3 billion containers produced annually, this company enables around 7,000 injections to reach patients every minute,” said Dr. Christian Mias, CEO of SCHOTT Pharma AG & Co. KGaA, SCHOTT Pharma India’s major shareholder. “The name change from SCHOTT Poonawalla to SCHOTT Pharma India reinforces our strategic partnership and confirms our long-term commitment to India as a key pharma hub.”
The new identity builds on the company’s strong foundation in India. During the COVID-19 pandemic, its pharmaceutical vials supported more than 4.3 billion vaccine doses worldwide, including 3 billion doses in India. As India’s only manufacturer of glass pre-fillable syringes and sterile formats, the company also strengthens local supply capabilities. Furthermore, the company continues to invest significantly towards manufacturing capacity expansions of pre-fillable syringes and cartridges, strengthening their ability to support the rapidly evolving needs of biologics, biosimilars, GLP-1 based treatments and other advanced injectable therapies.
Looking ahead, SCHOTT Pharma India will focus on expanding capabilities across pharmaceutical drug containment and drug delivery solutions, driving innovation through closer customer collaboration, and strengthening operational excellence and sustainability. These priorities will support the company as it responds to the evolving needs of pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies while contributing to India’s growing role in the global pharmaceutical value chain.
SCHOTT Pharma India is a manufacturer of advanced drug containment and delivery solutions, serving pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies across global markets. Based on innovation in specialty glass and advanced materials, the company offers a comprehensive portfolio of injectable drug containment and delivery products, including vials, cartridges, syringes and ampoules. Manufactured to stringent international quality standards, SCHOTT Pharma India’s solutions enable safe storage of vaccines and biologics. Through continued investment in innovation and operational excellence, and a strong focus on quality, reliability and customer partnership, the company addresses evolving healthcare needs and supports better patient outcomes worldwide.

content_text:
Eli Lilly hikes sales outlook, as CEO says there's room for 'dramatic' obesity market expansion
Published Thu, Oct 29 2026 6:13 AM EDT Updated Thu, Oct 29 2026 12:46 PM EDT 
Annika Kim Constantino @annikakimc 
WATCH LIVE 
Key Points
Eli Lilly reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that blew past estimates and hiked its full-year sales outlook.
Demand for its obesity drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro surged again and topped estimates for the quarter.
Despite that strength, sales of its new GLP-1 obesity pill Foundayo, which launched in the U.S. in April, were under Wall Street's expectations for the quarter.
In this article
LLY 
Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT 
watch now 
VIDEO 4:53 04:53 
Eli Lilly CEO Dave Ricks on the obesity market: The room for expansion is dramatic
Squawk on the Street 
Eli Lilly on Thursday reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that blew past estimates and hiked its full-year sales outlook, as demand for its blockbuster weight loss drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro soared again. 
Despite that strength, sales of its new GLP-1 obesity pill Foundayo, which launched in the U.S. in April, were under Wall Street's expectations for the quarter.
The pharmaceutical giant now expects 2026 revenue to come in between $91 billion and $92 billion, up from a previous guidance of $85 billion to $87 billion. 
Lilly projects its full-year adjusted earnings will be between $35 and $36 per share, which compares with a previous outlook of $35.50 to $36.50 per share. The company said it raised the underlying profit guidance by $4.07 per share at the midpoint, but noted that it is offset by $4.57 per share in charges tied to deals in the quarter.
The company's shares rose about 7% on Thursday. 
Lilly's massive diabetes and obesity windfall – and market share lead over chief rival Novo – shows no signs of slowing down, even as the company grapples with lower net prices in the U.S. The pharma giant is converting its massive profits into a deal-making spree, most recently striking an agreement to buy Merida Biosciences to develop a new class of treatments for serious autoimmune and allergic diseases. 
Here's what Eli Lilly reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: 
Earnings per share: $7.48 adjusted vs. $6.26 expected
Revenue: $24.40 billion vs. $22.61 billion expected
Resilient demand for Zepbound and Mounjaro has helped fuel several strong quarters for Lilly despite lower prices for the medications in the U.S., which came after a drug pricing deal struck with the Trump administration last year. In a release, Lilly also pointed to expanded U.S. coverage for obesity care, referring to Medicare's decision to start covering GLP-1s for weight loss in July under a temporary pilot program. 
"This is a program that's really working," Lilly CEO Dave Ricks said on CNBC's " Squawk on the Street ." "We're pleased with the early uptake and access, and I think doctors and patients are as well."
Mounjaro's worldwide revenue rose 65% to $10.72 billion for the quarter, including U.S. sales of about $5 billion. That surpassed the $10.10 billion in worldwide sales and $4.79 billion in U.S. revenue that analysts were expecting for the quarter, according to StreetAccount.
Mounjaro notably saw strength internationally, with sales outside the U.S. jumping 93%.
Zepbound, which entered the market roughly three years ago, posted $5.35 billion in revenue for the third quarter. That's up 49% from the year-earlier period, as demand for the drug also rose while realized prices dropped. The vast majority of those sales came from the U.S. 
Analysts were expecting $5.09 billion in global sales for Zepbound, including $4.99 billion from the U.S., according to StreetAccount.
One of Eli Lilly's buildings in San Diego, California, Nov. 21, 2025.
Mike Blake | Reuters
Lilly's newly launched obesity pill, Foundayo, which won U.S. approval in April, took in $184 million in sales for the third quarter. That fell under analyst forecasts of around $229 million in sales, StreetAccount estimates showed. 
It marks the second earnings report that includes revenue from the GLP-1 pill, which is competing head-to-head with a rival oral drug from Novo that launched in January. 
Total U.S. prescriptions for Foundayo and the number of new Foundayo patients in the third quarter doubled from the previous quarter, Lilly CFO Lucas Montarces said during a Thursday earnings call. Around 4 in 10 patients starting an oral obesity medicine choose Foundayo, he added.
Lilly expects Foundayo to win U.S. approval for Type 2 diabetes in the fourth quarter.
Lilly is working to maintain its dominance in the booming market for GLP-1 drugs, with the company holding 63% share of the U.S. obesity and diabetes drug market in the third quarter, according to an earnings presentation on Thursday. Novo's market share in the quarter was 36.6%. 
During the earnings call, Montarces said 7 out of 10 U.S. prescriptions for injectable obesity and diabetes drugs in the third quarter were for a Lilly medicine. 
Ricks told CNBC that he estimates 3% to 10% of eligible patients access obesity care in the U.S., but said the "room for expansion here of this market is dramatic." Lilly is at the front of that push, he added. 
Internationally, Lilly held 58.4% share of the market, while Novo had 41.6%, the presentation said. 
Eli Lilly's revenue in the U.S. climbed 34% to $15.1 billion. Lilly said it saw a 41% increase in volume — or the number of prescriptions or units sold — for its products, primarily for Mounjaro and Zepbound. That was partially offset by a 7% decrease in realized prices, primarily driven by Zepbound. 
Lilly's quarter was also boosted by a sales-based milestone payout of $410 million for its Type 2 diabetes medication Jardiance, related to the company's collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim.
Sales outside the U.S. jumped 47% to $9.3 billion, propelled by a 76% surge in volume and partly offset by a 29% drop in realized prices. 
The pharmaceutical giant booked net income of $6.45 billion, or $7.22 per share, for the third quarter, which includes the $4.57 per share deal charges. That compares with net income of $5.58 billion, or $6.21 per share, a year earlier. 
Excluding one-time items associated with the value of intangible assets and other adjustments, Eli Lilly posted earnings of $7.48 per share for the third quarter.

Mouser Electronics , the authorized global distributor with the newest electronic components and industrial automation products, is now stocking the XENSIV BGT60CUTR13AIP radar sensor from Infineon Technologies . 
The XENSIV BGT60CUTR13AIP sensor provides ultra-wideband FMCW operation in a single-chip solution. This sensor offers advanced sensing capabilities with high precision and ultra-low power consumption. The new XENSIV BGT60CUTR13AIP 60 GHz CMOS radar sensor includes on-chip processing powered by a hardware accelerator, providing customers the flexibility to access either raw or pre-processed data. By handling radar processing on-chip, Infineon’s solution offloads the host processor and enables a more efficient system architecture, enabling smaller form factors and cost efficiency. This sensor-integrated hardware sequencer with a Finite State Machine (FSM) offers the user full flexibility in configuring chirps and timing. The embedded motion/presence detection block, with a low false-alarm rate, further reduces system power by waking external hosts via a dedicated interrupt pin.
Typical applications include monitors, smart speakers, air conditioners, doorbells, sleep trackers, baby monitors, and security cameras and video doorbells.
As a global authorised distributor, Mouser offers the world’s widest selection of the newest semiconductors and electronic components — in stock and ready to ship. Mouser’s customers can expect 100% certified, genuine products that are fully traceable from each of its manufacturer partners. To help speed up the design process for customers, Mouser’s website hosts an extensive library of technical resources, including a Technical Resource Centre, along with product data sheets, supplier-specific reference designs, application notes, technical design information, engineering tools and other helpful information.

BASF Pursues Further Acquisitions as Evonik Takeover Talks Continue
Posted by Global Cosmetics News | Oct 29, 2026 | Europe , Finance , Ingredients | 
THE WHAT? BASF is exploring further acquisition opportunities across the chemicals industry while pursuing a potential takeover of Evonik, as stronger third-quarter earnings support its consolidation and portfolio restructuring strategy.
THE DETAILS BASF has reportedly increased its offer for Evonik to more than €11 billion following the rejection of an earlier proposal, although no agreement has been confirmed. Chief Executive Markus Kamieth identified Evonik as the company’s preferred acquisition target while indicating that further acquisitions and smaller asset disposals remain under consideration. BASF also raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA forecast to €7.4 billion–€7.8 billion, supported by a 12% increase in prices and 2% volume growth during the third quarter. The company has reduced net debt by approximately 20% over the past year, strengthening its capacity for acquisitions despite continued pressure on Europe’s chemicals sector.
THE WHY? The developments highlight accelerating consolidation and portfolio restructuring across Europe’s chemicals industry as manufacturers seek greater scale, higher-margin businesses and improved competitiveness. For the cosmetics and personal care supply chain, potential changes in ownership and production portfolios could influence speciality ingredient availability, supplier relationships and long-term sourcing strategies.

SCHOTT Pharma India marks a new chapter, building on its strong national presence and global capabilities
Spotlight Wire Synopsis
New identity reinforces the company’s focus on innovation, customer partnerships and pharmaceutical drug containment and delivery solutions 
Follow us 
Spotlight Wire Last Updated: Oct 29, 2026, 11:02:04 AM IST

The pharmaceutical and biotech industries continue to place growing emphasis on the quality, reliability and precision of drug containment and delivery solutions, making strong local expertise and global capabilities increasingly important. Reflecting this evolving landscape and its continued commitment to the Indian market, SCHOTT Poonawalla Private Limited will become SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, effective 28 October 2026. The change marks a new chapter for the business, more clearly aligning its identity with the global SCHOTT Pharma organisation while bringing together its established manufacturing footprint, long-standing customer relationships and deep understanding of the Indian market with SCHOTT Pharma’s global expertise, innovation and scientific excellence.
For customers, partners and employees, this is a change in name, not a change in commitment. There is no change in ownership, management, employees, business strategy, operations, products, services or existing customer commitments.
The transition reinforces SCHOTT Pharma India’s long-term commitment to customers in India and international markets, while creating a stronger and more consistent connection to the global SCHOTT Pharma brand.
Building on a heritage of more than 140 years, the new identity brings the company’s heritage and future ambition under one global name, reflecting the values that continue to define SCHOTT Pharma: innovation, quality, scientific excellence and trust.
SCHOTT Pharma India represents both continuity and progress: the same trusted business, capabilities and relationships, now with an identity that more clearly reflects the present and the future of the business. .
Roy Joseph, CEO & Managing Director, SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited , said, “SCHOTT Pharma India represents the next chapter of our journey, combining our strength in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global innovation and expertise. We see significant opportunities to build on our capabilities, deepen collaboration with pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners, and advance drug containment and delivery solutions. As we move forward, our focus remains on growing with our customers and contributing to the safe and reliable delivery of critical therapies to patients worldwide.”

“ SCHOTT Pharma India plays a critical role in patient care. With more than 3 billion containers produced annually, this company enables around 7,000 injections to reach patients every minute,” said Dr. Christian Mias, CEO of SCHOTT Pharma AG & Co. KGaA , SCHOTT Pharma India’s major shareholder. “ The name change from SCHOTT Poonawalla to SCHOTT Pharma India reinforces our strategic partnership and confirms our long-term commitment to India as a key pharma hub .”
The new identity builds on the company’s strong foundation in India. During the COVID-19 pandemic, its pharmaceutical vials supported more than 4.3 billion vaccine doses worldwide, including 3 billion doses in India. As India’s only manufacturer of glass pre-fillable syringes and sterile formats, the company also strengthens local supply capabilities. Furthermore, the company continues to invest significantly towards manufacturing capacity expansions of pre-fillable syringes and cartridges, strengthening its ability to support the rapidly evolving needs of biologics, biosimilars, GLP-1-based treatments and other advanced injectable therapies.
Looking ahead, SCHOTT Pharma India will focus on expanding capabilities across pharmaceutical drug containment and drug delivery solutions, driving innovation through closer customer collaboration, and strengthening operational excellence and sustainability. These priorities will support the company as it responds to the evolving needs of pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies while contributing to India’s growing role in the global pharmaceutical value chain.

content_text:
Corning's Generative AI-Related Sales More Than Double, but Morgan Stanley Cuts Target
Morgan Stanley raised its core earnings forecasts for 2026 and 2027 but kept an Equal-weight rating, identifying margin improvement as a test for a more positive view.
By Token Post Published Oct 29, 2026, 12:23 AM EDT 
Save Share 
Optical fiber strands curve across a layered glass surface / TokenPost.ai Morgan Stanley lowered its Corning price target to $155 from $165 while raising its core earnings forecasts for 2026 and 2027. In its Oct. 28 analysis, the bank identified stronger margins and profit conversion as tests for taking a more positive view.
Corning's optical communications business brought in $2.38 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 44% from a year earlier. Enterprise sales increased 84%, and generative AI-related sales more than doubled. Carrier revenue grew 4%.
Customer advances added $639 million to operating cash flow year to date, while free cash flow exceeded $2 billion. Long-term customer agreements support most growth-related capital spending. The advances provide cash before equipment and capacity begin generating sales, but Corning still must deliver products under those agreements and improve production efficiency.
Solar revenue climbed 37% from a year earlier to $436 million, roughly unchanged from the prior quarter. The business recorded a $7 million net loss as silicon wafer and module production ramp-ups lagged expectations and start-up expenses weighed on profit.
Variable compensation remained above normal in the third quarter, with most of the pressure outside optical communications. Management expects the expenses to stabilize in the fourth quarter and reset in 2027. Glass innovation revenue fell 3% to $1.51 billion, while net profit declined 10%. Higher memory prices weighed on consumer demand; display price increases are expected to contribute more in 2027.
Morgan Stanley raised its 2026 core revenue estimate to $19.4 billion from $19.3 billion and its core earnings-per-share estimate to $3.37 from $3.28. For 2027, it lifted core revenue to $23.2 billion from $22.8 billion and core earnings per share to $4.37 from $4.21. The bank maintained its Equal-weight rating.
The lower target reflects a reduced price-to-earnings multiple based on 2028 earnings: about 28 times, down from about 30 times. Morgan Stanley’s analysis said shrinking valuation multiples for AI-related stocks offset the higher earnings forecasts.
The bank identified sustained improvement in optical communications margins, strong profit conversion from added sales, and stabilization in solar and auto businesses as tests for a more positive view. It expects more substantial demand for optical links within AI clusters to build gradually in the second half of 2027. Risks include slower AI capital spending, delayed production ramps and continued weakness outside optical communications.

Related To: Mouser

3 min read

Courtesy of Mouser
Infineon Technologies XENSIV™ BGT60CUTR13AIP Radar Sensor 
October 13, 2026 – Mouser Electronics , Inc., the authorized global distributor with the newest electronic components and industrial automation products, is now stocking the XENSIV™ BGT60CUTR13AIP radar sensor from Infineon Technologies . 
The XENSIV BGT60CUTR13AIP sensor provides ultra-wideband FMCW operation in a single-chip solution. This sensor offers advanced sensing capabilities with high precision and ultra-low power consumption. The new XENSIV BGT60CUTR13AIP 60 GHz CMOS radar sensor includes on-chip processing powered by a hardware accelerator, providing customers the flexibility to access either raw or pre-processed data. By handling radar processing on-chip, Infineon’s solution offloads the host processor and enables a more efficient system architecture, enabling smaller form factors and cost efficiency.  This sensor-integrated hardware sequencer with a Finite State Machine (FSM) offers the user full flexibility in configuring chirps and timing. The embedded motion/presence detection block, with a low false-alarm rate, further reduces system power by waking external hosts via a dedicated interrupt pin.
Typical applications include monitors, smart speakers, air conditioners, doorbells, sleep trackers, baby monitors, and security cameras and video doorbells.
To learn more, visit https://www.mouser.com/en/new/infineon/infineon-bgt60cutr13aip-radar-sensor/ . For more Mouser news and our latest new product introductions, visit https://www.mouser.com/newsroom/ .
 
As a global authorized distributor, Mouser offers the world's widest selection of the newest semiconductors and electronic components — in stock and ready to ship. According to Reuters, the investment strengthens Rio Tinto's position in the global lithium market as demand increases for minerals used in electric vehicles and battery storage systems.
The company ranked fourth among publicly listed mining groups by market capitalisation in October 2026, with an estimated valuation of $139.4 billion.

Rio Tinto expands lithium production in Argentina
Sal de Vida is expected to produce 15,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent annually, while the Fénix 1B expansion will contribute another 10,000 tonnes once both facilities reach full capacity.
Rio Tinto is also developing its Rincón project in Argentina's Salta province, targeting annual production capacity of 60,000 tonnes as part of its broader ambition to reach 200,000 tonnes of global lithium capacity by 2028.
Speaking at the inauguration, chief executive Simon Trott outlined the company's production ambitions.
"We live in an era in which the world needs more lithium. At Rio Tinto, we have set ourselves the goal of reaching 200,000 tons of annual production capacity, with opportunities to raise that figure much higher," Trott said.

The expansion relies partly on direct lithium extraction technology, which can shorten processing times compared with conventional evaporation methods, although questions remain about operating costs and commercial scalability.
Rio Tinto's investments extend across Africa
Beyond Argentina, Rio Tinto is advancing its estimated $6.2 billion funding commitment to Guinea's Simandou iron ore project, one of Africa's largest mining and infrastructure developments.
The investment forms part of an $11.6 billion programme covering the SimFer mine and associated railway and port infrastructure.
Simandou is designed to support annual exports of up to 120 million tonnes of iron ore at full capacity, with Rio Tinto's SimFer joint venture responsible for blocks three and four, targeting 60 million tonnes.

Meanwhile, Rio Tinto approved a $473 million investment in March 2026 to restart the Zulti South mineral sands project at Richards Bay Minerals in South Africa.
The project, suspended since 2020, is expected to extend operations until 2050, with initial commercial production scheduled for late 2028.
Beyond Guinea and South Africa, the mining group also maintains mineral sands operations in Madagascar through QIT Madagascar Minerals, which produces ilmenite for international industrial markets.
The investments span different commodity markets, with Rio Tinto's Argentine operations focused on lithium for battery manufacturing, while its African projects supply iron ore and minerals used in construction, manufacturing and other industries.
