title: South Korea's East-West Power Weighs Rescue Role in Anma Offshore Wind After Equis Exit - BigGo Finance
query: ("Siemens-Gamesa" OR "Siemens Gamesa") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
South Korea's East-West Power Weighs Rescue Role in Anma Offshore Wind After Equis Exit
Add preferred source 
South Korea's Korea East-West Power has begun reviewing a potential equity investment in the 532 MW Anma Offshore Wind project off Yeonggwang, South Jeolla Province, after Singapore-based Equis was left stranded by the collapse of its controlling-stake sale talks. The state-owned utility plans to send requests for proposals to accounting firms soon to select advisers, examining structures including buying existing shares, subscribing to new shares and taking over shareholder loans. It says it has a stake as a counterparty to the project's renewable energy certificate (REC) sales contract and needs to assess whether the project can be carried out. The project company's borrowings more than doubled to 268.2 billion won (approximately $199.7 million) at the end of last year and it posted an operating loss of 42.6 billion won (approximately $31.7 million), while suppliers including Siemens Gamesa, SK Oceanplant, LS Cable & System and CS Wind have walked away.
Key Elements 
Korea East-West Power Anma Offshore Wind Equis Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) Korea Midland Power Hoban Industrial Korea Development Bank CS Wind Daemyung Energy Siemens Gamesa SK Oceanplant LS Cable & System Anma Island in Yeonggwang 
South Korea's Korea East-West Power has emerged as a candidate to buy a stake in the Anma Offshore Wind project off Yeonggwang, South Jeolla Province, after Singapore-based investor Equis put its controlling stake up for sale only to see negotiations collapse. Attention is focused on whether a South Korean state-owned power generator will step in as rescuer for the 532 MW project, which faces being stranded as its largest shareholder withdraws and its supply chain falls apart.
According to investment banking sources, East-West Power is reviewing the possibility of acquiring a stake in Anma Offshore Wind. The company will soon send requests for proposals (RFPs) to South Korean and foreign accounting firms to begin selecting advisers. The move is aimed at launching a review of various deal structures, including buying existing shares held by current shareholders, participating in a new share issue, and taking over loans extended by existing shareholders.
The reason East-West Power is eyeing the project is its existing contractual relationship. Anma Offshore Wind was selected in the South Korean government's competitive wind power tender in 2024 and signed a renewable energy certificate (REC) sales contract in September last year. East-West Power is one of the generators, along with Korea Midland Power, that joined the contract. The company says that as a contract counterparty it has an interest in examining how far the project progresses and whether the contract can be fulfilled going forward.
Anma Offshore Wind is a project to build a 532 MW generation complex in waters near Anma Island in Yeonggwang County, South Jeolla Province. The plan centers on installing 38 wind turbines of 14 MW each, with total project cost estimated at about 4.9 trillion won (approximately $3.6 billion). Equis is a Singapore-based investor that develops and invests in energy and infrastructure assets in the Asia-Pacific region, and as of the end of last year it was the largest shareholder with a 78.09% stake in Anma Offshore Wind. The remaining shares are held by Hoban Industrial (6.64%), Korea Development Bank (6.13%), CS Wind (4.38%), Daemyung Energy (4.11%) and Daemyung GC (0.65%).
The background to Equis's sale is cited as the funding burden swollen by project delays and uncertainty over profitability. Because the project site overlaps with a weapons testing area used by the South Korean Agency for Defense Development (ADD), consultations with the South Korean Ministry of National Defense on military operational suitability and procedures for permits to occupy and use public waters dragged on for a long time, pushing back the start of construction and the schedule for closing project financing (PF). Military consultations are said to have been largely resolved since then, but financial costs and project expenses snowballed as permitting was delayed. Industry analysts say securing project viability became difficult as a relatively low bid price was combined with rising PF interest rates and exchange rate volatility.
To recover its investment, Equis had been negotiating a stake sale with Danish offshore wind investor Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) since late last year. However, the two sides reportedly failed to narrow differences over the acquisition price, project costs, repayment of borrowings to the lender group and conditions for financial close. According to foreign media reports, CIP considered withdrawing its investment commitment, citing differences in corporate valuation amid macroeconomic uncertainty, and the $2.5 billion (about 3.4 trillion won) borrowing that Equis was seeking to arrange is also in doubt.
The project company's financial condition has also deteriorated rapidly. Borrowings at the end of last year stood at 268.2 billion won (approximately $199.7 million), more than double the 124.5 billion won (approximately $92.7 million) at the end of the previous year. Over the same period, the operating loss widened to 42.6 billion won (approximately $31.7 million) from 37 billion won (approximately $27.6 million), and the net loss widened to 40.2 billion won (approximately $29.9 million) from 36.2 billion won (approximately $27.0 million). Cash flow from operating activities also posted a net outflow of 50 billion won (approximately $37.2 million) as funds were deployed for acquisitions of tangible assets and other items during the development stage.
Item End-2024 End-2025 
Borrowings 124.5 billion won 268.2 billion won 
Operating loss 37 billion won 42.6 billion won 
Net loss 36.2 billion won 40.2 billion won 
Note: Based on the Anma Offshore Wind project company
The burden of restarting the project has grown further with the departure of the supply chain. Turbine supplier Siemens Gamesa terminated its supply contract in April last year, citing the expiration of the contract period. SK Oceanplant, which had a contract to supply substructures, halted performance at the request of the ordering party, and LS Cable & System's subsea cable supply contract was also canceled. CS Wind has also pulled out of the project.
Whether East-West Power steps in could also affect the landscape of South Korea's offshore wind industry. One of the large offshore wind projects the South Korean government is seeking to foster to expand renewable energy supply simultaneously faces two tasks: replacing its largest shareholder and rebuilding its supply chain. Expectations are that if a state-owned power generator buys a stake, continuity in fulfilling the REC contract can be secured and orders for new turbines, substructures and cables can be placed again. On the other hand, some argue it is inappropriate for a state-owned company to inject funds when project viability has deteriorated, and the due diligence results after advisers are selected are expected to be a watershed.
How the deal structure is designed is also a key issue. Buying Equis's existing shares would require handling existing shareholders' loans and obtaining consent from the lender group, while participating in a new share issue would require consultations with existing shareholders over the size of the capital increase and stake dilution. Whichever card East-West Power chooses, the conditions for financial close on the 4.9 trillion won (approximately $3.6 billion) project will inevitably have to be renegotiated, analysts say.

title: French firm Safran helps build aircraft wings of the future in UK factory - France 24
query: ("Safran" OR "Safran Group") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
French firm Safran helps build aircraft wings of the future in UK factory
Wolverhampton (United Kingdom) (AFP) – For the French aerospace company Safran the future runs through a century-old factory in Britain where it aims to manufacture mechanisms key for the folding wings that will enable the next-generation of Airbus planes to meet ambitious fuel reduction targets. 
Issued on: 28/10/2026 - 17:26 
3 min Reading time 
Share 
French firm Safran is looking to the future with its state-of-the-art production at a UK factory © STEPHANE DE SAKUTIN / AFP/File 
These new thinner and folding wings will require twice as many small motors, or actuators, that control the movement of an aircraft's movable surfaces.
Behind the red-brick facades at the plant in Wolverhampton, western England -- once typical of the UK's industrial heartlands -- Safran is developing its new business of actuation systems.
Previously better known as an aircraft engine manufacturer, the pivot follows its 2025 acquisition of the flight controls and actuation activities of US-based Collins Aerospace for $1.8 billion.
Actuation refers to the mechanisms that control the movement of wings and surfaces, allowing an aircraft to climb, descend, bank, or turn. 
Their proper functioning is essential for maintaining the aircraft's trajectory and ensuring flight safety.
"It was the last critical piece of equipment which Safran was lacking," said Franck Saudo, president of Safran Electronics & Defense.
Safran also manufactures landing gear, aircraft seats, and lavatories.
The Wolverhampton plant, opened in 1903 and which employs more than 1,500 people, is a key site among the 11 facilities acquired by Safran from Collins Aerospace.
In the defence sector, the site manufactures actuation systems for missiles and for the weapons-bay doors of the F-35.
According to Saudo, this technology helps preserve the stealth capabilities of the American fighter jet.
Less fuel
Airbus plans to launch the successor to its best-selling A320 family of single-aisle medium-haul aircraft around 2030 with 20 to 30 percent better fuel efficiency than current models.
Safran is seeking to contribute to this fuel savings with its wing actuators.
These mechanisms are used, among other things, to deploy wing flaps during the plane's landing approach, helping to slow the aircraft.
"When a bird lands, it spreads its feathers to increase the size of its wings. An aircraft does exactly the same thing," Saudo explained.
For the so-called wing of tomorrow -- a longer, folding wing being developed by Airbus in Britain -- twice as many actuators will be needed, he noted.
Flight tests of this experimental new wing, which is longer and lighter to maximise aerodynamic efficiency and reduce fuel burn, are scheduled to begin this year.
Another challenge is the limited space. Since the wing is thinner, there is less room for actuators, which must therefore be smaller.
This innovative wing structure means the aircraft would exceed the current maximum wingspan limit set by airports of 36 meters (118 feet) by 4.5 meters on each side.
Actuators would therefore also be needed to fold the wing tips while the aircraft is taxiing on the ground.
Today actuators are predominantly hydraulic. But in the next generation of aircraft about half are expected to be electric, making them lighter.
The acquisition of Collins, a hydraulic systems specialist, has allowed Safran to combine that expertise with its own strengths in electrical systems.
Open fans
To prepare for increased production rates, a robot installed a year ago now assembles gearbox units.
Other robots are used in the manufacture of metal parts, but many assembly operations are still performed by hand.
The innovative Rise open fan a joint production by Safran and GE Aeronautics which cuts fuel burn and carbon emissions © Thomas SAMSON / AFP/File 
"Humans are more agile," Eric Valentin, head of actuation, told AFP.
For the aircraft of tomorrow, Safran is also developing an "open fan" engine free of the nacelle or encasing, which traditionally encloses and protects the fan blades.
The company says this technology could reduce fuel consumption by 20 percent, but development on these fans is less advanced, with flight testing not expected until around 2029.
"Historically in aviation, the main driver of fuel-burn reduction was the engine," Bruno Fichefeux, Airbus head of future programs, told AFP at the Farnborough Airshow in July.
"Today, we realise that the engine remains a major contributor, but it's no longer the dominant contributor," he said.
"Wing shape delivers an equivalent contribution in terms of fuel-burn reduction."

content_text:
Schott Poonawalla now becomes Schott Pharma, as it strengthens presence in specialty glass market
1 min read 
1SXP 
Specialty glass company Schott Poonawalla Private Ltd will become Schott Pharma India Private Ltd, from Wednesday - strengthening its connection with German parent Schott Pharma, besides marking a new journey in the domestic market, it said. 
The new identity brings together the company’s strong manufacturing footprint, long-standing customer relationships and deep market expertise in India with Schott Pharma’s global capabilities, innovation and scientific excellence, it said, adding that there was no change in ownership, management, employees, business strategy, operations, products, services or existing customer commitments. 
The development comes at a time when media reports indicate that the company is taking steps to go in for an initial public offering. Last year, private equity firm TPG had acquired 35 per cent stake in Schott Poonawalla from Serum Institute of India (SII), following which Adar Poonawalla’s SII held a minority stake in the company. 
Responding to a businessline query on the shareholding pattern and the possible IPO, the company said, ‘the shareholding structure remains same, as it has always been. There is no change to the legal structure or operations of the organization except for the name being changed to Schott Pharma India’ 
Pharma hub “Schott Pharma India plays a critical role in patient care. With more than 3 billion containers produced annually, this company enables around 7,000 injections to reach patients every minute,” said Dr Christian Mias, CEO of Schott Pharma AG & Co, the India arm’s major shareholder. 
“The name change .... reinforces our strategic partnership and confirms our long-term commitment to India as a key pharma hub,” Mias added. 
Roy Joseph, CEO & Managing Director, Schott Pharma India Private Ltd, said, the company remained focussed on growing and contributing to the safe and reliable delivery of critical therapies to patients worldwide. 
The company said, during COVID-19, its pharmaceutical vials supported more than 4.3 billion vaccine doses worldwide, including 3 billion doses in India. 
“As India’s only manufacturer of glass pre-fillable syringes and sterile formats, the company also strengthens local supply capabilities. Furthermore, the company continues to invest significantly towards manufacturing capacity expansions of pre-fillable syringes and cartridges, strengthening their ability to support the rapidly evolving needs of biologics, biosimilars, GLP-1 based treatments and other advanced injectable therapies,” it said.

Albemarle (ALB) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price. 
The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 4. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower. 
While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise. 
Zacks Consensus Estimate 
This specialty chemicals company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $2.41 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +1368.4%. 
Revenues are expected to be $1.49 billion, up 14.2% from the year-ago quarter. 
Estimate Revisions Trend 
The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 21.37% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period. 
Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts. 
Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise 
Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for ALB Earnings Whisper 
Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction). 
The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier. 
Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only. 
A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP. 
Story Continues 
Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell). 
How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Albemarle? 
For Albemarle, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -5.79%. 
On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #3. 
So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Albemarle will beat the consensus EPS estimate. 
Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue? 
Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number. 
For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Albemarle would post earnings of $3.35 per share when it actually produced earnings of $3.75, delivering a surprise of +11.94%. 
Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates three times. 
Bottom Line 
An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss. 
That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported. 
Albemarle doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release. 
An Industry Player's Expected Results 
Another stock from the Zacks Chemical - Diversified industry, Innospec (IOSP), is soon expected to post earnings of $1.27 per share for the quarter ended September 2026. This estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +13.4%. Revenues for the quarter are expected to be $489.75 million, up 10.8% from the year-ago quarter. 
Over the last 30 days, the consensus EPS estimate for Innospec has been revised 1.1% down to the current level. Nevertheless, the company now has an Earnings ESP of -1.98%, reflecting a lower Most Accurate Estimate. 
This Earnings ESP, combined with its Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Innospec will beat the consensus EPS estimate. The company beat consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters.

Basf Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
Basf logo 
MarketBeat 
October 28, 2026 7 min read 
BAS.DE 
-0.79% 
BAS 
Key Points 
Interested in Basf Se? Here are five stocks we like better. 
Third-quarter performance improved: EBITDA before special items rose 15% year over year to €1.6 billion, driven by price increases, volume growth, stronger margins and lower fixed costs across all four core businesses. 
2026 outlook was modestly raised: BASF now expects EBITDA before special items of €7.4 billion–€7.8 billion, while maintaining its free-cash-flow forecast of €1.5 billion–€2.3 billion amid continued geopolitical and energy-market uncertainty. 
Capital discipline and portfolio actions continued: BASF reduced net debt by 20% year over year, lowered its capital-expenditure forecast, repurchased about €1.9 billion of shares and said Agricultural Solutions remains on track to be IPO-ready by mid-2027. 
Basf (ETR:BAS) reported higher third-quarter earnings before special items, supported by price increases, volume growth and lower fixed costs across its core businesses, while narrowing its full-year earnings outlook upward. 
EBITDA before special items rose 15% year over year to €1.6 billion in the third quarter, Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors Markus Kamieth said. He attributed the increase to stronger specific margins, solid volumes and restructuring-related cost reductions. All four core segments contributed to the improvement. 
→ Comfort Systems Earnings: AI Slowdown or More Growth Ahead? 
"BASF delivered another strong quarter with considerable growth in EBITDA before special items driven by all core businesses," Kamieth said. The company reported price increases across all core segments during the quarter, while Chemicals and Nutrition & Care made the strongest contributions to volume growth. 
Outlook Narrowed as Core Businesses Improve 
BASF now expects 2026 EBITDA before special items of between €7.4 billion and €7.8 billion, raising the lower end of its prior outlook and slightly increasing the upper end. The company maintained its free-cash-flow forecast of €1.5 billion to €2.3 billion, citing continued uncertainty around geopolitical and global economic developments, particularly their effects on oil and gas prices. 
→ A 70% Rally Isn't Chord Energy's Only Selling Point 
CFO Dirk Elvermann said the company expects Chemicals, Industrial Solutions and Nutrition & Care to post fourth-quarter earnings above the prior-year period. Materials is expected to be around the previous year's level, while Surface Technologies is expected to remain below it. 
Kamieth said the company remains cautious about the fourth quarter despite some improving economic indicators. He noted that energy prices had risen sharply and said markets are generally better supplied than during the second quarter, when supply-chain disruptions associated with the Middle East conflict supported pricing and volumes. 
Story Continues 
→ Not All Tech Is Getting Crushed: 5 Names Holding Up Through the AI Sell-Off 
On industry margins, Kamieth said BASF's portfolio had moved "significantly above the trough" but had not yet reached normalized or mid-cycle levels across the group. He said the company sees both upside and downside risks for 2027, though he expressed some optimism that conditions could improve. 
Cash Flow, Debt Reduction and Buybacks 
For the first nine months of 2026, EBITDA before special items increased by more than €900 million from the prior-year period to €6.4 billion. Cash fixed costs declined about 3% to €11.8 billion, while net income reached €5.2 billion, including a €3.5 billion after-tax disposal gain from the coatings transaction with Carlyle. 
Free cash flow for the nine-month period was negative €1 billion, compared with about negative €870 million a year earlier. Cash flow from operating activities fell to €823 million, primarily because net working-capital requirements increased by €1.5 billion. 
Elvermann said the working-capital increase reflected higher receivables from stronger sales and higher inventory values caused by elevated raw-material prices. He said BASF expects stronger cash collections in the fourth quarter, although the pace of inventory reduction will depend largely on feedstock prices. 
Payments for property, plant, equipment and intangible assets fell about €980 million to €1.9 billion in the first nine months. 
BASF now expects full-year capital expenditures of roughly €2.8 billion to €2.9 billion, clearly below its February forecast of €3.4 billion. 
Net debt was reduced 20% from the end of September 2025, and BASF expects it to reach about €15 billion by the end of 2026. 
Fitch confirmed BASF's single-A credit rating with a stable outlook. 
The company bought back approximately €1.9 billion of shares between Nov. 25 and Oct. 23, 2026, as part of a program of at least €4 billion announced in September 2024. BASF's equity ratio increased by nearly three percentage points to 47.2% despite the ongoing buyback program. 
Agricultural Solutions and Portfolio Actions 
Agricultural Solutions was a weaker area in the third quarter. Sales declined almost 20% to €1.4 billion, primarily because of lower volumes amid challenging conditions in South America and sales that had been brought forward into the second quarter ahead of an enterprise-resource-planning migration in the region. 
Pricing was also pressured by competition in South America. Elvermann said unfavorable weather conditions affected volumes in South America, Europe, Asia and North America. The company expects the business to strengthen seasonally in the fourth quarter and said it should perform broadly in line with the fourth quarter of 2025, though full-year earnings are still expected to be lower than last year. 
BASF said preparations for the planned initial public offering of Agricultural Solutions remain on track, with the business expected to be IPO-ready by mid-2027. The transition to separate legal entities and an industry-specific ERP system is largely complete. 
The company also highlighted portfolio proceeds, including around €1.3 billion from sales of Harbour Energy shares to date. BASF continues to hold about 16% of Harbour Energy's outstanding voting shares. Its coatings transaction with Carlyle generated net cash inflows of more than €6 billion, while the sale of Stahl Group's specialty coatings business to Henkel produced more than €250 million in cash proceeds through BASF's indirect stake. 
Evonik Discussion and Capital Discipline 
Kamieth addressed reports of a possible combination with Evonik, saying such a transaction could be strategically and financially compelling because the companies' portfolios and strengths complement one another. However, he emphasized that BASF would only pursue a deal if it creates value for shareholders. 
"Acquisitions are a could do, not a must do in our strategy," Kamieth said. He said the company would not overpay and remains committed to shareholder distributions of at least €12 billion between 2025 and 2028. 
BASF expects to continue smaller portfolio optimization measures but said investors should not expect anything "very significant" in terms of additional divestments. The company is also continuing restructuring efforts, having reduced employee positions by about 8,600 since January 2024, excluding divestiture-related reductions and workforce additions at its Zhanjiang Verbund site in China. 
About Basf (ETR:BAS) 
BASF SE operates as a chemical company worldwide. It operates through six segments: Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, Surface Technologies, Nutrition & Care, and Agricultural Solutions. The Chemicals segment provides petrochemicals and intermediates. The Materials segment offers advanced materials and their precursors for applications and systems comprising isocyanates, polyamides, and inorganic basic products, as well as specialties for plastics and plastics processing industries. The Industrial Solutions segment develops and markets ingredients and additives for industrial applications, such as polymer dispersions, resins, additives, electronic materials, and antioxidants for automotive, plastics, paints and coatings, electronics, and energy and resource industries.

content_text:
Breaking the Japanese monopoly grip, Korean display industry bets on new OLED technology
By KIM Nami 
Updated 
Oct 29, 2026, 
8:42 a.m. KST 
Published 
Oct 28, 2026, 
5:50 p.m. KST 
Korean companies spend 600 billion won annually on FMM purchases effectively monopolized by Japanese firms… LG Display develops new technology that eliminates the need for FMM
An LG Display-related product is on display at the 'K-Display 2026 Korea Display Industry Exhibition' at COEX in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. /NEWS1 photo by Lee Jong-soo 
Domestic display companies leading the global OLED (organic light-emitting diode) panel market have moved to reduce their dependence on a key component that has been effectively monopolized by Japan through a technological shift. 
They are pursuing both improved panel performance and technological self-reliance not only by domesticating Japanese-made components, but also by developing new processes that do not use the components themselves.
According to the electronics industry on Thursday, Japanese companies account for approximately 90% of the global FMM (fine metal mask) market. An FMM is a component made by drilling tens of millions of microscopic holes smaller than a human hair into a metal sheet thinner than paper. Much like a painter uses a stencil to spray paint, OLED red, green, and blue (RGB) light-emitting materials are deposited through these holes to form pixels.
Domestic companies lead the OLED panel market with approximately 70% market share. Since becoming the first in the world to sell large-size OLED TV panels in 2013, LG Display has expanded its business into monitors and achieved cumulative sales of 50 million large-size OLED panels. However, the supply chain for FMMs, a key component in OLED panel production, is effectively controlled by Japanese companies. Dependence on Japanese-made products is close to 100%.
In particular, Japan's DNP (Dai Nippon Printing) holds approximately 70% of the global FMM market, occupying a near-monopoly position. It is estimated that domestic companies spend at least 60 billion won annually on FMM purchases from DNP alone. An industry official explained that DNP holds the upper hand in supply negotiations based on its high market share and technological capabilities.
Effect of LG Display's FLiPP technology compared to existing FMM process / Graphic by Kim Hyeon-jung 
Japan's influence is also formidable in the raw materials sector for FMMs. 'Invar,' a thin film of iron-nickel alloy that serves as the core material for FMMs, is supplied primarily by Japan's Proterial (formerly Hitachi Metals). 
In the equipment market for depositing light-emitting materials using FMMs, Canon Tokki, a subsidiary of Japan's Canon, also exerts strong influence. A single Canon Tokki deposition machine costs well over 1 trillion won (based on 8.6-generation lines). Japanese companies thus exert strong influence across the entire spectrum of materials, components and equipment that are central to OLED production.
Domestic display companies have begun developing next-generation OLED processes that do not use FMMs in order to change this supply chain structure. A representative technology is 'FLiPP' developed by LG Display. 
FLiPP is a process that forms RGB pixels using photolithography technology, which is used in semiconductor manufacturing, instead of the conventional FMM. It involves depositing organic light-emitting material across the entire substrate and then using light to remove unnecessary parts. Because it does not use an FMM, it can reduce dependence on key Japanese-made components.
The effect on panel performance improvement is also significant. According to LG Display, utilizing FLiPP can raise the aperture ratio from approximately 42% in existing processes to 65%. 
The aperture ratio is the proportion of the total pixel area that actually emits light. As the light-emitting area expands, brightness can be increased by up to 1.6 times or lifespan extended by up to 2.4 times compared to conventional methods. A reduction in power consumption is also expected.
Furthermore, the existing FMM method has a problem where the center of the metal mask sags downward as its size increases. Consequently, the existing FMM method involves the constraint that large glass substrates must be cut for use. In contrast, FLiPP can utilize an entire 8.5-generation mother glass sheet measuring 2.2 meters wide and 2.5 meters long. 
Theoretically, it can produce everything from 1-inch-class smartwatches to ultra-large TVs of 100 inches or more using a single process. Material utilization efficiency can be raised from 40% to 74%.
The significance of FLiPP lies in changing the approach to technological self-reliance itself. It secures a new production process that does not require the component, going beyond merely domesticating components imported from overseas. 
LG Display is first pushing for application in IT products such as laptops and monitors, with plans to expand the scope of application according to future customer demand. Samsung Display is also researching and developing next-generation OLED patterning technology that does not use FMMs.
However, it is expected that new processes will be difficult to completely replace the existing FMM method in the short term. Investment burdens associated with introducing new equipment, securing mass production yields, and stabilizing the process are cited as challenges to be resolved. 
An industry official said, "It will be difficult to introduce non-FMM methods into all OLED production immediately," adding, "Even if the new technology enters the mass production stage, it is highly likely that it will run in parallel with existing FMM processes for a while."

VCU School of Nursing and VCU Health honored with national award for exemplary academic-practice collaboration
The American Association of Colleges of Nursing recognized the VCU partnership for building strong connections between academics and clinical care.
Share this story
Share on X (Twitter) 
Share on Facebook 
Share on LinkedIn 
Print page 
By Joe Schilling
School of Nursing 
The American Association of Colleges of Nursing has awarded the Virginia Commonwealth University School of Nursing and VCU Health System the prestigious 2026 AACN Exemplary Academic-Practice Partnership Award. This national honor recognizes an integrated model between the two institutions that bridges clinical care, academic inquiry and community health. 
The AACN Exemplary Academic-Practice Partnership Award celebrates member institutions and healthcare systems that demonstrate highly productive, collaborative relationships aligned with the eight AACN/American Organization for Nursing Leadership Guiding Principles and the 2021 AACN Essentials: Core Competencies for Professional Nursing Education. 
In an era marked by nationwide clinical staffing shortages and shifting healthcare demands, the VCU partnership stands out as a national benchmark — proving how a research-intensive urban university and Virginia’s largest safety-net academic health system can build a bidirectional ecosystem where clinical practice informs the classroom, faculty scholarship elevates bedside care and joint initiatives directly improve patient outcomes.
“Earning this award is a significant achievement and reflects the strength of our collaboration with our School of Nursing colleagues,” said Amber Balzer, DNP, director of advanced practice professional development and fellowship for VCU Health. “The application process was extensive and truly a team effort, requiring thoughtful contributions from partners across both organizations.”
The partnership rests on deliberately dismantling traditional academic and clinical silos. VCU Health operates VCU Medical Center , an urban academic medical center, as well as VCU Health Community Memorial Hospital and VCU Health Tappahannock Hospital . Less than three blocks away stands the VCU School of Nursing, a nationally ranked institution educating undergraduate, master’s, Doctor of Nursing Practice and Ph.D. scholars.
Formalized in 2021, the partnership’s executive governance structure includes quarterly strategic sessions among the School of Nursing dean, chief nursing officers, associate chief nursing officers and the associate vice president of advanced practice providers, along with monthly faculty practice assemblies. To ensure alignment across all clinical environments, 70 key stakeholders across 14 focus groups co-designed the shared leadership framework. 
“Quarterly gatherings of our respective leadership teams are crucial to building trust between the School of Nursing and VCU Health and to helping ensure the needs of both institutions are met,” said Patricia Kinser, Ph.D., dean of the VCU School of Nursing.
Central to this collaboration is a bidirectional model: numerous School of Nursing faculty members maintain active clinical practices embedded across VCU Health units. At the same time, the school’s appointment, promotion and tenure guidelines formally recognize clinical practice excellence, allowing five faculty members to earn academic promotion through clinical and scholarly excellence.
“Academic-practice partnerships cannot simply be administrative agreements on paper; they must live and breathe at the bedside and in the lecture hall,” said Lana Sargent , Ph.D., associate dean of practice and community engagement in the School of Nursing. “Our tripartite mission of teaching, scholarship and service works because the exchange is truly bidirectional. When our faculty practice inside a Level I trauma center, they bring current clinical complexities and evidence-based innovations straight back to our students. In turn, our students and scholars analyze real-time health system data to solve operational challenges, advance health equity, and elevate the standard of patient care. We are educating nurses in the exact environment where they will lead and heal.”
The collaboration has transformed nursing workforce development across Central Virginia. Between 2021 and 2026, the undergraduate nursing programs doubled, now training more than 650 undergraduate students, most of whom rotate directly through VCU Health facilities. At the graduate level, 237 health system clinicians have mentored 727 advanced practice students, completing 77,890 clinical hours — including 17,899 hours overseen directly through faculty practice.
To foster retention and career mobility for frontline healthcare workers, the partners established a guaranteed admission pathway into the RN-to-BS for VCU Health System registered nurses holding associate degrees . VCU Health supports these nurses by reimbursing application fees and providing tuition assistance, while the School of Nursing maintains dedicated web portals and streamlined application reviews.
After being hired into the health system, new graduates enter an enterprise-wide nurse residency program that recently earned a 10-year Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education accreditation. With School of Nursing faculty serving on the advisory board and guiding curriculum delivery, the program enrolled 318 nurse residents in CY2025 alone — nearly a third of whom graduated from VCU. The program boasts an 87.1% one-year retention rate (up from 86% in CY2024), with 90.5% of participants successfully advancing to Clinical Nurse II within 24 months, vastly outpacing national retention averages. 
"The AACN Exemplary Academic-Practice Partnership Award is undeniable proof of our shared commitment to measurable outcomes and practice readiness,” said Mary Marshman, DNP, chief nursing officer at VCU Medical Center. “Thanks to this partnership between the School of Nursing and VCU Health, graduates enter our workforce with clinical judgment, hands-on experience, and knowledge of VCU Health nursing practices that ensures they are ready to contribute effectively from day one.”
Beyond workforce numbers, the partnership drives healthcare quality improvement. DNP projects linked directly to health system strategic priorities have expanded from six in spring 2023 to 55 projected through 2027.
These efforts have also led to substantial financial impacts through cost-saving for the health system and increased patient satisfaction metrics. Demonstrating the health system’s commitment to advanced practice leadership, the health system appointed an advanced practice provider as its first associate vice president of quality and safety .
Scholarly dissemination has flourished concurrently. Collaborative teams have produced more than 30 conference presentations, 46 grand rounds sessions, six jointly funded research grants totaling over $128,000 and seven peer-reviewed publications in journals such as the Journal of the American Association of Nurse Practitioners, the American Journal of Critical Care and The American Surgeon.
The partnership’s impact reaches deep into medically underserved communities across the region. Through the Mobile Health and Wellness Program , faculty and nursing students deliver preventive and chronic disease care across eight rural and urban communities.
The 2026 AACN Exemplary Academic-Practice Partnership Award affirms the VCU School of Nursing and VCU Health’s shared vision: an academic-practice model that transforms nursing education into measurable community wellness and bedside excellence.

SCHOTT Poonawalla renamed SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited 
The name change takes effect on October 28, 2026, with no changes to ownership, management, operations, products or services
Latest Updates 
By EP News Bureau 
On Oct 28, 2026 
0 167 
Share 
SCHOTT Poonawalla Private Limited will become SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited with effect from October 28, 2026, marking a new chapter in the company’s journey and strengthening its connection with the global SCHOTT Pharma organisation. 
The new identity reflects the India business’s place within SCHOTT Pharma’s global network and its role in advancing drug containment and delivery solutions for the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries. It brings together the company’s manufacturing footprint, customer relationships and market expertise in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global capabilities, innovation and scientific expertise. 
The company stated that the change is limited to its name and does not affect its ownership, management, employees, business strategy, operations, products, services or existing customer commitments. 
The transition reinforces SCHOTT Pharma India’s commitment to customers in India and international markets, while establishing a consistent connection with the global SCHOTT Pharma brand. 
Building on a heritage of more than 140 years, the new identity brings the company’s heritage and future ambitions under one global name, reflecting SCHOTT Pharma’s values of innovation, quality, scientific expertise and trust. 
Commenting on the development, Roy Joseph, CEO and Managing Director, SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, said, “SCHOTT Pharma India represents the next chapter of our journey, combining our strength in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global innovation and expertise. We see significant opportunity to build on our capabilities, deepen collaboration with pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners, and advance drug containment and delivery solutions. As we move forward, our focus remains on growing with our customers and contributing to the safe and reliable delivery of critical therapies to patients worldwide.” 
Dr Christian Mias, CEO of SCHOTT Pharma AG & Co. KGaA, SCHOTT Pharma India’s major shareholder, said, “SCHOTT Pharma India plays a critical role in patient care. With more than 3 billion containers produced annually, this company enables around 7,000 injections to reach patients every minute. The name change from SCHOTT Poonawalla to SCHOTT Pharma India reinforces our strategic partnership and confirms our long-term commitment to India as a key pharma hub.” 
The new identity builds on the company’s operations in India. During the COVID-19 pandemic, its pharmaceutical vials supported more than 4.3 billion vaccine doses worldwide, including 3 billion doses in India. 
As India’s only manufacturer of glass pre-fillable syringes and sterile formats, the company also contributes to local supply capabilities. It continues to invest in manufacturing capacity expansions for pre-fillable syringes and cartridges to support the requirements of biologics, biosimilars, GLP-1-based treatments and other injectable therapies. 
Going forward, SCHOTT Pharma India will focus on expanding its capabilities in pharmaceutical drug containment and delivery solutions, driving innovation through customer collaboration, and strengthening operational excellence and sustainability. These priorities will support the company in responding to the needs of pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies and contribute to India’s role in the global pharmaceutical value chain.

content_text:
What NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
4 min read 
NXPI 
Why NXP Semiconductors Could Be the AI Stock Everyone Is Missing 
NXP Semiconductors NXPI reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.79 billion, up 19% from a year earlier and 8% sequentially, as automotive, industrial and data-center-related demand supported growth across its business. Revenue increased 22% year over year excluding the MEMS sensor business. 
President and CEO Rafael Sotomayor said every region posted double-digit year-over-year growth. Automotive and industrial, which together represent roughly one-third of company revenue, were key contributors, alongside continued strength in data-center infrastructure. 
These 3 AI Stocks Just Crushed Earnings: Still Time To Buy? 
Non-GAAP operating margin rose 330 basis points from a year earlier to 37.1%, while non-GAAP earnings per share increased 35% to $4.20. The company generated $1.21 billion in free cash flow during the quarter, equal to approximately 32% of revenue. 
Automotive crosses $2 billion 
Automotive revenue surpassed $2 billion for the first time in the quarter. Revenue in the segment was up 17% year over year excluding sensors, driven by content gains in software-defined vehicle, or SDV, products despite what Sotomayor described as a “flattish” vehicle-production environment. 
Why NXP Semiconductors’ Post-Earnings Dip Could Be a Buying Window 
NXP said SDV revenue was running at an annualized rate above $1.5 billion in the third quarter and remains on track to reach its $2 billion target in 2027. The company expects the transition from domain-based vehicle architectures to zonal and centralized computing to increase semiconductor content per vehicle by two to three times compared with current architectures. 
The company plans to begin shipping its next-generation SDV processors, including the S32K5 zonal and S32N central-compute platforms, in 2027. Sotomayor said RV Tech, the Volkswagen-Rivian joint venture, had standardized its zonal platform on NXP’s S32K5 across both companies. NXP also expects its first S32K5 shipments in China as early as the first quarter of 2027. 
During the quarter, NXP secured its first S32K5 design win in humanoid robotics with what Sotomayor described as a leading U.S. global technology company. He said the same components used in software-defined vehicles—including central compute, sensing, networking and secure control—are moving into robotics and other intelligent edge systems. 
In response to analyst questions, management said it had not seen broad-based automotive restocking. Sotomayor said customer visibility had improved as lead times extended and automakers became more directly involved in providing demand guidance. CFO Bill Betz added that NXP serves about 40% of automotive distribution directly, giving the company close visibility into that channel. 
Industrial and data center momentum 
Industrial and IoT revenue was $802 million, up 39% from a year earlier. The industrial portion of the business grew nearly 50%, led by data centers, factory automation and healthcare, and now accounts for about 70% of industrial IoT revenue, according to the company. 
NXP said AI-enabled processors are expected to represent approximately 15% of industrial IoT processor revenue in 2026, more than double the prior year’s level. Its Ara discrete neural processing unit is gaining traction in industrial automation and automotive AI applications, with volume production anticipated in 2028. 
Communication infrastructure and other revenue rose 54% year over year to $503 million, supported by data-center and secure-card demand. NXP now expects its data-center revenue to exceed the more than $500 million outlook it previously gave for 2026 and to surpass $1 billion in a couple of years. 
Sotomayor said NXP is focused on the data-center control plane, including top-of-rack switches, controllers, processors, secure elements and interfaces. The company views networking, security and processing requirements as increasing alongside higher-performance data-center infrastructure. 
Mobile revenue was $411 million, down 4% from a year earlier. 
Margins, cash returns and fourth-quarter outlook 
Third-quarter non-GAAP gross margin was 58.6%, up 160 basis points year over year, reflecting improved factory utilization and revenue growth, Betz said. The company ended the period with $3.94 billion in cash and $10.98 billion in debt, resulting in a net leverage ratio of 1.3 times. 
Inventory days declined to 148 from 156 in the second quarter, including about 13 days of pre-built inventory associated with planned front-end factory consolidations. NXP expects to have about 15 days of pre-built inventory at the end of 2026. 
The board authorized an additional $5 billion for share repurchases, bringing total authorization to approximately $6.3 billion. NXP returned $1.7 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks over the trailing 12 months and said it plans to accelerate repurchases in the fourth quarter and in 2027. 
For the fourth quarter, NXP forecast revenue of $3.85 billion, plus or minus $100 million, representing growth of 15% year over year and 2% sequentially. The outlook implies 18% annual growth excluding the MEMS sensor business. 
Automotive revenue is expected to rise in the low-double-digit percentage range year over year and low-single digits sequentially. 
Industrial and IoT revenue is projected to increase in the high-20% range from a year earlier. 
Mobile revenue is expected to decline in the mid-teens percentage range year over year. 
Communication infrastructure and other revenue is forecast to rise more than 50% year over year. 
NXP expects fourth-quarter non-GAAP gross margin of 59%, plus or minus 50 basis points, and non-GAAP operating margin of 37.5% at the midpoint. It forecast non-GAAP earnings per share of $4.36 at the midpoint, up 30% year over year. 
Looking into 2027, Betz said the company expects to continue delivering double-digit revenue growth, expand gross margin to 60%, and increase capital expenditures to about 5% of revenue as it adds back-end capacity and develops a new assembly and test facility in Malaysia for production in 2028. NXP also plans to realign its end-market revenue reporting beginning in 2027 and will host an investor day on March 3 in Boston. 
About NXP Semiconductors NXPI 
NXP Semiconductors N.V. is a global semiconductor company that develops technologies for automotive, industrial, communications infrastructure, mobile, and Internet of Things applications. The company provides processing, connectivity, security, sensing, and power-management solutions that help enable connected and automated systems. 
Its product portfolio includes microcontrollers and application processors, automotive networking and radar solutions, secure identification and authentication technologies, near-field communication products, radio-frequency power amplifiers, analog and mixed-signal devices, and wireless connectivity solutions.

NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) came out with quarterly earnings of $4.2 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.14 per share. This compares to earnings of $3.11 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items. 
This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +1.45%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this chipmaker would post earnings of $3.54 per share when it actually produced earnings of $3.61, delivering a surprise of +1.98%. 
Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times. 
NXP, which belongs to the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry, posted revenues of $3.79 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.41%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $3.17 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters. 
The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call. 
NXP shares have added about 13.3% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 12.1%. 
What's Next for NXP? 
While NXP has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock? 
There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately. 
Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions. 
Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for NXP was favorable. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to outperform the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here. 
It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $4.31 on $3.86 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $15.17 on $14.28 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

What We Thought of Boeing’s Earnings 
Boeing BA delivered 161 jets in the third quarter of 2026, just one more than a year ago, fueling 1% commercial revenue growth and a $700 million loss. Defense sales grew 15% and earned $492 million. Aftermarket services grew 4%, contributing $1 billion in operating profit.
Why it matters: We estimate that half of Boeing’s enterprise value is derived from its 737 product line. Increasing the rate at which the company can make and deliver these jets is the single biggest driver of its near- and long-term profitability and cash flow, and Boeing is working on upping its 737 output from 47 planes per month sometime in 2027.
Completion of flight testing and certification by the US Federal Aviation Administration of Boeing’s MAX-7 and MAX-10 variants of the 737 finally took place in late October, and we expect certification of the 777X soon.
Increasing the rate of production is proving tricky, and management pushed out its expectations of the rate of increase by about a year, resulting in an annual free cash flow target of $10 billion by 2029, rather than 2028.
The bottom line: We decreased our fair value estimate for wide-moat Boeing to $242 per share from $254, reflecting more gradual increases in 737 deliveries, revenue, and cash flow.
Investors disappointed by the moving goalpost traded Boeing’s stock down nearly 10% by midday Oct. 27, and the shares trade 30% below our revised fair value estimate. With a High Morningstar Uncertainty Rating, we would consider the shares a compelling value below $145.

By Rodney Jackson October 27, 2026

“God bless your hands,” was just one expression of gratitude for medical professionals from Carl R. Darnall Army Medical Center that helped support an Operation Panamanian partnership from late August to early September.
The team, comprising Army ophthalmologists, nurses, operating room technicians and patient administrators , performed more than 100 cataract surgeries at Hospital San Miguel Arcángel, helping Panamanians regain their vision and improve their quality of life.
Maj. Cameron Maxon and Maj. Shyam Patel, anesthesiologists; and Maj. Matthew Ricci, an ophthalmologist, represented the CRDAMC team
“From the surgeon’s standpoint, one of the main difficulties was the severity of the cataracts we were seeing,” said Ricci. “The cataracts were more severe than most we see in the United States, which made surgery more technically challenging.”
The collaboration with our Army nursing and anesthesia team and the local nurses and anesthesiologists made things easy for us and allowed us to focus solely on performing surgery, he added.
“Overall, it was an exceptional experience,” said Patel. “We made an impact on over 100 people directly, bonded with the local anesthesiologists and shared our various experiences and expertise.”
Cataracts, a clouding of the eye’s lens that can cause blurred vision and blindness, can significantly affect a person’s ability to perform everyday activities. Through the partnership program, the Army medical team provided surgical care to patients whose vision had been impaired by the condition for many years.
“Though not involved in the post-operative care as an anesthesiologist, I heard of all the gratitude from the various other ophthalmologists,” said Patel. “During the first week, one of the doctors informed me that a patient started crying as she was able to see for the first time in over 10 years. She was able to see her grandkids for the first time.”
Maxon, a father of three, felt the entire mission was defined as a success after treating a mother who had developed severe cataracts while undergoing chemotherapy for cancer. “A mother with children the same age as mine, hadn’t seen one of her children since they were an infant. Another child she hadn’t seen since birth,” said Maxon. “She said she could never thank us enough for restoring her vision and letting her finally see her babies.”
The mission demonstrated the value of collaboration among medical professionals and strengthened the partnership through the delivery of specialized care to the Panamanian community.
The team navigated a minor language barrier, a new environment, and new or unfamiliar equipment. By combining their expertise alongside local medical partners, the team demonstrated they were medically ready to perform cataract surgeries in a challenging environment, enhance their medical skills and support international medical cooperation.

A long-term shareholder who rules out any governance ambitions
BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) took note, on October 27, 2026, of a press release published the previous day by Applied Materials. In this statement, Applied announced that it had increased its strategic stake in the Dutch semiconductor assembly equipment manufacturer. According to the press release, Applied concluded an agreement intended to raise its stake to approximately 20% of Besi's outstanding shares, whose headquarters are located in Duiven, Netherlands.
Applied accompanied this announcement with three clarifications that frame its position. The group considers its investment in Besi as a long-term commitment. It does not intend to seek board representation in the company. It currently has no plans to acquire additional shares.
These statements have concrete significance for reading the shareholding structure. A stake expected to reach approximately one-fifth of the capital would make Applied Materials a significant shareholder in Besi's ownership structure. By forgoing a board seat and indicating it does not wish to increase further, Applied presents itself as a stable shareholder rather than as a player seeking to influence Besi's decisions.
Besi's press release reiterates these elements by explicitly citing Applied's statement as a source. Besi's ordinary shares are listed on Euronext Amsterdam under the symbol BESI, while its depositary receipts (Level 1 ADR) are traded on over-the-counter American markets under the symbol BESIY. Applied's new position therefore concerns a group whose value is tracked in both Europe and the United States.

The capital link is supported by an established industrial partnership. Besi and Applied have been working together since 2020 on the development and commercialization of integrated hybrid bonding production systems, intended for leading semiconductor manufacturers. This collaboration combines Applied's expertise in wafer-level chip manufacturing, upstream in the supply chain, with Besi's technologies in chip placement, interconnection, and assembly.
The partnership was recently expanded. Besi joined Applied's EPIC Center as an innovation partner. The joint work focuses on the next generation of three-dimensional integrated circuits, the integration of logic and memory, the scaling up of thermocompression bonding, as well as new wafer-to-wafer, chip-to-chip, and chip-to-panel assembly platforms.
Besi's Chief Executive Officer, Richard W. Blickman, welcomed this decision favorably. "We welcome Applied's increased strategic investment as further confirmation of Besi's strategy in hybrid bonding and wafer-level assembly," he stated, according to a translation of the press release. He added that the transaction highlights future areas of potential collaboration between the two companies, targeting next-generation artificial intelligence and photonics systems for leading customers in the industry.
An announcement following quarterly results publication and share price decline
This capital increase comes a few days after the publication of third-quarter results. On October 22, 2026, Besi reported revenue up 113.6% and quarterly net income of €107.2 million. Earnings per share came in at €1.33, against an average expectation of €1.30 from analysts, with the fourth quarter expected to remain stable.
On the market, the share has experienced a sharp decline in recent weeks. On October 15, 2026, the stock showed a decline close to 35% over one quarter. On October 23, 2026, it fell below its 150-day low, at €155.55, as several brokers, including JP Morgan and BofA, had lowered their price targets during the month.

Corning Earnings: Another Step Forward While Shares Stay Attractive 
For us, this is a moaty, diversified technology leader with strong AI exposure at a discount.
William Kerwin, CFA Oct 27, 2026

Fair Value Estimate : $155.00

Morningstar Economic Moat Rating : Narrow

What We Thought of Corning’s Earnings 
Corning GLW reported solid third-quarter results above the top end of guidance and guided to continued fourth-quarter growth. Non-GAAP sales rose 19% year over year to $5.1 billion, and generative AI sales doubled. Non-GAAP operating margin rose 310 basis points year over year to 22.7%.
Why it matters: Corning is well on track to its attractive “Springboard” targets. We like the firm’s consistent execution, growth, and margin expansion since unveiling Springboard three years ago. Its diversified portfolio and centralized cost advantage set it up well to achieve targets through 2030.
Optical fiber for AI leads Corning’s growth, and we continue to be impressed with the firm’s ability to rapidly increase its supply to capitalize on demand. Furthermore, Corning’s ability to derisk capital spending with co-investment by customers should please investors.
We expect optical growth to endure at a high level through 2030, and we believe it may even continue to accelerate. We see longer-term upside from scale-up networking and co-packaged optics, which make up no revenue today.
The bottom line: We maintain our $155 fair value estimate for narrow-moat Corning, and shares look attractive. Shares sold off 4% early intraday, with some market nitpicks about costs and consensus expectations. We focus on the long-term runway, which looks very positive.
Our model comes in ahead of Corning’s 2030 Springboard target, which calls for exiting 2030 with $40 billion in annualized sales. We model closer to $45 billion. We expect scale-up networking to drive upside, but we like Corning’s position even if we end up being aggressive here.
Shares are down 50% from late June. We did see exuberance priced into Corning at the peak, but now we think the market has oversold to the downside. For us, this is a moaty, diversified technology leader with strong AI exposure at a discount.

BASF strengthens U.S. production network with APG expansion in Cincinnati
Additional local capacity brings APG production closer to customers across North America
APGs combine high performance, mildness, and biodegradability, making them suitable for a wide range of consumer and industrial applications
CINCINNATI, OH, October 27, 2026 – BASF has inaugurated the expansion of its Alkyl Polyglucosides (APGs) production capacity at its Cincinnati, Ohio, site, further strengthening the company’s manufacturing footprint in the United States. First announced in 2023, the expansion reinforces Cincinnati’s role in BASF’s regional production network and strengthens the company’s position as a leading APG supplier in the United States. By increasing production close to its North American customers, BASF can combine a reliable regional supply point with its broad APG portfolio and formulation expertise. 
"The Cincinnati expansion represents an important step in reinforcing BASF's leadership in the U.S. APG market," said Gisela Pinheiro, BASF Senior Vice President Home Care and Industrial & Institutional Cleaning. "Combining our broad APG portfolio and formulation expertise with expanded regional production allows us to work even more closely with customers. It strengthens our ability to support innovation and sustainability targets across a wide range of applications."
APGs, marketed by BASF under the trade names Glucopon®, Plantaren®, Agnique® PG and Disponil® APG, are bio-based, readily biodegradable (according to OECD 301), mild, non-ionic surfactants derived from 100 percent natural and renewable feedstocks. Their excellent performance and compatibility with other surfactants make them highly versatile ingredients for personal care, home care, industrial and institutional cleaning, industrial formulations, and agricultural applications.
In addition to Cincinnati, BASF produces APGs at sites in Düsseldorf, Germany; Jinshan, China; and Bangpakong, Thailand. Together, these facilities enable BASF to provide reliable supply and respond more effectively to customer needs across regions.
Glucopon®, Plantaren®, Agnique® PG and Disponil® are registered trademarks of BASF SE.
About the Care Chemicals division at BASF 
The BASF division Care Chemicals offers a broad range of ingredients for personal care, home care, industrial & institutional cleaning, and technical applications. We are a leading global supplier for the cosmetics industry as well as the detergents and cleaners industry, and support our customers with innovative and sustainable products, solutions and concepts. The division’s high-performance product portfolio includes surfactants, emulsifiers, polymers, emollients, chelating agents, cosmetic active ingredients and UV filters. We have production and development sites in all regions and are expanding our presence in emerging markets. Further information is available online at  http://www.care-chemicals.basf.com/  
About BASF 
BASF Corporation, headquartered in Florham Park, New Jersey, is the North American affiliate of BASF SE, Ludwigshafen, Germany. BASF has more than 13,300 employees in North America and had sales of $18.1 billion in 2025. For more information about BASF’s North American operations, visit  www.basf.com/us .
At BASF, we create chemistry for a sustainable future. Our ambition: We want to be the preferred chemical company to enable our customers’ green transformation. We combine economic success with environmental protection and social responsibility. Around 95,000 employees in the BASF Group contribute to the success of our customers in nearly all sectors and almost every country in the world. Our portfolio comprises, as core businesses, the segments Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, and Nutrition & Care; our standalone businesses are bundled in the segments Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. BASF generated sales of around €60 billion in 2025. BASF shares are traded on the stock exchange in Frankfurt (BAS) and as American Depositary Receipts (BASFY) in the United States. Further information at  www.basf.com .

title: Anduril expanding into laptop manufacturing in partnership with Qualcomm - DefenseScoop
query: ("Qualcomm" OR "Qualcomm Incorporated") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Anduril expanding into laptop manufacturing in partnership with Qualcomm 
The companies plan to market the tech to government and military customers, among other potential buyers. 
By 
Jon Harper 
October 27, 2026 
Listen to this article
0:00
Learn more. 
This feature uses an automated voice, which may result in occasional errors in pronunciation, tone, or sentiment.
(Image courtesy of Anduril) 
Defense technology company Anduril, best known for building drones and AI-enabled software for the military, is branching out into a new product manufacturing business: laptops.
The company on Tuesday announced the launch of a computer initiative, dubbed BlueChip, in partnership with wireless tech giant Qualcomm.
Anduril has already developed “functional prototypes” of the laptops, according to a press release. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Series will provide the core computing capabilities for the devices, including “general-purpose processing, graphics, and on-device AI.”
The companies plan to begin taking orders next year.
Advertisement 
The firms touted BlueChip as an effort to boost manufacturing in America and reduce the nation’s reliance on foreign supply chains.
“The United States pioneered personal computing and continues to lead the world in designing advanced technology, but decades of offshoring have left America dependent on foreign manufacturers for the computers and components that power everything from personal devices to critical government infrastructure. This dependence creates a national security vulnerability. Conflict or disruptions to overseas supply chains could limit access to essential computing hardware and undermine America’s ability to sustain production when it matters most,” company officials wrote in the press release.
The organizations plan to market the tech to government and military customers, among other potential buyers.
“It might sound crazy for a company like Anduril to be doing something like this,” Anduril co-founder and leader Palmer Luckey told reporters ahead of the official announcement.
However, he suggested that the BlueChip product line isn’t far outside of Anduril’s wheelhouse.
Advertisement 
“What we’ve been doing at Anduril, including with Qualcomm, is not actually very different from building a computer. You look at any of our autonomous drones, we’ve got a CPU, a GPU, memory, storage, mainboard, battery, sensors, wireless radios. It’s basically all the same stuff you’d have in any computer. The only difference is the shape and that it has a screen and a keyboard. Even on the display side, actually, we have a number of drones that have status screens, so it’s really not all that different,” he said.
During a call with reporters ahead of the announcement, Luckey declined to say what the production targets are for the new laptops.
“We’re not sharing any quantities yet. We’re gonna have a lot more to announce next year. I think it’s really, really tough right now to announce these things. To be totally candid, we’re in an unprecedented time, as it were, for building computers given … the AI explosion, and so we’re not going into full-rate production until next year. We’re in very early prototyping production. Like, we have a very small line put together, very small quantities of these right now to build out the manufacturing process. But I’m not going to know quantities until we have a little more clarity on the manufacturing side, the vendor supply chain side. There’s a lot of moving pieces,” he said.
Anduril plans to use its Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio — where it’s also building autonomous drones for the Air Force’s Collaborative Combat Aircraft program — for BlueChip manufacturing.
Cristiano Amon, president and CEO of Qualcomm, told reporters during the call that chips for the laptops will be made at a TSMC facility in Arizona.
Advertisement 
Luckey added that the companies also have “some stuff going on” in California related to the effort, though he didn’t provide details.
“There’s certainly going to end up being other facilities. This is another one of those things where it’s still in flux, exactly which facility is going to do which step. So, I can’t get into as much detail as I’d like,” he said.
Luckey noted that, while the laptop will be the first product in the BlueChip line, the companies’ vision is to expand the offerings and it’s “very likely” that some of those will be made at other facilities.
Currently, the laptop’s bill of materials is about 90% from the U.S. and allies, according to Luckey. The aim is to eventually get that number up to 100%.
Regarding the workforce, the Anduril boss said he’s been “diverting some of our best people to this project for quite some time,” including those who worked on some of the other offerings that the company is better known for, such as attack drones.
Advertisement 
The U.S. government has not yet provided any subsidies or contracts to Anduril and Qualcomm to develop the laptops, according to Luckey, who noted that the companies have been putting their own R&D dollars into the initiative. He did not disclose how much money is being invested in the effort to get to full-rate production.
“I’d say the worst case here is that this is going to be a low-volume laptop for critical industries and government … that desperately need something like this to exist. That is a healthy business for Android to run, even if it doesn’t get bigger. I happen to believe it’s going to be much, much, much bigger,” he told reporters.
Amon noted the AI boom that’s unfolding across the economy.
“I think when you look at how AI is evolving, computers are also becoming token machines,” he said. “In addition to what you do with a laptop, it’s going to run models, it’s going to be part of this entire compute fabric that’s going to be running AI. And you’re going to have different ecosystems and needs for [the tech] across different industries. It’s very possible that you’re going to have certain industries … in addition to the federal government, that will want devices. They have different kinds of requirements and compliance with security and across the supply chain. … So, I think this could create an interesting opportunity when you think about the addressable market. It’s just a different world going forward when you think about the role of PCs.”
Luckey added that the chips in the new laptop are “extremely good” for AI inference.
Advertisement 
“Maybe not training large models, but on the inference side, they’re fantastic. And so, I’ve been using my BlueChip laptop to do a whole bunch of local model work where … I don’t want to — and actually am not allowed to — send certain information out into the cloud. And so having devices that can do a really good job of onboard AI inference running local models is actually really, really important,” he told reporters.
The BlueChip systems are designed for potential military customers.
“This is aimed squarely at the defense side of things as the pace-setting element of the design because it’s the most stringent part of the design. So basically I have to design for the military users because they’re the ones that are going to be beating these things up the most. They have the most stringent security requirements, the most stringent environmental requirements, shock and vibration, all of that,” Luckey said.
For the average individual consumer, the price tag for the extra-rugged devices might not be cost competitive with other laptop offerings on the market, he suggested.
Anduril has been testing out the BlueChip tech with multiple operating systems, Luckey noted.
Advertisement 
“As of right now, we have it running Windows and two particular flavors of Linux that are very popular with the U.S. military to make sure that all the drivers work, make sure that all the applications work,” he said.
One of the applications that has been integrated into the BlueChip system is Anduril’s Lattice software platform that serves as the backbone for some of the military’s high-priority modernization initiatives, such as Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2).
“It’s critical that we be able to run Lattice, both the version that processes locally and the version that commands and controls systems that are processing at the edge with Lattice,” Luckey said.
