This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +2.25%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this specialty glass maker would post earnings of $0.76 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.78, delivering a surprise of +2.63%. 
Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. 
Corning, which belongs to the Zacks Communication - Components industry, posted revenues of $5.08 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.04%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $4.27 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters. 
The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call. 
Corning shares have added about 45.9% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 12.1%. 
What's Next for Corning? 
While Corning has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock? 
There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately. 
Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions. 
Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Corning was favorable. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to outperform the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here. 
It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $0.91 on $5.19 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $3.30 on $19.09 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

content_text:
Boeing says it won't significantly ramp up 737 Max production until late 2027
Published Tue, Oct 27 2026 7:00 AM EDT Updated Tue, Oct 27 2026 4:32 PM EDT 
Leslie Josephs @lesliejosephs 
WATCH LIVE 
Key Points
Boeing narrowed its loss in the third quarter after defense sales rose.
The company beat revenue expectations but posted a bigger loss per share than expected.
Boeing also said it was targeting a production increase of its best-selling 737 Max aircraft in the second half of 2027.
In this article
BA 
Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT 
VIDEO 6:41 06:41 
Watch CNBC's full interview with Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg
Boeing doesn't expect to significantly ramp up output of its best-selling 737 Max aircraft until the second half of 2027 as it grapples with a slower-than-expected pace of wing production.
CEO Kelly Ortberg said Tuesday on the company's quarterly earnings call that Boeing is targeting a production rate of 52 planes a month in the second half of 2027. It has been manufacturing about 47 of its 737 Max planes a month.
Ortberg had told investors last month that the production stabilize was taking a "little bit longer" than expected because of the wings production pace.
Boeing stock fell 10% in trading Tuesday.
"I know everybody wants us to go faster, but we're going to do it right," Ortberg told CNBC's Phil LeBeau in an interview Tuesday.
Ortberg reiterated the company's priority in stabilizing production on Tuesday.
"Looking ahead, expectations are rising, and they should," Ortberg said in a note to staff on Tuesday. "That means elevating our performance through lean, productivity and efficiency improvements in our day-to-day work while upholding our high levels of safety and quality."
Aircraft production and deliveries are key to Boeing's recovery since the bulk of an aircraft's price is paid when the customer receives it.
Third-quarter earnings
The company also reported Tuesday that it narrowed its losses in the third quarter, thanks to a boost from its defense unit.
For the three months ended Sept. 30, Boeing reported a net loss of $116 million, or 26 cents a share, compared with a $5.34 billion loss, or $7.14 per share, a year earlier. Adjusting for one-time items, the company posted a loss of 34 cents a share. A year earlier, Boeing had taken a nearly $5 billion charge on its long-delayed 777X aircraft program.
Revenue climbed 4% on the year to $24.19 billion. Free cash flow rose to $464 million from $238 million in the third quarter of 2025.
The company's defense unit revenue jumped 15% in the third quarter from a year earlier to $7.94 billion.
Here's what Boeing reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street analysts expected, according to consensus estimates from LSEG:
Loss per share: 34 cents adjusted vs. a loss of 21 cents expected
Revenue: $24.19 billion vs $23.84 billion expected.
Boeing delivered 161 commercial airplanes in the third quarter, one more jet than a year earlier. 
Revenue in the all-important commercial aircraft business fell 3% to $10.72 billion. The unit had a negative operating margin of 6.5% because of a "less favorable delivery mix, higher projected costs associated with future production rate adjustments and higher estimated supply chain costs," Boeing said.
Ortberg told staff in a memo that the manufacturer has "more work to do."
Certification wins
The manufacturer had some wins lately. The U.S. Navy tapped Boeing to develop its next-generation fighter jet.
And the Federal Aviation Administration last week signed off on the 737 Max 10 , the largest in the Max family. That followed the approval of the 737 Max 7 in August and marked the final certifications for the aircraft line.

Applied Materials Raises BE Semiconductor Stake to 20%, Deepening AI Advanced Packaging Push; Deal Awaits U.S. Antitrust Review
Add preferred source 2 
Applied Materials announced it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries from 9% to approximately 20%, having signed an accelerated share purchase agreement, with the deal still pending U.S. antitrust review. Applied Materials became BE Semiconductor's largest shareholder after first taking a stake in April 2025, and the increased holding is aimed at AI chip advanced packaging. The two companies have collaborated on hybrid bonding technology since 2020 and have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer system. Applied Materials said it does not intend to push its stake above 20% or seek board seats. BE Semiconductor holds roughly 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market, with third-quarter orders up 96% year over year, and hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 already more than double the full-year 2025 level.
Key Elements 
Applied Materials BE Semiconductor Industries hybrid bonding EPIC Center Prabh Raja ASML Kinex Piotech 
U.S. semiconductor equipment giant Applied Materials announced Monday that it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (BESI) from the current 9% to approximately 20%, deepening cooperation between the two companies in advanced packaging for artificial intelligence (AI) chips. The increased holding has been signed under an accelerated share purchase agreement but still requires U.S. antitrust review.
Applied Materials became the largest shareholder of the Dutch company after first taking a 9% stake in April 2025. At that time, BE Semiconductor had a market value of about $13 billion. Under the plan, the stake will approach 20% once the increase is completed. However, Applied Materials made clear that at this stage it does not intend to push its holding above 20% or seek seats on BE Semiconductor's board, indicating that this is a long-term strategic investment centered on technology cooperation rather than a move toward a full acquisition.
The expanded cooperation focuses on next-generation chip interconnection and packaging technology, with the goal of supporting the next generation of AI semiconductors. The two companies have jointly invested in hybrid bonding process development since 2020, a technology regarded as a key link in advanced packaging and mainly used for high-performance chips.
Hybrid bonding is characterized by directly bonding copper interconnects and dielectric layers without the need for traditional bumps, allowing a substantial increase in connection density between chips. The two companies have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system, combining Applied Materials' expertise in etching, planarization, deposition and inspection with BE Semiconductor's technology in high-precision die placement and assembly. BE Semiconductor also recently formally joined Applied Materials' newly established chip equipment research organization, the EPIC Center.
Prabh Raja, president of Applied Materials' Semiconductor Products Group, said in a statement: "We look forward to further deepening our strategic collaboration with Besi to deliver the innovative products and technologies customers need to scale AI systems."
From a market structure perspective, BE Semiconductor holds a critical position in the advanced packaging equipment sector. According to market data, BE Semiconductor accounts for about 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market. Its flagship model, the Datacon 8800 CHAMEO ultra plus AC, achieves alignment accuracy of up to 100 nanometers and a throughput of up to 2,000 cycles per hour, with volume production potential.
Demand-side momentum is also strengthening. BE Semiconductor's third-quarter orders surged 96% year over year to €342.6 million (approximately $382.0 million); hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 were already more than double the full-year 2025 level. The company's latest financial report shows that its hybrid bonding customer base has expanded to 23 companies, with cumulative equipment demand exceeding 215 units.
It is worth noting that last week the market briefly worried that Dutch semiconductor equipment leader ASML might become a competitor to BE Semiconductor in the hybrid bonding arena, which BE Semiconductor has denied. Against the backdrop of advanced packaging becoming key to the AI chip computing power race, alliances and competitive-cooperative relationships among equipment makers are rapidly intensifying.
On the other hand, Chinese equipment makers are also catching up in hybrid bonding technology. China's Piotech recorded hybrid bonding equipment revenue of CNY 136 million (approximately $20.4 million) in 2025, up 41.92% year over year, and has secured repeat orders for wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding systems, meaning that this niche market previously dominated by a small number of vendors is gradually seeing new suppliers emerge.
For investors, the most direct significance of this deal is that Applied Materials is betting its resources on the "back-end" packaging link of AI chips. As advancing Moore's Law becomes increasingly difficult, improvements in chip performance increasingly depend on advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration, and hybrid bonding is one of the highest-barrier technologies in this area. By tying up with BE Semiconductor through a stake purchase rather than an acquisition, Applied Materials can share technology and customers while avoiding the operational risks and regulatory resistance of full integration.
However, the deal still must pass U.S. antitrust review, and the timetable and conditions remain uncertain. Applied Materials has also stated that it will not pursue board seats or increase its stake further, and whether the cooperation can be translated into substantive orders and revenue contribution will be a key focus for the market going forward.

content_text:
Rolls-Royce outlook as Safran and GE Aerospace earnings flag aviation risks
2 min de lecture 
RR. 
Rolls-Royce’s share price is in a bear market, a trend that accelerated after its top competitors published their earnings. The stock plunged to 1,160p on Friday before stabilizing at 1,220p today, and technicals suggest further downside over time. 
Rolls-Royce share price technicals point to more downside 
On the charts, we see that the RR stock price has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months. It dropped from a high of 1,585p in August to a low of 1,159p this month. This retreat happened after the stock formed a head-and-shoulders pattern, a common bearish sign in technical analysis. 
The stock has dropped below the 50-day and 200-day moving averages and the Major S/R pivot point of the Murrey Math Lines tool. Moving below that level confirmed that bears have prevailed. It has also remained below the Supertrend and Ichimoku cloud indicators. 
Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, potentially to the strong, pivot, reverse level of the Murrey Math Lines tool at 1,125p. A move below that level will point to more downside towards the support level of 1,000p. 
RR stock chart | Source: TradingView 
GE Aerospace and Safran earnings 
The ongoing Rolls-Royce stock weakness has coincided with that of other companies in the industry. GE Aerospace has slumped by 26% from its highest point this year, a trend that continued after publishing the recent earnings. 
Safran stock also dropped to 271 euros, its lowest level since May 18th this year. It has slumped by 26% from the year-to-date high. RTX, a company that owns Pratt & Whitney, has also fallen by over 12% from its peak. 
Safran and GE Aerospace stocks dropped because, while its earnings reports were strong, their guidance were a bit weaker. GE said that its earnings per share will be between $1.87 and $1.97, well lower than the expected $2.04. It also flagged higher costs and warned that its airline clients were cutting capacity. 
Safran, on the other hand, the company flagged the challenges in the aftermarket as companies slash their trips because of the rising costs. 
These factors may also affect Rolls-Royce’s business since it is in the same business. A cut in trips would have an immediate impact on its business since it makes most of its money in the civil aviation industry. In addition to selling engines, the company also offers services to airlines through long-term contracts. 
A key risk that the company faces is that the US-Iran war could resume in the coming weeks, pushing oil prices higher. Already, data compiled by IATA shows that the weekly average price jumped to $196.70, up by 6.6% from a month earlier. During this Iran war, we have seen that Rolls-Royce has always reacted to rising jet fuel prices. 
Another risk is that the Iran war could push Iran to bomb airports in the Middle East, as it did earlier this year. Bombing airports like in Dubai, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar, a move that will affect the civil aviation industry. Such a move will have an immediate impact on Rolls-Royce’s business since it counts companies like Turkish, Emirates, and EgyptAir as clients. 
The next key catalyst for Rolls-Royce shares will be its earnings report that comes out on November 12. These earnings will provide more hints on how the war is impacting its business.

Japan's Shin-Etsu Chemical Posts 11% Rise in Interim Net Profit to ¥286.9 Billion on AI-Driven Semiconductor Materials

Shin-Etsu Chemical reported interim consolidated results for the fiscal year ending March 2027, with net profit up 11.3% year-on-year to ¥286.9 billion (approximately $1.8 billion). Semiconductor demand grew on AI-related investment, particularly for data centers, driving the Electronic Materials Business, whose operating profit rose 28% to ¥218.9 billion (approximately $1.4 billion) and led overall performance. Meanwhile, the Infrastructure Materials Business, including PVC, saw operating profit fall 16% to ¥86.2 billion (approximately $546.3 million) amid oversupply and slowing demand in Asia. The full-year forecast was left unchanged, with net profit projected at ¥525 billion (approximately $3.3 billion).

Shin-Etsu Chemical (4063.T) on the 27th reported consolidated results for the interim period of the fiscal year ending March 2027 (April-September 2026), with net profit up 11.3% year-on-year to ¥286.9 billion (approximately $1.8 billion). Expanding artificial intelligence (AI)-related investment, centered on data centers, lifted the semiconductor market and drove growth in the Electronic Materials Business.
Net sales rose 10.6% to ¥1.42 trillion (approximately $9.0 billion), and operating profit climbed 15.6% to ¥385.9 billion (approximately $2.4 billion). The main driver was the Electronic Materials Business, whose operating profit rose 28% to ¥218.9 billion (approximately $1.4 billion). Semiconductor demand grew on the back of AI-related investment, and supply tightened for some products; the company advanced adjustments to its supply system and price revisions to boost semiconductor materials sales.
Meanwhile, operating profit in the Infrastructure Materials Business, which includes polyvinyl chloride (PVC), fell 16% to ¥86.2 billion (approximately $546.3 million). Oversupply and slowing demand in Asia weighed on market conditions.

Finance Banking Markets 
Infineon Invests €1.1 Billion in Austrian Power Semiconductor Plant
Infineon's Expansion and Technological Advancements
Investment Details
Oct 27 (Reuters) - German chip manufacturer Infineon is investing €1.1 billion ($1.23 billion) in an Austrian site to expand production of power semiconductors for data centres, it said on Tuesday.
World's First GaN Semiconductor Plant
• The company plans to build the world's first plant at its site in Villach for the mass production of gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductors based on 300-millimetre-diametre wafers.
Applications and Industry Impact
• "This paves the way for the widespread use of gallium nitride in a wide range of key applications in fields such as artificial intelligence, energy infrastructure, electric mobility and robotics," CEO Jochen Hanebeck said in a statement.
Technical Advantages of 300mm Wafers
• 300-millimetre wafers can hold 2.3 times as many chips as the most commonly used 200-millimetre version.
Market Response
• Infineon's share price, which has fallen around 40% since the middle of June, was up nearly 1% in early Frankfurt trading.
($1 = 0.8946 euros)
(Reporting by Danny Callaghan and Hakan Ersen, Editing by Friederike Heine)

Infineon’s share price peaked at around €87.8 in early June 2026 and has since corrected over 40%; as of late October it trades near €49–50, still down significantly from its summer highs ( admiralmarkets.com ).

Syensqo wins Avio award for critical space and defence materials
Syensqo supplies high-performance ablative materials, resin transfer molding (RTM) resins and adhesives for Avio's space launch programmes
By ICN Bureau | October 27, 2026 
L-R: Salvatore Mazzarella (AVIO), Stephane Souny (AVIO), Rosario Esposito (AVIO), Gerald Perrin (Syensqo), Gianluca Conti (AVIO), Giuliano Russo (Syensqo), Salvatore De Nicola (Syensqo). (Photo: Syensqo)
Syensqo has secured recognition from Avio for its role as a strategic raw materials supplier, earning an award at the Italian aerospace company's Supplier recently, at its facility in Colleferro, Italy.
 
The award highlights the strength of the companies' longstanding partnership and their shared commitment to quality, reliability and innovation across space and defence programmes.
 
The recognition comes months after the two companies announced a new long-term supply agreement in April 2026, further cementing their collaboration in advanced materials for demanding aerospace and defence applications.
 
Syensqo supplies high-performance ablative materials, resin transfer molding (RTM) resins and adhesives for Avio's space launch programmes, including Vega-C, as well as defence applications. Designed to withstand extreme thermal and mechanical stresses, these materials are used in critical components such as rocket motor nozzles, exit cones and structural elements.
 
"Receiving this recognition from Avio is a great honor and a testament to the dedication of our teams and the strength of our longstanding partnership. We are proud to contribute our advanced materials expertise to Avio's programs and remain committed to supporting the next generation of space launch systems." Rodrigo Elizondo, President of Syensqo Composite Materials.
 
The award also recognises the contributions of Syensqo's global operations teams in Winona, USA; Wrexham and Heanor, UK; and Östringen, Germany. Their expertise and commitment to excellence underpin the delivery of high-performance materials essential to Avio's programmes.
 
The recognition reinforces Syensqo's position as a key materials partner to Avio, supporting the performance and reliability demands of next-generation space launch systems and defence applications.

Infineon establishing first high-volume fab for GaN power semiconductors on 300mm wafers in Europe
Infineon Technologies AG of Munich, Germany is establishing the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for gallium nitride (GaN) power semiconductors on 300mm wafers in Europe. As part of the project, the firm will invest about €1.1bn in its existing cleanroom facilities at the site in Villach, Austria by 2034. Leveraging both the existing and upgraded infrastructure will enable efficient and cost-effective expansion of manufacturing capacity, it is reckoned. Production is scheduled to start by the end of 2027. 
Infineon’s investment addresses the rapidly growing demand for high-performance power supply solutions, as gallium nitride enables significant efficiency gains in applications such as AI data centers, energy infrastructure, e-mobility, robotics and consumer electronics. 
Picture: Infineon’s site in Villach, Austria. 
Two years ago, Infineon achieved the milestone of processing the world’s first 300mm GaN wafers. Compared with 200mm wafers, the 300mm diameter enables the production of 2.3 times as many chips per wafer. Infineon is now transferring this more efficient technology to the first high-volume manufacturing facility serving customers. 
“This substantial investment shows our clear commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem and Europe’s technological sovereignty. By establishing high-volume manufacturing on 300mm wafers, we will be the first company in the world to bring gallium nitride power electronics into volume production,” says Infineon’s CEO Jochen Hanebeck. “In doing so, we are paving the way for the widespread use of gallium nitride in a wide range of key applications in areas such as artificial intelligence, energy infrastructure, e-mobility and robotics,” he adds. 
“We are witnessing one of the largest single investments in the history of Austria’s high-tech industry,” states Christian Stocker, Federal Chancellor of the Republic of Austria. “This is not only a strong commitment to Austria as a business location but also helps ensure that the future of the semiconductor industry will not be shaped solely in Asia or the USA, but also in Austria and Europe,” he adds. 
“Europe currently accounts for only around 10% of global chip production… We must also manufacture this key technology in Europe,” says Wolfgang Hattmannsdorfer, Austrian Federal Minister for Economic Affairs. “Austria is already a leader in energy-efficient chips. Relative to our population, we rank first in the EU in business R&D spending in the semiconductor sector. With our industrial strategy, we intend to build on this lead and not only research new technologies but also manufacture them on an industrial scale,” he adds. “Every job in the chip industry can provide six additional jobs across the broader economy. That is why we intend to support Infineon’s new chip production with up to €319m — subject to clear funding criteria for the location. This will ensure that public funds strengthen value creation and jobs in Austria over the long term.” 
The investment is being supported under the European Chips Act. The European Commission has approved the €319m in state aid. The formal funding commitment by the Austrian Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism is expected within the stipulated time limits.
“Competitiveness and technological sovereignty emerge where excellent research is translated into industrial value creation. This is precisely where our flagship project comes in. From Austria, we are bringing innovation into industrial application, strengthening our technological leadership and securing highly skilled jobs,” says Infineon Technologies Austria AG’s CEO Sabine Herlitschka. “The entire Austrian semiconductor ecosystem benefits — from research organizations and universities to industrial partners. We are thus sustainably strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and strategic autonomy in microelectronics.”
Infineon reckons that the investment strengthens Villach’s role as a global competence center for power electronics and new semiconductor materials. Infineon Austria currently employs about 5800 people, including 4800 at the Villach site (as of end-September 2025). Together with universities, research institutions, start-ups and industry partners, Infineon forms the core of a microelectronics ecosystem in southern Austria. The establishment of the new 300mm GaN manufacturing facility is also expected to create synergies with the power electronics R&D activities in Villach.

title: HyProMag USA Pre-Feasibility Study Outlines Future Expansion Options to Quadruple Planned U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Capacity Indicating an Incremental Post-Tax NPV of up to US$2.1 Billion - Yahoo Finance

content_text:
HyProMag USA Pre-Feasibility Study Outlines Future Expansion Options to Quadruple Planned U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Capacity Indicating an Incremental Post-Tax NPV of up to US$2.1 Billion
ACCESS Newswire · HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA 
October 26, 2026 15 min read 
Independent Pre-Feasibility Study completed by PegasusTSI Inc. and BBA USA Inc. supports three new plants with a centralized finishing hub - in addition to the Company's first plant at Northlake, Texas - indicating an estimated incremental post-tax NPV of US$1.85 billion to US$2.06 billion, a post-tax IRR of 31% to 36%, competitive manufacturing costs and higher value, low-carbon finished magnet production. 
DALLAS-FORT WORTH, TX / ACCESS Newswire / October 26, 2026 / HyProMag USA LLC ("HyProMag USA" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the completion of an independent Pre-Feasibility Study ("PFS" or the "Study") undertaken by PegasusTSI Inc. and BBA USA Inc. evaluating the potential expansion of its proposed U.S. rare earth magnet manufacturing platform beyond its first plant in Northlake, Texas (the "Northlake Texas Facility"), which is in detailed engineering, with Phase 1 commissioning expected in mid-2028. 
The PFS evaluates a three-planti phased expansion strategy: three new regional production plants, supported by a centralized manufacturing, finishing and technology hub (the " Central Texas Hub "), to produce commercial neodymium iron boron ("NdFeB") magnet products in the United States from both end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy material. Together with the Northlake Texas Facilityii, the platform targets total salable material production of approximately 6,000 metric tons per year by 2034, an increase of 4,474 metric tons per year above production from the Northlake Texas Facility. 
Annual total magnetic material production in 2034 from the Company would comprise approximately 4,192 metric tons of magnets, 1,305 metric tons of magnetic NdFeB alloy powder and 503 metric tons of other salable material. The PFS economics listed below cover the three new plants, including the Central Texas Hub only; they do not include the Northlake Texas Facility, whose value is not included in the PFS results. 
The Study builds upon the engineering and development work completed for the Northlake Texas Facility and outlines a pathway for HyProMag USA to develop from a Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap ("HPMS")iii enabled magnet recycler into a fully integrated producer of commercial rare earth magnet products for U.S. customers. 
The Company believes the platform combines the cost advantages and operational flexibility of both end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy feedstocks, providing a flexible and scalable pathway to magnet manufacturing. 
HyProMag USA may also benefit from potential future access to primary sourced feedstock from Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited ("Mkango") pursuant to certain Mkango supply rights to the Company. 
Story Continues 
Highlights 
The PFS evaluated two development options, both based on modular production systems: 
Case 1 - Recycled feedstock only: HPMS recycling of magnet scrap to produce NdFeB alloy powder, sintered magnet blocks, finished and packaged magnets; and 
Case 2 - Recycled and primary feedstock: as Case 1, with the additional capex to support primary NdFeB alloy as a feedstock to produce NdFeB alloy powder, sintered magnet blocks, finished and packaged magnets. 
Project economics with a post-tax NPViv,v of US$1,854 million ( Case 2 ) to US$2,062 million ( Case 1 ) for the three new plants (excluding the Northlake Texas Facility), post-tax IRR of 31% ( Case 2 ) to 36% ( Case 1 ) and a Profitability Index (post-tax NPV divided by capital cost) of approximately 2.8x to 3.3x, based on forecast pricesvi and a Class 3 AACEvii capital cost estimate of approximately US$656 million ( Case 2 ) to US$623 million ( Case 1 ), respectively, with a payback of 3 years ( Case 2 ) and 2.3 years ( Case 1 ). 
Competitive Manufacturing Costs. For the first PFS Plant in 2030, the PFS estimates an All-In Sustaining Cost ("AISC") of approximately US$41.6 per kg ( Case 2 ) to US$37.4 per kg ( Case 1 ) of finished NdFeB products sold. AISC includes all downstream processing and finishing costs, including plating and epoxy coating. Based on forecast market prices and the forecast product mix, the weighted average realized all-in selling price in 2030 is estimated at approximately US$100.5 per kg, supporting strong margins and attractive project returns. 
Combined HyProMag USA platform value: The combined post-tax NPV range of the proposed Northlake Texas Facility and the potential PFS plants is estimated at US$2.6 billion to US$2.8 billion. 
The staged approach for the Northlake Texas Facility: viii Updated post-tax NPV of approximately US$723ix,x,xi,xii million based on forecast prices and a capital cost estimate of approximately US$167 millionxiii, increased due to the phased construction approach and the finalization of equipment orders. The reduction from the post-tax NPV of approximately US$797 million announced on June 22, 2026, reflects the later construction timetable, the higher capital costs and updated operating cost assumptions consistent with the PFS. 
Potential fourfold increase in U.S. magnet producing capacity: from approximately 1,048 metric tons per year of salable NdFeB magnets at the Northlake Texas Facility to approximately 4,192 metric tons per year across four plants by 2034. Phase 1 of the Northlake Texas Facility is expected to be commissioned in mid-2028. 
Integrated alloy processing and centralized finishing. The Central Texas Hub is expected to incorporate Vacuum Induction Melting ("VIM") and strip-casting operations, allowing the platform to process NdFeB alloy, provide magnet plating, passivation, coating, quality assurance and customer qualification for all plants. 
Higher-value magnet production: The production configuration would incorporate grain boundary diffusion ("GBD") capability, which would significantly increase the proportion of higher-value NdFeB magnet products. High-grade magnet production would increase from approximately 10% to 20% of total magnet output, supporting enhanced product mix, market access and project economics. 
Low-carbon production supported by a previously completed carbon footprint of approximately 2.35 kg CO₂-eq per kilogram of NdFeB sintered block product for the Northlake Texas Facilityxiv. 
Commercial qualification pathway: Product performance data and customer validation are underway with potential U.S. offtake customers, with the support of the HyProMag Group. 
Additional revenue opportunities: The platform would provide future opportunities for third-party magnet finishing activities, supporting enhanced utilization of manufacturing infrastructure and potential additional revenue streams. 
The platform is expected to play a key role in re-establishing domestic NdFeB magnet manufacturing in the United States, creating approximately 300 jobs across Texas, South Carolina, and Nevada, in addition to the 100 positions at the Northlake Texas Facility. 
Independent PFS: completed by PegasusTSI Inc. and BBA USA Inc. with support from HyProMag's international teams and the University of Birmingham, UK. Subject to ongoing review, the expansion strategy is expected to progress to a Feasibility Study at the appropriate time. 
Julian Treger, CoTec CEO commented : "This Pre-Feasibility Study confirms the opportunity to establish a significant domestic rare earth magnet manufacturing platform in the United States. The Study demonstrates robust economics and a pathway to producing higher-value NdFeB magnet products for strategically important sectors including advanced manufacturing, energy, defense and AI-driven technologies. Importantly, the platform is designed with the flexibility to utilize primary alloy feedstock alongside recycled materials, providing greater supply chain resilience and supporting long-term operational competitiveness. The results highlight the platform's potential to create substantial long-term value while strengthening the U.S. rare earth magnet supply chain." 
Will Dawes, Mkango CEO, commented: "The Study indicates the scalability of the HyProMag business model and provides a framework for disciplined growth in the United States using HyProMag USA's first plant in Northlake. Together with ongoing development activities in the United Kingdom and Germany, it strengthens the foundation for establishing a significant domestic rare earth magnet manufacturing capability for HyProMag. It also highlights the significant potential synergies between HyProMag USA and Mkango, including increased security of feedstock supply and enhanced supply chains into USA markets, respectively." 
Professor Allan Walton, Founder of HyProMag and Head of the Magnetic Materials Group at the University of Birmingham, commented: "The objective of the HyProMag platform has always been to demonstrate that HPMS technology can recover rare earth magnetic materials and convert them into high-performance commercial magnet products. The PFS outlines a pathway to scaling that capability through an integrated manufacturing platform incorporating magnet production, finishing and product qualification. Importantly, the enhanced production configuration would support the manufacture of a broader range of commercial magnet products for demanding industrial applications, while the inclusion of finishing, quality assurance and product development capabilities provides a foundation for continued product optimization and customer qualification." 
Platform Configuration 
The PFS assessed three new production plants in South Carolina, Nevada and a second location in Texas, which would operate alongside the Northlake Texas Facility. Each plant is intended to process feedstock, operate HPMS and produce unfinished sintered NdFeB blocks. 
The Central Texas Hub, located within the second Texas plant, is expected to incorporate alloy processing (VIM and strip-casting), GBD, machining, plating, passivation, epoxy coating, quality assurance, product qualification and technology development capabilities. 
Under the proposed configuration, unfinished sintered blocks produced from South Carolina, Nevada and the second facility in Texas would be transferred to the Central Texas Hub for advanced manufacturing and finishing. The Central Texas Hub is also designed to support future partnerships with specialist manufacturing and finishing providers, enabling the efficient scaling of advanced magnet production capability. 
Higher-Value Magnet Production 
A key outcome of the PFS was the optimization of the manufacturing configuration to increase production of higher-value NdFeB magnet products. This enhanced product mix would be supported by further incorporation of GBD technology, which enables the production of higher-performance magnet grades required for demanding applications across medical, industrial automation, robotics, energy infrastructure and advanced manufacturing markets. 
The increased proportion of higher-value magnet products would broaden exposure to premium end-use applications and is expected to support improved revenues, stronger operating margins and enhanced overall project returns. 
Recycling of Magnet End Cuts By-Products 
The PFS plants are designed to recover and reprocess manufacturing residues, including magnet machining end cuts, through the HPMS process, maximizing the use of rare earth materials. This integrated approach would support both production flexibility and the circular manufacturing characteristics of the HyProMag platform. 
Integrated Manufacturing Platform 
The Central Texas Hub is expected to create operating synergies through shared infrastructure and integrated processing capabilities. The Study indicates that the combination of integrated alloy processing, magnet manufacturing, finishing operations and flexible feedstock sourcing has the potential to support a competitive cost position for domestically manufactured rare earth magnet products. The Company believes these advantages will support the supply of U.S. manufactured magnets at competitive prices while providing customers with the benefits of domestic supply-chain security, traceability and low-carbon production. 
The Central Texas Hub is also expected to evolve into an advanced manufacturing, product qualification and technology development center serving the broader manufacturing platform. In addition to supporting HyProMag USA production, the facility would provide future opportunities to support third-party magnet finishing activities, creating the potential for additional revenue streams and improved utilization of manufacturing infrastructure. 
The proposed technology and product development center would leverage expertise from the wider HyProMag Group and the University of Birmingham's Magnetic Materials Group, supporting development, qualification and optimization of commercial magnet products. 
Flexible Feedstock Platform 
A key outcome of the independent PFS is the flexibility of a manufacturing platform capable of utilizing both recycled NdFeB materials and primary alloy feedstocks. This flexible sourcing model is expected to enhance supply-chain resilience, support production growth and provide the ability to optimize raw material inputs in response to market conditions and customer requirements. HPMS technology provides the foundation for processing recycled magnetic materials and integrating them into the broader manufacturing platform. 
Advancing Commercial Magnet Qualification with HyProMag Group 
Commercial magnet qualification activities continue across the wider HyProMag Group in the United Kingdom and Germany. These activities are expected to support qualification of future U.S.-produced magnet products, accelerate customer onboarding and reduce commercialization risk as the U.S. manufacturing platform expands. The Company believes this provides a meaningful advantage by allowing future U.S. operations to build upon existing technical and commercial progress rather than initiating qualification programs from a standing start. 
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for NdFeB magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary HPMS technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA is designed to deliver faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks - including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap - enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing. 
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec Holdings Corp. (TSXV: CTH; OTCQX: CTHCF) ("CoTec") and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited which is owned on a 79.4%/20.6% basis by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and CoTec.

Ha-young faces industry ouster over pro-Japanese ancestry while Ai-jing draws fan fundraising 
입력 2026.10.27. 08:00 업데이트 2026.10.27. 11:31 
조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 
Recently, cases have again emerged in the entertainment world of people being collaterally harmed by family-related risks. Actress Ha-young boasted of coming from a family of doctors and was swept into controversy over being a descendant of pro-Japanese collaborators, and A2O LITE member Ai-jing faced fallout after her parents' wage arrears controversy erupted right after her debut. Yet public reactions to the same type of family risk have been sharply divided, drawing attention.
In August, suspicions were raised that actress Ha-young had ties to pro-Japanese collaborators. At the time Ha-young had boasted on a variety show that she came from a family of doctors spanning four generations since her great-great-grandfather. She said, "My great-great-grandfather opened the first Western medicine clinic in Hanyang and treated Emperor Gojong." But later some claimed Ha-young's great-great-grandfather had worked as a doctor during the Japanese colonial period and was a figure named Ahn Sang-ho with suspected pro-Japanese actions. Ha-young's agency responded that it was true her great-great-grandfather was Ahn Sang-ho but that the allegations of pro-Japanese behavior were "groundless," drawing a line.
Later it was revealed that Ha-young's grandfather was Ahn Bu-ho, who was from Sorokdo and worked on leprosy treatment, but because records show that leprosy patients at Sorokdo were forcibly detained and subjected to inhumane surgeries for decades, public opinion worsened further. Some criticized Ha-young's side for trying to cover the great-great-grandfather's pro-Japanese suspicions with the grandfather's achievements and strongly condemned Ha-young's inadequate response.
As the controversy grew, Ha-young's side reversed its position within a day. The agency apologized in an additional statement, saying, "Upon further verification, we confirmed that there is indeed a record of Great-great-grandfather Ahn Sang-ho's name appearing on the 1916 Daijeong Chinmokhoe council member list. We sincerely apologize for hastily responding that the matter was 'groundless' without sufficient verification and for the confusion caused." Ha-young also belatedly posted a handwritten apology, saying she had known only fragments of her great-great-grandfather's life from family stories. She said, "Embarrassingly, in that ignorant state I spoke of my great-great-grandfather in many settings as if it were a family pride. Through this incident, while looking up related materials myself, I learned of my great-great-grandfather's pro-Japanese actions. I reflect on having lightly mentioned family history without properly knowing the painful history Korea endured during the Japanese colonial period," and bowed her head.
Despite that apology, public opinion had already worsened considerably. The timing, coinciding with the lead-up to Liberation Day, and the agency's careless response attempting to put out the fire without proper fact-checking, together with Ha-young's belated appearance despite the controversy arising from her own reckless words and actions, added to public anger. As a result, all interviews and promotional schedules for the Netflix series Our Sticky Love were canceled, and advertisers and broadcasters made Ha-young's videos private as they severed ties.
In particular, Ha-young proceeded with filming for her scheduled next project, the SBS drama The Long Shot Trial, despite the pro-Japanese controversy and even announced she was confirmed to appear in The Trauma Code: Heroes on call season 3. The public strongly protested and called for a boycott, and Ha-young voluntarily withdrew from The Trauma Code: Heroes on call season 3. SBS also decided this month to remove The Long Shot Trial from the lineup for the first half of next year, delaying its release schedule, and Ha-young naturally faced a suspension of activities and the risk of being driven out of the entertainment industry.
Meanwhile on the 14th, Ai-jing, a Chinese member of rookie girl group A2O LITE under A2O Entertainment founded by Lee Soo-man, suffered indignity when her parents' 'debt scandal' surfaced just one day after her debut. Chinese local media reported that Ai-jing's parents had been listed by the court as 'judgmental execution subjects (debt defaulters).' According to the verdict, the company registered under Ai-jing's mother's name, 'Beijing Sopies Education Technology Co. Ltd.,' had been involved in wage arrears disputes with employees for two years, and although it signed an installment payment agreement it failed to fulfill it and was subjected to court-ordered enforcement.
The total amount Ai-jing's parents face for forced enforcement is about 3.45 million yuan (about 660 million won in our currency), and the assets in their names have been subject to high-spending restrictions by the court. The whistleblower pointed out that the parents spent huge sums training and debuting Ai-jing, sending her to U.S. dance competitions and filming ads for a famous sports brand, and angrily asked, "You have the means to train and debut your child but no money to pay your debts?"
The next day Ai-jing's mother personally appeared and apologized. She said, "I used to run an education-related business, but the company's financial situation rapidly deteriorated and it fell into serious management difficulties, which led to these debt disputes. Regardless of the circumstances, failing to pay the amounts due on time is a wrongdoing I must face and take responsibility for. I sincerely apologize to everyone who suffered damage as a result."
She added, "I am contacting each of the parties involved one by one to discuss solutions and am maintaining continuous communication. I will not evade responsibility and will take full responsibility until all issues are resolved," while emphasizing that "this is a problem to be solved by the parents and the child has nothing to do with past businesses or disputes," stressing that Ai-jing is unrelated to the controversy.
Although public opinion in China did not calm easily after the mother's apology, there was also a substantial segment that defended her. That was because Ai-jing, born in 2013 (13 years old), is so young that it would be difficult for her to be aware of her parents' wage arrears. Some Chinese fans even planned voluntary fundraising to resolve the parents' wage arrears. The idea was to support Ai-jing's mother so she could promptly repay the debts, but as a loan to be repaid later. However, that was only the opinion of some fans, and the proposal has sparked debate among netizens domestically and abroad.
The issue of a punitive system by association stemming from celebrities' family risks has been raised consistently. The controversies involving Ha-young and Ai-jing also raised repeated questions about whether children should be held responsible. In the end, Ha-young lost not only domestic but also overseas fans, while Ai-jing still has a considerable number of fans on her side.
The divergent fortunes stem in part from the weight of the historical pain of the Japanese colonial period, but Ha-young's hasty and complacent handling of a matter that was both serious and sensitive also played a major role. Moreover, because Ha-young herself repeatedly promoted her family as a "four-generation medical family," using her household as a promotional tool and inflating the controversy, many say she cannot be free of responsibility. In this situation, attention is focused on what differing fates these figures will face going forward.

Overcoming Bottlenecks: Biopharma’s Big Challenge Is Execution
Closing the execution gap is one of the greatest opportunities biopharma has today to enhance resilience and unlock the full value of its science
By 
Gail Dutton 
October 26, 2026 
Credit: Extreme Media/Getty Images
The biggest challenge facing the biopharma industry isn’t scientific innovation. It’s manufacturing execution.
That’s the opinion of Nicolas Pivet, vice president and general manager of manufacturing and digital solutions at Cytiva. Major scientific advances have enabled the development of truly amazing therapeutics such as RNA technologies and cell and gene interventions, yet manufacturing innovation hasn’t kept pace. “Our ability to manufacture these therapies reliably, repeatedly, and at scale remains a major constraint,” Pivet tells GEN .
Nicolas Pivet, vice president and general manager of manufacturing and digital solutions at Cytiva. [Cytiva] 
“The industry often focuses on symptoms [of biomanufacturing bottlenecks] such as paper batch records, disconnected laboratory information management systems, fragmented automation architectures, isolated enterprise resource planning deployments, or data silos. Those challenges are real, but they are not the root cause,” Pivet stresses.
“The deeper issue,” he says, “is that many manufacturing environments evolved over decades and were never designed as connected systems. Digital capabilities were often layered on to solve local problems rather than integrated around end-to-end manufacturing performance. The result is an environment that is increasingly data-rich but…insight-poor.”
In that environment, organizations can’t extract actionable insights early enough to affect outcomes. They have a visibility problem.
Focus on observability 
The first step in resolving the bottlenecks is to solve specific problems.
“You cannot control what you cannot see,” Pivet says. He advises industry to focus first on improving observability. Gaining insights into process deviations early enables earlier intervention, which creates better decisions and improves confidence in those decisions, he explains. This is the foundation of advanced manufacturing.
“Then connect the data, workflows, and decisions required to improve the outcome,” Pivet advises. “Biopharma does not lack information. It lacks accessible, contextualized, and trusted information,” he says. “Connecting process, equipment, analytical, and workflow data establishes the foundation required for predictive analytics, advanced automation, digital twins, and AI.”
“Only after that [has occurred] should advanced control or AI-enabled decision-making become part of the discussion.”
Therefore, rather than starting with AI use cases—as many try—organizations should first focus on observability, and then address interconnectivity, data integrity, and maintaining operational context for those data flows. When those are resolved, AI can be added to the mix. “AI does not fix weak foundations,” he says. “It exposes them.”
Face organizational barriers 
The barriers to digital transformation are more often organizational than technical. That’s because biomanufacturers consider change riskier than maintaining current practices. In 2025, “more than a third of biopharma companies were still in early exploration or had not started their digital transformation journey,” he says, underscoring his point.
Trust is typically the rate-limiting step, and that is established only by reliable performance. Therefore, “the organizations moving fastest are those demonstrating value on real manufacturing problems, validating outcomes, and gradually scaling successful approaches rather than attempting sweeping transformations,” Pivet observes.
Manufacturing equipment in the future will not just be smarter; it will be designed from the outset as elements of connected, interoperable systems that provide early visibility and easy integration into automated and connected workflows.
Prepare the workforce 
“The conversation around AI often focuses on technology. The more important conversation is about people,” Pivet emphasizes.
Automation, agentic and generative AI, and other smart manufacturing technologies are changing roles throughout the workforce at, seemingly, warp speed. Everyone, from equipment operators, process engineers, data scientists, and quality professionals up through the executive suite, is coming to grips with new ways of working that require new skills and new ways of thinking.
“Data literacy, systems thinking, automation fluency, model interpretation, and cross-functional collaboration are becoming increasingly important,” Pivet points out. Consequently, people are spending less time collecting information and reacting to events, and more time interpreting data and optimizing processes.
The workforce, however, is still in transition. “The Global Biopharma Index reported that 29% of organizations experience severe shortages in digital and AI-related skills,” he says.
“Workforce readiness is one of the defining challenges of this decade,” Pivet continues. “The most successful manufacturers I encounter are not necessarily the ones deploying the most advanced technologies. They are the organizations creating confidence around new ways of working.”
Within five years, he predicts a plethora of hybrid roles that blend both process and digital expertise. Future titles may include digital process engineer, manufacturing data scientist, process intelligence specialist, and manufacturing systems architect, he adds.
Filling those new roles means preparing the workforce today. He advocates upskilling individuals enterprise-wide, ensuring the various functional teams learn together, rather than treating digital transformation as the purview of any particular group.
Even today, across industries, traditional learning programs are being complemented by immersive learning experiences. Biopharma will be no different, especially given its growing complexity and limited opportunities for hands-on learning in the face of good manufacturing requirements, production schedules, and equipment availability.
Immersive learning experiences involving mixed reality and augmented reality “allow operators, technicians, and engineers to interact with equipment and workflows, and troubleshooting scenarios in highly realistic digital environments,” he says. By accelerating learning, enhancing retention, and building confidence, workers are better prepared when they enter live manufacturing environments.
Eventually, Pivet says, “Immersive learning may become as important to workforce development as flight simulators became to aviation training.”
Ease tech transfer 
The tech transfer process also has a major bottleneck, but it has nothing to do with technology or human factors.
“The most common reason transfers fail is not because process instructions are missing,” he says. “It is because process understanding fails to transfer with them. Receiving organizations often inherit process descriptions, specifications, and operating procedures, but not the context explaining why those parameters matter or how the process behaves under changing conditions.”
Those gaps are becoming ever more important as therapies become increasingly complex. Successful tech transfer, therefore, includes transferring process understanding. Digital twins help minimize the gap between process instructions and process understanding by enabling teams “to test assumptions virtually before testing them physically,” Pivet says, thus enhancing success. In this way, “…uncertainty is removed rather than relocated.”
Lead with digital change 
If you can prioritize only one area for improvement, Pivet advises choosing digital infrastructure because, he explains, “people and processes increasingly depend on information. Digital infrastructure creates the conditions for successful technology transfer, effective workforce development, predictive analytics, process understanding, and operational improvement. Without trusted information flows, organizations struggle to scale knowledge, replicate success, or improve decision quality.”
High-quality information flows, he predicts, will be a major determinant of manufacturing competitiveness in the coming decade. “The companies best positioned to lead the next era of biomanufacturing will be those that combine AI initiatives with strong connected-data and observability foundations,” he suggests. By doing so, they will be better able to translate scientific innovation into predictable, scalable, operational performance.
“Biopharma does not have an imagination problem,” Pivet reiterates. “It has an execution problem. Closing that execution gap is one of the greatest opportunities our industry has to accelerate patient access, improve resilience, and unlock the full value of the science being developed today.”

October 26, 2026

L eading agrochemical company Sumitomo Chemical India Ltd on Monday reported a 12.4% year-on-year decline in net profit to ₹156 crore for the second quarter, compared with ₹178 crore in the corresponding period last year. Revenue declined 2.5% YoY to ₹891 crore from ₹914 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation fell 15.7% to ₹183 crore from ₹217 crore. The EBITDA margin contracted to 20.56% in the September quarter from 24% in the corresponding quarter last year. Japan's Sumitomo Chemical said its wholly owned South Korean subsidiary, Dongwoo Fine-Chem, has signed an agreement with Samsung Electro-Mechanics to establish a joint venture to manufacture glass-core substrates for advanced semiconductor packages.
The new company is expected to be incorporated in 2026, subject to regulatory approvals. Glass core substrates are emerging as a key technology for advanced semiconductor packaging. They offer superior rigidity, dimensional stability, lower thermal expansion and reduced warpage, making them well-suited for increasingly powerful AI chips, high-performance computing and data centre applications.
The partners aim to establish a commercial supply system by the second half of fiscal 2027, after which the venture plans to gradually expand manufacturing capacity for glass core substrates. The announcement aligns with Sumitomo Chemical's strategy to expand its semiconductor materials business, with ICT-related businesses identified as a key long-term growth driver, according to a press release.
The group has been strengthening both its front-end semiconductor materials portfolio, including photoresists and specialty chemicals, and its back-end business through investments in advanced package materials, substrate materials and next-generation process technologies.

Enphase Energy, Inc. FREMONT, Calif., Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Enphase Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ: ENPH), a global energy technology company, and Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) today announced that Enphase will deploy the world's first 900 V gallium nitride (GaN) monolithic bidirectional switch (BDS) devices, designed to operate in Enphase solid-state transformer power modules. The devices extend GaN technology to 900 V while retaining the high-frequency switching capabilities that enable compact, efficient power conversion. 
Enphase has pioneered the system-level development and demonstration, building on more than 10 years of in-house research into GaN power conversion, with device technology and engineering expertise from Infineon. Enphase is among the first to bring 650 V GaN BDS devices into volume production power electronics, and GaN HEMT technology is already operating in Enphase IQ9™ Microinverters deployed in the field. Extending that work with Infineon beyond 650 V, using Infineon's CoolGaN™ bidirectional switch portfolio, opens the door further to medium-voltage systems. 
The 900 V GaN devices allow Enphase to continue using components rated below 1 kV, expanding the design options towards high-performance power conversion typically governed by silicon carbide (SiC). This supports a single-stage architecture with high-frequency switching, low electromagnetic interference (EMI), and fewer points of failure. Switching at such high frequency shrinks the transformers and other magnetics needed in the power stage, cutting size, weight, and cost. 
Higher-voltage switches within that low-voltage envelope change the economics of power conversion. In a solid-state transformer, a medium-voltage input can be handled by fewer inverters connected in series while retaining the low switching losses and intrinsic bidirectionality of GaN BDS. Fewer building blocks means lower system-level losses at the same input current, fewer components in the power path, and a lower total switch count. On the DC side, higher-voltage unidirectional switch (UDS) devices allow power to be generated at a unipolar 800 volts rather than split +/-400 V buses, and support future 1,500 VDC bus architectures through split +/-750 V generation with fewer switches and lower bridge losses. 
The technology is particularly relevant to the Enphase IQ ® Solid-State Transformer (IQ SST), the company's solid-state transformer platform for AI data centers, where power density, efficiency, and uptime drive the economics of every megawatt deployed. The same devices are expected to benefit commercial solar inverters by enabling three-phase, line-to-line designs for 480 V applications in the United States and 400 V applications elsewhere, again with fewer switches, lower losses, and lower cost. 
Story Continues 
"Enphase asks more of our technology than almost anyone, and medium-voltage solid-state transformers are exactly where high-voltage GaN proves its value," said Johannes Schoiswohl, senior vice president and head of GaN Systems Business Line at Infineon. "Moving past 650 V lets system designers strip cost and loss out of the architecture rather than optimizing around it." 
"GaN is not new to us. It has been running in Enphase IQ9 Microinverters in the field, and that field data is why we trust it in a megawatt-class system," said Hans van Antwerpen, senior vice president and chief technology officer at Enphase Energy. "Moving to 900 V gives us more voltage headroom without giving up high-frequency switching, and it allows us to stay with components rated below 1 kV while reducing the number of converters in the system. Fewer parts in the power path means higher efficiency and fewer things that can fail." 
The 900 V GaN BDS devices have been successfully tested and are now being integrated into IQ SST development builds, with production qualification expected to follow. Learn more about the use of GaN in Enphase products in its white paper. 
About Enphase Energy, Inc. 
Enphase Energy is a global energy technology company advancing intelligent power systems for homes, businesses, and next-generation AI data centers. The company designs semiconductor-based energy technologies spanning solar, batteries, EV charging, energy management, and virtual power plants, and is developing solid-state transformer technology to address the rapidly growing power demands of AI data centers. Based in Fremont, California, Enphase is the world's leading supplier of microinverter-based solar and battery systems. The company revolutionized the solar industry with its microinverter technology and has shipped approximately 89.4 million microinverters, with approximately 5.3 million Enphase-based systems deployed in more than 165 countries. Enphase products enable people to harness the sun to make, use, save, and sell their own power, all controlled through the Enphase App. For more information, visit https://enphase.com/ .

Exclusive: Veolia sells R&E to Bricks Capital in deal worth about W70b

Firm expands resource-recycling portfolio with high-margin acquisition
R&E, a company specializing in recycling artificial marble waste. [R&E website] 
Global environmental services firm Veolia Industrial Development Korea is selling R&E, a company that recycles artificial marble waste.
According to investment banking industry sources, Veolia signed a share purchase agreement Monday to sell its entire 100 percent stake in R&E to private equity fund manager Bricks Capital. The deal is valued at around 70 billion won ($52.9 million).
Veolia appointed BDA Partners as the sale manager earlier this year and formally launched the divestiture process, selecting Bricks Capital as the preferred bidder in late July. The final contract was signed roughly three months after that designation.
Veolia first acquired a 60 percent stake in R&E in 2019, securing management control, and later bought the remaining 40 percent to make it a wholly owned subsidiary. The deal marks a full exit from the investment approximately seven years after the initial acquisition.
The preliminary bidding round drew competition from three to five financial and strategic investors. R&E's appeal lay in its established share of the artificial marble waste recycling market and its operating profit margin of around 20 percent.
R&E operates a distinctive dual-revenue business model. It first collects processing fees when it takes in waste generated during the manufacturing and fabrication of artificial marble. It then subjects that waste to high-temperature crushing and pyrolysis to produce recycled methyl methacrylate (rMMA) and alumina, which it sells for a second stream of revenue. The structure lets the company capture the benefits of both waste treatment and recycled materials manufacturing simultaneously.
On the production side, R&E operates its main factory in Changwon, South Gyeongsang Province, along with facilities in Oksan, North Chungcheong Province, and Haman, South Gyeongsang Province. It sources raw materials through a network of major domestic manufacturers and fabricators, commanding the bulk of the artificial marble waste processing market and holding relevant technology patents.
Recent financial results, however, show signs of strain. Sales grew only marginally, from 13.5 billion won in 2024 to 13.7 billion won in 2025, while operating profit fell from 3.1 billion won to 2.8 billion won over the same period. Cash flow from operating activities also declined, dropping from 3.45 billion won in 2024 to 2.31 billion won in 2025.
Bricks Capital, which is acquiring R&E, is a young private equity fund manager founded in 2022. It is co-led by Kim Sae-han-sol, who built hands-on experience in the battery and electric vehicle industry at LG Energy Solution and Apple, and Kang Hun-gu, who comes from Goldman Sachs and IMM Private Equity. The firm operates out of Seoul and Silicon Valley, focusing on advanced manufacturing and sustainable industries.
With North American battery technology companies Sion Power and Mitra Chem already in its portfolio, Bricks Capital is using the R&E acquisition to extend its investment reach from batteries and advanced materials into the eco-friendly resource-recycling sector. The move signals the firm's intent to build a stronger foundation for broader investment in recycled materials.

SPONSORED CONTENT BY 
Continuing innovation coupled with demonstrated patient benefit have been driving the design and manufacturing of newer classes of protein-based molecules. Among these novel protein and peptide therapeutics are antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), multispecific antibodies, antibody fragments and recombinant and synthetic peptides. 
While most approved antibodies are full-length antibodies, market approvals of antibody-derived molecules are on the rise, with many more in clinical trials. These next-generation molecules (Fig 1) offer benefits such as improved efficacy, enhanced selectivity and lower toxicity compared with available treatment options (1) . The structures of these molecules are complex, posing new challenges for both process development and manufacturing. 
Fig 1 . Illustration of the molecular diversity of antibody derivatives.
Antibody-drug conjugates 
One of the most rapidly expanding categories of therapeutic agents in the field of oncology (2) . While not a new concept in itself, there has been a wave of innovation around ADCs. However, developing and manufacturing these therapies poses unique challenges. High-potency antibody-drug conjugates require specific upgrades to ensure safety in operator handling. They also require the management of potential exposure to the highly toxic chemicals used to make payload-linker complexes, the ADC drug substance (DS) and drug product (DP). 
Single-use technologies are beneficial when preparing ADCs, as they can provide a functionally closed and disposable system to protect both operator and product and reduce the risk of cross-contamination between batches. A study to examine extractables in single-use components demonstrated low levels of extractables when exposed to solvents typically used in ADC production. A generic ADC workflow is shown in Figure 2. 
Fig 2. Simple workflow for preparing ADC from bulk mAb.
ADC production begins with the manufacture of the antibody intermediate, which necessitates the development of both upstream and downstream manufacturing capabilities. End-to-end solutions, like the FlexFactory™ biomanufacturing process train, provide options at every level of biomanufacturing—process, equipment, platforms, automation, consumables and services. 
Explore these white papers and web pages on ADCs: 
Exploring the world of antibodies: mAbs, Fabs, dAbs and bsAbs 
A translational perspective: Biacore™ systems in discovery and early-stage development of biotherapeutic antibodies 
Biacore surface plasmon resonance systems in late-stage development and quality control of biotherapeutic drugs 
Simulating chromatography processes with mechanistic modeling 
Cytotoxic drug filling 
Multispecific antibodies 
Bispecific antibodies are unique in that they can bind to two antigens or to two binding sites on a single antigen. Trispecifics and other multispecific antibodies are also being developed to further extend the number of binding sites. By binding to multiple sites, bispecifics and other multispecifics could enhance efficacy and reduce drug resistance. Bispecifics have been used primarily in oncology applications, but other disease types are being investigated (3) . Many structures are possible within the multispecific antibody umbrella and the complexity makes them challenging to produce and purify. An expanded toolbox of purification solutions, particularly for affinity capture and polishing, can be helpful to address specific needs for these novel molecule types.

Samsung's Exynos processor (Samsung Electronics) 
Samsung Electronics' next-generation Exynos 2700 mobile processor scored nearly 20 percent higher than Qualcomm's top-end Snapdragon chip in an internal multicore CPU test, ahead of its expected debut in the Galaxy S27 series early next year.
The results came from recent in-house benchmark tests comparing the Exynos 2700 with Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, which powers Xiaomi's 18 Pro Max, according to industry sources Sunday.
In Geekbench 6.5, the Exynos 2700 posted a multicore CPU score of around 13,000, compared with roughly 11,000 for Qualcomm's Extreme chip. The Samsung processor also scored about 15 percent higher in Geekbench 7.0 multicore tests.
Qualcomm has introduced two versions of its latest flagship mobile chipset: the top-end Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and the standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6. The Extreme variant powers the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, while the standard version is used in the Xiaomi 18 Pro.
Against the standard Snapdragon chip, the Exynos 2700 scored 44 percent higher in Geekbench 6.5 multicore tests and 36 percent higher in Geekbench 7.0.
The Samsung chip also outperformed Qualcomm's Extreme model in graphics tests, which measure capabilities important for gaming and video playback.
In a test of peak graphics performance under demanding gaming conditions using advanced graphics technologies, the Exynos 2700 scored about 20 percent higher than the Qualcomm chip. It also held a roughly 5 percent lead in a separate test measuring basic graphics processing capabilities in high-end 3D games.
Samsung's System LSI business designs the Exynos family of mobile processors, which handle core computing and graphics tasks in smartphones. The previous-generation Exynos 2600 powers select Galaxy S26 models and the Galaxy Z Flip8.
The Exynos 2700 is expected to be manufactured using Samsung's second-generation 2-nanometer foundry process, known as SF2P. The chip is also expected to feature an upgraded heat path block, packaging technology designed to improve heat dissipation and performance.
"Development of the Exynos 2700 is on track, with the aim of having it used in flagship models," Park Yong-in, president and head of system LSI business, said at a management briefing in June.

What Rio Tinto Group Holders Got Right
Bailey Pemberton

If you had paused on 23 October 2025 and asked whether Rio Tinto Group was worth backing as analysts argued over aging Pilbara assets, copper growth options and decarbonisation costs, the answer over the next twelve months turned out to be very real in your brokerage account. For Rio Tinto Group shareholders, the return over the past year was 22.8%, including dividends. If that decision were in front of you again today, how much weight would you give to long-term critical minerals demand versus the risk of rising project and ESG pressures? 
The move put Rio Tinto Group in the middle of this trade. Scan 16 top copper producer stocks for other companies exposed to it. 
The Argument Rio Tinto Investors Were Actually Having 
The shares cost £53.01 at the start of the period, and you were essentially being asked which Rio Tinto Group story felt more believable. 
The bullish narrative put Fair Value at £67.78, a price that only made sense if its copper, lithium and aluminum push really did support stronger long run earnings. That view leaned on assumptions of 4.6% annual revenue growth and profit margins edging up from 19.1% to 20.0% by 2028. 
The bearish camp saw Fair Value closer to £39.91, a level that reflected concern about aging Pilbara iron ore assets and rising costs. Their assumptions included revenue declining 1.8% a year and margins slipping from 19.1% to 16.9%, with decarbonisation spending and ESG pressures biting into future profits. 
LSE:RIO 1-Year Stock Price Chart What The Results Changed For Rio Tinto Group 
Rio Tinto Group's H1 2026 report gave copper and aluminum optimists fresh support. Revenue was US$31,028m and net income reached US$6,664m, versus US$26,873m and US$4,528m in H1 2025, with net margin moving from 16.8% to 21.5%. Cost and project-risk worriers still had ammunition from rising input and ESG pressures, so the evidence cut both ways. 
The lesson is simple: when a miner leans on a margin story, track net income and net margin in the next set of results and test whether project updates line up with that profitability pitch. 
What Rio Tinto's Recent Run Now Assumes 
Rio Tinto Group trades at £62.31 today after a 22.8% gain over the past year, with this bullish Narrative placing Fair Value above that level based on execution in growth projects and cost discipline. 
The Narrative argues the current price still does not fully credit Rio Tinto translating copper and lithium expansion into durable margins and steadier cash flow through the cycle.

Rio Tinto is a critical minerals story, but the opportunity set extends beyond copper and iron.

MELBOURNE, October 23, 2026 — Rio Tinto will invest US$1.9 billion in Queensland’s Kangwinan bauxite project, replacing aging production while expanding capacity at its Weipa operations.
The miner’s October 23 announcement targets first output in 2029 and full production by 2032. Kangwinan is designed for 20 million tonnes of annual capacity, but Weipa’s overall capacity is expected to reach about 44 million tonnes, against current production of around 38 million.
The project will replace Andoom as that mine approaches the end of its life and help compensate for Gove’s planned production closure in 2029. The capital estimate includes $150 million of early works approved in 2025 and sits within Rio’s existing medium-term capital guidance.
Construction is expected to ramp up in 2027 and support more than 1,300 construction jobs. Rio forecasts an internal rate of return of approximately 22%, based on third-party market forecasts, rather than a guaranteed return.
Reuters reported that the development follows Rio’s agreement last month to acquire the adjacent Aurukun project from Glencore and Mitsubishi, subject to regulatory approvals.
