title: Thermo Fisher Q3 Revenue Hits $12.14 Billion as Shares Touch Record $705 - BigGo Finance
query: ("Thermo Fisher" OR "Thermo Fisher Scientific") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Thermo Fisher Q3 Revenue Hits $12.14 Billion as Shares Touch Record $705
Add preferred source 
Thermo Fisher Scientific reported third-quarter revenue of $12.14 billion, up 9% year over year, with GAAP operating income of $2.263 billion, up 17%, and adjusted operating income of $2.968 billion, up 15%. After the results, the stock touched an intraday record of $705.79, and investment banks including Goldman Sachs and Rothschild raised their target prices to an average of $736.17. Consumables and other laboratory products remain the company's largest revenue source at 52% of sales. Thermo Fisher also opened its first AI automation innovation center in South Korea, where AI is used in cryo-electron microscopy products to cut some manual setup time by about 90%. The company disclosed the Precure research initiative with Mayo Clinic and is advancing clinical-side integration following its $8.875 billion acquisition of Clario.
Key Elements 
Thermo Fisher Scientific Nvidia Clario Mayo Clinic Marc Casper Orbitrap Isora Ion 560 Oracle AstraZeneca Tempus AI 
Thermo Fisher Scientific, the global leader in scientific services, this week delivered its third-quarter report card: quarterly revenue of $12.14 billion, up 9% year over year, and adjusted operating income of $2.968 billion, up 15%. After the results were released, the company's shares opened lower on Oct. 21 local time before rallying sharply, touching an intraday high of $705.79 to set a record. International investment banks including Goldman Sachs and Rothschild subsequently raised their target prices in unison, with the average target now around $736.17.
On the profit side, GAAP operating income for the quarter was $2.263 billion, up 17% year over year, growing faster than revenue, indicating simultaneous improvement in product mix and cost control.
Metric Amount Year-over-year growth 
Quarterly revenue $12.14 billion 9% 
GAAP operating income $2.263 billion 17% 
Adjusted operating income $2.968 billion 15% 
Note: Data from Thermo Fisher Scientific's third-quarter earnings report.
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Marc Casper attributed the growth to the company's ongoing growth strategy and the launch of a batch of high-impact innovative products. On the product front, the company introduced the Orbitrap Isora mass spectrometer — the first Orbitrap system designed specifically for isotope ratio analysis, aimed at extending high-end mass spectrometry applications from life sciences to environmental research. In gene sequencing, it released the Ion 560 sequencing chip, with sequencing capacity nearly double that of previous products, which can improve sample throughput for genomic analysis in oncology research. Mass spectrometry and sequencing are both core tools of wet-lab work in precision medicine, and together they form one of the company's current high-growth curves.
However, as a "pick-and-shovel" supplier upstream in the pharmaceutical supply chain, Thermo Fisher's largest revenue source remains laboratory products such as consumables, culture media and single-use bioprocessing, which account for as much as 52% of total revenue. The company explained its business logic at its 2024 investor day: a long-accumulated installed base of instruments will continue to drive consumables purchases, and consumables and services are the core components of revenue.
AI push extends from instruments to the clinical side 
Artificial intelligence has been the area the company has focused on most over the past two years. The third-quarter report disclosed that the company has opened its first AI automation innovation center in South Korea, integrating analytical technology, automation and AI to help customers shorten R&D cycles. Management said AI technology has been used in cryo-electron microscopy products such as Krios 5 and Glacios 3, cutting the time required for some manual setup steps by about 90%.
In January this year, Thermo Fisher and Nvidia announced a strategic collaboration aimed at using AI to advance the evolution of scientific instruments and improve overall laboratory performance. Gianluca Pettiti, executive vice president of Thermo Fisher, said in the announcement: "AI combined with laboratory automation will reshape how research is done. We can help customers improve experimental efficiency and accuracy, extract more value from every experiment, and ultimately accelerate scientific discoveries of major value." Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare at Nvidia, said the industry is entering the era of "lab-in-the-loop," where AI, agents and instruments come together to scale scientific discovery at industrial speed.
The collaboration points to underlying infrastructure: building automated laboratories for customers that can connect to AI systems, supporting high-throughput experimental iteration and new drug development.
But Thermo Fisher is clearly not content to be just a pick-and-shovel supplier. The third-quarter report also disclosed the Precure research initiative jointly launched with Mayo Clinic. The project will integrate longitudinal clinical sample data from more than one million patients and conduct multi-omics research relying on Orbitrap mass spectrometry and the Olink proteomics platform to capture biological signals in the early stages of disease, connecting molecular markers to real-world patient clinical phenotypes and serving early disease screening, target discovery and diagnostic solution development.
On merger integration, Casper provided an update on Clario: the business is operating smoothly, integration is proceeding as expected, revenue synergies are gradually being released, and the company will subsequently fold Clario's capabilities into its own clinical development services system. Clario is a leading global provider of clinical trial endpoint evidence services, covering digital endpoint solutions such as centralized blinded imaging review, patient outcome data collection and cardiac safety assessment. In March this year, Thermo Fisher completed its acquisition of Clario for $8.875 billion, aiming to extend its capabilities from the wet lab to the clinical side and form a closed loop.
Competitive focus shifts toward the clinical stage 
At the industry level, the competitive focus of global innovative drug R&D is extending from front-end target discovery to the clinical stage, and the combination of AI and real-world data has become the latest battleground. On Oct. 20, Oracle and AstraZeneca announced a collaboration to explore the use of AI and real-world data to identify patients eligible for clinical trials, accelerate medical evidence generation and embed research results into daily clinical workflows. On Oct. 8, AI healthcare company Tempus AI announced multi-year collaborations with Moderna and MSD, under which Tempus will handle tumor sample collection, NGS sequencing and patient molecular typing to screen subjects suitable for therapies, supporting vaccine development and commercialization.
Brokerage views point in the same direction. AVIC Securities believes that from a commercialization perspective, the main constraint on healthcare AI is shifting from model capability to clinical evidence and system integration capacity, and companies able to connect data, models, workflows, physician confirmation and continuous monitoring are more likely to form replicable delivery models. Orient Securities said the real bottleneck in new drug R&D lies in finding a biological mechanism whose intervention can change the course of a patient's disease; AI represented by virtual cells and virtual humans is expected to solve this problem — AI finds mechanisms that hold true in both human and cellular data, achieving a correct closed loop in drugmaking and growing stronger with each iteration, ultimately bringing a systemic restructuring of R&D productivity and turning drug discovery from a craft highly dependent on individual scientists' intuition into a scalable, iterable and predictable industrial process.
For investors, Thermo Fisher's valuation support is shifting from the stable cash flow of "instruments + consumables" to a growth narrative of "AI-automated laboratories + clinical data services." If the dry-wet loop and clinical-side integration land smoothly, the company is expected to occupy a more forward position in pharmaceutical customers' R&D outsourcing chain. However, AI-related revenue has not yet been disclosed separately, and the pace of scaling the clinical data business, as well as integration costs after large acquisitions, remain key variables that subsequent earnings reports will need to verify.

Sasha Jovanovic

Dow Inc. reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$11.27b and net income of US$458m, with earnings per share ahead of analyst expectations. 
The latest quarter shows Dow's pricing actions and cost savings programs contributing to higher earnings, while the firm continues a century long dividend record. 
This article examines how Dow's investment narrative is influenced by earnings exceeding forecasts as cost reduction initiatives gain visible traction. 
Scan how Dow's self help earnings story compares with other potential compounders in our hand picked list of 29 high quality undervalued stocks . 
Dow Investment Narrative Recap 
To own Dow, you need to believe that its self help plan in costs and portfolio mix can matter more than a choppy macro and feedstock backdrop. The latest quarter supports that thesis at an operating level, with pricing, higher earnings and cost savings all visible in the reported numbers. That helps the credibility of Dow's multi year efficiency and transformation targets. 
The key near term swing factor stays the same: execution on the US$1.3b of planned self help benefits and broader US$3b structural program, while managing energy and raw material pressures. Margin risk from elevated input costs and softer polyethylene demand is still the main operational overhang, even after this strong print. 
The most relevant fresh data point is the third quarter earnings beat, with US$11.27b in sales and US$458m in net income, plus adjusted EPS ahead of forecasts. Strength in Packaging & Specialty Plastics, helped by polyethylene pricing, and progress on cost reduction show the transformation program feeding into reported profit, not just slideware. 
For catalysts, this matters because Dow has laid out explicit targets for US$700m of growth and productivity benefits in 2026 and about US$2b of uplift by 2027. Better than expected earnings give management more room to prioritize debt reduction, fund projects like Alberta polyethylene and silicones upgrades, and still support an ongoing dividend, while interest coverage and litigation risks remain important to track. 
Dow Earnings Assumptions and Analyst Framework 
Analysts sketch a long term picture for Dow that leans heavily on gradual revenue growth and a sharp earnings recovery by the late 2020s. Forecasts point to revenue growth of 2.3% per year over the next three years, with profit margins moving from a loss position today to a mid single digit level as cost programs and mix shifts work through the income statement. The consensus view has earnings moving from a current loss of US$1.3b to US$2.1b by 2029, which is a value change of US$3.4b and implies a very large swing in profitability if the self help agenda lands as planned. 
Story Continues 
Dow's narrative projects US$44.3b revenue and US$2.1b earnings by 2029. This assumes 2.3% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of US$3.4b from current earnings of a US$1.3b loss. 
That earnings path sits at the core of how analysts are framing Dow today because the implied P/E also flips from loss making to a positive multiple on those 2029 numbers. The reporting suggests the shares would need to trade around 15.8x earnings on the consensus profit estimate to line up with current price targets. This is below the cited 21.3x P/E level for the wider US chemicals peer group. For readers, the key question becomes straightforward: do those revenue and margin assumptions feel reasonable given Dow's cost out plan, capital projects and the pressures still visible in polyethylene and energy markets right now?

Qualcomm RF Front End Expansion: Beyond Smartphones
Radu Trandafir
Cristiano Amon was excited and proud to announce Qualcomm Technologies’ deep forays into the automotive, Metaverse, PC and edge computing markets at CES 2022, in January.
 
Now we have the chance to hear directly from one of the key business units about Qualcomm’s world beyond mobiles: Christian Block, SVP and General Manager of Qualcomm’s RF Front End (FE) business unit presented how the modem-to-antenna solutions developed initially for smartphones and mobile communications are penetrating other key areas where data exchanges are happening wirelessly: automotive, IoT & edge networking, personal computing, wearables and extended reality (XR), and industrial IoT.
Having a true end-to-end, modem-to-antenna solution and capitalizing on the benefits of having developed class-leading mobile applications with integrated baseband (BB) processors/modems, there is nothing missing from Qualcomm’s portfolio.
Figure 1: Qualcomm’s modem-to-antenna device portfolio coverage (Source: Qualcomm Technologies Inc.) 
The “modem-to antenna” solution is not just a well garnished portfolio of stand-alone components, rather a well thought out, holistic system design, where RF H/W and BB processing together with other algorithms like SmartTransmit 2.0, work seamlessly to deliver their best performance.
Subscribe to TechInsights Blogs
Join our list to get the latest blog posts directly in your email.
There is still room for 3 rd party RF FE components to substitute some of Qualcomm’s own to better suit the OEM’s needs, however, it is to be expected that the Qualcomm modem + transceiver combinations perform at their best when used with the rest of the Qualcomm RF FE family.
Figure 2: The near future is bright, here are the projections for the RF FE business unit for the 2022 to 2024 interval. “In fiscal year 2021, Qualcomm Technologies reached the #1 position in RFFE revenues for handsets.” (Source: Qualcomm Technologies Inc.) 
Even though the specifications for IEEE 802.11be are still with the standards working groups – and it wouldn’t surprise us to learn that the modems are ready to receive updated firmware (F/W) loads to make them compatible with the standard when it will be released, Qualcomm is ready with their 3 rd generation of RF FE components which are being introduced today.
These are LNA – PA combo for WiFi applications, with and without RF shields, designed for 5G coexistence, “complement(ing) Qualcomm® ultraBAW™ filters to allow 5G/Wi-Fi concurrency” and are “purpose-built design(s) for Wi-Fi 6E/7 (to) showcase the Company’s leadership in both wireless technologies” .
Figure 3: Source: Qualcomm Technologies Inc. 
Introducing the 3 rd generation Qualcomm WiFi 6e/7 and Bluetooth RF FE modules: the QXM108x family and QXM1910AQ. “ The modules are designed for a wide array of device segments beyond smartphones – including automotive, XR, PCs, wearables, mobile broadband, IoT, and more .”
Figure 4: Third generation RF FE components Wi-Fi7 ready (Source: Qualcomm Technologies Inc.) 
The newly announced FE modules are expected to launch in H2 2022 but modules are already sampling to customers. These modules can be used “along with Qualcomm Technologies’ client connectivity products, such as Qualcomm® FastConnectTM 7800 Wi-Fi 7/Bluetooth Systems and Snapdragon® 5G Modem-RF Systems – for cutting-edge wireless devices such as those featuring Snapdragon® Connect. Or they can use 3rd party Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chipsets along with the modules.”

Hexagon AB (HXGBF) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Highlights: Record 13% Organic Growth, Margin ...
GuruFocus News 
October 23, 2026 
HEXA-B.ST 
-0.09% 
HXGBF 
0.00% 
This article first appeared on GuruFocus . 
Organic Growth: Accelerated to 13%, highest level in five years; all business areas grew. 
Net Sales: Reached EUR1.05 billion, up EUR73 million year-on-year (organic growth of ~EUR121 million, offset by EUR68 million divestment impact and boosted by EUR20 million currency). 
Gross Margin: Held stable at around 62%, same as last year despite 20% growth in sensor sales. 
EBIT AC Margin (excl. robotics): Rose to 25.3%, up from 23.1% a year ago; up 450 bps like-to-like excluding one-offs, and up 100 bps sequentially. 
EBIT AC (excl. robotics): EUR265 million in the quarter. 
EBITDA-C Margin (incl. robotics): 24% versus 22.5% a year ago, reflecting higher robotics investment (EUR13 million vs. EUR6 million in 2025). 
Organic EBITDA-C Growth: ~16% faster than sales; ~28% excluding last year's large one-off defense order. 
Cash Conversion: 82% in the quarter, reflecting normal seasonality. 
Operating Cash Flow: EUR208 million pre-tax; EUR119 million after taxes, interest, and non-recurring items. 
Adjusted EPS: EUR8.2, up 19% from EUR6.9 a year ago. 
Effective Tax Rate: 18.7%, slightly below the 19%21% guidance range. 
Net Debt: Fell from EUR532 million to EUR489 million during the quarter. 
Cost-Saving Program: Full contribution reached EUR18.5 million in Q3. 
Manufacturing Intelligence: 16% organic growth; EBIT-C margin up 310 bps to 25.2% (excluding D&E business). 
Infrastructure & Geospatial: 4% organic growth (up from 1% a year ago); EBITDA-C margin up 120 bps to 23.7%. 
Autonomous Solutions: 23% organic growth, strongest quarter ever; EBITDA-C margin up 250 bps to 31.5%. 
Regional Growth: EMEA +17%, China +15%, rest of Asia +14%, Americas +6%. 
Sensor Sales: Led product categories with 20% growth. 
Waygate Acquisition: ~EUR631 million revenue at ~10% EBIT (2025 figures); expected to dilute Group EBIT AC margin by ~150 bps and MI margin by ~300 bps initially; closing expected in Q4. 
Guidance Marine Acquisition: ~EUR22 million revenue in 2025; expected to close in Q4. 
Rock Science Acquisition: ~EUR50 million revenue; expected to close in Q4. 
Pro Forma Combined (LTM incl. acquisitions): Revenue ~EUR4.7 billion (from EUR4.0 billion); EBITDA-C ~EUR1 billion (from ~EUR0.9 billion); net debt/EBITDA ~1.4x (from ~0.3x), well below the 2.5x threshold.

HXGBF GF Value chart Release Date: October 23, 2026 
For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript . 
Story Continues 
Positive Points 
Hexagon AB ( HXGBF ) achieved 13% organic growth, the highest in five years, with broad-based growth across all business areas. 
EBIT AC margin, excluding robotics, rose to 25.3%, up 450 basis points year-over-year on a like-to-like basis, driven by cost savings and organic growth. 
Autonomous Solutions delivered record 23% organic growth, driven by strong demand for anti-jamming solutions and defense applications. 
Manufacturing Intelligence grew 16% organically with strong order intake, particularly in general manufacturing, aerospace, and electronics. 
Hexagon AB ( HXGBF ) maintains strong financial firepower with net debt/EBITDA of 1.4x post-acquisitions, well below the 2.5x threshold, enabling further M&A. 
Negative Points 
Waygate acquisition is expected to be dilutive to group EBIT margin by 150 basis points and MI margin by 300 basis points initially. 
Automotive market in China remains weak, with no clear recovery expected in the near term. 
Agriculture segment remains weak due to high fuel and fertilizer costs, with only 2% of sales. 
Tariff refunds were offset by headwinds from memory costs, semiconductor shortages, and higher transportation costs. 
Humanoid robotics (Aon) investments are increasing significantly, with $70-80 million expected in 2027, and profitability not expected until after 2031. 
Q & A Highlights 
Q : Simon Granath of ABG asked about the book-to-bill in Manufacturing Intelligence (MI) versus Q2 and visibility into 2027, specifically whether recent strong demand trends could reverse or cool off. A : CEO Anders Svensson explained that MI's book-to-bill is "basically flattish," with sales and order intake equally strong. Autonomous Solutions is considerably stronger on order intake than sales, and Infrastructure & Geospatial also has a positive book-to-bill. For 2027, he sees no dramatic demand changes: strong areas like aerospace, defense, electronics, and general manufacturing appear very stable, while weak sectors like agriculture, automotive, and construction are not expected to improve in the short term, as large markets don't shift from weak to strong in just one or two quarters. 
Q : Phil Buller of JPMorgan asked about the investment profile for Aon (humanoid robotics) into 2027, given the move into production and new customer additions, and whether the new customers are Europe-based. A : CEO Anders Svensson confirmed the new customers are Europe-based, chosen partly for proximity to the home base and R&D team, though they have global operations. On investment, he guided that Aon required $25 million last year, will end 2026 at $4550 million, and will likely rise to $7080 million in 2027 (not yet confirmed). Revenues will start next year through a mix of robot sales and robot-as-a-service models. He expects the project to break even around 2031, with humanoid sales taking off around 2032 as the market grows exponentially, and Hexagon intends to invest what is required to hold its strong position. 
Q : Phil Buller of JPMorgan asked about the geographic growth picture, noting EMEA, Asia, and China drove growth well above the U.S., and whether there is any change in tone or customer behavior in any region heading into Q4. A : CEO Anders Svensson highlighted 17% growth in EMEA, 15% in China, and 14% in the rest of Asia as encouraging. The Americas' 6% growth was depressed by a large one-off autonomous solutions defense order in the prior-year comparison; excluding it, group growth would have been 16% instead of 13%, and Americas would be significantly higher. He sees continued strong demand in North America and expects that to continue in coming quarters, with no slowdown observed. 
Q : Meihan Yang of Goldman Sachs asked for color on the acceleration of Autonomous Solutions' organic growth despite tough prior-year comparables, whether it will continue in Q4, and for the magnitude and division split of the tariff refund benefit. A : CEO Anders Svensson attributed the growth mainly to high demand for anti-jamming antennas, primarily in Europe, driven by countries re-equipping and modernizing defense amid the war on Europe's eastern border, plus applications for airplanes and marine. He noted Sweden's position helps win EU orders and that Europe's rearmament will take several years, providing a long positive tailwind, with some prior-year order effect lingering into Q4. CFO Enrique Patrickson said the tariff refund benefit (roughly 7090 basis points) was largely offset by headwinds of similar magnitude from memory/chip costs, Iran effects, and higher transportation costs, with the biggest impacts in IMG and MI, while in Autonomous Solutions much of the tariff was paid directly by customers. 
Q : Simon Granath of ABG asked for the rationale behind the sizable Rock Science acquisition, including pricing given that public software multiples have fallen. A : CEO Anders Svensson said Rock Science is a leading geotechnical analysis software company that perfectly complements Hexagon's radar monitoring of slopes, bridges, and tunnels by adding simulation of future movement, plus mining planning tools. He noted the acquisition multiple is very similar to Hexagon's own multiple (neither accretive nor dilutive), while Rock Science has a much stronger growth trajectory than the group, 80% recurring revenue, and an EBIT AC margin north of 40%, making it a clear value creation opportunity. 
Q : Daniel Djurberg of Handelsbanken asked whether the surprisingly strong automotive segment (about 10% of revenues, with growth in the Americas and positive in EMEA and rest of Asia, negative only in China) marks the beginning of a more positive trend or a temporary effect. A : CEO Anders Svensson said China's automotive manufacturing is declining amid large inventories of battery vehicles, with the highest-ever inventory of electric cars in Europe as Chinese players offload globally. Rest of Asia and EMEA show positive but single-digit effects with improved orders and sales. North America is very strong, likely driven by announced 50% tariffs on imported cars from January 1, which spur local manufacturing investment and reshoringa trend he believes is here to stay. He expects Europe to recover while China remains weaker for some time before turning. 
Q : Daniel Djurberg of Handelsbanken asked whether Hexagon has a ballpark timeline for improving Waygate's margins toward the MI level of 2124%. A : CEO Anders Svensson said a plan exists but it is too early to disclose externally. Hexagon first wants to include the company, get to know its people, and develop the plan together with them, since theynot managementwill execute it and must own the improvements. The company will communicate externally once that is done.

Positive Points 
Norsk Hydro ASA ( NHYDY ) delivered strong operational performance with record high liquid metal production at Norwegian smelters and stable alumina production despite gas supply disruptions. 
Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026 came in at NOK9.1 billion, with adjusted ROCE at 12.5%, well above the 10% target over the cycle. 
The company is making strategic progress in low-carbon and recycled aluminum, signing partnerships with Chanel, General Motors, and Mercedes-Benz, and achieving first aluminum production at the HalZero test facility. 
Norsk Hydro ASA ( NHYDY ) secured new long-term power purchase agreements with Statkraft and Babak Energy, adding 8.9 TWh towards 2040 and covering around 90% of Norwegian baseline power consumption in the 2030s. 
Extrusion sales volumes increased by 3% year-over-year, and recycling results remained strong, with improved results in Europe compensating for weaker U.S. performance. 
Story Continues 
Negative Points 
Safety metrics deteriorated with both TRI and HRI rates creeping up from record lows, requiring intensified efforts to achieve zero injuries and high-risk incidents. 
The gas supply disruption at Alunorte led to a financial impact of approximately $85 million in Q3, with an estimated $90-110 million negative impact expected in Q4 due to spot LNG purchases at elevated prices. 
Free cash flow was NOK1.4 billion, affected by a net operating capital build of NOK3.7 billion, and the company revised year-end net operating capital outlook up to around NOK32 billion from NOK30 billion.

Hydro sells a mix of products, with standard ingot carrying the lowest underlying premiums sold later in the quarter, so realized premiums typically come in below locked-in premiums. He also noted extrusion ingot premiums, which started above $1,000 some weeks back, are now around $850 and trending down, partly affecting the estimated realized premium for the quarter. 
Q : Regarding the Alunorte gas contract, will you issue indicative EBITDA scenarios or cost guidance at the November Capital Markets Day based on spot LNG prices? A : CEO Eivind Kallevik said Hydro has provided Q4 guidance as it currently sees it, and it will be natural to give a status update at the Investor Day, including commentary on the development of secured long-term contracts at that point in time. 
Q : What is your expectation for replacing the long-term Alunorte gas contracts? Hydro has guided for spot purchases in Q4 and will update the market on progress at the Investor Day in November.

A : The CFO said Qatalum is currently operating at around 60% of capacity, with the top priority being the safety of people in Qatar during the Middle East crisis. A stable setup for raw material inflows is in place, metal is now flowing out of the plant, and sales volumes are roughly in line with current production. The market will be updated when the picture changes. CEO Eivind Kallevik added that Hydro has a long-term gas supply agreement in Qatar, so no changes to the cost base are expected from that perspective. 
Q : What TTF price is embedded in the Alunorte guidance? A : The CFO said the guidance is based on the TTF price as read off the screens, which forms the basis for current spot purchases. Further guidance will come at the Investor Day, based on market development and progress on long-term gas sourcing.

Graco’s ETM and ABB Partner on Motor Technology for Data Center Cooling
The partners aim to install TFM-based direct-drive systems in data centers by the end of 2029, targeting reliability and simpler maintenance.
October 23, 2026 
Created by Refindustry using AI 
Electric Torque Machines (ETM), a wholly owned subsidiary of Graco Inc., has signed a technology license agreement with ABB to develop motor solutions for data center cooling towers and heat rejection systems. The agreement covers ETM’s patented Transverse Flux Motor (TFM) technology and expands an existing collaboration between the companies in industrial applications.
ETM’s TFM architecture is designed for high-torque, low-speed applications requiring efficient direct-drive operation. The technology can reduce mechanical complexity and the number of drivetrain components in cooling systems, potentially simplifying maintenance and supporting reliability requirements in data center environments.
Under the agreement, ABB and ETM will develop TFM-based products for cooling towers, heat rejection equipment, and related thermal management applications. The companies are targeting their first installations in data center environments by the end of 2029.
The collaboration will include product development, application engineering, customer qualification, and market development. ABB will contribute its market reach, distribution channels, and customer relationships, while ETM will provide its motor technology.
“Our work with ETM has shown the potential of direct-drive motor systems, and we are pleased to expand that work into cooling applications where performance and uptime matter,” said Jesse Henson, President, NEMA Motors, ABB.

content_text:
[News] Infineon and NVIDIA Expand GaN Power Collaboration for AI Data Centers
2026-10-23 
Emerging Technologies 
editor 
On October 21, Infineon Technologies announced an expanded collaboration with NVIDIA in AI data center power delivery during NVIDIA’s GTC developer conference in Berlin. The two companies will jointly develop high-voltage intermediate bus converter (IBC) solutions based on gallium nitride (GaN) power devices for 800V direct current (800V DC) architectures.
The expanded collaboration builds on the companies’ 800V DC power delivery initiative launched in 2025. It focuses on power conversion for high-power AI racks and will also support hot-swappable server rack maintenance.
The high-voltage IBC is a key component in the AI data center power delivery chain. Leveraging its CoolGaN product portfolio, Infineon will address multiple conversion configurations, including 800V-to-50V and 800V-to-12V, using high-frequency switching technology. The solutions are intended for NVIDIA’s MGX open modular reference architecture for AI factories.
The power architecture is designed for AI computing systems with power consumption of up to 1 MW per rack, with deployment expected to begin gradually in 2027.
Infineon and NVIDIA first announced their collaboration on 800V DC data center power delivery in May 2025. The initial initiative covered both silicon carbide (SiC) and GaN technologies.
The latest expansion places greater emphasis on GaN for intermediate bus conversion. The solutions aim to increase power density, reduce power losses across the delivery chain, and lower cooling hardware requirements. They are also designed to enable controlled pre-charging and discharging of server motherboards, as well as hot-swapping while the rack remains operational, helping reduce the risk of service disruptions during data center maintenance.
Beyond GaN-based IBCs, Infineon is supplying SiC devices, power protection components, and other power products for NVIDIA’s 800V DC ecosystem, covering the power delivery chain from the grid to AI processors.
NVIDIA’s 800V DC architecture is intended to simplify the multiple AC-to-DC and DC-to-DC conversion stages used in conventional data centers, reducing the number of conversion stages and associated components.
The ecosystem brings together power semiconductor suppliers, power system manufacturers, and data center infrastructure providers. Infineon is among the suppliers participating in the ecosystem with portfolios spanning SiC, GaN, and silicon-based power devices.

Hydro earnings rise year on year
The recycled-content aluminum producer saw net income rise more than 140 percent year on year in the third quarter.
“We continue to see strong demand for our low-carbon and recycled offerings from some of the world’s leading consumer brands,” says the CEO of Norsk Hydro.
Photo courtesy of Norsk Hydro ASA 
By
Brian Taylor, Senior Editor 
Published October 23, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
Norsk Hydro ASA, a Norway-based aluminum and energy producer with recycling-focused operations in the United States , says its third-quarter net income rose by 141 percent compared with one year earlier, though its profits declined by about 12 percent.
“Higher all-in metal prices and higher alumina prices contributed positively in the quarter, along with improved earnings in Recycling and Extrusions,” the company says, referring to a business unit that includes aluminum recycling as a major part of its operations. 
The company says its otherwise strong performance was offset partially by “higher anode and energy costs in Aluminum Metal, increased energy costs in Bauxite & Alumina due to gas supply disruptions, a stronger Norwegian krone versus U.S. dollar, and negative price area differences in Energy,” referring to several other of its business units.
“Hydro’s third-quarter results reflect strong operational performance amplified by market tailwinds,” says Eivind Kallevik, president and CEO of Hydro. “Record high liquid metal production from our Norwegian smelter system, combined with strong pricing throughout the quarter, drove solid earnings and strong profitability.”
She adds, “Operational excellence enables us to capture more of the upside when markets are strong and, more importantly, builds resilience when markets turn.”
The firm says its Aluminum Metal business unit, which includes primary aluminum production, benefited from higher metal prices while Recycling and Extrusions delivered improved earnings supported by strong recycling margins. 
“We continue to see strong demand for our low-carbon and recycled offerings from some of the world’s leading consumer brands,” Kallevik says. “When brands like Chanel Fragrances and Beauty  and Mercedes-Benz choose Hydro , they place their trust in our quality, reliability, and ability to help them achieve their ambitions. That trust has commercial value and reinforces our confidence in the long-term opportunities for low-carbon and recycled aluminum.”
Hydro  says adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) in its Extrusions business increased about 7.5 percent year on year in the third quarter of 2026 “driven by higher recycling margins in combination with increased sales volume, partly offset by higher maintenance costs.”
The company cites metals consulting firm CRU as estimating that European extrusion demand increased by 1 percent in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the same quarter last year, while North American extrusion demand was “broadly unchanged” year on year.

content_text:
Moderna Shares Plunge 26% Despite Cancer Vaccine Success
Shares of U.S. pharmaceutical company Moderna plummeted by up to 26% during intraday trading on October 22 (local time), marking the largest intraday decline in the company’s stock history. The drop followed the premature disclosure of clinical trial results for a personalized cancer vaccine co-developed with U.S. pharmaceutical company MSD, which showed lower efficacy compared to earlier studies. MSD’s stock also fell by 3.9% at one point.
◇Detailed Results Released in August
The personalized cancer vaccine developed by the two companies is called **Intismeran Autogen**. It analyzes a patient’s tumor tissue to identify mutations unique to their cancer cells, which are then encoded into mRNA to create a customized vaccine. Each patient receives a distinct vaccine tailored to their specific cancer. The vaccine is designed to be used in combination with the immunotherapy drug Keytruda.
In August, the companies announced the **topline results** (key indicator results) of a Phase 3 clinical trial involving over 1,100 melanoma patients. At the time, they stated the trial had met its primary goal, causing Moderna’s stock to surge. Specific data was initially withheld for a later academic presentation. However, oncology-focused media outlet *Oncology Central* reported the detailed results ahead of schedule, prompting the companies to release them early.
Patients who received the vaccine alongside Keytruda saw a 42% lower risk of cancer recurrence or death compared to those who received only Keytruda. The risk of metastasis or death was reduced by 38%. After two years, 82.2% of patients in the vaccine group remained cancer-free, compared to 70% in the Keytruda-only group.
Despite the clinical success, the market reacted negatively to the numbers. Earlier Phase 2b trials had shown a 49% reduction in recurrence/death risk and a 59% reduction in metastasis/death risk. The Phase 3 results fell short of these figures. Combined with the unexpected data leak, investors rushed to sell shares, eroding gains from previous rallies.
◇“Not a Failure, but Higher Expectations”
The results still confirm the trial’s success. Wall Street analysts had previously stated that a risk reduction of over 40% in Phase 3 would be viewed positively—a threshold the trial exceeded. Direct comparisons between Phase 2b and Phase 3 are also challenging due to differences in patient demographics and observation periods.
Market attention is now shifting to the full clinical data set, set to be presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) conference in Madrid on October 24. Analysts will scrutinize statistical significance, safety profiles, and outcomes across patient subgroups.

title: [Interview] Bayer sees Korea as key co-innovation partner, eyes deeper drug development ties - Korea Biomedical Review
query: ("Bayer" OR "Bayer AG") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:

[Interview] Bayer sees Korea as key co-innovation partner, eyes deeper drug development ties 
바로가기 
복사하기 
본문 글씨 줄이기 
본문 글씨 키우기 
스크롤 이동 상태바 
Bayer is seeking to deepen partnerships with Korean pharmaceutical and biotech companies in global drug development, viewing Korea as a key market for co-innovation.
The German pharmaceutical company sees growing opportunities for collaboration, citing Korea's strong clinical trial infrastructure and the rapid convergence of digital and data-driven technologies with life sciences.
"Korean pharmaceutical and biotech companies are making an increasingly significant contribution to the global drug development pipeline," Stefan Oelrich, president of Bayer's Pharmaceuticals Division and a member of the Board of Management of Bayer AG, said in a recent interview with Korea Biomedical Review (KBR).
"Across Asia, including Korea, Bayer is actively identifying promising biotech and pharmaceutical collaboration opportunities aligned with its strategic focus areas," he said.
Bayer's launch of its Co.Lab Connect open innovation platform in Seoul this year reflects its interest in Korea's innovation potential. External partnerships are already central to the company's growth strategy, with four of its six blockbuster assets originating from collaborations or acquisitions. Bayer is also expanding into new therapeutic modalities, including cell and gene therapies, targeted protein modulation, and radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT).
Oelrich also stressed that sustaining innovation requires a shift in how its value is assessed and rewarded. Rather than considering spending on medicines in isolation, he argued that evaluations should take into account broader healthcare outcomes, including the prevention of disease recurrence and progression and reductions in hospitalization and long-term care needs.
He said Korea, with its rapidly aging population, advanced healthcare system, strong digital capabilities, and extensive healthcare data, is particularly well positioned to lead the development of an outcomes-based approach to assessing the value of medical innovation.
KBR spoke with Oelrich about Bayer's innovation strategy and opportunities for collaboration with Korean companies.
Stefan Oelrich, president of Bayer's Pharmaceuticals Division and a member of the Board of Management of Bayer AG, speaks during a recent interview with Korea Biomedical Review in Seoul. (Courtesy of Bayer Korea) 
Korean biotech firms play growing role in global drug development 
Question: What brings you to Korea on this visit? 
Answer: I am a member of the Board of Management of Bayer AG and President of Bayer's Pharmaceuticals Division. I also serve as President of the European Federation of Pharmaceutical Industries and Associations (EFPIA).
I attended EFPIA Japan Day, an event hosted by EFPIA in Japan, where I met with representatives from the government and public sector. As part of this visit to Asia, I also wanted to visit Korea in person, given its growing importance to the global pharmaceutical industry.
Q: Compared with neighboring countries such as Japan and China, how do you assess the competitiveness of Korea's pharmaceutical and biotech industry? 
A: Healthcare systems differ significantly from country to country, so we need to be cautious when making direct comparisons. In Asia, Japan has long established itself as a major player in the global pharmaceutical industry, while China is emerging as one of the world's most important sources of biotech innovation.
Korea, too, has a highly advanced healthcare system, something Koreans can rightly take great pride in. Korea not only boasts world-class healthcare infrastructure but also has a dynamic innovation ecosystem where digital and data-driven technologies are rapidly converging with life sciences.
In particular, Bayer sees Korea as a market where the value of innovation can be translated quickly into tangible outcomes for patients and healthcare. Korean pharmaceutical and biotech companies are also making an increasingly significant contribution to the global drug development pipeline.
In fact, as of 2024, Korea ranked sixth globally in terms of its share of global clinical trials, with Seoul ranking second among cities worldwide. Korea is also one of the global leaders in biopharmaceutical pipeline activity, with 3,233 drug candidates in development, the third-highest total globally after the U.S. and China.
An increasing number of innovative drug candidates from Korean companies are being licensed out and co-developed with global pharmaceutical companies, creating a strong foundation for co-innovation.
Q: Do you see opportunities for Bayer to expand its partnerships with Korean companies? 
A: Across Asia, including Korea, Bayer is actively identifying promising biotech and pharmaceutical collaboration opportunities aligned with its strategic focus areas.
The launch of Bayer Co.Lab Connect in Korea is also a strong reflection of Bayer's confidence in the country's innovation potential.
The Korean government has clearly expressed its intention to support R&D and innovation in both academia and the private sector and to promote the growth of the pharmaceutical industry. Its efforts also appear to extend beyond fostering the domestic industry to expanding opportunities for Korean companies to enter overseas markets. Bayer is watching these developments with great interest.
Much of human biology remains unexplored. As our understanding of biology and digital science deepens, there is considerable potential for further innovative discoveries. Against this backdrop, it makes sense for Korea to invest actively in these fields.
Q: How does Bayer's open innovation strategy work in practice? 
A: We believe Bayer's role in open innovation is to nurture the biotech ecosystem and support translational medicine. This means helping academic research translate into actual treatments and, ultimately, enabling promising research to develop into startups.
To support this, Bayer operates Bayer Co.Lab in major innovation hubs around the world, with locations in Berlin, Germany; Cambridge, the United States; Kobe and Tokyo, Japan; and Shanghai and Beijing, China. In 2026, Bayer also launched Bayer Co.Lab Connect in Seoul and Switzerland.
Bayer Co.Lab supports early-stage startups in advancing their R&D by providing access to world-class expertise, resources, and a global network. As Bayer carefully selects participating companies, the program also gives us an opportunity to identify and evaluate promising assets at an early stage.
Another important pillar is Leaps by Bayer, Bayer's venture investment arm. Unlike conventional venture capital firms, it invests based on strategic objectives rather than financial returns alone. Its investments focus on areas of high unmet medical need, such as rare cancers and serious diseases that are difficult to address with existing treatment approaches.
External innovation behind 4 of Bayer's 6 blockbusters, with BD&L central to growth 
Q: Bayer has recently revised its R&D strategy. What will be the company's key growth drivers over the next five years? 
A: Bayer has built its strongest-ever pharmaceutical portfolio, centered on innovative treatments with blockbuster potential. We have also established a differentiated pipeline in areas of high unmet medical need and are entering a new phase of growth.
In 2025, we received five first approvals, including three new product approvals and two new indications, and achieved positive results in six phase 3 clinical trials.
We plan to sustain our growth through our Five Growth Catalysts. The first is Nubeqa, a treatment for prostate cancer. This is followed by Kerendia, which received an indication for chronic kidney disease associated with type 2 diabetes and was subsequently approved for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Lynkuet, a treatment for vasomotor symptoms (VMS) associated with menopause, is currently being launched in markets around the world. Beyonttra, a treatment for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), has also been launched in selected European markets. Finally, asundexian, which is being developed for secondary stroke prevention. Eylea 8 mg, a key treatment for retinal diseases, is also continuing to deliver solid growth in most markets worldwide.
Bayer currently has more than 30 projects in clinical development or regulatory review, including five phase 3 trials, eight phase 2 trials, 16 phase 1 trials, and six regulatory submissions. Against this backdrop, Bayer expects to return to mid-single-digit growth from 2027 onwards. We also anticipate subsequent improvements in operating profitability, with an ambition to achieve an operating margin of around 30 percent by 2030.
Q: Are M&A and external partnerships becoming increasingly important in securing new therapeutic modalities? 
A: Many medicines that reach the pharmaceutical market originate from external partnerships. Eylea and Nubeqa, for example, are products that Bayer secured through partnerships.
Business development and licensing (BD&L) is already a core growth driver for us. Our track record shows that external innovation matters: four of Bayer's six blockbuster assets originated from external partnerships or acquisitions.
In cell and gene therapy, Bayer has strengthened its capabilities through the acquisitions of AskBio and BlueRock Therapeutics, with multiple candidates from both companies having advanced into clinical development. BlueRock's bemdaneprocel is in phase 3 development for Parkinson's disease, while AskBio's AB-1002 is in phase 2 development for congestive heart failure.
Another notable example is Vividion Therapeutics, which is developing precision-targeted protein modulation technologies. Vividion has a platform that enables researchers to target proteins that were previously considered "undruggable" -- targets for which the underlying disease biology is understood but which have been difficult to address with conventional therapies. Several oncology candidates are now in clinical development.
Bayer has also established a platform for targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT). We are currently developing an alpha-emitter-based RLT for advanced prostate cancer.
Q: What factors will determine the future of innovation in the global pharmaceutical industry? 
A: Ultimately, the success of the pharmaceutical industry depends on its ability to innovate. Innovation does not result from a single factor; it emerges when several conditions come together: a strong academic ecosystem capable of generating breakthrough scientific discoveries, access to capital that can turn scientific innovation into viable businesses, and an attractive and dynamic market.
To remain competitive, Europe needs to strengthen all three areas. It must support the translation of scientific innovation from universities into industry, increase support from both the private and public sectors, improve access to capital for innovative companies, and make its market more attractive.
Europe has not fully recognized and rewarded innovation compared with some other regions. I believe Korea and Japan have faced similar challenges. It is encouraging that the Korean government has recently been exploring ways to ensure that the value of innovation is more appropriately recognized and rewarded.
AI will also be a major driver of innovation and productivity. Korea, in particular, combines strong scientific ambition, digital and AI capabilities, an excellent clinical research environment, and a clear determination to advance rapidly. In this respect, there is considerable scope for Europe and Korea to learn from each other and collaborate.
Across-the-board drug price cuts not the answer 
Q: As President of EFPIA, how do you view the U.S. government's most-favored-nation (MFN) drug pricing policy? 
A: While there may be a need for a more balanced approach if the U.S. is contributing disproportionately to global pharmaceutical R&D funding, it is equally important to ensure that the value of innovation is appropriately recognized.
However, the solution should not be to lower medicine prices uniformly across all countries. Doing so would make it more difficult to secure the resources needed to reinvest in innovation.
What we need is a pricing framework that enables a fairer global sharing of R&D costs and the value of innovation. Otherwise, there is a risk that new medicines may not be launched in certain countries or that their launches may be significantly delayed.
If markets with the economic capacity to contribute, including Korea, Japan, and major European countries, provide more appropriate recognition of the value of innovation, this could help reduce the imbalance between the U.S. and other countries and make these markets more attractive.
This is not an issue for the pharmaceutical industry alone; it also needs to be addressed at the policy level. It is an important topic for bilateral discussions between the United States and other major countries, as well as for forums such as the G7 and G20.
The pharmaceutical industry is not seeking to prioritize one country over another. Rather, our goal is to ensure that patients around the world have more equitable access to innovative treatments. Prices may vary to some extent according to the purchasing power of individual countries, but we need a fairer global framework for medicine pricing and the sharing of costs.
During this visit, I met with policymakers who were considering how to balance the affordability of medicines, timely patient access, and appropriate recognition of innovation. These are discussions that need to take place internationally as well.
Q: Korea is also facing growing pressure on its national health insurance finances due to population aging and the increasing prevalence of chronic diseases. How should the value of innovative treatments be assessed? 
A: Healthcare costs are often assessed separately, with spending on medicines, hospital care, and long-term care for older people considered in isolation. Going forward, however, we need to move away from this fragmented approach and adopt an end-to-end perspective across the entire healthcare pathway, focusing on the ultimate outcomes for patients.
The need for this perspective is clearly illustrated by recent advances in secondary stroke prevention. Asundexian, an oral small-molecule anticoagulant that selectively inhibits factor XIa, has been shown to reduce the risk of a second stroke by 26 percent in patients who have previously experienced a stroke, without increasing the risk of adverse events.
One in five stroke patients experiences a recurrent stroke, which can lead to disability, hospitalization or intensive care, and loss of economic productivity.
Therefore, while introducing a new treatment may raise drug costs in the short term, the costs of hospitalization, treatment, and long-term care associated with recurrent stroke must also be taken into account.
Innovative medicines should not be viewed simply as a driver of higher healthcare costs. Although spending on medicines may increase, these treatments can reduce the overall healthcare burden by preventing diseases, recurrences, and disease progression to more severe stages. The value of such innovation is particularly important in aging societies.
Hepatitis C treatment is a good example. When the first medicines capable of curing hepatitis C became available, there were concerns that their high prices would increase pharmaceutical spending. However, treatment significantly reduced hepatitis C and the subsequent healthcare burden associated with the disease.
In an ideal scenario, investment in innovative medicines can therefore deliver long-term savings in overall healthcare expenditure that outweigh the short-term increase in medicine spending.
In many developed countries, patented medicines and other high-cost innovative treatments account for approximately 5–10 percent of total healthcare expenditure, and this share is declining. The greater area of concern is spending on hospital care and inpatient treatment.
To reduce the healthcare burden, we therefore need to look beyond controlling medicine spending and consider how we can improve patient outcomes, prevent disease, and reduce the burden associated with hospital treatment.
Looking at healthcare systems in many developed countries, we still see a much greater emphasis on treatment than on prevention. It is almost as if prevention were written with a lowercase "p" and treatment with a capital "T."
However, we also need to recognize that medicines are one of the important tools for preventing disease. Greater emphasis should be placed on the ability of innovative medicines to prevent disease onset, recurrence, and progression to more severe stages.
Q: What role do you think Korea can play in this regard? 
A: Korea is particularly well positioned to lead the way in developing an outcomes-based healthcare system. By integrating its advanced healthcare system, strong digital capabilities, and extensive healthcare data, Korea could establish a more comprehensive approach to value assessment than current approaches.
This could demonstrate that appropriate rewards for innovation, patient access to treatment, and the sustainability of healthcare financing do not have to be competing priorities; instead, they can reinforce one another.

Correction: Norsk Hydro: Solid results and strong performance
October 23, 2026 04:22 ET 
  | Source:
Norsk Hydro 
Norsk Hydro 
Hydro’s adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was NOK 9,089 million, up from NOK 5,996 million in the same quarter last year. Higher all-in metal prices and higher alumina prices contributed positively in the quarter, along with improved earnings in Recycling and Extrusions. The strong performance was partially offset by higher anode and energy costs in Aluminium Metal, increased energy costs in Bauxite & Alumina due to gas supply disruptions, a stronger NOK vs USD, and negative price area differences in Energy.
Alunorte resumed regular operations following temporary gas supply disruptions 
Free cash flow of NOK 1.4 billion impacted by higher metal prices and associated working capital requirements and prepayments
First metal produced at HalZero test facility, marking important milestone for carbon-free technology track
Commercial momentum continues for Hydro's low-carbon and recycled aluminium portfolio
New PPAs secured, further strengthening Hydro's long-term power position
Hydro delivered strong profitability in the quarter, with adjusted earnings per share increasing from NOK 1.0 in the third quarter of 2025, to NOK 2.3 in the third quarter of 2026. Free cash flow was NOK 1.4 billion, as strong adjusted EBITDA was partly offset by higher net operating capital, primarily driven by increased metal prices and associated working capital requirements and prepayments. While this development reflects the current market environment, improving cash conversion and working capital efficiency remains a clear priority going forward. Consequently, Hydro has updated its year-end capex guiding to around NOK 12.5 billion, down from NOK 13.5 billion, and net working capital guiding to around NOK 32 billion, up from NOK 30 billion. The twelve month adjusted RoaCE ended at 12.5 percent.
“Hydro’s third quarter results reflect strong operational performance amplified by market tailwinds. Record high liquid metal production from our Norwegian smelter system, combined with strong pricing throughout the quarter drove solid earnings and strong profitability. Operational excellence enables us to capture more of the upside when markets are strong and, more importantly, builds resilience when markets turn,” says Eivind Kallevik, President and CEO of Hydro. 
During the third quarter, disruption in natural gas supplies to Alunorte temporarily reduced production at the refinery. Through mitigating actions, including securing alternative LNG supply, Hydro maintained operational continuity and successfully restored alumina production.
Aluminium Metal benefited from higher all-in metal prices and strong operational performance, while Recycling and Extrusions delivered improved earnings supported by strong recycling margins. Hydro's Norwegian smelters increased liquid metal production to record levels, reinforcing Hydro's position as a reliable supplier of low-carbon aluminium to European customers.
In parallel, Hydro experienced continued momentum for its low-carbon and recycled products, with leading brands like CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty, General Motors, and Mercedes-Benz integrating Hydro’s solutions in their product lines.
“We continue to see strong demand for our low-carbon and recycled offerings from some of the world’s leading consumer brands. When brands like CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty and Mercedes-Benz choose Hydro, they place their trust in our quality, reliability, and ability to help them achieve their ambitions. That trust has commercial value and reinforces our confidence in the long-term opportunities for low-carbon and recycled aluminium,” says Kallevik. 
Hydro reached an important milestone in the development of its HalZero technology by producing aluminium for the first time, demonstrating the core electrolysis technology beyond laboratory scale. The achievement marks an important step toward Hydro’s long-term ambition of eliminating emissions from electrolysis and anode production. Further testing, piloting and technology development remain before any potential industrial application. Enova awarded NOK 82 million in funding to support the concept development and planning of an industrial concept pilot.
“This is an important milestone and a significant step forward in the development of HalZero. Producing the first metal demonstrates that the electrolysis technology works and paves the way for the continued development of a game changing technology with the potential to enable emission-free aluminium production in the future,” says Kallevik . 
During the quarter, Slovalco began the restart of primary aluminium production following the agreement announced in July on long-term framework conditions with the Slovak government. The restart commenced in late August, marking the return of capacity curtailed during the European energy crisis in 2022. The first phase targets an annual production capacity of 75,000 tonnes by the end of February 2027. The restart reflects the importance of competitive power, predictable regulatory frameworks, and effective industrial policy in maintaining and rebuilding Europe's industrial base.
Results and market development per business area 
Adjusted EBITDA for Bauxite & Alumina decreased compared to the third quarter of last year, to NOK 283 million from NOK 1,290 million, mainly driven by lower alumina sales prices, natural gas supply disruptions resulting in higher LNG sourcing costs and unfavourable BRL/USD exchange rate effects.This was partly offset by lower raw material costs and lower fixed costs.
PAX traded up throughout the third quarter 2026 to USD 370 per mt at the end on the quarter, diverging from Chinese alumina prices moving down. Despite lower alumina production at certain refineries in Indonesia because of raw material supply challenges, the World ex-China alumina market was oversupplied in the quarter. China's alumina market became increasingly oversupplied during the quarter as new refinery capacity came on line. Chinese alumina prices were close to the marginal cash production cost. Approximately half of China’s alumina production depends on bauxite imported from Guinea. The government of Guinea is considering the possibility of restricting annual bauxite exports volume, but no formal announcement has been made.
Adjusted EBITDA for Energy decreased in the third quarter compared to the same period last year, to NOK 411 million from NOK 828 million. The decrease is mainly due to a loss on price area differences compared to a gain in the same period last year.
Average Nordic power prices increased in the third quarter compared with both the previous quarter and the same quarter last year. The increase was mainly driven by weak hydrological conditions and higher power prices in Continental Europe. Price area differences between the south and north of the Nordic market were above the previous quarter and below the same period last year. The price difference between central Norway and northern Sweden widened significantly compared with both the previous quarter and the same quarter last year.
The Nordic hydrological balance at the end of the quarter was 13 TWh below normal, compared to 15 TWh below normal at the end of last quarter and 1 TWh below normal at the same time last year. Norwegian hydropower reservoirs were around 67.8 percent of full capacity at the end of the quarter, which is below the normal for this time of year of 82.8 percent. The distribution was uneven, with lower than normal levels in the southern and central Norway, and higher than normal levels in the north.
Adjusted EBITDA for Aluminium Metal increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, to NOK 7,031 million from NOK 2,732 million, due to higher all-in metal prices, partly offset by lower sales volume, higher energy and carbon cost, and weaker USD to NOK. Global primary aluminium consumption was slightly higher compared to the third quarter of 2025, driven by a 3.0 percent increase in Asia. Primary consumption in the World ex. China is estimated to be down compared to the third quarter of 2025. The Middle East crisis continued to affect the aluminium market and prices during the third quarter. Following indications that the conflict might be nearing an end at the end of the second quarter, tensions increased again in the third quarter, directly contributing to higher aluminium prices. Throughout the quarter the market traded in a range between USD 3,100 per mt and USD 3,300 per mt. Consequently, the three month aluminium price increased slightly throughout the third quarter of 2026, starting the quarter at USD 3,076 per mt and ending at USD 3,170 per mt. 
Adjusted EBITDA for Metal Markets decreased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year, to NOK 125 million from NOK 154 million, due to lower results from sourcing and trading activities, partly offset by higher results from recyclers.
Adjusted EBITDA for Extrusions increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, to NOK 1,189 million from NOK 1,107 million, driven by higher recycling margins in combination with increased sales volume, partly offset by higher maintenance cost, higher SG&A cost and negative currency effects mainly from stronger NOK/USD.
CRU estimates that European extrusion demand increased by 1 percent in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, following weaker market conditions in the first half of the year. Automotive demand remained positive, supported by continued growth in battery electric vehicle production. Non-automotive transportation also turned positive after a weak start to the year, while building and construction remained broadly stable in the quarter.
CRU estimates that North American extrusion demand remained broadly unchanged in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, following a decline in the first half of the year. Commercial transportation continued to grow, supported by improving truckload rates, with further growth expected going forward. The industrial segment also remained solid, supported in part by continued datacenter investments. Automotive demand remained subdued, reflecting persistent headwinds in electric vehicle production.
Other key financials 
Compared to the second quarter of 2026, Hydro’s adjusted EBITDA increased to NOK 9,089 million from NOK 8,923 million, mainly due to higher all-in metal and alumina prices and lower fixed costs in the third quarter of the year. This was partially offset by higher energy costs in Bauxite & Alumina due to gas supply disruptions and seasonally lower Extrusion volumes and margins.
Net income (loss) amounted to NOK 5,263 million in the third quarter of 2026. Net income (loss) included unrealized derivative losses, mainly on LME related contracts of NOK 204 million, environmental cost of NOK 111 million, rationalization charges and closure costs of NOK 81 million, and impairment charges on fixed assets of NOK 70 million. The tax effect on these adjustments reflected a standardized tax rate for taxable gains and tax deductible losses. Adjusted net income (loss) for the first quarter ended at NOK 4,372 million.
Hydro’s net debt decreased from NOK 16.3 billion to NOK 15.4 billion during the third quarter of 2026. The net debt decrease was mainly due to positive EBITDA contributions, partially offset by net operating capital build, investments and negative other operating cash flow.
Adjusted net debt decreased from NOK 22.8 billion to NOK 21.9 billion, mainly driven by the decrease in net debt.
Reported earnings before financial items and tax (EBIT), and net income include effects that are disclosed in the quarterly report. Adjustments to EBITDA, EBIT, and net income (loss) are defined and described as part of the alternative performance measures (APM) section in the quarterly report.

Operating EBIT increased $386 million year over year to $585 million, supported by higher polyethylene prices and self-help benefits, partly offset by increased planned maintenance activity. 
Industrial Intermediates & Infrastructure's sales increased 8% year over year to $3.06 billion. Local prices rose 16%, while volume declined 7% due to weaker demand in Polyurethanes & Construction Chemicals, including impacts from the Middle East conflict. Growth in Industrial Solutions partially offset the decline. Operating EBIT improved to $176 million from a loss of $47 million a year ago, supported by higher margins, self-help benefits and the suspension of recognizing equity losses from Sadara. 
Performance Materials & Coatings' sales advanced 8% year over year to $2.25 billion. Local prices increased 5%, while volume grew 3%, driven by gains across both businesses, particularly downstream silicones. Consumer Solutions benefited from stronger demand across consumer, electronics and home care applications, while Coatings & Performance Monomers recorded higher acrylic monomers and architectural coatings prices and volumes. Operating EBIT increased $74 million year over year to $154 million, aided by pricing gains, higher volumes and cost savings. 
Story Continues 
DOW's Cash Flow and Financial Position 
Cash flow from operating activities for continuing operations reached $1.84 billion, up $709 million year over year and $515 million sequentially. The improvement reflected higher earnings and better working capital management. Free cash flow totaled $1.1 billion, while trailing 12-month cash flow conversion reached 84%. 
Cash and cash equivalents stood at $4.14 billion as of Sept. 30, 2026, compared with $3.82 billion at the end of 2025. Dow released more than $400 million in working capital during the quarter and reduced debt by approximately $600 million year to date. Shareholder returns through dividends totaled $253 million during the quarter. 
Dow's Outlook 
Dow remains on track to deliver $700 million in growth and productivity benefits from its Transform to Outperform program in 2026. Management expects approximately $2 billion in total uplift from the initiative by the end of 2027. Benefits from the company's three planned European asset shutdowns are also expected to build through 2027. 
The company expects its collective self-help initiatives to generate more than $1 billion in EBITDA uplift in both 2026 and 2027. Management plans to prioritize growth and innovation in higher-value applications, including AI infrastructure, home and personal care, electronics, flexible packaging and mobility. Dow also intends to strengthen its cost competitiveness by investing in differentiated low-cost operations while shutting down higher-cost upstream capacity.

Award recognizes contributions to South Korea's semiconductor competitiveness

Park Kwang-sun, president of Applied Materials Korea, poses for a commemorative photo at the 19th Semiconductor Day ceremony held at the Grand InterContinental Seoul Parnas in Gangnam, Seoul, on Oct. 21. (Photo: Applied Materials Korea) 
Applied Materials Korea received an Industrial Service Medal in recognition of its contributions to strengthening South Korea's semiconductor industry competitiveness.
Park Kwang-sun, president of Applied Materials Korea, received the medal at the 19th Semiconductor Day ceremony held at the Grand InterContinental Seoul Parnas in Gangnam, Seoul, on Oct. 21.
Applied Materials Korea said the award recognized its efforts to expand the global technology innovation ecosystem and strengthen collaboration on next-generation semiconductor research and development (R&D). Park has promoted cooperation among domestic customers and suppliers and led efforts to build industry networks.
Applied Materials Korea is establishing the Applied Collaboration Center Korea in Osan, Gyeonggi Province, as a regional hub. The center will expand collaboration with major domestic customers and suppliers, supporting activities from early-stage R&D to mass-production validation. It aims to develop local talent and strengthen the competitiveness of South Korea's semiconductor ecosystem.
The company also invests in domestic startups. Applied Materials Korea works with approximately 100 local suppliers. It has established a $50 million fund with Korea Venture Investment Corp. (KVIC) to support promising domestic startups. The company also organizes technology symposiums and site visit programs for university students and provides semiconductor simulation software to university research laboratories.
Semiconductor Day was established by the Korea Semiconductor Industry Association in 2008. Each year, the association recognizes individuals who have contributed to strengthening the competitiveness of South Korea's semiconductor industry.

Renishaw says first-quarter revenue jumped 47% to a record £251.8 million on chip and defence demand Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock Renishaw PLC (LSE:RSW) , the precision measuring and manufacturing systems maker, reported revenue of £251.8 million for the three months to 30 September, up 47% from £170.8 million a year earlier, or 48% at constant exchange rates. 
Revenue was 3% above the final quarter of the previous financial year, following a weak comparison a year earlier. 
At constant exchange rates, which exclude forward contract gains and losses and adjust for currency movements, revenue rose 48%, with all three business segments and all three regions recording year-on-year growth. 
Position Measurement revenue rose 84% to £96.0 million, driven by strong demand for optical and laser encoders used in semiconductor manufacturing equipment. 
Renishaw is investing in additional production capacity for those product lines, and its order book expanded further during the quarter. 
Industrial Metrology revenue rose 28% to £130.8 million, supported by demand for 5-axis co-ordinate measuring machines and shop-floor gauging systems, while its order book grew. 
Specialised Technologies revenue rose 50% to £25.0 million, led by additive manufacturing systems for customers in the aerospace, defence and medical sectors. 
Revenue in the segment was lower than in the exceptionally strong final quarter of the previous financial year, although its order book strengthened. 
The divestment process for the company's neurological business is continuing, while spectroscopy revenue was marginally lower than a year earlier, although its order book strengthened. 
Renishaw expects strong progress in revenue and operating margin for the 2027 financial year as a whole. 
It said it was working to scale up its supply chain and production capacity while remaining mindful of the cyclical nature of demand over the medium term.
