query: "Sumitomo Chemical" ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Sumitomo Chemical deepens India semiconductor push with Tata Electronics pact 
Sumitomo Chemical has signed an MoU with Tata Electronics to explore collaboration in semiconductor fabrication and materials supply, including a possible chemicals facility in India. The move reflects growing interest from upstream suppliers in India’s chip ambitions, where reliable access to high-purity chemicals and photoresists could shape future manufacturing capacity. 
ETChemicals 
Published On Oct 21, 2026 at 12:04 PM IST
Read by 2863 Professionals
Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook 
Bookmark 
India’s semiconductor ambitions are increasingly drawing in global materials suppliers, not just chip designers and fabricators. In a move that underlines that shift, Sumitomo Chemical has signed a memorandum of understanding with Tata Electronics to examine a possible collaboration in semiconductor fabrication and the supporting supply chain , according to specchemonline.com . 
The agreement is significant because semiconductor manufacturing depends on a tightly controlled ecosystem of chemicals, photoresists and high-purity inputs. Any serious effort to localise chip production in India will need those upstream materials to be available reliably, at scale and with consistent quality. That is the business opportunity Sumitomo Chemical appears to be targeting through the Tata partnership. 
What the agreement is meant to cover 
The companies plan to study specific steps that could help create a stable materials supply system for semiconductor manufacturing. One possibility being explored is the establishment of a semiconductor chemicals facility in India, which would give the Japanese supplier a local foothold in a market that is still building out its chip ecosystem. 
The MoU does not amount to a final investment decision, but it signals intent. For Tata Electronics , which is building its semiconductor ambitions in India, a dependable materials partner could be as important as equipment, talent and policy support. For Sumitomo Chemical, the arrangement offers a way to align with a customer base that may grow as India pushes harder into advanced electronics manufacturing. 
Why materials matter more than ever 
Semiconductor fabrication is often discussed through the lens of fabs, foundries and government incentives, but the industry is equally dependent on specialist materials. Photoresists and high-purity chemicals are essential in the patterning and processing steps that allow chips to be manufactured at advanced nodes. Supply disruptions in these inputs can quickly ripple through production schedules and yield outcomes. 
That is why localisation efforts are increasingly extending beyond assembly and packaging. Countries seeking to build semiconductor resilience are now looking at the full stack, including the chemicals that enable chipmaking in the first place. A domestic or regional supply base can reduce logistics risk, shorten lead times and improve control over quality assurance. 
Sumitomo Chemical is betting on semiconductor growth 
The semiconductor materials business has been positioned as a priority inside Sumitomo Chemical’s ICT and Mobility Solutions segment, which the Japanese group views as one of its growth engines. The company has built a reputation in advanced photoresists and semiconductor chemicals, particularly high-purity products used in demanding fabrication environments. 
Over the past few years, the company has expanded semiconductor chemicals capacity in Japan and South Korea while also setting up a new base in Texas. Earlier this year, it acquired Asia Union Electronic Chemical , which operates facilities in Taiwan and Nevada. The company has also started work at advanced high-purity chemical centres in Japan and South Korea, where it is developing new processes and recycling technologies. 
That sequence of investments suggests a broader strategy: deepen presence in major semiconductor geographies while improving supply resilience and technical capabilities. The India move fits that pattern, especially as chip manufacturing becomes more geographically diversified in response to geopolitical and supply chain concerns. 
India’s chip ecosystem is attracting upstream players 
India has spent the past few years trying to move from policy ambition to industrial execution in semiconductors . The country’s appeal is no longer limited to final-stage electronics assembly. Global suppliers are beginning to evaluate whether India can support the specialised materials and process infrastructure needed for chip fabrication. 
That shift matters because semiconductor projects are rarely built in isolation. A viable ecosystem requires chemical suppliers, gas suppliers, wafer handling, cleanroom services, logistics providers and a skilled technical workforce. The presence of a company such as Sumitomo Chemical would be a signal that India is moving closer to that broader industrial base. 
For Tata Electronics, the partnership could help strengthen its supply chain planning at a time when semiconductor manufacturing is becoming a strategic priority for large industrial groups in India. For Sumitomo Chemical, the arrangement could open a pathway into a market that combines scale potential with policy support for electronics manufacturing. 
Regional competition is also intensifying 
The India discussion comes as Japanese chemical companies continue to expand in other Asian semiconductor hubs. Another Japanese player, Nissan Chemical , has separately set up a wholly owned subsidiary in Zhangjiagang in Jiangsu province, China. That unit will manufacture anti-reflective coatings used in photoresists and multilayer semiconductor materials. 
Nissan Chemical has said demand for semiconductors in China has continued to rise, helped by digitalisation and other structural factors, while customers are also seeking more resilient supply chains. The parallel expansion by Japanese suppliers in China and India highlights a broader industry trend: materials companies are following chip manufacturing demand wherever it is likely to concentrate next. 
For India, the challenge will be to convert interest into durable industrial capacity. A materials facility, if it goes ahead, would not by itself create a complete semiconductor supply chain. But it would be an important marker of confidence, showing that upstream global suppliers are willing to commit capital and know-how to the country’s chip ambitions. 
The Tata Electronics tie-up therefore sits at the intersection of manufacturing policy, supply chain resilience and long-term industrial strategy. Sony Semiconductor Solutions Announces 1 mm Square Image Sensor for Medical Single-Use Endoscopes, Featuring Industry's First*¹5 m Digital Transmission and High Image Quality
PR Newswire 
October 21, 2026 4 min read 
Providing stable transmission of high-definition images for thin endoscopes 
ATSUGI, Japan, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sony Semiconductor Solutions Corporation (Sony) today announced the upcoming release of the IMX742, a CMOS image sensor with approximately 0.51 effective megapixels*2 for medical single-use endoscopes. This sensor is the industry's first*1 to support digital output and data transmission through a 5 m*3 cable. 
IMX742 CMOS image sensor for single-use endoscopes
Model name
IMX742 1/17.7-type CMOS image sensor with approximately 0.51 effective megapixels for single-use endoscopes Demand for disposable, single-use endoscopes is growing in the medical field to help prevent infections and reduce the burden of endoscope reprocessing and managing equipment after use. Cameras on such endoscopes require not only compact sensors that are compatible with today's increasingly small diameter insertion parts but also improved basic performance such as high image quality and stable signal transmission. 
By miniaturizing peripheral circuits, including the A/D converter (analog-to-digital conversion circuit), and using proprietary bi-directional communication technology to transmit control and video signals via the same cable, the IMX742 combines approximately 0.51 effective megapixels with a compact 1 mm-square sensor size. Furthermore, digitizing image signals on the sensor enables low-noise imaging at a high frame rate of 60 fps, with stable transmission via a 5 m cable, providing clear images for endoscopic visualization. These features will contribute to the miniaturization and improved image quality of thin endoscope cameras used in bronchoscopes and ureteroscopes. 
Sony has provided image sensors for reusable endoscopes and will expand its offerings to single-use endoscope applications, for which demand continues to rise, thereby contributing to the realization of endoscope systems designed to meet needs for reduced invasiveness and improved operability and visibility. 
Model name: IMX742 1/17.7-type CMOS image sensor with approximately 0.51 effective megapixels for single-use endoscopes. Sample shipment date (planned) November 2026. 
*1 Among CMOS image sensors for medical endoscopes. According to Sony research (as of announcement on October 22, 2026).
*2 Based on the image sensor effective pixel specification method.
*3 Transmission distance confirmed in a Sony evaluation environment using an AWG44 cable. 
Main Features 
Achieving high resolution and digital output in a compact 1 mm-square sensor 
The new sensor combines approximately 0.51 effective megapixels and digital output in a compact 1 mm-square sensor suitable for thin endoscopes.
Digital output requires the A/D converter to be integrated into the sensor, making sensor miniaturization more challenging. This product miniaturizes peripheral circuits, including the A/D converter, while preserving sufficient area for the pixel array, thereby achieving both high resolution and digital output in a compact sensor.
Additionally, it uses Sony's proprietary bi-directional communication technology to enable both the control and video signals to be transmitted via the same cable while keeping the number of sensor pins to six.
These features contribute to the further miniaturization and improved image quality of thin endoscopes, including bronchoscopes and ureteroscopes. 
Stable transmission of high-quality 60 fps images on a 5 m cable 
The new sensor outputs image signals digitized on the sensor, enabling lower-noise imaging in low-light environments compared with analog output. This provides high visibility in dark areas inside the body, even when the sensor is used in thin endoscopes equipped with compact LED light sources that offer limited brightness. It also supports a high frame rate of 60 fps, enabling smooth video display that keeps pace with rapid movement during diagnosis and treatment.
Additionally, outputting a digital signal enables stable video transmission, which makes it possible to configure a system using a 5 m-long cable.
With all these features, the new sensor supports stable image acquisition in thin endoscopes and increased flexibility in cable routing and system configuration, contributing to the realization of endoscope systems that support smoother observation.

Merck opens Korean chip materials plant to meet advanced memory demand
Published : Oct. 22, 2026 - 10:27:43
Add The Korea Herald on Google
Link copied!
Moon Joon-hyun 
Tech Reporter
Covers Korean companies at the center of global chips, AI and consumer technology, from Samsung and SK hynix to Apple suppliers
Subscribe + 
Merck Electronics CEO sees Korea as key market as company braces for potential doubling of chip materials demand
Benjamin Hein, CEO of Merck's Electronics business, speaks during a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday. (Merck Korea) 
German science and technology company Merck opened a new semiconductor materials plant in South Korea on Thursday, expanding local production of molybdenum as chipmakers adopt the metal for increasingly advanced memory chips.
The facility in Eumseong, North Chungcheong Province, will produce molybdenum dioxide dichloride, a chemical used to deposit ultrathin metal films during chip manufacturing. It will supply customers in Korea and elsewhere in Asia.
Benjamin Hein, CEO of Merck's Electronics business, described Korea as among the top three markets for semiconductor materials during a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday.
"What if the demand for semiconductor materials and solutions doubles within the next five years? Are we ready? We want to be ready," Hein said.
The plant will initially focus on materials for advanced 3D NAND flash memory, which increases storage capacity by stacking memory cells vertically.
Merck's Eumseong plant in North Chungcheong Province, where the German company opened a new molybdenum production facility for advanced semiconductor manufacturing on Thursday (Merck Korea) 
Samsung Electronics began using molybdenum in its ninth-generation V-NAND in 2024, while SK hynix has reportedly been preparing to introduce the metal in its next-generation 375-layer NAND.
Molybdenum offers an alternative to tungsten, whose electrical resistance becomes increasingly problematic as chipmakers shrink components and stack more layers. It can also reduce the need for barrier films that occupy valuable space inside microscopic structures.
Bing Han, executive vice president and head of Merck's Thin Films business, said adoption was beginning with NAND, with DRAM and logic chips expected to follow. "Eventually more of the smaller features will all move to Moly," Han said, while acknowledging that the pace of adoption depends on individual customers.
Merck will combine precursor production in Eumseong with chemical delivery systems manufactured at its Ansan facility in Gyeonggi Province. The company says the integrated system can use more than 99 percent of the material loaded into its containers, potentially reducing waste and manufacturing costs.
"Local for local is everything," Han said. "You can have the best offering, but you have to have your best offering in the right location."
The expansion forms part of Merck's 600 million euro ($674 million) investment program announced in 2021. Merck disclosed plans for the molybdenum facility in February, but declined to reveal its investment cost or production capacity.
Hein also identified advanced packaging, which combines multiple chips into increasingly complex systems, as another growth area. He said manufacturers face an immediate shortage of packaging capacity, with further technological changes expected over the next three to five years.
"On advanced packaging, short term, there is simply not enough capacity," he said. "So on the immediate, it is about debottlenecking."

3M expands collaboration with Amazon, forms GSEO partnership
The chemical company is working to expand and scale the R&D and manufacturing of its Expanded Beam Optical products, which it expects will generate $40 million by the end of 2026.
Published Oct. 22, 2026
Sara Samora 
Reporter

3M has reached agreements with Amazon Web Services and Genius Electronic Optical Co. to scale manufacturing and research and development of its expanded beam optical interconnect technology used within AI data centers.
Courtesy of 3M
Listen to the article
4 min 
This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback .
3M reached two agreements to scale manufacturing and research and development of its expanded beam optical interconnect products, the company announced this week . 
The effort will come through an expanded collaboration with Amazon Web Services and a formed partnership with Taiwan-based Genius Electronic Optical Co., the chemical maker said. 
The deals build on 3M’s strategy to invest an undisclosed amount toward expanding its EBO manufacturing capacity that it announced in March. The plan includes adding manufacturing equipment and production space to meet the global demand for high-speed interconnects in artificial intelligence data centers. 
3M anticipates EBO portfolio revenue in the $40 million range in 2026 and expects it to increase “considerably” next year between $80 million and $100 million, CEO and Chairman Bill Brown said during 3M’s third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday. 
The company has doubled its EBO manufacturing capacity to a little over 10 million ferrules per year, which Brown said will increase over time. 
3M is part of an alliance focused on advancing an open, interoperable specification for EBO connectivity products in the AI end-market called the Expanded Beam Optics Multi-Source Agreement Group . The MSA seeks to streamline EBO connectors for wide-scale adoption, according to the website. It also assists in connecting vendors with the supply industry. 
3M joined the MSA in May and as of Oct. 15, the group has 63 members, including Microsoft, AMD, Foxconn, Nvidia, Oracle and Meta. 
3M teamed up with MSA member Microsoft in July to collaborate on AI data center infrastructure and transforming enterprise technologies. 
Amazon Web Services 
AWS plans to deploy and ramp up 3M’s EBO platform for its data center infrastructure, according to a press release on Thursday . 
The two companies will collaborate to develop data-transfer technologies and critical infrastructure required for artificial intelligence. 
3M issued AWS a call warrant to buy up to about 3.2 million of the chemical maker’s shares at a purchase price of $164.89 over seven years, according to an Oct. 19 securities filing . 
Amazon will gain full ownership of a certain number of shares once “sales of optical connectivity and other data-center related products” reach $6 billion, Brown said. The securities filing said the remaining warrant shares will be subject to reaching certain goalposts. 
The partnership and related investments are expected to support over 500 direct and indirect jobs, and create over 100 jobs through 2027 across 3M’s operations in Minnesota, Texas and Wisconsin, according to the press release. 
The jobs will also support customer collaboration, advance technology and supply chain development across 3M’s optical networking portfolio and accelerate industry-wide EBO product adoption. 
Genius Electronic Optical 
3M’s partnership with GSEO will combine the chemical company’s optical interconnect expertise, materials science, manufacturing and customer relationships with the Taiwan-based entity’s precision optics production capabilities and scale, according to the Oct. 19 press release . 
3M and GSEO’s joint effort aims to support EBO commercialization and long-term capacity expansion to meet growing demand for data centers and other connectivity applications, according to a separate press release on Monday . 3M also plans to buy 4.7% of the Taiwan-based optical technology company’s shares, with the deal expected to close in the fourth quarter. 
GSEO’s manufacturing capabilities and technical development experience are expected to help 3M prepare its manufacturing process for its EBO ferrules connector , packaged optics, and other related optical interconnect products. 
While 3M is scaling up EBO production in-house, Brown said the company would not be able to meet market demand. GSEO has that capacity, and other manufacturing sources may help satisfy the “diversity of supply” over time, the CEO added.

The Korea Toray Science Foundation has selected Professor Kim Sang-kyu of KAIST’s Department of Chemistry and Professor Kim Yoon-hee of Gyeongsang National University’s Department of Chemistry as recipients of the ninth Toray Science and Technology Awards.
The foundation said it held the awards ceremony at Seoul Garden Hotel on Oct. 21, attended by approximately 150 guests, including award recipients, academics, industry representatives and students. The two professors, recognized for their research achievements in chemistry and materials science, each received a prize of 100 million won.
Five early-career researchers were selected for the foundation’s fellowship program: Song In-taek, professor of chemistry and physics at DGIST; Hong Seung-yoon, professor of chemistry at Seoul National University; Kim Hyung-jun, professor of chemical and biomolecular engineering at Sogang University; Chun Dong-won, professor of materials science and engineering at POSTECH; and Ham Dong-hyo, professor of chemical engineering at Hanyang University. Each will receive 150 million won in research funding over three years.
Since its establishment in 2018, the Korea Toray Science Foundation has selected 18 science and technology award recipients and 40 fellowship researchers. The foundation also provides annual scholarships to university students majoring in science and engineering, supporting a total of 255 students through the second semester of 2026.

Corning to invest $585M, add 414 jobs in Wilmington expansion 
Corning Inc. will invest $585 million at its Wilmington campus and add 414 jobs over the next five years, expanding one of the world’s largest optical fiber man 
By Hannah Hall 
Published : Oct. 21, 2026 at 10:31 AM EDT 
Share 
Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google 
WILMINGTON, N.C. (WECT) - Corning Inc. will invest $585 million at its Wilmington campus and add 414 jobs over the next five years, expanding one of the world’s largest optical fiber manufacturing plants.
The New York-based company announced the expansion Wednesday after the Wilmington City Council and New Hanover County Commissioners approved a package of incentives earlier this week to expand its operations. 
“We’re proud to expand our presence in Wilmington, where Corning made history with the world’s first optical fiber manufacturing plant and where our people continue to make the fiber that is critical to next-generation networks,” said John McGirr, senior vice president and general manager of Corning Optical Fiber and Cable.
NHC Commissioners approve incentive for Corning Inc. to expand in Wilmington 
Wilmington council backs $2 million deal to sweeten odds of landing Corning expansion 
Wilmington competed with several other locations for the project, known as “Project Pearl 2.” The project will supply fiber for next-generation networks and support long-term customer agreements, according to Corning.
The new jobs are expected to pay an average salary of more than $85,000 a year, and the company said the expansion will add more than $35 million in annual payroll for the region.
“Corning has been part of New Hanover County for decades, and when a company with that track record is ready to grow, this Board wants that growth to happen here,” said LeAnn Pierce, Chair of the New Hanover County Board of Commissioners. “Those are good paychecks for families in our community. The grant is tied to those jobs and that investment, and that is exactly how it should work.”
The company has maintained a civic commitment to the Wilmington area for 60 years, partnering with Cape Fear Community College on the Corning Technician Pipeline Program and investing in STEM education in local schools.
“It’s impossible to overstate how important this company is to Greater Wilmington,” said Scott Satterfield, CEO of Wilmington Business Development.

Toray Industries Inc. recently announced it had developed a polyester-nylon fiber containing at least 93 percent recycled content by mass, based on the total weight of the raw yarn.
The Japan-based company says the percentage applies to the newly developed raw yarn and does not represent the recycled content of the finished fabric or garment. It says the breakthrough drew on technologies the company cultivated through its &+ (and plus) recycled fiber brand, adding that the polyester and nylon components of the fiber incorporate recycled materials.
Composite fibers can provide added functionality, sophisticated textures and subtle visual effects, Toray says, but combining different polymers makes it difficult to use high proportions of recycled materials while maintaining consistent quality. The company says it tapped into its expertise in polymer design and composite spinning to overcome the challenge and achieve a product containing at least 93 percent recycled content by mass, and it plans to verify the technology’s viability for mass production and continue research to increase recycled content in composite fibers.
“The fashion industry is showing increasing interest in material containing recycled content,” Toray says. “Materials for high-end and luxury applications must also deliver exceptional aesthetic qualities, including appearance, tailoring and drape, texture and durability.”
These considerations prompted Toray to create Artirosa CX, which it says incorporates the newly developed fiber. The company notes that the recycled content in each Artirosa CX fabric may vary depending on its composition.
The company says Artirosa CX features a “dense, finely textured surface and a crisp, sophisticated feel,” adding that fabric design and finishing also can impart practical properties like waterproofing, durable water repellency and wind resistance. 
“Rather than emphasizing the distinctive appearance typical of conventional functional materials, Artirosa CX refines that look into an elegant, sophisticated texture,” Toray says. “The result is a cleaner, more contemporary urban aesthetic.”
Toray says it intends to market Artirosa CX for wide-ranging applications, including men’s and women’s outerwear, urban outdoor wear and premium casual wear. The company expects to launch the product in late-2027 and is targeting initial year sales of 200,000 meters (around 218,722 yards) of material.

Chemours Faces Investor Lawsuit Over Opteon Refrigerant Sales in the US
The complaint cites excess distributor inventory after 2025 advance purchases and questions the reliability of Chemours' 2026 guidance.
October 21, 2026 
Created by Refindustry using AI 
The Chemours Company faces a securities class action lawsuit alleging that it misrepresented aftermarket demand for Opteon refrigerants and the reliability of its 2026 financial guidance. According to law firm Levi & Korsinsky, the case concerns approximately $65 million in Opteon aftermarket sales recorded in 2025 that management later estimated should have been allocated more to 2026.
The complaint alleges that Chemours’ Thermal & Specialized Solutions (TSS) segment experienced excess distributor inventory following increased refrigerant purchases during the US residential air-conditioning equipment transition driven by the AIM Act. Plaintiffs claim the company continued to describe aftermarket demand as strong between February 20 and August 4, 2026, without adequately disclosing the inventory buildup.
In its second-quarter 2026 results, Chemours reported net sales of $1.6 billion, approximately 1% below the previous year, and a 4% volume decline attributed primarily to lower Opteon blends aftermarket sales. The company linked the decline to elevated demand in 2025, when customers purchased refrigerants ahead of need amid supply constraints. Chemours indicated that this comparison would affect both the second and third quarters of 2026.
In May 2026, Chemours disclosed an approximately $10 million adjusted EBITDA impact from TSS demand pulled forward into the first quarter and projected second-quarter TSS adjusted EBITDA of $210 million to $225 million. Following the company’s August 4 second-quarter report and reduced full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance, Chemours shares declined by $3.34, or 18.63%.
“The complaint raises serious questions about whether investors received accurate information about how much Opteon inventory was already sitting with Chemours’ aftermarket distributors. As alleged, the channel had been stocked ahead of demand in 2025 even as the Company projected continued TSS growth into 2026,” said Joseph E. Levi, attorney at Levi & Korsinsky. Investors who purchased Chemours securities during the specified period have until December 7, 2026, to seek appointment as lead plaintiff.

"We are very pleased to deliver another excellent quarter, with outstanding financial performance on both the top and bottom line," said Marc N. Casper, chairman and chief executive officer of Thermo Fisher Scientific. "We're advancing our proven growth strategy, which is resonating strongly with our customers, and our PPI Business System is enabling outstanding execution across the company." 
Company Overview 
With over 14,000 sales personnel and a portfolio spanning more than 2,500 technology manufacturers, Thermo Fisher Scientific (NYSE:TMO) provides scientific equipment, reagents, consumables, software, and laboratory services to pharmaceutical, biotech, academic, and healthcare customers worldwide. 
Revenue Growth 
Reviewing a company's long-term sales performance reveals insights into its quality. Any business can put up a good quarter or two, but the best consistently grow over the long haul. Unfortunately, Thermo Fisher's 3.9% annualized revenue growth over the last five years was tepid. This was below our standard for the healthcare sector and is a tough starting point for our analysis. 
Thermo Fisher Quarterly Revenue We at StockStory place the most emphasis on long-term growth, but within healthcare, a half-decade historical view may miss recent innovations or disruptive industry trends. Thermo Fisher's annualized revenue growth of 5.7% over the last two years is above its five-year trend, which is encouraging. 
Thermo Fisher Year-On-Year Revenue Growth Thermo Fisher also reports organic revenue, which strips out one-time events like acquisitions and currency fluctuations that don't accurately reflect its fundamentals. Over the last two years, Thermo Fisher's organic revenue averaged 3.1% year-on-year growth. Because this number is lower than its two-year revenue growth, we can see that some mixture of acquisitions and foreign exchange rates boosted its headline results. 
Story Continues 
Thermo Fisher Organic Revenue Growth This quarter, Thermo Fisher reported year-on-year revenue growth of 9.1%, and its $12.14 billion of revenue exceeded Wall Street's estimates by 1.4%. 
Looking ahead, sell-side analysts expect revenue to grow 4.8% over the next 12 months, similar to its two-year rate. This projection is underwhelming and implies its newer products and services will not lead to better top-line performance yet.

Adjusted Operating Margin 
Thermo Fisher has been an efficient company over the last five years. It was one of the more profitable businesses in the healthcare sector, boasting an average adjusted operating margin of 23.1%. 
Looking at the trend in its profitability, Thermo Fisher's adjusted operating margin decreased by 4.5 percentage points over the last five years. This raises questions about the company's expense base because its revenue growth should have given it leverage on its fixed costs, resulting in better economies of scale and profitability. 
Thermo Fisher Trailing 12-Month Operating Margin (Non-GAAP) In Q3, Thermo Fisher generated an adjusted operating margin profit margin of 18.6%, down 4.6 percentage points year on year. This contraction shows it was less efficient because its expenses grew faster than its revenue. 
Earnings Per Share 
We track the long-term change in earnings per share (EPS) for the same reason as long-term revenue growth. Compared to revenue, however, EPS highlights whether a company's growth is profitable. 
Thermo Fisher's flat EPS over the last five years was below its 3.9% annualized revenue growth. This tells us the company became less profitable on a per-share basis as it expanded due to non-fundamental factors such as interest expenses and taxes. 
Thermo Fisher Trailing 12-Month EPS (Non-GAAP) We can take a deeper look into Thermo Fisher's earnings to better understand the drivers of its performance. As we mentioned earlier, Thermo Fisher's adjusted operating margin declined by 4.5 percentage points over the last five years. This was the most relevant factor (aside from the revenue impact) behind its lower earnings; interest expenses and taxes can also affect EPS but don't tell us as much about a company's fundamentals. 
In Q3, Thermo Fisher reported adjusted EPS of $6.68, up from $5.79 in the same quarter last year. This print beat analysts' estimates by 4.3%. Over the next 12 months, Wall Street expects Thermo Fisher's full-year EPS to grow 8.3% from $24.72 to $26.78. 
Key Takeaways from Thermo Fisher's Q3 Results 
We enjoyed seeing Thermo Fisher beat analysts' organic revenue expectations this quarter. We were also happy its revenue narrowly outperformed Wall Street's estimates. Overall, we think this was a solid quarter with some key areas of upside. The stock remained flat at $685.72 immediately after reporting.

Billionaire Adar Poonawalla led Serum Institute of India also holds a minority stake in the firm
Ashwin Mohan 
October 21, 2026 / 14:50 IST

SCHOTT Poonawalla, backed by Germany's SCHOTT Pharma and private equity firm TPG Growth, has initiated preliminary steps for a domestic initial public offering (IPO), people familiar with the matter told Moneycontrol.
The Mumbai-based company is a leading primary packaging provider for India's pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries. If the listing plans materialise, it would join a growing list of multinational companies and their Indian subsidiaries tapping the domestic IPO market.
The company counts Serum Institute of India, the vaccine maker led by billionaire Adar Poonawalla, as a minority investor.
“SCHOTT Poonawalla has invited investment banks to make pitches for the proposed IPO next week. These are early days, but as of now, the intent is to raise around $400 million,” one of the persons cited above said, cautioning that the issue size and valuation have not been finalised and could change depending on market conditions.
A second person confirmed the development and said the proposed issue would likely comprise a combination of fresh shares and an offer for sale.

“The IPO provides a window for investor Serum Institute of India to further dilute part stake if deemed fit,” a third person said.
A fourth person also confirmed the listing plans.
All four people spoke to Moneycontrol on condition of anonymity.
An email query to SCHOTT Poonawalla remained unanswered at the time of publication. TPG and Serum Institute of India declined to comment.
A spokesperson for SCHOTT Pharma said, “As a matter of principle, we do not comment on market speculation or potential future transactions.”
Germany-based SCHOTT Pharma, which specialises in drug containment and delivery solutions, holds a 50% stake in SCHOTT Poonawalla, while TPG Growth holds 35%. The company was originally a 50:50 joint venture between SCHOTT Pharma and Serum Institute of India.
On May 6, 2025, SCHOTT Pharma announced a binding agreement with TPG to sell a 35% stake in the joint venture to the private equity firm. Novo Holdings joined TPG Growth as a co-investor.
Moneycontrol was the first to report , on November 28, 2024, that TPG Growth and Serum Institute of India were in talks over a stake sale.
Read More: Adar Poonawalla-led Serum Institute seals 30%-40% stake sale in SCHOTT Poonawalla to TPG Growth; target firm valued around $800 mn 
“SCHOTT Poonawalla is a unique asset and a clear market leader with an over 50 percent market share in injectable packaging and hence TPG saw an opportunity,” the report said, adding that the company's equity valuation was estimated at around $800 million.
Manipal Health Enterprises, Sai Life Sciences and Dr Agarwal's Health Care are among the healthcare companies backed by TPG that have made their stock market debuts in India.
In India's packaging sector, SCHOTT Poonawalla's listed peers include EPL Ltd, AGI Greenpac, Uflex Ltd, TCPL Packaging and Jindal Poly Films.
Hyundai Motor India, LG Electronics India, Orkla India and Tenneco Clean Air India are among the multinational companies that have launched IPOs in India in recent years. The Indian arms of Pernod Ricard and Carlsberg are also in the pipeline.
Earlier this week, the Rs 2,534-crore IPO of power transmission and drive solutions company Bonfiglioli Transmissions, entirely an offer for sale by its Italian promoter, was subscribed 46 times.
Lens on SCHOTT Poonawalla 
SCHOTT Poonawalla's product portfolio includes cartridges for auto-injector pens, prefillable syringes for a range of biologic drugs, vials and ampoules. It also offers regulatory services to biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies and contract development and manufacturing organisations (CDMOs).
Through its association with SCHOTT Pharma, the company draws on decades of expertise in pharmaceutical packaging, spanning drug administration, clinical trials, regulatory processes and commercial filings.
Speaking about TPG's entry into SCHOTT Poonawalla in May 2025, SCHOTT Pharma CEO Andreas Reisse had said: “India continues to be one of the most dynamic and strategically important manufacturing hubs for SCHOTT Pharma. Welcoming TPG to the partnership marks an exciting step forward in our collaboration. SCHOTT Pharma’s innovation capabilities and pure-play focus on injectables will be complemented by TPG’s local market expertise, relationships, and experience from its strong presence in the Indian healthcare sector. As we continue to expand our local production capacities and leading role in the Indian market, we are confident that this step will further enhance our global footprint and deliver exceptional value to our customers.”
Ashwin Mohan is Editor (Deals) at Moneycontrol and leads the M&A, private equity and equity capital market transactions coverage. He anchors the video show 'Deal Central ' and tweets at @ashwinmohansays. He has previously worked with ET NOW, CNBC TV-18 and The Times of India.

Thermo Fisher posts higher third-quarter revenue and earnings as margins improve
Published: 09:04 21 Oct 2026 EDT
Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc (NYSE:TMO, XETRA:TN8) increased third-quarter revenue by 9% to $12.14 billion, while adjusted earnings per share rose 15% to $6.68.
Revenue for the three months ended September 2026 increased from $11.12 billion a year earlier, with organic revenue growth, which excludes the effects of acquisitions, disposals and currency movements, reaching 6%.
Adjusted operating income rose 15% to $2.97 billion, while adjusted operating margin increased to 24.5% from 23.3% in the same period last year.
The company’s generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) diluted earnings per share increased 9% to $4.64, while GAAP operating income rose 17% to $2.26 billion.
GAAP operating margin improved to 18.6% from 17.4%, indicating that the company retained a larger share of revenue as operating profit.
Thermo Fisher chief executive Marc Casper said the company’s growth strategy and its Practical Process Improvement (PPI) Business System supported its performance during the quarter.
The company launched several products during the period, including a mass spectrometer designed for isotope ratio analysis, an electron detector for advanced materials research and a new autoimmune screening test cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration.
Thermo Fisher also partnered with Mayo Clinic to launch Precure, an initiative combining data from more than one million patient samples with its proteomics technologies to support disease research, earlier detection and precision medicine.
In South Korea, the company opened its first artificial intelligence and automation innovation centre to help customers improve research and development productivity.
Thermo Fisher also opened a highly automated distribution centre in Kentucky to improve supply chain speed and flexibility across North America.
The company completed the previously announced sale of its microbiology business during the quarter as part of its capital deployment strategy.
Thermo Fisher said it would provide updated financial guidance for 2026 during its third-quarter earnings conference call.
Shares were down around 2% in early Wednesday morning trading.

1.1 Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery Market Summary
Silicon-carbon anode materials for solid state batteries are high-capacity anode materials developed for solid-state and semi-solid lithium battery systems. They are typically based on nano-silicon, silicon oxide, graphite, and porous carbon, and are improved through composite structure design, surface coating, and interface stabilization. The materials are mainly used in automotive power batteries, high-end consumer electronics batteries, and next-generation high-safety energy storage batteries.
The market is still in an early commercialization stage as solid state batteries move from sample validation and pilot projects toward small-scale production. Demand for silicon-carbon anode materials is increasing as automakers, battery manufacturers, and material companies accelerate joint development programs. Compared with conventional graphite anodes, silicon-carbon systems offer much higher theoretical capacity, but they also face challenges such as volume expansion, interfacial side reactions, initial efficiency loss, and batch-to-batch consistency.
According to the new market research report "Global Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery Market Growth 2026-2032", published by LP Information, the global Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery market size is projected to reach US$111 million by 2032, at a CAGR of 18.0% during the forecast period.
According to LP Information, the global key manufacturers of Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery include Group14 Technologies, Sila Nanotechnologies, Amprius, etc. In 2025, the global top three players had a share of approximately 31.65% in terms of revenue.
To read the full report or request a free sample report, please use the link: https://www.lpinformationdata.com/reports/1866822/silicon---carbon-anode-materials-for-solid-state-battery 
1.2 Industrial Chain
The upstream segment mainly includes metallurgical-grade silicon, silane, graphite, and porous carbon, with representative suppliers such as Elkem, Hemlock, and East Hope Group. Raw material purity, particle size distribution, carbon structure, and supply stability directly affect capacity performance, swelling control, cycle life, and batch consistency, while also forming the basis for cost control and mass production.
The midstream segment focuses on silicon-carbon composite structure engineering, interface stabilization, swelling suppression, surface coating modification, and particle morphology optimization. The main challenge is to balance high capacity with long cycle life while controlling initial efficiency, tap density, and processing compatibility. Stable mixing, heat treatment, coating, and classification processes directly affect yield, customer qualification time, and unit manufacturing cost.
Downstream demand mainly comes from automotive power batteries and consumer electronics lithium batteries. Power battery customers focus on longer driving range, fast charging capability, safety, and long-term cycling performance, while consumer electronics customers emphasize volumetric energy density and thinner product design. Silicon-carbon anodes help battery makers improve energy density and create differentiated performance for solid state batteries, premium vehicles, and high-end devices.
1.3 Influencing Factors
Drivers:
The core growth driver is rising demand for high-energy-density batteries. Longer-range electric vehicles, fast-charging platforms, and thinner high-end consumer electronics are pushing anode materials from conventional graphite toward silicon-carbon systems. As solid state battery development and demonstration projects accelerate, battery makers are increasing validation demand for high-capacity, low-swelling, and long-life anode materials, supporting order growth and market expansion.
Challenges:
The main barrier is process stability and cost pressure. Silicon materials tend to expand and trigger interfacial side reactions during charge and discharge, which raises requirements for coating, structure design, and battery system matching. If batch consistency, initial efficiency, and cycle life cannot meet customer requirements steadily, qualification cycles will be extended and production expansion and profitability will be constrained.
Trend:
Future development will focus on higher capacity, lower swelling, and better adaptation to solid state battery systems. Material suppliers will use nano-structure design, porous carbon frameworks, elastic coating layers, and interface modification to improve cycling stability, while developing customized products for different solid electrolytes and cell processes. Companies with materials design, scale-up engineering, and joint customer validation capabilities will gain stronger competitiveness.

Qualcomm boosts Korea startups and robot tech at industrial AI expo 
입력 2026.10.21. 15:31 
조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 
A view of the QAIPI Pavilion, an exhibition space Qualcomm prepares at the Industry AI Expo 2026 to showcase technology from domestic artificial intelligence (AI) startups./Courtesy of Qualcomm 
U.S. semiconductor corporation Qualcomm showcased industrial AI technology with six Korea-based artificial intelligence (AI) startups.
Qualcomm said on the 21st that it would take part in Industrial AI Expo 2026 and operate the Qualcomm AI Innovators Program (QAIPI) Pavilion, an exhibition space for Korea-based AI startups. QAIPI is a program Qualcomm launched last year to support AI technology development and commercialization by startups in the Asia-Pacific region.
This exhibition features six Korea-based startups: ENERZAi, Withrobot, Undermilli, Clica, FladLabs, which were selected for QAIPI this year, and Sagak, which was selected last year. Five partners in the industrial and embedded Internet of Things (IoT) field—ICbanQ, Sapphire Stream Technology Korea, XSLAB Incorporation, MathWorks, and OSCO—also joined.
Qualcomm is supporting participating corporations with the Qualcomm AI Hub, an AI development tool, along with technical training and mentoring. The goal is to help startups use the Qualcomm platform to develop AI services for mobile, computing, and IoT and apply them in real industrial settings.
It will also unveil technologies developed in collaboration with Korea-based robotics corporations. In the Qualcomm Robotics Zone inside the exhibition hall, Rainbow Robotics' quadruped robot equipped with Qualcomm's industrial processor Dragonwing IQ-9075 will be demonstrated. An autonomous mobile robot (AMR) from auto parts company SL Corporation will also be unveiled. The robot uses Arduino's VENTUNO Q platform.
A quadruped robot from Rainbow Robotics is on display at the Qualcomm Robotics Zone, Qualcomm's exhibition space at the Industry AI Expo 2026./Courtesy of Qualcomm 
Qualcomm is expanding high-performance, low-power computing and On-device AI technology to industrial robots and automated equipment. On-device AI is technology that processes AI computations on the device itself without relying on external servers. It can be used for robots in industrial sites that must recognize and make judgments about their surroundings in real time.
Qualcomm will also hold the QAIPI-APAC 2026 Demo Day in Tokyo, Japan, on Dec. 2. Startups from the Asia-Pacific region, including Korea, will introduce their developed technologies and business results and seek opportunities to enter global markets.
Kim Sang-pyo, president of Qualcomm Korea, said, "As AI spreads across industries, the ability to apply innovative technologies in real environments and commercialize them is becoming even more important," and added, "Qualcomm will support startups from technology development to commercialization through QAIPI, and continue cooperating so that Korea's innovative corporations can create new growth opportunities in global markets."

Precision Lidar aids the search for resilient beech forests
October 21, 2026 
Terrestrial and UAV-based laser scanning systems from RIEGL have been purchased by Carinthia University of Applied Sciences (CUAS) for its new Interdisciplinary Center for Ecosystem Services and Biodiversity (ICEB). The investment establishes a combined TLS/ULS capability at the centre aimed at high-precision 3D data acquisition for biodiversity research and the quantitative assessment of ecosystem services.
The delivery comprises a RIEGL VZ-600i terrestrial laser scanner and a VUX-120-23 UAV laser scanning system, the latter integrated with a positioning unit and camera on a heavy-lift drone platform. The pairing allows the team to capture detailed stem and understory structure from the ground while covering canopy and larger survey areas from the air, producing complementary point clouds suited to forest structure analysis at both plot and landscape scale.
The equipment forms part of CUAS’s ‘BioDivTechLab’ project, funded by the Austrian Research Promotion Agency (FFG) through its R&D infrastructure program and co-financed by the European Union. It reflects growing investment by Austrian research institutions in remote sensing infrastructure for environmental applications, where quantifying ecosystem services such as carbon storage and habitat structure is increasingly in demand.
First deployment: linking genetics to forest structure
One of the first projects to use the systems is an international study funded by the Austrian Science Fund (FWF), titled ‘Seeing the Forest for the Trees’. It investigates how genetic variation among individual trees influences the performance of beech forests. The project integrates genomic data with terrestrial and UAV Lidar forest monitoring and satellite remote sensing, covering more than 1,000 beech trees across Europe.
The consortium includes the Spatial Genetics of the Environment group at the University of Zurich’s Department of Geography, CUAS’s ICEB in Villach, the Department of Genetics at Kazimierz Wielki University in Bydgoszcz, Poland, and partners in Romania and Germany.
In early September, CUAS’s Spatial Informatics for Environmental Applications (SIENA) department, led by Prof Gernot Paulus, visited the manufacturer’s headquarters in Horn for system handover, acceptance testing and in-depth training. SIENA is responsible for Lidar technologies within the newly founded ICEB.
From training to fieldwork: the terrestrial scanner will help researchers investigate how individual genetic differences influence beech forests across Europe. (Image courtesy: Prof Gernot Paulus)

Wilmington council backs $2 million deal to sweeten odds of landing Corning expansion 
The Wilmington City Council voted unanimously Tuesday night to approve $2 million in incentives for Corning Inc. to expand its operations in the city. 
By Hudson Steiner 
Published : Oct. 20, 2026 at 10:20 PM EDT 
Share 
Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google 
WILMINGTON, N.C. (WECT) - The Wilmington City Council voted unanimously Tuesday night to approve $2 million in incentives for Corning Inc. to expand its operations in the city, following suit with New Hanover County.
The council’s incentive package will provide annual payments of $400,000 a year for five years. In exchange, Corning would invest $585 million and create 414 new jobs.
The vote comes one day after New Hanover County commissioners voted to offer their own incentive package during a meeting Monday, putting up to $600,000 a year for five years from the county’s general fund, which is made up of taxpayer dollars.
PREVIOUS STORY: NHC Commissioners approve incentive for Corning Inc. to expand in Wilmington 
Corning is a glass products manufacturer based in Corning, New York.
“Based in Corning, New York, this multinational technology company specializes in glass, ceramics, and related materials,” Scott Satterfield, CEO of Wilmington Business Development, said during the county’s meeting. “For over 60 years Corning has been a vital employer here.”
Corning officials told commissioners that Wilmington is one of several locations under consideration for the expansion.
If the area is selected, the project would bring new jobs with salaries averaging more than $85,000 a year, along with the $585 million capital investment.
With both the city and county incentives now approved, the combined incentive package totals $5 million. Corning officials are now left to decide whether to proceed with the Wilmington expansion or pursue alternative locations.

Sasha Jovanovic

Chemours is facing a securities class action lawsuit filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware over alleged misstatements about Opteon demand and 2026 financial guidance, while also securing injunctions in Germany against companies accused of infringing its refrigerant patents at Chillventa 2026. 
The legal dispute cuts in two directions for Chemours, with questions around past demand disclosures for Opteon on one side and a clear signal that the business is prepared to defend the economic value of its refrigerant portfolio worldwide on the other. 
We will examine how Chemours' investment narrative is affected by alleged Opteon demand misstatements that sit alongside firm patent enforcement on refrigerants. 
Compare Chemours' situation with a curated set of industrials that are handling legal and patent pressure more quietly by scanning the 31 resilient stocks with low risk scores selections that still show resilient risk profiles. 
Chemours Investment Narrative Recap 
To own Chemours, you need to be comfortable with a chemicals producer that leans heavily on refrigerants, titanium dioxide and advanced materials, while currently reporting a loss of US$304 million on US$5.8b of revenue. The immediate swing factor is how quickly Thermal & Specialized Solutions stabilises after Opteon channel oversupply and softer HVAC activity. 
The new securities class action goes straight at that near term story, because it challenges disclosures about Opteon demand and 2026 guidance. If the allegations gain traction, the biggest risk is extra legal and credibility pressure on top of PFAS liabilities and interest costs that are already not well covered by earnings. 
The patent injunctions around Opteon related refrigerants at Chillventa 2026 are the clearest recent announcement that ties directly into this news. You have a business accused of overstating aftermarket demand while, in parallel, working with courts in Germany to block alleged infringing refrigerant products and protect its proprietary portfolio. 
For you, this combination keeps two clocks ticking at once. On one side, Chemours is trying to defend pricing and share in Thermal & Specialized Solutions through intellectual property enforcement. The implied earnings shift is sizeable, moving from a loss of US$304 million to a positive US$268.4 million, which is an earnings change of roughly US$572 million. By John Kim Published Oct 20, 2026, 7:01 PM EDT 
Save Share 
A gloved hand slides a sample plate into a laboratory instrument. / TokenPost.ai Citrini Research has singled out Charles River Laboratories and Revvity in an AI drug discovery thesis, arguing that faster candidate design could create more work for laboratory testing and research equipment providers.
The firm developed the thesis after testing Anthropic’s Claude Science. Its experiment produced protein binders for laboratory testing, an early research result rather than a completed treatment.
Charles River Laboratories provides drug-testing services. Revvity supplies research instruments and software. Citrini sees both companies as potential beneficiaries if AI helps researchers design candidates more quickly and more of those candidates move into physical experiments.
That increase in laboratory work is the premise of the thesis, not an observed rise in demand. Designing candidates faster would still leave researchers with the task of testing them. Citrini began exploring life sciences in June.

Dow boosted as markets rotate from tech shares
AFP 
October 20, 2026 3 min read 
CL=F

^DJI 
+2.15% 
Shares of industrial company 3M soared nearly six percent after it released earnings, lifting the Dow (Steve DYKES) Wall Street stocks mostly rose Tuesday, greeting a pullback in oil prices as investors steered funds towards industrial equities amid lingering caution over artificial intelligence shares. 
Comments from Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari describing US-Iran talks as "ongoing" pressured crude prices, despite no concrete changes in a conflict that has dented energy supplies for more than seven months. 
Saudi Arabia on Monday postponed a major investment conference due to repeated attacks from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis. 
International benchmark Brent oil futures finished down 0.7 percent at $108.79 a barrel after earlier hitting $111.99 a barrel. 
Wall Street stocks began meekly following losing sessions in leading European and Asian markets. But US equities picked up momentum as the day progressed, especially the blue-chip Dow index led by strong results from industrial company 3M. 
A more than one percent rise in the Dow showed a "rotation" from tech shares, said Briefing.com analyst Patrick O'Hare. 
"We still have some lingering softness in the tech trade and specifically the AI space so we're not getting a completely broad market rally," O'Hare said. 
"But a lot of stocks outside the tech sector are doing reasonably well today with oil prices having come down and entry trades remaining relatively well behaved." 
Tech shares have lately been volatile, with analysts pointing to worries over AI profitability and the hefty debt financing of some companies. 
The sector is also vulnerable after having outperformed the market for much of 2026. 
"There's some nervousness that perhaps the growth rates won't be as strong as people have assumed which is to say you could have really good news but it just might not be good enough to satisfy high expectations," O'Hare said. 
Earlier, AI worries hit Asian exchanges. 
Seoul and Tokyo again bore the brunt of the selling as chip giants SK hynix, Samsung and Kioxia took another beating owing to a sharp exit from a sector that saw blistering gains in the first half of this year. 
South Korea's Kospi stocks index sank nearly four percent, with SK hynix off 4.2 percent and Samsung down three percent. 
Further weighing on sentiment was the data center infrastructure firm Elice, whose shares collapsed more than 30 percent on their trading debut. 
The negative sentiment carried over to equity trading in Europe. 
The euro rose against the dollar but remained under pressure as violent protests in France and Italy have pushed up government bond yields. 
Story Continues 
The yield on France's 10-year government bond rose to 4.94 percent Tuesday, more than 150 basis points above the comparable German government bond, considered the European benchmark of creditworthiness. 
The resulting spread between the two yields reached the greatest level since 2011. 
Among individual companies, General Motors slumped 6.8 percent despite reporting better profits than expected. However, the automaker pointed to a recent uptick in commodity costs due to the US-Iran war, clouding its profit outlook.

According to Safran , its SkyNaute inertial navigation system has been selected for the Airbus A220, marking its first application on a commercial airliner. The company said the system combines inertial and satellite navigation technologies and is designed to maintain accurate navigation when GNSS signals are unavailable, jammed or spoofed.
Safran press release:
SkyNaute, the inertial navigation system developed by Safran Electronics & Defense, is entering commercial aviation on board the Airbus A220. By combining inertial navigation with hybridized satellite navigation (GNSS) data, it ensures that the aircraft maintains a precise and reliable trajectory in all circumstances.
Already selected for military aircraft, helicopters and drones operated by several European armed forces, SkyNaute demonstrates the full strength of Safran’s dual-use technologies. It now brings commercial air transport a decisive advantage from the defense world: resistance to interference. SkyNaute maintains a highly accurate trajectory even when GNSS signals are unavailable, jammed or spoofed. This capability has become essential for civil aviation, which faces a growing number of such disruptions in several regions of the world. This performance relies on proven technologies, first and foremost the hemispherical resonator gyroscope (HRG) patented by Safran Electronics & Defense. With no mechanical parts subject to wear, this sensor offers unmatched compactness and high resilience in harsh environments.
SkyNaute’s reduced weight, size and power consumption mean simpler installation and weight savings on board for airlines, while meeting the most stringent safety requirements of commercial air transport.
“ Seeing SkyNaute take its place on board the Airbus A220 is a source of immense pride for our teams: for the first time, our inertial navigation system will fly on an airliner. This is a strong signal for French industrial expertise. We sincerely thank Airbus for its trust,” said Benjamin Declety, Head of the Avionics Global Business Unit at Safran Electronics & Defense.
This expertise is rooted in Montluçon, in central France, where the HRG is fully developed and industrialized. In June 2026, Safran Electronics & Defense announced a €120 million investment to expand and modernize the site, tripling its HRG production capacity from 10,000 to 30,000 units per year by 2032.
With this selection, SkyNaute confirms its ability to adapt to aircraft with very different integration constraints. It has already been installed on helicopters subject to strong vibrations and wide temperature variations, on military aircraft exposed to shocks and jamming attempts, and on drones, which require high navigation accuracy and strong resistance to electromagnetic interference.

title: Vadzo Imaging Validates Bolt-234CGS Camera Compatibility with NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin: Onsemi AR0234 2MP Color MIPI CSI-2 Camera with Global Shutter and Onboard ISP - Newswire
