discovery_snippet: Vadzo Imaging Validates Bolt-234CGS Camera Compatibility with NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin: Onsemi AR0234 2MP Color MIPI CSI-2 Camera with Global Shutter and Onboard ISP    Newswire
content_text:
Vadzo Imaging Validates Bolt-234CGS Camera Compatibility with NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin: Onsemi AR0234 2MP Color MIPI CSI-2 Camera with Global Shutter and Onboard ISP
Press Release 
• 
Oct 20, 2026 
The Bolt-234CGS is a 2MP Color MIPI CSI-2 Camera built on the Onsemi AR0234 sensor, and Vadzo has validated its compatibility with NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. Jetson AGX Orin is a platform for multi-camera robots, retail systems, and surveillance nodes, and the camera modules attached to it decide how well that compute is used. Two choices matter most. A global shutter exposes every pixel at the same instant, so a moving robot, a passing shopper, or a vehicle appears undistorted. An on-board image signal processor finishes the image inside the module, so the Jetson receives a processed YUV image and its own ISP does not need to be tuned for the sensor. As a 2MP Global Shutter MIPI Camera and a 2MP AGX Orin MIPI Camera, the Bolt-234CGS delivers Full HD at up to 60 frames per second, with auto exposure and auto white balance applied in the module. Designed for warehouse robotics, smart surveillance, and retail analytics and automation, it gives AGX Orin systems consistent color and distortion-free frames. 
FORT WORTH, Texas, October 20, 2026 (Newswire.com)
-
Vadzo Imaging, a provider of embedded vision camera products for OEMs and system integrators, today announces validation of the Bolt-234CGS with NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin Camera. The Bolt-234CGS is a 2MP Color MIPI CSI-2 Camera built on the Onsemi AR0234 sensor with a global shutter and an on-board ISP. Part of Vadzo's MIPI camera portfolio, the module combines simultaneous pixel exposure with finished YUV output and two adapter board variants, one for 2-lane and one for 4-lane MIPI CSI-2. With this validation, Vadzo delivers a 2MP Global Shutter MIPI CSI-2 Camera for AGX Orin-based warehouse robotics, smart surveillance, and retail analytics and automation systems, together with guidance on how an on-board ISP changes the pipeline on NVIDIA Jetson Camera and on how to select the correct adapter board.
Technical Problem Definition: Why a Global Shutter MIPI Camera Needs Finished Output on Jetson 
Jetson AGX Orin Camera is built for demanding perception workloads. It combines a GPU, deep learning accelerators, and several camera inputs, so a single board can run navigation, detection, and recording for a robot or a retail system at once. The quality of what it perceives still depends on the camera, and two properties of the camera cause most of the trouble in practice. The first is how the sensor exposes the image. The second is where the image gets processed. Both are decided when the camera is chosen, long before the software team sees a frame.
Most sensors use a rolling shutter, which reads the image row by row. When the subject or the camera moves, the rows capture different moments, and straight lines bend. A forklift carrying a pallet, a robot arm sweeping past a shelf, a shopper walking through a doorway, and a camera on a moving vehicle all create this effect. For analytics that measure positions, read codes, or track people, the distortion matters, because geometry derived from a skewed image is wrong. Fast exposures reduce the skew but need strong light, which warehouses and stores do not always provide. A global shutter avoids the issue by exposing every pixel at the same instant, so moving subjects keep their shape. The benefit is greatest when subjects move quickly or when the camera itself is mounted on a moving platform.
Image processing raises the second problem. A raw sensor sends unprocessed Bayer data to the Jetson, which must demosaic, correct color, reduce noise, and manage exposure. On Jetson, that work is done by the host ISP, which needs a tuning profile for each sensor and lens, and good tuning takes time and expertise. Two products using the same Jetson can look quite different because of tuning alone. A module that finishes the image itself removes that task, but a buyer must then understand that the host ISP is not part of the pipeline. That is a fair exchange for many teams, and an unwelcome surprise for the few who expected raw access.
Connectors add a practical question. MIPI camera modules connect through a defined number of data lanes, and carrier boards differ in the connectors they offer. A camera that supports only one lane count limits where it can be used. Teams that discover these constraints late must redesign the carrier or change the camera after hardware is built. A short review of lane counts, connectors, and image processing needs at the start of a project avoids most of that rework.
Engineering Explanation: AR0234 On-board ISP MIPI Camera Behavior on Jetson AGX Orin 
The Bolt-234CGS is built on the Onsemi AR0234, a 2MP (1920 x 1200) color global shutter sensor with a 1/2.6 inch optical format and 3.0 micron pixels. The shutter is global, so the whole frame is captured in a single simultaneous exposure with no row-by-row timing. The 3.0 micron pixels are large for a 2MP sensor, which helps collect light in dim warehouse aisles and night scenes. Together they make the module an AR0234 AGX Orin Global Shutter Camera that delivers geometrically faithful frames to the platform. Teams that measure object positions or track motion between frames benefit most from that fidelity.
The on-board ISP is the second design choice. It converts the Bayer data into a finished image inside the module. According to the datasheet, it performs debayering, demosaicing, color correction, contrast correction, gamma correction, denoising, and lens corrections, and it supports automatic functions such as auto exposure and auto white balance. The module outputs YUV422 at 8-bit or 10-bit depth. Because the image is already processed, the camera is treated as a YUV source on Jetson. Frames reach the capture hardware directly, and the Jetson ISP is not used. This saves the effort of building and tuning an ISP profile, and it keeps color behavior the same on any host. The trade-off is that tuning is fixed in the module, so teams who want raw access and custom ISP control should choose a raw sensor module, which Vadzo also offers. Teams that are unsure can describe their pipeline, and Vadzo will recommend finished or raw output.
The module is a two-board solution, with the camera module board and an adapter board. The adapter comes in two variants, one for 2-lane MIPI CSI-2 and one for 4-lane. The 2-lane variant connects directly to Raspberry Pi and NVIDIA Jetson development kits, and the 4-lane variant provides the bandwidth for faster frame rates. In 4-lane mode, the supported video modes run at 120 frames per second at VGA, 60 at HD, and 60 at Full HD. The camera connector on each carrier board determines which adapter fits, so teams should match the adapter to their AGX Orin camera, and Vadzo supports that selection. Planning the connector choice early also lets the enclosure and cable routing be designed once.
Control and environmental details complete the picture. Camera controls include brightness, exposure, contrast, sharpness, saturation, gamma, gain, white balance, denoising, and LED flicker mitigation, with anti-flicker for 50Hz and 60Hz lighting. Still images can be captured as BMP files through a software trigger. The module draws between 0.80 W and 1.45 W at 3.3 volts, operates from minus 40 degrees C to 85 degrees C, measures 38 mm by 38 mm, is convertible to 32 mm by 32 mm, and weighs 13 grams without the lens. An S-Mount (M12) holder accepts a 74 DFOV lens, and two status LEDs show whether the module is powered with no streaming or actively streaming. Humidity is rated at 20 to 80 percent relative, non-condensing.
It helps to be clear about what the datasheet states and what it leaves to the integrator. The module delivers Full HD, HD, and VGA video, and the sensor's full 1920 x 1200 array is available as the maximum resolution. The two status LEDs, the software trigger for still capture, and the BMP still format are part of the module, while the GPIO lines are not connected by default. The lens is a fixed-focus S-Mount (M12) assembly, so working distance should be chosen during evaluation. Teams that need a different field of view can replace the lens with another M12 optic, and Vadzo can review the choice against the sensor.
Product Overview 
The Bolt-234CGS is a Full HD-capable global shutter module built on the Onsemi AR0234 sensor and validated with NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. As a 2MP MIPI CSI-2 Camera , it is built for AGX Orin-based systems that need undistorted frames and consistent color from a compact board. The module combines the sensor, an on-board ISP, and an S-Mount (M12) lens holder with a 74 DFOV lens, and it connects over a 2-lane or 4-lane adapter board. As an AR0234 AGX Orin Global Shutter Camera , it sends finished YUV frames to the platform, and as an AR0234 On-board ISP MIPI Camera , it applies debayering, color correction, denoising, auto exposure, and auto white balance before the frame leaves the module. The 2MP Global Shutter MIPI Camera designation confirms simultaneous exposure across the full frame. It also serves as a 2MP Color MIPI Camera and a 2MP AGX Orin MIPI CSI-2 Camera for designs that need finished color output.
Key Capabilities of the Onsemi AR0234 Global Shutter MIPI CSI-2 Camera for Jetson AGX Orin 
Key specs: 2MP (1920 x 1200) Max Resolution | Onsemi AR0234 1/2.6 inch Sensor Format | 3.0 micron Pixel | Color with Global Shutter | 2 Lane and 4 Lane MIPI CSI-2 Interface | S-Mount (M12 Standard) Fixed Focus Optics with 74 DFOV Lens
2MP Global Shutter MIPI Camera Exposure Without Motion Distortion 
A global shutter exposes every pixel at the same instant, so a moving subject keeps its shape. Warehouse robots, doorways, and moving vehicles produce motion that would skew a rolling shutter image. As a 2MP Global Shutter MIPI Camera, the Bolt-234CGS delivers geometrically faithful frames to the AGX Orin, so detection, tracking, and measurement work from accurate positions. Large 3.0-micron pixels also gather more light, which helps when exposure must stay short to freeze motion in dim scenes. Teams can confirm the result by recording a moving target at the intended mounting position.
NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin Compatibility for a 2MP AGX Orin MIPI CSI-2 Camera 
Vadzo has validated the module with NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, so it works as a 2MP AGX Orin MIPI CSI-2 Camera from the first day of evaluation. The module has also been integrated with Raspberry Pi, NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, and NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX-based solutions, which lets teams prototype on familiar hardware and move to AGX Orin without changing the camera. Because the output is finished YUV, the AGX Orin treats the module as a video source, and the platform's GPU and accelerators are free for perception. Teams should confirm the carrier board connector and choose the matching adapter. Prototyping on a familiar development kit first often shortens the path to a working AGX Orin design.
On-Board ISP Performing Debayering, Demosaicing, and Corrections 
The on-board image signal processor finishes the image inside the module. It performs debayering and demosaicing, color correction, contrast correction, gamma correction, denoising, and lens corrections, and the result is an image that looks the same on any host. For an AR0234 On-board ISP MIPI CSI-2 Camera, this means no host ISP profile has to be built or tuned, which saves weeks of engineering effort. The host receives YUV422 frames at 8-bit or 10-bit depth, ready for encoding or inference. Integrators who want to adjust processing can use the available camera controls, including denoising, sharpness, and gamma.
Auto Exposure and Auto White Balance for an AR0234 AE AWB MIPI Camera 
Warehouses, stores, and outdoor sites change their lighting through the day, and manual settings cannot follow. Auto exposure adjusts exposure and gain to keep brightness suitable, and auto white balance keeps whites neutral under mixed lighting. As a 2MP Auto White Balance MIPI Camera and an AR0234 AE AWB MIPI Camera, the module applies both inside the ISP, and manual control remains available through software. The controls also include denoising and LED flicker mitigation, which help in spaces lit by LED fixtures. Anti-flicker settings for 50Hz and 60Hz lighting add further protection against banding.
2 Lane and 4 Lane MIPI CSI-2 Adapter Board Variants 
The module is a two-board solution, and the adapter board comes in two variants. The 2-lane variant connects directly to Raspberry Pi and NVIDIA Jetson development kits and keeps wiring simple. The 4-lane variant carries more data, which allows faster frame rates, with Full HD at 60 frames per second and VGA at 120 frames per second. Teams choose the variant that matches their carrier board connector and the frame rate they need, and they can change it later without changing the camera board, which protects the investment in lens and enclosure design. The datasheet frame rates apply to the 4-lane variant, so teams that need the highest rates should plan for it.
Compact, Wide Temperature 2MP Color MIPI Camera for OEM Designs 
The module measures 38 mm by 38 mm, convertible to 32 mm by 32 mm, weighs 13 grams without the lens, and operates from minus 40 degrees C to 85 degrees C. That range suits robots, outdoor poles, and enclosed retail equipment. As a 2MP Color MIPI Camera with finished output, it supports lens matching, firmware customization, and enclosure design assistance from Vadzo, and teams moving from evaluation to volume can keep the same module and documentation. A wide temperature range also reduces the need for extra thermal protection in many enclosures.
"Jetson AGX Orin gives teams a great deal of compute, and the camera should not waste it. A rolling shutter skews moving subjects, and a raw module adds a tuning job to every project. The Bolt-234CGS was validated to remove both problems. The global shutter exposes the whole frame at once, and the on-board ISP delivers a finished image with auto exposure and auto white balance, so the Orin can spend its power on perception. We are also direct about the trade-off. Tuning lives in the module, so teams that want raw access should talk to us about a raw sensor option. For most warehouse, surveillance, and retail projects, a clean finished image is the faster path." - Alwin Vincent, Product Manager, Vadzo Imaging .
Application Specific Sections: Global Shutter MIPI Camera Systems in Practice 
Warehouse Robotics MIPI Camera and Global Shutter Robotics MIPI Camera Applications 
Warehouse robots scan objects and documents, read labels with OCR, and detect obstacles while they move. The Bolt-234CGS works as a Warehouse Robotics MIPI Camera whose global shutter keeps labels and shelf edges straight during motion, and as a Global Shutter Robotics MIPI Camera , it gives navigation and detection software accurate geometry. The same module serves a 2MP Warehouse Robotics Camera role for compact robots with several camera positions around one AGX Orin. Because the lens is fixed focus, the working distance should be matched to the task during evaluation. Robots that need to read at several distances may pair modules with different lenses.
Smart Surveillance MIPI Camera and Global Shutter Smart Surveillance Camera Applications 
Smart surveillance covers day and night video recording, smart parking, pedestrian safety, and facial recognition. The module serves as a Smart Surveillance MIPI Camera that records vehicles and people without motion skew, and as a Global Shutter Smart Surveillance Camera , it keeps fast subjects such as passing vehicles undistorted. As a 2MP Smart Surveillance MIPI Camera, it fits AGX Orin recording and analytics nodes, and the wide temperature range suits outdoor installations. Night scenes and recognition at a distance may need supplementary lighting and an optics review. Recorded footage also benefits from the steady color that automatic white balance provides across the day.
Retail Analytics MIPI Camera and Retail Automation MIPI Camera Applications 
Retail systems monitor inventory, verify age, analyze demographics, watch shelves, and support self-checkout. The module works as a Retail Analytics MIPI Camera and a Retail Automation MIPI Camera that keeps shoppers and products undistorted as they move, with automatic exposure and white balance that hold color steady under mixed store lighting. As a Global Shutter Retail Analytics Camera, it supports multi-camera shelf and checkout views on one AGX Orin. Age verification and demographic analysis involve privacy rules and consent requirements that belong to the solution provider and the retailer. Inventory and shelf monitoring need no such analysis and rely mainly on image quality.
Frequently Asked Questions About Global Shutter MIPI Camera Systems 
Q: What is the difference between a global shutter and a rolling shutter camera? 
A: Vadzo Imaging explains it simply: a rolling shutter reads the image row by row, so a fast-moving subject can look skewed, while a global shutter exposes every pixel at the same instant, so moving subjects keep their shape. A 2MP Global Shutter MIPI Camera suits robots, vehicles, and shoppers in motion. A rolling shutter can still be a good choice for slow or still scenes, and Vadzo Imaging offers both so customers can match the shutter to the application, with guidance from its engineers.
Q: Does a MIPI camera with an on-board ISP bypass the NVIDIA Jetson ISP? 
A: Yes. A camera with an on-board ISP sends finished YUV frames, so the Jetson treats it as a video source and does not run its own ISP on raw data. That saves the effort of building and tuning an ISP profile and keeps color the same on any host. Teams that want raw access and custom tuning can ask Vadzo Imaging about raw sensor modules, which use the host ISP instead. Either path is valid, and the right one depends on how much control a team wants.
Q: Can one NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin system run several MIPI camera modules? 
A: The platform supports multiple camera inputs, and the number that is available depends on the carrier board and its connectors. A 2MP AGX Orin MIPI Camera needs the adapter board that matches each connector, in either the 2-lane or the 4-lane variant. Vadzo Imaging recommends confirming the lane count, the connectors, and the total bandwidth on the real carrier before planning a multi-camera design. A short bench test with two modules usually reveals any limit quickly.
Q: Is a global shutter worth it for retail analytics and warehouse robots? 
A: It is worth it when subjects or camera units move. A Global Shutter Retail Analytics Camera keeps shoppers and products undistorted, and a Global Shutter Robotics MIPI Camera keeps labels and edges straight while a robot moves, so measurements and detections stay accurate. For slow or still scenes, the benefit is smaller. Vadzo Imaging suggests testing with the real motion in the target scene before choosing, since the benefit depends on how fast the scene moves.
Q: Why should OEMs choose Vadzo Imaging as their supplier of AGX Orin compatible camera modules? 
A: Vadzo Imaging offers more than a camera module built around a capable sensor. OEMs working with Vadzo Imaging receive a global shutter module with a documented on-board ISP, two adapter board variants, validated integration across Jetson and Raspberry Pi platforms, and honest guidance on when a raw sensor module is the better fit, plus engineering support for lens selection, firmware customization, and enclosure design. Vadzo Imaging maintains evaluation kits with no minimum order requirement, so teams can test on their own carrier boards before committing to volume production.
Availability 
The Bolt-234CGS 2MP Color MIPI CSI-2 Camera built on the Onsemi AR0234 sensor is available now for evaluation and production orders. Evaluation kits include the camera module, the 2-lane or 4-lane adapter board, and platform documentation, with no minimum order requirement. Engineering teams can confirm streaming on their own AGX Orin carrier board, check motion handling in their own scenes, and test the on-board ISP controls before committing to a production bill of materials, which tells them more than a datasheet comparison alone. Teams that need a different lens or adapter configuration can ask Vadzo to review the setup. Evaluation also lets teams compare the module's finished color against their own reference scenes, which is the quickest way to decide between finished and raw output. Its products are designed for seamless integration with leading embedded platforms including NVIDIA Jetson, Rockchip, Raspberry Pi, and NXP i.MX. Have you been searching for a stock that might be well-positioned to maintain its earnings-beat streak in its upcoming report? It is worth considering Thermo Fisher Scientific (TMO), which belongs to the Zacks Medical - Instruments industry. 
This maker of scientific instrument and laboratory supplies has an established record of topping earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The company boasts an average surprise for the past two quarters of 5.11%. 
For the last reported quarter, Thermo Fisher came out with earnings of $6.03 per share versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.71 per share, representing a surprise of 5.60%. For the previous quarter, the company was expected to post earnings of $5.2 per share and it actually produced earnings of $5.44 per share, delivering a surprise of 4.62%. 
Price and EPS Surprise 
Thanks in part to this history, there has been a favorable change in earnings estimates for Thermo Fisher lately. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the stock is positive, which is a great indicator of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with its solid Zacks Rank. 
Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven. 
The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier. 
Thermo Fisher currently has an Earnings ESP of +0.07%, which suggests that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This positive Earnings ESP when combined with the stock's Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) indicates that another beat is possibly around the corner. We expect the company's next earnings report to be released on October 21, 2026. 
When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss. 
Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

METiS Enters Collaboration with Eli Lilly for Next-Generation Tissue-Specific LNP Delivery Technologies
Author(s) Nicholas Jacobus 
METiS TechBio enters a collaboration with Eli Lilly to develop next-generation, tissue-specific lipid nanoparticle delivery technologies using METiS’s AI-driven lipid discovery platform.
Advertisement
METiS TechBio announced a strategic collaboration with Eli Lilly and Company focused on researching and discovering novel lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based delivery solutions designed to enable tissue-specific delivery of therapeutic modalities.
Under the agreement, METiS is eligible to receive an upfront payment in the low double-digit millions of dollars, upwards of approximately $1.1 billion in development, regulatory, and commercial milestone payments, and single-digit tiered royalties on annual net sales of any resulting products. 1 
What will each company contribute?
METiS is expected to apply its proprietary, AI-driven ionizable lipid discovery and optimization platform, AiLNP, to develop next-generation delivery technologies aiming at improving the targeting and biodistribution of LNP-based delivery systems. 1 Eli Lilly is set to contribute its drug discovery, development, and commercialization expertise to advance the collaboration.

The companies say combining METiS’s generative and predictive AI capabilities for rational LNP design with Eli Lilly’s scientific and development infrastructure is intended to yield novel LNP architectures with improved tissue specificity, enhanced therapeutic performance, and broader applicability across multiple disease areas. 1 
Why does delivery technology matter here?
Lipid nanoparticles have become a central modality for delivering therapeutic payloads to target tissues and cells, underpinning everything from mRNA vaccines to gene-editing therapies. 2 As the industry moves into more complex modalities, the ability to direct payloads precisely to intended tissues, while minimizing off-target exposure, has become a key bottleneck in translating novel therapeutics into approved products. METiS positions AiLNP as an answer to that bottleneck, using generative AI models, including one referred to as PhatGPT, to generate and optimize lipid candidates computationally rather than through traditional trial-and-error screening. 1,2 
What is METiS saying about the deal?
METiS frames the collaboration as validation of its AI-driven approach and an opportunity to scale its platform through a partner with substantial development reach. “Delivery remains a critical determinant of therapeutic success, particularly as the industry expands into increasingly sophisticated modalities,” says Chris Lai, chairman and CEO of METiS TechBio. “We are excited to collaborate with Lilly, a global leader in the discovery and development of innovative medicines. By combining METiS’ AI-powered platform with Lilly’s scientific expertise and development capabilities, we aim to unlock a new generation of tissue-targeted delivery technologies that have the potential to transform how medicines reach patients.”
What’s next? 
Terms of the agreement were not fully disclosed, including which disease areas or specific programs the collaboration will initially target. 1 The deal adds Eli Lilly to a growing list of large pharmaceutical companies turning to AI-native biotechs for delivery innovation, as sponsors look to extend LNP technology beyond its original mRNA vaccine applications into gene therapies, RNA interference, and other emerging modalities.

content_text:
Qualcomm to Unite Regional V2X Standards Under Global V2X Solution
Highlights: Qualcomm ® V2X chipsets to support the 760 MHz ITS Connect standard utilized in Japan, further extending a globally interoperable platform across major V2X deployments worldwide. Qualcomm advances globally interoperable V2X solutions to help accelerate deployment of connected safety technologies and help reduce road fatalities. Toyota welcomes Qualcomm’s efforts to foster broader industry collaboration toward a Zero-Accident society. Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. today announced that its Qualcomm ® vehicle-to-everything (V2X) chipsets will support nearly all major regional V2X deployments worldwide through a single platform. As the latest expansion of this capability, Qualcomm V2X chipsets will support the 760 MHz ARIB-T109 standard, bringing native compatibility with Japan's V2X band alongside the 5.9 GHz band already supported. These advancements are designed to reduce the need for region-specific hardware, lower deployment complexity, and accelerate the deployment of V2X technologies that can improve safety for drivers, passengers, and vulnerable road users (VRUs), including pedestrians, cyclists, and motorcyclists. V2X is a unique component of the vehicle safety stack, providing real-time awareness of hazards beyond a vehicle's line of sight while meeting the stringent security and reliability requirements of safety-critical applications. V2X enables direct communication to detect hazards around corners, through obstacles, and beyond visible range, enhancing safety for vehicle occupants and vulnerable road users. Recognizing the potential of connected safety technologies to help reduce road incidents, Qualcomm Technologies and Toyota recognize the importance of broad industry collaboration in advancing Vision Zero, the global initiative to eliminate traffic fatalities and serious injuries through greater industry collaboration, interoperability, and adoption of connected safety technologies. Achieving this vision requires collaboration among automakers, technology providers, governments, and infrastructure stakeholders. V2X can play a critical role in advancing this vision by providing reliable real-time communication to help improve safety for all road users, enable cooperation with smart infrastructure and augment the vehicle’s advanced driver assistance system as the only non-line-of-sight sensor. Through investment in globally interoperable V2X technology, Qualcomm Technologies aims to accelerate adoption with scalable solutions that can have a positive impact on road safety in all geographies and that can support additional use cases as vehicles and transportation systems continue to evolve.   “V2X has the potential to play a transformative role in road safety, but realizing its full impact requires solutions that can scale globally and operate across regional ecosystems,” said Nakul Duggal, Executive Vice President and Group General Manager, Automotive, Industrial and Embedded IoT, and Robotics, Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. “By extending our V2X technology abstraction to support Japan's 760 MHz standard, we are helping enable more interoperable and globally deployable V2X solutions. As adoption of V2X technology continues to grow, we are taking an important step toward accelerating the deployment and advancing a shared Vision Zero goal with Toyota and other stakeholders across the industry to help eliminate road fatalities.” “Toyota welcomes Qualcomm Technologies’ efforts to foster broader industry collaboration toward a zero-accident society,” said Keiji Yamamoto, Chief Officer, Digital Information and Communication Group, Toyota Motor Corporation, and Chair of ITS Japan. “Road accidents remain a global challenge that cannot be solved by any single company, industry sector, or region alone. Eliminating traffic accidents requires the collective efforts of automakers, technology providers, governments, and infrastructure stakeholders. We highly appreciate Qualcomm Technologies’ continued investment in innovative technologies and its leadership in bringing together stakeholders across the mobility ecosystem to help advance toward zero traffic accidents and Mobility for All.”

Can Qualcomm's PickNik Acquisition Strengthen Its Robotics Edge?

Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM is strengthening its position in the rapidly evolving robotics market through its proposed acquisition of PickNik Robotics, a developer of advanced robotics software. The transaction aligns with Qualcomm's strategy to expand its footprint in physical artificial intelligence (AI), edge computing and intelligent robotics.
PickNik is recognized for its stewardship of MoveIt, a widely adopted open-source robotics manipulation framework built on the Robot Operating System (ROS). The platform supports motion planning, manipulation and robotic control across industrial automation, service robotics and emerging physical AI applications. The transaction, subject to customary closing conditions, could strengthen Qualcomm's ability to offer integrated hardware and software solutions. 
Transaction Rationale 
The buyout is expected to enhance Qualcomm's Dragonwing Robotics platforms by integrating MoveIt and PickNik's commercial MoveIt Pro software. This combination could enable developers to leverage Qualcomm's AI processing, connectivity and heterogeneous computing capabilities alongside advanced motion planning and real-time robotic control.
The integration is also expected to extend to Arduino platforms, beginning with VENTUNO Q boards. This could make advanced robotics development more accessible to a broader developer community while accelerating the transition from prototypes to commercial deployments.
Importantly, Qualcomm intends to maintain MoveIt as an open-source framework supporting third-party hardware. This approach could encourage wider ecosystem participation and strengthen developer engagement, potentially boosting adoption of its Dragonwing platforms. 
Physical AI Opportunities Support Long-Term Diversification 
The planned acquisition complements Qualcomm's broader efforts to diversify beyond smartphones into automotive, industrial IoT and edge AI markets. Its March 2026 collaboration with NEURA Robotics to advance cognitive robotics and humanoid applications further underscores its growing focus on physical AI.
Combining PickNik's software expertise with Qualcomm's power-efficient computing capabilities could improve its competitive positioning as demand for intelligent automation increases across industrial and commercial applications.
However, the acquisition's financial terms remain undisclosed, limiting visibility into its immediate earnings contribution. Integration challenges, competition in robotics computing and uncertain commercialization timelines could also constrain near-term benefits. Stiff competition from NVIDIA Corporation NVDA, Broadcom Inc. AVGO and Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD further strains its margins.
Nevertheless, PickNik's established developer ecosystem and robotics software capabilities could help Qualcomm expand its addressable market and deepen customer engagement. Successful integration may strengthen QCOM's position in next-generation robotics while supporting its long-term diversification strategy.

Arkema Inaugurates New Acrylic Acid Purification Unit 
Arkema has opened a new acrylic acid purification unit at its Carling production site in France, deploying a new process that improves energy efficiency by 25 % and reduces carbon intensity by 20 %. The EUR 150 million investment is part of the company’s broader decarbonisation programme . 
20 October 2026 
Arkema 
Binders 
Expansion 
Save in bookmarks 
Arkema's new acrylic acid purification unit at the Carling site in France marks a significant step in the company's decarbonisation investment programme. 
Source: Arkema 
Advertisement:
Arkema has inaugurated a new acrylic acid purification unit at its Carling site in Saint-Avold, France. The unit operates on a new process and is located at one of Europe’s major acrylic monomer production facilities. Carling produces acrylic monomers used in performance coatings, adhesives, water treatment, and other advanced materials. 
According to Arkema, the new unit improves the energy efficiency of the purification process by 25 % and reduces the carbon intensity of site operations by 20 %. The company also states that the new technology optimises resource and waste management and significantly reduces solvent consumption. Arkema describes the investment as placing the Carling plant among reference sites in the industry, aligned with the highest operational and environmental standards. 
EUR 150 Million Investment Targets Decarbonisation of European Acrylic Production 
The project was decided in 2023 and was partly funded by the French State through the France 2030 programme, operated by ADEME and funded by the European Union via NextGenerationEU. Thierry Le Hénaff, chairman and chief executive officer of Arkema, commented: “With an investment of nearly €150 million, this new unit represents one of Arkema’s largest industrial projects in France. It will contribute to the Group’s ambitious climate plan, underpinned by a dedicated investment program supporting Arkema’s decarbonization, with a cumulative amount that could reach €400 million over the 2022-2030 period.” 
The inauguration ceremony was attended by Le Hénaff and Stéphane Séjourné, executive vice-president of the European Commission for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy. The event was held on the same day as the Critical Chemicals Alliance General Assembly, which brought together European industrial leaders and policymakers to address challenges related to sovereignty, competitiveness, and decarbonisation. 
European Industrial Policy and the Role of Low-Carbon Acrylic Materials 
Séjourné underlined the broader political significance of the investment: “Europe must keep its chemical industry. There can be neither industrial sovereignty nor strategic autonomy if we allow the essential building blocks of our economy to leave. Carling is showing the way forward: nearly EUR 150 million invested to produce in Europe, using less energy and generating less carbon, while building on decades of industrial know-how. This is exactly the model we want to promote: decarbonizing without deindustrializing, investing in our regions, and making our industrial hubs the driving forces of our future.” 
Arkema states that the unit is part of its decarbonisation investment programme and supports what the company describes as its ambitious climate plan. The company adds that the investment strengthens its position in the low-carbon acrylic materials market in Europe.

Industrial conglomerate 3M lifted its full-year profit forecast on Tuesday after cost-control initiatives and higher prices supported margins, while its safety and industrial business remained resilient.
The company now expects full-year adjusted profit per share of $9.10 to $9.15, up from its prior forecast of $8.80 to $8.95.
The company's shares were up 2.7% before the bell.
Robust U.S. industrial activity, along with rising sales of chipmaking machines and materials, has helped the company offset uneven demand in some end markets affected by inflationary pressures.
Under CEO William Brown, the company has also focused on improving customer service and operational execution to strengthen growth and profitability.
Its consumer-facing businesses have continued to operate in a challenging spending environment, reflecting cautious discretionary purchases by customers.

At the same time, higher energy costs have raised concerns about the potential impact on manufacturing activity and broader industrial demand.
While demand from automotive and consumer electronics customers has remained subdued, growth in data centers and semiconductor-related markets has provided a bright spot for 3M's Transportation and Electronics business, helping cushion weakness in some traditional end markets.
The Saint Paul, Minnesota-based company launched 87 new products in the third quarter. It expects to launch more than 350 products by the end of this year.
The Scotch-tape and Post-it maker reported adjusted quarterly revenue of $6.6 billion, up 4.2%.
The company's quarterly adjusted profit was $2.50 per share, up from $2.23 per share a year ago.

HyProMag USA deploys third mobile system
Several technology and recycling firms in the United States and Canada have collaborated to invest in mobile systems to process printed circuit boards and hard drives.
“The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project,” says Julian Treger, CEO of CoTec Holdings.
Photo courtesy of Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions 
By
Brian Taylor, Senior Editor 
Published October 20, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
A coalition of firms in the United States and Canada, some with ownership stakes in each other, have now deployed three mobile hard disk drive (HDD) separation system designed to recover rare earth element (REE) and magnet materials from discarded electronic components.
Canada-based Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. says HyProMag USA LLC, in which it owns a stake, has announced the deployment of its third Spanish-made Inserma Anoia S.L. HDD separation system to be used as a mobile processing unit, “expanding HyProMag USA’s processing and customer engagement capabilities across the U.S.”
Adds Mkango, “The deployment further strengthens HyProMag USA’s partnership with Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions (ILS) and supports the expansion of a scalable nationwide platform for the recovery and recycling of rare earth magnets from end-of-life HDDs.”
ILS is based in Nevada and has processing capacity there and in South Carolina, according to Mkango.
Also involved is HyProMag USA co-owner CoTec Holdings Corp., a Canada-based firm that says it “integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.” 
Mkango says feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs undertaken by the companies involved, “continue to strengthen the feedstock platform and are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up activities” at a planned HyProMag USA Texas Hub facility in the Dallas-Fort Worth scheduled to open in 2028.
The Canadian company says Delaware-based HyProMag USA also has completed commercial sales of recovered printed circuit board (PCB) material to downstream smelter partners, generating revenue that supports the acquisition and retention of magnet-bearing feedstock inventory.
“The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project,” says Julian Treger, CEO of CoTec Holdings.
“Together with continued progress in feedstock sourcing and commercial PCB recovery, it strengthens our operating platform and expands our ability to engage directly with customers across multiple end markets,” adds Treger.
Remars Graham Davy, Managing Director of ILS , “The focus of the ILS team has been on demonstrating that HDDs can be efficiently processed into separate, marketable material streams. The mobile unit allows us to work directly with customers at their facilities, supporting trial programs, demonstrating material recovery performance and creating opportunities to secure additional feedstock supply.”
The companies say they are tapping into diversified feedstock channels “across industrial, health care, government and IT asset disposition sectors.”

“ABB delivered record order intake, and improved operational performance with strong cash flow and return on capital. We advanced our leading position in direct current technology and today we progressed on M&A with a new electrification joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric.”
Morten Wierod, CEO 
CEO summary
Our third quarter order intake reached a record $12 billion, nudging up sequentially; a stronger outcome than the historical pattern of seasonal decline. Year-on-year, orders grew 40% (40% comparable), driven by strong growth in two of our three business areas with a positive development across the majority of customer segments. Most notably so in the data center segment where we saw a triple-digit increase. Revenues were strong, yet order intake was even stronger, yielding a book-to-bill of 1.24.
Overall, we progressed according to plan. We converted strong revenue growth of 14% (14% comparable) into a 24% increase in Operational EBITA which reached $2 billion with margin expanding 160 basis points to 20.8%. We also materially improved Income from operations by 15% with a margin of 19.0%. Earnings per share remained virtually stable, reflecting increased Net finance expenses mainly due to the non-cash revaluation of the deal contingent FX hedge linked to the announced Rotork acquisition. We continue to deliver strong Return on capital employed which improved to 29.9%.
This was yet another solid cash flow quarter. Free cash flow of $1.6 billion was supported by robust earnings combined with disciplined management of Trade net working capital, which more than compensated for higher capex spend. This supported a sustained solid Free cash flow margin of around 14%, on a 12-month rolling basis. At $3.7 billion year-to-date, we are well positioned to surpass last year’s annual level of $4.6 billion.
In the current strong market environment it is essential to maintain focus and discipline, and we incrementally scale capacity to support our strong delivery track record. We already trend at a higher capex level of around $1 billion and do not expect it to rise further in the mid-term. Our investment approach is deliberate: incremental capacity expansion, productivity through automation, and selectively leveraging third-party assembly; balancing capturing of near-term demand with long-term resilience.
A significant milestone was the launch of the Infinitus Direct Current (DC) portfolio, enabling AI data center customers to achieve higher power density and improved energy efficiency. Our portfolio comprises five building blocks that can be combined into complete systems tailored to specific architectures. This includes a Solid State Transformer commercially available in the second half of 2027. We are able to partner with our customers from source to rack across the full spectrum of DC architectures. The portfolio enables acceleration of adoption of DC architectures in data centers and other energy-intensive industries.
Our partnership with Ferrari Hypersail demonstrates our commitment to advancing DC technologies and promoting their broader adoption across industries. The project – a 100-foot, renewable-powered full-foiling monohull yacht - is conceived as an operational proving ground for next-generation microgrid architecture. Its focus on energy management, marine electrical systems, and energy storage closely aligns with our expertise in these areas. The vessel is designed to operate as a fully self-sufficient system, integrating 800 VDC architectures. The engineering challenge central to this partnership – real-time orchestration of renewable generation, storage, and power distribution – mirrors the critical dynamics of emerging industrial microgrids.
It is also good to see our M&A activities bearing fruit. Following the Rotork announcement in July, we today announced that we will acquire a controlling 51 percent stake in a joint venture (JV) to be formed with Mitsubishi Electric’s low voltage power distribution business, with an option for full ABB ownership in the mid-term. This deal will make us the low voltage market leader in Japan, one of the world’s largest electrification markets, allowing us to benefit from the broad electric power trends including any local data center build-out. It also opens doors to the Asia-Pacific region. The Mitsubishi Electric business to be contributed to the JV generated around JPY 102 billion (~$640 million) in revenues in its fiscal year 2025, with a low double-digit EBITDA margin. We expect the joint venture to improve to at least a 20 percent Operational EBITA margin within 5 years. Similar to our successful GEIS acquisition, the profitability improvement will be driven by expanding sales through combined channels, introducing ABB products and technology to Mitsubishi Electric’s customer base and optimizing manufacturing. We acquire a controlling 51% stake in the newly carved out company as well as full ownership of Mitsubishi Electric’s JV-related sales operations outside of Japan for a total consideration of around JPY 79 billion (∼$495 million). These sales operations outside of Japan represent approximately 15% of revenues. The transaction values the combined businesses at a total enterprise value (EV) of about $890 million. Combined, this translates to valuation multiples of EV/Sales ∼1.4 and EV/EBITDA of ∼11.1 based on reported fiscal year 2025. The latter reduces into the mid- to high single-digit range when assuming realization of expected synergies. We see long-term returns well above cost of capital.
Morten Wierod , CEO center 
Outlook
In the fourth quarter of 2026 , we expect comparable revenue growth to be broadly similar to the third quarter and Operational EBITA margin to sequentially soften although less than historical pattern. This excludes the positive impact of ∼CHF240 million related to the sale of properties already completed in Q4.
In full-year 2026, we expect a positive book-to-bill, and comparable revenue growth in the ”low teens” range, year-on-year. The reported Operational EBITA margin should improve by at least 270 basis points year-on-year.

query: ("ABB" OR "ABB Group") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
ABB joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric to expand position in Asia-Pacific markets
Group press release
Joint venture will transform ABB’s electrification position in Japan and expand access to key growth markets across Asia-Pacific
$495 million investment will further strengthen global leadership in low-voltage power distribution and protection
ABB to hold controlling 51 percent stake in a joint venture formed with Mitsubishi Electric’s carved-out low-voltage power distribution product business
ABB today announced the creation of a joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric’s carved-out low-voltage power distribution product business, forming a new company focused on low-voltage solutions for Asian markets. For a consideration of JPY 79 billion (~$495 million), ABB will acquire a controlling 51 percent stake in the newly carved out company as well as full ownership of the related sales operations outside of Japan of Mitsubishi Electric’s low-voltage power distribution products. The transaction, which provides an option for full ownership by ABB in the mid-term, is expected to close in the second half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.
The new company brings together ABB’s technology and global sales network with Mitsubishi Electric’s established market presence. It will transform the limited presence of ABB’s Electrification business area in Japan into a leading position in one of the world’s largest electrification markets, while strengthening ABB’s ability to grow across Asia-Pacific.
Giampiero Frisio, President of ABB’s Electrification Business Area, said: “Japan is one of the world’s most important electrification markets, where the people in Mitsubishi Electric’s low-voltage power distribution division have served customers and built deep expertise over many decades. This joint venture brings together that strong local foundation with ABB’s leading technologies and global reach, significantly strengthening our position in Japan and across Asia-Pacific. For customers and employees, it means continuity, greater opportunities, and access to a broader portfolio of low-voltage solutions. For ABB, this partnership brings together the best of both companies in a long-term commitment to growth in the region.”
Takayuki Tsuzuki, Mitsubishi Electric Corporation’s Senior Executive Officer, Group President, Factory Automation Systems, said: “Mitsubishi Electric’s power distribution business has continued to improve its technological and quality capabilities over the past 100 years. Currently, Mitsubishi Electric is well positioned in many product fields in Japan, supporting a stable supply of electricity and energy essential to society. Through this joint venture with ABB, Mitsubishi Electric will combine ABB’s global business foundation with the technologies, quality, customer base and sales channels it has cultivated over many years. By doing so, we aim to provide even higher value to our customers and further grow and develop our power distribution product business.”
Mitsubishi Electric’s power distribution business employs around 2,800 people, with dedicated manufacturing facilities in Fukuyama, Japan, and Hanoi, Vietnam. Its portfolio includes low-voltage circuit breakers, switches, motor starters, contactors and control devices, energy measurement and monitoring equipment, and uninterruptible power supply systems.
The joint venture advances ABB’s well-established local-for-local strategy, sourcing and producing close to customers in key markets. By combining ABB’s products and global sales network with Mitsubishi Electric’s customer relationships and local manufacturing footprint, the joint venture will create a broader offer for customers in Asia-Pacific, while giving ABB the opportunity to introduce proven technologies to Mitsubishi Electric’s customer base.
In FY2025 ending March 2026, Mitsubishi Electric’s Low-Voltage power distribution business achieved net sales of around JPY 102 billion (~$640 million) with a low double-digit EBITDA margin. The related sales operations outside of Japan represent approximately 15 percent of revenue. The transaction values the combined businesses at a total enterprise value (EV) of around $890 million and implies an EV/Sales multiple of around 1.4x and an EV/EBITDA multiple of around 11.1x based on FY2025.
ABB expects synergies to improve the joint venture’s earnings, reducing the implied EV/EBITDA multiple to the mid- to high- single-digit range. ABB expects the joint venture to be accretive to earnings per share after year one and to achieve an operational EBITA margin of at least 20 percent within five years, comparable with other ABB Electrification operations.

By connecting its engineering and digitalization expertise, ABB helps industries run at high performance, while becoming more efficient, productive and sustainable so they outperform. content_text:
AI worries weigh on ABB shares despite record orders
By Thomson Reuters 
Oct 20, 2026 | 1:10 AM 
By John Revill
ZURICH, Oct 20 (Reuters) – ABB dropped nearly 6% on Tuesday as market nervousness about the sustainability of investments in artificial intelligence weighed on the Swiss engineering company, which is a major supplier to data centres.
Record new orders and an increase in its full-year ​sales guidance failed to appease institutional buy-side investors who were looking for more, analysts said, ‌as AI-linked stocks fell more broadly.
On South Korea’s stock market, which has become one of the clearest measures of AI sentiment, traders sold heavily on Tuesday as concern mounted over rising costs.
While European semiconductor stocks also fell, ABB shares fell more than peers. The stock, which reached its highest level to date of 89.14 Swiss francs ($108.13) in June, dropped to 70.72 ‌Swiss francs ​on the Swiss exchange after the results.
“Operationally ABB remains strong, but ⁠waning AI enthusiasm is creating headwinds,” ⁠said Marco Estermann, an analyst at Luzerner Kantonalbank.
“Ahead of the third quarter there was a risk that even results exceeding expectations would not be enough to support the share price.”
During its third quarter, ABB said its revenue rose 14% to $9.70 billion, slightly below analysts’ forecasts of $9.74 billion in a ​company-gathered consensus.
Operational earnings before interest, tax and amortisation jumped 24% to $2.03 billion in the three months to the end of September, slightly ahead of analyst forecasts for $2.0 billion.
Another analyst said fears had increased about ⁠the number of companies that will survive in the artificial ⁠intelligence sector, concerns that drove selling in US cloud company CoreWeave last week.
Andreas ​Lipkow, chief analyst at broker CMC Markets, said concerns were increasing about high valuations and the financing of the ​AI boom, with questions raised whether the massive investments will pay off.
Research firm Gartner ‌Inc expects that by 2030, 80% of neocloud providers will cease independent operations because they will fail to generate enough revenue to meet their debts building and managing data centres.
“There is a feeling of insecurity and uncertainty in the market that even good numbers may not be good enough,” said ZKB analyst Florian Sager.
“People ⁠are worrying about the huge debts that the neoclouds are taking on to build their projects. Investors question whether these companies get the revenues they need in the future to survive,” he said.
ABB however remained bullish ⁠on the future of data centres ‌and CEO Morten Wierod said demand for its services had not slowed.
Orders ⁠surged 40% to $12 billion in the three months ended September 30, with ​data centres ‌the biggest driver. The company raised its full-year sales outlook and also announced ​a pending $495 ⁠million investment in a joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric.
“We see a continued acceleration in the market when we’re looking at the demand for the build-out of data centres,” Wierod told reporters.
“Data centres will be a growth market for many years,” he added, saying the value of ABB data centre orders for the third quarter had been the highest yet.
($1 = 0.8244 Swiss francs)
(Reporting by John Revill, additional reporting by Oliver HirtEditing by Linda Pasquini, ​Jochelle Mendonca and Barbara Lewis)

Archer Tops Joby in TipRanks AI Score Despite Both Rated Neutral on eVTOL Cash Burn
Add preferred source 
TipRanks' AI analyst favors Archer Aviation over Joby Aviation, scoring the two eVTOL developers 56 and 48 respectively while rating both Neutral. Archer's edge stems from roughly $1.6 billion in liquidity, modest leverage and a pending deal to acquire Boeing's Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid units, including the profitable Insitu, which generates more than $200 million in annual revenue. Joby counters with $39 million in quarterly revenue, $2.3 billion in cash and full-year guidance of $115 million to $125 million, but its wider losses and heavier cash burn weigh on its rating. Both stocks carry price targets near current levels.
Key Elements 
Archer Aviation Joby Aviation TipRanks Boeing Wisk Aero Insitu SkyGrid Federal Aviation Administration Midnight Blade Toyota Delta Air Lines Uber 
TipRanks' AI analyst gives Archer Aviation (ACHR) the edge over Joby Aviation (JOBY) in the race to commercialize electric air taxis, though it assigns a Neutral rating to both stocks. The model scores Archer at 56 against Joby's 48, with price targets of $4 and $4.50 respectively, according to TipRanks.
The gap between the two electric vertical take-off and landing developers comes down to balance-sheet strength, cash consumption and the pace at which each is converting certification work into revenue. Neither company has yet demonstrated it can turn technical progress into sustainable profit, which is why the ratings remain neutral.
Archer closed the second quarter with roughly $1.6 billion in liquidity and carries debt that is modest relative to its equity base. That cushion gives the company room to fund certification, aircraft development and operations before its Midnight aircraft reaches commercial scale.
The AI analyst also flags Archer's proposed purchase of three Boeing (BA) businesses - Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid - as a potential positive. Insitu, a military drone manufacturer, is already profitable and generates more than $200 million in annual revenue. If the transaction closes as planned, it would hand Archer a near-term revenue stream outside passenger air taxis.
Operationally, Archer has logged more than 150 piloted test flights, obtained an FAA-approved quality management system and advanced into the final phase of type certification for Midnight.
The weak spot is the financials. Archer booked just $5 million of revenue in the second quarter while posting an adjusted EBITDA loss of $177 million. Trailing free cash flow stood at about negative $659 million. The Boeing deal also carries dilution and integration risk, and it has not yet closed.
Joby, for its part, generated $39 million of second-quarter revenue, largely through Blade, and lifted its full-year revenue guidance to a range of $115 million to $125 million. Blade seat volumes climbed more than 50% year over year in the quarter, giving the company an operating business while it works toward commercial air-taxi service. Joby ended the period with about $2.3 billion in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments.
Manufacturing and certification are progressing. Joby had five electric aircraft in flight, including its first FAA-conforming aircraft, with another 12 in production. The company said manufacturing nonconformance fell about 40% in the first half.
Losses and cash burn remain heavy, however. The second-quarter GAAP net loss widened to $245 million, with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $197 million. Management expects cash use of $385 million to $415 million in the second half, and trailing free cash flow was about negative $744 million. An aircraft-availability constraint is also limiting how much passenger demand the company can convert into revenue.
Metric Archer Aviation (ACHR) Joby Aviation (JOBY)

Note: Figures are for the second quarter of 2026 and are drawn from company disclosures cited in the analysis.
The higher score for Archer reflects its stronger balance-sheet profile and the prospect that the Boeing assets add profitable revenue sooner. Joby has more current revenue and more cash on hand, but heavier losses, a larger debt load and steeper cash burn weigh on its rating.
The two companies are taking different paths toward certification. Archer in 2026 became the first eVTOL developer to complete Phase 3 of the FAA's four-phase type certification process, and in September it flew Midnight between Salinas and Hollister, California, a trip of about 12 minutes against roughly 40 minutes by car. Joby is working through a separate five-stage process and appears further along overall, though the two tracks are not directly comparable.
Both stocks have been punished by investors this year. Archer opened 2026 at about $8 a share and has since fallen to roughly $4, a decline of about 50%. The selloff has coincided with genuine corporate progress, including the certification milestones and the pending Boeing transaction.
Even with the acquisitions, risks remain substantial. Boeing would receive a significant ownership stake in Archer if the deal closes, diluting existing holders. And $200 million of annual revenue from Insitu would not come close to covering Archer's expenses, which totaled about $284 million in the latest quarter alone.
The broader opportunity remains speculative. Morgan Stanley once estimated the urban air mobility market could be worth $9 trillion by 2050, a projection that depends on certification, infrastructure and consumer acceptance arriving on schedule. Fortune Business Insights projects the eVTOL market growing at a 36.8% compound annual rate from 2026 to 2034.
For Joby, the central vulnerability is financing. The company has burned roughly $100 million to $200 million of cash per quarter over the past year, and its liquidity has risen only because it raised money through two stock offerings and a convertible debt issue. That approach lifted the share count 13% over 12 months, while total liabilities climbed 156% year over year to $985 million at the end of the second quarter. A recession that tightened credit conditions and forced partners such as Toyota, Delta Air Lines and Uber to trim spending would hit a stock already trading at about ten times its 2028 sales forecast.
Joby's S4 aircraft carries one pilot and four passengers, travels up to 150 miles on a charge and reaches a top speed of 200 miles per hour. It uses single tilt-rotor propellers for both lift and cruise rather than separate, heavier rotors, which lets it fly faster and stay aloft longer than many competing designs. Analysts expect Joby's revenue to climb from $53 million in 2025 to $432 million in 2028 if it completes certification and becomes a vertically integrated operator that builds, owns and flies its own fleet.
The investment case for both companies therefore rests on execution against a fixed cash runway. Archer's lower leverage and the potential for Insitu to contribute profit early give it the more balanced risk-reward setup in the near term, while Joby offers more visible commercial traction but faces greater financial strain. Investors weighing the pair are effectively choosing between a stronger balance sheet and a faster-moving operating business - a trade-off that the Neutral ratings suggest has yet to resolve in either company's favor.

Solvay's Financial Performance and Outlook

Revised Financial Guidance
The chemicals group now sees full-year EBITDA of €720 million to €740 million, slightly below the company-compiled consensus of €775 million, and free cash flow of between €120 million and €150 million.

Impact of Middle East Conflict
• It said the Middle East conflict reduced quarterly underlying EBITDA by about €25 million, including nearly €15 million linked to the shutdown of the peroxide plant at the Sadara complex in Saudi Arabia
Mitigation Strategies
• Solvay said it was pursuing options to limit the shutdown's financial impact, citing joint-venture contractual provisions that could allow it to recover lost profit

ABL Texcell Diagnostics Strengthens the Foundations of a Stable Shareholder Base and Pursues Its Growth Strategy
Business Wire 
October 19, 2026 5 min read

-2.46% 
Its principal shareholder, ABL Luxembourg, intends to prioritize long-term investors in connection with any potential future disposals of significant blocks of shares 
WOIPPY, France, October 19, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Regulatory News: 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics (Euronext Paris: ABLD – ISIN: FR001400AHX6), a company specializing in molecular diagnostic solutions, healthcare software and services supporting clinical research, informs the market of the principles communicated by its principal shareholder, Advanced Biological Laboratories S.A., a Luxembourg-based diagnostics company ("ABL Luxembourg"), regarding the future management of its shareholding. 
Following a recommendation by the Board of Directors of ABL Texcell Diagnostics, ABL Luxembourg has indicated that, should it consider any future disposal of significant blocks of shares in the Company, it intends to prioritize investors with a long-term investment horizon who would agree, where the terms of the proposed transaction allow, to a minimum twelve-month holding commitment, or lock-up. 
This approach is intended to foster a stable and long-term shareholder base, consistent with the Company's development strategy. It reflects ABL Luxembourg's current intention and does not constitute a commitment to sell shares or the announcement of any specific transaction. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics notes that previous block disposals were carried out by ABL Luxembourg in its capacity as a shareholder and not by the Company. As these transactions involved existing shares, they did not result in the issuance of any new shares, any dilution for existing shareholders or any proceeds being received by ABL Texcell Diagnostics. 
Furthermore, according to information provided by ABL Luxembourg, a final tranche of 10,000 ABL Texcell Diagnostics shares remains on loan to Alumni Capital. The return of these shares is expected by the end of October 2026. Subject to its effective completion, this return will mark the termination of the relevant share loan arrangement. No additional shares may be lent to Alumni Capital under this agreement. 
These principles reflect both the recommendations of the Board of Directors of ABL Texcell Diagnostics and the position expressed by ABL Luxembourg, in accordance with the respective powers and responsibilities of the governing bodies of each company. In this context, Dr Chalom Sayada acts in his respective capacities as Chief Executive Officer of ABL Texcell Diagnostics and as co-founder and principal shareholder of ABL Luxembourg. 
Story Continues 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics remains fully focused on the execution of its growth strategy. This strategy is based on the development of its molecular diagnostics and sequencing activities, the expansion of its services supporting biopharmaceutical development, the strengthening of its international presence, the implementation of synergies arising from recently completed strategic transactions and the selective assessment of external growth opportunities. 
Dr Chalom Sayada, Chief Executive Officer of ABL Texcell Diagnostics, stated: "The forthcoming completion of the share loan arrangement and the position expressed by ABL Luxembourg in favor of long-term investors contribute to creating a more stable shareholder environment for ABL Texcell Diagnostics. The Company can therefore remain fully focused on its operational priorities: developing its activities, accelerating its international expansion, leveraging the complementary nature of its expertise and pursuing sustainable growth for the benefit of all its shareholders". 
Forward-Looking Statements 
This press release contains forward-looking statements based on the information, assessments and assumptions available as of its date. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that may result in actual results or events differing from those expressed or implied herein. 
The intentions expressed by ABL Luxembourg do not constitute an irrevocable commitment or the announcement of any specific transaction. ABL Texcell Diagnostics undertakes no obligation to update these forward-looking statements, except as required by applicable laws or regulations. 
Main translation choices: "disposals of significant blocks of shares" clearly attributes any future transactions to ABL Luxembourg; "existing shares" and "no dilution" preserve the key investor message; and "current intention" avoids presenting the shareholder's position as an irrevocable undertaking. 
About ABL Texcell Diagnostics (ABLD) 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics (ABLD) is an international company that specializes in innovative molecular biology tests and global solutions for its customers: 
Molecular polymerase chain reaction (PCR) detection – UltraGene, and 
Genotyping by DNA sequencing – DeepChek®. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics markets its entire product range globally through its own sales team and a network of exclusive distributors active on all continents. ABL Diagnostics' customers are academic clinical pathology laboratories, private reference laboratories and researchers willing to implement innovative and robust microbiological content in constant expansion. 
Following the acquisition of TEXCELL's operations, ABL Texcell Diagnostics is expanding its activities in the life sciences sector by integrating expertise and services dedicated to virology, biosafety testing and biopharmaceutical development support. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics has been marketing the products and services of its sister company CDL Pharma since the second half of 2025 through an intra-group strategy agreement. 
An expanding portfolio of microbiology products: 
HIV – Drug resistance testing, including a whole genome kit. 
SARS-CoV-2, Tuberculosis, Hepatitis B and C – Advanced Detection Solutions. 
Microbiome and taxonomy – 16s/18s RNA-based analyses. 
Other viral and bacterial targets – Comprehensive molecular assays. 
Integrated Solutions 
Real-time syndromic PCR tests 
Nadis® – Patient Medical Record used in more than 200 hospitals in France for the management of HIV and hepatitis. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics, headquartered in Woippy, is a public limited company listed on compartment B of the regulated market of Euronext in Paris (Euronext: ABLD – ISIN: FR001400AHX6). These molecular biology products generate recurring revenues and cover one of the largest portfolios of applications in microbiology.

Merck KGaA buys Silence in $1.3B deal after siRNA drug's phase 2 blood cancer win
By
James Waldron 
Oct 19, 2026 8:57am 
Merck KGaA 
Silence Therapeutics 
mergers and acquisitions 
siRNA 
Merck KGaA CEO Kai Beckmann put today’s deal in the context of the pharma's "strategic priority to address attractive end markets through M&A." (Merck KGaA)
Germany’s Merck KGaA has picked up Silence Therapeutics to the tune of $1.3 billion in the wake of the British biotech’s mid-stage success for its challenger to Takeda’s Mimrylo.
The all-cash deal will see Darmstadt-based Merck pay $20 per American depositary share, with each ADS representing three ordinary shares of Silence.
The biggest prize for Merck is divesiran, a short interfering RNA (siRNA) drug candidate designed to treat a rare blood cancer called polycythemia vera (PV). The cancer is characterized by the excessive production of red blood cells and the idea is that divesiran silences the production of a protein, TMPRSS6, found in liver cells, in order to redirect iron delivery away from bone marrow and slow production of red blood cells.
This theory appeared to pan out in August, when Silence revealed that 88% of patients on divesiran in a phase 2 study had met the response criteria between Weeks 18 and 36. The response rate was 93.8% in people who received divesiran every six weeks and 81.3% in the 12-week dose cohort. 
The data, which Silence is using as a springboard into phase 3, puts the biotech as a strong follower to Takeda and Protagonist’s Mimrylo, which was approved by the FDA for PV in August.
Related
Silence brings the noise to Takeda with phase 2 blood cancer win 
Silence’s hopes for overcoming Mimrylo’s head start hinge on its dosing regimen. Mimrylo, which mimics a hormone that regulates iron homeostasis, was given as a weekly, self-administered injection in phase 3, while Silence plans to administer divesiran every 12 weeks in its own phase 3 trial. 
Silence’s pipeline also includes zerlasiran, a siRNA therapy designed to treat atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease by silencing the LPA gene. Future development plans for the drug were in limbo last year after China’s Hansoh Pharma pulled out of an mRNAi-focused collaboration with Silence.
The only other asset from Silence to make it into the clinic is SLN312, a siRNA therapy designed to silence ANGPTL3 as a way to treat dyslipidemia. AstraZeneca handed back its rights to partner on the drug earlier this year.
Iain Ross, interim principal executive officer and chairperson of Silence’s board, said the deal with Merck was “the result of a competitive sale process and delivers significant, immediate and certain value to our shareholders.”
“This transaction follows potentially best-in-class phase 2 polycythemia vera data for divesiran and reflects the important progress we have made advancing our differentiated siRNA pipeline,” Ross added. “It also provides a new home for our innovative programs within Merck KGaA ... placing divesiran with a company that has the scale, resources and commercial capabilities to accelerate its phase 3 development and bring this potentially best-in-class siRNA therapy to patients in need.”
The Silence acquisition validates the commitment of Merck’s new CEO Kai Beckmann to “broaden our M&A scope.” Beckmann took over in May after Belén Garijo moved to Sanofi, and the following month saw the German pharma front over $11 billion to buy Bio-Techne .
Beckmann put today’s deal in the context of Merck’s “strategic priority to address attractive end markets through M&A, creating value over the mid- to long-term.”
“The planned acquisition of Silence Therapeutics will strengthen our capabilities to serve patients with targeted specialty and rare diseases,” the CEO added in the release. “Following the acquisition of SpringWorks Therapeutics last year, we continue to transform our pipeline toward areas of high specialization and unmet medical need, with an ongoing commitment to external innovation.”

Applied Materials Cratered 20% Since July: Multiple Wall Street Firms Predict It’s Going to More Than Double From Here
By Alex Sirois 
Published October 19, 2026, 7:15am ET · 3 min read 
𝕏 
f
