This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
The upward trend depicted over a backdrop of semiconductor chips illustrates the significant growth potential within the AI sector, aligning with projections for Marvell Technology. © TechAnimationStock / Shutterstock.com 
Applied Materials ( NASDAQ:AMAT | AMAT Price Prediction ) is now priced at $409.29. The average analyst price target stands at $627.83, meaning 53.4% upside.
Applied makes the deposition, etch and inspection tools used to build virtually every new chip. AI infrastructure demand drove fiscal third-quarter revenue to $9.12 billion, up 24.8% year over year. Management guided the current quarter to about $10.25 billion.
The most bullish firms, including H.C. Wainwright and Susquehanna, have $900 targets. Those sit about 119.9% above the current price. Consensus upside stands above 40%.
Investor Day Silence Turned a Pullback Into a 37% Rout
The biggest hit came at Applied’s investor day, when the company declined to provide an industry spending forecast. Shares fell as much as 9% intraday, and the stock lost 19.28% over the past week. Since the start of July, Applied has dropped 37.05%. That leaves it 44.6% below its 52-week high of $738.88.
The first signs showed after the August earnings report. Shares fell about 4% even though guidance beat consensus. Morgan Stanley summed it up: “AMAT’s earnings were good, but not great.” Peers fell about 4% on investor day, so sector weakness made a company-specific hit worse.
33 of 40 Analysts Rate It a Buy as Estimates Climb
Of the 40 analysts who cover Applied, 4 rate it Strong Buy, 29 rate it Buy and 7 rate it Hold. None rate it Sell. Estimates rose while the stock fell. The fiscal 2027 EPS consensus is $18.4672, up from $16.7456 90 days ago. Over the past 30 days, analysts made three upward revisions and no cuts. The stock trades at about 22 times that figure.
Management guided fourth-quarter EPS to about $4.02. DRAM revenue, including HBM packaging, grew 52% year over year. Packaging revenue should grow more than 70% in calendar 2026. Leading-edge logic, DRAM and advanced packaging should account for about 80% of equipment growth.
The $900 camp argues that Applied is well placed in tools for Gate-All-Around transistors, backside power and HBM packaging. CEO Gary Dickerson set the timeline on the earnings call: “Based on the unprecedented visibility we’re receiving from our customers, we expect another strong record year in 2027.”
Lam, KLA and Teradyne Sold Off Too, but Applied Fell Hardest
The whole group fell over the past week, but Applied fell the most.
Lam Research ( NASDAQ:LRCX ) lost 14.74% to $263.94. Its average target is $375.81, meaning 42.4% upside. Twenty-nine of 35 analysts rate it Buy or Strong Buy.
KLA ( NASDAQ:KLAC ) dropped 12.82% to $165.74. Its target of $232.77 meaning 40.4% upside. Analysts are more cautious here, with 10 of 29 at Hold.
Teradyne ( NASDAQ:TER ) slid 15.33% to $325. Its target of $446.47 meaning 37.4% upside, and 12 of 17 analysts are bullish.
Applied has the largest consensus upside in the group. All of these targets are estimates, and they could fall if spending expectations drop.
A 59.83% Gain This Year Survives the Drawdown
Applied trades at $409.29. The average target from 40 analysts is $627.83, meaning 53.4% upside. Targets often lag sharp price moves, so treat that number as one input among several.
Even after the drop, the stock is up 59.83% year to date. The S&P 500 is up 11.93%. Over one year, Applied shares are up 80.75%.
Applied Materials Looks Like an Overcorrection Worth Researching
Applied Materials’ upside case strengthens if DRAM and leading-edge logic deliver the second-half surge management promised and fiscal 2027 earnings land near the $18.4672 consensus. At a forward P/E of about 23, that growth looks undervalued.
The upside story weakens if the investor day silence means equipment spending is peaking. Management claims multi-year visibility yet held back an industry forecast. China fell to 28% of revenue from 35%, and the Other segment’s loss widened to $118 million. A slowdown in AI capex would pull targets down toward the share price.
The data leans positive. Estimates are rising while the share price falls. Applied’s upside is also the largest of any peer. The next earnings report and its 2027 outlook will test that view. Qualcomm showcases V2X-based traffic safety technologies and solutions at the 2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress. (Photo: Qualcomm) 
Qualcomm announced on Oct. 19 that it will showcase traffic safety technologies and solutions based on vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communications at the 2026 ITS World Congress in Gangneung, South Korea.
The ITS World Congress is an event focused on intelligent transportation system policies, technologies and services. It addresses future mobility issues, including connected vehicles, autonomous driving, smart infrastructure and artificial intelligence (AI). This year’s event runs from Oct. 19 to 23 at Gangneung Olympic Park in Gangwon Province.
Qualcomm will demonstrate seven technologies during the event and exhibit real-world applications. These include scalable V2X, advanced driver assistance system (ADAS)-based V2X, smart infrastructure, global V2X solutions and products developed by partners using Qualcomm technologies.
V2X enables vehicles to exchange wireless data directly with other vehicles, road infrastructure, pedestrians, motorcycles and other surrounding objects. Using radio signals, the technology can identify potential hazards and warn drivers even in blind spots or adverse weather conditions where visibility is limited. Conventional camera and radar sensors have been limited to detecting obstacles directly ahead or objects within their line of sight.
Scalable V2X allows communication capabilities and data processing levels to be adjusted flexibly according to driving conditions and vehicle performance.
ADAS-based V2X combines onboard sensor systems with V2X communications. Rather than simply warning drivers of potential hazards, the technology enables vehicles to initiate automatic emergency braking (AEB) or steering control.
Qualcomm Korea President Kim Sang-pyo delivers a keynote speech titled “Accelerating Innovation in Traffic Safety.” (Photo: Qualcomm) 
Smart infrastructure refers to intelligent road environments equipped with communication modules and detection sensors installed in traffic lights, electronic road signs, streetlights and base stations.
Global V2X refers to V2X solutions based on worldwide standards.
Kim Sang-pyo, president of Qualcomm Korea, delivered a keynote speech titled “Accelerating Innovation in Traffic Safety.”
“Qualcomm has led mobile communications technology for more than 40 years and has worked with numerous partners to advance the V2X ecosystem, from standardization to commercialization,” Kim said. “We are supporting the development of safe and intelligent transportation systems that reflect real-world road conditions in South Korea.”

Add preferred source 2 
Qualcomm showcased V2X technology and related products that connect vehicles, road infrastructure, and pedestrians in real time at the 2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress, which opened on the 19th. The display featured extended-range V2X, V2X integrated with ADAS, smart road infrastructure, and partner products, along with use cases showing how combining vehicle sensors with communications can deliver early warnings of risks in blind spots. In his keynote address, Qualcomm Korea President Kim Sang-pyo said the company has led the ecosystem from V2X standardization through to real-world road deployment, drawing on more than 40 years of mobile connectivity expertise, and emphasized that it is supporting interoperability validation reflecting actual road conditions in South Korea.
Key Elements 
Qualcomm Qualcomm Korea Kim Sang-pyo V2X 2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) South Korea's Ministry of Land Infrastructure and Transport Gangneung City Korea Intelligent Transport Systems Association 
Qualcomm put V2X (vehicle-to-everything) technology front and center at the "2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress," which opened on the 19th, showcasing technology that connects vehicles, road infrastructure, and pedestrians in real time. At the event, running in Gangneung through the 23rd, the company is presenting V2X-based traffic safety solutions and related product lines.
V2X is a technology through which vehicles communicate directly with other vehicles as well as with road infrastructure such as traffic lights and with pedestrians to grasp surrounding traffic conditions. Unlike cameras or radar, it can relay hazard information from beyond the line of sight, making it useful for providing advance warnings of accidents that could occur in intersection blind spots or outside sensor detection ranges.
At this exhibition, Qualcomm is introducing extended-range V2X, V2X integrated with advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), smart road infrastructure, and global V2X solutions. It has also placed partner products built on its technology on display. In particular, the company presented use cases that combine vehicle sensors with communications technology to identify the movements of nearby vehicles and pedestrians and issue early warnings of hazardous situations. Qualcomm said the technology can compensate for the limitations of existing vehicle sensors and simultaneously raise road safety and traffic operation efficiency.
Delivering a keynote address on the first day of the event under the theme "Accelerating Traffic Safety Innovation," Qualcomm Korea President Kim Sang-pyo said, "Building on more than 40 years of experience leading innovation in mobile connectivity, Qualcomm has driven the development of the global ecosystem with a wide range of partners—from standardization of V2X technology to commercialization and real-world road deployment." He added, "In South Korea as well, we are supporting the construction of safer and more intelligent transportation systems based on interoperability validation that reflects actual road conditions," and said, "We will continue to enhance road safety and expand new possibilities for future mobility through forward-looking connectivity solutions."
The congress is hosted and organized by South Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Gangneung City, and the Korea Intelligent Transport Systems Association. Under the theme "A World United Beyond Mobility," it features high-level talks, academic sessions, an exhibition, cutting-edge technology demonstrations, and hands-on experience programs, with government, industry, and academic officials from various countries discussing the direction of intelligent transport systems (ITS) policy, technology, and services.
V2X is a core infrastructure technology underpinning the safety of autonomous driving and connected cars, and cooperation between automakers and communications chipset companies has been rising rapidly in this field recently. Qualcomm has extended connectivity technology honed in mobile communications semiconductors to automotive applications, and this exhibition is seen as targeting the shift in focus from standardization to real-world road deployment. In particular, with interoperability validation in actual road environments emerging as the key to commercialization, Qualcomm's move to highlight South Korea as one of its validation hubs stands out. If the V2X ecosystem expands, it is expected to affect demand for communications modules and automotive semiconductors as well.

HYPROMAG USA DEPLOYS MOBILE INSERMA SYSTEM, EXTENDING HDD PROCESSING TO CUSTOMER SITES ACROSS THE UNITED STATES 
Feedstock platform continues to build ahead of Dallas-Fort Worth commissioning, with commercial PCB sales to smelter partners generating revenue that supports magnet acquisition 
LONDON / VANCOUVER: 19 October 2026 – Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) (“Mkango”) is pleased to announce that HyProMag USA LLC (“HyProMag USA”) has announced the deployment of its third Inserma Anoia S.L. (“Inserma”) hard disk drive (“HDD”) separation system as a mobile processing unit, expanding HyProMag USA's processing and customer engagement capabilities across the United States. The deployment further strengthens HyProMag USA's partnership [1] with Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions (“ ILS”) and supports the expansion of a scalable nationwide platform for the recovery and recycling of rare earth magnets from end-of-life HDDs. 
Feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs, continue to strengthen the feedstock platform and are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up activities for Phase 1 at the planned Dallas-Fort Worth facility (the “Texas Hub”) in 2028. HyProMag USA has also completed commercial sales of recovered printed circuit board (“PCB”) material to downstream smelter partners, generating revenue that supports the acquisition and retention of magnet-bearing feedstock inventory. 
Julian Treger, Chief Executive Officer of CoTec Holdings Corp. (“CoTec”), commented : “The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project. Together with continued progress in feedstock sourcing and commercial PCB recovery, it strengthens our operating platform and expands our ability to engage directly with customers across multiple end markets. These milestones provide increasing confidence in our ability to support commissioning activities and establish a long-term domestic supply of recycled rare earth materials.” 
Graham Davy, Managing Director of ILS, commented: “The focus of the ILS team has been on demonstrating that HDDs can be efficiently processed into separate, marketable material streams. We have continued to build feedstock inventories, completed commercial sales of recovered PCB materials to smelter partners for HyProMag USA and expanded our capabilities through the deployment of a mobile Inserma system. The mobile unit allows us to work directly with customers at their facilities, supporting trial programs, demonstrating material recovery performance and creating opportunities to secure additional feedstock supply.” 
Key Highlights 
● Processing capability expanded: HyProMag USA's third Inserma HDD separation system has been deployed as a mobile processing unit to support customer qualification programs, secure on-site recovery campaigns and future feedstock growth opportunities across the United States. 
● Commissioning readiness advanced: Feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs, are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up of Phase 1 activities at the Texas Hub in 2028. 
● PCB revenue supports magnet acquisition: Commercial sales of recovered PCB material to smelter partners have generated revenue within the HDD processing flow sheet, partly offsetting the cost of acquiring and retaining magnet-bearing feedstock for future rare earth recycling operations. 
● Feedstock channels diversified: Sourcing activities continue to expand across industrial, healthcare, government and IT asset disposition sectors. 
● Secure processing platform: R2v3-certified operations, ISO-certified management systems and documented chain-of-custody procedures support secure handling of data-bearing equipment. 
● Data center market focus: Mobile processing capability enables on-site recovery programs within hyperscale data centers and secure IT asset disposition environments. 
● Inserma testing: A next generation Inserma system designed specifically for the high-capacity HDDs used in hyperscale data centers, including helium filled units, is currently being tested, with early results indicating processing times of under three seconds per drive and successful processing of modern high-capacity data center formats. 
● Partnership network expanding: Relationships across the data center, electronics recycling and rare earth magnet value chain continue to support platform growth. 
Expanding Feedstock Access 
To support continued growth in feedstock volumes, HyProMag USA has deployed its third Inserma HDD separation system as a mobile processing unit to complement existing operations in South Carolina and Nevada. Unlike the fixed installations currently operating through the ILS partnership, the system has been configured for mobile deployment and is intended to support customer trials, feedstock development programs and on-site processing campaigns across the United States. 
Feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs, continue to strengthen the feedstock platform and are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up activities at the Texas Hub. Feedstock sourcing activities continue to expand beyond HDDs into industrial, healthcare, government and IT asset disposition sectors, increasing confidence in the scalability of HyProMag USA's feedstock platform and supporting future supply requirements for the Texas Hub. 
Commercial PCB Recovery 
ILS has completed commercial sales for HyProMag USA of recovered PCB material to downstream smelter partners. The sales validate an additional revenue stream within the HDD processing flow sheet and show that value can be recovered from secondary material streams. Magnet-bearing materials are being retained as feedstock inventory for future rare earth recycling operations. Revenue from recovered PCB material partly offsets the cost of acquiring magnet-bearing feedstock, improving the economics of building the inventory required to support Texas Hub operations. 
Secure Recovery and Chain of Custody 
ILS operates under internationally recognized recycling and management standards, including R2v3 certification and ISO-certified management systems, supporting responsible recycling practices, operational controls and continuous improvement initiatives. The recovery process is supported by documented chain-of-custody procedures designed to provide traceability from collection through processing and final disposition. These controls support the requirements of data center operators, IT asset disposition providers, enterprise customers and government organizations seeking secure and auditable management of end-of-life electronic equipment. 
Building Strategic Partnerships 
HyProMag USA continues to expand relationships across the electronics recycling, data infrastructure and rare earth magnet value chain. Working alongside data center operators, IT asset disposition providers, recyclers, technology companies and downstream processing partners, HyProMag USA is developing an integrated platform for the collection, recovery and recycling of magnet-bearing materials. HyProMag USA is evaluating additional feedstock pathways, including industrial and transportation-related material streams, with pilot programs and commercial opportunities under review. 
About ILS 
Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions (“ILS”) provides secure recovery, processing and recycling services for end-of-life electronic equipment. Through its operating facilities in South Carolina and Nevada, ILS supports the recovery of valuable materials from electronic waste streams while maintaining robust data security and chain-of-custody protocols. 
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for neodymium iron boron (“NdFeB”) magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (“HPMS”) technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA delivers faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks – including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap – enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing. 
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec Holdings Corp. (TSXV: CTH; OTCQX: CTHCF) (“CoTec”) and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited which is owned on a 79.4%/20.6% basis by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and CoTec. 
About Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. 
Mkango is listed on the AIM and the TSX-V Stock Exchanges. Mkango’s corporate strategy is to become a market leader in the production of recycled rare earth magnets, alloys and oxides, through its interest in Maginito Limited (“Maginito”), which is owned 79.4 per cent by Mkango and 20.6 per cent by CoTec Holdings Corp. (“CoTec”), and the Remloy business acquired by its wholly owned German subsidiary, to develop new sustainable sources of neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium to supply accelerating demand from electric vehicles, wind turbines and other clean energy technologies. 
Maginito holds a 100 per cent interest in HyProMag Limited and a 90 per cent direct and indirect interest (assuming conversion of Maginito’s convertible loan) in HyProMag GmbH, focused on short loop rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing in the UK and Germany, respectively, and a 100 per cent interest in Mkango Rare Earths UK Ltd (“Mkango UK”), focused on long loop rare earth magnet recycling in the UK via a chemical processing route. 
Maginito and CoTec are also expanding Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (“HPMS”) recycling technology into the United States via the 50/50 owned HyProMag USA joint venture company. 
Remloy has developed a plant in Bitterfeld, Germany, which recycles end-of-life rare earth magnets via a melting process (medium loop rare earth magnet recycling) to produce NdFeB alloy powders for the bonded and hot deformed magnet markets, complementary to HyProMag’s short loop recycling process, to produce sintered magnets, and to Mkango UK’s long loop recycling process, to produce mixed rare earth carbonates and oxides. 
Mkango currently owns 100% of the advanced stage Songwe Hill rare earths project in Malawi and the proposed Pulawy rare earths separation plant in Poland. On grant of the large-scale mining licence the Government of Malawi may elect to take a free 10% interest in the entity holding that licence. The Songwe and Pulawy projects and HyProMag GmbH have been selected as Strategic Projects under the European Union Critical Raw Materials Act. Songwe has also received Development Funding from the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (“DFC”), the U.S. Government’s development finance institution, securing US$4.6 million in reimbursable funding for Front End Engineering and Design. Mkango Rare Earths Limited (“MKAR”) has signed a Business Combination Agreement with Crown PropTech Acquisitions (“CPTK”) to list the Songwe Hill and Pulawy rare earths projects on NASDAQ via a SPAC merger (the “Proposed Business Combination”) under the name Mkango Rare Earths Limited.

AURA AERO Opens Electric and Hybrid-Electric Aircraft Flight Test Facility in October 2026
Picture credits: AURA AERO
Click to view 
October 20, 2026
France – French aircraft manufacturer AURA AERO has officially inaugurated its new flight testing and electric propulsion development facility at Rochefort–Charente-Maritime Airport on 9 October 2026. The site will support the development and validation of electric and hybrid-electric aircraft technologies, including propulsion systems for its planned ERA regional aircraft, while expanding the manufacturer's civil and military aerospace development capabilities. 
The Rochefort facility occupies infrastructure previously developed for VoltAero, comprising approximately 2,412 square metres of building space on a 7,400-square-metre site with direct runway access. AURA AERO's establishment at the airport follows its acquisition of VoltAero's assets earlier in 2026. 
The facility will support aircraft prototyping, engineering and flight testing, with the manufacturer's X-VOLT hybrid-electric demonstrator serving as a flying testbed for the validation of propulsion technologies before their integration into future aircraft. 
AURA AERO returned X-VOLT, formerly VoltAero's Cassio S demonstrator, to flight at Rochefort in September 2026. The manufacturer reported that X-VOLT and its fully electric INTEGRAL E prototype had accumulated more than 350 hybrid-electric and electric flights between them. 
The 9 October inauguration included flight demonstrations by X-VOLT and an INTEGRAL aircraft. The manufacturer intends to use the site for continued technology development and testing, including applications supporting civil and military aviation. 
For the pilot training market, AURA AERO is developing the two-seat INTEGRAL E electric aircraft for ab initio instruction, Upset Prevention and Recovery Training (UPRT) and other training applications. The aircraft remains in the certification process, with the manufacturer's current product roadmap indicating availability from December 2027. 
AFM previously reported that AURA AERO opened its US headquarters and North American aircraft delivery and customer support facility at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University's Research Park in Daytona Beach, Florida, in November 2025. The 11,000-square-foot facility supports the company's INTEGRAL aircraft family and its wider international manufacturing plans. 
X-VOLT is equipped with Safran ENGINeUS electric motors, allowing AURA AERO to evaluate propulsion components under actual flight conditions. The technologies will contribute to the development of ERA, a proposed 19-seat hybrid-electric regional aircraft designed around eight electric motors and two turbogenerators, with its first flight currently targeted for late 2027. 
About AURA AERO 
AURA AERO is a French aircraft manufacturer founded in 2018 and headquartered at Toulouse-Francazal Airport, specialising in general aviation training aircraft, electric propulsion and hybrid-electric regional aircraft development. Its aircraft portfolio includes the EASA-certified INTEGRAL R two-seat training and aerobatic aircraft, the INTEGRAL S, the developing all-electric INTEGRAL E and the ERA regional aircraft, alongside military and unmanned aviation programs. 
Source: AURA AERO

The company said it will showcase V2X-based transport safety technologies and solutions at the 2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress in Gangneung Olympic Park. Kim Sang-pyo (김상표), president of Qualcomm Korea, delivers a keynote speech titled "Accelerating Transportation Safety" at the "2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress." [Photo: Qualcomm] 
Qualcomm Technologies is moving to target the transport safety market with communications technology linking vehicles and road infrastructure. Qualcomm said on Oct. 19 it is taking part in the "2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress" at Gangneung Olympic Park and will showcase V2X-based transport safety technologies and solutions, referring to vehicle-to-everything communications.
The ITS World Congress is the world’s largest event where government, industry and academia officials and technology experts gather to discuss intelligent transport system policies, technologies and services. This year’s theme is "One World Beyond Mobility." The agenda includes vehicle connectivity, autonomous driving, smart infrastructure, traffic management, mobility services, AI and data-based systems, and policies and standards.
Qualcomm will run seven demos during the event. Exhibits include expanded V2X, advanced driver assistance systems, or ADAS-based V2X, smart infrastructure and global V2X. Partner products incorporating Qualcomm solutions and products will also be shown. In each demo, the company said it will present use cases in which V2X complements vehicle sensors and connects vehicles, road infrastructure and road users in real time to improve safety and efficiency.
V2X is a technology that enables vehicles, road infrastructure, motorcycles and vulnerable road users such as pedestrians to communicate directly in real time. Cameras and radar can struggle to identify danger when visibility is blocked, but V2X allows vehicles and their surroundings to exchange information even in non-line-of-sight conditions. That is why it can warn in advance of hazards in blind spots and outside sensor detection range. V2X has moved beyond proof-of-concept, and real-world deployments are increasing in many parts of the world. Several countries have built road infrastructure applying V2X, and vehicles equipped with V2X functions have been released and are being used on actual roads.
Kim Sang-pyo (김상표), president of Qualcomm Korea, will deliver a keynote speech titled "Accelerating Transportation Safety." Kim said, "Based on experience leading mobile connectivity innovation for more than 40 years, Qualcomm has led the development of the global ecosystem with various partners from standardisation of V2X technology to commercialisation and real-road deployment." He added, "In Korea as well, we are supporting the building of safer and more intelligent transport systems based on interoperability verification that reflects real road environments," and, "We will continue to enhance road safety and expand new possibilities for future mobility through forward-looking connectivity solutions."

Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany to Acquire Silence Therapeutics, Strengthening Rare Disease Pipeline with Innovative siRNA Asset 
We enter into a definitive agreement to acquire biotechnology company Silence Therapeutics, focused on siRNA-therapies in areas of high unmet need.

Icons revealed to the left 
19 Oct 2026 
| 
Darmstadt, Germany 
Purchase price of $20 per ADS in cash represents an enterprise value of $1.1 billion and an equity value of approximately $1.3 billion 
Silence Therapeutics is a UK-headquartered biotechnology company with a potentially best-in-class Phase 3-ready investigational siRNA therapy for rare disease, polycythemia vera (PV) 
Planned acquisition will strengthen the position of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany in rare diseases, a high-value growth driver, and advance its Healthcare ambition to become a leading Global Specialty Innovator 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, today announced its entry into a definitive agreement to acquire Silence Therapeutics plc (Nasdaq: SLN), a global clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in London, UK, focused on pioneering the design and development of siRNA (short interfering RNA) therapies in areas of high unmet need.
The purchase price of $20 per ADS in cash, with each ADS representing three ordinary shares of Silence Therapeutics (or $6.6667 per ordinary share), represents an enterprise value of $1.1 billion and an equity value of approximately $1.3 billion. The consideration represents an 82% premium to Silence Therapeutics’ 30-day volume-weighted average price of $10.99, as of the close of trading on October 16, 2026, the last trading day prior to the transaction announcement. The transaction is subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions.
“The planned acquisition of Silence Therapeutics will strengthen our capabilities to serve patients with targeted specialty and rare diseases,” said Kai Beckmann, Chairman of the Executive Board and Group CEO of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Following the acquisition of SpringWorks Therapeutics last year, we continue to transform our pipeline toward areas of high specialization and unmet medical need, with an ongoing commitment to external innovation. The proposed transaction follows our strategic priority to address attractive end markets also through M&A, creating value over the mid- to long-term.”
The transaction, once completed, will add Divesiran ─ a potentially best-in-class, phase 3-ready siRNA investigational therapy, in development for phlebotomy-dependent polycythemia vera (PV) ─ to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s pipeline. Divesiran is dosed subcutaneously once every 3 months.
PV is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm ─ a type of rare blood cancer ─ characterized by the excessive production of red blood cells, which can be associated with a higher rate of death from cardiovascular and thrombotic events.
Divesiran is designed to selectively silence TMPRSS6, a gene involved in regulating hepcidin, the body’s key regulator of iron metabolism. By increasing hepcidin levels, Divesiran aims to limit iron availability for red blood cell production, helping to control hematocrit levels and potentially reducing the need for frequent therapeutic phlebotomies.
Divesiran met its primary endpoint in the Phase 2 SANRECO study with an 88% responder rate versus 19% for placebo (p “The planned acquisition of Silence Therapeutics marks a significant step forward in our strategy to become a Global Specialty Innovator in Healthcare,” said Danny Bar-Zohar, member of the Executive Board and CEO Healthcare at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Silence Therapeutics’ primary siRNA pipeline asset, Divesiran, is supported by promising Phase 2 efficacy data, a potentially best-in-class, once-every-three-month dosing schedule, and a safety profile that appears manageable, with the added advantage of targeting a well-defined, homogeneous patient population. The planned acquisition also provides an entry point into hematology through a biologically validated mechanism of action. With this transaction, we are advancing our efforts to build a differentiated, sustainable pipeline as we bring more medicines to more patients, faster.”
“We are pleased to have reached this agreement with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, which follows a competitive sale process and delivers significant, immediate and certain value to our shareholders,” said Iain Ross, Interim Principal Executive Officer and Chairman of the Silence Therapeutics’ Board. “This transaction follows potentially best-in-class Phase 2 polycythemia vera data for Divesiran and reflects the important progress we have made advancing our differentiated siRNA pipeline. It also provides a new home for our innovative programs within Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, placing Divesiran with a company that has the scale, resources and commercial capabilities to accelerate its Phase 3 development and bring this potentially best-in-class siRNA therapy to patients in need. We are incredibly grateful to our employees for their dedication and contributions in building Silence Therapeutics into the company it is today.”
The transaction has been unanimously approved by Silence Therapeutics’ Board of Directors and Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s relevant corporate bodies and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including receipt of required regulatory approvals and approval by Silence Therapeutics’ shareholders. In connection with the transaction, certain securityholders of Silence Therapeutics holding securities representing approximately 14% of Silence Therapeutics’ voting power have entered into a voting and support agreement with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, under which the securityholders have agreed among other things, to vote their voting securities of Silence Therapeutics in favor of the transaction. Silence Therapeutics is a UK company, with ADSs, each representing three of its ordinary shares, listed on NASDAQ. As is customary for similar transactions, the transaction will be effected through a UK scheme of arrangement.
The planned acquisition will be funded through proceeds from new debt.
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany is committed to leveraging advanced technologies and data science to accelerate the discovery and delivery of breakthrough medicines. This acquisition is another step forward in its broader strategy to enhance research productivity and the output of its pipeline sustainably, focusing on indications that can be derisked through proper preclinical and early clinical testing to ensure that more patients gain access to effective treatments.
Silence Therapeutics employs approximately 80 people and operates from locations in the UK, the US and Germany.
A&O Shearman is acting as legal counsel to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany.

SEMICON West 2026 highlights AI-era chipmaking, workforce development 
SEMICON West 2026 showcased innovations in semiconductor manufacturing, with new technologies from Zeiss, Mitsubishi Chemical Group, Von Ardenne, and Heidenhain. The event also focused on building a skilled workforce for new fab buildouts in the US. 
ETElectronicsWorld 
Published On Oct 17, 2026 at 12:45 PM IST
Read by 653 Professionals
Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook 
Bookmark 
Highlights
Zeiss SMT introduced Zeiss DUNE and NLX for advanced wafer inspection and chip package analysis.
Mitsubishi Chemical Group showcased new materials for equipment, PCBs, and advanced packaging applications.
Von Ardenne expanded its deposition portfolio to panel-level packaging, leading in glass substrate coating.
Workforce development for fab construction and operations was a key focus, including ABM's training programmes.
SEMICON West 2026 , held in San Francisco, highlighted advancements in AI-era chipmaking and workforce development . SEMI CEO Ajit Manocha stated that the semiconductor industry has become a trillion-dollar sector, driven by AI, IoT, and quantum computing. 
Manufacturing Technology Innovations
Zeiss Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology (SMT) announced its entry into wafer inspection systems at SEMICON West. The company showcased two new products, Zeiss DUNE and Zeiss NLX, for wafer topography measurement and internal chip package inspection. 
Zeiss DUNE measures and corrects wafer topography to address wafer bow, a critical challenge in complex fabrication processes. Raghu Nayak, head of US sales for Zeiss SMT , told EE Times that Zeiss DUNE helps flatten wafers and ensures overlay for subsequent fabrication steps. 
Zeiss NLX, designed for 300-mm wafers, makes internal structures in modern chip packages visible without destruction. This allows engineers to inspect connections between stacked dies and detect defects early, Nayak added. 
Mitsubishi Chemical Group (MCG) presented new materials for semiconductor manufacturing equipment, a biopolymer for PCBs in flexible electronics, and formulated silicon for advanced packaging applications. Fallyn Flaherty-Earp, MCG's global market director, spoke to EE Times about these developments. 
Von Ardenne , a vacuum coating equipment supplier, is expanding its semiconductor deposition portfolio to panel-level packaging (PLP). Stephen Strausser, the company's US CEO, told EE Times that Von Ardenne has a one- to two-year lead in coating for panel-level glass substrates. Its HiPIMS solution deposits barrier and seed layers in through-glass via (TGV) holes. 
Heidenhain unveiled its METIS HP, a new full air-bearing planar platform for demanding step-and-scan semiconductor applications. This platform offers ±150 nm accuracy over the full XY stroke after mapping. 
Workforce Development Initiatives
Workforce development for new fab buildouts was a significant theme at SEMICON West. Phoenix City Mayor Kate Gallego discussed fab apprenticeship programmes in her speech. 
ABM, a fab construction specialist, is preparing to provide workforce solutions following its merger with WGNSTAR. Darrell McDaniel, ABM's VP of Technical Training & Asset Relocation, highlighted the company's Technical Training Center in Boise, Idaho, which can accommodate about 500 participants annually for semiconductor manufacturing skills development.

WOIPPY, France, October 16, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Regulatory News: 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics (Euronext Paris: ABLD – ISIN: FR001400AHX6)("Company") informs its shareholders and all stakeholders that it has been notified of the notice of appeal filed by the Public Prosecutor attached to the Évry-Courcouronnes Judicial Court against the judgment rendered by the Évry-Courcouronnes Commercial Court on October 9, 2026, approving the offer submitted by the Cmpany for the acquisition of IntegraGen's assets and business activities. 
This appeal has suspensive effect. Pending the decision of the Paris Court of Appeal, IntegraGen is therefore placed once again under judicial reorganization proceedings. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics takes note of this situation and remains fully committed throughout the ongoing proceedings. 
The Company continues to believe in the industrial, scientific and social merits of its proposed acquisition project and will keep the market informed of any significant developments. 
About ABL Texcell Diagnostics (ABLD) 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics (ABLD) is an international company that specializes in innovative molecular biology tests and global solutions for its customers: 
Molecular polymerase chain reaction (PCR) detection – UltraGene, and 
Genotyping by DNA sequencing – DeepChek®. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics markets its entire product range globally through its own sales team and a network of exclusive distributors active on all continents. ABL Diagnostics' customers are academic clinical pathology laboratories, private reference laboratories and researchers willing to implement innovative and robust microbiological content in constant expansion. 
Following the acquisition of TEXCELL's operations, ABL Texcell Diagnostics is expanding its activities in the life sciences sector by integrating expertise and services dedicated to virology, biosafety testing and biopharmaceutical development support. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics has been marketing the products and services of its sister company CDL Pharma since the second half of 2025 through an intra-group strategy agreement. 
An expanding portfolio of microbiology products: 
HIV – Drug resistance testing, including a whole genome kit. 
SARS-CoV-2, Tuberculosis, Hepatitis B and C – Advanced Detection Solutions. 
Microbiome and taxonomy – 16s/18s RNA-based analyses. 
Other viral and bacterial targets – Comprehensive molecular assays. 
Integrated Solutions 
Real-time syndromic PCR tests 
Nadis® – Patient Medical Record used in more than 200 hospitals in France for the management of HIV and hepatitis.

ABL Texcell Diagnostics, headquartered in Woippy, is a public limited company listed on compartment B of the regulated market of Euronext in Paris (Euronext: ABLD – ISIN: FR001400AHX6). These molecular biology products generate recurring revenues and cover one of the largest portfolios of applications in microbiology.

content_text:
DGR Job Fair in Nagpur Offers Over 1,300 Employment Opportunities for Ex-Servicemen
Posted On:
16 OCT 2026 6:26PM by PIB Mumbai
Nagpur, 16 October 2026 
 
The Directorate General Resettlement (DGR), under the Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare (DESW), Ministry of Defence, organised an Ex-Servicemen (ESM) Job Fair at Nagpur on 16 October 2026, reaffirming its commitment to enabling meaningful second careers for veterans and strengthening the industry–veteran employment ecosystem. 
The Job Fair witnessed enthusiastic participation from over 480 Ex-Servicemen and 42 leading national and multinational companies, offering more than 1,300 employment opportunities across diverse sectors. The event provided a focused platform for connecting the skills, experience and leadership of trained Armed Forces personnel with the evolving talent requirements of industry. 
The event was inaugurated by Maj Gen Varun Malhotra, General Officer Commanding, UMANG Sub Area, who attended as the Military Chief Guest. Shri Amitabh Sinha, Chairman, CII Vidarbha Zonal Council, graced the occasion as the Corporate Guest of Honour. Maj Gen SBK Singh, SM, Director General Resettlement, and Brig Ranjan Keron, ADG, DRZ South, were also present. 
Senior military officers and corporate representatives interacted with participating veterans, discussing employment prospects, industry expectations and the competencies required in the civilian workforce. The interactions underscored the significant value that Ex-Servicemen bring to organisations through their leadership, discipline, integrity, technical proficiency, problem  solving abilities and experience in managing people and resources under demanding conditions. 
Prominent recruiters included Solar Group, Delhivery, Eros Group, Haldiram, JSR Dynamics and SBI Life, among other reputed organisations. Their participation reflected the growing scope for employing veterans across sectors and the importance of sustained industry engagement in expanding resettlement opportunities. 
The Job Fair went beyond employment facilitation to strengthen the connection between military experience and corporate requirements. It enabled employers to engage directly with a disciplined, skilled and experienced talent pool, while providing veterans with opportunities to explore new professional pathways and apply their capabilities in the civilian domain. 
DGR continues to advance the resettlement of retiring and retired Armed Forces personnel through employment facilitation, skill development, entrepreneurship promotion and partnerships with industry. These initiatives aim to ensure that the transition from military to civilian life is supported by dignified employment, sustainable livelihoods and opportunities for continued contribution to nation-building. 
DGR calls upon corporate organisations, industry associations and employers across sectors to deepen their engagement with Ex-Servicemen and recognise the immense potential of this proven talent pool. Stronger partnerships between government, industry and the Armed Forces can translate military experience into productive civilian employment thus benefiting veterans, their families, employers and the nation.

title: ASML Is Building a Hybrid Bonding Tool, Sending More Chills to Besi - SemiAnalysis
query: ("Besi" OR "BE Semiconductor Industries") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
ASML Is Building a Hybrid Bonding Tool!
Sherry Zhang , Gerald Wong , Steven Lee , and Dylan Patel 
Oct 15, 2026 
∙ Paid
140
18
Share
ASML has not announced anything yet, but its patent filings, a news report and its own roadmap all suggest so. We believe it will start with a die-to-wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding (HB) tool. This is harder to build than wafer-to-wafer but is where ASML could gain an edge. We see the move as a natural extension of ASML’s vertical integration, and one that should strengthen its customer ties. 
In this article we unpack the tool’s design end to end, starting with patent filings. What makes it unique is that it runs on a track . That changes how the tool and the dies move: each die rides its own holder past the process stations, and the tools get closer at each station to process the dies. The track’s independent shuttles also lift station utilization, save on duplicate tooling, and enable heterogeneous integration. 
We believe ASML could gain an edge in alignment accuracy and particle control for Hybrid Bonding. These are the two factors that set bonding yield. And ASML has expertise in solving the same problems in lithography. 
Despite the advantages, ASML still needs to solve challenges around feed-forward metrology, the die-to-wafer contact, the modification of the non-bonding tools so they can process dies on the track, and keeping the whole loop clean. 
We expect advanced logic, where D2W already runs in volume, to adopt ASML’s D2W HB tool first. This is bad news for Besi . Logic accounts for most of Besi’s HB business today concentrated at TSMC and Intel. ASML has been working with both for more than two decades and just announced a joint photomask initiative in September. We won’t be surprised to see a similar move in the back end process. Besi’s HBM prospects are also weakening. Korean challengers are catching up, in addition to an HBM adoption that we expect to slip to 2029 or beyond. 
ASML is Building a Hybrid Bonder 
We did a deep dive on hybrid bonding in 2024, and we still see it as the most transformative innovation in semiconductor manufacturing since EUV. Wafer-to-wafer (W2W) hybrid bonding (HB) is already in volume in image sensors and 3D NAND, and DRAM makers will be next. Die-to-wafer (D2W) HB is moving slower , because the industry still lacks mature tools that combine satisfying alignment accuracy and throughput (our check indicates upper bound in current applications is only one wafer per hour), which keeps cost per die high. Today D2W runs in volume only in logic: AMD has shipped hybrid-bonded V-Cache since 2022, and TSMC’s SoIC bonds at about 6um pitch today and targets 4.5um around 2029. The market expected HBM to become the big D2W volume driver from 2028. However, our view is different: we believe HBM will not adopt D2W HB before 2029 , if at all. 
Besi has led D2W and is the only supplier with tools in volume production. Everyone else is still trying to get a first tool qualified. But we believe the situation will soon change, because ASML is building a D2W hybrid bonding tool. Management hasn’t announced anything yet. But the company filed 27 bonding patent families between December 2022 and November 2024, most of them D2W, and the true count is likely higher because filings made after November 2024 are not yet public. The Elec also reported in March that ASML had started the architecture design of a hybrid bonder with Prodrive Technologies and VDL ETG. 
In the anchor filing ( WO2025201788A1 ), ASML drew how its bonding flow works. Interestingly, the system looks nothing like a traditional D2W bonder (see Advanced Packaging Part 5 for how those work). Instead of a bond head picking each die off a diced wafer and placing it, ASML moves single dies on independent holders around a track (Fig 1). Each die passes inspection, cleaning, plasma activation and metrology (topography, leveling and alignment) stations before it reaches the bonding station where the chuck lifts the bottom wafer up to meet the die. We unpack the design in the sections below. 
Fig 1: ASML’s track-based D2W bonder, SA annotated and simplified 
Source: ASML; SemiAnalysis Wafer Fabrication Equipment Model 
ASML could be building a W2W hybrid bonding tool as well. According to a patent analysis by Inha University , ASML is likely building W2W HB equipment on its TWINSCAN platform, leaning on its wafer overlay accuracy. We focus on the D2W machine in this note, because it is the harder tool to build and the one where ASML could gain a real edge. 
…as Part of its Vertical Integration Initiative 
We believe this is a continuation of ASML’s effort to integrate vertically and tighten customer relationships. ASML bought Cymer for its light source in 2013, HMI for e-beam inspection in 2016 and Berliner Glas for optics modules in 2020. It shipped its first back-end product, the XT:260 i-line packaging scanner, in 3Q25. And most recently, ASML announced joint initiatives with TSMC , Intel Foundry and Samsung to move the industry from 6-inch to 12-inch photomasks for High NA EUV. 
Building a bonder would be a natural next step. In fact, ASML’s own roadmap already puts bonding inside the front-end flow. Its 2024 Investor Day listed W2W and D2W hybrid bonding for NAND, DRAM and logic (Fig 2). And a July 2024 filing shows how the bonder and the scanner would work together by sharing die position data. Today a scanner printing on a bonded wafer must pre-align and coarse-align every die before it can expose. In ASML’s design the bonder already knows where it put each die and hands that map (a “coordinate system” in the filing) to the scanner, which checks a few marks and exposes. Customers get faster lithography on bonded wafers, and ASML gets to sell the bonder and the scanner as a pair. 
Fig 2: ASML’s map of front-end 3D integration 
Source: ASML Investor Day, 14-Nov-2024 
We expect advanced logic to be the first adopter. Logic is where D2W HB already runs in volume, and where the alignment requirement keeps tightening. TSMC calls overlay “always the biggest challenge” for SoIC. As its HB pitch moves from 6um to 4.5um by 2029, the placement accuracy requirement will tighten further. ASML is strong in alignment, as we will elaborate below, so an edge here should help it win logic customers first. Advanced logic dies are also among the most expensive chips, so logic customers can afford a premium tool. We expect ASML to price its tools at a premium to peers. 
In the next three sections, we discuss (1) the tool’s track system - the most unusual thing about it compared with what is on the market; (2) how ASML’s strengths in alignment, particle control and motion could make its HB tool superior; and (3) the challenges ASML or its supply chain partners still need to resolve to build a working tool. Let’s dive in.
What’s Unique About the Tool 
One of the most interesting things about the tool is that it runs on a track . ASML names SuperTrak CONVEYANCE (Fig 3) as an example in its patent filing , so we assume it uses that track and we base our analysis on the track’s published design. 
The fundamental difference from a traditional bonder is where the die lives. In a Besi-type tool, the die is prepared elsewhere, and a bond head picks it up only for the final placement. In ASML’s design, each die sits on its own holder from the moment it leaves the carrier and stays there until the bonding step . The process stations are built around the track: the die stops in front of a station, the station cleans, activates or measures it in place, and the die moves on. 
Fig 3: SuperTrak CONVEYANCE track (HORIZON10 platform) 
Source: Company website 
Now let’s go through the process step by step . For illustration, we took the patent drawing and labelled every station in Fig 4. A gripper takes the die off its carrier and sets it on an empty substrate holder (206), which carries it along the track (202). The die stops in turn at the inspection, cleaning, plasma activation, topographic inspection, leveling, coarse alignment, position adjustment and fine alignment stations (210 to 226). At each stop the die stays on its holder, and the station does its work. Note the reversal here: in the patent it is the station’s sensor or head that moves in to reach the die, not the die that is carried into the tool as in today’s flow. After these steps the die arrives at the bonding station (228). 
This bonding station deserves a closer look . The first thing to note is that the final placement is done by the holder (206) and the chuck (234), not the track: SuperTrak’s spec sheet puts the shuttles’ repeatability at about 10um, nowhere near the 50nm placement accuracy the bond needs. Next, zoom in on the right-hand part of Fig 4 for the bonding work. The chuck lifts the bottom wafer to within tens of microns of the die, the holder’s actuators adjust the die’s position, the die is pressed onto the wafer to form the bond, and the holder releases it. The empty holder then starts another loop. 
Fig 4: Patent WO2025201788A1 Fig. 2 (left) and Fig. 6 side view (right), SA annotated 
Source: ASML; SemiAnalysis Wafer Fabrication Equipment Model 
This design has three major benefits:
First, independent shuttles lift the utilization of every station . The number of stations per step can be set from that step’s cycle time: a three-second cleaning step gets three stations, and a 1.2-second bond step gets one, so every station stays busy. The patent asks for exactly this, to “occupy all process stations simultaneously”. 
Second, capacity is added by adding a station rather than a second tool, as long as the equipment chamber has room for it. That saves duplicate tooling and budget . 
Last but not least, the design suits heterogeneous integration : a new die type is a new software recipe, so mixed chiplets could share one line. 
That said, the track brings its own challenges around the non-bonding stations and the cleanliness of the whole loop. We come back to them later.
How ASML May Gain an Edge 
Before that, let’s look at how ASML could bring its existing strengths to the HB tool.
First, a reminder of why alignment accuracy and cleanliness matter so much in hybrid bonding. As we elaborated before , a single 1um particle between two full-thickness wafers can unbond an area around 10mm across , resulting in a defective bond (Fig 5). So particle control is extremely important for HB. Alignment matters for two reasons: placement accuracy sets bond yield directly, and alignment time weighs far more on D2W throughput than on W2W because it compounds with the die count. These two hurdles are what make hybrid bonding almost a front-end process. 
Fig 5: A small particle opens a void and an open contact in hybrid bonding 
Source: SemiAnalysis 
We believe ASML can tackle both with decades of experience solving the same two problems in lithography.
For alignment, we believe ASML can reuse its wafer-alignment sensor technology. Based on its patent filings , the bonding system puts a tiny diffraction grating on each die and reads the die’s position from the light the grating scatters. The principle is the same as ORION , the wafer-alignment sensor on every new TWINSCAN since 2017. ORION was built to read marks that CMP and etch have tilted or deformed (Fig 6), and a mark on a bonding die goes through the same CMP and plasma activation as the copper pads next to it, so it carries the same asymmetry. We believe the same sensor family can serve the D2W bonder. 
Fig 6: A symmetric and a tilted alignment mark. Process steps shift the apparent center; ORION’s multi-color readout was built to see through that 
Source: ASML, Aligning lithography to the nanometer, Dec-2021 
Its sensing and motion capabilities also provide it with more room in total alignment error budget. Its NXT:2100i holds 0.9nm overlay on a single machine. And ASML can already measure the distortion of a W2W bonded wafer and correct the next lithography layer for it, bringing post-bond overlay from 40-60nm down to below 4nm (Fig 7). These are litho numbers, not bond results. But they mean ASML’s sensor and stage errors sit more than an order of magnitude below the 50nm a bonder needs. Higher stage precision leaves more room in a bonder’s error budget for the other factors: die shift on the holder, thermal drift and movement during contact. 
Fig 7: ASML metrology plus scanner correction brings post-bond overlay to 2.5-3.9nm 
Source: ASML Investor Day, 14-Nov-2024 
Prodrive Technologies and VDL ETG are the likely component suppliers to help ASML’s bonder move fast on motion. Prodrive makes the linear motors and drives for ASML’s EUV maglev stages and has also built Hanwha Semitech’s SHB2 Nano bonder. VDL ETG builds ASML’s frames and modules (Fig 8). 
Fig 8: Prodrive’s linear motor (left) and VDL ETG’s wafer handler module (right) 
Source: Company websites 
On cleanliness, the requirements for ASML’s EUV systems are more strict as a bonder’s. Few tool makers have fought particles at the nanometer scale for as long as ASML. EUV scanners move reticles and wafers in vacuum and keep reticle particle adders at a level “ compatible with HVM requirements for sub-10nm node lithography ”. We believe ASML has thought about the bonding surfaces too: its bonding apparatus filing adds a tool that cleans the substrate supports and a sensor that watches their flatness, particle load and distortion. 
That said, contaminants in a bonder differ from those in a scanner. Most are dicing debris on die edges and particles landing on freshly activated, hydrophilic surfaces. We look for more detail on how ASML handles these bonder-specific contaminants in future filings.
After the paywall we discuss the challenges ASML needs to tackle to build a working tool, and how its tool will impact on Besi’s business prospects.
Open Questions ASML Needs to Solve

The week in cell therapy 
This week: a new manufacturing facility for Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) grade small molecules opened in Bristol, UK, a collaboration leveraging cGMP Next-Generation Sequencing-based viral safety testing to advance a stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis was announced, and a pre-clinical CAR-T portfolio was sold for €8 million.
The news highlights:
New UK facility boosts GMP small molecule manufacturing for cell therapies 
Collaboration to advance stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis 
Early-stage CAR-T portfolio sold for €8 million 
New UK facility boosts GMP small molecule manufacturing for cell therapies
Bio-Techne Corporation (MN, USA) has announced the opening of its new purpose-built 10,000-square-foot GMP manufacturing facility in Bristol, UK, strengthening the company’s global GMP manufacturing infrastructure.
The facility has five ISO-8 multifunctional cleanrooms and two ISO-7 cleanrooms dedicated to small molecule manufacturing and product handling.
“As the cell therapy field continues to mature, success increasingly depends on the ability to manufacture therapies consistently and at scale,” said Kim Kelderman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Bio-Techne. “Our investment in Bristol demonstrates Bio-Techne’s commitment to providing customers with the GMP materials, manufacturing expertise, and supply chain reliability needed to accelerate development and ultimately bring transformative therapies to patients worldwide.”
Read more 
Collaboration to advance stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis
Charles River Laboratories (MA, USA) and Magellan Stem Cells (Victoria, Australia) have announced a partnership to advance the development and commercialization of Magellan’s lead proprietary allogeneic, off-the-shelf stem cell therapy candidate (Zelestrocel) for osteoarthritis.
Magellan has recently completed Phase I/II trials for Zelestrocel and is now moving toward a Phase III study. The company has also built manufacturing capacity directly into its development process, having obtained GMP certification from Australia’s Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) for its production site in Melbourne.
Under the agreement, Charles River will provide cGMP Next-Generation Sequencing-based viral safety testing for Zelestrocel to support regulatory readiness.
“As we prepare for the next stage of Zelestrocel’s development, having access to advanced testing technologies and collaborating with experienced partners is critical to our success,” said Magellan Stem Cells CEO Julien Freitag.
Read more 
Early-stage CAR-T portfolio sold for €8 million
Lakefront Biotherapeutics (formerly Galapagos NV; Mechelen, Belgium) has announced the completed sale of its early-stage cell therapy portfolio to Armed Cell Therapeutics (Brussels, Belgium). Under the deal terms, Lakefront will receive €8 million upfront, with the possibility of earning up to $230 million in future milestone payments plus a modest royalty on sales.
The divested assets include a range of multi-targeting and armed CAR-T constructs engineered to enhance the potency and persistence of CAR-T therapies while addressing treatment resistance in hematological cancers and solid tumors.
“I’m pleased we were able to complete this sale of the early-stage cell therapy programs as it provides a path to continue to advance these assets on behalf of patients. Additionally, it offers Lakefront shareholders the opportunity to benefit from their potential future progress by the experienced team at Armed Cell Therapeutics,” said Sooin Kwon, Chief Business Officer of Lakefront. “Lakefront continues to be in an enviable position with a rich legacy of innovation, an exciting newly established pipeline of T-cell engagers and a strong cash balance.”

SEMICON West 2026: Dutch company to strengthen support for local customers, including Hanwha Semitech

Prodrive Technologies participates in SEMICON West 2026, held at the Moscone Center in San Francisco from Oct. 13 to 15. (Photo: THE ELEC) 
Dutch company Prodrive Technologies plans to open an office in South Korea between late 2026 and early 2027 to strengthen support for local customers, including Hanwha Semitech, and expand its presence through sales activities.
At SEMICON West 2026, held at the Moscone Center in San Francisco on Oct. 13, Prodrive said it was recruiting local employees in preparation for the office opening. “We expect to open around the end of this year or early next year,” the company said. It is considering Dongtan and Pangyo as potential locations.
The Korean office will handle sales and customer support, with a small team being recruited. Prodrive is also building a new manufacturing facility in Malaysia. It operates production sites in the Netherlands, Boston in the US, and China, as well as sales offices in Japan and Israel. The company employs approximately 2,300 people worldwide.
Prodrive develops modules and provides system integration services for semiconductor equipment manufacturers. Rather than selling finished equipment directly to chipmakers, it designs and integrates equipment modules to meet manufacturers’ requirements. Its core products include precision stages, motion controllers, motors, actuators and high-speed cameras used in applications requiring high-precision control. It also produces equipment for front-end metrology and inspection and back-end hybrid bonding.
In South Korea, Hanwha Semitech collaborated with Prodrive to develop a hybrid bonder. Earlier this year, the second-generation hybrid bonder, SHB2 Nano, was manufactured and assembled at Prodrive’s Netherlands facility before being brought to South Korea. Prodrive also supplies linear motors and servo drives for magnetic levitation systems used in ASML’s extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment.
“The Korean office will be responsible for sales and customer support,” a Prodrive representative said. “We have no plans to establish manufacturing facilities in Korea because we can support Korean customers from Malaysia, China and Europe.”

Vestas Secures 92 MW Wind Turbine Orders in Germany in Partnership with BBWind
By Kavitha 
15th October 2026 
138

Representational image. Credit: Canva 
Vestas has announced new wind turbine orders totalling approximately 92 MW across three onshore wind projects in Germany, in collaboration with BBWind Projektberatungsgesellschaft mbH. The orders, included in the company’s third-quarter (Q3) order intake, cover the supply of 13 wind turbines and include 20-year Active Output Management (AOM) 5000 service agreements.
The projects, located in Borken and Raesfeld, will feature Vestas’ V172-7.2 MW and V162-5.6 MW turbine models, supporting the continued expansion of Germany’s onshore wind energy capacity.
The first order covers the 42 MW Borken Kierit wind project, developed by Windenergie Kierit GmbH & Co. KG in association with BBWind Projektberatungsgesellschaft mbH. Vestas will supply five V172-7.2 MW turbines and one V162-5.6 MW turbine for the project. Deliveries are scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027, with commissioning expected to commence in the second quarter of 2028. The agreement includes a 20-year AOM 5000 service contract to support long-term turbine performance and operational reliability.
The second agreement involves the 29 MW Raesfeld Lanzenhagen wind project, developed by Windenergie Lanzenhagen GmbH & Co. KG in collaboration with BBWind. The project will feature four V172-7.2 MW wind turbines, with deliveries planned to begin in the first quarter of 2028 and commissioning scheduled to commence in the fourth quarter of 2028. The contract also includes a 20-year AOM 5000 service agreement.
The third order covers the 22 MW Borken Deepschlatt wind project, developed by Windenergie Deepschlatt GmbH & Co. KG alongside BBWind. Vestas will deliver three V172-7.2 MW wind turbines, with deliveries expected to begin in the first quarter of 2028 and commissioning scheduled to start in the third quarter of 2028. The project will also benefit from a 20-year AOM 5000 service agreement.
Also Read   China’s Installed Power Capacity Reaches 4,132 GW As Solar And Wind Drive Growth In 2026 
Across the three projects, Vestas will supply 12 V172-7.2 MW turbines and one V162-5.6 MW turbine, representing a combined turbine capacity of approximately 92 MW. The long-term service agreements are designed to support operational efficiency, turbine availability, and reliable electricity generation throughout the projects’ operating lives.
The latest orders highlight continued investment in Germany’s onshore wind sector and reinforce Vestas’ collaboration with BBWind in developing renewable energy infrastructure.
The projects are expected to contribute to Germany’s renewable energy expansion by increasing wind power generation capacity, strengthening domestic clean electricity supply, and supporting the country’s broader energy transition and decarbonisation objectives.

title: Dow Partnership Advances Recyclable Polymer Technology - Northwestern University
query: ("DOW" OR "Dow Inc") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Dow Partnership Advances Recyclable Polymer Technology
Award honors Northwestern-Dow collaboration to make crosslinked polymers recyclable
Oct 15, 2026 Brian Sandalow 
The Problem
Conventional crosslinked polymers found in car tires, rubber bands, and other everyday items are durable, but their permanent crosslinks prevent them from being recycled.
Our Idea
Researchers developed crosslinks that remain strong during use but can break and reform during reprocessing, allowing the material to be recycled multiple times.
Why It Matters
The approach could make widely used crosslinked polymers recyclable using improved industrial processes.
Our Team
Professor John Torkelson; PhD graduates Boran Chen (PhD ’24), Logan Fenimore (PhD ’25), Yen-Wen Huang (PhD ’26), and Mathew Suazo (PhD ’26); Dow researchers Evelyn Auyeung (PhD ’14), Stephanie Barbon, Hayley Brown, and Colin Li Pi Shan.
Northwestern Engineering’s John Torkelson and eight collaborators from Northwestern University and the Dow Chemical Company have been selected to receive the 2027 Cooperative Research Award in Polymer Science and Engineering from the American Chemical Society’s (ACS) Division of Polymeric Materials: Science and Engineering (PMSE). An award symposium in their honor will be held at the Spring 2027 National ACS Meeting in New Orleans. The award recognizes outstanding cooperative research among industrial, academic, and national laboratory scientists. 
Along with Torkelson, Walter P. Murphy Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering and Materials Science and Engineering at the McCormick School of Engineering, honorees include four researchers who conducted the work as PhD students in his group : Boran Chen (PhD ’24), Logan Fenimore (PhD ’25), Yen-Wen Huang (PhD ’26), and Mathew Suazo (PhD ’26). In addition, recipients include four collaborators from Dow: Evelyn Auyeung (PhD ‘14), Stephanie Barbon, Hayley Brown, and Colin Li Pi Shan.
The collaboration, supported through Dow’s University Partnership Initiative , has spanned nearly seven years to address a persistent problem in polymer recycling: how to give crosslinked polymers the durability that makes them useful without making them permanently unrecyclable.
For Torkelson, who joined Northwestern in 1983, the recognition also reflects a research direction he has pursued for decades. 
“Sometimes the most important thing to do is to work on things that people think can’t be done,” said Torkelson, an expert in polymer science and engineering, particularly sustainable and recyclable polymers, polymer processing, and polymer nanotechnology, who has been energized by the success of the partnership.
The project began with skepticism. The team’s first paper demonstrating its reprocessable polyethylene networks was rejected. The team then submitted the manuscript to another journal, where it received strong reviews and was later recognized as one of the journal’s most popular papers of 2022. That paper became the foundation for much of the research now being recognized by the ACS PMSE award and pursued toward commercial application.
The research has since produced more than 20 publications and multiple patent filings. Torkelson sees its development from a small-scale university experiment to commercialization research as an example of what sustained relationships between universities and companies can accomplish.
Making crosslinked polymers recyclable
Crosslinked polymers are everywhere, from rubber tires and rubber bands to foam mattresses. Crosslinks tie long polymer chains together, creating some of the most robust materials.
That durability, however, creates a recycling problem. Unlike thermoplastics, whose molecular chains can move past one another when heated, conventionally crosslinked materials cannot return to a flowing melt state that allows them to be reshaped.
“Once it’s made, you can never take a rubber band back into a melt state, Torkelson said.
His group developed a different approach. They created crosslinks that remain robust under normal use conditions but become dynamic at the elevated temperatures used during reprocessing. At those temperatures, the bonds forming the crosslinks can dissociate, allowing the material to be reshaped. As the material cools, the bonds reform.
The approach has been demonstrated with polyethylene and polypropylene, which together account for more than half of the roughly 1 trillion pounds of polymers and plastics produced globally each year. Currently, less than 10 percent of that total is recycled, Torkelson said.
The new method is designed as a relatively simple modification of an existing industrial process. Permanently crosslinked polyethylene is already manufactured by adding an initiator to polyethylene. Torkelson’s approach adds a small amount of a dynamic crosslinker to that process.
“Industry doesn’t have to develop a whole new process to accommodate this,” Torkelson said. “We can modify the existing process.”
That alignment can eliminate the need for new machinery and reduce the amount of process development required before adoption. Torkelson said the approach might require adjustments to some processing conditions, but it remains a relatively small variation on technology already used commercially.
The research could have implications beyond recycling. In recently published work, Huang and Torkelson found that converting polyethylene into the group’s crosslinked systems also made the material more resistant to wear. In tests, the materials exhibited more than a one-third reduction in wear, measured through volume or mass loss, compared with the polyethylene from which they were derived.
Because everyday wear of plastics can produce microplastics, Torkelson said the increased durability raises another possibility for the research.
“The crosslinks just lead to more durable materials that will actually wear less,” he said. “This even has an implication for potentially mitigating microplastic formation.”
From the university lab and commercial research
Much of the project’s development has depended on the complementary capabilities of Northwestern and Dow.
At Northwestern, Torkelson’s group develops ideas, studies their underlying science, and demonstrates them at laboratory scale. Dow brought expertise and facilities needed to test whether those concepts could move toward larger-scale manufacturing and commercial applications.
“This was a case where they have real expertise in terms of large-scale processing, and we do everything at the university at small scale,” Torkelson said. “I’ve learned a lot from Dow. They have learned a lot from us.”
What began as a three-year Dow project supporting one graduate student expanded as the results accumulated. Fenimore, who had received a National Science Foundation fellowship, also joined the effort. Torkelson said Dow typically supports university projects for about three years before moving to new research questions, but the polymer work continued beyond that initial period with funding for two graduate students.
This was a case where they have real expertise in terms of large-scale processing, and we do everything at the university at small scale. I’ve learned a lot from Dow. They have learned a lot from us. John Torkelson 
Dow has since conducted commercialization research based on the Northwestern technology at facilities in Lake Jackson, Texas, and Shanghai, China.
One area Dow has explored is molded footwear. Such products offered a relatively small consumer application through which the company could test the technology and its recyclability. Torkelson said Dow researchers demonstrated that a used crosslinked product could be cut into pieces, reprocessed, and used to make a new product. Waste material created during injection molding could similarly be fed back into the manufacturing process rather than discarded.
The partnership also provided an education that extended beyond Torkelson’s laboratory.
Chen, Fenimore, Huang, and Suazo carried out the bulk of the university research, Torkelson said, while gaining exposure to industrial research and the process of moving a scientific idea toward application.
The 2027 honor marks the first time the Cooperative Research Award has recognized the graduate students who performed much of the university research in addition to faculty and industrial researchers. For Torkelson, their inclusion in the Cooperative Research Award is particularly meaningful.
The four researchers have since moved into industry and academic research. Huang joined Dow, Suazo joined AOC Formulations, and two are pursuing postdoctoral research, including Fenimore at the National Institute of Standards and Technology and Chen at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.
While Torkelson cautioned that not every university-industry research project will produce the same results, he said this collaboration has proven mutually beneficial for a relatively modest industrial investment.

Arkema officially opens the expansion of its R&D center in Shanghai 
Download the PDF 
Arkema announces the opening of the expansion of its Shanghai R&D Center, which will take the center to the next level and strengthen its strategic role as an innovation platform serving all the Group’s businesses. The center will enable synergies among teams and co-development with customers in China and across Asia, to accelerate innovation in cutting-edge applications and the successful deployment of advanced and sustainable material solutions. This expansion is fully aligned with the Group’s investment strategy in its global R&D laboratory network.
During his visit in China, Thierry Le Hénaff, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Arkema, inaugurated the expanded center alongside the Consul General of France in Shanghai, local government representatives, customers, partners and management representatives.
China is Arkema’s second-largest market and one of the most dynamic innovation hubs worldwide.
