content_text:
Albemarle Jumps as Mizuho Sees Battery Storage Demand Tightening Lithium Market
Add preferred source 2 
Albemarle shares rose 4% in premarket trading after Mizuho Securities upgraded the lithium producer to Outperform from Neutral, citing strong demand from battery energy storage systems, though the stock gave up the gain and closed 0.4% lower at a fresh year-to-date low. Analyst John Roberts kept a $130 price target, implying 33% upside. Mizuho projects lithium carbonate prices to reach $22,500 per metric ton by 2027 and $19,500 by 2028, above prior forecasts, driven by a 10% increase in projected 2027 demand from stationary storage. The firm also raised adjusted EBITDA estimates for Albemarle to $3.2 billion in 2027 and $2.9 billion in 2028. Roberts noted that regulatory delays at CATL's Jianxiawo lithium mine in China could further tighten supply. Albemarle has fallen 31% year to date amid weaker lithium prices, but the company's low-cost position and improved balance sheet are seen as key advantages.
Key Elements 
Albemarle Corp Mizuho Securities John Roberts Benchmark Minerals Contemporary Amperex Technology NYSE LSEG 
Albemarle Corp (ALB) climbed 4% in premarket trading Wednesday after Mizuho Securities lifted its rating on the world's largest lithium producer, betting that surging demand for utility-scale battery storage will tighten the market and push prices higher.
Analyst John Roberts upgraded the stock to Outperform from Neutral while keeping his $130 price target, a level he had trimmed from $140 about two weeks earlier, implying roughly 33% upside from Tuesday's close. The Charlotte, North Carolina-based company has fallen 31% year to date as lithium prices weakened, but the firm now sees a more favorable supply-demand balance taking shape.
The gain did not hold. By Wednesday's close the stock was 0.4% lower at a fresh year-to-date low. Earlier in the week, Chinese lithium carbonate futures posted their steepest one-day fall since March, closing down 11.8% at 104,740 yuan a metric ton on Oct. 12 after the European Union proposed capping imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles at about 350,000 units a year. Spot battery-grade carbonate in China was assessed at 115,400 yuan a metric ton that day, down 5.7%.
"We are raising ALB rating to Outperform as strong Battery Energy Stationary Storage (BESS) demand has tipped market balance into favorable territory," Roberts wrote in a note to clients. "ALB is the lowest-cost lithium producer and its improved balance sheet provides downside resilience while providing flexibility to invest as project returns improve."
The catalyst is accelerating deployment of grid-scale energy storage systems, which is consuming global lithium supply faster than previously expected. Albemarle's own numbers make the same point: on its August earnings call, the company raised its 2026 forecast for global stationary-storage battery production to 900-1,100 gigawatt-hours, about 100 GWh above its prior range, and said storage would account for roughly 30% of global lithium demand this year — nearing parity with light-duty electric vehicles. Global lithium consumption was up 45% year over year through May, and the company described inventories as low and the physical market as tight.
Revised forecasts from industry consultant Benchmark Minerals project lithium carbonate prices reaching $22,500 per metric ton by 2027 and $19,500 per metric ton by 2028, substantial upward revisions from earlier estimates of $18,375 and $14,500, respectively.
Mizuho noted that the surge in stationary storage requirements lifted projected 2027 demand by about 10%, while expected global supply and inventory drawdowns remained essentially unchanged. That widening gap prompted the firm to raise its price forecasts for Albemarle's core Energy Storage segment to $21,000 per metric ton in 2027 and $19,000 per metric ton in 2028.
Revised Price Forecasts 
Metric Previous 2027 New 2027 Previous 2028 New 2028 
Benchmark lithium carbonate $18,375/t $22,500/t $14,500/t $19,500/t 
Mizuho Energy Storage segment — $21,000/t — $19,000/t 
Note: Per metric ton.
Reflecting higher realization assumptions, Mizuho boosted its adjusted EBITDA estimates for Albemarle to $3.2 billion in 2027 and $2.9 billion in 2028, up from $2.4 billion and $2.5 billion previously. As the industry's lowest-cost producer, the company is well positioned to convert higher market prices into expanding operating margins and stronger cash flow generation.
Earnings Sensitivity to Lithium Prices 
Albemarle's own 2026 outlook, published in August, shows how much of its earnings power hinges on where lithium settles:
Lithium price assumption ($/kg LCE) FY2025 average (~$10) Q1 2026 average (~$20) 2021-2025 average (~$30) 
Net sales $4.1-4.3 billion $5.7-6.0 billion $7.5-7.8 billion 
Adjusted EBITDA $0.9-1.0 billion $2.4-2.6 billion $4.2-4.4 billion 
Mizuho's 2027 EBITDA estimate sits roughly 30% above the midpoint of the $20/kg scenario, reflecting its $21,000 a metric ton realization assumption for the energy storage segment and the volume growth expected as the CGP3 plant at the Greenbushes joint venture ramps to full capacity in the first quarter of 2027. Management said on the same call that 2027 volumes should return to a 240,000-260,000 metric ton trajectory.
Supply Constraints Could Add Fuel
Roberts also flagged that lithium demand could intensify further if regulatory hurdles delay the resumption of Contemporary Amperex Technology's upstream production. The reference is to Jianxiawo, a lepidolite mine in Jiangxi province that is China's largest lithium operation by capacity, with nameplate capacity approaching 150,000 metric tons of lithium carbonate equivalent a year. Its permitting saga has dragged on for more than a year:
The same consultancy now expects the mine to produce 32,000 metric tons LCE in 2026, half its previous forecast, while keeping its 2027 estimate at about 99,000 metric tons. The environmental review could stretch into 2027, and authorities are also inspecting other Jiangxi mines that were expected to produce about 108,000 metric tons LCE this year. The Chinese battery giant is a major player in the lithium supply chain, so any slowdown removes supply from an already tightening market.
"Lithium remains a volatile, capital-intensive commodity, but the near-term supply/demand outlook has tightened as demand continues to exceed expectations while new supply is constrained by long project lead times and reduced industry capital spending," the analyst wrote.
Mizuho's call aligns with broader Street sentiment. Of the 23 analysts covering Albemarle, 15 hold a buy or strong buy rating, while eight maintain a hold, according to LSEG data. Investors will likely watch whether accelerating stationary storage deployment can offset ongoing volatility in consumer electric vehicle adoption over the coming quarters. The next checkpoint is Nov. 4, when Albemarle reports third-quarter results; management has guided for sequential declines in both net sales and adjusted EBITDA, citing lower volumes and softer pricing.

What We Thought of ASML Holding’s Earnings 
Last quarter, ASML Holding ASML announced plans to expand low-NA EUV and immersion DUV capacity by 30% in 2027 and another 30% in 2028. These plans seem already outdated, as management has acknowledged this might not be enough to meet customer demand.
Why it matters: ASML’s backlog keeps growing, with 2027 fully booked and significant order intake already for 2028. In our view, the most important disclosure from these earnings was that ASML is having first conversations with customers for 2029 and 2030 orders. DRAM makers seem the most open to talking about 2029-30 already.
While we still see some upside to our 2028 revenue and EPS forecast as ASML tries to expand capacity beyond 30% with its existing footprint, we believe most of it is already priced in. What could push the stock higher is order visibility that confirms 2029 and 2030 as “growth years.”
The bottom line: We maintain our wide Morningstar Economic Moat Rating and EUR 1,800 fair value estimate.
After 28% sales growth in both 2027 and 2028, reaching EUR 56 and EUR 71.5 billion respectively, we model a return to low-double-digit growth in 2029 and 2030, with sales reaching EUR 88 billion in 2030. Should management confirm the first 2029 orders over the next six months, our 2029-30 forecast would gain credibility, and the stock price could converge toward our fair value estimate.
Our bull case would require 2029 to book as quickly and as fully as 2028 has. If customers place orders at a fast pace in the coming months, sales growth in 2029-30 could exceed our low-double-digit forecast.
Key stats: Beyond expanding capacity, ASML continues to aggressively develop upgrades to low-NA EUV and immersion DUV output. Installed base management revenue reached EUR 3.3 billion, EUR 400 million higher than expected, thanks to the upgrade business, as customers look to extract more productivity from their machines. Upgrades were the main driver of the 57.5% gross margin this quarter, above guidance of 55.0%-57.0%.

Tosoh to acquire Asahi Kasei’s stake in HDI monomer JV, taking full ownership
October 14, 2026 | By Mary Bailey 
Tosoh Corp. (Tokyo) has decided to acquire all shares (50%) of Nanyo Kasei Co., Ltd. (Tokyo), a joint venture with Asahi Kasei Corp. (Tokyo). The deal will make Nanyo Kasei a wholly owned subsidiary of Tosoh.
Nanyo Kasei was established in 1980 through equal investment by Nippon Polyurethane Industry Co., Ltd. (now Tosoh) and Asahi Kasei to manufacture hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) monomer .
Currently, Tosoh and Asahi Kasei supply raw materials and other inputs to Nanyo Kasei, which manufactures the HDI monomer. Each company then purchases the monomer for its own operations. Tosoh will acquire the 50% of Nanyo Kasei shares held by Asahi Kasei.
Through the full acquisition, Tosoh aims to secure a stable supply of HDI monomer and support the stable operation of its HDI derivatives business. The transaction will also contribute to the stable procurement of HDI monomer for Tosoh’s new HDI derivatives plant, which began commercial operations in September 2026.
Tosoh expects the impact of the transaction on its consolidated financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, to be minimal.

Shortlist revealed for 2026 Hull & East Yorkshire Business Awards
Business News 
Oct 14 
Written by Rick Lyon 
CELEBRATING SUCCESS: The 2025 HEY Business Awards winners
By Rick Lyon, Co-Editor
Judges have had their say on the best and the brightest businesses across the region.
A total of 27 different organisations remain in the running for the prestigious annual accolades at the Hull & East Yorkshire Business Awards, with the leading figures at the helm of three of the category contenders also competing for the coveted Entrepreneur of the Year title.
It is the third edition of the awards under the tenure of talent champion Simon Jones and events specialist Jane Smallwood, and the level of support generated has surpassed even that garnered for last year’s silver anniversary celebration.
And with the quality of entries also praised, the gala celebration promises to be another great night under the guidance of top television host Gethin Jones, when it is held next month.
Simon said: “Our partnership numbers are incredible this year, the highest we’ve seen since taking the awards on, and we see that as a real show of confidence in what we’re delivering.
“The strength and depth of the submissions have been extremely good, and we feel that is a result of the whole process being taken a lot more seriously.”
Judging of the nominations has been made more rigorous, moving from a desktop exercise with independent representatives of the business community, to in-person interviews and site visits by a far wider supporting cast.
Jane said: “Since taking the awards baton on from Reach Plc, who remain our media partner, we’ve refreshed the judging process – taking it from a paper exercise to a deep dive with face-to-face meetings. We feel it enhances the credibility of the accolades, and this is reflected in the quality of our contenders.”
Headline partner is For Entrepreneurs Only, with three new principal partners also involved in 2026 – BAE Systems, H&H and Siemens Gamesa.
Winners will be crowned at the Doubletree by Hilton Hotel Hull on Thursday, November 19. There will be a dozen awards presented, including the Lifetime Achievement Award, with packages of support tailored to the individual category, again part of the deeper focus on a richer event, taking it beyond the night.   
Tickets are available at £90 plus VAT each or £850 plus VAT for a table of ten, at https://heybusinessawards.co.uk/

content_text:
Ocugen Expands Into Europe Ahead of Gene Therapy Filings
October 14, 2026 October 12, 2026 - by Timothy Alexander 
MALVERN, PA — Ocugen Inc. (NASDAQ: OCGN) has established a European affiliate in Amsterdam and appointed former Moderna Netherlands executive Jolanda Crombach to lead it, positioning the Malvern biotechnology company for potential regulatory approvals and commercialization of three experimental gene therapies for retinal diseases.
The expansion comes as Ocugen advances three Phase 3 clinical programs toward planned regulatory submissions in the United States and Europe, with key trial results expected in 2027 and 2028.
Crombach will serve as general manager of the newly established European operation, overseeing the development of personnel and infrastructure needed to support regulatory and commercial activities.
The company plans to pursue European Marketing Authorization Applications following the anticipated clinical data readouts. Those submissions would be necessary steps toward securing permission to market the treatments in Europe.
READ:   Meridian Profit Falls 22% as Mortgage Business Weakens 
Ocugen’s lead programs target three retinal conditions associated with vision loss: retinitis pigmentosa, geographic atrophy secondary to dry age-related macular degeneration, and Stargardt disease.
OCU400 is being developed for retinitis pigmentosa, a group of inherited retinal disorders that cause progressive vision deterioration.
OCU410 targets geographic atrophy associated with dry age-related macular degeneration, while OCU410ST is being evaluated for Stargardt disease, an inherited condition affecting the retina.
All three candidates use Ocugen’s modifier gene therapy approach and remain investigational. Their eventual commercialization depends on clinical results and regulatory review.
READ:   Innovative Aerosystems Wins Dornier Seastar Avionics Contract 
“As we advance our three Phase 3 modifier gene therapy programs toward regulatory submissions and potential commercialization, establishing a strong presence in Europe is an important component of our growth strategy,” said Shankar Musunuri, Ocugen’s chairman, chief executive officer and co-founder.
Crombach joins Ocugen after serving as managing director and a board member of Moderna Netherlands, where she established the company’s Dutch affiliate and subsequently managed its operations.
Her appointment brings experience in developing pharmaceutical operations within European healthcare markets, including commercial strategy, market access and medical affairs.
Before Moderna, Crombach held leadership positions at MSD, also known as Merck, and Pfizer, spanning commercial operations, market access, medical affairs and corporate and public affairs.
READ:   Meridian Profit Falls 22% as Mortgage Business Weakens 
She began her career as a pharmacist and holds an MSc PharmD degree from Utrecht University in the Netherlands.
The Amsterdam affiliate will be responsible for building Ocugen’s regional organization as the company approaches clinical milestones and prepares for potential European regulatory submissions.
The expansion establishes a European operating presence before the company has secured marketing authorization for any of the three therapies covered by its late-stage development program.

Charles River partners with Magellan Stem Cells on cell therapy
The partnership focuses on biologics quality control as well as viral and release testing under cGMP standards.
Salong Debbarma 
October 14, 2026 
Share

Charles River will supply viral safety assessments using NGS for cell and gene therapy. Credit: Gorodenkoff/Shutterstock.com. 
Charles River Laboratories International (CRL) has collaborated with Australian biotechnology firm Magellan Stem Cells to advance the development and clinical progress of Magellan’s regenerative medicine candidate, Zelestrocel.
The partnership focuses on biologics quality control as well as viral and release testing under current good manufacturing practice (cGMP) standards.

Magellan recently completed Phase I/II clinical studies evaluating Zelestrocel, an off-the-shelf, allogeneic stem cell therapy designed to treat osteoarthritis.
The company is now preparing to initiate a pivotal Phase III clinical programme.
Charles River global manufacturing corporate senior vice president Kerstin Dolph said: “Working with organisations at the forefront of innovation allows us to expand our GMP testing capabilities and help accelerate the delivery of safe, compliant therapies to patients.
“We are excited to support Magellan as they work towards advancing Zelestrocel from the clinic to potential commercialisation.”
To support the therapy’s progress towards international regulatory standards, Charles River will provide viral safety assessments using next-generation sequencing (NGS) for cell and gene therapy (CGT).
The testing protocols comply with regulatory benchmarks from the European Medicines Agency (EMA), the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), GMP standards, and International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) Q5A and Q5B guidelines.
Charles River expanded its sequencing capabilities through the acquisition of Pathoquest, a company specialising in biopharmaceutical quality control and characterisation.
Magellan COO Nick Bliesner said: “Charles River’s GMP NGS capabilities provide an innovative approach to viral safety testing that supports both product quality and regulatory readiness. This collaboration strengthens our ability to advance Zelestrocel toward commercialisation with confidence.”
Magellan manufactures the cell therapy internally at its Melbourne facility, which holds GMP certification from the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA).
It is one of only four cell therapy manufacturing centres in Australia to hold GMP certification.
The sequencing work also aligns with Charles River’s Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP), an initiative guided by a scientific advisory board chaired by Dr Namandjé Bumpus to reduce animal testing by implementing new approach methodologies (NAMs).
In addition, Charles River operates nine CGMP-compliant International Organization for Standardization-6 (ISO-6) cleanroom suites, offers cell bank release within eight to ten weeks, and has produced more than 2,000 cell and viral banks.
In August this year, CRL and Medigen Vaccine Biologics (MVC) entered into a collaboration to support the characterisation and validation of the virus seed bank for MVC’s next-generation multivalent enterovirus vaccine.

Tosoh to take full control of PU monomer producer
14 Oct 2026
Share: 
Acquisition from Asahi Kasei to support supply to newly commissioned HDI derivatives plant
Tokyo – Tosoh Corp. is to acquire Asahi Kasei's 50% interest in Nanyo Kasei, taking full ownership of the Japanese producer of hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) monomer.
Nanyo Kasei was established in 1980 as a 50:50 joint venture between Asahi Kasei and Nippon Polyurethane Industry, now part of Tosoh, to manufacture HDI monomer.
Under the current arrangement, Tosoh and Asahi Kasei supply raw materials and other inputs to Nanyo Kasei and subsequently purchase the HDI monomer produced by the company.
In a 13 Oct statement, Tosoh said the acquisition would enable it to “secure a stable supply of HDI monomer” and support the stable operation of its HDI derivatives business.
In particular, the group said the transaction would support HDI monomer supply to its new HDI derivatives plant, which started commercial operations in September.
The acquisition is scheduled to close by the end of March 2027.

ASML says it's getting order interest through 2030 as profit smashes expectations
Published Wed, Oct 14 2026 1:14 AM EDT Updated Wed, Oct 14 2026 4:45 AM EDT 
Arjun Kharpal @/in/arjunkharpal/ @ArjunKharpal 
WATCH LIVE 
Key Points
ASML said some customers are "expressing an interest" in placing orders with the company in 2029 and 2030, providing investors with a view into longer-term demand.
The Dutch chip giant said it is looking at ways to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase it had previously forecast as demand remains strong.
The company also raised the lower end of its sales forecast for 2026.
In this article
ASML

ASML said Wednesday that some of its customers are expressing interest in placing orders for its critical semiconductor tools for 2029 and 2030 as the company reported third-quarter profit that beat expectations.
The comments will likely comfort investors who have been looking to assess the longer-term demand outlook for ASML's lithography machines.
"Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments," CEO Christophe Fouquet said in a press release. 
"In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030."
ASML is the only company in the world that produces extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, a key tool used by the likes of TSMC to make the world's most advanced semiconductors. 
Investors closely watch the Dutch company's earnings for signs of AI-related chip demand. 
watch now 
VIDEO 3:47 03:47 
ASML races to expand capacity on strong AI-driven demand
Squawk Box Europe 
Fouquet said current supply planned for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet the demand of its customers. The company is "investigating ways" to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase it had previously forecast. 
ASML has now updated its guidance three times this year, upping its full-year forecast for the second time in July, and on Wednesday it raised the lower end of its sales forecast for 2026. 
The company now expects net sales of between 44 billion euros and 45 billion euros ($49.3 billion to $50.4 billion). The previous lower end of the forecast was for 43 billion euros.
ASML also said it expects fourth-quarter net sales of between 14.2 billion euros and 15.2 billion euros. The upper end of the range is ahead of LSEG consensus estimates of 14.2 billion euros. 
ASML's stock was around 2% higher in early trade in Europe. Shares of the company have rallied 56% this year. 
ASML shares year-to-date
During the quarter, Samsung and TSMC, the world's two biggest chipmakers, committed to using ASML's High NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. High NA EUV is ASML's next-generation tool, which analysts see as key to the Dutch firm's future growth.
For the third quarter, here's how ASML did versus LSEG consensus estimates:
Net sales: 11.66 billion euros versus 11.72 billion euros expected
Net profit: 4.96 billion euros versus 4.1 billion euros expected 
ASML sticks to China forecast 
The semiconductor equipment maker said it expects China sales to account for 20% of its total business, sticking to a prior forecast.
While ASML holds an effective monopoly on EUV machines, a July report from The Information suggested an unnamed Chinese company had begun manufacturing an immersion deep ultraviolet lithography (DUV) machine, citing people familiar with the matter.
ASML dominates the manufacturing of DUV machines, which are less advanced than EUV. China has been ramping up its domestic semiconductor supply chain, with some investors concerned it could challenge the European and U.S. dominance. However, analysts raised questions about China's ability to ramp up its own DUV technology. 
ASML meanwhile has faced challenges in China over the last few years. The company is restricted from selling EUV and some DUV tools to China.

Rio Tinto expects lithium output to be constrained by weather and delays in Argentina, while still waiting on Chile 
Bnamericas Published: Wednesday, October 14, 2026 
Production Public-private partnership (PPP) Market Prices and Forecasts Lithium Electrolyte Building Materials Brine extraction Evaporation Mergers & Acquisitions Environmental conflict Private Investment Lithium Financing Project Finance Lithium Hydroxide Prospecting, exploration and extraction of mineral resources Direct lithium extraction (DLE) Mining Companies Lithium Carbonate Show 13 More Hide 13 Topics 
Rio Tinto increased lithium output in 3Q26 and pressed on with construction of its Rincon project and commissioning of the Fénix 1B expansion in Argentina, though logistics problems at Sal de Vida and poor weather will weigh on its full-year performance.
For 2026, the Anglo-Australian miner expects to come in at the low end of its 61,000-64,000t global lithium production guidance, hit by maintenance at its assets and delays in the ramp-up of Sal de Vida due to equipment availability.
Sal de Vida, built with initial capacity of 15,000t/y of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE), achieved first production in 2Q26.
At Salar de Olaroz, in which Rio holds a 66.5% stake, output was affected by scheduled annual maintenance and lower lithium concentrations in the evaporation ponds as a result of adverse weather linked to the El Niño phenomenon.
At Fénix, the 1B expansion, which adds 10,000t/y of LCE and secures a 40-year life for the operation, is progressing well, although scheduled annual maintenance on lines 0 and 1A hit 3Q26 output. Fénix mainly uses direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology.
At Rincon, a US$2.5bn project, construction is ongoing. Earthworks and infrastructure works were carried out in 3Q26, and the camp expansion moved forward.
Rincon is slated to start production in 2028, followed by a three-year ramp-up to full capacity of 60,000t/y of battery-grade LCE over a 40-year life using selective adsorption DLE technology.
Two hubs 
Rio Tinto plans two lithium hubs in Argentina. One will be in Catamarca province, home to Fénix and Sal de Vida in the Salar del Hombre Muerto, which holds some 19Mt of LCE.
The second will span Salta and Jujuy provinces and comprise Rincon, Olaroz and Cauchari, around the Olaroz, Cauchari and Rincón salt flats, which together hold 37Mt of LCE.
Chile 
In Chile, Rio Tinto expects to finalize its binding agreements with state-owned companies between late 2026 and early 2027.
With Codelco, it will develop the Salar de Maricunga project through a joint venture in which Rio will hold a 49.9% stake, while with Enami it will develop Salares Altoandinos through another JV in which it will hold 51%.
Both projects are located in the Atacama region in northern Chile, and although they have high potential in terms of resource quality, development has been slower than expected.
Unlike in Argentina, lithium in Chile is not subject to mining concessions, so only the state or its companies can exploit it, along with private firms that obtain special contracts from the mining ministry.
"The non-concessibility of Chilean lithium is a barrier to production. The right approach would be to allow concessions to private companies under appropriate regulation," Santiago Montt, CEO of law firm Montt Group, told BNamericas.
Montt believes Chile's current lithium system neither protects the interests of indigenous peoples nor generates more jobs or wealth for the country.
Finance and market 
The results come amid a favorable lithium market. In 3Q26, LCE prices averaged US$19,000/t, supported by strong and growing demand from battery energy storage systems (BESS), according to Rio Tinto's latest report.
Rio has managed its capital efficiently and closed 3Q26 with agreements that have already allowed it to reallocate more than US$2bn to higher-return opportunities, including lithium sales contracts with prepayments.

North Korean IT fraud case cites crypto transfers in alleged $3m scheme 
By Lawrence Mondal 
Oct 13, 2026 at 9:00 PM UTC 
Edited by Lawrence Mondal 
News
The payment rail for your crypto. One card. Every chain. No KYC. Spend with Apple Pay or Google Pay in 180+ countries. 
Share 
Link copied 
The U.S. Department of Justice has announced the arrests of two Americans accused of helping North Korean IT workers obtain jobs at more than 70 U.S. companies in a scheme that generated approximately $3 million.
Summary 
Two Americans face fraud, money laundering, and identity theft conspiracy charges under an Ohio indictment.
More than 70 U.S. employers allegedly hired overseas workers using stolen or fabricated identities.
Approximately 187 laptops and remote-control devices were seized during a separate operation across Texas.
Cryptocurrency transfers appear in the indictment’s account of how participants moved employment earnings overseas.
The U.S. Department of Justice announced on Oct. 13 that authorities arrested Michael James Bostelle of Pennsylvania and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo of Texas under an indictment in the Northern District of Ohio.
Under the filing, both men face charges of conspiracy to commit wire and mail fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and conspiracy to commit identity theft. Pena also faces an aggravated identity theft charge.
Alongside the arrests, the department disclosed searches at more than 40 Texas residences and the seizure of approximately 187 computer devices in an operation targeting suspected North Korean “laptop farms.”
You might also like:
Coinbase joins DOJ and UK crime agency to target West Africa scams 
DOJ indictment describes jobs obtained through false identities
According to the Ohio indictment, overseas workers secured remote IT positions by presenting stolen or fabricated identities while domestic facilitators supplied the equipment, addresses and financial accounts needed to support the deception.
Receiving employer-issued laptops at American homes, the alleged facilitators configured the computers for remote access so workers abroad could use company systems while appearing to work inside the United States.
Through remote-access software and other equipment, prosecutors allege, the overseas workers performed assignments on computers physically located at U.S. residences. Domestic participants then helped receive employment payments and transfer earnings overseas, according to the filing.
The indictment alleges that the operation compromised the identities of more than 25 U.S. people and caused false information to reach the Department of Homeland Security, Internal Revenue Service and Social Security Administration.
Beyond the approximately $3 million in worker revenue, the filing alleges that affected companies incurred at least $3 million in legal expenses, computer network repair costs and other losses.
Within the alleged network, prosecutors identify Ohio resident Trey Michael Nolte as a co-conspirator who is named but not charged in this indictment. The filing alleges that Nolte recruited, trained, and managed U.S.-based facilitators, including Bostelle, who received a share of the proceeds.
The department said all defendants remain presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.
Crypto transfers feature in the alleged payment network
In its account of the money movements, the indictment identifies cryptocurrency as one method participants used to transfer funds overseas.
Describing a July 8, 2024 conversation, the filing alleges that Nolte discussed using spreadsheets to manage transfers between bank accounts and virtual currencies before sending funds to defendant Sun Sheng Ming.
As crypto.news previously reported in September , a separate federal case resulted in the forfeiture of approximately $212,700 in stablecoins connected to North Korean IT worker payments.
In that case, U.S. District Judge Rudolph Contreras issued a Sept. 3 ruling covering funds in a wallet beginning with “0x81c4,” according to the report. Prosecutors traced approximately 158,123 USDC to at least 10 worker payment addresses and another 54,574 USDT to at least four such addresses.
The report said the ruling granted only part of a Justice Department request involving more than $7.74 million in digital assets. Contreras declined to grant forfeiture of the remaining property because the government had not adequately identified it in its public notice, leaving prosecutors able to submit another request.
Texas laptop farm searches seize 187 devices
Between Sep. 21 and Sep. 25, the FBI carried out searches and other enforcement actions at more than 40 Texas residences known or suspected to house laptop farms, according to the department.
Under “Operation Lonestar Roundup,” investigators seized approximately 187 laptops and keyboard, video, and mouse devices used to control computers remotely, the announcement said.
The department said the Northern District of Texas U.S. Attorney’s Office, FBI Dallas Field Office and FBI Cyber Division coordinated the operation, with assistance from federal prosecutors in Ohio.
For American businesses, U.S. Attorney David M. Toepfer described the charges as “an urgent alert to all U.S. companies to remain vigilant in their hiring practices.”
Earlier enforcement also produced prison terms for domestic facilitators. In its May 8 coverage of two laptop farm sentences , the outlet reported that Matthew Issac Knoot of Nashville and Erick Ntekereze Prince of New York each received 18 months in prison.
According to the Justice Department’s findings cited in that report, their separate schemes generated more than $1.2 million for North Korea and affected nearly 70 American companies.
In Knoot’s case, prosecutors said employers paid more than $250,000 to workers associated with his laptop farm and incurred more than $500,000 in audit and system repair costs. Prince was ordered to forfeit $89,000 paid to him by North Korean IT workers, the report said.
FBI warning details how Americans are recruited
In an Oct. 13 warning , the FBI said North Korean IT workers increasingly recruit Americans facing financial pressure to help conceal fraudulent employment.
According to the bureau, paid tasks can include attending interviews, appearing on camera during meetings, verifying false identities, providing access to professional accounts, and keeping employer-issued computers connected at home.
The advisory said workers have also begun spreading equipment across more residences, with fewer laptops at each location, to reduce disruption when one site is discovered.
For employers, the FBI recommended checking combinations of suspicious behavior throughout employment rather than relying on one name, document, or technical signal. The bureau cautioned that poorly calibrated checks could harm legitimate remote employees and people whose identities had been stolen.
The FBI also reported that some North Korean workers obtain jobs at Western companies and subcontract assignments to freelancers in Pakistan, India, Nigeria, and neighboring countries, paying them a fraction of the salary received from the employer.

content_text:
Rivian’s Mind Robotics snags Doug Field, ex-Tesla and Ford EV chief
Fred Lambert  | Oct 13 2026 - 12:40 pm PT 
18 Comments 
Source: Rivian 
Doug Field, the engineer who ran Tesla’s Model 3 program and later Ford’s entire EV operation, is now president of Mind Robotics, the industrial robotics startup Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe spun out of Rivian last year.
He lands at a company that has now raised more than $1 billion in under a year, and he’ll run product, engineering, and operations alongside Scaringe.
Field’s next job is robots
Field’s résumé reads like a tour of the most ambitious hardware programs in the industry. He was Tesla’s SVP of Engineering through the Model 3 launch, ran Apple’s car effort inside its Special Projects Group, and then spent nearly five years at Ford as chief EV, digital and design officer.
We reported in April that Ford was folding Field’s EV group into manufacturing as he left the company . Ford didn’t replace him with an outside hire, and his department ended up under COO Kumar Galhotra. Five months later, he has his next job.
Advertisement - scroll for more content 
In Mind’s announcement, Scaringe called Field “a remarkable leader with a track record of delivering new technologies in successful products,” adding that’s “exactly what Mind needs as we deploy robots into real factories and beyond.”
Field called the combination of AI and robotics “one of the most important—and difficult—engineering challenges of our time.”
A $1 billion war chest and a factory to practice in
Mind Robotics first surfaced as part of Rivian’s Q3 2025 earnings report , with a $115 million seed round led by Eclipse. The money has piled up fast since then:
$115 million seed, led by Eclipse (late 2025)
$500 million Series A, co-led by Accel and Andreessen Horowitz (March 2026)
$400 million round led by Kleiner Perkins (May 2026), which Reuters reported valued Mind at $3.4 billion
That’s roughly $1 billion for a company that hasn’t shown a product publicly. Mind says it’s building foundation models plus “purpose-built” robot hardware for dexterous manufacturing work. It hasn’t said whether any of that hardware is humanoid.
Mind’s real edge is its access. Rivian is a major shareholder and its launch customer, which gives the startup a live, high-volume auto plant to collect training data and deploy robots in. And that plant is busy: the R2 is ramping in Normal, Illinois, and Rivian delivered 19,248 vehicles in Q3 alone.
The Tesla comparison is unavoidable
Field’s hire puts Mind on a direct collision course with the program Tesla now uses to justify much of its valuation: Optimus.
Tesla’s track record there isn’t great. Elon Musk predicted about 10,000 Optimus robots built in 2025, with roughly 1,000 doing useful work in Tesla factories by year-end. In January, he admitted none were doing “useful work.” Tesla then ended Model S and Model X production at Fremont to convert those lines for Optimus, and it has pushed back the Optimus V3 reveal repeatedly . In July, Musk said production would be “extremely slow at first” .
Mind is taking a quieter route. No stage demos, no unit targets. Just robots trained on a real assembly line, with a customer that already owns a stake in the company.
Electrek’s Take
This is a smart hire.
Field is a hardware industrialization guy. That’s his whole career: taking a product that works in a lab and making it work at volume. The Model 3 got to mass production on his watch. It was messy, and he took a leave at the height of “production hell” in 2018 before leaving Tesla, but the car shipped and became the best-selling EV in the world for years.
Top comment by Belafonte 
Liked by 7 people 
Field also led the effort to build zonal architecture at Ford. That failed miserabaly and then he tried downplaying it by saying zonal architecture doesn't matter. 
This guy hasn't had any success in the past ten years and has actively advocated against the very technology that has kept Rivian afloat recently. Not a lot of confidence this hire will work out for Rivian.
View all comments 
His record since then is more mixed. The Apple car was canceled after he left. At Ford, Model e lost more than $5 billion in 2024 alone, and the company has since scaled back its EV ambitions. But the low-cost Universal EV Platform and the $30,000 midsize pickup coming out of Louisville in 2027 are his team’s work, and that’s the most promising thing Ford has going in EVs.
So why does Mind need him? Because foundation models are the easy part to fundraise on. Getting robot hardware reliable enough to run shifts in a car plant is where everyone, Tesla included, has struggled.
It also tells us how serious Scaringe is about this. He’s running Rivian through the most important launch in its history, plus Also and now Mind. Bringing in a president with Field’s profile is how you keep Mind from becoming a side project while focusing your needed attention on Rivian.

Boeing delivers 57 aircraft in September as orders surge to 165 jets
Deliveries reached their highest monthly level of 2026, with Turkish Airlines accounting for 100 orders and the 737 MAX leading production
Ricardo Meier 
October 13, 2026 17:58 
Boeing delivered 57 aircraft in September 2026, its highest monthly total of the year, an increase of 11.8% from the 51 jets delivered in August and 3.6% above the 55 recorded in September 2025. 
The U.S. aircraft manufacturer also secured 165 gross orders during the month, compared with just 15 in August. The increase was largely driven by Turkish Airlines, which ordered 100 Boeing 737 MAX passenger jets.
According to figures released on October 13, Boeing delivered 43 737 MAX aircraft, eight 787 Dreamliners, two 777 freighters and four 767s during September.
The company has delivered 475 aircraft in the first nine months of 2026, compared with 440 during the same period last year, an increase of 8%. The total includes 363 737 MAX jets, the highest number delivered by the program during the first nine months of any year.
September also brought Boeing's third-quarter deliveries to 161 aircraft, narrowly above the 160 recorded during the corresponding quarter of 2025.
Boeing 737 MAX 10 Aviation Capital Group 737 MAX leads deliveries
The 737 MAX accounted for approximately 75% of Boeing's September deliveries, with 43 aircraft handed over to airlines and leasing companies.
Southwest Airlines was the largest individual recipient, taking nine jets, followed by United Airlines with five and VietJet Air with four.
Flydubai and Norwegian Air each received three aircraft, while Singapore Airlines and Virgin Australia took one each.
Leasing companies accounted for another significant portion of the deliveries. AerCap received six 737 MAX jets, followed by Aviation Capital Group and Dubai Aerospace Enterprise with three each.

Freighter deliveries included two 777Fs, one each for Air China Cargo and FedEx Express, and a 767-300F for UPS.

The stock was recently down 7.5% at $461.50, recovering from an earlier drop of as much as 9% to $452.81. The decline marked its steepest intraday selloff since July 28. 
The weakness extended across the semiconductor equipment sector. KLA Corp. and Lam Research each fell about 4%, while ASML Holding declined 3%, with all three stocks recovering from their session lows. ASML is scheduled to report earnings Wednesday, putting the European chip-equipment maker's results and outlook in focus as investors assess the strength of semiconductor capital spending. 
Chief Executive Gary Dickerson expressed confidence that demand for computing power would continue to expand rapidly, supporting long-term investment in semiconductor manufacturing. However, the company stopped short of offering a specific forecast for wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending, a key indicator of demand for its chipmaking tools.

Dickerson pointed to several variables that could influence the industry's near-term trajectory, including available factory space, supply-chain constraints and the financing of energy infrastructure. Those factors could affect how quickly manufacturers translate growing demand into actual spending on production equipment. 
The distinction is important for Applied Materials and its peers. While AI-related demand is driving investment in advanced semiconductors, the timing of factory construction and equipment installations can determine when that spending translates into revenue. 
Applied Materials has also emphasized the role of AI within its own operations, arguing that the technology can improve performance and strengthen its competitive position. Dickerson described AI as fundamental to the company's competitiveness, reinforcing management's confidence in the longer-term opportunity even as it withheld a near-term industry estimate. 
ASML's upcoming results could provide another indication of whether AI-related demand is translating into sustained investment across the semiconductor supply chain. As the leading supplier of extreme ultraviolet lithography systems used to manufacture advanced chips, the company is closely watched for signals about demand from major chipmakers and their willingness to expand production capacity. 
Story Continues 
For Applied Materials, the lack of a WFE forecast leaves investors without a concrete benchmark against which to measure management's growth expectations. After this year's substantial rally, the reaction highlights a key challenge for semiconductor equipment stocks: strong AI demand does not necessarily translate into a predictable timetable for capital spending.

CoTec Holdings Corp. Notes HyproMag USA Secures Power and Advances Project Readiness for Texas Rare Earth Magnet Recycling and Manufacturing Hub
CoTec Holdings Corp. 
October 13, 2026 • 7 min read 
Power capacity secured with Oncor; contractor selection and permitting underway ahead of targeted H1 2027 commissioning of cutting and finishing operations and Phase 1 completion targeted for mid-2028 
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 13, 2026 / CoTec Holdings Corp. (TSXV:CTH)(OTCQX:CTHCF) (“CoTec” or the “Company”) notes the press release issued today by its joint venture, HyProMag USA, LLC (“HyProMag USA”), providing an update on development activities for its Texas Hub rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing project in Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas (the “Texas Hub”). Following the commencement of formal power supply discussions announced on June 22, 2026, i HyProMag USA has secured electrical power capacity with Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (“Oncor”) for the Texas Hub development and expects the facility’s electricity requirements to be supplied predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Key Highlights 
Power capacity secured: Power capacity secured with Oncor for both cutting and finishing operations and the Phase 1 development, with a pathway through a sub-station upgrade to provide power for Phase 2.
Contractor selection and permitting underway: Pegasus TSI, Inc. (“Pegasus”) has commenced contractor selection for cutting and finishing operations and Weston Solutions, Inc. (“Weston”) is advancing permitting activities.
Cutting and finishing operations targeted for H1 2027: Targeted commissioning of cutting and finishing operations in H1 2027 with the processing of neodymium iron boron (“NdFeB”) magnet blocks, initially supplied from HyProMag Group operations, to produce finished magnets.
Phase 1 development: Phase 1 development is targeted for completion in mid-2028 and is designed to produce approximately 550 tonnes per annum (“tpa”) of NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets and approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing approximately 1,034 tpa of total payable production.
Phase 2 development: Phase 2 development envisions expansion to approximately 1,526 tpa of total payable production.
Renewable energy supply: Electricity supply expected to be sourced predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Julian Treger, Chief Executive Officer of CoTec Holdings Corp., commented: “Securing power with Oncor, advancing permitting activities through Weston Solutions and commencing contractor selection are important milestones for the Texas Hub. Initial cutting and finishing operations in 2027 are expected to establish U.S. magnet finishing and qualification capabilities aligned with internationally recognized magnetic material and quality standards, while the full Phase 1 development will deliver integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing capacity. Together, these activities further de-risk the project and demonstrate continued progress towards establishing a domestic and sustainable rare earth magnet supply chain in the United States.” 
Cutting and Finishing Operations 
Cutting and finishing operations in 2027 comprise the initial magnet finishing and qualification facility, enabling production and qualification of finished NdFeB magnets using magnet blocks supplied from HyProMag Group operations. The facility is designed to process NdFeB magnet blocks and support qualification of finished magnets in accordance with ASTM A977/A977M, the national classification standard for magnetic materials, together with quality management systems aligned with ISO 9001 and customer-specific quality, performance and traceability requirements. The objective is to establish qualification capabilities that meet the requirements of U.S. customers and establish a strategic training facility for the finishing of NdFeB magnets in advance of the main Texas Hub developments.
Permitting and Contractor Selection 
Weston is advancing permitting activities for the Texas Hub, while HyProMag USA’s engineering partner Pegasus has commenced a Request for Quotation (“RFQ”) process for the selection of a general contractor for cutting and finishing operations. Pegasus and BBA USA Inc. are HyProMag USA’s U.S.-based engineering, procurement and construction management firms.
Phase 1 and Phase 2 Development 
Phase 1 represents the first integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing stage of the Texas Hub and is designed to produce approximately 550 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets, together with approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,034 tpa. Upon completion of Phase 2, the Texas Hub is expected to produce approximately 1,048 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and cylinders, together with approximately 478 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,526 tpa.
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for NdFeB magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (“HPMS”) technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA delivers faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks – including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap – enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing.
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited, which is owned 79.4% by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and 20.6% by CoTec.
For more information on HyProMag USA, please visit www.hypromagusa.com 
About CoTec 
CoTec Holdings Corp. (TSXV:CTH)(OTCQX:CTHCF) is redefining the future of resource extraction and recycling. Focused on rare earth magnets and strategic materials, CoTec integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.
CoTec’s mission is clear: accelerate the energy transition while strengthening strategic mineral supply chains for the countries we operate in. By investing in and deploying disruptive technologies, the Company delivers capital-efficient, scalable solutions that transform marginal assets, tailings, waste streams, and recycled products into high-value critical minerals.
From its HyProMag USA magnet recycling joint venture in Texas, to iron tailings reprocessing and reclamation in Québec, to next-generation copper and iron solutions backed by global majors, CoTec is building a diversified portfolio with long-term growth, rapid cash flow potential, and high barriers to entry. The result is a differentiated platform at the intersection of technology, sustainability, and strategic materials.

That operation will not initially manufacture magnet blocks from recycled material in Texas. Instead, it is designed to cut, finish and qualify NdFeB magnet blocks supplied from other HyProMag Group operations .
The facility is intended to establish US finishing capability, customer qualification processes and workforce training ahead of the larger integrated development.

Importantly, those figures are design capacities rather than current production or confirmed future output .
CoTec chief executive Julian Treger said securing power, advancing permitting and commencing contractor selection further de-risk the project and support the goal of establishing a domestic US rare earth magnet supply chain.
For investors, the significance is that the Texas Hub is moving from engineering and planning towards site infrastructure, permitting and contractor procurement .
The next tangible milestones are the award of construction contracts, permitting progress and successful commissioning of the initial cutting and finishing operation in H1 2027 , followed by execution of the larger integrated Phase 1 development targeted for 2028.

Sponsors and strategics vie in second round for Evonik’s C4 division
13th October 2026 09:09 AM
By Patrick Harris , Philipp Fischer , Georgina Barnard and Peter Cromberge 
AURELIUS, ICIG and AEQUITA are among suitors 
Final bids for hydrocarbons unit due next month
Disposal progresses amid BASF takeover furore
German chemicals conglomerate Evonik Industries is engaged with several private equity sponsors and strategics as it advances the sale of its C4 division, five sources familiar with the matter said.
Final bids for the performance intermediaries subsidiary, which is also known as Oxeno, are due in November, two of the sources said.
Sponsors AURELIUS Group and AEQUITA, and privately-owned International Chemicals Investor Group (ICIG) are among those groups in the second round and still in contention, three of the sources said. Other sponsors and strategics also remain in the fray, another of the sources added. ICIG’s interest is driven in part by the potential to unlock synergies with the superabsorbents business it previously acquired from Evonik in 2024, a banker following the deal noted.
AEQUITA could likewise unlock synergies by acquiring the C4 division, as previously noted by this news service.
C4’s performance intermediates are produced at the Marl Chemical Park, in Germany, for which it sources feedstock from the nearby Gelschenkirchen refinery. The refinery, which was acquired by Klesch Group from BP in a transaction that completed on 3 August, also hosts the production facilities of AEQUITA’s recently acquired olefin business, now renamed Velogy.
The listed Essen-based specialty chemicals manufacturer was expected to collect first-round bids for C4 at the end of August, as reported by this news service.
On 21 September, this news service first reported that Evonik was in discussions with its larger German peer, BASF, on a potential takeover. This was confirmed by Evonik on 28 September following further press reports.
On 22 September, the company noted that the sale of C4 was progressing as planned, in addition to a sale of its infrastructure business, Syneqt, but provided no more details on the disposals.
The sale of C4, which is codenamed Project Abraham, is being advised on the sellside by Deutsche Bank and first came to market earlier this year, as per a report by this news service. The same report noted that the business is highly cyclical and generates EBITDA of less than EUR 30m.
Evonik first announced plans to dispose of the performance intermediates business in 2022, as part of a portfolio finetuning.
The unit sits within Evonik’s Infrastructure segment, which reported 2Q26 adjusted EBITDA of EUR 100m, an increase from EUR 47m in 1Q26, driven by higher margins for C4 caused by the Iran conflict.
The C4 unit, which processes raw ‘crack C4’ hydrocarbons used in the automotive, rubber, plastics, and cosmetic products industries has long been a divestment candidate.
Evonik operates across three core segments globally: Infrastructure; Advanced Technologies, which manufactures polymers and feed additives; and Custom Solutions, which serves end-markets, including cleaning and pharmaceuticals.
Frankfurt-listed Evonik has a market capitalisation of EUR 9.79bn.
Evonik, Deutsch Bank, and AURELIUS declined to comment. AEQUITA and ICIG did not respond to requests for comment.

CoTec Holdings Corp. Notes HyproMag USA Secures Power and Advances Project Readiness for Texas Rare Earth Magnet Recycling and Manufacturing Hub
Investing News Network 
October 13, 2026 
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 13, 2026 / CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) ("CoTec" or the "Company") notes the press release issued today by its joint venture, HyProMag USA, LLC ("HyProMag USA"), providing an update on development activities for its Texas Hub rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing project in Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas (the "Texas Hub"). Following the commencement of formal power supply discussions announced on June 22, 2026, i HyProMag USA has secured electrical power capacity with Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC ("Oncor") for the Texas Hub development and expects the facility's electricity requirements to be supplied predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Key Highlights 
Power capacity secured: Power capacity secured with Oncor for both cutting and finishing operations and the Phase 1 development, with a pathway through a sub-station upgrade to provide power for Phase 2.
Contractor selection and permitting underway: Pegasus TSI, Inc. ("Pegasus") has commenced contractor selection for cutting and finishing operations and Weston Solutions, Inc. ("Weston") is advancing permitting activities.
Cutting and finishing operations targeted for H1 2027: Targeted commissioning of cutting and finishing operations in H1 2027 with the processing of neodymium iron boron ("NdFeB") magnet blocks, initially supplied from HyProMag Group operations, to produce finished magnets.
Phase 1 development: Phase 1 development is targeted for completion in mid-2028 and is designed to produce approximately 550 tonnes per annum ("tpa") of NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets and approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing approximately 1,034 tpa of total payable production.
Phase 2 development: Phase 2 development envisions expansion to approximately 1,526 tpa of total payable production.
Renewable energy supply: Electricity supply expected to be sourced predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Julian Treger, Chief Executive Officer of CoTec Holdings Corp. , commented: "Securing power with Oncor, advancing permitting activities through Weston Solutions and commencing contractor selection are important milestones for the Texas Hub. Initial cutting and finishing operations in 2027 are expected to establish U.S. magnet finishing and qualification capabilities aligned with internationally recognized magnetic material and quality standards, while the full Phase 1 development will deliver integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing capacity. Together, these activities further de-risk the project and demonstrate continued progress towards establishing a domestic and sustainable rare earth magnet supply chain in the United States." 
Cutting and Finishing Operations 
Cutting and finishing operations in 2027 comprise the initial magnet finishing and qualification facility, enabling production and qualification of finished NdFeB magnets using magnet blocks supplied from HyProMag Group operations. The facility is designed to process NdFeB magnet blocks and support qualification of finished magnets in accordance with ASTM A977/A977M, the national classification standard for magnetic materials, together with quality management systems aligned with ISO 9001 and customer-specific quality, performance and traceability requirements. The objective is to establish qualification capabilities that meet the requirements of U.S. customers and establish a strategic training facility for the finishing of NdFeB magnets in advance of the main Texas Hub developments.
Permitting and Contractor Selection 
Weston is advancing permitting activities for the Texas Hub, while HyProMag USA's engineering partner Pegasus has commenced a Request for Quotation ("RFQ") process for the selection of a general contractor for cutting and finishing operations. Pegasus and BBA USA Inc. are HyProMag USA's U.S.-based engineering, procurement and construction management firms.
Phase 1 and Phase 2 Development 
Phase 1 represents the first integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing stage of the Texas Hub and is designed to produce approximately 550 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets, together with approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,034 tpa. Upon completion of Phase 2, the Texas Hub is expected to produce approximately 1,048 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and cylinders, together with approximately 478 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,526 tpa.
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for NdFeB magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap ("HPMS") technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA delivers faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks - including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap - enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing.
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited, which is owned 79.4% by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and 20.6% by CoTec.
For more information on HyProMag USA, please visit www.hypromagusa.com 
About CoTec 
CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) is redefining the future of resource extraction and recycling. Focused on rare earth magnets and strategic materials, CoTec integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.
CoTec's mission is clear: accelerate the energy transition while strengthening strategic mineral supply chains for the countries we operate in. By investing in and deploying disruptive technologies, the Company delivers capital-efficient, scalable solutions that transform marginal assets, tailings, waste streams, and recycled products into high-value critical minerals.
From its HyProMag USA magnet recycling joint venture in Texas, to iron tailings reprocessing and reclamation in Québec, to next-generation copper and iron solutions backed by global majors, CoTec is building a diversified portfolio with long-term growth, rapid cash flow potential, and high barriers to entry. The result is a differentiated platform at the intersection of technology, sustainability, and strategic materials.
For more information, please visit www.cotec.ca

​Overview
CoTec Holdings (TSXV:CTH, OTCQX:CTHCF) is redefining the future of rare earth magnet recycling and strategic material extraction. Its portfolio spans rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing, iron tailings reprocessing and emerging copper extraction technologies, all directed at fast-tracking revenue generation and reducing energy and capital intensity compared to conventional mining.
Key Technologies
The company’s modular, capital-efficient model — including joint ventures and strategic subsidiaries — positions it for scalable growth and streamlined execution. With significant advancement in project execution, one completed feasibility study and a second underway, CoTec is moving toward transforming its technology suite into commercial operations.
Why Invest in CoTec?
Differentiated Growth Model: Capital-light strategy deploying modular technologies at brownfield assets to accelerate timelines and reduce capital intensity.
Strategic Commodity Exposure: Exposure to rare earths, iron and copper — key materials for electrification, AI infrastructure, robotics and other critical supply chains.
Execution-Stage Portfolio: Three projects advancing through feasibility, engineering and financing stages.
Aligned Leadership: Strong insider ownership and experienced management with deep mining and capital markets expertise.
Lower-Carbon Production: Technologies designed to reduce energy use, water consumption and emissions relative to conventional mining.
Investor Insight
CoTec Holdings combines proprietary processing technologies with undervalued and legacy resource assets to create high-margin opportunities across rare earths , iron and copper sectors. With three execution-stage projects and a significant discount to attributable NAV, CoTec provides differentiated exposure to strategic minerals tied to electrification, AI infrastructure and supply-chain security.
Company Highlights
Technology-Driven Value Creatio n: Deploys proprietary, low-carbon processing technologies to extract value from waste, tailings and marginal deposits that traditional mining overlooks.
Execution-Stage Projects : Advancing three core assets — HyProMag USA rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing, the Lac Jeannine iron tailings project, and MagIron iron ore feedstock, concentrator and pelletizer — with clear development pathways.
Expanding Rare Earth Footprint: HyProMag USA advances its scalable US hub-and-spoke rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing roll-out using the Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (“HPMS”) technology, with Inserma HDD pre-processing machines on site in South Carolina and Nevada, supporting feedstock preparation and future commissioning.
Strategic Copper Focus : Established a new subsidiary, CoTec Copper , to accelerate targeted investment in copper tailings and copper sulfide deposits globally, leveraging CoTec’s core technologies to unlock value.
Iron Ore & Green Steel : Advancing iron tailings reprocessing at Lac Jeannine and supporting the restart of the MagIron pellet project to supply high-grade feedstock for low-carbon steel production.
Strong Insider Support : Management and insiders own a majority of shares, reinforcing alignment with long-term value creation.
Experienced Leadership : Board and executives bring deep mining, technology and capital markets experience from leading global organizations.
Key Technologies and Assets
HyProMag USA Project
HyProMag USA is CoTec’s flagship rare earth recycling platform and a cornerstone of its strategy to localize critical mineral supply chains. The project deploys Hydrogen Processing of Magnetic Scrap technology to recover neodymium iron boron magnets from end-of-life electronics and industrial equipment through a simplified hydrogen-based process that bypasses traditional chemical separation and smelting. This short-loop approach dramatically reduces energy use, water consumption and emissions while lowering operating complexity and cost.
The company’s phased development plan is targeting commissioning of its initial finished neodymium-iron-boron magnet production equipment in Texas in 2027. Up to 20 tonnes of magnet blocks supplied by HyProMag Group in the United Kingdom and Germany will be shaped and finished at HyProMag USA's operations for U.S. customers. Integrated Texas Hub's Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap section targeted for Q2 2028.
Watch an overview of HyProMag USA here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v0d7rKdwu_s 
Highlights 
CoTec holds a 60.3 percent economic interest.
Bankable Feasibility Study supports a single hub after-tax NPV of US$797 million at forecast prices or US$416 million at current prices with recent updated economics published June 22, 2026
Capex estimated at US$152 million per hub.
First revenue targeted for Q2 2028.
Expansion concept envisions three hubs producing 4,656 tonnes annually with potential NPV of up to US$2.2 billion.
Inserma pre-processing machines have arrived at South Carolina and Nevada facilities to support feedstock preparation and scale-up of the hub-and-spoke rollout.
Integrated Texas Hub's Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap section targeted for Q2 2028.
Lac Jeannine Iron Project
The Lac Jeannine project is an advanced tailings reprocessing initiative designed to transform legacy mining waste into high-purity iron concentrate for steelmaking. By leveraging existing infrastructure and modern processing technologies, the project aims to unlock value from previously discarded material while simultaneously advancing environmental reclamation. This approach aligns economic return with environmental remediation and supports domestic iron supply.
Metallurgical test work has demonstrated the project's ability to produce a high-purity iron concentrate grading in excess of the standard 67 percent. CEO Julian Treger said that this is a validation resource’s quality and the effectiveness of the company’s processing strategy. “(It also supports) our vision of transforming a historic environmental liability into a strategic asset capable of supporting the global transition to lower-carbon steel production."
Highlights 
Inferred resource of about 71 Mt at 6.8 percent iron.
After-tax NPV7 of US$91.9 million and IRR of 29.6 percent from the recently reported Mineral Resource Estimate announced on Jun. 16, 2026
Initial capex estimated at US$65 million.
15-year mine life
A 41 percent increase in the resource according to the 2026 PEA , with a global increase in total iron grade from 6.7 to 6.8 percent.
MagIron Project
MagIron represents a restart-ready brownfield iron ore deposit, concentrator and pelletizer project in Minnesota and Indianna, that benefits from an estimated $660m in historical capital investment, targeting the production of direct-reduction grade pellets for low-carbon steelmaking. The project benefits from extensive existing infrastructure and prior capital investment, allowing rapid recommissioning compared with greenfield developments. Its strategic positioning targets rising demand for domestically sourced feedstock for electric arc furnaces and decarbonized steel production.
Senior leadership changes have been made to support the ongoing development of MagIron, especially regarding restarting its iron ore concentrator in Minnesota and pellet plant in Indiana. 
Highlights 
CoTec owns approximately 17 percent.
Definitive Feasibility Study shows after-tax NPV of about US$1.60 billion and IRR about 27.6 percent.
Average annual production is about 2.6 Mt DR-grade pellets.
Life of mine is about 32 years.
Payback period is about 3 years and 7 months.
Raised additional capital at a pre-money valuation of US$550 million from existing shareholders
CoTec Copper
CoTec Copper is a dedicated subsidiary created to accelerate the company’s exposure to copper, one of the most strategically important electrification metals. The unit focuses on acquiring and advancing copper tailings projects and sulphide deposits, particularly in historically productive mining jurisdictions where modern processing technologies can unlock additional value from previously uneconomic material. It leverages CoTec’s existing technology portfolio to enhance recoveries and lower operating costs.
Highlights 
Targets assets in Tier 1 mining regions across the United States, Australia and Africa.
Focuses on both tailings reprocessing and sulphide copper deposits.
Designed as a scalable growth platform to expand CoTec’s copper exposure.
Binding Solutions
Binding Solutions provides a cold agglomeration technology that converts ultrafine mineral waste into ISO-compliant pellets or briquettes suitable for industrial use, particularly in green steel production. Unlike traditional pelletizing processes that rely on high-temperature furnaces, this approach operates at low temperatures, drastically reducing energy consumption and emissions while enabling monetization of low-grade or waste materials.
Highlights 
Uses about 95 percent less energy than conventional pelletizing.
Generates about 98 percent fewer emissions.
Applicable to iron and other mineral fines.
Ceibo
Ceibo’s oxidative heap-leaching technology is designed to improve copper recovery from sulphide ores such as chalcopyrite, which account for the majority of global copper reserves but are traditionally difficult and costly to process. The process enhances recovery rates while lowering environmental impact and capital intensity, potentially transforming the economics of many existing copper assets.
Highlights 
Potential recovery improvement from about 31 percent via traditional leaching/concentration to approximately 70-80 percent.
Targets refractory sulphide deposits often considered uneconomic.
CoTec holds a minority equity interest and a seat on the technical advisory board.
Completed Series B C$30M financing led by Energy Impact Partners to fund the scaling of the technology.
WaveCracker
WaveCracker is a microwave-assisted mineral processing technology being advanced in collaboration with McGill University. The system uses targeted microwave energy to weaken mineral structures before conventional processing, improving metal liberation, reducing reagent consumption and lowering overall processing costs.
Highlights 
Focused initially on copper sulphide applications.
Designed to accelerate leaching and recovery kinetics.
Builds on more than 30 years of microwave mineral processing research.
Salter Cyclones
Salter Cyclones technology uses multi-gravity separators to recover ultra-fine minerals from tailings streams that traditional processing methods cannot efficiently capture. By enabling recovery of metals from waste material, the system creates new revenue streams while reducing environmental liabilities associated with tailings storage.
Highlights 
Applicable to iron, manganese and other fine mineral commodities.
Exclusive global rights for iron applications and regional exclusivity for manganese during the initial agreement period.
Converts waste into high-grade concentrates suitable for market.
Management Team
Julian Treger - Chief Executive Officer and Director
Julian Treger previously served as the CEO of Anglo Pacific Group before establishing Audley Capital Partners. At Audley, Treger directed the team through acquisitions totaling $570 million and achieved a realized Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 38 percent. Treger continues to serve as the chairman of Audley Capital and holds both a BA and an MBA from Harvard.
Abraham Jonker - Chief Financial Officer
Abraham Jonker has 30 years of experience in mining finance. He previously served as the Lead Independent Director at Mandalay Resources and has been instrumental in leading over $750 million in equity and debt raises. Jonker is a Chartered Accountant in the UK, Canada, and South Africa and holds a Master's in Tax from Rand Afrikaans University.
John Singleton - Chief Operating Officer
John Singleton possesses over 25 years of experience in mining. His career began at De Beers, and he has since held senior leadership roles at Centamin and Rio Tinto. Singleton is a Fellow of the Royal Geological Society and holds degrees from Imperial College London and the University of Bristol.
John McGagh - Technology Consultant
John McGagh has more than 35 years of experience in digital transformation across various industries. He served as the head of innovation at Rio Tinto and is currently the chief digital officer at Snowy Hydro. McGagh is an adjunct professor at the University of Queensland and a Fellow of the Australian Academy of Technology Science and Engineering.
Eugene Hercun - VP Finance & Investor Relations
Eugene Hercun is a CPA, CA, with 15 years of varied experience in mining finance. He has led metal sales negotiations for more than $200 million annually and holds Level 1 of the CFA designation.
Board of Directors
Lucio Genovese, Independent Chairman
Lucio Genovese currently serves as the CEO of Nage Capital and as the chairman of Ferrexpo plc. He previously held senior roles at Glencore , including CEO of the CIS region. Genovese is a Chartered Accountant with degrees in Commerce and Accounting from the University of Witwatersrand.
Tom Albanese, Non - Executive Director
Tom Albanese is the former CEO of Rio Tinto and Vedanta Resources. He serves as lead independent director of Nevada Copper and as a director at Franco-Nevada Corporation. Albanese holds Master's and Bachelor's degrees from the University of Alaska Fairbanks.
Robert (Bob) Harward - Non-Executive Director
Robert Harward is a retired US Navy Vice Admiral (SEAL) and former deputy commander of US Central Command. He served on the US National Security Council and held senior strategy roles at Lockheed Martin and Shield AI.
Erez Ichilov - Non-executive Director
Erez Ichilov previously served as managing director at Traxys Projects, where he led investments in companies such as Nouveau Monde Graphite, Talon Metals, and Li-Cycle. Ichilov holds LLB and MBA degrees.
Sharon Fay - Non-executive Director
Sharon Fay previously served as head of equities and head of responsibility at AllianceBernstein. She built the firm's Corporate Responsibility and Responsible Investment teams. Fay is a Chartered Financial Analyst with a BA from Brown and an MBA from Harvard.

Major indexes are trading on either side of the aisle this morning, as investors parse through a huge batch of big bank earnings and a heavy selloff from the Kospi in South Korea, as valuation concerns expand. Futures on the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) are up nearly 500 points, while the Nasdaq-100 Index (NDX) is suffering a more than 200-point setback, and S&P 500 Index (SPX) futures inch lower. September's existing home sales data is also on the docket, due out at 10 a.m. ET.
Continue reading for more on today's market, including: 
October could bring midterm election gains , per Schaeffer's Senior V.P. of Research Todd Salamone.
Software stock cools off after hitting its annual top .
Plus, two blue-chip stocks after earnings; and memory stock giant takes a hit.
5 Things You Need to Know Today
The Cboe Option Exchange saw roughly 2.2 million call contracts and 1.4 million put contracts traded on Monday. The single-session equity put/call ratio rose to 0.62, while the 21-day moving average remained at 0.59. 
UnitedHealth Group Inc (NYSE:UNH) stock is up 4.9% before the open, after the health insurance giant posted a third-quarter earnings and revenue beat.
