JPMorgan Chase & Co (NYSE:JPM) is up 1% ahead of the bell, rising after posting a rise in profit, brushing over the company's third-quarter miss. If these gains continue into the open, JPM will be headed for a fourth-straight daily win, following a bounce off three-month lows last week.
Western Digital Corp (NASDQ:WDC)  is off 7.7% in pre-market trading, as the memory sector takes a brutal hit amid South Korea's Kospi valuation-triggered selloff. WDC hit is lowest mark since April just yesterday, though the shares remain 124% higher year to date.
Big bank stocks will continue to be the main headliner for this week.
Interest Rate Update Drags Memory Stocks, Kospi 
Asian markets were mixed on Tuesday. China's Shanghai Composite added 1%, as September exports showed accelerating growth and continued momentum. South Korea's Kospi plunged 5.5%, amid a pullback in memory stocks and AI valuation concerns, while President Lee Jae Myung signaled that interest rates may need to rise in the near future. Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained 0.3%, while Japan's Nikkei shed 1.8%.
European bourses are modestly higher at midday, recovering from earlier weakness in chip stocks. At last glance, London's FTSE 100 was up 0.5%, while France's CAC 40 and Germany's DAX were trading 0.01% and 0.07% higher, respectively.

Vestas Completes Taiwan's First V236-15.0 MW™ Offshore Wind Turbine Hub Assembly Ahead of Schedule; Achieves Milestone in CIP's Fengmiao 1 Project
Share
Vestas has completed the assembly of Taiwan's first V236-15.0 MW™ offshore wind turbine hub , marking a milestone in the introduction of next-generation offshore wind technology to Taiwan. The achievement was supported by steady progress on the CIP's 495 MW Fengmiao 1 Offshore Wind Farm (渢妙一期) , the first project in Taiwan's Round 3 offshore wind zonal development to secure full financing and commence construction.
Since entering Taiwan in 2000, Vestas has established a strong presence in both onshore and offshore wind, employing more than 500 people locally. The successful assembly combined the company's global technological expertise with the capabilities of its Taiwan team, which has developed specialized skills in quality management, testing and safety procedures for critical turbine components. The hub was delivered ahead of schedule, with safety and quality remaining top priorities.
Vestas Asia-Pacific President Purvin Patel said, "Completing Taiwan's first V236 hub assembly is an important milestone for Vestas. It demonstrates that our Taiwan team can deliver safely, to a high standard of quality and on schedule. The skills and experience gained through this work will also serve as an important foundation for the continued development of Taiwan's offshore wind industry."
The V236-15.0 MW™ is Vestas' flagship offshore wind turbine platform, designed to support standardized, large-scale production and improve project execution efficiency. Upon completion of Fengmiao 1, Vestas' cumulative offshore wind capacity delivered in Taiwan is expected to reach approximately 1.7 GW, reinforcing the company's long-term commitment to Taiwan's offshore wind sector and its contribution to the country's energy security.
【About Vestas】 
Vestas is a global leader in sustainable energy solutions, specializing in the design, manufacturing, installation, and servicing of onshore and offshore wind turbines. The company has installed more than 207 GW of wind power capacity across 88 countries worldwide and currently services wind turbines with a combined capacity of more than 165 GW. 
Leveraging industry-leading data analytics capabilities and a global service network, Vestas continues to deliver efficient and reliable wind energy solutions to its customers. With more than 36,000 employees worldwide, Vestas is committed to advancing energy security and building a more sustainable future.

Decreasing process variability in fluid management systems
Published Oct. 13, 2026
By 
Chris McCoy, Senior product manager, Global Batch 360
Share

Cytiva

SPONSORED CONTENT BY 
Connectivity represents something much larger than component compatibility. It is the foundation for standardization, predictability and control. Every connection influences whether a process can be reliably transferred, consistently executed and confidently scaled. When done right, early process decisions can translate to accelerated progress across development and scale‑up. 
For organizations developing mAbs, mRNA therapies, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), multispecific antibodies and cell therapies—process robustness, technology transfer and manufacturing scalability increasingly rely on the effectiveness of single-use assemblies. Yet one factor remains consistently underestimated: physical connectivity or fluid management. The tubing, connectors, sensors and fluid transfer paths that link unit operations together can have a profound impact on flow behavior, process consistency, scalability and regulatory compliance. 
As therapies become more complex and manufacturing networks expand across sites, every connection point in a process becomes a potential source of variability. These connectors are not merely passive components. Together, they define how material moves through a process, how consistently the process performs and how easily it can be transferred, replicated and scaled. 
The challenge is that bioprocesses may evolve over time based on modality-specific requirements, which means incorporating new equipment or retrofitting technologies. A straightforward process can then become a patchwork of connection types, tubing dimensions, materials and supplier specifications. As manufacturers document deviations and are forced to troubleshoot flow inconsistencies and validate component changes, they’re left repeatedly asking the question, Why does this process behave differently here than it did there? 
Physical connectivity is not simply about ensuring components fit together, it’s ensuring that the entire manufacturing system functions together. The performance of a process is influenced not just by a connector, tubing segment or flow kit, but by how all the elements of the fluid pathway interact as an integrated system. Small decisions made upstream can have significant consequences downstream. In this article, we discuss a few examples of why connectors can’t be chosen with only one piece of the process in mind. 
End-to-end fluid management: why flow kits can’t be designed in isolation 
In modern biomanufacturing, every transfer step must behave as expected. Unexpected flow behavior can result in batch delays, troubleshooting efforts, product loss or deviations that impact manufacturing efficiency. Yet flow path design decisions are often evaluated at the equipment level rather than at the process level. Because fluids do not recognize equipment boundaries, the performance of a flow kit is influenced by the entire transfer system surrounding it. Designing flow kits in isolation can therefore create hidden risks that are not discovered until the process is operating under real manufacturing conditions. 
A common misconception in bioprocessing is that a flow kit can be designed around the requirements of the processing unit alone. The entire fluid transfer pathway within this skid, from the origin through the flow kit and to the destination, must be considered. Take, for example, a chromatography skid with a flow kit designed around a bore size of “X.” In chromatography, bore size refers to the internal diameter (ID) of the tubing. At first glance, it may seem reasonable to use X as the bore size through the system. However, many manufacturing facilities operate with long transfer distances between buffer preparation areas and process skids. Over those distances, pressure losses can become significant. 
In these cases, MSAT and process engineers may intentionally specify a bore size larger than X, even though this is larger than the bore of the system flow path itself. The larger tubing diameter helps reduce pressure drop across long runs, minimizing the risk of cavitation, tubing collapse, pump performance issues and process interruptions. 
A successful design requires consideration of the entire transfer pathway, including: 
Mixer bag and tote outlet sizes 
Tubing diameters across transfer distances 
Transfer set configurations 
Pump requirements 
Pressure-drop limitations 
Aseptic connector sizing 
Final flow kit geometry 
What appears to be a simple tubing selection decision is often a system-level engineering decision. For organizations seeking predictable manufacturing performance, every connection point must be considered within the context of the complete process. A well-designed fluid management strategy accounts not only for the flow kit itself, but also for the entire network of components that deliver fluid to and from the process (Fig 1).

Many connectivity challenges are not discovered when a component is selected. They are discovered during scale-up, technology transfer or commercial manufacturing. Cytiva works alongside you to design, evaluate and optimize manufacturing systems with the goal of reducing complexity, improving standardization and creating more robust processes from development through commercial production. content_text:
FDA approves Asahi Kasei's Hovilpri for treatment-refractory HSV infections
Edited by Robert McTiernan · October 12, 2026 · 2 min read 
The US FDA has approved Hovilpri (pritelivir) for mucocutaneous lesions caused by herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection refractory, with or without documented resistance, to acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir in immunocompromised adults, according to Asahi Kasei Therapeutics. ​ 
As noted by Asahi , the approval marks the first HSV therapy with a novel mechanism of action to reach the US market in nearly 30 years. It also gives patients access to an oral alternative to existing treatments for refractory HSV infection, which have often required intravenous administration and can present significant tolerability and treatment-management challenges.
Pritelivir inhibits the HSV helicase-primase complex, blocking viral DNA unwinding and primer synthesis independently of viral thymidine kinase activation, retaining activity against thymidine kinase-deficient strains that resist nucleoside analogs. The drug is formulated as 100 mg oral tablets; the label carries warnings regarding drug interactions with acid-reducing agents, which may reduce pritelivir exposure and risk resistance, and notes that pritelivir is a breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) inhibitor that may increase plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates.
The approval is supported by Part C of PRIOH-1 (NCT03073967), a Phase III randomized, open-label trial enrolling 101 immunocompromised adults with mucocutaneous HSV refractory to standard antivirals. Complete lesion healing by Day 28 was achieved in 63% of pritelivir-treated participants versus 34% receiving Investigator's Choice treatment, an adjusted difference of 28.4% (p=0.0047), the company reported.
Adverse reactions occurred in 22% of pritelivir-treated participants versus 54% in the Investigator's Choice arm; discontinuations due to adverse drug reactions were 2% versus 20%, respectively, with headache the most common adverse reaction at 6%.
The approval marks a key milestone for Asahi Kasei following its EUR 780 million acquisition of AiCuris Anti-infective Cures AG in April 2026, which brought pritelivir into its portfolio. The drug was a principal asset underpinning the acquisition.

Asahi Kasei Acquisition Pays Off With FDA Approval for Novel Herpes Drug 
Asahi Kasei’s Hovilpri is now approved for treating lesions caused by herpes simplex virus infection. This daily pill came from the $919 million acquisition of AiCuris Anti-Infective Cures.
By Frank Vinluan on October 12, 2026 10:44 am 
Share 
Share Options 
Share a link to this article
Copy Link 
Copy Link 
Email 
Facebook 
LinkedIn 
X 
Patients with lesions caused by herpes simplex virus have a new FDA-approved treatment option, an oral antiviral drug from Asahi Kasei.
The late Friday regulatory decision covers the treatment of adults whose lesions do not respond to the three oral antivirals that make up the current standard of care. Asahi Kasei’s once-daily pill, known in development as pritelivir, will be commercialized under the brand name Hovilpri.
In people with healthy immune systems, herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection is often asymptomatic or causes mild disease. But in people with weakened immune symptoms — those who have undergone a transplant procedure, or patients with HIV, cancer, or autoimmune disorders — HSV infection can occur more frequently and with greater severity. While oral antivirals are available to treat HSV, viral mutations can lead to resistance to these older drugs. There are alternative treatment options, but they require intravenous dosing.
presented by 
Sponsored Post 
From Blind Spots to Better Outcomes: How SNF Data Transparency Strengthens LTSS 
What if health plans could identify member decline before an avoidable hospitalization occurs? Real-time clinical visibility into long-stay SNF members uncovers risk earlier and drives better outcomes. 
By Anna Keith, Vice President of LTSS Product & Strategy at Centene Corporation, and Phyllis Wojtusik, RN, Executive Vice President of Value-Based Care at Real Time Medical Systems 
Hovilpri gives patients the choice of an oral drug with a different mechanism of action. This small molecule is designed to inhibit a complex of enzymes key to the synthesis of viral DNA. The drug was developed to treat both types of HSV, HSV-1 and HSV-2.
The regulatory submission for Hovilpri was based on the results of a Phase 3 study that showed statistically significant superiority in lesion healing up to day 28 compared to the physician’s choice of treatment. The most common adverse reaction reported for the study drug was headache.
“Today’s approval delivers the first FDA-approved treatment for refractory mucocutaneous HSV lesions with a novel mechanism of action in nearly 30 years and marks an important advancement for immunocompromised adults,” Stacy Wheeler, CEO of Asahi Kasei Therapeutics in the U.S. and Europe, said in a prepared statement. “Hovilpri offers a new oral treatment option for adult patients with a persistent, difficult-to-treat disease.”
Hovilpri was originally developed by AiCuris Anti-Infective Cures, a Germany-based biopharmaceutical company acquired by Asahi Kasei for €780 million (about $919 million). In the February acquisition announcement, Tokyo-based Asahi Kasei said the deal strengthens the company’s presence in severe infectious disease. It added that HSV patients addressed by Hovilpri are commonly seen in transplant centers and specialized hospital settings where the company has established commercial relationships and infrastructure.
Sponsored Post 
The Hidden Administrative Tasks Draining Small Practices 
Small practices play a critical role in healthcare delivery, but they cannot continue to absorb ever-increasing administrative demands without consequences. 
By Michael Blackman, MD, MBA Chief Medical Officer, Greenway Health® 
Asahi Kasei has been expanding its portfolio and pipeline via business deals. In 2020, the company closed the 8.3 billion Danish krone (about $1.3 billion) acquisition of Veloxis Pharmaceuticals , a company that develops and sells therapies for organ transplant patients. The Japanese company’s 11.8 billion Swedish krona (about $1.18 billion) acquisition of Calliditas Pharmaceuticals in 2024 brought a portfolio that includes Tarpeyo, which has FDA approval for treating the rare kidney disorder immunoglobulin A nephropathy.
The Aicuris acquisition brought more than Hovilpri. Asahi Kasei gains royalty income from Prevymis, a cytomegalovirus drug whose global rights Aicuris had licensed to Merck. Lithium futures tumble 10% in China after E.U. deal cuts hybrid car exports
Less than 1 min read 
ALB SQM LAR SGML 
Albemarle ALB and other lithium stocks traded sharply lower pre-market Monday after lithium carbonate futures prices in China plunged to a nearly 10-month low, as an agreement to limit hybrid car exports to the European Union added to concerns over demand prospects for the battery material. 
In pre-market trading, Albemarle ALB down 4.2%, SQM SQM down 4.2%, Lithium Argentina LAR down 3.2%, Sigma Lithium SGML down 1.9%, Atlas Lithium ATLX down 1.7%, Lithium Aericas LAC down 0.8%. 
The most active lithium carbonate contract on the Guangzhou Futures Exchange fell to its weakest since December 17, 2025, before settling down 11.8% to 104,740 yuan/ton ($15,649), marking its steepest daily decline since March. 
China and the European Union reached an agreement that could cut Chinese exports of hybrid cars to the bloc by more than half, the European Trade Commission said Friday. 
Lithium prices have been on a downward trajectory since hitting a 33-month high at 209,880 yuan on May 13 on concerns about demand from electric vehicles and larger-scale energy storage systems. 
Lithium's supply-demand balance is shifting in a bearish direction, Goldman Sachs analysts said in a note, forecasting that both the Chinese and global markets will move from a deficit to nearly balanced in Q4 followed by surpluses in the next two years. [News] ASML Reportedly Plans 10% Parts Price Hike in South Korea Starting Jan. 2027; Equipment Prices May Also Rise
2026-10-12 
Semiconductors 
editor 
With ASML set to report its latest earnings on October 14, the semiconductor equipment industry is seeing stronger demand and growing pricing power as chipmakers expand capacity to support AI-related growth. According to The Elec , ASML reportedly plans to raise prices by 10% on all replacement parts supplied to South Korea, covering both extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography systems. Citing industry sources, the report notes that ASML notified Samsung Electronics and SK hynix of the planned increase through its South Korean subsidiary in early September. The new prices will apply to deliveries starting in January 2027.
The increase will cover everything from regularly purchased consumables to major components replaced due to failures or declining performance. While ASML has previously adjusted prices for individual parts in response to rising raw material costs or supply shortages, an across-the-board 10% hike is unusual. Industry sources suggest the company is seeking a larger share of its customers’ profits.
The price increases may also extend beyond replacement parts, with ASML reportedly discussing higher prices for newly ordered lithography equipment with major customers.
For context, ASML generated €8.193 billion in revenue from services, replacement parts, and upgrades for installed equipment last year, accounting for roughly 25% of its total revenue of €32.667 billion. The company expects revenue from this business to grow by more than 30% this year, according to the report.
ASML’s pricing push comes as demand for its lithography systems remains strong. According to Reuters , the company’s existing EUV machines, priced at around US$200 million each, are nearly sold out through 2027, while major chipmakers are also committing to its next-generation High-NA EUV systems, priced at roughly US$400 million each.
Equipment Suppliers Gain Pricing Power as AI Investment Accelerates
ASML’s pricing push is not limited to South Korea. According to Reuters in July, citing The Information , the company has also sought a 10% price increase for DUV lithography equipment, with some Chinese customers reportedly accepting the adjustment. TSMC, however, is said to be resisting price hikes for both EUV and DUV systems.
Other major equipment suppliers are also pursuing price increases. According to Wall Street Journal , Applied Materials said during its August earnings call that higher prices for both new and existing products were supporting margin expansion. The Elec adds that Tokyo Electron said in late July that it was negotiating price adjustments, including for existing models, to offset rising costs.
Supply constraints are adding to pricing pressures across the industry. According to ETNews , lead times for certain deposition equipment components have increased from four months to as long as 10 months, while some Japanese-made components used in laser processing equipment reportedly face delivery times of up to 40 months.
As The Elec notes, AI-driven capacity expansions among memory makers and foundries are pushing equipment and component demand beyond suppliers’ ability to ramp up production, while inflation and rising raw material costs add further pressure. Industry observers believe ASML’s price increases, reportedly accepted by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, could strengthen other suppliers’ bargaining positions.

title: Aicuris acquisition delivers new drug for Asahi Kasei - pharmaphorum
query: "Asahi Kasei" ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Aicuris acquisition delivers new drug for Asahi Kasei
News
Asahi Kasei's $920 million takeover of German biotech Aicuris in April has paid off with FDA approval for the herpes simplex virus (HSV) drug at the heart of the deal. 
The oral drug, called Hovilpri (pritelivir), has been cleared for treating adults with weakened immune systems who have sores on the skin or mucous membranes – such as lips, nostrils, eyes, and genitals – that are caused by HSV and have not responded to standard nucleoside analogue therapies like acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir.
Hovilpri, which acts as a helicase-primase inhibitor, represents the first FDA approved HSV therapy with a novel mechanism of action in nearly 30 years, according to Asahi Kasei. It also provides an oral alternative to intravenously administered antivirals used to treat immunocompromised adults with refractory HSV infection, with or without resistance to current drugs.
There are two types of HSV infection – HSV-1 and HSV-2 – which cause common infections like cold sores and genital herpes. Most people are exposed to the virus in childhood and recover from the primary infection, although in many cases the virus lies dormant.
HSV is a major threat to immunocompromised people, as the virus can quickly reactivate and cause lesions that release contagious virus particles.
The FDA approval of Hovilpri draws on the pivotal, open-label PRIOH-1 study, which enrolled 101 immunocompromised adults and compared the drug with investigator's choice of available treatments for up to 28 days until all mucocutaneous lesions healed, which was extended up to 42 days if lesions were improving, but not completely healed, after 28 days.
The primary endpoint was the proportion of participants with all lesions healed during the treatment period up to 28 days, which was achieved in 63% of patients receiving Hovilpri, compared with 34% of patients receiving one of the other medications.
The study recruited adults who had weakened immunity due to a wide range of causes, including haematopoietic stem cell transplants (HSCT) for serious illnesses, various forms of cancer, HIV infection, autoimmune diseases, and solid organ transplantation.
Asahi Kasei said that it expects to launch Hovilpri in the US before the end of the year, but has not released pricing details as yet.
Aicuris , which now operates as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Asahi Kasei, previously developed another antiviral used for HSCT patients, MSD-marketed Prevymis (letermovir), which is used to prevent infection with cytomegalovirus (CMV).
It is also developing AIC468, which aims to prevent and treat BK virus infections in kidney transplant recipients.
Asahi Kasei has a long history in the anti-infectives arena, with products like antifungal Cresemba (isavuconazonium sulfate) and aminoglycoside antibiotic Exacin (isepamicin), and has said that adding Aicuris will help it reach its goal of driving pharma sales to around $1.9 billion) by its 2030 fiscal year.

Norway transforms 20 tonnes of recycled aluminium from oil platform into 55-metre bridge
Edited by : Pratyusha Chatterjee 5 min read 
The image used in this article is generated with an AI tool and does not depict any real-time moment
Norway has given aluminium recovered from a decommissioned North Sea oil platform a second life as a 55-metre pedestrian and cycle bridge in Trondheim. The Hangarbrua project uses 20 tonnes of recycled aluminium from the former Gyda platform. The project shows how industrial scrap can be converted into long-lasting public infrastructure while opening new possibilities for aluminium bridge construction.
From North Sea oil platform to urban infrastructure 
The story behind Hangarbrua begins with Gyda, an oil platform that operated in the North Sea from 1990 until its decommissioning in 2021. During dismantling, Aker Solutions recovered approximately 18,000 tonnes of steel and other metals, including aluminium from the platform's topsides.
Stena Recycling sorted the recovered aluminium scrap before supplying it to Hydro for recycling. Hydro processed the material at its facilities in Sweden, casting it into extrusion ingots at its Sjunnen casthouse before transporting it to its extrusion plant in Finspång. There, the recycled metal was transformed into new aluminium profiles for the bridge deck.
The Norwegian Public Roads Administration commissioned Hangarbrua as a pilot project. Leirvik AS designed and built the bridge in collaboration with COWI, while Hydro, Aker Solutions and Stena Recycling contributed to the recycled aluminium supply chain.
The project also marks Norway's return to aluminium bridge construction for the first time since 1995, when Leirvik delivered the Forsmo Bridge.
Join the fourth edition of webinar " Hedging for recyclers - Become an expert in 6 hours " by Jorge Dyszel.
What makes Hangarbrua different? 
Hangarbrua is a network arch bridge designed for pedestrians and cyclists. It crosses the railway lines at Leangen Station, forming part of Trondheim's main walking and cycling route towards the city centre.
Its defining feature is the bridge deck, which uses 100 per cent recycled aluminium recovered from Gyda. The wider structure is made from aluminium, while stainless-steel tension rods provide additional structural support.
The choice of aluminium also offers a construction advantage. According to the project information, an aluminium version weighs approximately one-third as much as a comparable steel bridge, allowing the structure to be assembled away from the railway before being lifted into place.
A carefully planned installation over an active railway 
The bridge's installation required close coordination to minimise disruption to railway operations.
Leirvik test-assembled the structure at its facility in Stord in December 2024. The four main segments were transported to Trondheim in March 2025, where they were joined and fitted with suspension rods, railings and safety nets.
On 19 June 2025, Nordic Crane lifted the completed bridge into position at Leangen Station using a 650-tonne crawler crane with a 72-metre boom. The components arrived in 21 truckloads, and the final lift was carried out during a scheduled railway closure.
The installation was completed within the designated window, with the critical structural elements aligning as planned.
Looking for aluminium recycling equipment providers? Browse through a comprehensive list here at AL Biz 
Can recycled aluminium reduce the carbon footprint of bridges? 
Beyond recycling industrial scrap, Hangarbrua offers an opportunity to examine aluminium's environmental performance in structural applications.
A life cycle analysis conducted by COWI compared the aluminium bridge with a stainless-steel alternative based on the same network arch design. The assessment estimated emissions of 120 tonnes of CO₂ for the aluminium bridge when the benefits of recycling at the end of its life were included, compared with 500 tonnes for the stainless-steel alternative.
Without accounting for those end-of-life recycling benefits, the estimated emissions were 420 tonnes for the aluminium design and 620 tonnes for the stainless-steel version. These figures highlight the importance of considering a material's full life cycle, rather than evaluating its initial production alone.
Aluminium's corrosion resistance is another consideration. The project partners expect the bridge to require minimal maintenance over its lifetime, while the Norwegian Public Roads Administration anticipates maintenance-free performance for 100 years.
Sensors to inform the next generation of aluminium bridges 
Hangarbrua is also part of the Norwegian Public Roads Administration's FjordX research and development programme, which focuses on infrastructure that is cost-efficient, environmentally sustainable and safe.
Sensors installed across the bridge will monitor its structural behaviour, generating data that could help researchers understand how aluminium performs under real-world conditions. The findings may contribute to future design standards and support the development of aluminium bridges with different designs and spans.
The structure has already become a research subject for master's and doctoral students at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology. For Leirvik, which has extensive experience in large aluminium structures for the oil and gas sector, the project represents a renewed opportunity to apply that expertise to bridge construction.
Hangarbrua demonstrates how aluminium recovered from an industry associated with fossil fuel extraction can be redirected towards public infrastructure. More importantly, it provides a practical test case for combining recycled materials, lightweight structural design and life cycle assessment in future construction projects.

ABB Robotics introduces two new high-performance robots for precision manufacturing
Press releases
New, compact IRB 1700 and IRB 1700ID deliver up to 20% shorter cycle times with higher motion accuracy, higher payloads 
Meeting growing demand for high-speed and precision manufacturing, from electronics to automotive 
Lower total cost of ownership by reducing power consumption and increasing service intervals 
ABB Robotics is expanding its industrial robot portfolio with two new compact, high-performance robots, the IRB 1700 and IRB 1700ID , delivering up to 20% shorter cycle times than comparable robots on the market. 
“Precision manufacturing across sectors from electronics, automotive, to general industries is facing the pressure to produce more, while maintaining quality and reducing operating costs,” said Craig McDonnell, Managing Director, Business Line Industries, ABB Robotics. “The IRB 1700 family addresses these challenges with a new level of speed, accuracy, reliability and energy efficiency. It gives manufacturers and system integrators a flexible platform for high-performance automation.” 
Offering payloads from 6 kg to 12 kg across five variants and powered by OmniCore TM controllers, the new robots help manufacturers increase productivity, with up to 20% shorter cycle times, and improve uptime and reduce operating costs, with up to 15% lower power consumption 1 and service intervals of up to 20,000 hours between oil changes. 
Precise path repeatability of down to 0.03 mm and joint speeds of up to 700 degrees per second make the new robots ideal for high-speed precision tasks such as material handling, arc welding, deburring, sanding, and machine tending. The high-performance robots are also suited to new electronics applications such as AI server rack assembly, meeting the surging demand for AI servers 2 and computing. 
The new robot offers a footprint 50% smaller than its predecessor, and for even greater packaging efficiency, the IRB 1700ID model features ABB Robotics’ Integrated Dressing (ID) design, routing cables and hoses inside the robot arm, simplifying installation across industrial applications. 
The IRB 1700 family extends ABB Robotics’ comprehensive mechatronics portfolio and ABB Robotics’ development of more autonomous and versatile robotics ( AVR TM ), with access to an expanding portfolio of programming and AI-powered software, including RobotStudio ® , AI Robot Trainer, OmniCore EyeMotion and automatic collision-free path planning. 
The IRB 1700 and IRB 1700ID will make their public debut at China International Industry Fair (CIIF), Shanghai, October 12–16, 2026, demonstrated in a fully functional arc welding and sanding application on the ABB Robotics stand.

Airbus Asia Training Centre Welcomes South Korea's Jin Air as 97th Customer
October 12, 2026
Singapore & South Korea – Airbus Asia Training Centre (AATC), the Singapore-based flight simulator training joint venture between Airbus and Singapore Airlines, has welcomed South Korean low-cost carrier Jin Air as a customer for Airbus A320 type rating training. 
Jin Air becomes AATC's 97th customer, according to the training centre's October 2026 announcement, extending its portfolio of airline training customers across Asia-Pacific. 
The training arrangement comes as Jin Air transitions from its historically Boeing-focused fleet toward Airbus A320-family operations. In 2026, the airline began incorporating Airbus A321 aircraft, including an A321-200 previously operated by Asiana Airlines, alongside plans to introduce additional A321neo aircraft. 
Jin Air signed an agreement in August 2026 to merge with Air Busan and Air Seoul, targeting the launch of an integrated low-cost airline under the Jin Air brand on 17 March 2027. The integration will consolidate Airbus and Boeing operations, creating additional flight crew training and fleet standardisation requirements. 
Jin Air has also been investing in domestic simulator capacity, having introduced an A320neo full flight simulator in May 2026 and outlined plans to operate two FFS devices and one flight training device. 
Airbus' September 2026 disclosure identified nine installed FFS devices at AATC, comprising two A320, one A330, four A350, one A380 and one ATR 72-600 simulator, alongside six fixed cockpit training devices. 
About Airbus Asia Training Centre 
The Airbus Asia Training Centre, located in Singapore’s Seletar Aerospace Park, provides pilot type-rating and recurrent training for all Airbus jetliner models. Established in 2015, AATC is part of the Airbus global Flight Training network, serving the Asia-Pacific region and beyond. This 10, 000-square-foot facility is fitted with x10 Full Flight Simulators (FFS), including x2 A320, x2 A330, x4 A350, x1 A380 and x1 ATR. This makes AATC the largest flight crew training facility within the Airbus Training Centre network and the largest operator of A350 FFS worldwide. It also features a ATR 72-600 FFS.

ABL Texcell Diagnostics Strengthens Its Presence at Genopole and Opens a New Chapter in Precision Oncology With the Acquisition of IntegraGen’s Assets and Operations
Business Wire 
October 12, 2026 8 min read 
ABLD.PA 
-2.46% 
A few months after integrating Texcell's activities, ABL Texcell Diagnostics strengthens its expertise in precision oncology, human genetics and rare diseases, while continuing to build a leading French life sciences platform 
WOIPPY, France, October 12, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Regulatory News: 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics (Euronext Paris: ABLD – ISIN: FR001400AHX6), a company specializing in molecular diagnostic solutions, healthcare software, and services supporting clinical research and biopharmaceutical development, today announces the acquisition of IntegraGen's assets and business operations ( www.integragen.com , Euronext Growth Paris: ALINT – ISIN: FR0010908723), pursuant to the ruling handed down by the Evry Commercial Court on Friday, October 9, 2026. 
This transaction comes just a few months after the integration of Texcell's activities, which strengthened the Company's capabilities in virology, biosafety and scientific services for the biopharmaceutical industry. It marks a new milestone for ABL Texcell Diagnostics by extending its expertise into clinical genomics, human genetics, rare diseases and precision oncology. 
A Takeover Offer Underpinned by a Long-Term Industrial and Social Commitment 
As part of the offer approved by the Court, ABL Texcell Diagnostics submitted a comprehensive industrial plan based on the continued operation of the acquired activities, the retention of key expertise and the continuity of contracts required to conduct the business. 
The Company acquires IntegraGen's strategic assets, inventories and contracts essential to the continuation of its operations. It will also welcome 16 employees with critical expertise in sequencing, bioinformatics, quality and laboratory operations. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics has also committed to maintaining the contractual benefits of the transferred employees and assuming their accrued paid-leave entitlements. The offer further provides that no redundancies for economic reasons will be implemented for a period of 24 months following the takeover. 
These commitments reflect the Company's intention to pursue the transaction as part of a sustainable industrial project combining operational continuity, the preservation of expertise and the gradual development of the acquired activities. 
An Overall Economic Commitment Extending Beyond the Acquisition Price 
The total acquisition price amounts to €100,000, comprising €95,000 for tangible and intangible assets and €5,000 for inventories. 
In addition to this price, the offer submitted by ABL Texcell Diagnostics includes several economic and operational commitments. These notably cover the assumption of employees' accrued entitlements, the continuation of contracts required for business operations and the commitments associated with the transferred equipment, together with an initial investment program estimated at €150,000 to support the redeployment of the activities. 
Story Continues 
The Company also estimates that the funding requirements associated with restarting operations, ensuring business continuity and integrating the activities could amount to approximately €900,000 during the first few months following the takeover. 
Considering the acquisition price, the planned investments, the identified funding requirements and the other commitments associated with the transaction, the project undertaken by ABL Texcell Diagnostics represents an overall economic commitment estimated at more than €1.27 million. 
The transaction is not subject to any conditions precedent and is being financed from the Company's own resources. This financing structure reflects ABL Texcell Diagnostics' confidence in the potential of the acquired activities, while remaining consistent with a disciplined approach to investment and capital allocation. 
A First Strategic Milestone in Precision Oncology and Human Genetics 
IntegraGen combines established commercial activities in next-generation sequencing, or NGS, and genomic analysis software with a portfolio of proprietary precision-oncology technologies. These include solutions developed for the detection and monitoring of minimal residual disease, or MRD, referring to cancer cells that may remain after treatment even when the disease is no longer detectable using conventional testing methods. 
For ABL Texcell Diagnostics, this acquisition represents the first milestone in molecular oncology, human genetics and rare diseases. It broadens the Company's positioning beyond its historical core business in the molecular diagnosis of infectious diseases, while adding complementary expertise, technologies and commercial activities in clinical genomics and bioinformatics. 
The combination of IntegraGen's expertise with that of the Texcell and ABL Diagnostics divisions also creates the conditions for developing new offerings for pharmaceutical laboratories and biotechnology companies. Combining Texcell's viral clearance studies with IntegraGen's NGS and bioinformatics capabilities could support the development of integrated biological characterization, viral safety and genomic analysis services for biopharmaceutical products. 
At the same time, ABL Texcell Diagnostics intends to initiate discussions with companies specializing in oncology diagnostics to explore potential technological and commercial synergies, as well as possible collaborations. These initiatives could contribute to leveraging IntegraGen's sequencing capabilities, genomic analysis software and proprietary technologies in connection with new precision-oncology applications. 
These opportunities may also benefit from IntegraGen's experience in providing services under the US CLIA and CAP frameworks. Their implementation will be gradual and will remain subject to the completion of the integration process, the validation of market needs and confirmation of the regulatory scope and accreditations applicable to the relevant services. 
A Stronger Presence Within Genopole 
The acquired activities will continue to operate from the Evry site, enabling ABL Texcell Diagnostics to strengthen its presence within Genopole, an ecosystem dedicated to genomics, biotechnology and healthcare innovation. 
The Company intends to preserve the scientific and technical expertise developed by IntegraGen while providing employees, customers and partners with a stable environment in which to ensure business continuity and support the future development of the activities. 
During the integration phase, priority will be given to continuity of service, support for employees and the maintenance of the quality standards expected by customers. In parallel, ABL Texcell Diagnostics will conduct a structured assessment of the commercial and scientific opportunities that may arise from bringing these activities together. 
" We welcome IntegraGen's teams and activities with great respect for the work accomplished over more than 20 years in the field of genomics. This acquisition is fully aligned with our commitment to preserving recognized scientific expertise and providing it with a stable environment that supports its long-term development ," said Dr. Chalom Sayada, Chief Executive Officer of ABL Texcell Diagnostics and co-founder of ABL Luxembourg, the parent company and principal shareholder of the ABL Group. 
" Following the integration of Texcell, this transaction marks a new stage in the development of ABL Texcell Diagnostics. It strengthens our presence at Genopole while expanding our expertise across several strategic areas of Life Sciences. It also marks our entry into highly science-driven segments such as precision oncology, human genetics and rare diseases, which naturally complement our historical expertise in molecular diagnostics and infectious diseases. " 
" Our priority remains to ensure business continuity, support the teams joining us and sustain the satisfaction of the customers who place their trust in u s," concluded Dr. Sayada. 
The Acquisition of IntegraGen's Activities Opens a New Phase of Development 
The acquisition of IntegraGen's activities opens a new phase of development for ABL Texcell Diagnostics. Following the acquisition of Texcell, this transaction further expands the Company's scientific and operational scope. 
Considering this recent evolution, ABL Texcell Diagnostics is currently reviewing its operational priorities, integration requirements and development roadmap. Based on this work, the roadmap and objectives previously communicated for the 2026 financial year may, where appropriate, be updated to reflect the Company's new scope. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics will keep the market informed, in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, of any material development likely to affect its business, outlook or financial position. 
About ABL Texcell Diagnostics (ABLD) 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics (ABLD) is an international company that specializes in innovative molecular biology tests and global solutions for its customers: 
Molecular polymerase chain reaction (PCR) detection – UltraGene, and 
Genotyping by DNA sequencing – DeepChek®. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics markets its entire product range globally through its own sales team and a network of exclusive distributors active on all continents. ABL Diagnostics' customers are academic clinical pathology laboratories, private reference laboratories and researchers willing to implement innovative and robust microbiological content in constant expansion. 
Following the acquisition of TEXCELL's operations, ABL Texcell Diagnostics is expanding its activities in the life sciences sector by integrating expertise and services dedicated to virology, biosafety testing and biopharmaceutical development support. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics has been marketing the products and services of its sister company CDL Pharma since the second half of 2025 through an intra-group strategy agreement. 
An expanding portfolio of microbiology products: 
HIV – Drug resistance testing, including a whole genome kit. 
SARS-CoV-2, Tuberculosis, Hepatitis B and C – Advanced Detection Solutions. 
Microbiome and taxonomy – 16s/18s RNA-based analyses. 
Other viral and bacterial targets – Comprehensive molecular assays. 
Integrated Solutions 
Real-time syndromic PCR tests 
Nadis® – Patient Medical Record used in more than 200 hospitals in France for the management of HIV and hepatitis. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics, headquartered in Woippy, is a public limited company listed on compartment B of the regulated market of Euronext in Paris (Euronext: ABLD – ISIN: FR001400AHX6). These molecular biology products generate recurring revenues and cover one of the largest portfolios of applications in microbiology.

By Nitisha Dubey

Hand robot manipulator for packaging products 
October 12, 2026 
The partnership aligns with India’s efforts to establish a domestic outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) industry 
Tata Electronics and Dutch semiconductor assembly equipment supplier Besi have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to develop advanced semiconductor packaging capabilities in India. The partnership will support Tata Electronics’ planned $3 billion semiconductor packaging facility in Jagiroad, Assam.
Under the agreement, Tata Electronics will evaluate Besi’s advanced packaging equipment and technologies for the facility. The companies will also explore local equipment support, technical collaboration and measures to ensure equipment readiness for production operations.
The collaboration will include engineering development, knowledge-sharing programmes, and specialised training and certification for Tata Electronics employees. The companies also plan to develop a joint technology roadmap and processes to address future packaging requirements and strengthen India’s semiconductor supply chain.
The partnership aligns with India’s efforts to establish a domestic outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) industry. It also follows a bilateral agreement between India and the Netherlands to strengthen cooperation in semiconductors and related emerging technologies.
- Advertisement - 
“Advanced packaging is rapidly becoming one of the most critical differentiators in semiconductor innovation,” said Dr Randhir Thakur, CEO and Managing Director of Tata Electronics. He added that combining Besi’s expertise with Tata Electronics’ expanding manufacturing capabilities would help accelerate advanced packaging development in India, foster innovation and build a semiconductor ecosystem serving domestic and global customers.
Richard Blickman, CEO and Chairman of Besi, said the company’s range of advanced packaging solutions would support Tata Electronics’ ambition to become a global semiconductor manufacturing player. He added that the collaboration reflects both companies’ commitment to innovation, technology development and the advancement of the semiconductor industry.

Renishaw completes first phase of £70m Welsh manufacturing site expansion 
Posted on 12 Oct 2026 by James Devonshire 
Share this article: 
Share on Linkedin 
Share on Twitter 
Share on facebook 
Copy Link 
Company: 
Renishaw 
Engineering technologies business Renishaw has completed the first phase of a £70m expansion at its Miskin facility in South Wales, increasing manufacturing capacity to meet rising demand for its precision measurement and additive manufacturing technologies. 
The development, first announced in 2022, forms part of a long-term investment programme that will ultimately double the size of the site, west of Cardiff, establishing it as one of the UK’s largest advanced manufacturing facilities.
The completion of Hall 3 has increased the site’s usable space to 617,000 sq ft (57,350 sqm). Once Hall 4 is completed and operational, the facility will cover 880,000 sq ft (81,765 sqm). The expansion coincides with the 15th anniversary of Renishaw’s acquisition of the 193-acre site from Robert Bosch Ltd in September 2011. From an initial operation employing around 25 people when the facility officially opened in October 2012, the site now employs approximately 950.
Renishaw has invested around £150m at Miskin to date, covering the site acquisition, refurbishment of existing buildings, new construction and the installation of advanced manufacturing equipment.
Meeting demand for advanced manufacturing technologies 
The latest development will help Renishaw increase production of its precision metrology, additive manufacturing and position measurement products, with growing demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment creating an immediate requirement for additional capacity.
Hall 3 houses manufacturing operations for the company’s metal additive manufacturing (AM) systems and AGILITY co-ordinate measuring machines (CMMs), alongside a multimillion-pound automated storage and retrieval warehousing system.
Hall 4 was initially constructed as a shell building, allowing Renishaw to bring the space into use as customer demand and production requirements evolved. Exceptional demand for the company’s position encoders, driven by the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), means part of the building will now be occupied over the coming months.
The Miskin facility currently operates 134 CNC machine tools, producing around one million parts per month, alongside three printed circuit board (PCB) assembly lines, robotic assembly systems and automated warehousing. Further equipment is on order to support customer requirements.
Our long-term commitment to manufacturing is exemplified by the investment that we have made in Miskin over the past 15 years and I would like to thank the many people from across our business who have supported the development of this world-class facility.
Jim Long, Director of Group Manufacturing at Renishaw 
Sustainability and workforce investment 
The expansion has also been designed to improve the facility’s environmental performance. Both new halls have been designed to achieve Net Zero Carbon in Operation, supporting Renishaw’s commitment to reaching Net Zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scopes 1 and 2 by 2028. The company’s longer-term ambition is for all buildings at Miskin to operate at Net Zero.
Alongside the manufacturing investment, Renishaw has developed an employee wellbeing centre incorporating a restaurant and fitness suite. Improvements to the wider site include landscaped outdoor spaces, picnic areas and a 2km perimeter walking route.
The investment underlines Renishaw’s commitment to South Wales, with additional manufacturing space intended to support future growth in demand for advanced engineering technologies.
“The significant ongoing investment by our Board to increase our production capabilities demonstrates a huge vote of confidence in our manufacturing operations and people, at an exciting time for the business,” Long added.

ASML, the world's largest semiconductor equipment maker, will raise prices by 10% across replacement parts supplied to South Korea.
​The increase covers all parts for extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography systems. The new prices will take effect for deliveries starting in January 2027.
​ASML headquarters notified Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix of the proposed increase through its South Korean subsidiary in early September, according to industry sources. The increase was finalized after discussions with the purchasing organizations of both companies.
​Prices will rise for everything from consumable parts purchased regularly to major components replaced because of failures or performance degradation. Lithography systems contain numerous components, including optical parts such as lenses and mirrors that direct light, light sources and precision motion-control systems. The increase will raise the cost of keeping the equipment operational.
​ASML has traditionally adjusted prices for individual parts when raw material costs rose sharply or specific materials became difficult to procure, according to industry sources. A blanket 10% increase is unusual.
​"Prices have risen across the board for the components that make up these parts, but ASML also appears to be seeking a larger share of the profits its customers are making," an industry official said.
​ASML separately reports revenue from services, parts and upgrades for equipment already installed at customer sites. This revenue totaled €8.193 billion last year, accounting for 25% of total sales of €32.667 billion. ASML forecast that revenue from this business would grow by more than 30% this year.
​Prices for newly ordered ASML equipment are also likely to increase, following the spare-parts hike. The company is discussing equipment price increases with major customers.
​The Information, a US technology news outlet, reported in July that ASML had notified Chinese semiconductor manufacturers and other customers of a 10% increase in DUV equipment prices, with some customers accepting the change. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), ASML's largest customer, was reportedly opposing the increase.
​Industry observers expect ASML's decision to raise prices across the board, accepted by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, to strengthen the position of other semiconductor equipment and component suppliers seeking price increases.
​Price hikes are already under way. US-based Applied Materials said during its earnings announcement in August that prices had risen for both new and existing products. Japan's Tokyo Electron also said at an earnings briefing in late July that it was pursuing price adjustments, including for equipment already on the market, to offset rising costs. US plasma power supply maker Advanced Energy Industries likewise said it had raised prices for some product lines.
​The broader price increases reflect a supply-demand imbalance. Investment in artificial intelligence (AI) data centers has prompted memory makers and foundries to expand capacity simultaneously, driving up orders for equipment and components. Suppliers need time to expand their facilities and increase production. Rising inflation and raw material costs have also added to their cost burdens. Unlike in the past, when semiconductor manufacturers used their purchasing power to demand lower prices, suppliers now have greater leverage in negotiations.
​"Large-scale capacity expansion is translating into actual demand, pushing equipment and components into a supply-shortage phase," an industry official said. "As wafer input volumes increase, the materials used in production will also face large-scale supply shortages."

Hexagon to acquire Rocscience for $535m
Posted on October 11, 2026 at 8:34 am by AEC Magazine 
215 
0 
Deal aims to connect geotechnical simulation with live monitoring data across infrastructure and mining projects
Hexagon has signed an agreement to acquire geotechnical analysis software developer Rocscience from TA Associates and the company’s founders and management. The transaction values the Toronto-based business at US$535 million on a cash-free, debt-free basis and is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary conditions.
Rocscience develops software for modelling the behaviour of rock, soil and structures, analysing slope stability and ground movement, and assessing the performance of tunnels, dams and other infrastructure. Its products are used by mining, civil engineering and energy customers in around 125 countries. The software also offers AI-assisted workflows, including a natural-language interface.
The acquisition is intended to bring Rocscience’s simulation capabilities together with Hexagon’s sensor and monitoring technologies, including radar monitoring systems. Hexagon envisages a continuous feedback loop in which live sensor data informs, updates and calibrates engineering models throughout design, construction and operation.

👉 Subscribe FREE here 
For infrastructure teams, the proposed integration could help connect predictions of ground and structural behaviour with measured site conditions. Hexagon says this would support earlier detection of emerging risks, faster intervention and reduced analysis time. Rocscience will join the Radar & Monitoring Division within Hexagon’s Infrastructure & Geospatial Business Area.
“Its software is complementary to our sensor and monitoring businesses in mining, and increasingly in civil and infrastructure applications,” said Henning Sandfort, president, Infrastructure & Geospatial, Hexagon AB.
“By connecting what our sensors measure with how Rocscience’s models predict, we can help customers move from data capture to informed action with far greater confidence.”
Rocscience is expected to generate revenue approaching US$50 million in 2026, with annual recurring revenue equivalent to more than 80% of revenue. Hexagon expects the acquisition to be accretive to net income from closing and reports EBITAC margins above 40%.

title: $17-million Boeing investment expands Indigenous aviation training in Saskatchewan - WestCentralOnline

content_text:
$17-million Boeing investment expands Indigenous aviation training in Saskatchewan
Jenny Hagan, 
WestCentralOnline.com | 
Saturday, Oct 10 2026, 6:00 AM 
Share: 
Copied!
SIIT president and CEO Riel Bellegarde said the project reflects years of collaboration and a shared commitment to expanding educational opportunities. 
Article continues below advertisement ↴ 
A $17-million investment from Boeing is helping expand aviation training opportunities for Indigenous students in Saskatchewan while addressing a growing demand for skilled workers in Canada's aerospace industry.
The Saskatchewan Indian Institute of Technologies (SIIT) and Boeing celebrated the grand opening of the expanded Saskatchewan Aviation Learning Centre (SALC) in Saskatoon on Sept. 25, marking another milestone in a partnership that began more than 15 years ago.
The expansion includes modern classrooms, a specialized avionics laboratory and additional hands-on training spaces designed to prepare students for careers in aircraft maintenance and aerospace technology.
The upgraded facility will also support SIIT's new Aircraft Maintenance Engineer – Category E (AME-E) Avionics program, providing students with opportunities to develop specialized skills in aircraft electrical and electronic systems. 
Expanding opportunities for Indigenous learners
The Saskatchewan Aviation Learning Centre plays a role in preparing Indigenous students for careers in aviation, an industry facing ongoing challenges in recruiting and retaining qualified workers.
The expansion is expected to increase training capacity for future aircraft maintenance engineers while creating additional pathways into Saskatchewan's aerospace sector.
SIIT president and CEO Riel Bellegarde said the project reflects years of collaboration and a shared commitment to expanding educational opportunities.
"More than 15 years ago, Boeing saw the potential in what SIIT was building through the Saskatchewan Aviation Learning Centre, and they have continued to walk alongside us as that vision has grown," Bellegarde said. 
"Today, as we celebrate our 50th anniversary as an institution we can reflect on how far that vision has come and what this expansion will make possible for Indigenous learners in aviation and aerospace."
The grand opening coincides with SIIT's 50th anniversary. Established in 1976 by Saskatchewan First Nations chiefs representing all treaty areas, the institution provides academic, vocational and technical training, along with employment and career development services.
Indigenous students account for more than 95 per cent of SIIT's student population.
Related Stories:

Boeing investment supports workforce development
The expansion is supported by Boeing's $17-million investment through Canada's Industrial and Technological Benefits program. 
The investment is connected to the federal government's selection of Boeing's P-8A Poseidon aircraft for Canada's multi-mission aircraft program.
The Industrial and Technological Benefits program requires companies awarded major defence contracts to undertake business activities and investments that benefit Canada's economy.
Boeing's partnership with SIIT dates back to 2010, when the company first contributed to establishing the Saskatchewan Aviation Learning Centre.
Boeing Canada president Al Meinzinger said the expanded facility will help strengthen the province's aviation workforce.
"We're very proud of what our longstanding partnership with SIIT has achieved, particularly in expanding access to high-quality aerospace education here in Saskatchewan," Meinzinger said. 
"This will help create meaningful opportunities for Indigenous learners and it's exciting to know that students trained at the SALC will bring their talent and skills to the aerospace sector for years to come."
Addressing Canada's aviation workforce needs
The expanded training centre is intended to help address shortages of skilled aviation workers by increasing access to specialized aircraft maintenance education.
Aircraft maintenance engineers are responsible for inspecting, maintaining and repairing aircraft to ensure they meet safety and operational standards.
The new avionics program will provide training focused on aircraft electronic systems, an increasingly important field as aviation technology continues to advance.
Federal Secretary of State for Defence Procurement Stephen Fuhr said the investment demonstrates how defence procurement can support Canadian workforce development. 
"Canada's Industrial and Technological Benefits program is delivering tangible results for Canadians," Fuhr said.
"The new Saskatchewan Aviation Learning Centre will create new training opportunities in the aerospace sector and continue to grow Canada's aviation capabilities."
Provincial government welcomes expansion
Saskatchewan Advanced Education Minister Ken Cheveldayoff said the expanded facility will provide students with opportunities to pursue technical careers without leaving the province for specialized training.
"This expansion is an important investment in Saskatchewan students, communities and industries," Cheveldayoff said.
"Partnerships like this ensure our students have access to high-quality, hands-on training close to home." 
Saskatchewan Immigration and Career Training Minister Eric Schmalz also welcomed Boeing's continued investment, noting the province provides funding for SIIT's aircraft maintenance engineer program.
Schmalz said the partnership represents an important investment in Saskatchewan's skilled trades workforce.
Building on 50 years of education
As SIIT marks five decades of providing educational opportunities, the expanded aviation centre represents another step in the institution's efforts to connect Indigenous learners with employment in specialized industries.
SIIT is a First Nations-governed institution and one of four credit-granting post-secondary institutions in Saskatchewan.
The expanded Saskatchewan Aviation Learning Centre is expected to support future generations of aircraft maintenance professionals while contributing to the province's aviation industry. 
The announcement did not specify how many additional students the expanded facility will accommodate or when the new avionics program will begin accepting students.

title: Samsung's HBM Market Share Jumps to 33%; Hybrid Bonding Technology Could Be Key to Overtaking Rivals - BigGo Finance
